   In pcalg, the PC interface requires a conditional-independence test and its significance
level. Its stable skeleton option addresses ordering in the skeleton search; it does not by
itself settle all orientation conflicts. Conservative and majority-rule variants treat ambiguous
triples differently. Some configurations can return a partial graph that is not extendable to
a DAG, and conflict-handling options can introduce bidirected marks with an algorithmic
meaning (pcalg contributors, 2026). An importer must preserve that meaning. Such a conflict
is not automatically evidence of a latent common cause, even though bidirected edges have a
substantive interpretation in other graphical formalisms.
   A particularly consequential default is NAdelete=TRUE: a missing independence-test result
can cause an edge to be deleted. In the proposed banking boundary, a failed statistical
calculation should produce a diagnostic response with its cause. It should not become evidence
that two financial variables are independent. Merely changing the option to false is also
insufficient if a failed test is then silently treated as dependence. The wrapper must detect
a missing or nonfinite result and stop that numerical request. The package’s documented
flexibility and the product’s selected behavior are therefore different layers of the comparison.
  The bnlearn family provides a different breadth. Its constraint-based defaults depend
on variable type, while its score-based and hybrid methods expose different search controls.
The inspected documentation gives an α of 0.05 for constraint procedures, locally complete
18.4. An exact funding example: identical observations, different actions                     165


observations for individual tests with missing data, BIC defaults for common score searches,
and no random restarts by default for hill climbing. The MMHC and H2PC names denote
compositions of restriction and maximization procedures, rather than new independent guar-
antees. DirectLiNGAM uses a separate functional-model route with its own ordering and
selection choices (Marco Scutari and contributors, 2026). For a bank, this breadth supports
useful baselines, but it also makes an unqualified “bnlearn result” an inadequate description of
an experiment.
   BCDAG makes graph uncertainty explicit through a Gaussian DAG model and posterior
sampling. Its compatible DAG-Wishart construction is described in the original preprint; the
inspected version 1.1.4 manual distinguishes structure-only sampling, joint graph/parameter
sampling, effect summaries and credible intervals (Federico Castelletti and Alessandro Mascaro,
2022, 2026). The fast option changes the proposal-ratio calculation through an approxima-
tion; its default is false. A comparison must therefore specify the graph prior, parameter
hyperparameters, burn-in, retained draws, chain configuration and approximation setting. A
stable trace is useful diagnostic evidence but is not a proof that a finite chain explored all
consequential graph regions.
   BiDAG’s order and partition samplers expose another tradeoff. A search space can begin
with a PC-derived skeleton and then be expanded. A MAP graph under that space and a
sample from a specified posterior serve different purposes. Parent limits and the expansion
strategy influence both computation and what can be learned (Polina Suter and Jack Kuipers,
2026). If a true funding relationship was excluded during search-space construction, a later
apparently stable graph sample cannot recover it without a mechanism that admits it. A
benchmark must consequently compare declared search procedures, not only the final graphs
after favorable tuning.
   The mcmcabn documentation starts from a precomputed score cache, commonly constructed
with abn, and describes structural MCMC moves, priors and structural queries (Gilles Kratzer
and contributors, 2023). This provides an alternative for mixed node distributions and explicit
structural prior beliefs. It also introduces a scoring dependency whose assumptions and version
belong to the scientific input. The inspected documentation contains a conversion issue: a
named example places the Smoking-to-LungCancer prior at the row for the child and column
for the parent, while explanatory prose in the vignette describes rows as parents and columns
as children. A proposed integration must resolve this discrepancy with named-node source
and runtime checks. Silently choosing one convention would be an avoidable scientific error.
   These comparisons support a narrow initial choice: a pcalg route for explicitly typed
discovery and effect multisets, bnlearn as a method-specific alternative, and Bayesian routes as
separately configured sensitivity comparisons. They do not justify porting every algorithm into
a new library. The Bayesian routes may be particularly informative when prior restrictions
are part of the scientific question; their value should be assessed by changing those restrictions
and reporting the resulting decision sensitivity.


18.4      An exact funding example: identical observations, differ-
          ent actions
Consider centered continuous variables X, M and Y . In this constructed example X is an
offered-rate margin measured in percentage points, M is a continuous funding-response index,
and Y is subsequent net funding value in thousands of currency units. The index is not a
binary take-up indicator. For this first comparison, the admissible class uses the cross-sectional
law and acyclicity alone: assignment and temporal-order evidence have deliberately been
166                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


withheld. A verified banking clock would exclude any reverse model that contradicts it. The
example isolates what the observational law itself can establish. Let the disturbances below be
mutually independent standard Gaussians:

                     X = εX ,       M = 0.6X + εM ,        Y = 0.8M + εY .                  (18.3)

Under the causal interpretation of these equations, replacing the equation for X by a fixed
assignment gives a total derivative of 0.6 × 0.8 = 0.48. The observational covariance matrix, in
the order (X, M, Y ), is                                    
                                          1     0.6     0.48
                                 Σ =  0.6 1.36 1.088  .                                (18.4)
                                                            
                                        0.48 1.088 1.8704
The partial covariance of X and Y given M vanishes because 0.48 − 0.6(1.088)/1.36 = 0. For
the Gaussian law this is the conditional independence X ⊥ Y | M .
   That same covariance admits the fork X ← M → Y . Take Var(M ) = 1.36, regress X on M
with coefficient 0.6/1.36, and retain the coefficient 0.8 from M to Y . Independent residual
variances are 1 − 0.62 /1.36 for X and 1 for Y . They are positive, and the resulting covariance
is exactly (18.4). Intervening on X now changes neither M nor Y , so its total effect on Y is
zero.
   The reverse chain X ← M ← Y provides a third representation. Let Var(Y ) = 1.8704, use
coefficient 1.088/1.8704 from Y to M , and 0.6/1.36 from M to X. The residual variance for
M is 1.36 − 1.0882 /1.8704, and that for X is again 1 − 0.62 /1.36. This gives the same observed
law and again gives zero effect of X on Y . The distinct effect values across these three models
are therefore
                                           {0, 0.48}.                                      (18.5)
The repeated zero matters if a procedure retains graph multiplicities; the set of distinct values
and a multiset must not be confused. All covariance equalities and effects in this example
have been checked with exact rational arithmetic (Causal banking research project, 2026g).
No discovery engine was run to obtain them, and no finite-sample recovery rate is implied.
   An observational search that preserves the undirected path X − M − Y is consistent with
this ambiguity. A procedure that selects the forward chain has supplied a graph choice in
addition to the observational information. This is precisely the distinction the IDA multiset
makes useful in its specified linear Gaussian setting (pcalg contributors, 2026). Additional
knowledge can change the model class: a justified temporal ordering, an intervention or a
substantive structural restriction may exclude one of the alternative graphs. Merely naming
X an “offer” does not document that restriction. The bank must establish how the offer was
assigned and when the relevant variables were generated and observed.
  The difference has an immediate monetary consequence. If Xbp = 100X and Ycurrency =
1000Y , then the forward-model derivative becomes

                        ∂E[Ycurrency | do(Xbp = x)]   1000
                                                    =      0.48 = 4.8.                      (18.6)
                                     ∂x                100
A 25 basis point change gives 120 currency units per eligible customer in this linear construction,
or 1.2 million over 10,000 such customers if the same additive, noninterfering mechanism
applies to each. The other two compatible models give zero. These are conditional planning
calculations, not measured revenue or an investment recommendation. Aggregation and a
currency conversion cannot remove the underlying identification ambiguity.
18.5. Keep graph ambiguity, statistical uncertainty and prior uncertainty apart               167


18.5      Keep graph ambiguity, statistical uncertainty and prior
          uncertainty apart
The example separates uncertainties that are often compressed into one picture. Even with
the population covariance known exactly, the three causal representations disagree about
the intervention. Finite observations introduce additional uncertainty about covariance and
conditional independences. If a graph is chosen from those observations, subsequent effect
estimation also depends on that choice. A graph-equivalence multiset is consequently not a
confidence interval with a nominal repeated-sampling coverage level. Taking its convex hull
may be useful for a conservative decision rule, but the hull loses information about disconnected
possibilities and multiplicity.
  A Bayesian analysis describes another object. Write G for a DAG and ϑG for its parameters.
The posterior distribution of an effect can be expressed as
                                X               Z
               Π(θ ∈ B | D) =        Π(G | D)       1{Ψ(G, ϑG ) ∈ B} dΠ(ϑG | G, D),        (18.7)
                                 G

where D denotes the observed data and B a measurable set of effect values. The graph prior,
conditional parameter prior and likelihood jointly determine this distribution. Compatible
priors can assign the same marginal likelihood to Markov-equivalent Gaussian DAGs, as
described in the BCDAG construction (Federico Castelletti and Alessandro Mascaro, 2022).
Observational equivalence has not disappeared: different graph weights can still reflect prior
restrictions or different admissible model classes.
   The BCDAG method named confint.bcdagCE explicitly reports credible intervals (Federico
Castelletti and Alessandro Mascaro, 2026). Its function name is not a reason to label the
output a frequentist confidence interval. The proposed result therefore stores the uncertainty
family, conditioning assumptions and computational method alongside the numerical bounds.
It also retains the prior and MCMC configuration for posterior results. If a later simulation
claims coverage, that is a separate empirical statement about a specified repeated-sampling
experiment, with all failed and unavailable requests retained in its denominator.
   The distinction is consequential for investment. A concentrated posterior under a strong
orientation prior can support a conditional decision while still leaving the prior’s banking
justification unsettled. Conversely, an effect collection containing zero can reveal that a
proposed rate experiment has informational value. The relevant question is then whether a
feasible experiment can distinguish the mechanisms sufficiently to change the action. The
product should make that unresolved decision visible rather than display a more precise-looking
number obtained by silently discarding alternatives.


18.6      Targets must survive an identification or estimation
          boundary
DoWhy provides a useful model of separating a supplied causal model, identification and
estimation. The inspected source revision is b06369ed from 4 October 2026. Its graph-learning
entry point is deprecated, and its identification path operates on supplied graph, treatment,
outcome and observed-node information (PyWhy contributors, 2026a). The proposed reuse is
therefore an optional identification service for an explicit reviewed graph. It does not treat the
package as an automatic authority on the bank’s diagram or as a universal discovery engine.
  An exact second example shows why the target belongs to the interface. Let W be a baseline
customer characteristic, A a binary invitation and Y an outcome measured in thousands of
168                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


currency units. Suppose

        P(W = 1) = 21 ,                        e(W ) := P(A = 1 | W ) = 0.2 + 0.6W,         (18.8)
      E[Y (a) | W ] = 3W + a(1 + 2W ).                                                      (18.9)

Under consistency, exchangeability conditional on W , positivity and no interference, the
population average effect is
                          1
                          X
                ATE =         {E[Y | A = 1, w] − E[Y | A = 0, w]}P(W = w) = 2.             (18.10)
                          w=0

The treated group has P(W = 1 | A = 1) = 0.8, while the untreated group has P(W = 1 | A =
0) = 0.2. Their average effects are consequently ATT = 2.6 and ATC = 1.4. The unadjusted
outcome difference is 5 − 0.6 = 4.4. These values are exact calculations from the declared
law (Causal banking research project, 2026g). The same records therefore support different
numbers for different targets, and an association can differ from all of them.
   An adapter must retain whether the question concerns all eligible customers, the invited
customers or the uninvited customers. It must also retain the contrast and the outcome scale.
If W is instead unobserved in the graph W → A, W → Y , A → Y , the stated adjustment
is unavailable. No instrument or front-door mediator has been supplied in this example. A
predictive regression on A is not a repair of the missing identification argument.
   The source review suggests two additional precautions in a narrow DoWhy boundary.
Confidence intervals are not requested by default and depend on the selected estimator. Further,
the inspected identification function assigns the argument proceed_when_unidentifiable but
does not forward it to the identifier (PyWhy contributors, 2026a). This is a source observation,
not an executed package failure. The interface must validate the returned estimand and its
assumptions directly, instead of treating the presence of that flag as a verified safeguard. An
empty adjustment set, an unavailable estimand, a model-implied zero and an engine exception
need different responses.


18.7     A proposed R boundary with explicit failure behavior
The first R path is deliberately narrow: independently sampled continuous Gaussian obser-
vations for PC, and singleton total-effect multisets for IDA under its linear causal model.
The request supplies unique variable IDs, the actual unit of observation, sampling design,
measurement clock, units, assumptions and algorithm choices. An initial engineering design
can bound the number of variables, use one process and expose a resource budget. Such limits
are proposed workload choices, not measurements of pcalg’s maximum capability. Hitting
a limit must produce an incomplete or refused request rather than silently reducing the
conditioning-set search.
   Discovery may use a correlation matrix and sample size where those are sufficient for the
selected test. Effect calculation needs the original covariance scale, matching node coordinates
and a validated graph. If D = diag(c1 , . . . , cp ) changes variable units, covariance transforms
as Σnew = DΣDT and an effect from coordinate i to j transforms by cj /ci . A correlation
matrix alone does not retain the information needed to reconstruct monetary units. The
transformation in (18.6) should therefore be a routine semantic check at the boundary.
  Graph conversion needs its own type. In the documented pcalg ancestral-graph matrix,
entry (i, j) describes the endpoint at j: zero denotes absence, one a circle, two an arrowhead
and three a tail (pcalg contributors, 2026). Thus i → j is represented by the pair (2, 3) in
18.8. Reuse, porting and the next comparison                                                 169


entries (i, j) and (j, i). This rule cannot be reused indiscriminately for a binary DAG adjacency
matrix or a structural coefficient matrix. The initial PC/IDA service does not accept a PAG
merely because its entries form a square matrix. Named endpoints, graph class and algorithmic
conflicts travel separately.
   A useful pre-admission oracle includes an asymmetric named chain and a column permutation,
the collider X → M ← Y , the unresolved path X − M − Y , and the exact covariance and unit
examples above. The converter must preserve each object’s meaning. A deliberate transpose
must fail the direction check. Missing independence tests, singular inputs, invalid partial
graphs and resource exhaustion need explicit failure cases. Observations consisting of repeated
monthly rows for the same customer should receive an unsupported-sampling response on this
iid path, even when the matrix is numerically well formed.
   These are proposed adapter requirements. The exact algebraic examples have been repro-
duced, but an R environment, converter and package-level oracle run are distinct implementa-
tion evidence. Separating these claims makes it possible to recommend a concrete prototype
without treating a contract as an installed integration. Library, command-line and MCP
clients should consume the same typed results; a display layer must not orient an unresolved
edge or relabel a missing interval merely to simplify its presentation.


18.8     Reuse, porting and the next comparison
The reuse choice should follow the selected operation and deployment need. Using a package
in an optional environment preserves upstream algorithms but adds dependency, conversion
and upgrade costs. Porting moves those obligations into this project, including the burden of
reproducing statistical behavior. An apparent reduction in installation complexity can therefore
increase scientific maintenance. A small native reference implementation may be an excellent
oracle for a few graphs without being an adequate substitute for a general identification or
discovery library.
   License and dependency evidence belong to this choice at the exact source revision. The
inspected pcalg, bnlearn and BiDAG metadata declare GPL version 2 or later; mcmcabn
declares GPL version 3; BCDAG declares MIT with its license file (pcalg contributors, 2026;
Marco Scutari and contributors, 2026; Polina Suter and Jack Kuipers, 2026; Gilles Kratzer
and contributors, 2023; Federico Castelletti and Alessandro Mascaro, 2026). DoWhy’s source
license permits reuse with the specified notice, but that grant does not establish the rights or
compatibility of every dependency (PyWhy contributors, 2026b). Separating processes can
isolate versions; it does not itself settle distribution obligations.
   The inspected DoWhy dependency declarations include Python version constraints, NumPy
greater than 2, and several numerical and causal packages. They are constraints rather than
a resolved environment, and the displayed 0.0.0 is explicitly a dynamic-version placeholder
(PyWhy contributors, 2026c). The proposal selects a narrow identification path for further
prototyping and defers its executable admission until a resolved environment, dependency
review and semantic oracle are available. It does not infer performance or a support commitment
from repository activity.
   The same evidence structure applies to commercial comparisons. A documented feature
in a named edition can be compared with a proposed operation, but absence from a search
result cannot establish absence from the product. A meaningful trial would hold the target,
observation law, assumptions, failed-request denominator and uncertainty requirements fixed,
then compare scientific coverage, workflow effort and total cost. Public documentation can
support a proposal before a paid trial is justified; a claim about actual runtime behavior
170                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


requires the corresponding execution evidence.
   The next useful experiment is thus a matched test of a selected path, with its alternatives
and failure cases fixed in advance. For the funding example, one question is whether the
integration preserves the two distinct effect possibilities and their units. Another is whether a
specified intervention or justified background restriction resolves a decision-relevant ambiguity.
Neither requires an enterprise deployment merely to formulate and evaluate the prototype.
Each has a clear evidential limit, an inexpensive reference calculation and a direct connection
to the eventual banking decision.


18.9     From search records to a defensible coverage claim
A systematic comparison needs a rule for what one entry represents. Let P be the set of
canonical implementations, A the method areas and L the language or commercial access paths.
A source may support a relation (p, a, ℓ) ∈ P × A × L. This is a many-to-many relation. One
implementation can supply several methods; one method can have several implementations;
and a wrapper can expose an implementation in another language. Counting each relation as a
new package would overstate the number of independent alternatives. Collapsing all relations
to the package name would conceal unsupported methods and access paths. The survey
therefore needs both a canonical implementation index and an operation-specific comparison.
   The pcalg example illustrates this distinction without requiring a hypothetical new package.
Its PC discovery and IDA effect calculation belong to the same implementation family, but
their inputs and outputs differ. Reading the PC interface does not establish an IDA claim.
Similarly, the documented R interface does not establish that a proposed Python process
wrapper has preserved its graph semantics. The inspected manual supports the named native
operations; the wrapper requires additional evidence (pcalg contributors, 2026). The canonical
entry can share identity and license facts while keeping separate evidence for each operation.
  For each comparison, define the claim as a tuple

                                      c = (p, v, a, ℓ, d, q, o),

where v is a release or source revision, d the supported data regime, q the scientific request
and o the output meaning. A useful source record answers a specific question about this tuple.
A manual can describe an operation on complete iid continuous records without establishing
behavior on clustered monthly histories. A license can establish a permission subject to
conditions without establishing algorithmic correctness. An executed roundtrip can establish
endpoint preservation without establishing coverage of a confidence interval. These evidence
types are complementary; none should replace the others in a single undifferentiated confidence
score.
   The comparison can use five explicit evidence states: a discovered lead; an identified primary
source; a technically inspected claim; an executed behavioral reference; and a statistically
evaluated claim in a declared law. An entry moves between these states only for the relevant
claim tuple. Failure is retained separately: an inaccessible manual is an acquisition failure, an
unsupported input is an interface restriction, and an invalid effect calculation is a substantive
problem. Each implies a different next action. A search result identifying a package cannot
advance a numerical claim, and a successful trial cannot establish that an undocumented
edition shares the same feature.
  This structure also clarifies survey coverage. The fraction of predefined comparison cells
with a reviewed disposition measures completion of that declared plan. It does not estimate
the fraction of all software in the world that has been found. Ranked bibliographic results
18.10. A matched comparison includes eligible requests and justified refusal                  171


have unknown inclusion probabilities, aliases can occupy several results, and broad queries
return method papers without an implementation. Dividing ten inspected records by the
1,648 reported matches would therefore provide no defensible software recall estimate. The
bounded R comparison in this chapter reports its search route and five primary-inspected
paths, without attaching a census percentage.
   A practical extension procedure is to search exact package names and aliases, method names,
implementation languages and competing commercial descriptions; then inspect the primary
technical sources for the resulting candidates. Reference following adds implementations that
keyword choice may miss. Backward and forward search have different date constraints: a
later search service can locate an earlier work, but a post-cutoff technical revision must not
be presented as the earlier implementation. Conflicting manuals or source versions create a
comparison question that needs resolution at a specific version. A later edit cannot silently
repair what a preserved earlier inspection established.
   The stopping rule should be chosen before interpreting omissions. A bounded proposal
pass may inspect a fixed number of query pages and one reference generation, retain every
discovered identity, and defer unresolved leads. Those are resource limits on the search, not
absence findings about a market. For a consequential adoption choice, the stopping condition
is stricter: each proposed operation needs its technical source, deployment and rights path,
alternatives and a testable behavior contract. If an essential source is missing, that adoption
decision stays conditional while other comparisons continue. This makes the unknown part of
the landscape visible and gives the next search a reason tied to a decision.


18.10       A matched comparison includes eligible requests and
            justified refusal
The common contract makes it possible to define a fair comparison before measuring a package.
First choose a service regime: for example, Gaussian iid discovery and singleton linear effects,
with the same named variables, sampling unit, units and background restrictions for every
candidate. Then separate three case families. In the first, the target is identified and a
reference is available. In the second, several causal models remain observationally compatible
and an effect set is the reference. In the third, the request violates the service regime or lacks
necessary input. A correct response in the last two families can be an unresolved set or a typed
refusal. Forcing every case into a point-estimate error would reward unsupported answers and
penalize scientifically useful ambiguity.
  Let zi indicate that case i has a reference answer within the agreed service, and let rij
indicate that path j returned a valid answer. Eligible availability is
                                                 P
                                               i zi rij
                                          Aj = P        .
                                                 i zi

An unavailable estimate on an eligible case remains in this denominator. For cases outside the
service, separately record the fraction receiving an unjustified causal answer. An invocation
that completed successfully but changed the population, units or graph class belongs in the
latter error category when those changes make its answer unsupported. A library exception
and a justified scientific refusal are also different outcomes: the former can indicate a broken
supported path, whereas the latter can be the intended response to an unsupported request.
   For each successfully answered identified case, numerical error and interval quality have
their own references. A small error conditional on returning an answer does not establish good
service if difficult cases fail. Conversely, high availability does not establish valid inference.
172                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


Report the joint event of an available interval covering the target, its conditional coverage
when available, and width, alongside failures. For an effect-set case, compare the complete
required object: missing an admissible effect and unnecessarily adding impossible effects are
different defects. If a benchmark grants credit for preserving a convex hull, it must say so;
that does not test preservation of a disconnected set or multiplicity.
   An exact planning example shows why these distinctions can change a choice. Suppose a
generated comparison contains 100 requests, with 60 inside the shared service and 40 requiring
refusal under its declared scope. These counts are stipulated for illustration. Path A answers
54 eligible cases correctly, fails on six, gives eight unjustified answers and correctly refuses
32. Path B answers 48 eligible cases correctly, fails on twelve and correctly refuses all 40
ineligible cases. Eligible availability is 90% for A and 80% for B, while false acceptance among
ineligible requests is 20% and zero. Their valid-answer fractions among all requests are 54%
and 48%. No single completion rate contains all this information (Causal banking research
project, 2026ag).
   To connect the same example to a decision, let a valid answer have expected incremental
value v, an unjustified answer expected loss h, and the full operating costs for the 100 requests
be cA and cB . The assumed net values are

                           VA = 54v − 8h − cA ,       VB = 48v − cB .

With hypothetical currency values v = 100, cA = 400 and cB = 600, the two paths tie
at h = 100 with net value 4,200. A is preferred only below that harm threshold, under
this deliberately simple loss model. The counts, prices and values are project assumptions,
reproduced by exact arithmetic; they are neither vendor measurements nor observed bank
returns (Causal banking research project, 2026ag). The example makes a practical point:
extra answered requests have to be valued together with the consequences of answering an
unsupported question.
   Actual prototype comparisons should therefore retain individual case results, not merely
aggregates. The case identity carries the declared law and target; the result records the returned
object, failures and resource use. Paired comparisons use the same cases and distinguish a
numerical discrepancy from a different target. Tuning and adapter repairs use development
cases, while a later evaluation freezes the selected procedure. If a package changes the search
space or target to obtain a result, that becomes a different procedure to evaluate. These rules
allow a favorable or adverse finding to be traced to a concrete operation and make a new trial
useful when a source version or proposed wrapper changes.
   The same protocol informs reuse cost. The full cost includes acquisition and dependency work,
conversion, analyst interpretation, failed requests and future maintenance. A free download
can still require expensive scientific adaptation; an enterprise license can be worthwhile if
its documented service and measured workflow fit the request. Before paying for a trial, the
proposal can identify the unresolved comparison and calculate the decision threshold at which
its answer matters. The next expense then purchases information about a specific choice. The
present source survey supplies candidate paths and testable restrictions; the proposed matched
trial supplies the evidence needed to choose among them.
Chapter 19

Discovery across independent, latent,
temporal and experimental settings

19.1     Choose the observation experiment before the discovery
         engine
A bank may want a causal diagram for several quite different reasons. It may need to identify
an adjustment set for an offer, investigate whether a funding relationship survives a policy
change, or decide which experiment would resolve an ambiguity that matters financially. These
uses do not imply the same learning problem. A discovery engine can be useful while leaving
the effect unresolved; it can also orient more edges under assumptions that the bank has no
reason to accept. The proposal therefore treats discovery as a conditional inference about
a declared observation experiment, followed by a separate decision about what the inferred
object permits.
   Let V = (V1 , . . . , Vp ) denote the measured variables, G a causal graph and P their observa-
tional distribution. The observed data may be independent customer records, selected records
conditional on inclusion S = 1, trajectories Vit indexed by customer i and physical time t,
or observations from regimes e with different intervention targets. The symbol P must be
expanded accordingly. A pooled table need not represent independent observations from one
distribution. Independence across customers does not establish independence across their
months, and differences across regimes need not be interventions on the variables named by
an analyst.
   A discovery request should first state its admissible model family M, the observed law
or laws and the graph object it seeks. Under causal sufficiency and the relevant acyclicity,
Markov and faithfulness conditions, an observational conditional-independence procedure
can aim at a Markov equivalence class represented by a CPDAG. With hidden or selection
variables, the appropriate ancestral-graph representation and its guarantees change. Temporal
and interventional methods add further restrictions concerning lags, regimes, mechanisms and
sampling. The pcalg, Tetrad and causal-learn comparisons make these differences concrete at
their actual interfaces. (pcalg contributors, 2026; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; py-why/causal-learn,
2026; Colombo et al., 2012)
   There are then three separate outputs to consider. The first is an estimated structural
object, such as a CPDAG, PAG, fitted structural model or candidate DAG. The second is
the collection of causal answers compatible with that object and the declared assumptions.
The third is a statistical statement about the uncertainty of the complete procedure. An
estimated graph is not automatically a confidence set for graphs. A collection of effects

                                              173
174                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


computed from compatible DAGs is not automatically a confidence region. The inspected
pcalg IDA documentation, for example, describes a multiset of possible total effects under its
model assumptions. Keeping its multiplicities can be useful for checking the computation, but
counting repeated values does not establish probabilities on causal worlds. (pcalg contributors,
2026; pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024b)
  These distinctions give a practical order for the software comparison. First admit an
observation experiment and causal model family. Then compare methods that target the
same structural object. Inspect what the implemented method actually returns, including
unresolved marks, conflicts and failures. Finally connect that result to a stated banking action
and loss. The detailed language comparisons that follow supply the package evidence; the
present chapter explains how to use them together.


19.2     Independent observations: three ways to obtain direction
Constraint-based methods use conditional independences to remove adjacencies and orient
features shared by compatible graphs. Their empirical behavior depends on the independence
test, conditioning sets, missing-data treatment and orientation procedure. The test must
correspond to the observed variables and sampling law. A Fisher-Z partial-correlation test for
a Gaussian model, for example, is not a generic nonlinear conditional-independence oracle.
The inspected Tetrad implementation exposes missing-data, rank and degrees-of-freedom
choices that affect its returned decisions. Its PC path and its score-based FGES path therefore
need separate admission profiles even though they come from the same software family.
(cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a)
  Score-based search compares candidate parent sets or equivalence classes through a specified
model score. The relevant questions include the likelihood family, score equivalence, penalty,
search neighborhood, admissible constraints and stopping behavior. A finite optimum of a
numerical objective supplies no general causal guarantee. A local maximum may be a useful
candidate, but it should remain a candidate with its objective and search settings attached. The
R and native comparisons distinguish equivalence-class search from a selected representative
and distinguish a package wrapper from the numerical kernel it invokes. (pcalg contributors,
2026; Achille Nazaret and XGES contributors, 2026; cran/pcalg, 2024)
  Functional-model methods can extract direction from restrictions beyond conditional inde-
pendences. Linear non-Gaussian, additive-noise and differentiable structural-model approaches
should therefore be compared on their actual assumptions, not merely on whether each returns
a weighted matrix. A non-Gaussian independence argument cannot be inherited by a Gaussian
example simply because the same optimizer accepts its data. Likewise, a small acyclicity
penalty or thresholded coefficient matrix is a numerical diagnostic; the graph and the conditions
behind an intervention interpretation still need checking. The inspected LiNGAM, NOTEARS,
DAGMA and Causica paths offer different candidate computations and require different pro-
posed acceptance tests. (cdt15/lingam, 2026; xunzheng/notears, 2026; kevinsbello/dagma,
2026; microsoft/causica, 2026)
  The proposal does not select one of these families universally. A sufficient linear Gaussian
model with credible independent units gives a transparent starting point for constrained PC
and score-search comparisons. A credible non-Gaussian structural restriction may justify a
separate functional-model comparison. A concern about hidden risk changes the admissible
graph class before it changes the preferred implementation language. The analyst should be
able to inspect the reason for that change and the additional assumptions needed to reverse it.
19.3. A common observational law can support different actions                                  175


19.2.1    Faithfulness and the business target can fail in different ways

Consider an authored structural example with independent, centered, unit-variance Gaussian
disturbances U, V, W :

                   X = U,       M = X + V,         Y = (−1 + ε)X + M + W.

The variables are standardized indices; their labels do not assert a real bank mechanism.
Substitution gives Y = εX + V + W . Thus
                                       ∂E[Y | do(X = x)]
                 Cov(X, Y ) = ε,                         = (−1 + ε) + 1 = ε.
                                              ∂x
At ε = 0, X and Y are marginally independent even though the structural graph contains
a direct edge and a directed indirect path. A discovery conclusion that interprets every
independence as a graphical separation would lose this cancellation structure. The direct effect
is −1, the indirect effect is 1 and the total effect is zero. These are different targets even
though they arise from the same three equations. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
   The example also shows why graph error and decision error should both be reported.
Suppose that changing X by one unit has value USD 30 per unit of Y and costs USD 8. With
|ε| ≤ 1/20, its net value lies between USD −9.5 and USD −6.5. Declining this action is robust
within that stipulated family, even while the mechanism decomposition is unresolved. An
intervention on M would answer a different question and would require its own operational
interpretation and cost. More arrows are not necessarily worth acquiring for the original action.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
   Near cancellation is also relevant to finite discovery. When an empirical test has little
power against a small nonzero association, treating a nonrejection as a known absence can be
consequential for other targets. Changing the test threshold after observing the desired graph
does not repair that problem. The proposed result should retain the tests, separation sets,
search limits and unresolved features needed to explain the conclusion. Stability under column
order is one diagnostic, but it is not identification or calibration. The order-independent
literature explicitly separates stable skeleton estimation, collider decisions and later orientation
rules. (Colombo and Maathuis, 2014; py-why/causal-learn, 2026)


19.3      A common observational law can support different actions
The following three-variable example makes the bridge from graph discovery to decision explicit.
All variables are centered. Within each model the listed disturbances are independent Gaussian
variables with the stated variances:

                      F : X = UX ,      M = X + UM ,       Y = M + UY ,
                      R : Y = UY ,      M = 32 Y + UM ,     X = 21 M + UX ,
                      C : M = UM ,      X = 12 M + UX ,      Y = M + UY .

In the order (UX , UM , UY ) the variance vectors are respectively (1, 1, 1), (1/2, 2/3, 3) and
(1/2, 2, 1). Here F is the forward chain, R the reverse chain and C the common-parent
model. The noise labels are local to each model. In the coordinate order (X, M, Y ), all three
observational distributions have covariance
                                                      
                                             1 1 1
                                        Σ = 1 2 2 .
                                                 
                                             1 2 3
176                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


For example, in C, Var(X) = 14 (2) + 12 = 1, Cov(X, Y ) = 12 (2) = 1 and Var(Y ) = 2 + 1 = 3.
The other two factorizations give the same matrix. As centered Gaussian laws they are
therefore identical, rather than merely having the same least-squares fit. Their conditional
covariance of X and Y given M is 1 − (1)(2)/2 = 0. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
   The three graphs have the same chain skeleton and no collider. If this three-model family is
the stipulated scientific scope, observations alone leave all three possibilities. The effect of
changing X from zero to one on Y is one in F and zero in both R and C. The compatible
effect set is {0, 1}; a convex interval [0, 1] is a conservative enclosure, not the same exact
set. Selecting one representative DAG would turn an unresolved direction into a selected
action effect. Conversely, a verified ordering that truly rules out some directions is additional
information and should be recorded as such. Simultaneous quarterly summaries with convenient
names do not supply that ordering. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
   For a hypothetical offer, retain the stipulated USD 30 outcome scale and USD 8 action
cost. Net values are USD 22 in F and USD −8 in R and C. Different decision criteria can
consequently recommend different actions. The worst-case value of offering is −8, compared
with zero for declining, so a maximin rule declines. The largest regret from offering is 8,
while the largest regret from declining is 22, so a minimax-regret rule offers. If one stipulates
equal weights on the three models, expected net value is 22/3 − 8/3 − 8/3 = 2, and that
expected-value rule also offers. The equal weights are a scenario assumption, not a probability
distribution learned by a CPDAG procedure. A product should retain the distinction between
the compatible model set and the sponsor’s decision criterion. (Causal banking proposal,
2026bo)


19.4     Hidden variables and selection change the object being
         learned
Unmeasured borrower risk, market shocks and selection into a reviewed sample can invalidate
a causally sufficient graph interpretation. Introducing a hidden node in a diagram is not
enough: the learning procedure and the representation must preserve the relevant conditional-
independence and ancestral information. An ancestral graph can represent relationships
after marginalizing hidden variables. A partial ancestral graph records invariant endpoint
information across a class, with circles retaining unresolved marks. Its directed edge is not
generally a promise that an unconfounded regression coefficient equals a direct causal effect.
The inspected ancestral-graph definitions and the software comparisons distinguish these
meanings. (Zhang, 2008; pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024a)
   FCI and RFCI illustrate why even two outputs called PAGs need additional method identity.
The RFCI definition permits an adjacency with a weaker interpretation than the corresponding
FCI adjacency. Its graph can retain edges that a more extensive search removes, and can
correspond to more than one Markov equivalence class. The oracle soundness statement
assumes a faithful distribution and the required conditional-independence information; it
is not a finite-sample confidence claim. The faster procedure is therefore a substantive
information/computation alternative, not a lossless substitute whose edges can automatically
be read under the stronger definition. (Colombo et al., 2012)
  Selection is equally concrete. Let X and U be independent fair binary variables, let Y = U ,
and retain a record only when S = 1, where S = 1{X = U }. The four population configurations
each have probability 1/4, while the retained sample consists of (X, Y ) = (0, 0) and (1, 1)
with equal conditional probability. Its observed conditional contrast is one. Yet replacing the
equation for X leaves U and Y unchanged, so the population intervention contrast is zero.
19.5. Temporal discovery begins with a physical clock                                      177


These are exact properties of a generated law. They show why the inclusion event and target
population belong in the request. They do not claim that a latent-discovery routine can recover
the omitted population law from the selected table alone. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
   The practical candidate portfolio therefore keeps pcalg FCI/RFCI, corresponding Tetrad
and causal-learn paths, and selected native or other-language latent methods as distinct
comparisons. Source-specific endpoint conversions, conditioning bounds and failure semantics
remain relevant. A PC conflict represented by two arrowheads must not be silently relabeled
as a latent confounding conclusion. A latent mixture model or a supplied Bayesian network
with hidden states is also a different capability from learning an ancestral equivalence class.
The commercial and native latent comparisons develop those alternatives without treating all
hidden-node software as an FCI replacement. (py-why/causal-learn, 2026; pcalg contributors;
CRAN source mirror, 2024a; agrumery/aGrUM, 2026a; miicTeam/miic_R_package, 2026;
BayesFusion, LLC, 2024i; Muthen and Muthen, 2026b)


19.5      Temporal discovery begins with a physical clock
For a bank panel, write a candidate structural process as
                                                 L
                                                 X
                                Vit = B0 Vit +         Bℓ Vi,t−ℓ + Uit .
                                                 ℓ=1

The ordering convention here is target by source: entry (j, k) of Bℓ describes the effect
of coordinate k at lag ℓ in the equation for coordinate j. This is a proposed model, not
a description of all temporal packages. Its interpretation requires a physical time unit, a
definition of the contemporaneous interval, an admissible structure for B0 and a law for Uit .
If I − B0 is invertible, the reduced lag coefficient is (I − B0 )−1 Bℓ . Predicting the reduced
equation does not by itself identify the structural contemporaneous matrix.
  A customer boundary and a calendar gap matter before any conditional test. Joining
the final month of one customer to the first month of another creates a fictitious transition.
Treating a three-month gap as one ordinary lag changes the physical model. A recorded variable
can also be unavailable at the action time even if its event time is earlier. Neither column
order nor a lagged dataframe constructor certifies these conditions. The R, Python, Java
and C++ temporal comparisons trace their different window, subject, regime and state-label
contracts. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ak; cran/pcalg, 2024; agrumery/aGrUM, 2026b;
JBSants/sDBN, 2021)
   A small impulse calculation shows why the outcome horizon belongs beside the graph.
Consider a two-period response with a unit action at the first period, no second action and
persistence ρ = −1/2. In the stipulated linear process the two outcome changes are (1, −1/2).
The average change is 1/4, while the end-of-period change is −1/2. At USD 40 per outcome unit
and USD 3 action cost, their net values are respectively USD 7 and USD −23. Both calculations
are correct for their respective targets. An adapter that returns an average under an endpoint
label has reversed the decision without necessarily changing any estimated coefficient. These
values are authored illustrations, not evidence about actual negative persistence in banking.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
   The software options address different portions of this problem. Tigramite’s PCMCI-
related procedures distinguish temporal conditional-independence, contemporaneous and
latent-variable settings; context and regime extensions add their own declarations. The
inspected JPCMCIplus path treats specified context classes specially, and the inspected
regime method has a restricted data/mask contract. Those choices cannot be inferred from
178                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


one generic “time series” capability label. CausalAI, VARLiNGAM and DYNOTEARS
supply other comparisons under their stated model and input restrictions. Their results
must be evaluated against a common physical target before speed or prediction quality is
compared. (jakobrunge/tigramite contributors, 2026; salesforce/causalai contributors, 2025;
mckinsey/causalnex contributors, 2026; cdt15/lingam, 2026)
   Dynamic Bayesian network inference is a useful alternative when the structure is
supplied rather than discovered. The inspected aGrUM unrolling helper and Mocapy++
inference/parameter-learning paths illustrate that role. A supplied model can support
a transparent finite-state experiment even when no structure-learning claim is justified.
Conversely, a learned temporal graph need not provide calibrated effects under shared
calendar shocks or latent confounding. The product should expose the supported operation
and sampling boundary rather than merge forecasting, structural discovery and intervention
evaluation into one completion flag. (agrumery/aGrUM, 2026b; juliusHuelsmann/MocapyPP,
2019; JBSants/sDBN, 2021)


19.6     Interventions provide information only under a mecha-
         nism contract
Regimes are scientifically informative when their relation to the system is specified. Under
a perfect intervention on a target set I, the original mechanisms for variables in I are
replaced, while the stipulated mechanisms outside I remain unchanged. In the inspected
interventional-equivalence formulation, observations are independent across draws but need
not be identically distributed across known targets. A conservative target family leaves each
variable unmanipulated in at least one regime; an observational regime supplies that property.
This condition should not be confused with a claim that every such experimental design
identifies every graph direction. (Hauser and Bühlmann, 2012)
   The likelihood contribution of a variable’s original mechanism should not come from rows
on which that mechanism was replaced. This explains why regime-to-row maps and target
indices are part of the score, not incidental metadata. The inspected pcalg GIES path includes
R preprocessing, conversion to native indices, local-score configuration and a distinction
between an essential graph and a representative. The Python GIES and UTIGSP-related
comparisons likewise need their actual target, test and dependency contracts. Unknown targets
and soft interventions are separate methodological questions; the assumptions of one known-
target procedure cannot be silently transferred to them. (cran/pcalg, 2024; juangamella/gies
contributors, 2025; uhlerlab/causaldag contributors, 2022)


19.6.1    Which additional measurements resolve the three-model example

Return to the three observationally equivalent models F, R, C. Replace the equation for M by
the fixed value m and compare m = 1 with m = 0. The population mean changes in coordinate
order (X, M, Y ) are
                                         ∆X ∆M ∆Y
                                     F    0     1     1
                                     R 1/2      1     0
                                     C 1/2      1     1
For F , replacing M leaves X unchanged and changes Y by one. For R, it changes X through its
half-unit coefficient and leaves the root Y unchanged. For C, both children respond. Thus the
joint population contrast (∆X, ∆Y ) distinguishes all three fixed models, while observing ∆Y
19.7. A software portfolio organized by admissible questions                                 179


alone distinguishes R from {F, C} but does not separate the two different effects of intervening
on X. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
  This is a design insight rather than a finite-sample discovery result. An actual experiment
would observe noisy outcomes, would need sufficient precision to distinguish relevant contrasts,
and would have to justify that the intervention really replaces only the stipulated mechanism.
A marketing message that also changes expectations through an unmodeled path is not
automatically the intervention in the displayed table. The feasible action, its target set and
the measurements retained must be approved as scientific design inputs before the comparison
can be interpreted that way.
   The example also distinguishes effect information from graph orientation counts. Under
the equal model weights and payoffs specified above, current expected optimal value is USD 2
per decision. Perfect knowledge of the model would yield 22/3 dollars, because the offer
would be selected only in F . The ideal incremental value is therefore 16/3 dollars. If only the
population Y response to the intervention on M were revealed, the {F, C} group would have
equal conditional weights and expected offer value (22 − 8)/2 = 7 dollars. That group has
prior probability 2/3; the R group would decline. Expected optimal value would be 14/3, an
improvement of 8/3 dollars. The omitted X measurement can therefore matter to the decision
even though Y is the final outcome of interest. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bo)
   These are ideal population-information values under stipulated weights. They are not
trial budgets, package performance or bank ROI. Sampling noise, intervention cost, delayed
outcomes, operational constraints and model misspecification can lower the value of a proposed
experiment. Their role in the proposal is to identify a concrete question for a cheap generated
prototype: does the complete discovery and reporting path retain the regime and measurement
information needed to make the right conditional decision?


19.7      A software portfolio organized by admissible questions
The detailed survey supports a portfolio rather than a single discovery winner. For a first
causally sufficient independent-observation profile, pcalg, Tetrad and causal-learn supply
transparent constraint-based reference paths, with score-search candidates kept separate.
Their output contracts should preserve equivalence classes, settings and test failures. For a
latent profile, FCI/RFCI and the inspected native alternatives need their own graph semantics
and computational limits. For temporal observations, a chosen Tigramite or other temporal
path needs a physical clock and explicit sampling law. For known perfect interventions, a GIES
candidate needs accurate targets and retained unmanipulated mechanisms. These are proposed
scoped comparisons, not permission to enable every operation from a package name. (pcalg
contributors, 2026; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; py-why/causal-learn, 2026; pcalg contributors;
CRAN source mirror, 2024a; jakobrunge/tigramite contributors, 2026; cran/pcalg, 2024)
   There are also good reasons to choose a different role for a package. A classification network
can be a predictive baseline. A supplied dynamic model can be an exact or numerical reference.
A functional-model optimizer can generate a candidate under a declared structural family. A
commercial editor can contribute elicitation and model inspection while leaving identification
and calibration to a separate component. The latent commercial comparisons show why
latent-class estimation, parameter learning with missing values and discovery of an ancestral
equivalence class must remain distinct in a competitive capability matrix. (Waikato/weka-3.8,
2022a; agrumery/aGrUM, 2026b; juliusHuelsmann/MocapyPP, 2019; BayesFusion, LLC, 2024i;
Muthen and Muthen, 2026b)
  Direct adoption is most attractive when the existing method and its public interface
180                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


already preserve the required scientific object. A language bridge can retain an established
implementation while translating units, names, endpoint encodings and failures explicitly. A
port becomes a separate procedure to compare, including preprocessing, defaults, stopping
and numerical diagnostics. Source-only reference use is appropriate when rights, dependencies
or essential semantic behavior remain unresolved. Rejecting a proposed use should specify
the mismatch: for example, supplied-model inference does not satisfy a structure-discovery
request. This does not establish that the package is unsuitable for every other operation. The
source-specific reuse sections develop those decisions beyond this scientific portfolio.
   The next inexpensive comparison can use the exact generated mechanisms in this chapter
together with permitted public covariate and calendar structures. Each engine should receive
the same declared question when a matched-method comparison is intended. A deliberately
different method family should instead be labeled an alternative with its own assumptions.
Retain candidate graphs, equivalence marks, failed requests, conditional effects and decision
losses. Evaluate graph features and the chosen action separately. Include the cost of scientific
preparation and review, rather than reporting only optimizer time. No public financial table
is to be relabeled as intervention truth merely because its columns look appropriate. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026bn)
   The wider survey remains bounded by inspected originals and recorded omissions. Additional
versions, less common languages, unknown-target methods, dependent latent regimes and
some commercial capabilities still need source-specific work. A working numerical example
cannot close those search branches. Equally, an unavailable commercial manual need not
block a generated comparison of the known independent-observation or interventional profiles.
The proposal can advance each admissible question while keeping these limits visible. Its
central product requirement is that the path from observations through graph uncertainty to
the banking decision remain inspectable, with an explicit explanation when the supported
assumptions do not permit an answer. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bn)


19.8     Reusing gCastle without changing the meaning of a dis-
         covered graph
A bank comparing discovery tools needs to know what an output edge means before it can
decide whether a package belongs in the proposed platform. An adjacency matrix is insufficient:
the same two nonzero entries can represent an unresolved orientation, a directed cycle, or
a different graph convention. The earlier Python survey identifies gCastle as a source of
selected PC and gradient-based comparators. The reuse choice developed here retains those
method-specific references and proposes a bounded original-engine experiment. It does not
extend the choice to the entire catalog or treat a discovered graph as an identified intervention
effect. The primary evidence is the gcastle subproject of huawei-noah/trustworthyAI at
its 29 May 2026 revision, fd8a04f3b57a0f00930406257d5c30dcb91da0a5; the distribution is
named gcastle, while the import namespace is castle. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle
contributors, 2026)


19.8.1    Graph types and variable identity are part of the result

The inspected PC orientation routine documents a completed partially directed acyclic graph
(CPDAG). Under its encoding, Aij = 1, Aji = 0 represents i → j, while Aij = Aji = 1
represents a single unresolved edge i − j. The latter must neither be interpreted as two causal
arrows nor converted to a latent-confounding bidirected edge. A returned array also does not
certify that statistical assumptions or graph-class validity hold. The proposed result type
19.8. Reusing gCastle without changing the meaning of a discovered graph                        181


must therefore include the graph family, ordered variable identifiers, orientation convention,
restrictions and diagnostics alongside the matrix. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle
contributors, 2026)
  For an exact conversion reference, consider four illustrative variables: offer O, response R,
margin M and cost shock C. In the ordering (O, R, M, C) let
                                                        
                                         0       1   0   0
                                        1       0   1   0
                                      A=                 .                                 (19.1)
                                                         
                                        0       0   0   0
                                         0       0   1   0
This represents O − R → M ← C. Both choices of orientation for O − R produce acyclic
completions with the displayed collider; neither is selected by the unresolved pair alone. A
decoder that treats every nonzero entry as a directed edge instead reports the artificial cycle
O → R → O. Simultaneously permuting rows, columns and their labels to (M, O, C, R) must
preserve all named edges. This property is checked by the authored reference; it is not a report
of native package conformance. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026an)
   The distinction matters when a bank combines several algorithms or asks an agent to explain
the diagram. A common graph object may hold unresolved edges, but a downstream DAG-only
estimator must receive a justified completion, an effect set across admissible completions,
or an explicit unsupported response. It cannot silently select an orientation to satisfy an
API. The inspected Tensor constructor checks input container types and label lengths; it
does not explicitly validate unique labels, finite values or an exactly two-dimensional input.
Its documentation and finalization method also show that operations such as slicing replace
label metadata with numeric indices. The wrapper must bind immutable identifiers before
transformations and return the explicit map with every result. Otherwise a correctly shaped
matrix can be attached to the wrong banking variables. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle
contributors, 2026)

19.8.2    Support and knowledge restrictions require their own diagnostics

The PC skeleton implementation removes an edge when a conditional-independence test
returns p ≥ α. The original, stable and parallel variants are separate choices; the stable path
copies adjacency at each conditioning depth. A supplied base skeleton is modified in place,
including its diagonal, so a service must copy it if the original request is to remain reproducible.
Required and forbidden prior edges also need validation before construction: the inspected
methods append to separate lists without an explicit contradiction or directed cycle check.
The orientation helper applies required entries and then forbidden entries. These are concrete
conversion obligations, not evidence that arbitrary business knowledge has been translated
into a consistent causal model. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026)
  The default Fisher-z path computes a partial correlation using a matrix inverse  p     with a
pseudoinverse fallback, clips the correlation, and multiplies its transformation by n − |Z| − 3,
where n is the row count and Z the conditioning set. The inspected routine has no explicit guard
requiring a positive residual sample size. An integration contract must reject or separately
qualify constant variables, singular conditioning designs and insufficient residual support,
and must expose the chosen singularity policy. A pseudoinverse is a numerical rule; it does
not establish the reference distribution of the test in a degenerate population. Dependence
among repeated account histories also needs a statistical treatment beyond these source-level
conversions. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026)
   For categorical tests, the conditional power-divergence routine sums statistics and degrees
of freedom across observed strata, warns and skips strata raising ValueError, and sets p = 1
182                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


when the aggregate degrees of freedom are zero. At α = 0.05, that value satisfies the PC
edge-removal branch. This literal source implication is useful for designing a prototype test,
but is not a native experimental result. It does not mean that the data supplied informative
evidence about independence throughout a target population. A bank segmentation with
almost no within-stratum variation needs an insufficient-support result and a description
of the population restriction. The service should retain skipped strata, support counts and
test diagnostics, rather than reducing all such outcomes to a favorable independence verdict.
(Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026an)
   An LLM may propose a restriction such as “the later offer cannot cause an earlier balance.”
The proposal should retain the source of that temporal claim and check it against the
observation clock. It should reject contradictory restrictions before invoking the engine.
Natural-language confidence and the existence of a prior-knowledge API provide neither the
truth of the restriction nor the validity of the conditional-independence test. The same typed
restriction and refusal must survive a direct library request, a CLI request and an MCP call.


19.8.3     Numerical stopping and thresholding are different decisions

For the inspected linear NOTEARS routine, the fitted predictor is XW : row i, column j
of W gives the coefficient from variable i to variable j. The least-squares path centers the
columns of X; logistic and Poisson losses have separate formulas. The implemented acyclicity
expression is the polynomial
                                           "             d #
                                                   W ◦W
                                h(W ) = tr      I+               − d,                         (19.2)
                                                     d

where d is the number of variables and ◦ denotes elementwise multiplication. The binary
result uses the strict rule Bij = 1{|Wij | > τ }, with default τ = 0.3, and the weighted matrix is
retained separately. At equality the edge is absent, despite the docstring’s informal description
of dropping weights below the threshold. The inspected optimizer consumes sol.x without
testing sol.success; stopping may follow the residual tolerance, penalty bound or iteration
budget. The inspected routine does not separately validate final binary topology. None of these
observations establishes an actual failed fit. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle contributors,
2026)
  An exact witness explains the extra topology requirement without assuming what the
optimizer returns. For two variables with off-diagonal weights a = b = 1/100,

                                  a2 b2       1
                        h(W ) =         =           = 5 × 10−9 < 10−8 .                       (19.3)
                                   2      200000000
At the explicitly chosen threshold τ = 1/200, both edges survive and form a directed cycle. The
default threshold 0.3 removes both; this is not a counterexample to default native behavior. It
demonstrates that a positive residual tolerance alone is not a topological certificate for arbitrary
threshold choices. The proposed worker must return the weighted result, threshold, residual
and actual topology status separately. If the public engine surface does not expose required
solver diagnostics, the service must report that qualification is unavailable or use a separately
reviewed instrumented variant. A successful return cannot fill in missing convergence evidence.
(Causal banking proposal project, 2026an)
  Units are equally consequential. Consider the stipulated linear equation Y = (3/10)X + ϵ,
with Y measured in dollars. A strict threshold of 3/10 drops its coefficient. Expressing the
predictor as X ′ = X/100 changes the same equation to Y = 30X ′ + ϵ and retains the coefficient
19.8. Reusing gCastle without changing the meaning of a discovered graph                       183


at the same numerical threshold. This is a statement about representation, not a claim that
refitting a penalized objective is scale invariant. Units, scaling and penalties must be fixed
together in a discovery comparison. For an authored causal model in which the displayed
arrow is indeed structural, an intervention increment of 100 predictor units and an assumed
cost of USD 20 give
                              ∆V = 100(3/10) − 20 = USD 10.                             (19.4)
Mistakenly transposing the graph assigns zero response in this simple model and gives USD
−20. This makes the economic consequence of a convention error visible; it does not license
treating an arbitrary fitted weight as an identified effect. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026an)


19.8.4    The reuse choice and a proportionate public prototype

The selected source declares version 1.0.4, and its README dates that declaration to 7 March
2025. The May 2026 monorepo commit does not by itself show recent maintenance of each
gCastle method. Environment declarations also differ: the README states Python 3.6–3.9,
while setup states only Python at least 3.6. README and requirements include PyTorch;
setup’s installation dependencies omit it, even though the inspected validator imports torch
unconditionally. The algorithm surface selects PyTorch by default and imports several gradient
methods. A proposed lightweight PC or NOTEARS worker therefore needs an actual resolved
and tested environment; a numerical routine’s apparent simplicity does not establish a minimal
installation profile. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026)
   The original root license supplies Apache 2.0 terms, including grant and redistribution
conditions. Reuse must preserve applicable licenses, notices and modification disclosures, and
review the actual distribution and dependencies. This source-level finding is not a completed
rights inventory for all optional backends. The catalog’s static IID methods, event-sequence
TTPM and HPCI marked under development remain distinct evidence scopes. (Huawei Noah’s
Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026)
   The selected upstream test wrappers call a shared harness. Its PC and NOTEARS methods
iterate parameter combinations, catch exceptions and log them without assertions or rethrow
in those methods. That design is useful for exploring execution problems, but an ordinary
successful test-run status alone would not establish graph correctness or even that all attempted
fits succeeded. This inspection makes no claim about every upstream test, and no downloaded
test has been run here. The proposed public prototype needs explicit expected outputs and
failures for graph decoding, variable permutations, threshold equality, units, inconsistent priors,
insufficient support and topology, plus separately designed statistical comparisons on known
generated mechanisms. (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026an)
   The bounded recommendation is to retain selected PC and linear NOTEARS as references
and evaluate a pinned original Python worker if those comparators justify the prototype
cost. Direct whole-catalog adoption would conceal method-specific assumptions. Porting now
would add responsibility for CI degeneracy, orientation, stopping, thresholds and dependencies
without a measured platform advantage. A small independent exact reference remains valuable
for conversion checks, but is not a replacement implementation. The first prototype can use
public or generated observations; bank data is unnecessary to test these software contracts. It
should measure environment setup, serialization, support diagnostics, optimization, memory
and upgrade effort before any cost advantage is asserted. Statistical usefulness and executable
admission require their own evidence after that prototype, while the present proposal can
already state a reasoned reuse choice.
