19.9     Original NOTEARS: preserving the numerical meaning
         of a discovery reference
A bank investigating funding transmission needs to know whether a proposed edge represents
a signed structural coefficient, a measure of connectivity, or a decision made by thresholding.
The original xunzheng/notears implementation and the inspected gCastle implementation
are separate software candidates. Their source revisions, threshold operators and numerical
constraints must remain visible in a comparison. The original source is retained here as a
reference for a proposed public prototype; its output does not establish bank identification or
calibrated effect uncertainty. (Xun Zheng and NOTEARS contributors, 2026; Huawei Noah’s
Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026)
   The selected original revision precedes the 7 October 2026 cutoff. Its setup declares version
3.0, an alpha classifier and Apache License 2.0, with unpinned NumPy, SciPy and python-
igraph requirements. The nonlinear path also imports PyTorch, although it is absent from
the setup requirements; selected Gaussian-process simulation paths import scikit-learn. The
root license text and optimizer wrapper attribution are retained in the source audit. These
observations establish the selected source and declared terms; they do not establish a resolved
distribution or transitive dependency review. The README points to DAGrad for newer
differentiable methods. That pointer is a separate candidate lead, not evidence of a validated
successor or a measured performance advantage.(Xun Zheng and NOTEARS contributors,
2026)


19.9.1    A weighted matrix is a contract, not a complete causal result

For an n × d matrix X of observations, the original linear routine uses XW to predict columns.
Thus Wij is the coefficient associated with source variable i and target variable j. The least-
squares path centers a new data array; logistic and Poisson losses use different response models.
A wrapper must preserve the selected loss, variable order, units, centering and sampling
interpretation. The routine consumes returned optimizer parameters without exposing its
success status. Termination can follow an acyclicity tolerance, a penalty bound or the iteration
budget. Its public function returns a thresholded matrix. A graph assertion appears in the
standalone demonstration and CLI, but not as a final guard inside the linear function. An
adapter must check the returned support itself and retain a reason when it cannot certify a
DAG.(Xun Zheng and NOTEARS contributors, 2026)
  The original CLI reads a numerical CSV, invokes the routine, asserts acyclicity and saves a
matrix. It does not serialize variable identities, solver termination, the information clock or
uncertainty semantics. Those fields belong in the proposed common library, CLI and MCP
operation contract; they cannot be reconstructed from matrix dimensions after a restart.
Bounds on elapsed time, nonfinite results and retries must also contribute to the failure
denominator. A missing output cannot disappear from the comparison. (Xun Zheng and
NOTEARS contributors, 2026)


19.9.2    Threshold equality can change a banking decision

The original removes an entry when |Wij | < τ , retaining equality. The inspected gCastle
binary output keeps an entry when |Wij | > τ ; its weighted output remains a separate object.
Even on a supplied identical matrix, the two support conventions disagree at equality. This
is a conversion boundary, not an empirical ranking of fitted algorithms. (Xun Zheng and
NOTEARS contributors, 2026; Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026)
19.9. Original NOTEARS: preserving the numerical meaning of a discovery reference                   185


   Consider a stipulated linear causal relation between funding support and a monetary
response, with coefficient 3/10 dollars per intervention unit. Let the contemplated intervention
be 100 units and its cost USD 20. At a threshold τ = 3/10, retaining the supplied coefficient
gives
                              ∆V = 100(3/10) − 20 = 10 USD.                               (19.5)
If a consumer reconstructs a coefficient model from a binary support that removes this boundary
edge, its implied response is zero and its computed margin becomes USD −20. This deliberately
constructed discrepancy concerns using a support mask consistently; it does not say that either
package has estimated the coefficient or that graph selection justifies a causal effect. The
source-row convention, threshold strictness and distinction between weights and support must
accompany the proposed output. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026bw)
   Units add another constraint. With Z = XD−1 for a positive diagonal scaling matrix D,
the same supplied linear equations have WZ = DWX D−1 . For the three-variable chain with
W12 = 2, W23 = 3 and W13 = 1, the total path coefficient is 1+2·3 = 7. If D = diag(10, 1, 100),
the transformed coefficient is 7/10. The change is exactly the change in units. A fixed numerical
threshold need not preserve support under this transformation. This is an algebraic conversion
identity; refitting a penalized objective after scaling need not reproduce the transformed
original fit.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bw)

  The polynomial trace residual used in the selected gCastle linear routine is a different

19.9.4    Nonlinear adjacency cannot stand in for a signed response

The original MLP and Sobolev paths return nonnegative norms of first-layer weights. Such an
adjacency summarizes connectivity and cannot recover the sign or magnitude of an intervention
response. The MLP uses local output layers after the first layer; the model is mutated by
186                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


optimization. Its SciPy bridge moves through NumPy and the default PyTorch dtype, and the
trace-exponential helper crosses a NumPy/SciPy boundary. Device and dtype compatibility
are obligations for a future installed prototype, not inferred from the existence of a PyTorch
class.(Xun Zheng and NOTEARS contributors, 2026)
    Let s(x) = 1/(1 + e−x ) and consider two stipulated structural functions f+ (x) = 4s(2x) − 2
and f− (x) = −4s(2x) + 2. Both have first-layer norm 2 and baseline output zero. Since
s′ (0) = 1/4, their local derivatives at zero are respectively 2 and −2. With assumed value
USD 100 per outcome unit and local cost USD 20 per intervention-intensity unit, the net local
derivatives are USD 180 and USD −220. These are local derivatives in stipulated models, not
finite policy returns. Identical adjacency norms cannot choose between them. A downstream
intervention query needs the fitted structural functions, noise assumptions, unit conversion
and an identification argument. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026bw)


19.9.5    Reuse choice and the proposed public experiment

A pinned original linear worker is a reasonable prototype route because it preserves the
reference method while a wrapper owns input validation, source identity, diagnostics and graph
semantics. Direct adoption of the entire package is deferred: the declared environment is not
locked, nonlinear outputs have different meaning, and solver status is not exposed by the
inspected entrypoints. A port into another language is not selected for this proposal because
there is no demonstrated deployment or cost benefit to offset new numerical and maintenance
obligations. gCastle and DAGMA remain separately reviewed comparators; they do not inherit
one another’s qualification. (Xun Zheng and NOTEARS contributors, 2026; Huawei Noah’s
Ark Lab and gCastle contributors, 2026; Causal banking research project, 2026aq)
   The selected sources warn against treating bundled experiments as completed reproducibility
evidence. The two-variable experiment retains a legacy import and function name absent from
the selected package tree. The nonlinear CLI constructs a randomly initialized model without
setting an explicit seed; the utility seed function sets Python and NumPy state, while local
layer initialization uses PyTorch. These are static observations requiring native compatibility
and repeatability checks. No downloaded experiment was run for this review.(Xun Zheng and
NOTEARS contributors, 2026)
   A prospective comparison should first replay the conversion examples, then use predeclared
public or generated mechanisms under matched causal and sampling restrictions. It must count
refused, failed and incomplete fits; retain variable permutations, scale changes, near-threshold
cases and weak signals; and distinguish optimizer, topology and statistical diagnostics. The
scientific owner must justify model restrictions and effect queries; the maintainer must own the
environment and failure contract; the future operator must resolve actual distribution terms
and custody. Installation, full job cost, serialization, diagnostics and upgrade effort should be
measured before arguing for costly bank experiments. The reference decision supplies that
experimental rationale without declaring an implemented or qualified bank product.(Xun
Zheng and NOTEARS contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026bw)
Chapter 20

Identification, counterfactuals and
effect sets

A bank can know that an offer increases average completion and still be unable to say which
completed applications the offer caused. It can identify the effect of sending an encouragement
without identifying the effect of making every customer receive the service. It can also possess
a valid identifying formula whose numerical evaluation is too fragile to support the proposed
decision. These are different limits on what a causal product can say. The choice between
software components depends on preserving those limits through the calculation.
   This chapter develops that choice around a binary servicing action and a binary successful
outcome. The examples are project-authored probability laws, evaluated exactly, with a
stipulated value of USD 100 per success and USD 12 per action received. They are neither
estimates of bank behavior nor measurements of upstream software. Their role is to make
a proposal testable: an implementation can be asked to preserve the target, recover the
appropriate answer or set, and explain a refusal without confusing a scientific obstacle with a
computational one.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)


20.1     A causal question is relative to information and a model
         class
Let A ∈ {0, 1} denote receipt of a specified intervention, Y ∈ {0, 1} the outcome at a fixed
horizon, and C information measured before receipt. The intervention includes its delivery
version: sending a message and completing a counseling session are different actions even if
both are recorded as contact. Write Y (a) for the response under receipt a, P for the observable
population law and M for the admitted causal models. A common target is

                          θ(M ) = EM {Y (1) − Y (0)},       M ∈ M.

Consistency links the observed outcome to the potential response under the action actually
received. Assumptions about delivery versions, interference, information availability and the
horizon determine whether that link describes the banking question. A graph supplies restric-
tions on mechanisms and omitted causes; it does not certify these operational premises.(Pearl,
2009; Richardson and Robins, 2013)
  For a fixed observable law, define the compatible model class and effect set by

              M(P ) = {M ∈ M : PM = P },            Θ(P ) = {θ(M ) : M ∈ M(P )}.


                                              187
188                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


The target is point identified at P if this set is a singleton. A graphical identification theorem
usually establishes that a functional T works for every admitted compatible law, so that
θ(M ) = T (PM ) throughout its stated domain. Special numerical coincidences at one law are
weaker evidence. Conversely, finding two admissible models with the same P and different
θ disproves point identification for that law and class. Estimating P more accurately does
not distinguish such models. A smaller scientifically defensible class or additional intervention
information may do so.(Shpitser and Pearl, 2006; Pearl, 2009)
   The distinction matters when evaluating a proposal. A held-out likelihood score assesses
a distributional prediction. It cannot establish uniqueness of a causal answer across models
that share that distribution. An optimizer that returns one fitted model has selected one
element; it has not shown that all compatible elements agree. A prior can produce a posterior
over models, but its concentration has to be interpreted with the restrictions and prior that
supplied the missing information.
   There is another boundary: a formula may involve P (Y | A = a, C = c) where P (A = a |
C = c) = 0. The observed law then does not supply that conditional response. A smooth
extrapolating regression can return a value, but the value uses additional restrictions. The
proposal should declare whether it restricts the target population, changes the action, acquires
information or adopts an explicit extrapolation model. A numerical nonzero fitted propensity
does not create observed support.


20.2      Adjustment changes the comparison, not the action defi-
          nition
Suppose consistency, conditional exchangeability Y (a) ⊥ A | C and positive receipt probabilities
hold in the target population. Iterated expectation then gives
                                      X
                        E{Y (a)} =        E{Y (a) | C = c}P (C = c)
                                      c
                                      X
                                  =       E{Y | A = a, C = c}P (C = c).                     (20.1)
                                      c

The first equality standardizes to the chosen population; the second uses exchangeability and
consistency on the supported cells. If the sponsor wants the treated population, replacing
P (C = c) by P (C = c | A = 1) changes the target. It is not an innocuous estimation option.
   An exact generated law makes the cost of ignoring that distinction visible. Let P (C = 0) =
P (C = 1) = 1/2 and stipulate

              P (A = 1 | C) P (A = 0 | C) P (Y = 1 | A = 0, C) P (Y = 1 | A = 1, C)
      C=0          1/5           4/5             1/10                  1/5
      C=1          4/5           1/5              3/5                 7/10

This is a stipulated exchangeable-within-C construction, rather than evidence that a real
baseline variable removes every common cause. Both strata have a receipt effect of 1/10.
Standardization yields E{Y (0)} = 7/20 and E{Y (1)} = 9/20. The observed receipt groups
have different compositions:

                    P (C = 1 | A = 1) = 4/5,       P (C = 1 | A = 0) = 1/5.

Their outcome means are 3/5 and 1/5, producing a raw contrast of 2/5. All cells are positive,
so the problem is not an absent observation cell. Receipt selection overweights the high-success
stratum in the treated group.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)
20.3. Completeness must retain the procedure’s domain                                         189


   For universal receipt versus no receipt, define incremental expected net value V = 100θ − 12
in USD per eligible customer. The causal contrast implies V = −2; substituting the association
implies V = 28. A product that chooses an accurate predictive model but compares its
predictions over the wrong receipt groups can therefore recommend the opposite action. The
USD 30 discrepancy here is exact under the generated law, not a forecast of attainable financial
improvement.
   The relevant diagnostics follow the derivation. Check treatment versions and baseline
timing; inspect supported cells and overlap; state the standardization weights; and compare the
proposed graph against substantive common causes and selection. Balance after weighting can
diagnose a particular imbalance in measured variables. It does not demonstrate exchangeability
with respect to unmeasured variables.
  Adjustment can also answer the wrong causal question when it conditions on a mediator.
Consider the separate linear structural example

                            M = A + εM ,       Y = 2A + 3M + εY ,

with randomized A and independent zero-mean errors. Substitution gives E{Y | do(A = a)} =
5a up to the zero baseline intercept. The total mean effect of changing A from zero to one
is 5. Holding M fixed by intervention instead gives a controlled direct effect of 2. These are
continuous illustrative responses, not the binary success law above. Including the mediator has
changed the intervention comparison. In a bank, completion assistance and the downstream
information it elicits may both contribute to the total effect; controlling away the information
channel is appropriate only if that direct-effect question is actually intended.(Causal banking
proposal, 2026ca; Pearl, 2009)


20.3     Completeness must retain the procedure’s domain
Perković and colleagues characterize adjustment in DAGs, CPDAGs, MAGs and PAGs using
amenability, exclusion of a forbidden set and blocking of proper definite-status noncausal
paths. Their Theorem 5 gives an if-and-only-if result for adjustment; Theorem 7 supplies
the equivalent proper-back-door separation condition. The MAG and PAG treatment in this
source excludes selection bias. These conditions require the graph’s endpoint semantics, not
merely its adjacency matrix.(Perković et al., 2018)
   Completeness here means that the criterion characterizes the existence of adjustment sets
within the stated classes and definition. It does not mean that failure to find such a set proves
failure of every identification method. The same source explicitly distinguishes that claim
from identification by other functionals. An adapter should therefore report the attempted
route and its domain with its result. No valid adjustment set in the admitted graph leaves a
different question open from nonidentification in the admitted model class. A search that stops
after small candidate sets is weaker again, because it may not have exhausted the adjustment
problem.(Perković et al., 2018)
   For a supplied CPDAG or PAG, a successful adjustment set must be valid under the relevant
equivalence-class interpretation. Selecting one convenient orientation can create an answer
that does not survive the remaining graphs. It is reasonable to ask a domain expert for the
orientation of a particular edge, but that additional restriction must remain visible in the
scientific model. The resulting effect is conditional on it.
  This motivates three substantive alternatives when adjustment fails. One can seek a more
general identifying functional under the same information, retain a set of effects compatible with
the information, or change the information through an admissible experiment or measurement.
190                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


Choosing a convenient regression is a fourth computational action, but it only answers the
causal question if its added restrictions are justified. The banking consequence should be
assessed before choosing among these routes: a set lying entirely below the receipt cost
threshold can already rule out an action.


20.4      Joint and conditional intervention questions need different
          routes
For a semi-Markovian causal graph, ID identifies unconditional intervention distributions or
returns a graphical nonidentification witness in its formal domain. The district decomposition
and hedge criterion are scientific statements about that model class. They are not properties
of every exception a software implementation can throw. Shpitser and Pearl’s conditional
algorithm, IDC, first uses action–observation exchange where the graphical condition permits it.
After the maximal eligible exchange, it invokes the appropriate joint identification problem and
normalizes. Their Theorems 6–9 establish the conditional reduction, soundness, completeness
and do-calculus result for the stated queries.(Shpitser and Pearl, 2006)
  The order matters. In general it is valid to normalize an identified P (Y, Z | do(A = a)) to
obtain P (Y | do(A = a), Z = z) where the denominator is positive. It is invalid to infer that the
conditional target is nonidentified merely because this particular joint target is nonidentified.
The conditional may cancel a component that the joint requires. A component that supports
only joint-first normalization is consequently a conservative partial route to conditional queries.
   Consider the graph with A → Z → Y and A ↔ Z, with no hidden common cause involving
Y . Let U be a fair bit, E an independent Bernoulli(1/4) bit, and let the outcome be generated
from an independent random input with
                               P (Y = 1 | Z = z) = 1/5 + (3/5)z.
Two structural models compatible with the graph are
                                          A    Z
                                       M0 U U XOR E
                                       M1 U A XOR E
The graph permits an arrow with zero effect in a particular model; no faithfulness assumption
is imposed on this witness class. Observationally A = U , so both models give the same strictly
positive law for every triple (A, Z, Y ). Under do(A = a), however, U remains random in M0 ,
whereas Z responds to the set action in M1 .(Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)
  The interventional means are
                          E{Y | do(A = 0)} E{Y | do(A = 1)} contrast
                    M0          1/2              1/2           0
                    M1          7/20            13/20        3/10.
Thus the observational law cannot identify the marginal effect in this class; it also cannot
identify the joint law of (Y, Z) under the action. Yet throughout the stated graph class
the outcome mechanism has only the observed parent Z and independent exogenous input.
Consequently, on supported conditioning events,
              P (Y = 1 | do(A = a), Z = z) = P (Y = 1 | Z = z) = 1/5 + (3/5)z.
The equality follows from the graph’s mechanism restriction; agreement of the two numerical
witnesses alone would not prove identification. All relevant conditioning events are positive in
the displayed witnesses.(Shpitser and Pearl, 2006; Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)
20.5. A population response is not an individual counterfactual                               191


  In a servicing interpretation, Z could be a completed information step and Y a later
successful resolution. Knowing the outcome response among a specified post-action Z group
does not tell the bank how much an action changes the frequency of that group. The conditional
success probability therefore does not substitute for the total-value question. Conditioning on
the observed Z also does not identify the effect within the principal stratum that would attain
that Z under either action. That stratum is a different, cross-world target.


20.5      A population response is not an individual counterfactual
Single-world intervention graphs make counterfactual variables under one intervention explicit
and connect their factorization to the extended g-formula. Richardson and Robins distinguish
the FFRCISTG model from the stronger NPSEM with independent errors; single-world and
cross-world restrictions should not be silently interchanged. Pearl’s structural definition
computes an individual’s counterfactual by changing the intervention while retaining the
same exogenous state. That gives a counterfactual meaning within a fully specified structural
model. It does not show that observational or experimental marginals identify that structural
specification.(Richardson and Robins, 2013; Pearl, 2009)
  The distinction is exact even for a randomized action. Suppose the experiment identifies

                         P {Y (0) = 1} = 2/5,       P {Y (1) = 1} = 3/5.

Let t = P {Y (0) = 1, Y (1) = 1}. Every response-type law below has these same two marginals:

                         (Y (0), Y (1)) (0, 0) (0, 1)   (1, 0) (1, 1)
                               P          t    3/5 − t 2/5 − t   t.

Nonnegative cell masses require and suffice for 0 ≤ t ≤ 2/5. Randomizing A independently
of the response type then produces the same complete observable (A, Y ) law for every t.
Intermediate t values are feasible as well as the endpoints, so these are sharp ranges within
the stipulated response-type class.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)
   The average effect is always 1/5, but the fraction helped is 3/5 − t ∈ [1/5, 3/5] and the
fraction harmed is 2/5 − t ∈ [0, 2/5]. At t = 0, sixty percent benefit and forty percent are
harmed. At t = 2/5, twenty percent benefit and nobody is harmed. Both populations have
the same average effect and randomized outcome frequencies. Larger replications of the same
parallel-arm experiment do not select between these couplings.
  The retrospective attribution question is different again. Among treated successes, consis-
tency and randomization imply

                                                     P {Y (0) = 0, Y (1) = 1}
                    P {Y (0) = 0 | A = 1, Y = 1} =
                                                          P {Y (1) = 1}
                                                     3/5 − t
                                                   =         ∈ [1/3, 1].
                                                       3/5

One can therefore identify a positive average effect and still be unable to assign a unique
probability that a treated success was caused by the treatment. An explanation screen that
labels a particular completion as caused by an offer would need additional information and
assumptions.
   Assuming monotonic response, Y (1) ≥ Y (0) for every customer, eliminates the harmful
response type, forcing t = 2/5 here. It implies a benefit fraction 1/5 and attribution probability
1/3. This is a meaningful substantive restriction: assistance must never prevent a success that
192                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


would otherwise occur. Delays, confusion or competing actions can make it implausible in a
bank. The positive average experiment result neither proves nor requires this restriction.
  Expected net value under universal receipt is nevertheless 100(1/5) − 12 = 8 USD in every
coupling, under the stipulated linear reward and uniform receipt cost. A sponsor concerned
only with that average reward can compare receipt with no receipt without resolving t. A
sponsor imposing a bound on the fraction harmed cannot. The unresolved individual quantity
becomes economically material through the actual loss function or constraint, rather than by
declaring every nonidentified quantity equally blocking.


20.6     Encouragement, receipt and the population are separate
         targets
Suppose Z is a randomized encouragement, D receipt of assistance and Y the outcome.
Let D(z) be receipt under encouragement z. With stable treatment definitions, assignment
independence, exclusion of a direct encouragement effect, relevance and monotonicity D(1) ≥
D(0), the Wald ratio identifies the mean receipt effect among compliers. This is the LATE
interpretation developed by Angrist, Imbens and Rubin, rather than a general population
ATE statement.(Angrist et al., 1996)
   The distinction follows algebraically. Exclusion lets us write Y (z, d) = Y (d). For binary
receipt,
                    Y {D(1)} − Y {D(0)} = {Y (1) − Y (0)}{D(1) − D(0)}.
Monotonicity makes the second factor one for compliers and zero for never-takers and always-
takers. Averaging and using random assignment gives

              E(Y | Z = 1) − E(Y | Z = 0)
                                          = E{Y (1) − Y (0) | D(1) > D(0)}.
              E(D | Z = 1) − E(D | Z = 0)

Both the nonzero denominator and the change from receipt to encouragement are part of the ar-
gument. A large fitted first stage does not verify exclusion or assignment independence.(Angrist
et al., 1996)
  Consider the authored law with principal strata and observable response means

                     stratum   P   D(0) D(1) E{Y (0)} E{Y (1)}
                       never  3/10  0    0     1/5    unknown
                     complier 2/5   0    1     3/10     1/2
                      always 3/10   1    1   unknown    2/5.

Encouragement is an independent fair bit. Within each stratum we can construct binary
potential responses with the stated means; product couplings provide one explicit construction.
The receipt means under Z = 0, 1 are 3/10, 7/10; the outcome means are 3/10, 19/50. The first
stage is 2/5, the outcome intention-to-treat effect is 2/25, and LATE is 1/5.(Causal banking
proposal, 2026ca)
  What remains unknown is not remedied by calling LATE the effect for an average customer.
Let n = E{Y (1) | never} and b = E{Y (0) | always}. Each may range from zero to one without
changing any observable (Z, D, Y ) probability. The population receipt effect is
                                 3
                          θpop = 10 (n − 15 ) + 25 ( 12 − 10
                                                          3      3 2
                                                             ) + 10 ( 5 − b)
                                 7    3
                               = 50 + 10 (n − b) ∈ [−4/25, 11/25].
20.7. Instrument diagnostics do not supply the missing assumptions                            193


Both endpoints and every intermediate value are attainable. The calculation gives sharp
bounds for this particular observed law under the declared binary IV class, not a claim that
this simple expression is the general IV bounds algorithm.
   Universal receipt versus no receipt has net value in [−28, 32] USD per person. Receipt for a
complier has mean incremental net value 8 USD, but a bank cannot generally identify each
person’s principal stratum from the observed assignment and receipt. It cannot implement
treating only compliers merely because their average effect is identified.(Angrist et al., 1996;
Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)
   Changing the feasible action to universal encouragement gives a different, implementable
comparison. Only the 2/5 compliers change receipt; with the stipulated success value and
receipt cost, incremental net value is

                               100(2/25) − 12(2/5) = 16/5 USD.

A direct encouragement cost of USD 2 reduces this to 6/5. Thus a proposal can support the
encouragement action under its assumptions while refusing to claim that universal receipt is
beneficial. The difference is substantive, not merely a choice between two estimation libraries.


20.7     Instrument diagnostics do not supply the missing assump-
         tions
The IV analysis suggests concrete review questions. Was the encouragement randomized at
a customer or cluster level? Did a message alter outcomes through attention even when no
assistance was received? Could some customers avoid assistance because of the encouragement,
violating monotonicity? Are nonreceipt and receipt defined consistently across encouragement
groups? These questions determine the target model before selecting a Wald, two-stage or
structural estimator.
   Observed constraints may reject parts of an IV model; a fit that satisfies them does not
certify every unobserved restriction. Likewise a numerical first-stage diagnostic assesses a
feature of the observable encouragement law. It cannot establish the population effect among
never-takers under receipt, or among always-takers under nonreceipt. The construction above
holds the entire observed law fixed while changing those two responses, so no diagnostic based
solely on that law can identify them.(Angrist et al., 1996; Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)
   Numerical and inferential weakness also need distinct treatment. With a fixed positive
first-stage denominator d, perturbing the outcome intention-to-treat numerator by δ changes
the ratio by δ/d. A numerator perturbation of 1/1000 changes the ratio by 1/400 at d = 2/5
and by 1/20 at d = 1/50. At USD 100 per success these are USD 1/4 and USD 5 per
receipt. This exact algebra explains why small denominators demand precision. It is not a
weak-instrument confidence procedure: a random denominator and its dependence on the
numerator require an inferential argument of their own.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ca)
   A conditional population extrapolation is possible only with added information or restrictions.
A new experiment that can change receipt in previously unchanged groups supplies a different
information route. A structural effect-homogeneity assumption supplies a different model route.
Repeatedly estimating the same LATE with greater precision supplies neither. The proposal
should compare feasibility, scientific credibility and cost of these routes before promising that
a larger historical sample will settle the population question.

20.8      Effect sets can already guide a decision
Return to the first generated law, but now suppose the analyst receives only (A, Y ) and
assumes consistency, with no exchangeability or instrumental restriction. Its observed cell
probabilities are
                                         Y =0 Y =1
                                  A=0      2/5    1/10
                                  A=1      1/5    3/10.
The treated successes reveal a mass 3/10 with Y (1) = 1. Among untreated customers, a total
mass 1/2, the treated potential response is missing. Hence E{Y (1)} ∈ [3/10, 4/5]. Similarly,
E{Y (0)} ∈ [1/10, 3/5]. The target ATE therefore lies in
                                          [−3/10, 7/10].
For the lower endpoint, give every untreated customer a missing treated response of zero
and every treated customer a missing untreated response of one. Reverse those choices for
the upper endpoint. Both completions satisfy consistency and preserve every observed cell;
mixtures attain the intermediate values. Exact enumeration of the sixteen cellwise extreme
completions verifies the construction. The limits are sharp for this law and model class.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026ca)
   The point answer 1/10 obtained with the baseline and exchangeability assumptions lies
inside this set, but the set does not select it. The two analyses answer questions under
different information and restrictions. More rows from the unadjusted observational table
reduce sampling error around that table; they do not impose exchangeability. Recovering a
useful baseline is potentially valuable only if the scientific assignment argument justifies how it
changes the compatible class.
   With linear reward, mapping the effect set through V = 100θ − 12 gives [−42, 58] USD. For
a risk-neutral expected-value decision, a point probability distribution over compatible models
would produce a mean value, but no such distribution is supplied by the bounds. Selecting
their midpoint adds an arbitrary decision rule. Under a maximin criterion, no receipt has
value zero and universal receipt has worst value −42; no receipt is preferred in this two-action
problem.
   Under minimax regret the calculation differs. Relative to the best of receipt and no receipt
in each compatible world, receipt’s worst regret is 42, whereas no receipt’s worst regret is 58.
If only these deterministic actions are admissible, minimax regret prefers receipt. Allowing
a randomized receipt fraction r, with no interference and proportional costs, equalizes the
endpoint regrets at
                               42r = 58(1 − r),      r = 29/50.
The common regret is 609/25 USD. This is a derived decision illustration, not an ethical recom-
mendation to randomize a banking service. Operational, equity and capacity constraints may
exclude that action. It shows why a causal product must obtain the sponsor’s decision criterion
rather than turn an ambiguous effect into an unexplained binary recommendation.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026by)

law. They are not confidence intervals from sampled data. If a separate justified procedure

   Identification does not by itself control numerical evaluation. Suppose an identified con-

   For the product proposal, this distinction creates different remedies. A true zero denominator
requires revisiting the target or support assumptions. An uncertified small positive denominator

20.10       Choose software by the scientific route it preserves
The detailed software comparisons distinguish graphical adjustment, general intervention
identification, estimation and supplied structural-model simulation. The synthesis here uses
three inspected routes to show how a product should choose between them; it is not a claim
that these exhaust available identification or counterfactual software.
196                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


   DAGitty’s inspected adjustment routines reason about a supplied graph and query. Their
useful role is to expose admissible adjustment choices with the graph’s endpoint meaning
intact. They do not learn the graph’s scientific truth from a bank table. The inspected
source leaves some full MAG/PAG validation work as a TODO, and graph conversion can
discard endpoint information. A proposed integration should therefore validate the admitted
graph class and preserve the original graph alongside any computational projection. It should
reject an unsupported projection before interpreting an adjustment result.(jtextor/dagitty
contributors, 2024a; jtextor/dagitty, 2026)
   The inspected y0 high-level API dispatches unconditional queries to ID and conditioned
queries to IDC. Its default handling turns a particular Unidentifiable exception into None;
strict handling retains that exception. This makes the exact exception type and query
construction scientifically relevant. A generic missing return should not erase whether a hedge
was obtained, the input was invalid, an algorithm was unsupported or an unexpected exception
occurred.(y0 contributors, 2026a,d,e)
   The earlier source trace also identifies narrower concerns. A conditional branch of the
inspected query expression convenience property does not construct interventions in the same
way as the unconditional branch, although separately stored query fields remain available.
Graph operations can lose an isolated conditioning node: in the test question with A → Y and
an isolated Z, this may make computation unavailable even though the stipulated positive
law identifies P (Y | do(A), Z). These are static source findings, not new installed runtime
observations or proofs of mathematical nonidentification. A suitable integration uses explicit
query fields, checks node preservation and admits a joint-first conditional fallback only with
its incompleteness clearly stated.(y0 contributors, 2026a,c,b,k,h,i)
   The inspected DoWhy model code distinguishes its IDIdentifier route from its AutoIdentifier
route; choosing an identification method is not equivalent to choosing an estimator. Its
inspected model call also assigns a local proceed_when_unidentifiable value without passing
that local at the examined call. The proposal should test the effective option propagation
for the pinned route and preserve an identification result separately from later estimation.
Repeated refutation exercises on an estimate cannot establish assumptions that the underlying
observation law does not identify.(PyWhy contributors, 2026a)
   For these components, adopting a narrow documented route behind a scientific interface
is preferable to copying an entire package into a new engine without a parity argument. A
direct port changes the maintenance and verification obligation: graph surgery, conditional
reduction, expression semantics and failure witnesses all need matched cases. The existing
source-specific rights and environment reviews remain necessary inputs. The present evidence
supports a prototype comparison, not a declaration that one stack has been qualified for every
graph or banking regime.


20.11      A bounded prototype can resolve implementation choices
The six exact law families supply complementary tests for a proposed public/generated
prototype. The adjustment family checks population weighting and the distinction between
total and controlled direct effects. The extended bow family checks conditional identification
without an identified joint. The coupling family checks refusal to turn identified experimental
marginals into identified personal attribution. The encouragement family checks LATE, the
observable assignment law and the population effect bounds. The consistency family checks
sharp extreme completions. The rare-event family checks whether an otherwise valid formula
survives numerical evaluation. Each family has its own expected scientific answer; agreement
on one does not replace the others.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ca,by,bz)
20.12. The complete observable table constrains an instrument analysis                             197


   Compare components only on a declared shared domain. An adjustment-only route should
be assessed on adjustment queries; its refusal of a nonadjustment query should not count as a
false identification. For supported ID/IDC routes, retain the graph, intervention and condition
sets, positivity domain, formula or witness, and exact expected result. For a supplied structural-
model simulator, retain the additional mechanisms and exogenous coupling; agreement with
one selected model must not be scored as identifying the whole observational class.
  A meaningful result distinguishes at least a point functional, a supported effect set, a valid
nonidentification witness, an unsupported scientific route, invalid input or support, numerical
unavailability, and an execution failure. These distinctions guide action. Extra assumptions
can shrink a scientific set; a fuller algorithm may support an unimplemented route; a software
repair may restore a valid answer; additional observations may reduce sampling uncertainty.
Confusing them would direct the bank toward the wrong investment.
   The initial public prototype can use generated mechanisms with known responses and
permissible public covariates to make the information structure realistic. Such covariates do
not reveal unobserved potential responses. Before broader comparisons, the proposal needs
a fixed domain, version and rights decision for each candidate, matched output semantics
and a separate registered finite-sample study wherever statistical performance is claimed.
Exact identities and deterministic error envelopes are a necessary reference, not that study’s
outcome.(Causal banking proposal, 2026bz)
   Several limits have a known next step without a known positive answer. Additional primary-
source review can expand software coverage, but uninspected candidates cannot yet receive
an adoption decision. Generated comparisons can reveal whether the adapters preserve the
mathematical distinction, but cannot establish a bank’s assignment truth. Domain work and
later intervention evidence can assess plausible instruments, delivery versions, interference and
harm restrictions. Independent review, accepted loss thresholds, actual precision requirements
and real costs are later inputs. The proposal can specify those questions and the evidence that
would answer them while proceeding with the implementation comparisons whose requirements
are already concrete.


20.12       The complete observable table constrains an instrument
            analysis
The instrument example above leaves a practical question unanswered. When the bank doubts a
premise, which conclusions survive, and what additional information would narrow the answer?
A Wald ratio alone cannot answer this. It discards restrictions in the joint receipt–outcome
distribution, while an assumption change alters the compatible population. We develop the full
binary problem before making either change. Every probability in the following construction
is authored; the sensitivity budgets express hypothetical scientific judgments rather than facts
recovered from bank records. (Causal banking proposal, 2026cb)

Thus the receipt first stage is d = 2/5 and the outcome intention-to-treat contrast is τZ = 2/25.
Their ratio is 1/5. These two contrasts are summaries of eight cells, rather than a substitute
for them.


20.13      Sharp population bounds with monotone receipt
Monotonicity, D(1) ≥ D(0) for every customer, removes the four defier response types. Let
N, C, A denote never-receivers, compliers and always-receivers. Their masses are determined
by the receipt means:

                          πN = 3/10,        πC = 2/5,            πA = 3/10.

Under Z = 1, D = 0 the observed group consists only of never-receivers; its success mass
is 3/50. Under Z = 0, D = 1 it consists only of always-receivers; its success mass is 3/25.
Subtracting those contributions from the other two success cells gives

                     E{Y (0) | stratum} E{Y (1) | stratum}
                N           1/5                 n
                                                                           0 ≤ n, b ≤ 1.
                C          3/10                1/2
                A             b                2/5

Here n and b are conditional means. Below, when principal-stratum masses vary, we will use
different symbols for unconditional success masses. The distinction prevents multiplication by
a stratum weight twice.
  The complier effect is 1/2 − 3/10 = 1/5, as the LATE argument predicts under independence,
exclusion, relevance and monotonicity.(Angrist et al., 1996) The population receipt effect instead
20.14. A bounded departure from monotonicity                                                  199


is
                                  3

The table supplies neither the outcome of giving receipt to never-receivers nor the outcome of
withholding it from always-receivers. These are missing counterfactual responses, even with
infinite observational precision and perfect randomization of encouragement.
  It remains to prove attainability rather than merely bound a formula. Within a stratum of
mass m > 0, let s0 , s1 be its success masses under receipt zero and one, each in [0, m]. One
admissible coupling is

                                   a0 (y0 )a1 (y1 )
                 ps (y0 , y1 ) =                    ,   aj (1) = sj ,   aj (0) = m − sj .   (20.4)

Its four nonnegative cells sum to m and have the required two margins. Zero-mass strata

construct a witness; it is not imposed on every model in the bounded class. Other couplings
are allowed.
   Choose (n, b) = (0, 1) for the lower endpoint and (1, 0) for the upper endpoint, and apply
(20.4) in each of N, C, A. Substituting the resulting twelve possibly nonzero type masses into
(20.2) reproduces every cell of the displayed table. Convex mixtures of the two type laws
reproduce that same table and attain every intermediate population effect. Equation (20.3) is
consequently a sharp range for this class. At the stipulated USD 100 per success and USD 12
per receipt, universal receipt has incremental net range [−28, 32] USD per eligible customer. A
positive complier effect therefore does not settle this population-wide decision.(Causal banking
