20.14      A bounded departure from monotonicity
Suppose some customers may refuse the service because the encouragement was sent. Retain
randomization and exclusion, but stipulate

                              f = P {D(0) = 1, D(1) = 0} ∈ [0, 1/10].

The observed first stage identifies πC − f = 2/5, rather than πC itself. Consequently

                             πN = πA = 3/10 − f,              πC = 2/5 + f.

The 1/10 budget is an assumed substantive restriction. Neither the observed first stage nor an
absence of obvious complaints verifies it. The admitted complier population now varies across
compatible models; it should not be described as a fixed set of known customers.
  Let hj = P (defier, Y (j) = 1) be a defier success mass. Subtracting principal-stratum
contributions from all four observed success cells gives

                            P (stratum, Y (0) = 1) P (stratum, Y (1) = 1)
                      N           3/50 − h0                 uN
                       C          3/25 + h0               1/5 + h1
                     defier          h0                      h1
                       A             uA                  3/25 − h1
200                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


where the two unobserved masses satisfy 0 ≤ uN , uA ≤ 3/10 − f . Nonnegativity and the
stratum sizes imply, for the declared range of f ,

                            0 ≤ h0 ≤ min(f, 3/50),           0 ≤ h1 ≤ f.                       (20.5)

There are no further constraints on these margins for this example. For instance, the never-
receiver Y (0) mass is at most its stratum mass since 3/50 ≤ 3/10 − f , and the always-receiver
Y (1) mass is nonnegative since h1 ≤ 1/10 < 3/25. The complier success masses are below
2/5 + f throughout. Applying (20.4) separately to all four strata then proves sufficiency. It
also reproduces the failure cells, since the receipt totals and success cells agree.
  The complier target becomes

                                                     2/25 + h1 − h0
                                θC (f, h0 , h1 ) =                  .                          (20.6)
                                                        2/5 + f

For fixed f it is increasing in h1 and decreasing in h0 . Its smallest feasible numerator uses
h1 = 0 and h0 = min(f, 3/50). On 0 ≤ f ≤ 3/50 the lower ratio is (2/25 − f )/(2/5 + f ), with
strictly negative derivative. On 3/50 ≤ f ≤ 1/10 it is (1/50)/(2/5 + f ), again decreasing. The
maximum uses h0 = 0, h1 = f and (2/25 + f )/(2/5 + f ), whose derivative is positive. Both
extrema occur at f = 1/10, yielding

                      θC ∈ [1/25, 9/25] ,        100θC − 12 ∈ [−8, 24] USD.                    (20.7)

The lower witness has (h0 , h1 ) = (3/50, 0); the upper has (h0 , h1 ) = (0, 1/10). Their complier
mass is the same, 1/2. Product couplings give complete nonnegative response-type laws at
both endpoints; mixtures preserve the table and this denominator, attaining every intermediate
complier effect.
  Keeping only d and τZ would give a weaker answer. The contrast identity under exclusion is

                                  τZ = (2/5 + f )θC − f θdefier .

Allowing any defier mean effect in [−1, 1] gives the outer range [−1/25, 9/25] for the same
budget. Its negative lower endpoint would require f = 1/10 and h0 = 1/10, which violates the
observed-cell restriction h0 ≤ 3/50. Thus fitting a Wald decomposition is insufficient to certify
full-law compatibility. The complete table rules out that negative effect, while still leaving the
USD 12 receipt decision unresolved.
  The population effect has a different response to this relaxation:
                                     7
                                 θ = 50 + h1 − h0 + uN − uA .

For any admitted f , its lower bound is −4/25 + f − min(f, 3/50) ≥ −4/25 and its upper bound
is 11/25 − f + h1 − h0 ≤ 11/25. The monotone endpoint laws remain admitted at f = 0, so
the sharp population range stays [−4/25, 11/25]. The larger model class widens uncertainty
for the complier target without widening this population range. Sensitivity is a property of a
specified target and information class, rather than a single discount applied to every reported
effect.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cb)


20.15      Exclusion sensitivity needs a different response model
A bank message may affect confidence or repayment even when the customer does not receive
the proposed counseling. Exclusion then fails. The notation Y (d) hides that pathway; use
20.16. A feasible encouragement decision and the next experiment                              201


Y (z, d) instead. In this section restore monotone receipt and retain randomized encouragement,
but allow direct encouragement effects. Define

            θC0 = E{Y (0, 1) − Y (0, 0) | C},     Γ = E{Y (1, D(1)) − Y (0, D(1))}.

The first target changes receipt while holding encouragement at zero, among the receipt
compliers. The second averages a direct encouragement contrast while fixing each customer’s
receipt to its Z = 1 value. It averages over all principal strata. A budget on Γ is therefore not
automatically the same as a bound on each individual’s direct effect.
  Add and subtract Y (0, D(1)) inside the randomized contrast:

                            τZ = E{Y (1, D(1)) − Y (0, D(0))}
                                = Γ + E{Y (0, D(1)) − Y (0, D(0))}
                                = Γ + dθC0 .                                                (20.8)

The last equality uses monotonicity to make the receipt-changing group precisely the compliers.
It does not require exclusion. If the scientific judgment is |Γ| ≤ g, the implication is

                                     τZ − g τZ + g
                                                      
                               θC0 ∈       ,       ∩ [−1, 1].                               (20.9)
                                        d      d
This is an outer sensitivity envelope. The derivation uses a necessary contrast equation; it
does not prove that every point can satisfy all eight observed cells in the enlarged Y (z, d)
model. Solving that larger response-type feasibility problem would be required before calling
the envelope sharp.
  For the authored table, the implications are

                 g   θC0 outer envelope 100θC0 − 12 outer envelope, USD
                1/50     [3/20, 1/4]                 [3, 13]
                1/25    [1/10, 3/10]                [−2, 18]

Under the smaller budget every compatible receipt effect would exceed the stipulated cost
threshold. Under the larger budget this necessary envelope cannot settle the decision. It also
does not prove that both signs of net value are attainable in the complete response model. The
budgets are economically consequential assumptions: doubling a permitted direct contribution
changes what this calculation can recommend. Neither excellent predictive fit nor a small
standard error on the Wald ratio validates those budgets.


20.16      A feasible encouragement decision and the next experi-
           ment
There is an action whose value uses less causal structure. Suppose the bank can randomize
the encouragement, value every success at USD 100, pay USD 12 for every receipt, and
pay an additional USD 2 when encouragement is sent. Its incremental expected net from
encouragement one versus zero is

   100{E(Y | Z = 1) − E(Y | Z = 0)} − 12{E(D | Z = 1) − E(D | Z = 0)} − 2 = 56 USD.

Randomization and consistency for these well-defined assignment policies identify the two mean
contrasts. This calculation remains valid in the presence of direct encouragement effects or
defiers; it does not divide by the receipt first stage. It concerns offering encouragement, rather
202                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


than assigning receipt to unknown compliers. Its positive value in this exact law is compatible
with the unresolved population receipt range and the sensitive complier comparison.
   The information needs now follow from the particular uncertainty. Recording receipt
and outcome jointly preserves the full-cell restrictions that sharpened the defier calculation.
Randomizing encouragement more precisely estimates those cells but does not observe both
receipt responses for the same person. To narrow population receipt bounds, an ethically
feasible study would need information on responses currently missing in the never- and always-
receiver strata, or defensible additional restrictions. A design that varies message content
separately from service availability could address the direct pathway, but only if its delivery
and exclusion claims are justified for the new target. Repeating the same encouragement
experiment cannot by itself certify its own exclusion restriction.
   These exact-law results also do not supply sampling confidence intervals. With estimated
cell probabilities, the equality-constrained feasible set may be empty because of sampling
noise even when the population law is compatible. A proposed inferential extension could
form a justified joint confidence region for the entire conditional table, then optimize over
both that region and admissible response laws. If the region contains the true table and the
assumptions hold, the optimized set contains its compatible effects. Establishing the region’s
coverage requires the actual assignment, clustering and missingness law. Optimizing over eight
unrelated point estimates, or treating a solver’s feasibility tolerance as statistical uncertainty,
does not establish that guarantee.
   For a small prototype, the full response-type map offers a concrete oracle: check all
cells, distinguish an empty compatible class from a wide effect set, retain the positive ratio
denominator, and return feasible extremal laws with their bounds. The authored reference
evaluates thirty-six piecewise-domain vertices and separately reconstructs every observable
cell by principal-stratum mixing. Analytic derivatives establish that the ratio extrema occur
among those vertices. This verifies the finite construction and its attainable ranges; it is a
proposed comparison standard for a future implementation and a basis for choosing a useful
public or generated experiment.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cb)


20.17      Commercial mediation software and the meaning of a
           channel
A credit team may know that a servicing offer improves repayment while still not knowing
whether the improvement travels through customer understanding, available liquidity or a
change in staff behavior. That distinction matters when the proposed investment changes only
one channel. An effect attributed to a mediator is not automatically the effect of a feasible
intervention on that mediator. Commercial mediation software supplies developed estimation
and reporting workflows, but the comparison must begin with the intervention, counterfactual
target and observation clock.
  The selected Stata manuals and Mplus chapter document concrete capabilities. The
StataNow two-mediator manual is a separate product feature from the one-mediator command.
The selected Mplus chapter has March 2017 PDF metadata and supports a historical technical
profile; it does not establish current feature absence or exact licensed entitlement. Sources
acquired after the literature cutoff cannot, through an internal date alone, authenticate their
exact bytes on that cutoff date. The available comparison therefore supports scoped design
choices while retaining unresolved versions and commercial alternatives.(StataCorp, 2026t,s;
Muthen and Muthen, 2017)
20.17. Commercial mediation software and the meaning of a channel                            203


20.17.1    Four nested means and two valid decompositions

Let A ∈ {0, 1} indicate an offer, M (a) the mediator that would follow offer a, and Y (a, m) the
outcome under offer a and mediator setting m. For example, M might describe a measured
comprehension score and Y a net recovery amount over a fixed subsequent horizon. The
intervention on a score needs its own operational interpretation: administering a quiz, improving
understanding and changing a recorded answer are distinct actions. Define

                             µab = E{Y (a, M (b))},     a, b ∈ {0, 1}.                   (20.10)

The means with a = ̸ b combine an outcome under one offer with a mediator under another.
Observing the offer, mediator and outcome on many customers does not directly reveal these
nested outcomes.
  Using labels that state which component is held fixed, the additive total effect has two
decompositions:

                             µ11 − µ00 = (µ10 − µ00 ) + (µ11 − µ10 ),
                                       = (µ11 − µ01 ) + (µ01 − µ00 ).                    (20.11)

The first pairs a pure natural direct effect with a total natural indirect effect. The second
pairs a total natural direct effect with a pure natural indirect effect. Each identity follows
by adding and subtracting its intermediate mean. Mixing the direct term from one line with
the indirect term from the other generally fails to recover the total. Stata’s one-mediator
manual documents these alternatives and includes treatment–mediator interaction by default.
Its supported model combinations also matter: a logit outcome cannot be combined with the
listed linear or exponential-mean mediator model in this interface.(StataCorp, 2026t)
  Under the manual’s stated identification assumptions, a nested mean is represented by
averaging an outcome regression under A = a over the mediator distribution under A = b and
the baseline population:
                 ZZ
         µab =        E(Y | A = a, M = m, X = x) dF (m | A = b, X = x) dF (x).           (20.12)

Here X contains permitted pretreatment covariates. The assumptions include treatment and
mediator ignorability, appropriate support and the absence of a treatment-induced mediator–
outcome confounder for this standard formulation. Regression software can calculate the
integral under its models; it cannot infer those scientific conditions from a converged fit.
Stata’s introductory workflow explicitly places question, decomposition and assumptions before
estimation and interpretation.(StataCorp, 2026t,r)


20.17.2    Interaction changes the channel attribution

An authored continuous example makes the labels consequential. Suppose

                                  M (a) = 2 + 3a + U,
                               Y (a, m) = 5 + 4a + 2m + am + V,                          (20.13)

where U and V have mean zero and are independent under the stipulated causal model. The
four means are µ00 = 9, µ10 = 15, µ01 = 15 and µ11 = 24. The total effect is 15. Its pure-
direct/total-indirect decomposition is 6 + 9, while its total-direct/pure-indirect decomposition
is 9 + 6. Multiplying the mediator coefficient 3 by the untreated outcome slope 2 gives 6; that
is the pure indirect component, not the total indirect component 9. Dropping the interaction
204                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


changes the scientific model instead of merely simplifying a report.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ar)
  The controlled direct effect at a fixed mediator value m is
                                E{Y (1, m) − Y (0, m)} = 4 + m.                             (20.14)
It is 4, 6 or 9 at m = 0, 2, 5, respectively. A bank specifying an operational mediator setting
should request that setting explicitly. If Y is measured in dollars and the full offer costs an
incremental USD 10 per customer, the stipulated total-effect margin is USD 5. Charging
that cost against one natural component would answer a different question unless a feasible
component intervention and its cost were separately justified. This example supplies a finite
analytical reference, not a commercial engine benchmark or a measured banking return.
   The inspected Mplus chapter distinguishes conventional coefficient-product effects from
counterfactually defined effects. Its conventional branch allows multiple mediators and out-
comes; categorical mediator or outcome paths can use underlying latent response variables. A
product on a latent-response scale is not thereby a difference in repayment probabilities. The
chapter separately documents total natural indirect, pure natural direct and total effects for a
single mediator, with IND and MOD syntax and explicit controlled-effect mediator values. The
appropriate branch and scale should be part of the requested target, not inferred from the
word indirect in an output table.(Muthen and Muthen, 2017)
   The selected MODEL INDIRECT command uses delta-method standard errors by default, with
documented bootstrap and interval alternatives. The chapter excludes this command for
TYPE=RANDOM, the CONSTRAINT option of the VARIABLE command and TYPE=EFA. Those are
statements about this inspected command and version profile. They do not prove that every
other Mplus modeling route lacks a desired effect. Likewise, a documented interval option
does not establish its calibration under shared bank or calendar shocks.

20.17.3     Randomizing an offer does not identify every channel

Consider two authored worlds with independent fair binary variables A and U . The offer A is
randomized, and the mediator is
                                     M (a) = a ⊕ U,                                  (20.15)
where ⊕ denotes exclusive OR. In the direct world, Y (a, m) = a. In the mediated world,
Y (a, m) = m ⊕ U . In both worlds the observed mediator is equally likely to be zero or one
within each offer arm, and the observed outcome is exactly Y = A. The complete observed
joint distribution of (A, M, Y ) is identical. There is observed mediator overlap, and the offer’s
total effect is 1 in both worlds.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ar)
   The nested means differ. In the direct world, Y (1, M (0)) = 1, so the pure natural direct effect
is 1 and the total natural indirect effect is 0. In the mediated world, Y (1, M (0)) = U ⊕ U = 0,
so those components are 0 and 1. The latter world contains unobserved mediator–outcome
confounding through U , violating the assumptions needed for the ordinary mediation integral.
The construction therefore does not contradict software operating under qualified assumptions.
It shows why randomizing A and checking the observed support of M are insufficient to justify
the natural-effect decomposition.
  Even the mediated world’s natural indirect effect of 1 is not the effect of setting everyone’s
mediator to one rather than zero. Under either constant mediator setting, m ⊕ U has mean
1/2, so this controlled mediator-only contrast is zero. At an assumed USD 100 per beneficial
outcome and USD 20 intervention cost, offering A has a stipulated incremental margin of
USD 80, whereas the mediator-only contrast gives USD −20. These refer to different proposed
actions. A channel attribution cannot be sold as the return from changing a dashboard score.
20.17. Commercial mediation software and the meaning of a channel                             205


   An interventional mediator target would instead specify a feasible distributional intervention,
for example a draw from a declared reference mediator distribution conditional on eligible
baseline information. That differs from retaining each person’s own unobserved M (b) inside a
nested counterfactual. Its identification conditions and practical implementation need their own
derivation, especially when treatment changes mediator–outcome confounders. The selected
documents do not establish that every such target is available. The proposal should preserve
that unresolved target rather than relabel a natural effect as interventional.


20.17.4     Population averaging, signs and multiple mediators

Stata’s controlled-effect postestimation averages counterfactual predictions over covariates
by default; its atmeans option evaluates them at covariate means. In the inspected Mplus
moderation syntax, continuous control variables evaluated at zero can instead be evaluated at
their means by centering them. A comparison must therefore specify the target population
and the reference point before interpreting numerical disagreement.(StataCorp, 2026u; Muthen
and Muthen, 2017)
  For an exact nonlinear illustration, let X be equally likely to equal −1 or 1 and stipulate
                                                                                  
                                                                              x2
                P {Y = 1 | do(A = a), do(M = m), X = x} = 15 + a         1
                                                                         10 + 10       .   (20.16)

The mediator has no role in this law. The population-average controlled effect is 1/5, while
evaluation at the mean covariate value E(X) = 0 gives 1/10. At an assumed value of USD
100 and cost of USD 15, those two targets imply margins of USD 5 and USD −5. The
example isolates the averaging operation and does not claim that a selected vendor’s available
parametric family reproduces this law automatically.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ar)
   The proportion mediated is also a derived quantity whose denominator and signs must
remain visible. Under the simple stipulated law M (a) = a, Y (a, m) = 3a − 2m, the total
effect is 1, the pure direct component is 3 and the total indirect component is −2. The ratio
of indirect to total is −2, not a share between zero and one. With total effect approaching
zero, such a ratio can become arbitrarily unstable even when the components are meaningful.
Stata’s postestimation manual normally refuses conflicting effect signs and permits an explicit
force override. That override authorizes a computation, not an interpretation as a percentage
of benefit.(StataCorp, 2026u; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ar)
   The separate StataNow two-mediator manual documents parallel and causally ordered
sequential mediators. Its selected syntax supports continuous outcome and mediator variables,
with binary or continuous treatment. Interaction switches distinguish treatment–mediator,
mediator–mediator and first-mediator/treatment interactions in the second mediator equation.
The stated model requires no unmeasured confounding across the treatment, mediator and
outcome system, with independent zero-mean errors in the displayed parametric model. More
path components create more scientific assumptions and more possible decompositions; they
do not reveal a causal ordering from the data alone.(StataCorp, 2026s)
   For a bank, understanding and liquidity may be parallel channels, understanding may
change liquidity management, or an unobserved hardship shock may affect both. The business
description does not select among these graphs. An assistant can draft alternatives, retrieve
source-supported mechanisms and request the relevant measurement clocks. It should retain
unresolved arrows and refuse to convert an expert’s preferred story into verified mediator
independence. The resulting graph and estimand should be reviewed before a vendor command
is constructed.
206                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


20.17.5    Sensitivity parameters do not define probability intervals

The absence of a measured confounder can motivate a sensitivity analysis, but the parameter
and its interpretation must be explicit. Consider the authored structural model
                             M = aA + u,       Y = cA + bM + e,                          (20.17)
where A is independent of the errors, Var(u) > 0 and ρ = Corr(u, e). After removing the linear
contribution of A, the coefficient of M in an ordinary outcome regression satisfies
                                            Cov(u, e)     σe
                               bOLS = b +             =b+ρ .                             (20.18)
                                             Var(u)       σu
This follows directly by projecting bu + e onto u. Under the stated additive structural
intervention, the indirect effect is ab. If a = 2, bOLS = 3 and the structural scale ratio
σe /σu = 2 is assumed, varying ρ over [−1/2, 1/2] produces effects from 4 to 8, with value 6 at
ρ = 0. At an assumed USD 100 per effect unit and USD 500 cost for a separately justified
intervention, the corresponding arithmetic margins range from USD −100 to USD 300.(Causal
banking proposal project, 2026ar)
   This is a set of declared sensitivity scenarios, not a 95% confidence interval or a posterior
credible interval. The structural scale ratio is an assumption; it must not be substituted
silently by the residual standard deviation from a regression that has already projected part of
e onto u. Sampling uncertainty within each scenario is a separate calculation. The scenarios
have not been shown to preserve every feature of a common observed law, so the displayed
range is not claimed as a sharp identified set either.
   Negative controls can provide additional falsification information only under their own
exclusion and confounding structure. A variable called a negative control by an assistant or
a user does not gain those properties by declaration. The present commercial comparison
has not completed a product-specific census of negative-control or sensitivity procedures. No
failure to locate an option in these selected manuals establishes that a vendor or an extension
lacks it. Completing that survey requires matched originals and explicit parameter mappings,
not broader interpretation of an existing bootstrap confidence interval.

20.17.6    Commercial alternatives and a proposed integration contract

Stata supplies a documented parametric causal-mediation workflow, including potential-
outcome means, interaction, controlled effects, multiple output scales and several variance
options. Mplus supplies a different modeling environment with latent-variable and conventional
path capabilities alongside a counterfactual branch. These are substantive strengths against
a proposal whose current executable evidence in this comparison consists of exact authored
references. There is no measured accuracy, speed or integration advantage over either vendor.
A future adapter should preserve their documented scientific conventions before comparing
matched targets.
  Three further candidate families need matched technical originals: SAS/STAT
CAUSALMED, IBM/AMOS and PROCESS. The available evidence does not sup-
port a complete edition-specific comparison for these families. The PROCESS author
website establishes an independent extension for SPSS, SAS and R, and explains that its
documentation is version sensitive. This extension must not be counted as a native IBM
or SAS capability without verifying the concrete host, version, terms and implementation.
The author’s book page is a discovery source; the book and linked scholarly papers are
not represented as inspected originals here. Missing technical evidence leaves a comparison
unresolved and does not establish product absence.(Andrew F. Hayes, 2026)
20.18. R mediation and sensitivity contracts                                                   207


   The proposed library request should identify treatment and mediator intervention values,
the permitted information clock, graph assumptions, natural/controlled/interventional/path-
specific target, effect scale, interaction structure and target population. It should also identify
resampling units, covariance options, sensitivity parameters and source versions. Outputs
should preserve the four nested means when available, compatible decompositions, denomi-
nator/sign diagnostics, uncertainty type and unsupported status. A client must not receive
a sensitivity range under a confidence-interval field or a latent-response coefficient product
under a repayment-risk field.
   CLI and MCP transport should preserve that same typed object, including failure and
refusal. An agent can compare requested semantics with a vendor command and expose
mismatches. It cannot supply missing ignorability, historical entitlement or calibration through
a fluent explanation. The first public prototype experiments should check the exact interaction
means, the two indistinguishable observed worlds, covariate averaging, conflicting effect signs
and sensitivity arithmetic. Subsequent licensed numerical comparisons should measure fitting,
conversion, review time and failed requests under frozen versions and generated mechanisms.
Bank data and measured commercial value become relevant after those public experiments
establish why a prototype deserves a costly institutional trial.


20.18      R mediation and sensitivity: preserving the intervention,
           the mixture and the unit of uncertainty
A bank considering a servicing intervention needs to distinguish an improvement caused by the
intervention from an improvement transmitted through a particular mechanism. Let A denote
an offer of restructuring, M subsequent payment engagement, and Y loss over a fixed horizon.
Baseline information W precedes the offer. A later liquidity assessment Z may be changed
by the offer and affect both engagement and loss. The question therefore requires a declared
intervention on engagement, a target population, an information clock and assumptions linking
the intervention to observed data. R packages supply useful approaches, but their targets
and uncertainty calculations are not interchangeable. This comparison extends the preceding
mediation, medflex, sensemakr and EValue discussions with CMAverse, medoutcon, regmedint,
causalsens, tipr and BayesGmed. Inspected sources and authored examples support conditional
reuse decisions; they do not establish native qualification. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026ge)

20.18.1     A causal target before a software method

Write Ya,m for the outcome after setting offer and mediator to (a, m), and Ma for the mediator
under offer a. Two complementary natural decompositions on an additive scale are
                 TE = E(Y1,M1 − Y0,M0 ) = PNDE + TNIE = TNDE + PNIE .
Here PNDE = E(Y1,M0 − Y0,M0 ) and TNIE = E(Y1,M1 − Y1,M0 ); the other pair interchanges
the reference treatment. The controlled direct effect E(Y1,m − Y0,m ) instead holds engagement
at the same specified level. It need not equal a natural effect, and subtracting it from TE
need not yield a natural indirect effect. The selected BayesGmed primary text develops
these distinctions under consistency, positivity, no unmeasured confounding and a cross-world
condition. Randomizing the offer alone does not supply every mediation assumption; a posterior
interval does not establish them either. (Yimer et al., 2022)
  When offer-induced liquidity confounds engagement and loss, an alternative draws a new
mediator Gb from the distribution of Mb conditional on W , independently of the realized
208                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


intermediate confounder under the declared intervention law. Let µ(a, z, m, w) = E(Y | A =
a, Z = z, M = m, W = w). The selected Díaz and colleagues paper identifies the corresponding
mean as                 Z
               θ(a, b) = µ(a, z, m, w) p(z | a, w) p(m | b, w) p(w) d(z, m, w).
The identifying requirements include the relevant treatment and mediator exchangeabilities,
consistency and conditional support. This intervention differs from drawing a mediator
conditional on the intermediate confounder as well as baseline information. Changing the
conditioning set changes the pathways assigned to direct and indirect components. (Diaz et al.,
2019)
   Define IDE = θ(1, 0) − θ(0, 0) and IIE = θ(1, 1) − θ(1, 0). Their sum is the total contrast
under the randomized mediator intervention, which need not equal the ordinary treatment
effect. An authored example takes P (Z = 1 | A = 0) = 1/4, P (Z = 1 | A = 1) = 1/2,
P (M = 1 | Z) = 1/4 + Z/2, and Y = ZM . The ordinary treatment effect is 3/16, whereas
IDE is 3/32 and IIE is 1/16, summing to 5/32. All mediator probabilities are positive. The
difference arises from changing dependence in the intervention, not estimation error. The
product must label the two totals explicitly. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)

20.18.2     CMAverse: a broad interface with a consequential draw contract

CMAverse version 0.1.0 documents regression, weighting, inverse odds weighting, natural-
effect, marginal structural and g-formula approaches. Its interface restricts methods when
post-treatment confounders are supplied and changes natural-effect labels to randomized
analogues. Parameter-function and imputation estimators have different applicability; the
documented logistic and Cox parameter-function cases require a rare outcome. Its sensitivity
interface distinguishes unmeasured confounding from measurement error and documents a
single-variable measurement-error scope. These are useful capabilities to compare, provided
the proposed product exposes method, scale and restrictions. (BS1125/CMAverse contributors,
2025)
  The selected g-formula delegate simulates intermediate confounders from exposure and
baseline covariates, then mediators using those variables and the simulated intermediate values.
In its post-treatment-confounder branch, it subsequently permutes each mediator column
across eligible rows. Outcome prediction retains the row’s baseline and intermediate variables.
Global permutation requires a different justification from a draw conditional on that row’s
baseline information; separate column permutations also require justification when a joint
mediator law is intended. (BS1125/CMAverse contributors, 2025)
   For W ∼ Bernoulli(1/2), mediator probabilities 1/4 and 3/4 in the two baseline groups, and
outcome regression W M , the baseline-conditioned stochastic mean is 3/8. A global shuffle
pairs each row with the marginal mediator probability 1/2, yielding 1/4 in expectation. For
two identical balanced binary mediators, E(M1 M2 ) = 1/2; independently permuting columns
yields 1/4 in expectation. These exact witnesses specify invariants for an adapter. They are
neither native failure frequencies nor a rejection of g-computation. The route is to declare
the conditional joint draw, reconcile the delegate, and retain an explicitly different target or a
separately reviewed repair. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)
   Conditional R invocation is preferable to porting a large method collection before resolving
its target. Requests should carry mediator order, conditioning set, treatment contrast, scale,
simulation budget and random state. Resampling units must match the data law: a row boot-
strap is not automatically branch-cluster or shared-calendar inference. Imputation, simulation
integration and bootstrap variation require separate accounting. The GPL declaration and
full dependency inventory also accompany contemplated redistribution; this source review
20.18. R mediation and sensitivity contracts                                                  209


does not clear every artifact. (BS1125/CMAverse contributors, 2025; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ge)

20.18.3     medoutcon: efficient scores and the sampling contract

medoutcon targets natural and interventional effects using one-step and targeted minimum loss
estimators. The primary paper assumes independent, identically distributed observations, de-
rives an efficient influence function, and requires positivity and products of nuisance-estimation
errors vanishing faster than n−1/2 . Cross-fitting relaxes empirical-process restrictions; it does
not prove those rates for arbitrary learners or remove hidden confounding and dependence.
A low-dimensional intermediate-confounder representation avoids directly estimating a high-
dimensional mediator density, a useful advantage for multivariate engagement measurements
within the stated conditions. (Diaz et al., 2019)
   The selected source switches to natural effects when Z is explicitly absent, constructs binary
contrasts, and rescales outcomes by their observed range. A constant outcome makes that
scaling denominator zero. Contrasts subtract influence scores before variance calculation;
propensity clipping must be recorded as a numerical choice rather than proof of population
support. For two-phase mediator measurement, the source uses
                                         R         R
                                                       
                                 Dobs = D −          − 1 mD ,
                                         π         π
where R indicates observation, π is inclusion probability and mD predicts the complete-data
influence quantity. With D = 3, mD = 1 and π = 1/2, the observed and missing cases give 5
and 1, averaging to 3 under that law. False inclusion probabilities do not become valid through
calculation. (nhejazi/medoutcon contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)
   In the inspected one-step survey-weight branch the estimate is a weighted mean, but the
variance expression multiplies the influence quantity by supplied weights without corresponding
normalization. For scores (1, 3), changing weights from (1, 1) to (2, 2) retains estimate 2 while
changing the displayed variance-of-the-mean expression from 1 to 4. Requiring normalized
weights may reconcile that convention; an adapter accepting arbitrary relative weights cannot
silently assume it. The proportion-mediated option is a log-ratio functional, distinct from
an additive proportion. These observations motivate qualification tests rather than establish
installed-estimator coverage. (nhejazi/medoutcon contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ge)
   The conditional adoption route retains the R learner stack until independent fixtures
establish target, score, contrast, rescaling and uncertainty parity. Public trials should include
weak support, constants, weight rescaling, incomplete mediator measurement and deliberately
invalid dependent sampling. A port needs a deployment benefit sufficient to maintain these
scientific invariants. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)

20.18.4     regmedint: interactions and conditional effects

regmedint supplies a more explicit parametric alternative, carrying baseline evaluation values,
mediator and outcome model families, treatment–mediator interaction and effect modification.
Its case-control branch fits the mediator in controls and states a rare-outcome requirement.
The selected delta calculation constructs separate regression covariance blocks. Evaluation at
mean covariates is not automatically population standardization, and a block covariance is not
automatically appropriate for clustered servicing data. (kaz-yos/regmedint contributors, 2026)
  Consider M = 1+2A+εM and E(Y | A, M ) = 3A+4M +5AM , with mean-zero disturbance
and the necessary causal assumptions. PNDE and TNIE are 8 and 18; TNDE and PNIE are 18
210                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


and 8; TE is 26. The controlled direct effect at zero is 3, and the coefficient product 2 × 4 = 8
gives only one indirect component. Output must retain interaction, reference treatment and
mediator setting. Proportion mediated also needs a nonzero interpretable total and need not
lie between zero and one. (kaz-yos/regmedint contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ge)
  Use this package conditionally as a parametric comparator and fixture source. When a
marginal effect is needed, define the standardization explicitly. Logistic formulas, log effects
and rare-outcome approximations should be checked against exact binary enumeration at both
small and substantial baseline risks. A port should preserve the chosen approximation rather
than present an exact general risk decomposition. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)


20.18.5    Sensitivity measures have units, directions and domains

causalsens asks how a linear outcome analysis changes under a specified selection-bias function.
It adjusts outcomes and refits the linear model using model-based uncertainty. Its one-sided
adjustment is α(A − e) for propensity e, whereas alignment uses α{(1 − e)A + e(1 − A)}.
With e = 1/2 and α = 4, the first reduces a treated-minus-control mean gap by 4; the second
subtracts 2 from both groups and leaves the gap unchanged. Treated-population functions
differ again. Thus α carries outcome units and a confounding direction. A sensitivity curve does
not identify a mediation mechanism. (mattblackwell/causalsens contributors, 2024; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026ge)
   tipr provides coefficient adjustment and tipping-point interfaces. Its selected partial-R2
and robustness functions delegate to sensemakr. A simple coefficient
                                                                 p      adjustment subtracts a
declared bias product. Its numeric E-value helper applies r + r(r − 1), after reciprocating
an input at or below one, without a baseline-risk or effect-scale argument. An odds ratio of 2
at baseline risk 1/2 corresponds to risk ratio 4/3. Applying the formula to 2 gives about 3.414,
whereas applying it to 4/3 gives 2. This exact example rejects silent scale substitution; it does
not supply a universal hazard-ratio conversion. Nonpositive inputs and intervals crossing the
null need explicit handling. (r-causal/tipr contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026ge)
   The inspected boundary helper contains a fallback that resets outcome partial-R2 when an
interval misses its zero-boundary check. An adapter must preserve the requested scenario and
verify its endpoint, reporting a failed boundary calculation when appropriate. Conditional
interface reuse can build on the previously reviewed underlying methods while keeping their
scientific and numerical contracts visible. (r-causal/tipr contributors, 2026; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026ge)


20.18.6    BayesGmed: verify the latent-state likelihood before sampling

BayesGmed offers Bayesian parametric g-computation for continuous or binary mediators and
outcomes. Its selected primary text describes independent observations, identifying assump-
tions, correctly specified conditional models, posterior simulation and bootstrap integration
over baseline covariates. The sensitivity discussion introduces a binary unobserved confounder
with a prevalence model and bias parameters. The paper describes uniform bias priors; selected
version 0.0.3 instead supplies a multivariate Gaussian prior through a covariance matrix. These
are different analyses requiring explicit justification. The wrapper’s link arguments also do not
alter its fixed binary/continuous dispatch. Unsupported link requests should be rejected rather
than reported as model changes. (Yimer et al., 2022; cran/BayesGmed contributors, 2024)
  More fundamentally, if p = P (U = 1 | A) and fu (m, y) is the conditional mediator–outcome
20.18. R mediation and sensitivity contracts                                                  211


density in state u, the normalized mixture is

                             L(m, y) = (1 − p)f0 (m, y) + pf1 (m, y).

All four inspected Stan sensitivity files attach log(1 − p) to both latent states before log-sum-
exp. The two inspected generated C++ counterparts retain the same expression. It therefore
becomes                                                         Z
              Lsrc (m, y) = (1 − p){f0 (m, y) + f1 (m, y)},       Lsrc = 2(1 − p).

This is a static normalization discrepancy at the selected revision, not a measured sampler
failure rate. It concerns the inspected sensitivity paths and does not by itself reject ordinary
models or Bayesian mediation generally. (cran/BayesGmed contributors, 2024)
  An exact binary witness takes p = 4/5, mediator probabilities (1/4, 3/4) and outcome
probabilities (1/5, 4/5) in states zero and one, conditionally independent within each state.
The intended probability of (M, Y ) = (1, 1) is 49/100. The source expression gives 13/100 and
sums to 2/5 over the four observations. Renormalization gives 13/40, still different because it
substitutes equal mixing weights. When the components coincide, the intended likelihood loses
dependence on p, but the source expression retains it. These checks should precede expensive
sampling. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)
   Defer the selected sensitivity implementation until mixture, prior, link and artifact semantics
are reconciled. A repair needs a versioned successor, independent likelihood enumeration,
posterior and predictive checks, integration diagnostics and public known-law comparisons.
Ordinary-model review can proceed independently. Rights also need clarification: package
metadata declares MIT while a retained separate Stan license include states GPL3 or later.
Its applicability to a redistributed artifact is unresolved; neither an installed binary nor all
dependency rights is qualified here. (cran/BayesGmed contributors, 2024; Causal banking

20.18.7     A common contract and public qualification route

A CLI or MCP request should name baseline and post-treatment variables, mediator ordering
and joint law, intervention conditioning, treatment values, target population, outcome scale
and horizon, sampling units, measurement inclusion law and sensitivity parameters with their
units. Responses should distinguish unsupported identification, support failure, undefined
ratios, numerical failure and an admissible estimate. They should retain exact source revision,
method, prior, folds, resampling unit, integration budget and uncertainty definition. An LLM
can help elicit declarations and present alternatives, but cannot infer scientific truth or choose
a conditioning set merely to make a backend run. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)
   Public qualification starts with finite known-law examples, followed by frozen simulations
with supported and intentionally unsupported structures. Parametric formulas, semiparametric
scores, sensitivity wrappers and Bayesian likelihoods can be tested independently. Complete
request counts, refusals, target errors, interval behavior and end-to-end costs are needed. For
hypothetical USD30,000 spent on 1,000 requests, 600 returned results and 400 scientifically
admissible results, costs are USD30, USD50 and USD75 per respective denominator. Runtime
alone cannot select a denominator or establish bank value. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026ge)
   Four bounded repository queries returned 105 unique leads, with unreturned and uninspected
tails. They do not establish an exhaustive R census. Source inspection, artifact and rights
resolution, and public native experiments remain necessary. Unknown cross-world relationships,
hidden mediator confounding and unrestricted dependence need information or justified
212                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


restrictions. These distinctions preserve a practical route to R mediation and sensitivity
qualification. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ge)


20.19      Python mediation and sensitivity: effects, resampling,
           and the limits of computed bounds
A bank evaluating a digital servicing channel needs more than a coefficient labelled indirect
effect. Let A denote the assigned channel, M a subsequent customer response, X information
fixed before assignment, and Y the net outcome over a specified horizon. A response measured
after a collection decision cannot silently become a baseline adjustment variable. The proposal
therefore treats the observation clock, intervention, population and outcome scale as part
of the request. A package comparison is useful only after these quantities have been fixed.
The Python ecosystem supplies several different services: regression path summaries, model-
based potential-outcome integration, graph-guided orchestration, and partial-identification
calculations. They should be compared at the level of their estimands and failure conditions
rather than placed behind one interchangeable mediation command.statsmodels/statsmodels
contributors (2026c); raphaelvallat/pingouin contributors (2026); py-why/dowhy contributors
(2026); QuentinAndre/pyprocessmacro contributors (2026); Causal banking proposal project
(2026gb)


20.19.1    An estimand contract before a package choice

Write M (a) for the mediator under assignment a, and Y (a, m) for the outcome under joint
interventions. A useful nested mean is

                                  θ(a, a′ ) = E{Y (a, M (a′ ))}.

For a binary contrast, θ(1, 1) − θ(1, 0) is one natural indirect effect and θ(1, 0) − θ(0, 0) its
complementary direct effect. Their sum is the total effect, provided these nested quantities
are justified. The corresponding definitions with the outcome exposure fixed at zero need not
give the same indirect effect when there is interaction. Identification additionally requires
a defensible causal model, consistency, overlap, and the relevant treatment–mediator and
mediator–outcome exchangeability or stronger cross-world restrictions. Neither a fitted path
nor a sensitivity plot certifies those assumptions. The preceding R comparison develops
alternative interventional targets; the Python interface must retain that distinction.Causal
banking proposal project (2026gb); Frauen et al. (2023)
   For a concrete scale check, suppose P {M (0) = 1} = 1/4, P {M (1) = 1} = 3/4, and
E{Y (a, m)} = 3a + 4m. Under an otherwise identified law, either natural indirect effect is
4(3/4 − 1/4) = 2. A logistic regression of the binary mediator on A instead has slope log 9;
multiplying this slope by the outcome coefficient gives 4 log 9 ≃ 8.789. This is a coefficient
product on mixed scales, not the same outcome contrast. Reporting the latter number as the
former would change the business quantity before any uncertainty calculation begins. This
is an authored population example, not an observed error rate from a fitted package.Causal
banking proposal project (2026gb)


20.19.2    Potential-outcome simulation versus regression paths

The inspected statsmodels mediation implementation is a useful reference for explicit counter-
factual construction. Its formula route rebuilds the design matrix after exposure and mediator
20.19. Python mediation and sensitivity contracts                                              213


interventions; this matters for interaction terms. Its matrix route directly replaces columns
and cannot be assumed to rebuild derived interaction columns. It simulates mediator draws,
uses the same mediator realization for both outcome-exposure levels within a given mediator
assignment, and computes direct and indirect differences. The selected loops fix assignments to
zero and one, so another treatment contrast requires an explicit transformation or an extended
implementation.statsmodels/statsmodels contributors (2026c)
   Uncertainty requires a separate review. The parametric route draws mediator and outcome
parameters in separate calls. The bootstrap route calls a fitting helper twice; each call generates
its own row indices. These operations do not preserve arbitrary cross-equation dependence
merely because both equations originated in one customer table. An exact toy calculation
makes the distinction visible. Draw two values with replacement from {−1, 1}, and let Z ∗
be their mean. Its distribution is (−1, 0, 1) with probabilities (1/4, 1/2, 1/4). If two fitted
components share this perturbation, E[(Z ∗ )2 ] = 1/2 and Var(2Z ∗ ) = 2. Independently drawing
the components gives product expectation zero and sum variance one. This does not prove that
every statsmodels mediation interval is invalid: joint covariance can vanish under additional
model conditions. It proves that a shared-resample contract and a separate-resample contract
need a stated justification. Customer, household and calendar dependence introduce further
choices that an ordinary row bootstrap does not settle.statsmodels/statsmodels contributors
(2026c); Causal banking proposal project (2026gb)
   Two smaller boundaries also deserve tests before exposure through a product interface.
Initial method validation accepts a prefix beginning with para, whereas the iteration dispatch
selects parameter simulation only for the exact string parametric; accepting a prefix can
consequently change the computational route. The sign-tail expression for reported significance
counts strict positive and strict negative draws. With four exact zeros its arithmetic returns
zero, which is not evidence against the null. The proportion-mediated calculation also divides
by the total effect without defining an economic interpretation when that total is zero or
changes sign. We would wrap a narrowly qualified version with exact enumerations, typed
zero-total results and an explicit sampling contract, rather than infer qualification from the
API name.statsmodels/statsmodels contributors (2026c); Causal banking proposal project
(2026gb)
   Pingouin exposes a compact parallel-mediation workflow. The inspected implementation
drops incomplete rows, detects binary mediators and uses logistic mediator regressions for them,
fits a linear outcome model, and returns products of the mediator and outcome coefficients. The
source therefore directly motivates the mixed-scale example above. Its bootstrap applies one
row-index array to the mediator and outcome inputs, preserving the sampled row pairing. Its
bias-corrected interval is explicitly not an accelerated BCa interval, and its documentation warns
that bootstrap sign tails are not a null-conditioned permutation test. The zero-point-estimate
branch returns a significance value of one, unlike the strict-sign expression just discussed.
Moreover, the displayed Y ∼ M + X path omits treatment while the coefficient used for the
indirect product comes from the full treatment-and-mediator outcome model; the product
should not be reconstructed by multiplying arbitrary displayed rows.raphaelvallat/pingouin
contributors (2026)
   For continuous linear models with appropriately justified assumptions, Pingouin can be
a conditional comparator. For binary mediators it should be presented as a regression-path
summary unless a separate target derivation is supplied. Complete-case selection changes
the analyzed population and requires its own missingness argument. Multiple mediator
coefficients do not establish a causal ordering, joint intervention or absence of mediator–
outcome confounding. These distinctions justify retaining the package as a candidate while
rejecting a universal causal-effect interpretation.raphaelvallat/pingouin contributors (2026);
214                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


Causal banking proposal project (2026gb)
   The selected PyProcessMacro revision extends this regression-path family with moderated
and serial constructions, categorical coding and outcome-family choices. Its serial path
calculation multiplies coefficients along each ordered path. The bootstrap code fits the
equations on the same resampled rows and retains a count of failed fits. It continues until the
requested number of successful resamples is obtained, with an explicit failure cap. This is
useful instrumentation, but the retained draws are conditional on successful fitting. A later
public evaluation must report attempted, failed and accepted draws, separation and rank
failures, and the effect of those failures on the reported interval. A request that produces

20.19.3     Graph orchestration does not make all two-stage estimates equiva-
            lent

DoWhy supplies graph-oriented identification and estimator orchestration. In the inspected
mediation branch, variables on directed paths are collected and separate adjustment searches
are performed for the treatment–mediator and mediator–outcome stages. These are valuable,
inspectable steps. The selected two-stage estimator nevertheless restricts treatment and
mediator dimensions, defaults to linear regression stages, multiplies the two estimated effects,
and obtains a direct effect by subtracting that product from an estimated total. The request
must therefore bind the graph assumptions to this estimator’s actual algebra. An identifier
returning a mediation expression is not certification of arbitrary nonlinear mediation.py-

   A nonunit contrast exposes an especially concrete interface issue. Suppose M = 2A+εM and

regression intervention contrasts are therefore four and eight; multiplying gives 32. Subtracting
that from the total contrast 22 gives −10. The intended unit mediator slope has been replaced
by a second nonunit contrast. The source route agrees with the product formula for a unit

exact algebra for the inspected calls, not a native execution result.py-why/dowhy contributors

20.19.4     Sensitivity bounds with explicit mathematical scope

The generalized marginal sensitivity model of Frauen, Melnychuk and Feuerriegel is particularly
relevant to channel pathways. It bounds the change in the latent-confounder distribution
between conditioning on treatment and intervening. For each relevant mediator or outcome

                                             W ≤ 1 ≤ sW on a density ratio. Its framework
allows a sequence of discrete mediators, but excludes additional unobserved confounding
between mediators and the outcome for the stated path-effect interpretation. For a weighted
construction, a sensitivity parameter ΓW ≥ 1 and weight qW (a, x) ∈ [0, 1] give

                   W =                    ,         s+

   The paper derives extremal distribution shifts and a backward recursion over ordered
mediator states. Sharpness has additional conditions: the intervention must leave the relevant
latent distribution equal to its baseline conditional distribution, with the specified discrete-
treatment feasibility condition or continuous treatment. The paper explicitly excludes its
time-varying extension from that sharpness conclusion. Its inclusion of a longitudinal sensitivity
model must therefore not become a claim of generally sharp longitudinal bounds. Nor does a

specialization, so s− = 1/3, s+ = 3, and c+ = 3/4. For an ordered binary mediator with
probabilities (3/4, 1/4), the first category lands exactly on the threshold and satisfies none of

encounter such a configuration. Continuous integration should be checked against exact finite-

20.19.5     Neural bounds need both a theorem and numerical certificates

NeuralCSA generalizes the sensitivity family using two conditional normalizing flows. The
retained primary paper assumes independent observations, consistency, positivity and latent
unconfoundedness. Its key sufficiency theorem concerns a transformation-invariant generalized
treatment sensitivity model, an invertible map that exactly reproduces the observational
outcome distribution, and optimization over the full admissible distribution class. That result
motivates the two-stage construction. It does not say that any fitted flow, finite Monte Carlo
sample and stopped optimizer produces certified extrema.Frauen et al. (2024)
   The selected implementation samples latent variables, evaluates sensitivity constraints
and updates a constrained objective using multipliers and a penalty. For supremum-type
restrictions, sampled extrema can miss a small violating set. If a violation occupies probability
0.001 and 100 independent probes are drawn, the probability of seeing none is 0.999100 ≃ 0.905.
This is an authored diagnostic, not an assessment of the paper’s experiments. A feasible
maximization iterate is generally a lower bound on the optimal maximum, not by itself a
valid upper bound on the true causal query. A proposal for certified output therefore needs a
feasibility assessment, a justified optimization-gap bound or analytic outer envelope, and a
separate account of density-estimation and sampling uncertainty.DennisFrauen/NeuralCSA
contributors (2023); Frauen et al. (2024); Causal banking proposal project (2026gb)
   The source inspection also finds that a public sensitivity-check helper calls a three-argument
sensitivity method with only the training batch and latent sample; both selected subclass
definitions require the additional mixture sample. That static signature mismatch is a focused
candidate for a native regression test, not evidence about every training route. Continuous
Rosenbaum sensitivity is explicitly unimplemented. No license-named file was found in the
complete selected NeuralCSA and SharpCausalSensitivity trees; publication of source does not
settle permission to copy or redistribute it. We would compare their methods and seek artifact-
specific rights and delegate completion before code adoption or a port.DennisFrauen/NeuralCSA
contributors (2023); DennisFrauen/SharpCausalSensitivity contributors (2023); Causal banking
proposal project (2026gb)
   Overcast supplies a contrasting continuous-treatment workflow. The retained Jesson and
colleagues preprint bounds a treatment density ratio rather than inserting a density into the
binary-treatment odds-ratio formula. Its consistency theorem requires convergence of the
fitted outcome density and conditional mean, increasing Monte Carlo effort and a positivity
condition; its uncertainty section proposes bootstrap intervals for the bound endpoints. The
retained version is the April 2022 author original. A later title and author list in the repository
README are not substituted for that original.Jesson et al. (2022); anndvision/overcast
contributors (2022)
   In the selected continuous-treatment source, the sensitivity input is logarithmic, the code
exponentiates it, and an epsilon regularizes the expression near the no-confounding boundary.
It forms pairwise differences between outcome draws to evaluate threshold candidates. The
intermediate array has order m2 bd values for m draws, batch size b and d outcomes. For
m = 1000, b = 256, d = 1 and four-byte values, one such array alone is 1,024,000,000
bytes, before masks and other working arrays. This is a storage calculation, not a measured
platform limit. A sorted cumulative-sum alternative is a possible port only after tie handling,
centering, endpoint semantics and numerical parity have been demonstrated. The method is a
conditional dose-response candidate, not a substitute for a longitudinal policy or mediation

model.anndvision/overcast contributors (2022); Causal banking proposal project (2026gb)


20.19.6     A public qualification sequence with economic consequences

The package decisions imply independent, executable prototype questions. First, freeze a
graph, target, contrast, units, missingness policy and observation clock. Use public synthetic
laws with known nested means, including binary mediators, interaction, nonunit treatments
and exposure-induced confounding. Compare a regression-path service and a potential-
outcome service only where their assumptions imply the same target. Next, enumerate small
resampling distributions and finite-support sensitivity sets to check shared-row behavior, failed-
fit denominators, probability normalization, ties, contrast scaling and explicit refusal. Neural
candidates additionally require held-out density diagnostics, sensitivity feasibility, increasing
integration effort, repeated optimization and an external bound oracle. Dependent customer
and calendar experiments form a distinct qualification branch.Causal banking proposal project
(2026gb)
   The same interface must preserve the economics of uncertainty. Suppose, purely for
illustration, that a proposed intervention serves 10,000 customers, its benefit lies between
USD2 and USD8 per customer under the declared sensitivity model, and delivery costs
USD5 per customer. The resulting net interval is USD[−30,000, 30,000]. Neither the positive
endpoint nor a narrower optimizer output establishes a profitable decision. Further information
is valuable only if its expected decision benefit justifies acquisition, computation and review
costs. Public known-law fixtures can establish whether the proposed interface preserves this
reasoning before expensive bank data work is commissioned.Causal banking proposal project
(2026gb)
   Accordingly, statsmodels and DoWhy are conditional integration candidates with explicit
counterfactual and contrast wrappers; Pingouin and PyProcessMacro are useful regression-path
comparators with restricted causal interpretations; SharpCausalSensitivity and NeuralCSA
require the stated mathematical, numerical and rights conditions before implementation admis-
sion; and Overcast is a continuous-dose sensitivity candidate with a measurable integration-cost
question. Selected BSD-style, MIT, GPL and Apache declarations must be assessed together
with the actual artifacts and dependency chain; no umbrella rights clearance is inferred. Search
tails, negative-control and path-specific alternatives, installed-artifact validation and public
native trials remain open. The proposed product should expose an informative refusal whenever
a request exceeds the admitted target and sensitivity qualification.statsmodels/statsmodels
contributors (2026c); raphaelvallat/pingouin contributors (2026); py-why/dowhy contributors
