20.36.2     A stop event is a control state, not a scientific certificate

In LlamaIndex’s inspected agent workflow, structured-response generation can raise an excep-
tion that is converted to a warning before the workflow returns a stop event. Its early-stop
20.36. Framework delegates and scientific completion                                         283


generation option can also make another model call to construct a final response. Thus, a
terminal event alone cannot certify a valid structured answer. In LangChain’s classic agent,
forced stopping returns a limit response, while the generation option can request a final
model answer. The synchronous loop updates elapsed time between steps; that observation is
narrower than a claim that all outstanding remote operations are cancelled at a wall-clock
limit.(llama index project contributors, 2026; langchain project contributors, 2026b)
   Let T indicate terminal control flow, V validation of the scientific envelope, and I admission
of the requested effect under declared assumptions. The proposed scalar-effect gate is T ∧ V ∧ I.
An exact four-case construction admits only the terminal, valid, identified case. A completed
nonidentification result remains a legitimate answer with a different disposition; a terminal
structured-output failure remains a failed representation; an incomplete stream remains
incomplete. The gate specifies responsibility, not the truth of a bank’s assumptions. A
framework owns its execution state, the adapter checks representation and preserves errors,
and the causal library supplies the identification argument.(Causal banking proposal project,
2026go)
   Semantic Kernel’s inspected chat agent combines arguments and execution settings before
delegating to a selected provider. Its function wrapper invokes filters, records errors and
propagates exceptions; the streaming path can yield partial results. These hooks are useful
integration locations, but the inspected wrapper does not establish a causal validator. Haystack
validates components, sockets and mandatory inputs; its execution wrapper checks the returned
mapping and output names, and a blocked queue can raise an error. Such checks protect
pipeline structure. They should be retained alongside a separate validation of the target,
information clock, graph, estimand and uncertainty claim. A proposed CLI command and
MCP tool should return the same typed scientific disposition even when their orchestration
frameworks differ. (semantic kernel project contributors, 2026; haystack project contributors,
2026b)


20.36.3     Budgets must count actual attempts and side effects

LangChain recommends placing retries around the smallest operation that needs them. Its
inspected retry wrapper has configurable exception handling and backoff; the batch path retains
successful items and retries failed original indices. Suppose three independent items a, b, c
run once, only b fails, and b needs two further attempts. Selective retry makes 1 + 3 + 1 = 5
item attempts, whereas repeating the whole three-item batch three times makes nine. At a
stipulated USD 0.25 per item attempt, the costs are USD 1.25 and USD 2.25. These exact
accounting examples are not vendor prices. They also assume that retained successes are
valid and that the repeated operation is safe to retry; neither property follows merely from
an exception class. (langchain project contributors, 2026b; Causal banking proposal project,
2026go)
  Google GenAI’s inspected HTTP path converts configured milliseconds into seconds and
supports request-specific retry settings in addition to client defaults. The inspected server-
timeout header rounds seconds upward. Haystack’s visit limit applies to an individual
component, while a workflow can traverse several components. A business-request budget must
therefore count HTTP attempts, tool attempts, generation calls, waiting time and unresolved
outcomes explicitly. A framework iteration cap, a component visit cap and an HTTP timeout
are different limits. (google project contributors, 2026; haystack project contributors, 2026b)
   Anthropic’s pinned tool-runner documentation describes dispatch by native stop reason.
Tool-use responses trigger tools; paused turns and compaction can require continuation; other
stop states terminate the iterator after yielding the message. Its documented eager streaming
284                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


mode can execute a tool before the overall reply finishes. If that reply is interrupted, the tool’s
effect cannot be undone merely by discarding the conversation, and the model may request
the call again. The same documentation describes compaction calls outside the ordinary
iteration count and nested usage accounting. Two ordinary turns plus one separate compaction
make three calls in an authored counting example. A top-level counter cannot be assumed
to represent the complete cost denominator. (anthropic project contributors, 2026; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026go)
   For the reminder-policy workflow, graph inspection and effect calculation can be read-only
tools; dispatching an actual reminder is a different operation. The proposal should assign stable
operation identities, preserve pending results, and require a deduplication or reconciliation
policy before retrying actions with external effects. Cancellation requested and cancellation
observed must be separate states. A failed or unknown outcome remains in the denominator
when comparing cost and reliability. These are proposed architectural requirements, not a
claim that any reviewed framework already supplies end-to-end exactly-once execution.


20.36.4     Recovery, native stop reasons and learned programs

The inspected delegated workflow context describes a process-local store and serialization
of state, event queues, buffers and related execution metadata. Cancellation is delegated
for an external context, while other context states issue warnings. Serialization can support
resumption, but this source path alone cannot establish that a remote action and a local
checkpoint commit atomically. The proposed recovery record must therefore include both
local state and unresolved external-operation identities. Tests should interrupt immediately
before and after issuing a tool, receiving its result and recording the result.(workflows project
contributors, 2026b)
   Native stop reasons also need to survive compatibility adapters. Anthropic’s selected type
includes refusal, pause, tool use, output limits and context exhaustion. In vLLM’s inspected
serving path, parser selection depends on tool and reasoning settings, strictness, the model
and tokenizer. Its compatibility finish reason can depend on tool mode and generated tool
content while retaining the native stop reason. llama.cpp distinguishes native end-of-sequence,
stop-word and limit states before constructing compatibility fields; the task structure also
retains cancellation targets and parent-child identities. These source representations support
a concrete preservation requirement. They do not independently prove that cancellation
has reached every child or that two servers with similar response fields provide equivalent
behavior.(anthropic project contributors, 2026; vllm project contributors, 2026; llamacpp
project contributors, 2026)
   Optimization introduces another boundary. DSPy’s inspected bootstrap procedure selects
traces from training examples. A variable called validation contains the unbootstrapped
training subset, and success depends on the configured metric; without a metric, the inspected
branch accepts success. The threshold branch also depends on its truth value. These are
selected source semantics, not a claim of a general empirical defect. A causal assistant still
needs separately held-out tasks with independent expected answers, including nonidentification,
invalid adjustment and ambiguous graph cases. Optimizing a demonstration-selection metric
cannot by itself establish causal validity on new banking questions.(dspy project contributors,
2026b)

20.36.5     A bounded adoption and qualification decision

The proposal favors thin adapters around selected original clients and orchestration compo-
nents. LangChain contributes composable calls and scoped retries; Semantic Kernel contributes
provider and function hooks; Haystack contributes explicit pipeline structure; LlamaIndex
and its delegated workflow package contribute orchestration and recovery representations;
DSPy contributes a candidate optimization layer subject to an independent evaluation con-
tract. The decision is conditional integration, with scientific validation owned by the causal
library. It rejects automatic promotion of terminal messages into effects, implicit schema
weakening, unmeasured retry economics and unqualified wholesale ports.(langchain project
contributors, 2026b; semantic kernel project contributors, 2026; haystack project contributors,
2026b; llama index project contributors, 2026; workflows project contributors, 2026b; dspy
project contributors, 2026b)
  For hosted backends, client source inspection and service qualification remain separate.
For local backends, the exact server build, model, tokenizer, template, parser and grammar
configuration are part of the candidate. Ollama’s selected README itself requires a separately
running server and a selected model; its client identity cannot substitute for those artifacts.
README migration or product-focus statements likewise supply leads, not inherited qualifi-
cation: the Semantic Kernel README names a successor framework, and the LlamaIndex
README names parsing products and benchmarks. Those separate products require their
own primary-source comparison before adoption claims. (ollama project contributors, 2026;
semantic kernel project contributors, 2026; llama index project contributors, 2026)
   A low-cost public qualification suite can now be specified precisely. It should present an
invalid original-schema value, a handled tool error, a structured-output failure followed by
a terminal event, a partly failed batch, an interrupted side-effecting call, a compaction call
outside the ordinary counter, and a limit stop containing a valid-looking prefix. Each fixture
needs an independent expected scientific disposition, attempt ledger and recovery outcome.
Subsequent native trials require exact artifacts, rights and declared budgets; bank effectiveness
remains a later experiment. The comparison supports these targeted experiments without
converting static source inspection into measured merit. The causal answer is trustworthy
only when its meaning survives validation, scheduling, stopping and recovery.


20.37      Discovery delegates and local model boundaries
A banking proposal must preserve variable identity across discovery and execution boundaries.
Consider a collections team asking whether an early reminder changes later repayment. Its
proposed workflow first represents an information clock and candidate graph, then asks whether
the reminder effect is identified under that graph and the available observations. A Python
discovery wrapper and a local language-model endpoint can help implement this workflow,
but each introduces a separate conversion contract. The first can change the names attached
to a matrix; the second can change the place or completion state of a computation. Neither
conversion may silently redefine the causal question. The following comparison concerns
selected original source paths and exact authored examples, not an executed integration.


20.37.1     What an R delegate actually contributes

The selected CausalDiscoveryToolbox (CDT) commit delegates PC and GES through R
templates. The PC template loads pcalg, kpcalg, methods and RCIT, selects its conditional-
test route, and sets algorithm options including the stable.fast method and majority/conflict
286                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


behavior. Although the template’s options list contains a core-count field, the inspected call
does not pass that field to PC. A proposal therefore cannot infer parallel scaling from the
existence of the field. The data and constraint matrices cross the boundary as headerless CSV,
and a matrix returns through another CSV. The representation has lost the protection that
named variables could otherwise provide.(CausalDiscoveryToolbox and pcalg contributors,
2026)
   The GES path provides a second semantic warning. Its wrapper describes an int option
with a categorical label while mapping that option to GaussL0penIntScore. The selected
template constructs the chosen score using the data alone, runs GES, extracts the essential
graph and writes a matrix. In the separately inspected pcalg source, that class is Gaussian;
its default target list is empty and its default row assignment places every row in the first
environment. This comparator explains why an adapter must inspect the actual likelihood and
intervention metadata. It does not prove which pcalg version a particular CDT installation
resolves. An intervention-labelled class name does not create an intervention design, and a
Gaussian score is not made appropriate for categorical banking outcomes by a wrapper’s label.
The exact R and package versions, endpoint conventions and categorical alternative remain
explicit selection requirements.(CausalDiscoveryToolbox and pcalg contributors, 2026)
   Variable order is independently consequential. In the inspected direct-orientation paths,
skeleton or output labels are sorted while the input data retain their original column order.
This source observation motivates a conversion fixture; it is not a measured defect rate. Let
the declared data order be v = (z, a) and suppose the interface convention interprets Aij = 1
as a directed edge from row variable i to column variable j. For the authored matrix
                                                     !
                                                0 1
                                         A=         ,
                                                0 0

the edge is z → a. If the matrix stays fixed but labels become (a, z), the named edge
becomes a → z. A correct reordering uses the same permutation for the data, constraint

matrix is P AP T ; changing labels alone does not perform that operation. The two-node

   The launcher introduces a different boundary. It creates a UUID-based template copy and

20.37.2     A local endpoint is only one part of a model profile

The previously inspected Ollama Python client requires a separately selected server and

20.37.3     Completion, residency and scientific admission

Selected endpoints stream newline-delimited JSON. The documented protocol includes nonter-
minal chunks, a terminal done field and a stop reason. In the inspected stream handler an
error before output can set an HTTP error status; after output begins, an error is encoded
in the stream. The documentation correspondingly warns that an error arriving midstream
cannot change the status already sent. Receiving HTTP 200 and a plausible text prefix
therefore does not establish successful completion. Moreover, the inspected Chat handler can
return done=true with reason unload; successful unloading is not successful inference. The
full response state must survive the adapter boundary.(Ollama project contributors, 2026)
  Define T to mean a recognized inference terminal state, E an error anywhere in the trace,
V successful validation against the original response contract, and I an identified causal target
under explicitly recorded assumptions. A proposed admission rule is
                                   admit = T ∧ ¬E ∧ V ∧ I.
The precise terminal reasons allowed by T belong to the chosen endpoint and profile. In
an authored six-trace example we stipulate an HTTP 200 status for every trace and allow
stop as the successful inference reason. Only the complete, valid, identified trace passes. A
midstream error, truncated trace, unload response, invalid representation and nonidentified
query each fail a different conjunct. Exactly one trace is admitted and five are rejected. This
is a transparent specification example, not evidence of a six-request model test or an estimate
of error frequency. A rejected inference may still yield a useful explanation, identified set or
request for more information; rejection must not be hidden as a numeric zero. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026gm)
  Model residency must also be separated from workflow recovery. The request type describes
keep_alive as how long a model stays loaded, and the inspected scheduler decrements
288                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


reference counts and schedules unloading after the residency duration. This does not persist
the banking decision, original assumptions, tool effects or a recoverable conversation. Similarly,
the generation path propagates a request context and cancels it on a selected parser error, but
source-level context propagation is not an observed guarantee that all downstream work has
stopped. The request’s format is passed to a runner; this forwarding alone does not establish
conformance to every original schema constraint. Native cancellation and format fixtures
remain necessary for the chosen runner and model.(Ollama project contributors, 2026)


20.37.4     Public prototype route and adoption decision

These observations define a finite next prototype without requiring costly bank experiments.
The discovery fixture should use public or generated labelled columns, permutations and
constraint matrices, plus intentionally failing children, to test whether the selected CDT/R
path preserves the declared graph representation and refuses incomplete output. The model
fixture should bind one permitted build and weight profile, exercise complete and interrupted
streams, validate against the original schema, and retain routing and stop-state evidence. The
two exact authored witnesses provide independent expected behavior for narrow interface
contracts; they do not provide a truth oracle for an arbitrary discovered graph or language-
model answer. Native implementation, rights review and actual trial results remain separate
work.
   The proposed investment choice is therefore conditional reuse, with explicit alternatives.
CDT can supply selected discovery orchestration if its conversions and dependencies are
controlled; direct R usage can reduce wrapper ambiguity; a port is justified only when the
maintenance and equivalence burden is preferable. Ollama can supply a selected inference
service boundary after build, model, routing and termination contracts are pinned. A man-
aged service is a different choice with its own entitlement, cost and data-handling evidence.
Neither choice earns causal identification from a successful call. The resulting proposal keeps
source-supported capabilities, project specifications and future empirical qualifications distinct.
Variable identity and execution identity must survive every boundary before a causal result is
admitted.


20.38      Reinforcement search and discovery contracts
Reinforcement learning can search for a causal graph without establishing that the graph is
identified. For a bank considering early reminders, the graph-search problem is to compare
possible relations among eligibility,reminder assignment,repayment and recorded customer
characteristics. This is different from learning a servicing policy that will act on customers. In
the discovery methods reviewed here, the reinforcement learner is an optimizer: its actions
generate graphs or variable orders, and a statistical score supplies a reward. A better search
can improve a score while leaving the information needed for a causal effect unchanged. Public
or generated data can test the search and interface contracts before costly bank experiments,
provided the score’s assumptions and the target graph are declared separately.(Zhu et al., 2020;
Wang et al., 2021)


20.38.1     Graph search versus ordering search

Zhu,Ng and Chen formulate discovery as a search over directed graphs with a score and
acyclicity penalties. Their model discussion assumes scalar structural equations with jointly
independent additive noises,causal minimality and independently sampled observations. The
20.38. Reinforcement search and discovery contracts                                           289


paper explicitly recognizes that further restrictions are needed for unique graph identification;
its selected experiments use identifiable families. Its encoder-decoder proposes adjacency
matrices,and the best-scoring sampled graph is the output of the search. Those statements do
not establish validity under a latent common cause,a persistent panel or unmeasured selection
into reminders. In a banking application, such features must be represented or restricted
before the graph score can be interpreted scientifically.(Zhu et al., 2020)
   Wang and coauthors instead search variable orderings. Each complete ordering defines
a fully connected acyclic candidate; variable selection subsequently removes edges. Their
sequential decoder masks previously selected nodes,and the paper distinguishes episodic and
dense rewards. The consistency discussion assumes an identifiable structural equation model
and a suitable distribution family. Its proposition explains why an ordering-compatible model
reproducing the same distribution must cover the true graph under those assumptions. It
does not guarantee global optimization by policy gradients; the paper explicitly discusses local
convergence and approximation. Ordering removes a combinatorial acyclicity burden from
the candidate construction, but does not remove misspecification,finite-sample selection error
or causal nonidentification. Attention in an encoder is a representation mechanism,not an
edge-confidence or identification certificate.(Wang et al., 2021)


20.38.2     A precise qualification at the penalty boundary

For a graph G with binary adjacency matrix A,write S(G) for the score to minimize and
h(A) = tr(eA ) − d for the nonnegative cycle measure on d nodes. The graph-search formulation
adds λ1 1{G ∈/ D} + λ2 h(A),where D is the set of DAGs. Proposition1 in the inspected Zhu
preprint gives the non-strict condition

                                    λ1 + λ2 hmin ≥ SU − SL ,

with SL a lower bound on all graph scores,SU an upper bound on the optimum DAG score,and
hmin > 0 the smallest cycle measure over cyclic candidates. Its proof establishes that an optimal
DAG cannot be beaten by a cyclic candidate under this bound. At equality,however,that
argument need not exclude a cyclic candidate tied with the optimal DAG. The reverse proof
uses a strict improvement that does not follow from being a distinct tied minimizer. The
distinction matters if an implementation returns any maximizer of reward.(Zhu et al., 2020)
  An exact project construction isolates the boundary without making a claim about the
paper’s empirical BIC results. Enumerate the four loopless directed graphs on two nodes.
Assign score1 to each of the three DAGs and score0 to the two-cycle. Set SL = 0, SU = 1, λ1 = 1
and λ2 = 0. The displayed condition holds with equality,and every penalized score is1. The
cyclic graph is therefore also a minimizer. The optimal value still equals the DAG-constrained
optimum,and an optimal DAG remains available; what fails is the stronger conclusion that
every unconstrained minimizer is acyclic.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026gv)
   A sufficient repair for that stronger conclusion is strict domination, λ1 + λ2 hmin > SU − SL .
Then every cyclic penalized score is strictly greater than SU ,whereas some optimal DAG has
score at most SU . Alternatively,an exact optimizer can explicitly prefer a DAG among tied
optimal candidates,if such a candidate is available. In the finite witness,λ1 = 3/2 makes
the cyclic score 3/2 and leaves the DAG scores1. Neither repair proves that a practical
policy-gradient search finds the global optimum or samples a DAG. A returned candidate must
still pass an independent acyclicity check,and approximate cycle thresholds need a declared
tolerance policy. The construction qualifies the stated general score condition; it does not
assert a failure rate for the original experiments. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026gv)
290                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank

The selected gCastle source gives concrete contracts beyond the algorithm names. The RL

  The selected CORL entrypoint documents a dag_mask keyword but retrieves it using

   The reward comparison requires similar care. CORL’s selected score branches omit the

20.38.4     Dependency profiles and a finite public qualification

The complementary CDT inspection shows why listing dependencies is insufficient. The

   A finite public prototype can address these known interfaces without requiring bank truth.

20.39. Delegate-level temporal and evaluation protocol                                        291


and interruption into the R boundary. Each fixture needs an independently declared expected

   Conditional reuse remains the defensible product decision. A narrow discovery adapter can
retain upstream search mechanics while imposing explicit variable,score,constraint and failure

20.39      Delegate-level temporal and evaluation protocol
A precise temporal/evaluation contract keeps a predictive graph separate from banking
intervention evidence. The primary method description and the code path are different
evidence. Tracing the selected temporal and event-discovery delegates determines which
predictions are comparable and what a public qualification must measure. Four inspected
TACD configuration profiles explicitly request a training/validation pair split ratio of one.
They therefore enter the shared-pair branch described below; this conclusion is tied to those
exact profiles and commit.


20.39.1     Temporal support is not a learned causal delay

For a one-dimensional convolution with stride one and left padding p = (K − 1)d, the source
uses cross-correlation, so output index t can depend on input indices t−p+qd, q = 0, . . . , K −1.
The final point is t and the first is t − (K − 1)d. The selected Chomp1d removes the rightmost
p padded outputs, preserving sequence length and excluding future indices under this index
convention. With layer dilations dℓc , the largest support lag across L layers is
                                                   L−1
                                                   X
                                         (K − 1)         dℓc .
                                                   ℓ=0

For K = 2, dc = 2 and L = 3, non-target channel support may include lags zero through
seven. The TCDF data path separately shifts only the target channel by one row, zero-fills
the initial shift, and predicts the unshifted target. Thus the target’s raw-history support in
this finite index calculation is lags one through eight, while non-target variables may still
contribute at the contemporaneous index zero. A method called temporal or causal does not
thereby exclude same-row predictors; the variable clock and allowable information time must
be explicit. (M-Nauta/TCDF contributors, 2019; Causal banking proposal project, 2026gk)
  The final temporal block also applies a learned linear map across channels at each time point.
The source extracts maxima from depthwise kernel weights and turns them into candidate
delays. That statistic does not describe every path through channel mixing and residual
connections. The support calculation bounds which indexed inputs could matter; it does not
say which parameters the trained model uses, establish a stable delay estimate, or identify
an intervention. The application should preserve an explicit representation for candidate lag
support, learned predictive attribution, and causal-effect timing rather than serializing each as
one integer lag. (M-Nauta/TCDF contributors, 2019)
292                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


   There are concrete boundary conditions for a native fixture. If K = 1, then p = 0 and the
selected source still applies the slice :-0; ordinary Python indexing yields an empty sequence.
A zero-layer Sequential stack is an identity on the input, so its support is lag zero; this is not the
same as an empty output. The proposal does not silently assign behavior to these parameter
values. A version-pinned adapter must either reject them with an informative contract error
or establish valid supported semantics using a native trial. The source-free reference records
the empty-slice fact and proposed expectations without importing the acquired model.(Causal
banking proposal project, 2026gk)


20.39.2     Four TACD profiles use the same event-pair sets

The selected configuration file contains four named profiles: simulated events and the 18V, 24V
and 25V network datasets. Each explicitly assigns split_ratio=1.0. The selected entrypoint
shuffles event pairs and, for ratios at least one, assigns the complete pair list to both training
and validation. For these four profiles the overlap is therefore source-confirmed; it is not
merely an inference from a missing configuration key. Shared event histories can make the
effective dependence even broader than pair identity. No value of a generic row-level validation
metric from this branch should be described as held-out graph discovery. (Aquariuaa/TACD
contributors, 2026b)
   On selected real-data paths, the data processor loads a supplied graph matrix; the wrapper
passes that matrix to the discovery method; the training method uses it for threshold selection
and F1 checkpoint selection; and the top-level driver again selects an output threshold and
prints metrics against the same graph. This is an oracle-assisted result. It can support
an explicitly labeled method-debugging comparison, but not a blind discovery-performance
estimate on untouched graph truth. The selected command-line interface offers a simulation
label, while the inspected data processor has no matching branch that assigns its returned locals
for that choice. Its selected source tree also omits an imported data-mapping module. These
packaging and control-flow facts require repair or a supported external component before any
execution claim; no runtime failure was measured in this source-only review.(Aquariuaa/TACD
contributors, 2026b)
   The evaluation code compares graph scores using a strict greater-than threshold after
choosing an F1 maximizing value. A labelled tied-score fixture demonstrates why inclusive and
strict comparisons can create different graphs at the same numeric threshold. The source’s
manual confusion-count loop includes diagonal cells, whereas the threshold helper removes them
before selection; any report that exposes both must define its denominator and graph universe.
The selected device path chooses cuda:4 whenever CUDA is available and the method sets its
own seed. A reproducible run must record visible devices, the effective configuration and all
sources of randomness, not just the top-level CLI seed. These are scoped static observations;
the reference fixture does not assert that any installed external metric implementation disagrees.
(Aquariuaa/TACD contributors, 2026b; Causal banking proposal project, 2026gk)


20.39.3     A public protocol that preserves information boundaries

A low-cost public experiment should have graph instances, rather than just rows, as part of its
identity. Before running a candidate, freeze an independently generated training graph set, a
validation set used for thresholds and model selection, and a held-out evaluation set. If the
target is an event process, also freeze the calendar horizon, history-window rule, event-pair
construction and any purge gap between training and later evaluation. Where multiple rows
share an initiating event, device or graph, do not treat them as independent assignments
20.40. Enforcing a public discovery evaluation contract                                        293


without a declared sampling argument. Record graph truth access as hidden until final scoring,
available for training/debugging only, or deliberately oracle-assisted.
   The selector must receive only its declared validation labels. After its threshold and
checkpoint are frozen, the evaluator binds held-out graph identity and truth, then computes
a predeclared off-diagonal metric. All requested graphs remain in the denominator. Invalid
or missing scores retain separate requested and valid counts; zero valid batches produce an
unavailable outcome, not a numerical loss of zero. Tied scores require an explicit comparison
convention and deterministic tie resolution. Missing topology, an unavailable simulation
delegate, CUDA index selection and source package identity are logged as input conditions,
not repaired by undocumented defaults. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026gk)
   The source-free fixture implemented here verifies only these proposal-owned contracts on a
tiny stipulated example. It selects a threshold on a validation instance, checks that a distinct
evaluation instance is scored afterward, rejects overlapping identities, returns unavailable for
an empty valid denominator and checks exact lag/tie expectations. It does not call TACD,
TCDF, PyTorch, gCastle or scikit-learn. It provides a reviewable test shape before a native
environment and rights packet are ready, not evidence that either external algorithm meets
the contract.
   This supplemental trace sharpens reuse decisions without broadening their scope. TCDF may
remain a conditional temporal candidate after native window, padding and delay-conversion
fixtures. TACD remains a specialist event/topology candidate whose supplied-graph results
must be segregated from truth-free evaluation and whose four selected profiles share their
training/validation pairs. Both must pass exact source closure, rights intake and a registered
public known-truth comparison before those candidates can enter a product adapter.
  A temporal discovery result is admissible only when its observation window, graph truth
access and failure denominator are explicit.


20.40       Enforcing a public discovery evaluation contract
A public discovery comparison needs an information contract that can fail visibly. The
preceding small fixture illustrates a split-and-score design. Its case objects still carry graph
truth, and its checks do not enforce every duplicate identity or nonfinite denominator boundary.
The stronger proposal-owned successor separates case identity from labels and checks these
conditions explicitly. Its demonstrated scope is a trusted local interface, with no external
discovery engine execution. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026gp)


20.40.1     Declared identity and permitted truth access

A case reference contains an identifier, graph-instance identifier, exact data SHA-256 and one
of training, validation or evaluation. It contains no graph truth. A frozen registry binds the
node universe and all case references to a deterministic digest. The registry rejects repeated
case identifiers, graph-instance identifiers and data hashes across every declared split, including
repeated evaluation requests. This is a policy on supplied identities and exact bytes; it does
not prove that two differently encoded mechanisms are independent. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026gp)
   Validation labels must match exactly the validation case identifiers. The threshold selector
checks both this split role and the registry digest; an evaluation truth view is refused. A
selected threshold is then carried into a separate evaluation call that checks the evaluation
labels and retains every requested case. Neither a digest nor a frozen Python object prevents a
294                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


malicious caller from fabricating a new validation label view or obtaining labels elsewhere. A
later native experiment therefore also needs a separately operated truth store, declared access
paths and a recorded selection freeze. These local checks specify a reviewable boundary before
that more costly experiment. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026gp)
   The graph universe is directed off-diagonal edges over the frozen node set. Unknown nodes,
self edges and mutable edge sets are refused. For a predicted edge set E and truth T , the
fixture computes
                                                  2|E ∩ T |
                                     F1 (E, T ) =
                                                  |E| + |T |
when the denominator is positive and explicitly assigns one to an empty/empty pair. That
convention is part of this comparison, rather than an inferred property of a third-party scorer.
Threshold candidates use exact rational numbers in [0, 1]. Equal validation macro scores
select the smallest threshold, so reversing candidate insertion order cannot resolve a scientific
choice differently. A future score-to-edge adapter must additionally freeze its strict or inclusive
comparison and record the predictions associated with each candidate; this fixture accepts
those candidate graphs as inputs. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026gp)


20.40.2     Availability changes the interpretation of an average

Let m > 0 be the requested graph count, v the finite valid count and s the sum of valid scores.
The reported conditional mean is s/v when v > 0 and the declared minimum valid count is
met. Availability is v/m. Missing results, NaN and either infinity remain in the requested
count and have separate reason counts. When no valid result remains, the mean is unavailable.
Increasing a minimum valid count can also make the mean unavailable even when a finite score
exists. These are accounting and interface rules, not statistical calibration results. (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026gp)
   The exact example retains two evaluation requests: one perfectly reconstructed graph and
one unavailable prediction. Its conditional mean is one and its availability is 1/2. If a score for
every unavailable request is known only to lie in [0, 1], the mean over all requested graphs lies
in
                                    s s+m−v
                                                 
                                      ,             = [1/2, 1].
                                    m       m
This is an elementary bound on missing scores, not a confidence interval. A bank comparing
workflows should preserve both the conditional quality and availability before assigning value
to returned graphs. Reporting only the conditional score of one would conceal the unresolved
request. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026gq)
   The performed suite contains 48 adversarial cases with no failures, errors or skips. It covers
duplicate identities, split-role confusion, graph-universe errors, invalid thresholds, deterministic
ties, missing/nonfinite denominators and retained failed evaluation requests. It establishes
these selected local behaviors. It does not establish authentic graph labels, process isolation,
general calibration, an implemented third-party adapter or bank performance. A causal
comparison is credible only when the missing results and permitted information remain part
of the reported question.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026gp)


20.41      Java delegates and conditional adoption
A banking discovery adapter must preserve the oracle as well as the graph. The seven
newly inspected Aitiotita delegates at the pinned 9 September 2023 revision clarify the
20.41. Java delegates and conditional adoption                                                  295


earlier source-access limit. Their abstract interface accepts correlation, conditional-correlation
and independence callbacks. The bundled discrete implementation instead counts linguistic
cognate overlaps and subtracts flow explained through other languages. Its unexplained
count is compared to a pair-specific threshold. The class name alone supplies no Gaussian
partial-correlation test or calibrated banking p-value. (jdellert/aitiotita contributors, 2023)


20.41.1     The earlier conditioning witness has a precise scope

The earlier exact six-variable Gaussian construction separates a concession X and response Y
after three independent baseline factors are held fixed. Adding their common consequence
opens dependence again: conditional covariance changes from zero to −1/3, with residual
variances 2/3 and correlation −1/2. It refutes a general argument that dependence given every
neighbor rules out all smaller separators. Because the generic algorithm accepts a supplied
oracle, a proposed covariance-based port must address this objection. It is not an empirical
failure of the bundled linguistic-flow oracle. Retain that domain distinction when deciding
whether to remove the shortcut or prove validity in a narrower graph and oracle family. (Causal
banking research project, 2026x; jdellert/aitiotita, 2023; jdellert/aitiotita contributors, 2023)


20.41.2     Three separating-set policies need different interpretations

For an unshielded triple, let m be the number of registered separating sets and k the number
containing the middle variable. The inspected default arrow finder orients in its conservative
branch when k = 0, in its stable branch when k ≤ ⌊m/2⌋, and in its remaining branch when
the first set excludes the middle. Thus an exact half vote is included by the stable comparison.
With two sets, one containing the middle and one excluding it, that branch orients and the
conservative branch refuses; reversing the set order can alter the first-set result. The authored
finite truth table checks all 27 (m, k) states for 1 ≤ m ≤ 6. The differences from a strict
minority occur at (2, 1), (4, 2) and (6, 3). None of these policies supplies a probability that
the proposed collider is true.(jdellert/aitiotita contributors, 2023; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026gq)
   The optional collider callback in the discrete-flow class makes a separate literal-source choice:
it sets p = 0.2, leaves the distribution calculation commented, and compares p < 0.10. Every
invocation reaching that comparison returns false. The registered-separating-set arrow finder
is a different path, so this observation does not imply that every algorithm configuration
refuses every collider. Reuse requires tracing the selected call path rather than inferring global
behavior from a method name.(jdellert/aitiotita contributors, 2023)


20.41.3     Propagation and prior knowledge need enforcement

In the inspected propagation rule 3, an outer condition requires an endpoint to equal the arrow
constant two; an inner condition requires the same endpoint to equal the circle constant zero
before the assignment. The intervening path helper reads adjacency without changing endpoint
state. Under unchanged single-threaded graph reads these requirements are contradictory. The
three-state authored truth table confirms this local logical obstruction; it does not prove the
behavior of every other rule or concurrent execution. A port needs an independently derived
intended rule and graph-level witnesses, rather than an unreviewed textual replacement of one
index. (jdellert/aitiotita contributors, 2023; Causal banking proposal project, 2026gq)
  The low-level graph methods also differ from an enforcing knowledge boundary. Link
removal and endpoint/arrow setters inspect preset flags but proceed with mutation. Some
296                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


callers guard particular writes. Such guards do not make every method safe for an arbitrary
caller with an earlier-time causal restriction. For example, a prohibition on a later collections
action causing an earlier balance must be enforced at the adapter boundary and checked

neighbor getter exposes a live stored set, so a consumer should use a copy. (jdellert/aitiotita
contributors, 2023)
   The acquired root text is Apache-2.0. Dependency and redistributed-artifact rights still
require their own review. The POM declares Java 8 and test-only JUnit 3.8.1; the acquired test

   The proposal should retain this revision as a transparent comparison and a conditional

20.42      Bundled discovery engines and semantic boundaries
A repository name is too coarse a unit for a banking reuse decision. A collections analyst
may ask whether changing a contact policy affects repayment, while a bundled program
learns a high-scoring discrete network or converts one graph representation into another. The
implementation can be useful without answering that intervention question. The inspected
reliableAI revision of 2 September 2026 contains selected Spot and BLIP components with
different source origins, licenses, numerical targets and operating boundaries. Twenty exact
text originals support the following comparison; no downloaded engine, Java class, JAR or
setup script was executed.(reliableAI and nested package contributors, 2026)


20.42.1    Source identity is finer than the enclosing repository

The repository root contains MIT license text, Spot contains Apache-2.0 text, and the nested
BLIP directory contains LGPL-3 text. The BLIP README attributes the package to Mauro
Scanagatta and IDSIA. These declarations cannot be collapsed into a root-wide permission or
proof that a vendored derivative equals an upstream release. The selected POM files declare
version 1.0 and Java 1.6 source/target settings, while the CLI banner declares version 0.9.
Record both identities and reconcile the exact distribution before proposing a native adapter.
Dependency terms, source changes, compiled artifacts and notices require their own review.
This is a source inventory, not an approval of redistribution. (reliableAI and nested package
contributors, 2026)
   Spot’s requirements list pins a broad numerical and machine-learning stack, including
causal-learn 0.1.2.8 and ananke-causal 0.1.5. A requirements list is not evidence that those
packages, their transitive dependencies and the saved Java binaries agree with the source under
review. The setup script downloads Tetrad 6.8.0 with certificate checking disabled, downloads
XOM 1.3.5, and compiles only the MAG-to-PAG helper. Its companion PAG-to-MAG source
is present, but that script does not rebuild it. The proposed integration therefore replaces
this installation path with authenticated, fixed artifacts and a reproducible build before any
20.42. Bundled discovery engines and semantic boundaries                                     297


execution is claimed.(reliableAI and nested package contributors, 2026)


20.42.2    Graph conversion must preserve the object being inferred

The Java MAG-to-PAG helper calls Tetrad’s MagToPag, enables the complete rule set and
saves the result. The reverse helper calls pagToMag and saves one graph. That call site
specifies neither random sampling nor a probability distribution over the equivalence class.
Accordingly, the Python name sample_mag is not evidence that its output represents posterior
graph uncertainty. A proposed effect query must preserve the original class or justify the
selection rule and its scientific consequences. (reliableAI and nested package contributors,
2026)
   The surrounding Python converter invokes the shell without checking its return status
and then reads the expected output. The Java helpers catch conversion exceptions and print
generic error messages. A future worker needs a structured result that distinguishes launch
failure, parse failure, invalid graph, missing output and successful conversion. In a batch of
banking questions, failures must remain in the requested denominator rather than become
absent files. The existing public evaluation contract supplies a local accounting pattern; it
does not already implement this Java adapter.(reliableAI and nested package contributors,
2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026gp)
  A further source-level workaround changes meaning: the inspected reader maps an undirected
token –- to a bidirected edge, just as it maps <->. Those endpoint marks are distinct inputs.
An adapter must reject unsupported marks or retain them explicitly; it cannot silently treat
the workaround as an endpoint-preserving round trip. The other parser also constructs node
names from integer labels. Customer-variable identity and time ordering therefore need an
explicit bijection, with roundtrip checks, rather than an assumption that every dataset already
uses the expected names. (reliableAI and nested package contributors, 2026)


20.42.3    A good endpoint score can conceal the wrong neighboring variable

For each arrowhead at variable v on the edge joining u and v, a neighbor-preserving key is the
ordered pair (v, u). The inspected compare_pag function uses such a pair for the first stored
endpoint, but encodes an arrowhead at the second endpoint as (v, v). The same pattern appears
in its tail keys. Consequently, distinct edges entering one variable can collapse to the same
key. Its full-edge and skeleton metrics are separate and need not share this failure.(reliableAI
and nested package contributors, 2026)
   Consider a truthful edge A → B and an estimated edge C → B, each stored with B second.
The arrowhead key sets both become {(B, B)}, so their reported arrowhead F1 is one even
though the neighbor-preserving sets are disjoint and their F1 is zero. Conversely, store the same
truthful edge as (B, A) with an arrow at its first endpoint: its key becomes (B, A), and the
inspected key comparison against the original storage gives zero although the semantic graph
is unchanged. Two incoming edges A → C and B → C also collapse to one second-endpoint
key. These are exact authored logical witnesses of the inspected encoding, not measured native
failure rates. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026gt)
  The proposal should adopt the invariant that endpoint identity includes its neighbor,
canonicalize storage independently of meaning, and retain empty-graph and unavailable-result
conventions. The selected skeleton-only scorer returns an empty dictionary on arithmetic
exceptions; the PAG scorer instead uses several explicit zero conventions. Their outputs cannot
be silently pooled into a common average without an adapter-level contract. A comparison of
contact-policy graphs is decision-relevant only if a correct arrowhead at the wrong business
298                                                                 Causal analysis for a universal bank


variable is still recognized as an incorrect result. (reliableAI and nested package contributors,
2026)
   The bootstrap module has a separate call-boundary problem. It imports fci and then
defines another function with that name. Inside the local function, the call fci(sub_X)
resolves to the local global binding, which expects an object with an X attribute, although
the supplied subsample is a NumPy array. This static name-resolution finding concerns that
default route; the module’s main block explicitly chooses RFCI instead. The RFCI branch
launches a bundled JAR and exits after a missing-output condition. Neither reading the source
nor counting one hundred subsamples establishes that the numerical procedure ran or that its
aggregate is calibrated. (reliableAI and nested package contributors, 2026)

20.43      Attention discovery and evaluation contracts
Attention can rank predictive relationships without identifying the effect of a banking interven-
tion. Consider a bank asking whether an earlier reminder changes repayment, using histories of
reminders, balances, delinquency and recorded contacts. A prediction graph relates information
available at specified times to future repayments. An intervention question instead changes
an assignment rule and asks what would happen under that change. Shared financial stress,
servicing selection and measurement delays can make these different questions even when
prediction is accurate. The proposal therefore treats attention as a candidate-construction
mechanism whose sampling law, variable clock, graph meaning and evaluation procedure must
be stated explicitly.


20.43.1     Distinct meanings of attention and of a causal graph

The inspected Liu preprint defines a DAG of Granger relationships, with Markov, faithfulness,
strict-order and minimum-signal assumptions. Its strict ordering is written as i < j for a
relationship from variable i to variable j, and the text excludes contemporaneous causation.
That is a substantive restriction on the admitted graph, rather than a consequence of computing
self-attention. A bank with feedback between arrears and subsequent reminders must decide
whether its nodes are time-indexed events, entire series, or a restricted ordering of series. A
series-level DAG cannot be silently substituted for an unfolded temporal graph with feedback
across dates. The inspected method aggregates attention contributions across tokens, selects
potential edges using an order-statistic threshold, and compares predictions after permuting a
candidate series. These operations support a particular predictive discovery procedure under
the stated model; they do not supply a general intervention-effect confidence region.(Liu et al.,
2026b)
   Attention also describes different computational objects. In the selected TCDF implementa-
tion, a trainable vector supplies a softmax gate on input variables before depthwise convolution
and a pointwise convolution. Candidate selection uses attention scores, and a later permutation
step compares a fitted model’s loss on the original training target. The delay extraction reads
300                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


maxima of convolutional kernel weights. These are concrete mechanisms, but neither a gate
weight nor a kernel maximum is automatically an intervention coefficient. The inspected
source’s significance parameter enters a loss-improvement fraction; that expression alone
does not establish a calibrated p-value or a familywise graph error guarantee. The software is
cited for these selected source mechanics; its scholarly article remains a separate primary-source
obligation.(M-Nauta/TCDF contributors, 2026)
   The selected CAMCNs model likewise contains a softmax feature gate followed by depthwise
and pointwise convolutions, while its discovery path adds correlation and lag selection. A
README’s multihead description does not establish that every selected module implements
query-key-value multihead attention. The proposal should compare the actual selected com-
putation, not collapse all architectures into one label. Its entrypoint imports train and
VAL from the model module, whereas the inspected definitions are methods of TCFMODEL
rather than top-level functions. The namespace mismatch is a static integration finding at
the pinned source revision. It calls for a supported entrypoint or a documented repair and
conformance fixture before native evaluation; no runtime failure rate was measured here.
(nicoirribarra/CAMCNs-Causal-Discovery contributors, 2026)


20.43.2     What permutation changes

The inspected Liu text states that shuffling a candidate series while holding the other variables
fixed preserves the original data distribution. This requires qualification. A permutation
preserves that series’ empirical marginal multiset, but generally changes its joint alignment
with other series and its temporal arrangement. The change can be the intended perturbation;
it cannot simultaneously be assumed to preserve every relevant observational law. (Liu et al.,
2026b)
  An exact author construction makes the distinction explicit. Let the four observations be
x = z = (0, 0, 1, 1), and keep z fixed. Replacing x with xπ = (1, 1, 0, 0) leaves the marginal
counts unchanged. With empirical covariance defined using denominator four, however,

                             Cov(x,
                             d      z) = 14 ,     d π , z) = − 1 .
                                                  Cov(x        4

The fitted predictor f (x) = x has mean squared error zero before the permutation and one
after it. A different permutation, (0, 1, 0, 1), changes the proportion of adjacent equal values
from 2/3 to zero. Thus even this small example separates preservation of the marginal, the
joint distribution and temporal structure.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026gl)
   The predictive-loss increase does not by itself identify an effect. Suppose the structural
model is X = U , Z = U , where U is a fair binary common cause. The displayed observations
are compatible with that model. Intervening on X leaves the equation for Z unchanged, so
E[Z | do(X = 1)] − E[Z | do(X = 0)] = 0, despite the loss increase of the fixed predictor
under the displayed permutation. This is a project witness against a universal interpretation
of permutation importance as intervention effect. It is not an empirical reproduction of the
paper, an estimate of its error rate, or a claim that a properly specified permutation test can
never be valid.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026gl)
   For repayment histories, the resampling design must answer a precise null question. An
unrestricted shuffle, a within-calendar shuffle, a block permutation and a conditional resampling
scheme alter different information. Restricting permutations can preserve some nuisance
structure, but then requires an exchangeability or conditional-law argument for the chosen
null. Refitting after a perturbation asks a different question from measuring reliance of a
fixed predictor. Training, candidate screening, threshold choice and held-out scoring also
need separate information sets. These are proposed design requirements; the exact witness
20.43. Attention discovery and evaluation contracts                                           301


establishes neither their calibration under arbitrary banking dependence nor a universal repair
for hidden common causes.


20.43.3     Evaluation truth, empty denominators and temporal splits

TACD addresses topological event sequences in telecommunications. Its selected source
combines attention with excitation, learned ordering and a regularized likelihood. This is a
specialist candidate for questions about event propagation, not an interchangeable estimator for
IID tabular reminder data. Any banking adaptation would first define devices or counterparties,
event types, network exposure and observation time. The resulting point-process or event
target must remain explicit through the adapter.(Aquariuaa/TACD contributors, 2026a)
   Two selected evaluation branches are especially consequential. When dag_matrix is supplied,
the training routine passes it to threshold optimization and computes graph F1 for checkpoint
selection. Such an experiment uses graph truth in model selection. It can be legitimate as a
declared oracle-assisted or training-graph study, but its score cannot be presented as blind held-
out discovery on that same truth. A public qualification should freeze thresholds and selection
rules on training graphs, then evaluate once on separate unseen graphs and independent
realizations under the intended deployment information. A prediction-loss selection branch
is also available in the selected source; it addresses a different objective and still requires
an explicit connection between prediction and graph quality.(Aquariuaa/TACD contributors,
2026a)
   The evaluation routine omits NaN losses and divides the accumulated loss by max(nvalid , 1).
If no batch has a valid loss, this returns zero. Zero is then a sentinel produced by an empty
effective denominator, not observed perfect prediction. The adapter must preserve requested,
valid and failed counts and return an unavailable score when the predeclared valid-data rule
fails. Likewise, the entrypoint randomly shuffles event pairs and uses a default split_ratio
of one when that key is absent; at values at least one, the training and validation pair lists
are the same. This is a conditional source branch, not a claim about every supplied dataset
configuration. Event pairs may also share history, so a row split alone need not isolate
information. The exact configuration and event-construction delegates must be inspected
before a native trial’s split is described as temporal or independent. (Aquariuaa/TACD
contributors, 2026a)
   The appropriate public experiment therefore separates four denominators: candidate graphs
requested, graphs returned, graphs selected using available training information, and graphs
scored on untouched evaluation truth. Failed batches and unsupported graphs remain visible.
Evaluation on a known synthetic graph can verify mechanisms cheaply, while observational
public financial data can test data contracts and sensitivity without supplying nonexistent
graph truth. Neither exercise should be promoted to bank validation solely because the dataset
is public.


20.43.4     Reproduction scope and dependency identity

The selected CausalTransformer repository illustrates a further boundary. Its README
describes figure regeneration from recorded benchmark results and explicitly says that model-
training benchmarks are not rerun. A reproduction command for those figures therefore
does not by itself reproduce learning, data generation, selection or reported performance. In
the inspected revision, the runner also conditionally requests two LaTeX source files that
are absent from the complete selected tree. That is a static packaging mismatch, not an
observed execution result. The stated journal target and current repository description cannot
302                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


establish publication acceptance, and an academic-review notice alone does not establish a
broad reuse grant. The defensible proposal disposition is to retain the artifact as a limited
reproduction lead until the training source, primary article and reuse terms are resolved.(sgao-
academics/CausalTransformer contributors, 2026)
   Dependency identity is equally important for a method that delegates to R. The inspected
CDT installer is itself pinned, but installs unversioned operating-system and R packages,
uses several unauthenticated-package options, references HTTP CRAN endpoints, sources a
mutable Bioconductor script, and requests GitHub packages without commit pins. Freezing
the wrapper’s bytes does not freeze those remote inputs. The installer was inspected as
text and was not run; the immediate remote script and package-installation bodies remain
unresolved dependencies. A proposed replacement should bind the operating system, interpreter,
compiler, package archives, digests and component terms, then qualify a selected isolated
environment on public fixtures. Verified HTTPS acquisition and an archive identity are
necessary provenance steps, but do not by themselves establish scientific correctness or
transitive rights.(CausalDiscoveryToolbox contributors, 2026a)


20.43.5     A conditional product decision

The present evidence supports a differentiated reuse strategy. TCDF and CAMCNs can
inform a time-series candidate-generation comparison after their selected source and depen-
dency contracts are resolved. Their inspected GPL notices require component-level intake
for the intended use; this proposal does not declare a legal clearance. TACD is a specialist
event-network candidate whose truth-assisted selection and split routes need an explicit pub-
lic protocol. CausalTransformer currently contributes a figure-reproduction artifact rather
than an established native learner route. Porting any method would add an equivalence
and maintenance obligation; an isolated adapter may be preferable when it can retain up-
stream computation and expose the required semantics. (M-Nauta/TCDF contributors, 2026;
nicoirribarra/CAMCNs-Causal-Discovery contributors, 2026; Aquariuaa/TACD contributors,
2026a; sgao-academics/CausalTransformer contributors, 2026)
   Before enablement, a finite fixture set should check variable and timestamp identity, permit-
ted lags, target shifting and padding, missing and nonfinite values, candidate threshold ties,
empty score denominators, training/evaluation separation and failure propagation. A second
layer should compare generated confounded and unconfounded systems with independently
specified truth, including a fixed-predictor permutation witness. These are proposed public
qualification steps, not results of executing the acquired packages. The final report should
retain predictive and interventional targets separately, state which identification assumptions
are substantive, and refuse an effect claim when the required information is absent. Attention
discovery becomes a useful proposal component only when its predictive target, evaluation
information and reuse conditions remain explicit.


20.44      Identification software must preserve what is and is not
           identified
Suppose a bank is considering an encouragement to make an additional repayment. Let A
denote randomized access to a reminder and Y denote repayment by twelve months. The
business question may ask for the effect of offering the reminder, whether a particular customer
would repay only if reminded, or the range of possible repayment effects when an assumption is
unavailable. Those are three different targets. A fitted conditional association, an interventional
functional, a cross-world probability and a sharp identified set do not have interchangeable
20.44. Identification software must preserve what is and is not identified                     303


meanings. The proposed interface must name the target and information regime before it calls
an R package.
   For a supplied directed acyclic graph, dagitty can enumerate sufficient adjustment sets
under its documented graphical criteria. That is a useful graph diagnostic; it is not a general
algorithm for deriving every interventional functional under latent confounding. The existing
pcalg and bnlearn comparison adds equivalence-class and causal-network procedures, but
their returned graph or effect list has its own model class and assumptions. In particular,
pcalg’s IDA manual assumes a faithful multivariate Gaussian law and a causal DAG without
hidden variables, and estimates total effects over admissible DAG extensions. It is neither
an arbitrary nonlinear effect region nor a confidence set for a bank decision. The ivmodel
confidence-set interface answers another question again: its documented AR/CLR inversion
returns interval components under its declared IV design, with CLR described as robust to
weak instruments. The proposed wrapper must preserve these set components and admit
infinite endpoints where the inversion yields them. A single label such as “causal effect” would
erase these distinctions (jtextor/dagitty contributors, 2024a; pcalg contributors, 2026; Marco
Scutari and contributors, 2026; ivmodel contributors, 2023).
   The R package causaleffect supplies symbolic ID/IDC functionality and selected trans-
portability and selection-recovery procedures. Its pinned R function accepts outcome, treat-
ment, optional conditioning variables and a graph; it can return an expression or a derivation
object. The selected implementation has an important adapter consequence: with its default
stop_on_nonid=TRUE, nonidentification raises an error; with the option false, a failed identifica-
tion can be represented by id=FALSE in the step result, an empty string, or NULL, depending on
the other output options. A production wrapper must distinguish that documented algorithmic
result from parse errors, unsupported graphs and runtime exceptions. It should also retain the
graph class and functional, not just a Boolean or formatted string (Tikka, 2025a).
   The pinned dosearch package asks whether an interventional target follows from multiple
observational or experimental distributions and a graph, including selected transport, selection
and missingness mechanisms. Its 2021 paper describes a sound search over do-calculus rules,
with completeness tied to the specified problem class. Its Table 1 distinguishes complete ID/IDC
cases, unknown completeness for general multiple-source identification, and an incomplete
missing-data extension. The package documentation expressly says its missing-data search
is not complete. More subtly, the pinned C++ source applies a positive time limit by
returning early from the search; its initializer then decides identifiability from whether a target
distribution was found and does not expose a separate timeout state in that result. Therefore,
under that code path, a limit-truncated search can be represented like “not identifiable by this
search.” An adapter must not promote that output to a proof of nonidentifiability. It must either
disable the limit for the bounded admitted problem, instrument a distinct timeout/unknown
state, or report the uncompleted search as unknown. This is a source-level review of a pinned
revision, not an executed package trial (Tikka et al., 2025, 2021).
   Counterfactual identification is a further level. cfid implements ID*/IDC* for counterfactual
conjunctions by constructing a parallel-worlds graph with shared latent variables and then
applying recursive identification. Its function defaults to identifying from interventions,
not from observations; the observational level must be requested or obtained through the
documented alternatives. A true id field is not sufficient on its own: an inconsistent conjunction
may be identifiable with probability zero, and a conditional query may be undefined when its
conditioning event has zero probability. An adapter therefore retains the requested data level,
identifying formula, returned undefined field and query itself; an inconsistency represented by a
zero formula must retain that meaning. The package paper explains why shared latent variables
connect the counterfactual worlds; treating them as independent simulated populations would
304                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


change the query (Tikka, 2025b, 2023).
   When point identification fails, bounds may still be useful, but their scope is not universal.
causaloptim encodes certain graph-defined response-function problems as linear programs
and permits added constraints; its documented graph attributes and admissible left/right
structure delimit the class. bpbounds implements binary treatment and outcome bounds for
an instrument with two or three categories, in a single trivariate table or a specified two-source
bivariate design, with separate monotonicity outputs. Neither manual claims to deliver a
sampling confidence region for every reported plug-in endpoint. The distinction matters: an
identified set describes values compatible with a population law and assumptions; sampling
uncertainty concerns how an estimator or set varies across repeated samples. A posterior
interval from a separate Bayesian model is different again. The software contract should return
these objects with different types and labels, including empty, unbounded, undefined and
unknown states where relevant (Sachs et al., 2024; Palmer et al., 2026).
   CausalQueries is a useful adjacent tool rather than a substitute for a graphical identification
test. Its documentation defines binary causal models, updates model parameters and supports
queries over priors, parameters or posterior draws. Its query manual calls the default interval
a “confidence interval” under the statistics argument, but names the interval endpoints as
credible summaries and allows a prior or posterior distribution as the input. The proposed
interface must attach the distribution and uncertainty meaning explicitly instead of inheriting
that ambiguous label. Such a posterior answers a question conditional on the declared graph,
response-type parameterization, restrictions, prior and update model. It need not equal a
likelihood-identified set, and a narrow credible interval cannot certify that omitted graphs
or cross-world dependence have been resolved. For the proposed library, the package is a
reference for probabilistic model-query syntax and an optional R adapter candidate. The
described package and its compiled Stan dependencies have not been installed, executed or
cleared for redistribution in this review (Humphreys et al., 2026).


20.44.1     An exact repayment example separates four outputs

Let Y0 , Y1 ∈ {0, 1} be repayment under no reminder and reminder. Randomization identifies
Pr(Y0 = 1) = 1/4 and Pr(Y1 = 1) = 3/4 in this deliberately stipulated population example.
Write qij = Pr(Y0 = i, Y1 = j) and let t = q11 . The observed arm risks imply
