response types with probabilities qij , independently of randomized assignment. This supplies
20.44. Identification software must preserve what is and is not identified                    305


a constructive sharpness argument. The population risks above are stipulated constants;
observing one success versus three in two samples of four would not establish those risks
without sampling uncertainty.
   The same distinction survives Bayesian updating. Consider the three compatible worlds
t ∈ {0, 1/8, 1/4}. With four randomized units in each arm and the stated one-of-four versus
three-of-four successes, the likelihood of the ordered outcomes is (1/4)2 (3/4)6 = 729/65536
in every world. Thus the data do not change their relative weights. A uniform prior on
these three worlds gives posterior mean PN 5/6; prior weights (1/6, 1/3, 1/2) give 7/9. These
are exact project calculations, not output from CausalQueries and not a defect in Bayesian
computation: the difference records prior sensitivity along a likelihood-flat fiber. The aggregate
binomial likelihood is 729/4096 in every world, including the common combinatorial factor.
   For an illustrative retrospective accounting rule, assign USD 1,000 to a responder whose
repayment is attributed to the reminder and subtract USD 800 per responder. The compatible
net amount per responder ranges from 1000(2/3) − 800 = −$400/3 to 1000(1) − 800 = $200.
The two posterior means are USD 1000(5/6)−800 = 100/3 and USD 1000(7/9)−800 = −200/9,
respectively. These stipulated amounts are not observed economics or ROI, and attribution
after the outcome must not be misread as prospective treatment selection on future repayment.
The executable Fraction reference enumerates all three response-type distributions and checks
every displayed likelihood and monetary value (Causal banking research project, 2026be).


20.44.2     Conditional reuse and the boundary of a negative answer

The lending case makes the graph restriction concrete. Suppose unrecorded risk U affects both
the offer A and repayment Y . In a deliberately simple example, take U ∼ Bernoulli(1/2) and
A = U . Two structural models, Y = A and Y = U , give the same observed A = Y distribution,
yet their average effects of intervening on A are respectively one and zero. The graph allowing
U → A, U → Y and A → Y contains both models, because an allowed parent may have zero
effect. No precision of fitting that observed distribution selects the intervention answer. This
is an identification failure relative to that information and graph class. The earlier randomized
example changes the information and identifies the average effect, while leaving cross-world
attribution ambiguous.
   For this use, the proposed adapter result retains three epistemic states: identified with a
functional or point; not identified by a complete algorithm for its declared graph/data class;
and unknown because the class is unsupported or computation ended before a certificate.
Invalid input is a separate validation failure, with no scientific conclusion. Sharp identified
sets, sampling confidence sets and Bayesian posterior summaries have separately named result
types and assumptions. A zero-probability conditioning event is an undefined query, not a
negative identification certificate.
   The practical proposal is to retain causaleffect as a candidate symbolic R service and cfid
as a counterfactual-query service, preserving their query objects and derivations. dosearch
complements those services for multiple source distributions, but an adapter must record
admitted search rules and termination before interpreting a negative result. Disabling a time
limit does not make an incomplete rule system complete. Porting any of these algorithms
requires an independently checked mathematical contract and differential fixtures; matching a
formatted expression alone would miss a changed conditioning event or data level. For that
reason direct source ports are deferred while optional process-bound R adapters are designed.
This is a proposed interface boundary, not an executed integration or a conclusion about
license compatibility (Tikka, 2025a,b; Tikka et al., 2025).
  The restricted bounds engines offer a different reuse choice. causaloptim is a candidate
306                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


optimization reference when its response-function class is appropriate; bpbounds supplies a
smaller binary-IV reference with explicit monotonicity and two-source assumptions. The
proposal rejects either as a universal sharp-bounds backend. It retains CausalQueries as
an optional model-query path when priors and sensitivity are substantively justified, while
rejecting a posterior interval as a replacement for identification. Dependency and license
observations inform these choices but do not qualify redistribution, linked dependencies,
numerical behavior or installed package execution (Sachs et al., 2024; Palmer et al., 2026;
Humphreys et al., 2026).
   These comparisons establish distinct candidate roles and failure semantics. Coverage of
the wider R ecosystem remains incomplete; selected packages and their inspected versions do
not exhaust the available methods. The exact examples establish the stated mathematical
distinctions and illustrative accounting consequences, while implementation and broader source
coverage remain future work.


20.45      Preserve the adjustment question across the DAGitty
           wrapper
A bank analyst who supplies a causal diagram still needs to specify which intervention and
outcome the diagram is meant to relate. A graph editor, a test of an adjustment set, an
enumeration of such sets and an estimator of an effect answer different questions. Our proposed
use of DAGitty is deliberately narrow: a supplied observed directed acyclic graph, one exposure,
one outcome and a total-effect adjustment query. The proposed first implementation would
call a pinned original-language R wrapper and preserve its graph and query semantics. This is
a proposal selection, not an installed adapter or a claim that the bank’s supplied arrows are
true. (jtextor/dagitty contributors, 2024b)
   The selected repository commit is dated 6 December 2024; its R description declares version
0.3-4 and date 7 December 2023. Those dates identify the inspected historical source and do
not establish present support. The README describes the shared JavaScript core and the
R/V8 boundary. The R adjustment entry points check that exposure and outcome variables
are supplied and stop with an error if either is absent. The inspected JavaScript Boolean check
instead returns false in that case. An application that interprets every false as a scientific
finding that adjustment is impossible would turn a missing question into a causal conclusion.
The adapter must validate the question before interpreting the upstream value. (jtextor/dagitty
contributors, 2024b)
   For a complete supported query, three distinct outputs remain necessary. A valid empty
covariate set means no adjustment is required; an empty collection of valid sets means
that this adjustment search supplied none; an incomplete search or invalid request remains
unresolved. In particular, {∅} and ∅ have different meanings. The first contains one set and
the second contains none. Even an exhaustive failure to find an adjustment set does not exclude
identification through a method outside covariate adjustment. The documented max.results
argument caps minimal-set enumeration. A capped listing cannot be reported as a list of all
valid choices, and an interrupted or unqualified computation cannot be promoted to a proof of
nonidentification. These distinctions belong in the returned result and its completeness field.
(jtextor/dagitty contributors, 2024b)

20.45.2     Choose a runtime boundary without erasing graph uncertainty

The wrapper documents graph classes beyond observed DAGs, but the proposed first admission
does not inherit every advertised class. The inspected JavaScript validation code leaves proper
MAG/PAG validation as a TODO, and the inspected pagToPdag transformation changes
endpoint marks and graph type. Replacing a partial ancestral graph by a directed representation
may discard the ambiguity relevant to an intervention. A future extension must preserve
endpoint marks, latent and selection meanings, class validity and the scope of the adjustment
308                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


criterion. Syntax acceptance alone does not supply those guarantees. Restricting the initial
adapter to an observed DAG keeps this unresolved composition visible. (jtextor/dagitty
contributors, 2024b)
   Original-language reuse is preferred to an immediate port because it gives a concrete
comparison surface: parse the same supplied graph, validate the same query, and compare
typed adjustment results against independent finite references. This is an engineering rationale,
not evidence that a wrapper already conforms. A direct JavaScript integration remains an
alternative when its preconditions and packaging are independently qualified; a port would
additionally need algorithmic equivalence, graph-class preservation and a maintenance plan.
Browser editing can support human review, but it does not establish that a discovered or
expert-supplied diagram is causal. No browser, R, Node or upstream test execution supports
the current choice. (jtextor/dagitty contributors, 2024b)
   Rights also follow the selected components. The root contains GPL version 2 text; the R
description declares GPL-2; one inspected helper has a GPL version 2-or-later header, and
other helpers declare MIT terms. The tree contains vendored Underscore versions 1.8.3 and
1.13.1 and a separate test dependency range. Those observations do not establish which copy a
proposed runtime loads, a vulnerability, or a complete transitive-rights inventory. The release
artifact, dependency resolution, notices, intended distribution and source obligations must be
examined together. Neither a separate process nor a public download alone settles the rights

admission deferred until that bounded trial and rights review are complete. (jtextor/dagitty

20.46      Python identification:                the question determines the
           reusable capability
A lending analyst may ask whether changing an offer improves average repayment, or whether
a particular customer who failed to repay would have succeeded under another offer. These
questions share variables but require different information. Let A be a binary intervention and
Y (a) the repayment outcome under its assignment to a. An average contrast E{Y (1) − Y (0)}
uses two marginal intervention distributions. The retrospective question P {Y (1) = 1 | A =
0, Y = 0} also links the factual outcome to that person’s unobserved outcome under another
assignment. A package capable of computing the first quantity does not thereby identify
the second. Nor does a representation of a counterfactual variable establish an algorithm for
identifying its law. The distinction changes the proposed product boundary: a request must
state its query class and available information before an engine is selected. (y0 contributors,
2026b; Causal banking proposal project, 2026w)


20.46.1    Four complementary source boundaries

The inspected DoWhy revision separates model specification, identification and estimation. Its
identification method chooses between an ID identifier and an automatic identifier. It can also
construct a graph from supplied inputs, so the proposed banking route requires an explicit
reviewed graph instead of treating that convenience as elicitation evidence. In the selected
revision, the function assigns the proceed_when_unidentifiable option but does not forward
it to either identifier; validation must inspect the returned estimand and assumptions. This
is a static source finding, not a demonstrated runtime failure. Optional reuse of the pinned
identification boundary remains the preferred initial path; the GCM counterfactual interfaces
20.46. Python identification: the question determines the reusable capability                  309


require a separate review of their structural assumptions and factual-noise reconstruction.
(PyWhy contributors, 2026a)
   The selected pgmpy adjustment interface offers a narrower complementary role: generation
of candidate sets for a specified exposure and outcome. Candidate generation must be followed
by independent causal validation. The reviewed implementation checks exposure parents
in a way that can accept a supplied mediator set when the exposure has no parents; its
minimal_variance branch is advertised but raises NotImplementedError. An adapter must
exclude that branch and validate the chosen total-effect adjustment criterion. Neither a minimal
separator nor a successful role check guarantees a globally minimum-variance adjustment
set. These restrictions do not establish anything about uninspected pgmpy modules.(pgmpy
contributors, 2026a)
   The pinned y0 implementation gives a symbolic ADMG identification route. Its conditional
algorithm invokes a rule-2 exchange test and otherwise normalizes an identified joint distribution.
The inspected separation path has the previously developed bidirected-collider counterexample:
conditioning on the collider can give probability 9/10, whereas replacing the relevant variable
by intervention gives 1/2. The proposed native conditional path therefore remains disabled.
Identifying the joint distribution and then normalizing is a possible restricted alternative
when that joint is identified and its denominator is positive. This sufficient route is not a
completeness claim for conditional identification: failure to identify the entire joint does not
prove failure to identify a particular conditional target. (y0 contributors, 2026d,e,h,i; Causal
banking research project, 2026am)
   Ananke adds a differently organized source reference. The selected authentic ananke-causal
0.5.0 distribution was uploaded on 5 December 2023; it is not presented as the newest release.
Its OneLineID object fixes intervention vertices, finds relevant outcome ancestors and checks
whether each district’s kernel can be obtained by fixing other vertices. The id() method
returns a Boolean. The functional() method returns a string describing the fixing expression
and prints fixing-order diagnostics. That string is not yet a typed portable expression, a fitted
estimator or an uncertainty statement. Proposed reuse would preserve variable identities,
sums, products and fixing operations in a restricted expression representation; it would never
evaluate arbitrary returned text as program code. (Ananke community, 2023f; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026w)
   Ananke’s experimental identification variants also show why exception names cannot be
the scientific result contract. OneLineAID raises NotIdentifiedError when the experimental
graphs fail its ancestral precondition; OneLineGID uses the same exception for nonconform-
ing experimental graphs. A precondition failure must be distinguished from a valid query
proved nonidentified in a declared model class. The source’s supplied-model witness routines
compare observational marginals and interventional distributions of two supplied models.
They do not establish automatic witness construction for every query or arbitrary cross-world
identification.(Ananke community, 2023f)
    Other Ananke components answer different questions. Its oracle intervenes in a sup-
plied true model and explicitly states that identification is not considered. Conditional
normalization inside that oracle cannot be cited as identification from observed data. The
missing-data routine addresses full-law identification with explicit R_ and X_ naming and
colluding-path checks. The CausalEffect estimation interface targets the average contrast
E{Y (1) − Y (0)} and selects among adjustment-, primal- and nested-fixability strategies. A
file named counterfactual_mean.py is therefore evidence about that average-effect interface,
not a guarantee for a customer’s joint potential outcomes.(Ananke community, 2023g,e,c)

20.46.2    What even a randomized study leaves undetermined

Consider an exact illustrative population, rather than a fitted bank dataset. Let A and a
latent response type U be independent fair binary variables, and impose consistency Y = Y (A)
and no interference. In the stable model Y (0) = U and Y (1) = U . In the switching model
Y (0) = U and Y (1) = 1 − U . Both are compatible with an allowed A → Y causal model when
faithfulness is not imposed. The first has no individual response to assignment; in the second,
improvements and harms cancel in the mean. Direct enumeration gives

                       P {Y (0) = 1} = P {Y (1) = 1} = 12 ,                                  (20.33)

   Suppose, solely to interpret the target, a successful recovery is worth USD400 and changing

action, available history and outcome horizon. The example motivates a refusal or an explicit
identified set, not hindsight-based deployment.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026x)
   Additional scientific restrictions can change the answer. Monotonicity Y (1) ≥ Y (0) rules
out the harmed response type, so p10 = t = 0 under these equal marginals. It then forces the
stable coupling. Randomization alone does not supply that restriction. Repeated observations,
20.46. Python identification: the question determines the reusable capability                 311


mechanistic evidence or a richer structural model would have to justify their own connection
across worlds and time; simply collecting more independent assignments does not reveal both
incompatible assignments for the same occasion. The proposed service must record the added
assumption and its scientific owner before narrowing the set.(Causal banking proposal project,
2026x,w)


20.46.3     Integration choices follow semantics and dependency constraints

The reuse proposal is deliberately component-specific. DoWhy supplies a candidate explicit-
graph identification boundary. pgmpy supplies candidate adjustment sets with independent
admissibility checks. y0 supplies a candidate symbolic ID route, with its native conditional
path excluded pending a separation repair. Ananke supplies a district-fixing reference and a
possible isolated comparator. Directly adopting all four packages would not create one uniform
counterfactual service. Porting their source would transfer symbolic, graph and maintenance
obligations to this project without a demonstrated deployment advantage; it is not selected
initially. (PyWhy contributors, 2026a; pgmpy contributors, 2026a; y0 contributors, 2026d;
Ananke community, 2023f; Causal banking proposal project, 2026w)
   There is also a concrete environment conflict. The selected Ananke release declares NumPy
at least1.23 and below2, statsmodels at least0.13.2 and below0.14, and pgmpy at least0.1.21
and below0.2. The selected DoWhy revision requires NumPy above2 and statsmodels at
least0.14; the selected pgmpy revision declares NumPy at least2 and statsmodels at least0.14.5.
These declared intervals cannot all be satisfied in one unchanged environment. Separate pinned
processes communicating through a named-variable result contract are a design option, not
a tested environment resolution. Ananke also imports Sympy in the identification source
without explicitly declaring it in the inspected wheel metadata; whether a resolved transitive
dependency supplies it remains to be checked. No import failure has been observed here.
(Ananke community, 2023d,f; PyWhy contributors, 2026c; pgmpy contributors, 2026a)
    The proposed boundary validates cycles, node identity, edge type, latent status and experi-
mental preconditions before dispatch. Ananke’s graph constructor contains segregation and
cycle checks, but their presence and the nearby correctness TODO do not constitute either a
qualification or a demonstrated defect. Engine diagnostics are retained separately from scien-
tific disposition. An identified expression, an identified set, a model-specific nonidentification
result, an unsupported question, invalid input and an engine failure remain distinct outcomes.
An empty valid adjustment set must not become a failed query, and an exception must not
become a proved impossibility. (Ananke community, 2023a,f; Causal banking proposal project,
2026w)
   Rights are similarly tied to the actual component and distribution. The selected DoWhy
source carries MIT text and y0 carries BSD three-clause text. The Ananke archive contains two
byte-identical Apache2.0 license files, while its metadata also includes an Other/Proprietary
classifier. The conflicting declarations remain visible for distribution review rather than being
silently resolved by a package badge. Notice retention, modified-file marking where applicable
and dependency-specific obligations belong in the selected distribution design. Process sepa-
ration does not settle those questions. (PyWhy contributors, 2026b; y0 contributors, 2026f;
Ananke community, 2023b,d)
  This comparison leaves explicit survey work. DoWhy’s GCM counterfactual paths, imple-
mentations of general counterfactual identification and Python partial-identification optimizers
need their own authenticated technical sources, model classes and output checks. A solver
would need to distinguish a feasible witness from a certified sharp endpoint; a counterfactual
engine would need to state what structural information permits abduction and coupling. The
312                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


four inspected families support the bounded reuse choices described here. They do not establish
exhaustive Python coverage, installed adapters or qualified banking decisions.(Causal banking
proposal project, 2026w)


20.47      Java identification requires a typed scientific result
A lending analyst may ask whether approving a loan changes repayment, or whether a particular
declined borrower would have repaid if approved. Those questions differ from updating a
supplied Bayesian network after observing borrower attributes. They also differ from collecting
regression coefficients over possible graph orientations. A Java integration must preserve these
distinctions before it exposes a probability or an effect. Interface names alone cannot determine
the scientific contract.
   The selected Tetrad source, version 7.6.11-SNAPSHOT at preserved revision b89afaf952a4,
contains an Identifiability interface in addition to Ida and PdagPagIda. The identification
implementation constructs c-components and Q-expressions and evaluates them using an
observational joint-probability representation. It is a distinct candidate from continuous-data
effect enumeration. The source header names a 2002 algorithm report, but the report’s proof
has not been inspected for this comparison. Code observations establish interface and failure-
path requirements; they do not establish theorem completeness or unrestricted latent-variable
identification. Nine selected original files support a bounded Tetrad comparison, not an
exhaustive census of Java software.(Tetrad contributors, 2026b)

20.47.1     Observation, intervention and individual counterfactuals

Consider two authored lending mechanisms. Let U be a binary borrower state, A approval, and
Y a binary repayment outcome. Let U have probability 1/2 of being one, and let independent
noise variables N, E each have probability 1/4 of being one. Write ⊕ for exclusive-or and set
                    A = U ⊕ N,        M1 : Y = U,        M2 : Y = A ⊕ E.                  (20.37)
Both mechanisms are compatible with the allowed supergraph U → A, U → Y , A → Y
when an allowed arrow may have zero functional effect. This construction does not impose
faithfulness. Both yield the same strictly positive observed joint law,
                             Y =0 Y =1
                     A=0      3/8  1/8 ,           P (Y = 1 | A = 1) = 3/4.               (20.38)
                     A=1      1/8  3/8
Nevertheless, the intervention risks are (1/2, 1/2) in M1 and (1/4, 3/4) in M2 , ordered by
approval zero and one. Their average causal effects are zero and 1/2. The positive observed
law does not select one of these effects under the declared model class. These are two explicit
witnesses to nonuniqueness, not an enumeration of a sharp identified set. A conditional
probability cannot be relabeled as an intervention risk merely because both are between zero
and one.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ag)
   For a purely illustrative monetary conversion, stipulate USD 200 per unit increase in
repayment probability and an approval-action cost of USD 20. The two mechanisms give
incremental net values
      200{E[Y | do(A = 1)] − E[Y | do(A = 0)]} − 20 ∈ {−20, 80} USD per case.             (20.39)
The sign changes without changing the observed joint law. These amounts are stipulated
arithmetic, not loan-pricing evidence, a measured bank return or the valuation of a real
20.47. Java identification requires a typed scientific result                               313


approval policy. Additional causal restrictions or intervention evidence would be needed to
choose a mechanism for decision use. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ag)
   Even marginal intervention risks may not settle an individual counterfactual. In a second
exact construction, let A and U be independent fair binary variables. Compare potential
outcomes (Y (0), Y (1)) = (U, U ) with (Y (0), Y (1)) = (U, 1 − U ). Both generate the uniform
observed distribution over (A, Y ) and both have intervention risks 1/2 for either approval
value. For an observed case with A = 0, Y = 0, however,
                                                    (
                                                      0, (Y (0), Y (1)) = (U, U ),
                P {Y (1) = 1 | A = 0, Y = 0} =                                           (20.40)
                                                      1, (Y (0), Y (1)) = (U, 1 − U ).

The missing information concerns the joint coupling of potential outcomes, which the two
marginal intervention distributions do not supply. An agent translating the business question
must specify whether it asks for a population intervention, conditional intervention or cross-
world event. Substituting a Bayesian conditional for the last answers another question. (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026ag)


20.47.2      The selected updater has a narrower evidence contract

The selected BayesUpdater documentation describes a joint marginal conditional on
evidence. The Identifiability implementation instead comments its target as Pt (s), with
intervention values obtained from its evidence object. Evidence.getVariablesInEvidence
collects variables with a single allowed category without checking manipulation flags.
Identifiability.getJointMarginal uses those variables as interventions and explicitly
assumes they are manipulated. Its separate graph-construction method removes incoming
edges only where manipulation flags are true. Ordinary and manipulated evidence are
therefore not interchangeable merely because they share a container. A first proposed profile
should admit validated singleton interventions and reject mixed evidence until that mismatch
is resolved by a reviewed interface and native tests.(Tetrad contributors, 2026b)
   There is also a subtype obligation. The public constructor accepts BayesIm, but the no-
evidence path and Q-expression evaluator cast it to MlBayesImObs to access the observed
joint-probability table. A generic Bayesian-model object is insufficient evidence that the call
will work. The wrapper must preserve the observed-variable/category mapping and validate
the representation, finite probabilities, normalization and support. The selected probability
setter permits NaN; the Q-expression evaluator computes a reciprocal denominator without a
local zero guard. These observations require numerical and support checks. They do not prove
which end-to-end native inputs produce a nonfinite result.(Tetrad contributors, 2026b)
   Failures need distinct types. A recursive identification failure returns null; the public
joint-marginal path maps that branch to −1. Internal consistency failures throw exceptions,
whereas contradictory target and intervention assignments return the valid probability zero and
removing all target variables returns one. The updated-model getter itself returns null. The
inspected GUI wrapper formats numeric marginals but does not supply a typed identification
certificate in that path. Clamping −1 to zero would fabricate a probability; treating a
null model as a zero effect would confuse object availability with causal meaning. Signed
treatment contrasts are a separate type and can legitimately be negative, so a universal
negative-means-failure rule would also be wrong.(Tetrad contributors, 2026b)
314                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


20.47.3     An effect list is not a confidence set

The IDA-related interfaces need separate graph and sampling contracts. The PdagPagIda
documentation mentions PAGs, but its constructor checks for a legal DAG or PDAG and
continuous data. A nearby comment says that the rPAG-IDA route is disabled because it still
needs work. A class name, dormant branch or broader comment cannot admit a PAG-only
input. Fully oriented graphs may satisfy more than one graph predicate; the observation is the
actual guard, not a categorical claim about every object labeled a PAG. (Tetrad contributors,
2026b)
   Candidate failures complicate interpretation. In a selected optimal-adjustment branch, an
exception can append zero and continue. An outer handler instead logs an error and omits a
candidate. A returned zero or shortened list cannot automatically certify a structural zero
or exhaustive graph-compatible effect enumeration. A proposed adapter should retain every
attempted candidate with its graph, adjustment set, regression status and exclusion reason,
and refuse scientific publication when failures collapse into values. This source-level observation
is neither a native reproduction nor a claim that every call fails. (Tetrad contributors, 2026b)
   The distance functions show another distinction. For candidates {−2, 2} and target zero,
finite-set distance is two, whereas distance to the interval hull [−2, 2] is zero. The selected code
uses the extreme range for multiple candidates. For an empty list it returns the target value
itself, so target minus one yields minus one rather than a valid nonnegative distance. These
source-branch examples require an explicit empty status and an accurately named metric.
Neither an effect list nor its hull is a calibrated confidence region without an argument for
graph uncertainty, sampling error and observation law. (Tetrad contributors, 2026b; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026ag)


20.47.4     A proposal route with explicit unresolved obligations

The proposed Java schema separates graph and probability inputs, singleton interventions,
ordinary evidence, query variables and cross-world conditioning. Its output distinguishes a com-
pleted identified query, a reviewed nonidentification certificate, unknown scope, unsupported
input, and execution or numerical failure. The source’s −1 branch must not be upgraded
to a universal nonidentification certificate before the algorithm’s assumptions and proof are
reviewed. The original-language engine remains a candidate; no port, native qualification or
distribution permission follows from this comparison.
   The remaining public research must inspect the named algorithm original, graph-legality and
probability-storage helpers, and other Java candidates under a recorded search boundary. It
must establish whether conditional ID, general counterfactual or partial-identification queries
have actual supported interfaces, rather than infer absence from selected files. A later admitted
native prototype can test subtypes, manipulation flags, failure sentinels, zero support, nonfinite
values, skipped candidates and graph guards against the exact references. R and Python
symbolic engines are distinct comparators with their own graph and failure contracts. These
tasks can use public sources and synthetic laws without requiring authentic bank data to
clarify the proposal.
20.48. Julia and JavaScript: preserving the meaning of an identification request             315


20.48       Julia and JavaScript: preserving the meaning of an
            identification request
A bank deciding whether to make a lending-support offer must distinguish a graphical search
from an answer about repayment. A set of variables may justify one adjustment formula
without providing its numerical value. Conversely, failure to find such a set need not rule out a
different identifying formula. An interface that turns both outcomes into an empty array loses
information precisely where a business user needs an explanation. Julia’s CausalInference.jl
and the JavaScript core of DAGitty expose useful graph operations, but their selected inter-
faces require different conversions. The inspected Julia commit of 10 August 2026 declares
version 0.19.4; the JavaScript revision is dated 6 December 2024. These immutable source
identities define the comparison, rather than an assumed correspondence with an installed
release.(CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026; DAGitty contributors, 2026)


20.48.1     The graph operation, the observable variables and the target

Write A for the binary offer, M for a subsequent customer response and Y for a binary
repayment outcome. An unobserved factor U may influence both offer assignment and
repayment. A graphical intervention deletes the incoming arrows to A; evaluating P (Y |
do(A = a)) additionally needs a model or an identified functional of an observed law. The
selected Julia do! method performs the former operation: it removes incoming edges and
returns the modified graph. Its name alone therefore cannot justify a numerical intervention
answer.(CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026)
   The inspected adjustment searches expose a mandatory set I and an allowed set R. Their
intended result is a set Z satisfying I ⊆ Z ⊆ R and the selected graphical criterion. The
default R contains all nonendpoint vertices. This is convenient for a fully observed graph,
but a banking graph often contains expert-specified unobserved variables. Such vertices must
be excluded from the permitted controls: a mathematically useful hidden variable is not an
available data column. The package’s example explicitly removes two unobserved vertices
from R, and its selected tests include the corresponding restricted enumeration. These are
inspected examples and test assertions, not tests executed in this proposal.(CausalInference.jl
contributors, 2026)
  For the proposed boundary, observed status is consequently part of the request, not an
optional display annotation. A request must also retain the outcome horizon, whether M is
pre-action or post-action, and the distinction between a total, direct or path-specific effect. A
proposed control set that contains an unavailable variable is refused before estimation. An
analyst cannot silently replace a missing pre-action cause by a post-action response and retain
the original estimand. The following exact construction makes the monetary cost of such a
substitution explicit.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ah)


20.48.2     A positive-law lending example with three different answers

Consider the project-authored structural law

                    U ∼ Bernoulli(1/2),              P (A = 1 | U ) = 14 + 21 U,
       P (M = 1 | A) = 41 + 12 A,                P (Y = 1 | M, U ) = 18 + 21 M + 14 U.   (20.41)

The structural randomizations are independent. The graph is U → A, U → Y , A → M → Y ;
it has no direct A → Y arrow and no hidden common cause of A and M . Every joint cell has
positive probability. This is a stipulated mechanism, not a fitted loan portfolio. It supplies a
316                                                                 Causal analysis for a universal bank


transparent exact reference against which a later adapter can be compared.(Causal banking
proposal project, 2026ah)
  Under intervention, U retains its fair marginal distribution while the law of M is set by a.
Thus direct structural enumeration gives

                r(a) = P (Y = 1 | do(A = a)) = 81 + 12 ( 14 + 21 a) + 14 12 = 38 + 41 a.        (20.42)

The interventional risks are 3/8 and 5/8, with effect 1/4. In the observed law, Bayes’ rule
instead gives P (U = 1 | A = a) = 1/4 + a/2. Hence P (Y = 1 | A = a) = 5/16 + 3a/8: the
observed risks are 5/16 and 11/16, with contrast 3/8. The observed comparison mixes the
offer response with selection on U .(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ah)
  The frontdoor expression evaluated from this law is
                                    X               X
                          f (a) =       P (m | a)       P (Y = 1 | b, m)P (b).                  (20.43)
                                    m               b

Here U and M are conditionally independent given A. Therefore P (Y = 1 | b, m) = 3/16 +
m/2 + b/8 and P (b) = 1/2. The inner average is 1/4 + m/2, so f (a) = 3/8 + a/4 = r(a). This
verifies the expression for the stipulated law. It is not a proof of a general frontdoor theorem,
a completeness claim for the selected software, or an upstream execution. The proof originals
named by the source remain separate inspection obligations. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026ah; CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026)
  Using M as an ordinary standardization control gives a third answer. Its marginal success
probability is P (M = 1) = 1/2, so
                                    X
                                                                7
                           h(a) =       P (Y = 1 | a, m)P (m) = 16 + 81 a.                      (20.44)
                                    m

The resulting contrast is 1/8, not 1/4. It is neither the total-effect answer nor a justified
direct-effect answer merely because the mediator has been included as a control. In the graph,
the empty set leaves A ← U → Y open, and the only observed nonendpoint candidate M does
not block that backdoor path. The absence of a permitted backdoor set therefore coexists, in
this example, with the successful expression (20.43).(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ah)
  For an assumed incremental success payoff of USD 100 and an offer cost of USD 20, the
three contrasts imply

      100(1/4) − 20 = 5,        100(3/8) − 20 = 35/2,            100(1/8) − 20 = −15/2.         (20.45)

The same positive observed law can thus tempt a user to overstate the proposed offer value
as USD 17.50 or to reject it at USD −7.50, whereas the stipulated intervention has value
USD 5. These are assumed-money consequences of query semantics, not observed profits,
estimated confidence intervals or an investment recommendation. Sampling uncertainty and
the credibility of the graph would still require separate analysis.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ah)


20.48.3    A failed search needs a reason and a completion status

The Julia find methods return a set or false; their enumeration iterator returns nothing
when exhausted and declares an unknown iterator size. One empty set is a valid candidate
distinct from an enumeration that emits no sets. The inspected find_backdoor_adjustment
path passes the result of find_covariate_adjustment directly into setdiff, without an
explicit local guard for false. This is a specific native conformance question, not a reproduced
20.48. Julia and JavaScript: preserving the meaning of an identification request             317


exception. A future wrapper must preserve an error as an error rather than converting it to
scientific nonidentification.(CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026)
   DAGitty illustrates why a single Boolean or list cannot carry the full contract. Its selected
total-adjustment path admits DAG, PDAG, MAG and PAG tags, whereas its direct-effect
check restricts the graph to a DAG and rejects selection nodes. Missing source or target
markings, an invalid adjustment set, and selected failures of adjustment or selection conditions
can produce false or an empty list through different interfaces. Its total-effect enumeration
retains latent and selection annotations and accepts a maximum result count. The selected
MAG/PAG validation branches themselves retain comments that proper validation is unfinished.
Acceptance of a graph tag must therefore not be promoted into validation of every scientific
premise. (DAGitty contributors, 2026)
   The proposed shared result has separate fields for request validity, graph profile, search
criterion, emitted solutions, completion and scientific conclusion. A budget-limited result
preserves every emitted set and reports incomplete or unknown completion. Reaching a cap
does not by itself prove that another solution exists; nor does it certify exhaustiveness. A
valid completed adjustment search can support “no route under this adjustment criterion.” A
general “not identified” conclusion instead needs an applicable reviewed certificate. A missing
endpoint, unsupported graph, implementation exception or unverified proof premise remains
a different outcome. None defaults to a zero effect.(CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026;
DAGitty contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ah)


20.48.4     A narrow adoption route and the questions it leaves open

A first prototype can use a narrow declared DAG profile with explicit observed vertices, disjoint
query sets, validated I ⊆ R, and an exact enumeration oracle on small graphs. It should test
a valid empty adjustment set, no permitted adjustment set with a separate frontdoor route,
an invalid mandatory set, a hidden candidate, missing endpoints, invalid graph marks and a
deliberately capped enumeration. Compare sets independently of order and retain completion
separately from the count. Execute pinned upstream tests only after recording the native
environment and distribution; their presence in a repository is useful evidence of intended
behavior, not a passing local run. (CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026; DAGitty contributors,
2026)
   The Julia metadata supplies dependency ranges and an MIT notice, rather than a fully
resolved distribution. The JavaScript candidate retains the component and dependency review
obligations already identified in its reuse comparison. An adapter boundary is a candidate
for evaluation, while a wholesale port would additionally require maintained correspondence
with the original algorithms and tests. A source-level convenience is not sufficient reason
to incur that maintenance burden. No executable integration permission is awarded by this
comparison.(CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026; DAGitty contributors, 2026)
   Three unresolved tasks remain distinct. Broader language and package discovery is needed
before claiming coverage. The source-linked adjustment, frontdoor and path-specific originals
require genuine PDF acquisition and inspection before their general guarantees are cited.
Finally, native failure behavior, graph validation and distribution correspondence need a
separately reviewed prototype. The recanting-witness helper concerns a specified path-specific
question under complete observations; its name is not evidence of arbitrary latent or cross-
world identification. Public graph fixtures and stipulated laws can address these prototype
questions before any expensive bank trial. Authentic assignment knowledge, outcome truth and
institutional acceptance remain later evidence.(CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026; DAGitty
contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ah)
Chapter 21

Effect estimation, heterogeneous
actions and threshold comparisons

A servicing team may want to know the value of offering assistance to every eligible account,
the value among accounts already receiving assistance, or the value in the population where
receipt remains uncertain. Those questions need not have the same answer. Nor does learning
a large conditional benefit identify the best use of a scarce specialist team. A threshold
experiment can support a local comparison while leaving the portfolio decision unresolved.
The proposal therefore needs a vocabulary for comparing estimators through their population,
uncertainty and decision consequences.
   This chapter develops three connections: assignment-dependent populations and orthogonal
estimation; joint heterogeneous comparisons and resource allocation; and threshold identifica-
tion versus finite approximation. The numerical laws are stipulated, reproducible examples in
USD per eligible account over a fixed thirty-day horizon. They establish algebra and decision
consequences under those laws. They are neither bank observations nor new executions of the
external software discussed below.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)


21.1     The population can depend on the assignment mechanism
Let O = (X, A, Y ) denote one independent account observation, where X is information
available before a binary action A, and Y is the subsequent monetary outcome. Assume
consistency, no interference, conditional exchangeability of the two potential outcomes given
X, and positive probabilities for both actions on the population being studied. These are
scientific restrictions; fitting a flexible regression does not verify them. Define

 e(x) = P (A = 1 | X = x),        ma (x) = E(Y | A = a, X = x),     τ (x) = m1 (x) − m0 (x).

Throughout the following derivations, the moments exist and the denominators are nonzero.
Uniform overlap and suitable higher moments will be imposed when an asymptotic variance or
remainder bound needs them.
  A useful family of targets is

P (A = 1)E{f (X) | A = 1}. Overlap weighting emphasizes accounts with uncertain receipt; it

does not estimate the value of treating every account. The bank must decide whether that

overlap weight as fixed in a variance calculation can discard a component of uncertainty. A
randomized experiment with a known, fixed assignment design is yet another model: its allowed
perturbations do not include arbitrary changes to that assignment law. The relevant derivative
must match the model being claimed.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce; Chernozhukov et al.,

                     E(N − θh D) = E δ 2 (τ − θh ) + δ{qδ1 + (1 − q)δ0 } .                  (21.6)

For example, the coefficient on δ1 before simplification is E(D | X) − e(1 − q) = q(q − e); the
coefficient on δ0 is −E(D | X) + (1 − e)q = (1 − q)(q − e). These identities explain both the
second-order propensity term and the product term. The population fitted ratio differs from
θh by the second line divided by H + Eδ 2 .(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
  If q = e, the remainder vanishes even with inaccurate arm means. If the arm means
are correct but q is arbitrary, the first term generally remains. Thus this corrected overlap
construction is locally orthogonal while lacking global double robustness in that second direction.
For a fixed external weight and an ATE-style augmented score, the usual product remainder is
a different calculation. The word “augmented” cannot resolve the distinction.
   Under bounded τ − θh and fitted probabilities in [0, 1], a bound on the absolute numerator
error is
               ∥τ − θh ∥∞ ∥q − e∥22 + ∥q − e∥2 {∥m
                                                 b 1 − m1 ∥2 + ∥mb 0 − m0 ∥2 }.

Sufficient conditions for this bound to be op (n−1/2 ) include a squared-propensity-error condition
and a propensity/outcome product-rate condition, with a denominator bounded away from
zero. An asymptotic linear expansion also needs control of the fitted score in L2 , moments, and
the fold evaluation terms. Cross-fitting addresses training/evaluation dependence; it neither
proves those rates nor supplies exchangeability. The conditions in the DML paper similarly
accompany its own specified scores and statistical model. They are not a theorem for an
arbitrary callable score.(Chernozhukov et al., 2018; Bach et al., 2022)
21.3. Clipping, population change and apparent precision                                      321


   In a bank proposal these conditions create a useful design decision. An overlap target
can avoid assigning large inverse weights to nearly deterministic receipt, but the target itself
uses the receipt mechanism. An independently specified segment can have a simpler fixed-
weight target while retaining difficult support. Neither option makes the scientific population
choice unnecessary. The appropriate comparison holds the target fixed first and then studies
estimation error, rather than treating every numerically stable answer as an improvement.


21.3     Clipping, population change and apparent precision
Consider three pre-action strata with the following exact law:
                       X    P (X) e(X) m0 (X) (USD) τ (X) (USD)
                       1      1/4 1/10           30          −4
                       2      1/2  1/2           50           4
                       3      1/4 9/10           70          20
Within each stratum the action is generated independently of potential outcomes. The ATE is
6, ATT is 54/5, and ATC is 6/5 USD. Those basic target differences motivate the example;
the new issue is what fitted weight changes do to its score and uncertainty. The true overlap
mass is H = 17/100, giving θh = 86/17 USD. True-propensity trimming to [1/5, 4/5] retains
only the middle stratum and gives 4 USD. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
   Now clip the two extreme propensities to obtain q = (1/5, 1/2, 4/5). The unnormalized
plain inverse-weighted contrast
                                             AY   (1 − A)Y
                                                            
                                     E          −
                                              q     1−q
equals 107/8 USD, despite an ATE of 6. Its coefficients on baseline outcome levels no longer
cancel in each stratum. This is a population calculation, so more observations do not remove
the discrepancy. An ATE augmented score with correct arm means still gives 6; its residual
terms have conditional mean zero. That result does not apply to every weighted target simply
because the same fitted q is used.
   If one instead freezes the weights q(1 − q) and averages the true effects, the target is 228/41
USD. The corrected overlap ratio in Equation (21.5), still using correct arm means, gives 36/7
USD. Its bias relative to the true overlap effect is 10/119. All four quantities—ATE, true
overlap, frozen fitted-weight average and corrected fitted ratio—can be estimated precisely
while answering different questions. With the stipulated arm-mean errors δ1 = (1, −2, 3)
and δ0 = (−1, 1, 2) USD, the corrected ratio’s unnormalized error is −239/3400 USD and
its denominator is 7/40; the normalized error is −239/595 USD. The exact decomposition
therefore checks the sign and size of a genuine product remainder, rather than merely showing
that a program terminates.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
   The familiar effective-sample-size diagnostic can also look better after clipping. For the
treated weight W = A/q(X), its population analogue is
                                      ESS    {E(W )}2
                                          −→          .
                                       n      E(W 2 )
Under the true propensity it is 9/34; under the clipped propensity it is 841/2024. The larger
second fraction measures concentration of those weights. It neither proves target preservation
nor yields an outcome-specific standard error: outcome noise, effect heterogeneity and fitted-
score error still matter. A self-normalized estimator would be a further algorithm with its own
population ratio, not a justification for the unnormalized contrast used above.
322                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


  The assignment derivative can be checked directly in this same law. Perturb the three
propensities by t(1/20, −1/10, 1/20), holding stratum masses and outcome laws fixed. The
ATT derivative is 27/50 USD per unit t and the overlap-effect derivative is −24/17. The
covariance of the first line of Equation (21.2) alone with the assignment score is zero; the
complete influence function gives exactly these derivatives. Mean zero of a candidate influence
function is therefore insufficient. The derivative test detects what a simple centering test
misses.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)


21.4     Selected software paths embody different estimators
The inspected DoubleML paper describes linear score architecture and model-specific nuisance
estimation, with extension routes for callable scores and sample splitting. The inherited local
execution used the selected IRM ATE path in version 0.11.4, released 10 August 2026, with
externally supplied nuisances and folds, no IPW normalization and truncation at 0.01. That
is evidence for its recorded operation only. The inspected source adjusts fitted propensities
before score evaluation. Changing truncation, target or callable score would require a new
comparison, including the remainder appropriate to that functional.(Bach et al., 2022; doubleml
contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026cf)
   The pinned R grf implementation takes a different route for its binary-treatment overlap
target. Its average-effect source fits a regression of outcome residuals on treatment residuals,
with an intercept, and uses a heteroskedastic or cluster sandwich calculation. It does not
simply run the all-population AIPW average with another averaging weight. At true nuisance
functions, write µ(X) = E(Y | X) and Y − µ = (A − e)τ + ε, with E(ε | A, X) = 0. The
residual-regression slope is

                            E{(A − e)(Y − µ)}   E{e(1 − e)τ }
                                        2
                                              =               .
                              E{(A − e) }            H

Because both residuals have mean zero at truth, an intercept does not change this population
slope. Its first-order residual-regression influence function at truth is

                                 (A − e)2 (τ − θh ) + (A − e)ε
                                                               ,
                                              H
which equals the full overlap influence function in Equation (21.2) for binary A. This algebra
connects the selected implementation to the assignment-dependent target.(GRF contributors,
2026c; Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
  Equality at truth does not make fitted algorithms identical. In the clipped three-stratum
example, retain the true marginal outcome mean µ but use q for treatment residuals. Here
E(A − q) = 0, E(q − e)2 = 1/200, and the residual-regression slope is

                                    E{e(1 − e)τ }    172
                                                 2
                                                   =     .
                                    H + E(q − e)     35

It differs both from the true overlap effect 86/17 and from the corrected ratio 36/7 using
correct arm means. These nuisance specifications are deliberately different: true µ is not the
same fitted object as the two true arm means combined with an incorrect q. The example
shows why a common target and common limiting influence function do not establish finite
fitted equivalence.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
  At revision 5bee99b5, the selected grf source’s overlap branch does not use the method
choice after entering that branch. Earlier guards still reject particular TMLE calls with
21.5. Shared controls make heterogeneous comparisons joint                                  323


clustering or sample weights. Thus “method ignored” must be qualified by control flow. Other
inspected forest types also have restrictions on target and method combinations. An adapter
should validate the exact combination, preserve package diagnostics and record the actual
route used. The generalized-forest paper’s pointwise normality result is conditional on its
assumptions and honest, regular, subsampled forest construction; it does not establish inference
for every selected policy or every fitted forest.(GRF contributors, 2026c,b; Athey et al., 2018)
  These comparisons favor wrapping selected public interfaces before porting their internals.
Reproducing an R or Python score in a common C++ core could eventually reduce interprocess
overhead, but would create an additional statistical implementation to maintain. First establish
the mathematical target, nuisance convention, supported uncertainty unit and failure behavior
on matched examples. Reject unsupported target/method combinations at that boundary. No
current source inspection establishes complete dependency rights or the performance of a new
wrapper.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cc)


21.5     Shared controls make heterogeneous comparisons joint
Suppose the bank can choose no contact, a message or specialist assistance, indexed by
A = 0, 1, 2. Let ej (X) and mj (X) denote action probabilities and arm means. Under the
corresponding multiarm consistency, exchangeability and support assumptions, define every
contrast on the same eligible-account law:

                           θj = E{mj (X) − m0 (X)},          j = 1, 2.

Its population influence function is

                                       1{A = j}             1{A = 0}
                ϕj = τj (X) − θj +              (Y − mj ) −          (Y − m0 ).
                                          ej                   e0

For distinct noncontrol actions j, k, mutually exclusive arm indicators eliminate their outcome-
residual cross-products, but the shared control residual appears twice. Therefore

                    Cov(ϕj , ϕk ) = Cov{τj (X), τk (X)} + E{σ02 (X)/e0 (X)},              (21.7)

where σ02 (X) = Var(Y | A = 0, X). Conditional mean-zero residuals remove the remaining
cross terms. The first term can have either sign; a positive shared-control term does not imply
positive total covariance in every heterogeneous population.
  Take constant effects, assignment probabilities (1/2, 1/4, 1/4), and conditional outcome-noise
variance 4 USD2 in all arms. The influence covariance matrix and variance of the difference are
                                           !
                                  24 8
                           Σ=          ,          Var(ϕ2 − ϕ1 ) = 32.
                                  8 24

Adding marginal variances as though the contrasts were independent would give 48. In this
example the shared control cancels in the difference. For an iid mean, the corresponding
asymptotic covariance is Σ/n; these are not empirical standard errors and are not formulas
for clustered bank histories. Joint confidence regions or multiple-comparison decisions require
an explicitly chosen simultaneous procedure. Two marginal intervals alone do not specify
one.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
  This issue is concrete in the pinned CausalML T-learner path. Its point mean uses the full
prediction covariate matrix, while the inspected analytic variance uses the observations in the
current treatment/control pair. Under unequal assignment or covariate composition, those sets
324                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


can represent different populations. The finding is about the selected revision and path, not a
claim that every CausalML estimator behaves that way. A proposed multiarm wrapper should
standardize every action prediction to one explicit evaluation population, then construct the
joint score and covariance there. It should keep package-specific uncertainty as a separately
named result until equivalence is established.(uber/causalml, 2026; Causal banking proposal,
2026cf)
   The same source offers a row bootstrap. Rows from repeated accounts or a shared calendar
shock are not independent sampling units simply because they have distinct row indices.
Whether the comparator uses independent accounts, households, branches or time blocks
belongs in the statistical specification. A bootstrap setting cannot repair an undeclared unit
or create joint support for an action rarely observed in a subgroup.


21.6      A resource constraint changes the optimal action
Let g(x) = τ (x) − c(x) be the incremental net value of one action, where c(x) includes the
action’s incremental cost in the same USD units and horizon. Let r(x) > 0 be specialist
resource units and let d(x) ∈ [0, 1] be the fraction of that stratum assigned to the action. With
expected resource budget B per eligible account, consider

              max E{g(X)d(X)} subject to         E{r(X)d(X)} ≤ B,        0 ≤ d ≤ 1.         (21.8)
                d

Fractional decisions describe randomization or divisible allocation in this population problem.
They are not a guarantee that a finite day’s integer roster fits a hard capacity constraint.
  For a multiplier λ ≥ 0, every feasible policy obeys the dual bound

                                 E(gd) ≤ λB + E{(g − λr)+ }.                                (21.9)

Indeed, gd = (g − λr)d + λrd and (g − λr)d ≤ (g − λr)+ . Equality is attained if the policy uses
the action wherever g > λr, avoids it wherever g < λr, and allocates any equality stratum to
meet the budget when the multiplier is positive. This is a checkable optimality certificate. It
explains why ranking by effect, or even by net gain without resource units, can be wrong.
  Consider four strata:
                                stratum         1    2   3    4
                                 P (X)        2/5 3/10 1/5 1/10
                           gross effect, USD    4    9 15    25
                        incremental cost, USD   1    3   7   14
                              g(X), USD         3    6   8   11
                              r(X), units       1    1   2    4

Set B = 1/2 unit per eligible account. The policy d = (0, 1, 1/2, 0) uses exactly 1/2 unit and
produces 13/5 USD of net value. At λ = 4 USD per resource unit, the adjusted gains g − λr
are (−1, 2, 0, −5); the dual bound is 4(1/2) + (3/10)2 = 13/5. The feasible allocation therefore
attains the global bound. Sorting by gross effect or by unadjusted net gain fills stratum 4
first and then a quarter of stratum 3, giving d = (0, 0, 1/4, 1) and 3/2 USD. The loss is 11/10
USD per eligible account, even though the ranked effects are known exactly.(Causal banking
proposal, 2026ce)
   This example deliberately separates scientific estimation from operational optimization. The
cost schedule is stipulated, specialist time is a separate constraint, and the value is incremental
relative to no action. If monetary cost already prices the same scarce time, the sponsor must
21.7. From effect error to decision loss                                                         325


explain whether the hard constraint remains necessary and avoid counting the same resource
twice. Risk limits, fairness conditions and action eligibility can further restrict the feasible set.
For indivisible actions on a finite roster, the appropriate optimization can become a knapsack
or assignment problem; the fractional certificate does not assert that a greedy integer solution
is optimal.
   For multiple actions, replace d by dj (x) ≥ 0 with j dj (x) ≤ 1, action-specific gains and
                                                         P

resources. At a fixed multiplier, each account receives the action with the largest positive
gj − λrj , subject to any additional declared constraints. Shared controls and common target
populations remain essential because the optimizer compares these action values directly.
Exporting unrelated pairwise targets to an optimizer can produce a feasible but scientifically
meaningless plan.


21.7      From effect error to decision loss
Prediction error and policy error need not move together. For the same fixed feasible policy class
D, let d∗ maximize E(gd) and db maximize E(gbd). Suppose the pointwise bound |gb − g| ≤ ϵ(X)
is valid. Adding and subtracting the fitted objective gives

                       E{g(d∗ − d)}
                                b = E{(g − gb)(d∗ − d)}
                                                    b + E{gb(d∗ − d)}
                                                                  b

                                      ≤ E{ϵ(X)|d∗ − d|}.
                                                    b                                        (21.10)

The last fitted-objective difference is nonpositive by optimality. If the optimizer is within η
USD of its optimum, add η to the bound. This is a deterministic comparison conditional on
the two gain functions, the common population objective and the same feasible class. It is not
a confidence bound supplied by an arbitrary learner. If the fitted optimizer uses an empirical
objective, a population-to-empirical discrepancy must also be controlled. If costs or capacity
are estimated, their errors can change the feasible set, so this derivation no longer covers them
by itself.
   With 0 ≤ d ≤ 1, a uniform gain-error bound ϵ0 gives the coarse bound ϵ0 per account.
The sharper expression charges error only where the two policies disagree. This explains why
errors near a resource threshold can be more consequential than equally large errors in strata
where the same action remains optimal. A low global squared prediction loss does not alone
demonstrate low constrained decision loss. The finite reference enumerates 81 signed-error
configurations over the binary feasible policies and confirms the inequality, while the algebra
establishes its stated general domain.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
   The observational policy-learning analysis of Athey and Wager (2021) supplies a more
substantive statistical route: construct doubly robust scores and learn within a controlled-
complexity policy class under overlap, noise and nuisance rate conditions. Its regret theorem
is tied to the admitted binary-decision problem and assumptions. It does not automatically
cover every resource constraint, multiarm action, dependent history or optimizer introduced
here. Likewise, a pointwise conditional-effect interval from a forest is not an interval for the
value of a policy selected using the same sample.
   A proposal comparison should therefore split learning and evaluation at the appropriate
independent unit, declare the reference population and feasible class, and evaluate the frozen
selected policy with a justified value score. It should report infeasibility and inability to
estimate value as outcomes. An exact reference can verify the optimizer; a prospective
generated-outcome study can investigate selection and finite-sample inference. Neither supplies
the true net effect of an untested bank action.

21.8     Threshold estimates include an approximation problem
Now let S be a pre-action eligibility score, centered at a cutoff of zero. A sharp rule assigns
the action when S ≥ 0. Continuity of the relevant potential-outcome conditional means at
zero, suitable support approaching the cutoff and a well-defined assignment rule can identify a
local cutoff effect. Sorting, manipulation, concurrent threshold rules and delivery versions can
invalidate that interpretation. The following calculation assumes the scientific cutoff question
has already been justified and asks what a finite-bandwidth approximation estimates.
  On the right side write S = hu, with u ∈ [0, 1], and take uniform local design density and
uniform weights for an exact population local-linear projection. Suppose the side’s conditional
mean is b0 + b1 S + κS 2 . The normal equations are
                      !       Z 1    !                                                 !
                α                   1                                             1 1/2
              G           =           (b0 + b1 hu + κh2 u2 ) du,         G=              .
                β              0    u                                            1/2 1/3
                         
                   4 −6
Since G−1 =       −6 12   , the intercept equals

                                                                         κh2
                                         Z 1
                                    α=         (4 − 6u)m(hu) du = b0 −       .                   (21.11)
                                          0                               6
The equivalent kernel integrates to one and has zero first moment, but its second moment is
−1/6. Its negative weights beyond u = 2/3 are part of boundary trend correction. They are
not positive population weights. Here κ is the quadratic coefficient; the second derivative is
2κ. Confusing the two would double the bias correction. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
   Using S = −hu on the left changes the linear term’s sign and leaves the quadratic intercept
bias unchanged. With equal bandwidths, the difference between projected intercepts has bias
−(κ+ − κ− )h2 /6. Unequal bandwidths replace this by −(κ+ h2+ − κ− h2− )/6. These are exact
projection identities for the stipulated quadratic and uniform-density law. A general density,
another kernel or a nonquadratic regression requires its own expansion and remainder. A finite
random-sample local regression is not identical to the population projection; its expected ratio
of random matrices is another object.
   Reducing bandwidth can reduce approximation bias while removing nearby observations
and destabilizing the local design. Estimated curvature, bandwidth selection and robust bias
correction add their own uncertainty. An interval using a variance formula for an uncorrected
intercept cannot be declared valid merely because a point bias adjustment was subtracted.
The inspected rdrobust help documents local-polynomial, bias-corrected and variance choices;
the formula above is a transparent reference for a particular population calculation, not a
substitute for its full inference theory.(RD Packages developers, 2026b)


21.9     A fuzzy ratio can amplify approximation error
With incomplete receipt, let ∆Y and ∆A denote the true outcome and receipt discontinuities.
Under the separately required exclusion, monotonicity and local continuity restrictions, their
ratio θ = ∆Y /∆A has a local complier interpretation when the receipt jump is nonzero. Let
bY , bA be the biases in the population projected discontinuities. Exact algebra gives
                                          ∆Y + bY      bY − θbA
                                                  −θ =          .                                (21.12)
                                          ∆A + bA      ∆A + bA
Even before sampling uncertainty, an apparently small bias in the receipt jump can change the
denominator’s magnitude or sign. Correcting only the outcome projection does not generally
correct the ratio.
21.10. Finite contrasts, score support and portfolio transport                               327


   Set the true local effect to 8 USD, the outcome curvature-coefficient difference to 12 USD per
score-unit squared and the receipt difference to 1/2 per score-unit squared. Then bY = −2h2
USD and bA = −h2 /12. The exact projected ratios are
                       ∆A     h ∆A + bA (∆Y + bY )/(∆A + bA ) (USD)
                       1/2   1/2  23/48            168/23
                       1/2   1/4 95/192            744/95
                      1/50   1/2 −1/1200            408
                      1/50   1/4 71/4800           168/71
All rows have the same true ratio of 8. At the weak receipt jump, the first projected ratio
is 408 USD, although no sampling noise has been introduced. At the narrower bandwidth
it is approximately 2.37 USD. These values expose approximation interacting with a weak
denominator. They are not expectations of an upstream ratio estimator and do not show that
an actual package returns these values.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
   Knowing the exact curvature in this artificial law would permit exact population correction.
In data, estimating curvature creates another random quantity, and a weak first stage remains a
sampling problem after correction. The product should distinguish an approximation certificate,
an interval for the ratio, and a scientific assessment of exclusion and local compliance. It
should preserve unbounded or disconnected uncertainty where the selected valid procedure
permits it. A finite number from a stabilized denominator is not itself evidence for a bounded
causal effect.


21.10       Finite contrasts, score support and portfolio transport
A second approximation arises when software evaluates predictions at nearby scores. In the
selected pinned CausalPy regression-discontinuity path, the contrast uses design rows for
treatment above +ϵ and control below −ϵ. This is a finite contrast, not automatically the
limiting cutoff effect. For example, let the two mean functions be
                         m1 (s) = 18 + 5s + 12s2 ,       m0 (s) = 10 + 3s.
Their cutoff difference is 8 USD, while
                                m1 (ϵ) − m0 (−ϵ) = 8 + 8ϵ + 12ϵ2 .
At ϵ = 1/10, 1/100, 1/1000, the contrasts are 8.92, 8.0812 and 8.008012 USD. Decreasing ϵ
reduces this particular deterministic approximation. It does not create data near the cutoff or
eliminate model misspecification. A numerical tolerance should therefore be expressed in score
units and translated into a justified monetary approximation bound when the model permits
one.(pymc-labs contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
  The same CausalPy source distinguishes expected mean predictions from posterior predictive
observations. Predictive variation can include outcome noise; posterior uncertainty in a mean
contrast is a different object. The inspected scikit-learn route’s singleton draw axes are not a
posterior sample. A common result schema should state the uncertainty object and supported
backend. Admitting an array shape as evidence of a distribution would turn a formatting
convention into an unsupported scientific claim. (pymc-labs contributors, 2026; Causal banking
proposal, 2026cf)
   Discrete eligibility scores can remove the limiting comparison entirely. Suppose S takes only
−1 and 1, action is 1{S ≥ 0}, and observed outcomes are respectively 10 and 14 USD. Two
response systems agree on every observation:
                   system I: Y (a) = 10 + 4a,        system II: Y (a) = 12 + 2S.
328                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


Both have smooth extensions as functions of the score. The cutoff treatment effect is 4 in
the first system and 0 in the second. Continuity alone cannot distinguish them because the
score support never approaches zero. Fitting a line across the gap chooses an extrapolation
restriction. A mass-point diagnostic or a bandwidth adjustment can reveal or respond to
the observed support, but cannot supply the unobserved response surface. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026ce)
   Possible remedies depend on the bank’s decision. A defensible local randomization model for
a specified finite window would be a different scientific assumption. A justified functional-form
or curvature restriction could support extrapolation or bounds. A redesigned randomized
encouragement could provide additional intervention information. Without such informa-
tion or restrictions, the correct product result is an unresolved effect set, not a universal
recommendation to use a different smoother.
   Even a well-identified continuous-score cutoff effect need not equal a portfolio effect. Suppose
τ (0) = 8 USD and stipulate the sensitivity restriction

                      |τ (s) − τ (0)| ≤ L|s|,   L = 6 USD per score unit.

For a target population with equal mass at s = −1/2 and s = 1/2, integrating the pointwise
envelope gives
                                5 ≤ ET {τ (S)} ≤ 11 USD.                           (21.13)
These bounds are sharp relative to the stipulated cutoff, sensitivity restriction and observed
sharp-threshold law. To construct witnesses, take the observed arm mean to be 10 + 2s + 8a
with a = 1{s ≥ 0}. Preserve that mean on the observed arm, set the effect to 8 − 6|s| or
8 + 6|s|, and fill in the unobserved arm mean by subtracting or adding the effect. The two
continuous response systems agree on every observed mean and at the cutoff while attaining
the two portfolio endpoints.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ce)
   At a cost of 7 USD per action, the portfolio net-value set is [−2, 4] USD. The local cutoff
net value of 1 USD does not determine its sign. The constant L is a scientific sensitivity
parameter, not an estimate certified by the local effect. Additional justified shape restrictions,
intervention data away from the cutoff or a narrower portfolio could reduce the set. A posterior
extrapolation can also be reported, provided its model-dependent meaning remains explicit.
General policy eligibility and transport cannot be inferred from a local ratio alone.

not evidence that a newly ported common core has the same target or interval behavior. The

No proprietary price, actual deployment entitlement or new vendor runtime is established by
the present source review.
   A bounded public/generated prototype can test the proposed advantage without waiting
for bank data. First freeze the package revisions, environments, complete dependency rights
and target contracts. Replay the exact weighted, multiarm, resource and threshold laws above
to test population arithmetic, score conventions and expected refusals. Use the same declared
330                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


target when comparing algorithms; deliberately changed targets form separate cases. The
current exact reference calculations perform only the mathematical part of that work.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026cc)
   For finite-sample statistical claims, separately register a prospective study: sampling and
assignment laws, outcome noise, independent units, nuisance learners, folds, bandwidth
rules, all uncertainty procedures, seed, fixed request counts and complete failure accounting.
Public covariates can supply realistic margins while generated potential outcomes preserve
known causal truth. Their public origin does not make a generated intervention mechanism
authentic bank evidence. Compare common-target bias and error, interval coverage and width,
availability, allocation feasibility, policy loss and full observed computation cost. Include
clipped propensities, weak receipt jumps, discrete support and dependent-unit mismatches as
declared stress regimes, rather than silently excluding failed requests.
   Successful arithmetic and statistical comparisons would justify a bounded prototype and
identify where wrapping suffices or porting merits investment. They would leave real confound-
ing, score manipulability, feasible bank actions, institutional capacity, acceptable loss and
actual total prices to the later qualification decision. Where two scientific models still agree
on the observations but disagree on the effect, more software cannot resolve the ambiguity.
The product must either acquire the missing information, narrow its assumptions or preserve
the effect set through the financial decision.

The shared-control calculation becomes more informative when the action groups have different
