23.7.1    A conditional truncation budget

An infinite-horizon claim needs a defended tail restriction. Suppose uniformly over a declared
admissible regime |mh Rh | ≤ Crh with known C ≥ 0, r ≥ 0 and dr < 1. Then the absolute
omitted gross benefit after horizon H is bounded by

                                                  (dr)H+1
                                     TB (H) = C           .                                    (23.41)
                                                   1 − dr
This follows by applying the triangle inequality to each omitted term and summing the
geometric series. It is an approximation budget conditional on a uniform structural envelope,
rather than a sampling standard error. With C = 100, d = 0.95, r = 0.9 and H = 3, it is about
USD 368.55. Reporting the four observed periods to cents does not reduce this stipulated
omitted-benefit budget.
  For the linear action envelope |∆Ah | ≤ |kβ|rh−1 at h ≥ 1, the omitted quadratic cost after
H ≥ 0 is nonnegative and bounded, if dr2 < 1, by

                                                      dH+1 r2H
                                  TA (H) = qk 2 β 2            .                               (23.42)
                                                       1 − dr2
Consequently, absent further sign information on the margin response, the omitted net value
belongs to [−TB (H)−TA (H), TB (H)]. This uses the known nonnegative sign of the cost instead
of adding a symmetric cost allowance to both ends. If benefits are also known nonnegative,
the lower endpoint can be tightened to −TA (H). Such sign information is another premise; it
is not supplied by the word “benefit.”
  If C = 0, the gross tail is zero at every horizon. For C > 0, an ex ante gross-tail tolerance
ε > 0 and 0 < dr < 1, the smallest admissible nonnegative integer horizon satisfies

                                           log{ε(1 − dr)/C}
                                 H +1 ≥                     .                                  (23.43)
                                                log(dr)

The reversed inequality follows because log(dr) < 0. In the numerical envelope, a USD 10
gross-tail tolerance needs H = 27: H = 26 still has a bound above USD 10, whereas H = 27
is below it. This is a requirement for the chosen envelope, not an instruction to forecast 28
periods (indices 0 through 27) from an uninformative short history. More credible long-horizon
restrictions, a finite contractual decision horizon, or an explicit unresolved value set may be
preferable.
   In statistical use, a simultaneous confidence region for structural parameters can be prop-
agated through finite-horizon value and a tail bound valid uniformly on that region. If the
region includes a parameter with an unbounded adverse tail, its corresponding lower value
cannot be replaced by the value at the stable point estimate. A claim about the region’s
coverage remains conditional on identification, dependence and estimation assumptions; the
deterministic tail inequality supplies none of them. This separation makes it possible to report
parameter, trend, donor, numerical and horizon limitations in their correct units without
calling every budget a confidence interval.


23.8     Software routes must preserve the comparison
The proposal should reuse a mature estimator where its target and sampling conditions
fit. The relevant choice is more specific than “run a panel package.” The required state
includes the rollout calendar, the permitted untreated comparisons, the population and horizon
23.8. Software routes must preserve the comparison                                            427


weights, and the observation or innovation law. The selected primary documentation supports
three complementary routes below. It is a bounded comparison of inspected versions; the
wider software survey, complete dependency rights and runtime qualification remain separate
obligations.(Causal banking proposal, 2026co)


23.8.1    Cohort estimates followed by trend sensitivity

The first route uses a cohort-aware event-study estimator and passes a correctly normalized
estimate vector with its joint covariance to a trend-sensitivity procedure. The inspected
HonestDiD example for did requires a dynamic event study, a universal base period, consecutive
relative times and a reference period of −1. It constructs covariance from the dynamic influence
vectors and removes the normalized zero coefficient. Its example target vector selects one post
period. A discounted banking total needs an explicitly changed target vector and matching
outcome units, rather than adding the endpoints of several separately reported intervals.
(asheshrambachan contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026co)
   The bridge’s influence-product covariance is not a universal remedy for shared regional
calendar shocks. Its validity depends on the sampling units represented by the input influence
rows and the underlying estimator’s inferential regime. A proposed wrapper must either justify
the joint covariance for the bank’s actual design or decline the requested inferential claim.
Retaining the whole matrix also permits the noisy-slope contrast in (23.11); exporting only
marginal standard errors would lose that possibility.
  The selected eventstudyinteract route is a community Stata estimator. Its saved e(b_iw)
and e(V_iw) describe the weighted estimates; e(b) and e(V) retain the underlying interacted
regression. A subprocess wrapper should export the intended pair, its cohort weights and
support, rather than rely on whichever object a generic post-estimation command reads.
The manual says to exclude periods after the last cohort becomes treated when that cohort
supplies the controls. It also warns that the cited validity result is for balanced panels without
covariates, although the implementation accepts unbalanced data. Admitting the broader
input format does not establish the broader causal or inferential claim.(EventStudyInteract
contributors, 2023)
   We propose wrapping these existing routes when their regimes and rights are satisfied.
Reimplementing their inference in another language has no demonstrated benefit at this stage
and would create new numerical and semantic obligations. Stata runtime rights and the
community package’s unresolved redistribution rights must also remain distinct. Their absence
from this bounded inspection is a reason to defer redistribution, not evidence that the estimator
is scientifically inferior.


23.8.2    Augmented donors and block synthetic DiD

The inspected augsynth dispatcher has separate single-outcome, multiple-outcome and stag-
gered paths. It exposes outcome-model, balance and regularization choices, with some options
specific to the dispatched path. The saved declaration is version 0.2.0 at its recorded source
commit. We propose evaluating the original R path and preserving the dispatcher result, donor
identities, penalty, weight signs and chosen uncertainty method. The entry-point manual does
not establish every downstream implementation or inferential detail; those need inspection
before admission. In particular, the oracle minimizer in (23.17) should not be used as a claim
about the output of its ridge option. (augsynth contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal,
2026co)
  The proposed synthdid route is narrower: the inspected matrix interface uses an untreated-
428                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


unit count and a pre-period count with simultaneous treatment onset. The transformation from
long banking observations to that matrix must preserve the meaning of both axes. Dropping
early-treated cells to create a rectangle changes the observed comparison and may change
the population target. For a staggered request, a collection of separately justified cohort
comparisons is an alternative design, rather than a hidden preprocessing trick that makes the
block estimator universal. Its beta-interface status also argues for a version-bound wrapper
before considering a port.(synth-inference contributors, 2026)
   These routes solve related but different balance problems. Augmentation can spend ex-
trapolation to improve unit balance; synthetic DiD also changes the pre-period comparison.
The product identity (23.24), norm penalty (23.25) and contamination radius (23.19) explain
concrete reasons their outputs can differ. They do not provide a ranking until the uncertainty
class, sampling law, common target and actual estimator behavior are specified. We therefore
propose retaining both original engines for matched evaluation. We reject automatic substitu-
tion between their outputs and defer a native port until a measured requirement justifies its
maintenance and verification cost.


23.8.3    A prototype can expose semantic errors before a bank trial

A useful first prototype compares meanings before comparing leaderboard scores. The exact
event-study table supplies a known false-lead reference, including the full design rank and
projection matrix. The curvature laws supply sharp endpoints and a noisy-slope variance check.
The donor and double-weight tables supply known bias, variance and contamination tradeoffs.
The signed-calendar and feedback laws then expose two failures that a purely tabular fit score
can miss: the wrong source of replication and the wrong intervention after a rule change. These
are proposed admission tasks, supported by local authored algebra; no upstream estimator
has been run here. (Causal banking proposal, 2026cn,cl)
   Permitted public panels can make the exercise more realistic by supplying calendar spacing,
exposure sizes, missingness and covariate patterns. Their license, revision date, units and local
identity would be retained. They do not by themselves reveal the untreated outcome of a
treated region. One defensible design overlays explicitly generated potential outcomes on a
permitted public covariate structure, disclosing that the causal truth is constructed. Another
compares descriptive behavior on a real policy episode while preserving unresolved causal
truth. Those designs answer different questions and should be reported separately. Existing
public-data survey entries can be screened for these purposes without treating a dataset’s
availability as scientific validation of the rollout design.
  After semantic admission, a prospective statistical comparison would freeze each engine
and its dependency environment, the common estimand, a fresh generating law and seed,
sample sizes, repetitions, inference methods, stopping rule and failure accounting. Scenarios
would vary treatment-effect heterogeneity, factor extrapolation, donor contamination, calendar
dependence, action excitation and post-change stability. Methods should be compared only
where their targets coincide and their claimed regimes are declared; a justified refusal is an
observable outcome. No favorable preliminary result should be used to revise the final scenario
denominator.
  The resulting report would retain target error, interval coverage under the constructed law,
availability, width, monetary decision loss and observed end-to-end cost. It would also retain
unsupported requests, convergence failures, nonfinite outputs and unresolved rights. Statistical
qualification of one frozen regime would remain different from acceptance of arbitrary panels
or a bank’s actual assignment and shock law. Only after such a prototype demonstrates
useful behavior is a costly authentic-bank trial justified by evidence from this program.(Causal
23.9. Choosing the unit and calendar weights together                                              429


banking proposal, 2026cl)
   For the proposed library, CLI and MCP interface, a single result should therefore carry
the same target vector, reference period, supported cells, signed weights, uncertainty method,
sensitivity restrictions and horizon budget. A scalar “effect” field would erase the distinctions
developed here. The transport should also preserve a set-valued result or refusal when
assumptions or support do not admit a scalar claim. This is a proposed semantic contract
for later integration; the documented estimator interfaces and these exact references do not
establish interoperability with another repository.


23.9      Choosing the unit and calendar weights together
The block comparison above evaluates particular choices of weights. A bank designing a
comparison faces a further question: should it improve the donor balance, the calendar balance,
or both? The two choices interact. A residual factor mismatch is a product of their imbalances,
while independent-cell noise is multiplied by both squared weight norms. Optimizing one
axis while holding the other fixed need not reveal the best joint choice. We can solve one
small reference problem completely, including its global alternatives, without claiming that
an estimated synthetic-control routine solves that oracle problem.(Causal banking proposal,
2026cm)
   Use a new symmetric factor table, rather than change the inputs of the earlier comparison.
There is one treated region with loading 2, two donors with loadings 0 and 1, one post period
with factor 2, and two pre periods with factors 0 and 1. The untreated mean in each cell is the
product of its loading and factor, plus unrestricted additive unit and time effects. The outcome
errors in the nine cells are independent, centered and have common known variance s > 0.
A constant treatment effect τ enters only the treated post cell. All choices below therefore
estimate that same τ ; they do not change the population or horizon to improve a score.
  Put donor weights (1 − a, a) on the two donors and pre-period weights (1 − b, b) on the two
pre periods. Both pairs sum to one, even when a weight is negative. In row order treated,
donor zero, donor one, and column order post, pre zero, pre one, the signed contrasts are
                                                                        3 X
                                                                          3
               q = (1, a − 1, −a)′ ,    r = (1, b − 1, −b)′ ,
                                                                        X
                                                                 τb =             qi rj Yij .   (23.44)
                                                                        i=1 j=1

Each contrast sums to zero, so the additive unit and time effects cancel. The coefficient of the
treated post cell is one. The remaining factor bias is (2−a)(2−b). Define Q(x) = 1+(1−x)2 +x2 ,
the squared norm of one axis’s contrast. Independence of the nine cell errors gives the exact
risk
                            Rs (a, b) = (2 − a)2 (2 − b)2 + sQ(a)Q(b).                   (23.45)
The first term is squared bias for τ , and the second is its variance. This expression is conditional
on the declared factors and fixed weights. It is a mean squared error, with squared outcome
units. It is neither a confidence radius nor a realized profit. Monetary scaling of an estimation
error would need the exposure and decision loss to be specified separately.
  For any fixed b, this is a strictly convex quadratic in a. Its derivative and unique conditional
minimizer are
                            1 ∂Rs
                                    = (a − 2)(2 − b)2 + sQ(b)(2a − 1),

The denominator is positive for s > 0. There is a corresponding expression for b∗ (a) by
symmetry. When the other axis is already exact, for example b = 2, the optimum is a = 1/2:
factor bias is already zero, so the remaining axis minimizes its noise norm. Matching the factor
exactly on both axes spends variance twice without reducing bias below zero. Conversely,
when the other axis retains imbalance, moving a toward the extrapolating value 2 can have a
benefit. Separate coordinatewise convexity does not establish joint convexity or the uniqueness
of a joint solution.

One coordinate is about 1.7676 and the other about 0.5657. The first solution extrapolates
across donor regions while using positive pre-period weights; the second extrapolates across
calendar periods while using positive donor weights. Neither axis is exactly balanced. Equal
risk comes from the reference table’s symmetry and common cell variance, rather than from
a general equivalence between borrowing information across regions and borrowing it across
time. A bank with common calendar shocks or unequal exposures would usually break that
symmetry.
  At the boundary s = 1/2, the certificate has only one real minimizer, a = b = 1, with risk 3.
To see uniqueness directly, at a = 1 + x, b = 1 + y,

                          R1/2 (1 + x, 1 + y) − 3 = 3(x + y)2 + 3x2 y 2 .                   (23.50)

Equality requires both x + y = 0 and xy = 0, hence x = y = 0. The pair of asymmetric optima
at smaller positive noise therefore merges at this boundary. This is a property of this finite
reference objective. It is not an asymptotic phase transition established for a fitted estimator.

23.9.2     What constraints and exact matching cost

Suppose policy requires nonnegative weights on both axes. Then (a, b) ∈ [0, 1]2 . At s = 1/8, the
first derivative in (23.46) is strictly negative throughout the square. Indeed (a−2)(2−b)2 ≤ −1,
while sQ(b)(2a − 1) ≤ 1/4, since Q(b) ≤ 2 on that interval. Thus ∂R1/8 /∂a ≤ −3/2. The
same bound holds for the other derivative. Increasing either coordinate until it reaches one
strictly lowers risk, proving the constrained global optimum (1, 1). It is not merely the best
point found on a grid.
  The four comparisons on the same nine-cell law are

         Choice                                      a             b Mean squared error
         Best nonnegative pair                       1             1                   3/2
         Exact unit balance, minimum time norm       2           1/2                   9/8
         Exact balance on both axes                  2             2                   9/2
         Unrestricted joint optimum                  pair in (23.49)                     1

The exact-unit solution is also the best choice with a constrained to 2: its zero bias leaves
6sQ(b), minimized at b = 1/2. Requiring both axes to fit exactly multiplies two norms of 6
and gives 36s = 9/2. For the nonnegative pair the residual bias is one, and the variance is
4s = 1/2. The joint optimum accepts some residual bias to reduce the total risk below the
exact-unit alternative. These identities explain the comparisons; observing a small pre-period
residual alone would not do so.
   There is a separate direct check. Each of the nine noise coefficients is qi rj . Enumerating all
29 = 512 independent signs for standardized cell errors gives zero mean and second moment
P       2 2
   i,j qi rj . Adding the squared factor-table contrast recovers the displayed risks. For the
irrational weights in (23.49), multiplying their exact cell coefficients and summing squared
coefficients also gives risk one. Thus neither a floating-point optimizer nor a rounded square
root determines the ranking. (Causal banking proposal, 2026cm)
   The result suggests a useful prototype diagnostic: retain both weight vectors and the declared
noise law when investigating a discrepancy between two synthetic comparisons. It does not
prescribe the oracle weights for an actual bank. Its post factor and loadings are known here; a
real untreated post factor is counterfactual. Learning the weights from noisy pre outcomes
can correlate them with those errors. A contamination class, common shocks, missing cells or
a constraint on extreme weights changes the objective. The earlier signed-contamination and
calendar calculations show concrete ways that the apparent gain can disappear. An estimated
procedure needs its own target-preserving selection rule and uncertainty argument. The global
certificate supplies an exact reference for a deliberately restricted law, with which such a future
implementation can be compared.


23.10       Valuing replacement of the entire feedback rule
The response to a new action innovation within a regime leaves a different investment question
unresolved. A bank may propose replacing the old feedback rule for an already occupied
portfolio, without adding an action innovation. We now compare those entire regimes from
the same nonzero initial state, charging the actions each would actually take. An apparently
accurate model of the old path still leaves an interval of replacement values, because the
observed controller can hide the separate persistence and action-effect parameters.
   Retain the structural outcome law in (23.31), with future structural disturbances and action
innovations zero. Set Y−1 = 1, k = 2/5 and the observed reduced coefficient λ = 9/10. Supply

insufficient as an operational admissibility criterion. Feasible capital, funding and action limits
would need to be imposed before calling such a rule implementable.

23.10.3     A tail certificate for the whole paired comparison

The earlier innovation tail cannot be reused unchanged for this question. Subtracting (23.54)
from (23.58) leaves four tails:
                                     (                             )
                                         a(da)H+1 λ(dλ)H+1
                      V∞ − VH = m                −
                                          1 − da   1 − dλ
                                         (                                     )          (23.62)
                                             (k ′ )2 (da2 )H+1 k 2 (dλ2 )H+1
                                   −q                         −                    .
                                                   1 − da2        1 − dλ2

For the positive coefficients in the two-rule example, the triangle inequality gives an absolute
bound by adding these four positive magnitudes. Maximizing the new-state and action terms
at a = 0.98 and k ′ = 0.44 yields a uniform bound of USD 4.3532, below USD 4.36, at H = 80.
The actual largest endpoint tail is about USD 4.3231; cancellation makes it smaller than the
four-term bound. A uniformly safe truncation allowance should use the defended envelope,
rather than an observed cancellation at a convenient world.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cm)
   Directly evolving old and new states, taking their separate actions and accumulating
discounted gains reproduces the finite geometric formula. Adding the exact remaining tails
reproduces the infinite value, for both endpoint worlds and an interior world with β = 3/2.
These checks also retain the first action and its cost. They would fail if the calculation were
silently replaced by a within-regime innovation response or if the initial state were set to zero.
   The decision implication remains conditional. A positive worst-case value for rule 0.44
is warranted only for this supplied structural class, action feasibility, initial exposure, cost
law and horizon. The old observations cannot certify the class or structural invariance. An
exogenous action perturbation, a credible restriction on persistence, or a justified controlled
pilot could narrow the class; a public panel can supply realistic clocks and exposures without
supplying that missing causal truth. These are concrete next information choices. Until they
are resolved, the proposal should return the class of values and the convergence restrictions
alongside any chosen policy, so that an attractive forecast is not mistaken for an identified
bank investment.


23.11      Conclusion
A panel or time series supplies a comparison only after the target, counterfactual information
and sampling law are specified. The exact rollout regression produces positive leads without
anticipation. A target-specific trend budget becomes more demanding with the horizon and
with uncertainty in the pre-period slope. Exact donor balance can lose to a regularized
comparison, while an explicit contamination class can reverse that ranking. Synthetic DiD’s
two axes of balance interact with noise and shared shocks. A maintained feedback response
can value a different intervention from the one the bank proposes to implement.
   These results motivate concrete reuse and prototype routes. They also identify the infor-
mation still needed: credible counterfactual restrictions, appropriate independent replication,
action excitation, stable intervention meaning, feasible costs and a defended horizon. An
integrated proposal should preserve those requirements through the estimator, uncertainty
calculation and monetary decision. A successful software call cannot replace them.

Uncertain relationships, transported
policies and the information to audit

24.1      A banking relationship is an input to a policy’s meaning
Consider an outreach proposal intended to improve repayment through a customer’s business
contacts. A contact may share information, coordinate a payment or pass on an offer. The
bank has candidate relationships assembled from several files, and a pilot population differs
from the proposed rollout population. The question is the incremental value of changing the
outreach allocation. It requires a definition of the relationships through which the action
can operate, the joint allocation of actions, the population receiving the benefit and the
observations that establish those quantities. An accurate estimate conditional on an invented
network can answer the wrong banking question.
   There are three distinct objects. An identity link says that two records refer to the same
entity. A relationship link says that two distinct entities have a specified connection. An
influence link asserts that an action can affect an outcome through that connection. A
common telephone number can suggest the first or second object without establishing the third.
Conversely, a one-to-one customer match does not establish a one-to-one guarantee network: a
firm can have many guarantors. The observation methods in Chapter 11 and the allocation
methods in Chapter 35 address parts of this problem. Here the issue is their composition:
uncertainty in the first objects changes the exposure, target population and monetary value
used by the later methods.
   Let G denote the scientifically relevant relationship graph, L an identity assignment, R the
observation indicators and Z a pretreatment population stratum. For an action vector a, an
exposure mapping hi (G, a) specifies which part of that vector can affect customer i. A policy g
is a joint probability law for feasible action vectors, conditional on information available at its
decision time. It need not factor into independent customer-level coins. A useful population
value is                               "                                     #
                                        X
                    V∗ (g; M ) = EM,∗       g(a | F− ){Yi (hi (G, a)) − Ci (a)} ,            (24.1)
                                        a

where M specifies the outcome, graph and observation law, ∗ denotes the target population,
and costs are allocated once to the stated beneficiary or population denominator. For a
finite population the outer expectation includes a uniformly selected target member. Other
population weights require an explicit replacement. A policy contrast subtracts the old value
and the incremental investment cost.
  This notation does not identify the value. It reveals the inputs that must remain common

                                                 436

when comparing software: the observation law for L, G, R; the exposure mapping; the full
action law; the target population; and the currency and horizon. If several admissible models
agree on the supplied observations, the scientifically warranted result can be a set of values.
The examples below are project derivations with exact, hypothetical monetary inputs. They
establish semantic and information limits before a fitted estimator or an expensive bank
experiment is chosen.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cr)


24.2      Separate edge probabilities do not determine policy ex-
          posure
Start with disjoint candidate neighborhoods. Each has one focal beneficiary and two distinct
actionable contacts. Let U, V ∈ {0, 1} indicate whether the respective influence relationships
are real. Assume their marginal probabilities are both 1/2. The statement concerns a
population distribution of actual neighborhoods; it is not a claim that a particular customer’s
graph changes randomly at every decision. Conditional on a fixed neighborhood, independently
assign each contact an action with probability p, independently of (U, V ). The focal beneficiary
benefits if at least one real contact receives an action.
  Inclusion and exclusion of the two successful-contact events gives

                                q(p | U, V ) = p(U + V ) − p2 U V.                         (24.2)

The first term counts both possible contacts; the second removes double counting when both
relationships are real and both contacts are treated. Write θ = Pr(U = V = 1). The supplied
margins imply

                           Pr(1, 1) = Pr(0, 0) = θ,
                           Pr(1, 0) = Pr(0, 1) = 21 − θ,      0 ≤ θ ≤ 12 ,                 (24.3)
                          q(p) = p − p2 θ.

Every member of this family is a coherent joint graph law. At θ = 0 every beneficiary has
exactly one real contact; at θ = 1/2 half have two and half have none. Both populations have
the same separate edge probabilities. They produce different saturation of outreach because
the second contact has less incremental value when the first already reaches the beneficiary.
   Suppose a successful exposure contributes USD 100. An action costs USD 20 for each of
the two potential contacts, including contacts whose influence relationship is absent. Raising
p from 1/5 to 3/5 increases expected contact expense by 2(20)(2/5) = 16 dollars per focal
beneficiary. Therefore

                       ∆q = 52 − 25
                                 8
                                    θ,       ∆Vbefore investment = 24 − 32θ.               (24.4)

An additional USD 16 investment per beneficiary gives

                       v(θ) = 8 − 32θ,        {v(θ) : 0 ≤ θ ≤ 21 } = [−8, 8].              (24.5)

The bounds are sharp because the endpoint graph distributions in (24.3) attain them. Enu-
merating the four graph states and four action states reproduces the expectation. These are
exact structural calculations; the interval is not a confidence interval from a sampled bank.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026cr)
   Completing the two edges independently selects θ = 1/4 and reports zero net value after
investment. Independence of graph edges is additional scientific information, distinct from
438                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


independent allocation of actions. The latter was specified as a policy; the former was not
supplied by the edge margins. A calibrated probability of each edge does not alone calibrate
their joint occurrence. This matters even when the outcome model and monetary inputs are
known exactly.
   It also changes what should be audited. Suppose indefinitely many independent neighbor-
hoods are audited, but each audit randomly chooses only one of the two edges and never records
both. Under every θ in the family, the selected edge is a fair Bernoulli observation. With this
observation design the complete audit-data law is identical across all θ. More separate-edge
labels cannot distinguish the endpoint policy values. Joint observations, a justified depen-
dence restriction or a different policy are needed. If outcomes from a rich experiment were
also supplied, they could contain more information; that is a different experiment from this
deliberately limited audit design.


24.3     The joint action law is a substantive alternative
Uncertain relationships need not force the bank to choose a graph completion. Sometimes it
can change the action design to reduce reliance on the unknown graph moment. Let the two
contact actions have equal marginal probability p and joint probability r = Pr(A1 = A2 = 1).
Suppose the pair of actions is independent of the graph. Its feasible distribution is
                       Pr(1, 1) = r,   Pr(1, 0) = Pr(0, 1) = p − r,
                       Pr(0, 0) = 1 − 2p + r,   max(0, 2p − 1) ≤ r ≤ p,                    (24.6)
                       q(p, r) = p − rθ.
The same separate action probabilities can thus represent independent coins, all-or-none
outreach or a plan that disperses actions across contact pairs. Their expected action expense
is the same, but their policy exposure differs.
  For a matched comparison, fix the old action law at p0 = r0 = 1/5: both contacts receive
outreach with probability 1/5, otherwise neither does. All new plans have p1 = 3/5. Retain
the USD 100 exposure benefit, USD 20 contact expense and USD 16 incremental investment.
The value becomes
                                v(r1 ; θ) = 8 − 100(r1 − 51 )θ.                      (24.7)
Table 24.1 compares three feasible new plans against this same old law. Its baseline differs
from the independently randomized old law in (24.5); keeping the reference explicit prevents
unmatched claims of improvement.

      New allocation            r1              Net value                Sharp value set
      Independent contact coins 9/25            8 − 16θ                  [0, 8]
      Both contacts together    3/5             8 − 40θ                  [−12, 8]
      Dispersed contact pairs   1/5             8                        {8}

Table 24.1: Exact hypothetical USD values per focal beneficiary, with the same old allocation
and the same marginal action expense.

   The dispersed new plan assigns both actions with probability 1/5 and each single-action
configuration with probability 2/5; it never assigns neither. Its overlap probability equals
the old one, so the unknown θ cancels from the contrast. The plan has a positive USD 8
value throughout the supplied graph class. The conclusion relies on the stipulated saturation
response and linear contact expense. An action interaction in cost or a benefit depending on
which contact is reached would change it.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cr)
24.4. A population can change through its graph                                              439


   Feasibility is equally substantive. Disjoint actionable pairs allow these pair distributions
to be implemented jointly. In overlapping neighborhoods, one contact can belong to several
pairs, and separately specified pair laws may not extend to a common global action law. The
product must then solve or verify the global allocation problem before presenting the policy
value. It must also preserve a common action clock: a sequential rule that reacts to the first
contact’s response is a different intervention.
   This example offers a route beyond requesting more labels. Information acquisition and
intervention design are alternatives to compare. Where coordination is feasible, changing the
plan can remove the particular unknown moment at unchanged expected contact expense.
Where coordination is infeasible, the original value set and the need for joint relationship
information remain. A software field containing only a scalar allocation probability would lose
this distinction unless its meaning explicitly fixes the entire action law.


24.4     A population can change through its graph
Transporting a pilot result requires invariant causal mechanisms or a justified formula combining
the available populations. Selection diagrams express such invariance claims; the pretreatment
admissibility result of Pearl and Bareinboim (2014, Theorem 2 and Corollary 1) allows target
averaging of an invariant conditional intervention response under its graphical conditions.
Equal observed customer characteristics do not establish that the relevant conditional response
is invariant when relationship structure changes.
   An exact finite example makes the distinction visible. Take eight customers with the same
recorded covariates. At the source they form four disjoint undirected pairs, so everyone has
degree one. At the target, four customers are isolated and four form a cycle, so half have degree
zero and half degree two. Both graphs have four edges and mean degree one. Independently
assign each customer an action with probability p. An individual’s stipulated benefit is USD
100 if at least one of its neighbors receives an action; its own action costs USD 20. There is no
direct own-action benefit, and no influence beyond immediate neighbors.
  For degree d, the exposure probability is 1 − (1 − p)d . Averaging over these two actual
graphs gives
                     qs (p) = p,  q∗ (p) = 12 {1 − (1 − p)2 } = p − 21 p2 .          (24.8)
When p rises from 1/5 to 3/5, the source exposure gain is 2/5, whereas the target gain is 6/25.
The expected own-action expense increases by USD 8 in both populations. Net benefits before
a USD 24 investment are therefore USD 32 and USD 16; after investment the decisions have
values +8 and −8 respectively. Global enumeration of all 28 action vectors on each graph
verifies these population means.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cr)
   The response mechanism was held fixed; the graph distribution changed. Balancing customer
covariates or matching mean degree cannot reproduce the nonlinear saturation in (24.8). Degree
distribution would suffice for this particular supplied outcome law, but the source has no
degree-zero or degree-two observations. Adding degree to a transport regression therefore
reveals a support failure; it does not establish the missing response surface. The exact target
calculation used an explicit structural saturation law beyond nonparametric source evidence.
   For more general responses even degree is inadequate. Direction, weighted connections,
shared neighbors or actions outside the measured graph may affect exposure. Which graph
summaries can be transported depends on a sufficient exposure mapping and the invariances
of the outcome law. A claim of unchanged graph semantics should specify the relationship
type, observation coverage and availability clock. A cycle observed after outreach can itself be
an effect of outreach and cannot silently replace the pretreatment influence graph.
440                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


  This establishes a concrete comparison requirement. A transport package that accepts
a covariate table may still be useful after a valid graph reduction. Its table interface does
not justify that reduction. A network package that accepts a target graph may compute
the stipulated target exposure accurately, but it does not validate the invariant response
mechanism or recover omitted relationships. The uncertainty and support diagnostics must
accompany both operations.


24.5     A pooled graph audit may be inadequate for target rollout
Return to disjoint two-contact neighborhoods and independent action coins at p0 = 1/5 and
p1 = 3/5. Suppose an observed pretreatment stratum Z ∈ {0, 1} has source weights (3/4, 1/4)
and target weights (1/4, 3/4). Within each stratum the two edge margins are 1/2. Write
their overlap probabilities as θ0 , θ1 ∈ [0, 1/2]. Assume these conditional joint graph laws are
invariant between populations. Benefits per successful exposure are stipulated at USD 100
and USD 200 respectively. Incremental contact expense is USD 16 and investment USD 32
per focal beneficiary in either stratum. Consequently

               v0 = −8 − 32θ0 ,       v1 = 32 − 64θ1 ,       v∗ = 22 − 8θ0 − 48θ1 .           (24.9)

The target coefficients combine stratum-specific exposure sensitivity, benefit and population
weight. They show why the second stratum is much more important to the rollout decision
than its source prevalence suggests.
  Suppose the available source audit reports the exact pooled joint moment
                                         3      1      1
                                         4 θ0 + 4 θ1 = 4 .                                   (24.10)

It does not release joint labels by stratum. This is an information restriction: the analyst has
the stratum proportions, separate edge margins and the pooled overlap, together with the
stipulated response law. Unrestricted source experiments with stratum-specific outcomes are
not additionally supplied. They could identify information absent from this example.
  Combining the pooled constraint with the probability bounds yields
                                         1        1
                     θ1 = 1 − 3θ0 ,      6 ≤ θ0 ≤ 3 ,        v∗ = 136θ0 − 26.                (24.11)

                                         V∗ = [− 10  58

For the lower endpoint take (θ0 , θ1 ) = (1/6, 1/2); for the upper take (1/3, 0). Each stratum
then has the coherent four-state graph law in (24.3), and both populations obey the same
supplied pooled audit. Rational mixtures of disjoint neighborhoods realize these laws. The
bounds are attained, rather than obtained by unconstrained independent choices of impossible
stratum parameters.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cr)
  Assigning θ0 = θ1 = 1/4 reports USD 8. It satisfies the pooled constraint but introduces
homogeneous overlap without evidence. More precise measurement of the same pooled moment
does not distinguish the endpoint worlds. This is different from the topology example:
conditional graph invariance was granted here, yet the source information was aggregated in a
way that loses what target weighting needs.
   The practical remedy is not to discard the pilot. Preserve the pooled constraint and collect
or release the missing stratified joint information. If privacy or custody limits prevent release
of individual joint labels, an approved stratum-level sufficient audit statistic may resolve this
particular moment. If a stratum is unobserved, defend a structural restriction or retain the
24.6. Completion uncertainty and sampling uncertainty answer different questions             441


value set. Replacing the target weights with the source weights would answer a different
population question.
   There is a related software hazard. A workflow can report a correct source graph posterior and
a correct target reweighting routine while using them incompatibly. If the posterior has already
collapsed the stratum-specific parameters to one pooled quantity, later reweighting cannot
recreate their joint feasible set. The proposed representation should retain the constraints
on (θ0 , θ1 ) and apply the target value to that set. This is a small linear optimization in the
example, but the essential requirement is scientific preservation of the joint information.


24.6     Completion uncertainty and sampling uncertainty answer
         different questions
The intervals above express compatibility with supplied exact information. They are not
repeated-sampling error bars. When the graph and observation model are estimated, at
least three uncertainty sources must be distinguished: which completions remain admissible,
uncertainty conditional on a completion, and numerical error in averaging action assignments.
More Monte Carlo draws reduce the last component without resolving the first two.
   For an illustrative model-based analysis, suppose the two endpoint graph completions in
(24.5) have posterior weights 1/2 each. Conditional value means are −8 and 8, and conditional
variances are each one square dollar. The law of total variance gives

       Var(v | O) = E{Var(v | G, O) | O} + Var{E(v | G, O) | O} = 1 + 64 = 65.           (24.13)

A four-point construction with independent conditional noise {−1, 1} checks the arithmetic.
Reporting the variance one after selecting a graph omits the between-completion variation.
Computing a value at the mean graph also need not equal averaging the value: (24.2) depends
on the product U V .(Causal banking proposal, 2026cr)
   These posterior weights are supplied model statements. They do not establish frequentist
coverage, a justified prior or authentic probabilities for bank relationships. The joint Bayesian
linkage construction of Guha et al. (2022) illustrates how outcome information can inform
uncertain matching in a common likelihood. Its no-duplicate one-to-one linkage, no-interference
SUTVA and ignorability assumptions must remain attached. It does not supply a theorem
for replacing G by an arbitrary banking influence network. Adding a network outcome model
changes the likelihood and the causal assumptions and needs its own derivation and evaluation.
   A different route is a sampling confidence region for the graph moments. Suppose a procedure
produces Cn with Pr{(θ0 , θ1 ) ∈ Cn } ≥ 1 − α under a declared truthful audit design. Mapping
this region through (24.9) gives
                                    "                        #
                                        inf v∗ (θ), sup v∗ (θ) .                         (24.14)
                                        θ∈Cn      θ∈Cn

It covers the true value whenever the region contains the true moments, provided the structural
response, target weights and monetary inputs are indeed known as stipulated. If these are
estimated too, a joint argument must include their error. Separate conditional intervals on
arbitrarily selected graphs do not prove graph retention.
  For simultaneous stratum intervals [Lz , Uz ], intersect the rectangle with any warranted
pooled constraint and the probability bounds. Without the pooled restriction, the image is

                             [22 − 8U0 − 48U1 , 22 − 8L0 − 48L1 ].                       (24.15)
442                                                                  Causal analysis for a universal bank


With the restriction, optimize over the intersection; independently selecting both pessimistic
endpoints may be infeasible. An empty intersection is a diagnostic of incompatible inputs or
sampling variation under a misused exact constraint, not permission to drop an inconvenient
audit. A noisy pooled estimate requires its own uncertainty rather than an exact equality.
   Sensitivity regions, posterior mixtures and confidence regions can all be useful. Their
interpretations differ. The product should state whether a negative lower endpoint reflects
unresolved graph information, sample precision, uncertain transport or a numerical enclosure.
Each has a different remedy. Reporting one generic uncertainty number would hide the next
decision.


24.7      Audit the joint unit that the value requires
Return to v(θ) = 8 − 32θ. A truthful whole-neighborhood audit records both relationship
indicators and hence B = U V . Under independent draws of eligible neighborhoods, B1 , . . . , Bn
are independent Bernoulli variables with mean θ. This is a new observation design. It is not
justified by calling the two edge labels independent when they concern the same customer.
Shared contacts, common ownership errors or calendar-specific adjudication can also violate
independence between nominal neighborhoods.
   For completeness, an elementary concentration argument yields a prospective design bound.
If B ∈ {0, 1}, the second derivative of its centered log moment-generating function is the
variance of a tilted Bernoulli variable, at most 1/4. The function and its first derivative vanish
at zero, so integrating this bound twice gives

                                     log E exp{t(B − θ)} ≤ t2 /8.                                (24.16)

Independence, an exponential Markov bound and minimizing over t > 0 give Pr(θb − θ ≥ r) ≤
exp(−2nr2 ); the lower tail has the same bound. Consequently a two-sided radius is
                               s
                                   log(2/α)
                        rn =                ,      Pr{|θb − θ| ≤ rn } ≥ 1 − α.                   (24.17)
                                      2n
Intersect the interval with [0, 1/2]. A lower value certificate is

                                     v n = 8 − 32 min( 12 , θb + rn ).                           (24.18)

On the concentration event this bound is no greater than the true value. The construction
depends on the specified truthful neighborhood law; it does not validate adjudication, inclusion
probabilities or network independence.
   Suppose design information separately supports θ ≤ 1/8. On that same event, θ+r b n ≤ θ+2rn ,
so strict positive-value certification is assured if 2rn < 1/8. At α = 0.05 this is

                                      n > 128 log 40 ≃ 472.1766.                                 (24.19)

Thus 473 independent truthful neighborhood audits are sufficient under these conditions. The
radius is approximately 0.062446; direct high-precision checks distinguish 472 from 473. This
is a conservative prospective statement: conditional on the stipulated parameter restriction
and sampling law, the concentration event has probability at least 0.95 and implies a positive
certificate. No audits have been sampled for this calculation. It neither promises that an
arbitrary observed dataset passes nor estimates audit cost. (Causal banking proposal, 2026cr)
  If only one edge can ever be audited per neighborhood, B is never observed. The earlier
nonidentification remains even with infinitely many such labels. If whole-neighborhood inclusion
24.8. Allocate audit effort to the transported decision                                        443


is unequal but known, a design-based weighted joint-moment estimate may be possible; its
boundedness and variance must use that inclusion law. If some relevant neighborhoods have
zero joint inclusion, an extrapolation restriction or a partial-identification result is necessary.
Untruthful joint labels require an error model or independent gold information; larger n alone
does not correct systematic error.
   This gives a practical audit question for the banking owner: can the audit establish the two
scientifically defined influence links together, for the population and information time that
the policy uses? Auditing two customer names or confirming legal ownership may be easier
and still answer a different question. The costed experiment should be designed around the
missing moment, not around the most convenient field to label.

composition. A large pooled source audit can leave a decision unresolved, while a smaller

targeted joint audit may supply the missing information. Whether that audit is worth buying
still needs actual prices, feasible coordination, defended outcome values and a bank loss

24.9     Software composition must preserve the observation as-
         sumptions
The existing catalog identifies software that can supply useful pieces. The proposed integration
decision is narrower: admit each piece for a declared subproblem and preserve the unresolved
quantities at the boundary. The saved source versions through the 7 October 2026 cutoff
support the following comparisons. They are technical-source findings, not executed package
trials.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cs)


24.9.1    Linkage output should retain the joint information needed down-
          stream

The inspected Splink README describes a Fellegi–Sunter-based probabilistic linkage workflow,
pair predictions and clustering into estimated identities. It says multiple fields that are
not highly correlated are favorable inputs. Its saved documentation snapshot is content-
hashed; it is not assumed to belong to a subsequently retrieved mutable branch HEAD.
Performance statements in that README remain project-reported claims.(moj-analytical-
services contributors, 2026)
   An original Python adapter is a candidate for identity resolution. For the present policy it
must preserve candidate pairs, comparison information, blocking coverage, estimated probabil-
ities and the clock of the fields. A thresholded cluster can be a proposed identity assignment,
but should not be relabeled as a verified influence graph. Pair probabilities alone cannot
recover the overlap moment in (24.3). A coherent joint linkage model or sensitivity class must
also respect constraints such as one-to-one identity matching where scientifically appropriate.
Independent pair completion can violate those constraints.
   Guha, Reiter and Mercatanti’s joint outcome/linkage likelihood offers a substantive alter-
native to fixing matches before inference. Their saved publisher paper is specifically about
duplicate-free bipartite files under one-to-one matching and causal no-interference assumptions.
Outcome feedback can alter linkage uncertainty within that model.(Guha et al., 2022) For a
network policy, such feedback is a research starting point: the exposure depends jointly on
several links and the outcome law permits interference. A direct port of the one-to-one causal
likelihood would impose the wrong causal model. Preserving the original linkage engine and
developing the new joint model explicitly is preferable to claiming that a language translation
supplies the missing argument.


24.9.2    Missingness recovery and graph discovery require separate admission

The missing-data discovery study of Tu et al. (2019) assumes no confounding or selection bias
relative to its substantive variable set, causal Markov and faithfulness conditions, missingness
indicators that are not causes of substantive variables, faithful observability, no specified
deterministic relations between missingness indicators and no self-masking missingness. These
restrictions matter if unpaid balances are selectively unrecorded or account closure changes
later actions. A value being absent from a table does not establish the source’s missingness
graph assumptions.
24.9. Software composition must preserve the observation assumptions                        445


  In the pinned causal-learn 0.1.4.8 source, the PC entry point dispatches mvpc=True to its
missing-value path; a supplied Fisher-Z test is replaced by the missing-value variant and
the correction name is passed downstream. The observed commit is 0dacacf36390 from
4 September 2026.(causal-learn contributors, 2026) This establishes dispatch semantics. It
does not establish a theorem for arbitrary nonrandom missingness, unknown identity links or
dependent customer networks. The proposed Python bridge must require a source-compatible
missingness and testing regime, retain the correction choice and preserve graph ambiguity.
The downstream test and correction paths need their own inspection and runtime comparison.
   Agarwal and Singh’s corruption-aware route uses a different information structure: bounded
approximately low-rank signal, mean-zero subexponential measurement errors independent
across rows, and a specified masking model that permits within-row dependence while requiring
independent rows. (Agarwal and Singh, 2022, Section 5.1, Assumptions 5.1–5.3) Repeated
measurements can supply useful structure for selected corrupted covariates. They do not
establish truthful missing edges or independent rows when several table rows share a customer,
household or guarantee. A native reconstruction of the algorithm would retain the same
scientific restrictions. Before adopting this route, define what constitutes a row and show how
the bank’s observation law supplies the required repetition and independence.
   These are substantive alternatives to blind imputation. A compatible missingness model
can identify a target; a low-rank structure can supply additional information; a sensitivity
class can preserve unresolved values; and an audit can observe the missing joint unit. Their
outputs should be compared on a common target. Completing a table first and selecting the
best-looking causal output afterwards would hide which information supplied identification.


24.9.3    A sensitivity parameter should correspond to the unresolved mecha-
          nism

The pinned sensemakr 0.1.6 documentation describes regression sensitivity in terms of partial R2
quantities and observed-covariate benchmarks. Its kd and ky arguments specify how strongly a
hypothetical unobserved confounder relates to treatment and outcome compared with a chosen
benchmark. They are assumptions supplied to the analysis. The manual also distinguishes
coefficient, standard-error and degrees-of-freedom inputs. (sensemakr contributors, 2024)
   An original R adapter is a useful proposed report for a supported regression question. It
cannot convert a benchmark choice into evidence about the missing overlap θ or about an
invariant transport mechanism. In the present example the sensitivity parameter has a direct
joint-event meaning, an explicit feasible set and a monetary slope. Mapping it to a partial
R2 restriction would require an outcome/assignment model and a derivation; the package
name supplies neither. Conversely, even knowing every edge may leave hidden-confounding
sensitivity relevant for an observational outcome model. The two reports can coexist with
their separate targets and inputs.


24.9.4    Network and group engines should receive a complete causal request

The inspected MossSpider NetworkTMLE source at the July 2022 commit documents direct-
contact stochastic allocation, Monte Carlo averaging and complete node attributes, with no
missing-data procedure. Its unweighted adjacency, degree-restriction background population
and directed-influence convention need explicit semantic treatment.(MossSpider project, 2026)
The earlier network chapter develops those individual findings. Their new consequence here is
a composition boundary: a completed graph can be an input to a conditional evaluation, but
it cannot silently close the outer graph-value set or qualify the uncertainty after completion.
446                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


   A proposed original Python wrapper should first compare conditional values on every
small graph completion against exact action enumeration. A separate outer calculation can
then map a scientifically warranted joint graph region through those conditional values. If
stochastic integration is used, its numerical error must be bounded or recorded for the extremal
completions; a spurious numerical minimum is not a scientific bound. The coordinated pair
policy also needs support for its actual joint allocation. A routine documented only for
independent allocation cannot accept the same scalar p and claim to have evaluated that
coordinated plan.
   Inferference 1.0.3 supplies grouped formulas, allocation probabilities and an IPW path with
several propensity-model choices in the saved May 2025 source. The default logit integrand
permits one random effect, the code requires at least two groups, and the prose/signature
disagreement about integrate_allocation requires an explicit recorded argument. (inferfer-
ence project, 2026) None of these checks establishes independent neighborhoods or a feasible
global joint action law. A grouped R adapter is a candidate when disjoint groups, the target
allocation and the sampling law really coincide. Crossing guarantees or common audit errors
require another dependence argument. The complete integrands, variance calculations and
numerical tolerances remain to be qualified.
   Original-language adapters retain mature upstream implementations and make these bound-
aries easier to inspect. A shared request must retain the graph or graph class, identity map,
exposure definition, target weights, full allocation law, observation assumptions and distinct
uncertainty components. The observed MIT text for MossSpider, GPL declaration for infer-
ference and GPL-3 declaration for sensemakr inform a rights review; they do not clear every
dependency or distribution.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cs) A native port is deferred until
semantic and numerical parity plus the complete rights basis are established. No evidence
here supports a universal missing-data, transport and interference engine assembled merely by
chaining package calls.


24.10      A public and generated comparison before costly bank
           experiments
A narrow prototype can answer useful questions with public structure and explicit generated
truth. A permitted public graph or relational table can provide heterogeneous degree, group
sizes and covariate imbalance. Its relationships should retain their published meaning: a public
transaction edge is not thereby a verified repayment influence link. Generated graph truth,
action laws, response mechanisms, linkage corruption and missingness can then be added
transparently. This supplies a controlled test of the proposed composition while avoiding a
claim that public records reveal the bank’s counterfactual outcomes.(Causal banking proposal,
2026cp)
   The first comparison should use the exact finite examples in this chapter. Admit the identity
and exposure translation, matched policy baseline, population denominator and cost accounting
before testing any statistical performance. Independent-edge and coherent-joint completions
should agree only where the supplied graph law warrants it. Independent and coordinated
allocations should reproduce their distinct values. Target reweighting must retain the pooled
constraint and reveal support failure in the topology example. Negative controls should include
one-edge-only audits, wrong relationship direction, shared-neighborhood adjudication errors
and an unsupported missingness regime.
   The next stage can register fresh generated mechanisms and audit samples, fixed versions,
all scenarios, repetitions, numerical tolerances and stopping rules. Compare hard matching,
24.11. Use the pooled information when choosing the next audit                                  447


a justified joint probabilistic model, partial identification and targeted whole-neighborhood
audits. Compare original engines only where they evaluate the same target and action law.
Report graph-region retention, target error, value-set containment, finite availability, interval
width, decision loss and numerical integration error separately. Include failures and refusals in
the request denominator. The unit for uncertainty must follow the generation and audit law;
repeating several requests on one shared graph does not create independent worlds.
   The software decision then has concrete evidence requirements. Adopt an original engine
for a supported subproblem after semantic, rights and runtime checks. Integrate it through a
preserving adapter when the common request can express its restrictions. Develop a new joint
model when the scientific composition is absent. Retain a bounded answer or refuse a specific
unsupported request when information is insufficient. Porting is an engineering option after
parity, not a source of identification.
  Actual bank experiments remain a later investment decision. They need an owned influence
definition, truthful joint audits, a feasible action plan, the real target population, accepted
precision and loss thresholds and measured costs. The prospective public/generated comparison
can demonstrate why acquiring those inputs is worthwhile. The exact examples already show
what would be lost by a pooled audit or a premature graph completion; they do not estimate
the institution’s benefit from purchasing a prototype.


24.11      Use the pooled information when choosing the next audit
The earlier allocation deliberately estimated both stratum moments without using the exact
pooled audit. That is a useful baseline, but the bank should also ask whether information it
already owns changes the next purchase. Retain precisely the same hypothetical target, the
same independent truthful neighborhood law and the same known response and monetary inputs.
Grant the pooled constraint in (24.10); no additional outcome experiment or homogeneous
graph restriction is introduced. In this section the pooled information is already available to
every compared method. Its original acquisition cost is outside the incremental comparison,
and would have to be restored in a complete investment case.

24.11.1     An estimated pooled constraint has a measurable error cost

An actual pilot is unlikely to deliver its population pooled moment exactly. Write τ =
3θ0 /4 + θ1 /4, without fixing it at 1/4. Eliminating θ0 from the target gives the identity
                                     v∗ = 22 − 32   136
                                               3 τ − 3 θ1 .                               (24.31)

                             Var(vb∗ ) = 1024
