intervention responses back to meaningful units. The proposed conformance example should
therefore include an asymmetric signed matrix, a variable permutation, a unit change, and
explicit DAG versus CPDAG output. These are separate tests of direction, identity, scale and
retained ambiguity, not repeated checks of one serializer.


27.6        Functional parity, restricted derivatives and adoption
            choices

27.6.1      An implementation name does not establish numerical parity

The inspected DirectLingam helper supplies a small but revealing parity question. After
standardizing its input it calculates

                                 1 X x2i              1X
                          b1 =           ,     b2 =       xi exp(−x2i /2),
                                 n i 2                n i

and uses these moments in an entropy-style expression. For unit population variance, b1 = 1/2
regardless of the distribution’s shape. For a sample containing symmetric positive-negative
pairs, the odd second ingredient is zero. With sample-variance standardization the common
first ingredient becomes (n − 1)/(2n), so equal-length symmetric samples still share it. This is
an observation about the exact source expression, which is more specific than its accompanying
description of a log-cosh-style approximation. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a)
526                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   For example, standardizing (−3, −1, 1, 3) and (−1, −1, 1, 1) gives fourth moments 41/25 and
1, respectively, under population normalization. The two ingredients above are nevertheless
identical. The reproduced project calculation establishes that this helper cannot distinguish
these shapes from those ingredients alone. It does not establish the selected order for a full
dataset, the intended reference expression, or a failure frequency of the complete algorithm.
Those stronger questions require authentic reference derivations and matched execution,
including residualization and parent selection. The proposed adoption decision is to investigate
this path before claiming parity with another implementation bearing the same algorithm
name. (Causal banking research project, 2026x; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a)

27.6.2    Banjo: preserve the original rights and the application boundary

The inspected Banjo lead is a derivative whose README describes dynamic gene-network
analysis. It constructs pseudotime from single-cell measurements, uses lag one, a stated
discretization policy and a maximum parent count, and selects gene subsets using supplied
gold-standard connectivity. The selected greedy-search source includes time, iteration and
restart termination. These are descriptions of an application and its implementation choices;
they are not banking benchmarks or evidence that an inferred order is the recorded time of a
bank action. Selecting variables with reference to supplied graph truth would also have to be
disclosed when interpreting that application’s evaluation. (daniel-315/slingshot-modified-banjo,
2026a)
   The source notice preserves Duke University and Alexander Hartemink’s rights. It says that
non-commercial use may be licensed under a non-commercial license and directs commercial
users to contact the rights holders. Public availability of the derivative therefore does not
support classifying it as an unrestricted open-source component. The original official distri-
bution, full terms and derivative changes remain necessary for a reuse decision. Until those
are established, the proposal should compare the documented search family while holding
redistribution and commercial adoption. Rewriting only an interface would not resolve the
rights of copied implementation code. (daniel-315/slingshot-modified-banjo, 2026a)

27.6.3    What to integrate, what to retain as a baseline, and what to investi-
          gate

Tetrad is the leading candidate in this inspected Java subset for a narrow PC/FGES integration
because the chosen paths expose graph semantics, tests, scores and configuration separately.
The proposed first implementation should use a pinned Java process with an explicit request and
response schema. This keeps its runtime and dependencies identifiable and avoids immediately
maintaining a second numerical port. It does not remove GPL obligations or settle which
runtime is required: the inspected root compiler setting and bridge README name different
Java requirements. The actual dependency and bridge combination needs its own build check.
(cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a)
   Weka should be retained for a separately labeled predictive comparison, with current official
sources obtained before promising current-release behavior. Aitiotita offers a permissively
licensed alternative whose separation of components may be useful, but the conditioning
shortcut and delegated paths need focused examination before direct adoption. The Banjo
derivative supplies an additional search-family lead, with original rights and technical identity
still unresolved. A source port is justified only when a specific integration constraint outweighs
the cost of preserving and validating the mathematical behavior. It is not the default response
to having several implementation languages. (Waikato/weka-3.8, 2022a; jdellert/aitiotita, 2023;
daniel-315/slingshot-modified-banjo, 2026a)
27.7. Python discovery: choosing a computation that preserves the question                   527


   The next prototype comparison should separate deterministic conformance from statisti-
cal assessment. Deterministic cases check the funding matrix, endpoint roundtrips, oracle
separating sets, duplicate accounting columns and typed numerical failures. Statistical cases
subsequently vary sample size, minimum signal, graph density, non-Gaussianity, missingness
and departures from the declared graph class, with common generated truth and fixed replica-
tion budgets. A single seeded package test can support a regression check; it cannot estimate
whole-graph error rates. The inspected Tetrad tests include oracle-graph fixtures and a seeded
chain/collider simulation, and one test expressly calls its expected graph a regression snapshot.
They motivate these distinct levels of validation rather than replacing them. (cmu-phil/tetrad,
2026a)
   Scale should be assessed at the same scientific boundary. A skeleton search over p variables
with at most d neighbours and depth bound k can face a workload proportional to p2 kj=0 d−1
                                                                                   P
                                                                                            j
candidate tests before accounting for pruning and the cost of each test. That expression is a
planning envelope, not a runtime measurement or a tight bound for every algorithm. Dense
graphs and expensive conditional tests can dominate the result. Thread settings must be
recorded from the selected code path: the inspected FGES field and constructor initialize
one worker even though a nearby comment says all processors, and a setter can change that
value. Observed runtime, peak memory, interrupted requests and retained failures should be
measured only after a specific runtime and workload are chosen. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a)
   The resulting proposal is actionable without treating source review as a finished product. It
identifies a first Java boundary, preserves Weka’s predictive role, gives a concrete mathematical
challenge for Aitiotita, states the Banjo rights dependency, and defines the tests that would
distinguish a successful adapter from an attractive but scientifically altered output.


27.7     Python discovery: choosing a computation that preserves
         the question
A funding analyst can obtain three apparently plausible answers from the same table: a partially
directed graph, a matrix of regression coefficients, and a distribution over neural structural
models. Their common Python interface does not make these answers interchangeable. The
first can preserve directions that the data have not resolved. The second can describe one
selected ordering. The third can express uncertainty conditional on a generative model, its
prior and an approximation to its posterior. A product that converts all three into a single
directed network would discard precisely the distinctions needed to decide whether changing a
quoted rate is supported by evidence.
   The comparison below examines nine implementation families at identified source revisions
preceding the 7 October 2026 cutoff: causal-learn, pgmpy, LiNGAM, NOTEARS, DAGMA,
gCastle, CausalNex, Causica and the CausalDiscoveryToolbox (CDT). It develops selected
static discovery paths, rather than attributing every algorithm advertised by a package to the
code inspected. These are proposed reuse choices supported by primary implementation and
documentation. The financial and mathematical examples are reproducible project calculations;
they are not fitted outputs from these engines. Broader Python search coverage, some delegated
implementations and empirical comparisons remain open.


27.7.1    The funding calculation establishes the matrix contract

Consider three variables measured over a fixed decision horizon. Let F be a change in a
quoted funding rate, in percentage points, R the change in retained funding, in millions of US
528                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


dollars, and C the corresponding change in contribution margin, in the same monetary units.
A hypothetical structural model is

                    F = εF ,      R = 4F + εR ,      C = −F + 21 R + εC .                (27.3)

The disturbances are centered and mutually independent, and intervention on F replaces its
first equation. These assumptions define the illustration; the coefficients are not estimated
bank responses. The direct margin cost of raising the rate is offset by the margin earned
on retained funding. A rate increase of 0.25 percentage points therefore changes expected
retention by USD 1 million and expected margin by USD 0.25 million.
   For a data matrix whose columns have order (F, R, C), write the row convention as X =
XW + E, with Wij the coefficient on the edge i → j. The corresponding column-vector
structural convention is x = Bx + e, where B = W ⊤ . In this example,
                                                                            
            0 4 −1                                              1 4 1
       W = 0 0 1/2 ,          T = I + W + W 2 = (I − W )−1 = 0 1 1/2 .               (27.4)
                                                                    
            0 0 0                                               0 0 1

Thus TF C = 1 = −1 + 4(1/2) is the total margin response per percentage point. The matrix
identity holds because W 3 = 0. More generally, a finite DAG with d nodes has a nilpotent
weighted adjacency matrix and a finite path sum I + W + · · · + W d−1 . This algebra concerns
a supplied linear structural model; it is not a discovery or identification theorem.
   The reference NOTEARS and DAGMA linear losses predict columns through XW . The
inspected LiNGAM adjacency routine instead assigns coefficients to B[target,predictors]
and its path helper multiplies entries in that convention (xunzheng/notears, 2026; kevinsbel-
lo/dagma, 2026; cdt15/lingam, 2026). An adapter that interprets LiNGAM’s matrix as W
reports zero for the F → C response in this example and invents the reversed path response.
Both matrices are acyclic, both have identical dimensions, and both pass a check that merely
counts edges. Node order, direction convention and units must therefore be carried as data,
verified before any intervention query.
   Endpoint matrices require a separate decoder. In causal-learn’s PC/GES return contract,
entries (Gij , Gji ) = (−1, 1) denote i → j; a pair of minus ones denotes an undirected edge.
These entries are endpoint marks, not negative and positive causal coefficients (py-why/causal-
learn, 2026). Treating them as weights would invent both magnitudes and interventions. The
proposed common result must distinguish a weighted DAG, a partially directed graph and a
posterior over structural models before it exposes any common plotting or effect-evaluation
interface.

27.7.3      Constraint and score methods preserve different qualifications

The selected causal-learn PC interface exposes the significance threshold, conditional-
independence test, stable skeleton option, collider rule, conflict priority, background knowledge
and conditioning-set bound. It also has a separate missing-value route. These arguments
control substantive choices in the graph construction. They should appear in the result’s
explanation whenever they affect the decision, rather than disappearing into an undifferentiated
“PC” label (py-why/causal-learn, 2026).
  For its ordinary Fisher test, the source computes a partial correlation from an inverse
correlation submatrix, then forms
                         q
                    Z=       n − |S| − 3 atanh(rbij|S ) ,     p = 2{1 − Φ(Z)}.                  (27.5)

Here S is the conditioning set, n the row count and Φ the standard normal distribution
function. The Gaussian independent-row sampling model motivates this reference approxima-
tion; correlation zero does not imply conditional independence for an arbitrary non-Gaussian
530                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


distribution. The code raises an error for a singular correlation submatrix and clips a computed
correlation at the numerical boundary. Neither clipping nor returning a number establishes
adequate information. A sensible adapter must reject nonpositive n − |S| − 3, constant columns
and singular designs with an explanation, not translate failure into an independence finding.
   Repeated observations from one account also challenge this reference law. If a correlation
of 0.1 is supplied with 100 independent units, the displayed statistic is approximately 0.988.
Substituting 1,000 duplicated rows gives approximately 3.168, although the duplicated data
contain no new independent information. The example compares the formula under two
declared row counts; it does not propose a universal effective-sample-size correction (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026q). A panel or time-series request must use a sampling argument
appropriate to that dependence, or be declined by this static interface.
   The inspected pgmpy PC path defaults to a partially directed graph and limits conditioning
sets to five variables unless configured otherwise. Its optional DAG is one completion of the
learned partial graph. Its documented background knowledge includes required and forbidden
directions, while collider conflicts can still generate a warning. Consequently the proposed
adapter should check the returned graph against declared constraints instead of treating the
mere presence of an expert-knowledge argument as proof that every input condition was
satisfied (pgmpy/pgmpy, 2026). A five-variable search limit is a computational scope choice,
not an assertion that larger separators cannot matter in the bank’s model.
   Score methods make a different tradeoff. causal-learn GES accepts several local scores,
including Gaussian BIC, discrete BDeu and regression-based alternatives. Its inspected BIC
routine computes residual variance and can use a pseudoinverse or a small positive replacement
for a nonpositive numerical variance. pgmpy’s inspected GES performs forward, backward
and turning moves, uses a minimum improvement threshold, and converts its final equivalence
graph to a DAG only if requested (py-why/causal-learn, 2026; pgmpy/pgmpy, 2026). A larger
score in one engine cannot be compared directly with a number from another engine without
matching sign, constants, likelihood, penalties and preprocessing. The proposal should compare
graph/effect consequences under matched assumptions, not select an engine because its default
score is numerically larger.


27.7.4    Functional restrictions can orient graphs, but must be stated

LiNGAM is attractive when the banking question justifies a linear acyclic model with indepen-
dent non-Gaussian disturbances and no unobserved confounders. Those are explicit premises in
the original work, including independent repeated observations from the same model (Shimizu,
Shohei and Hoyer, Patrik O. and Hyvärinen, Aapo and Kerminen, Antti, 2006). The original
paper describes an ICA route; the current DirectLiNGAM implementation inspected here
selects an ordering through residual comparisons, then estimates coefficients using that order.
The original result should not be quoted as if it had independently verified every modern
option and integration.
   The selected helper standardizes variables for an adaptive-Lasso pruning step, uses a BIC
criterion, and refits the retained predictors in original units. The separate total-effect helper
sums directed path products and checks that variables along those paths satisfy its continuous-
variable condition (cdt15/lingam, 2026). These are valuable implementation details for a
funding adapter: they explain where a sparse edge set comes from and how the reported
monetary slope is recovered. They do not show that bank disturbances are independent or
non-Gaussian. Heavy tails in an observed balance series alone do not establish the required
disturbance model after conditioning on the structural parents.
  The observational ambiguity introduced earlier provides an exact adverse case. For a
27.7. Python discovery: choosing a computation that preserves the question                         531


standardized pair, consider two centered Gaussian models,

       M→ :     X = U,     Y = 0.6X + V,            var(U ) = 1,             var(V ) = 0.64,     (27.6)
       M← :     Y =U
                   e,      X = 0.6Y + Ve ,          var(U
                                                        e ) = 1,             var(Ve ) = 0.64.    (27.7)

Disturbances are independent within each model. Both laws have covariance ( 0.6        1 0.6 ), so the
                                                                                          1
complete observational distributions coincide, not just a selected correlation. The effect of
intervening on X is nevertheless 0.6 in the first model and zero in the second. Within this
declared two-model class the effect set is {0, 0.6}; the interval [0, 0.6] is its convex hull, not an
assertion that every intermediate effect belongs to the two-model class.
   No algorithm using observations alone can distinguish these two Gaussian laws reliably
in both worlds. A non-Gaussian identifying premise, a justified temporal direction, or an
intervention changes the available information. An optimizer’s ability to return one orientation
does not. The proposed DirectLiNGAM integration therefore retains this example as a refusal
or assumption-failure case, rather than interpreting a selected order as empirical proof of its
own premises.


27.7.5     Continuous acyclicity is a numerical condition with a domain

Continuous methods replace a combinatorial acyclicity constraint by a smooth one. Let
S = W ◦ W , the entrywise square of W . NOTEARS uses
                                                            X tr(S k )
                             hexp (W ) = tr(exp S) − d =                 .                       (27.8)
                                                            k≥1
                                                                   k!

Because S is nonnegative, its diagonal powers accumulate nonnegative closed-walk products.
A directed cycle creates a positive term; in a DAG all such terms vanish. This is the exact-zero
characterization developed in Zheng et al. (2018). Its numerical implementation uses tolerances,
iteration limits and thresholding, each of which must be distinguished from the exact statement.
  The source inspected for gCastle’s class named Notears instead uses the polynomial
expression
                            hpoly (W ) = tr{(I + S/d)d } − d.                  (27.9)
The reference NOTEARS linear implementation uses a matrix exponential. The two expressions
share an exact-zero acyclicity property but have different values, derivatives and numerical
scaling away from zero. gCastle also keeps the weighted estimate separately from a binary
matrix formed with the strict comparison |Wij | > τ , whereas the reference removes weights
satisfying |Wij | < τ . At equality, the reference retains the edge and gCastle’s binary output
does not (huawei-noah/trustworthyAI, 2026; xunzheng/notears, 2026). A benchmark that
silently compares one weighted matrix with another binary matrix can mistake a representation
choice for a scientific result.
  DAGMA uses the log-determinant characterization

                     hlog,s (W ) = − log det(sI − S) + d log s,         s > ρ(S),               (27.10)

where ρ(S) is the spectral radius. The domain ensures that sI − S is a nonsingular M-matrix.
The domain condition is part of the theorem, not an optional numerical detail (Bello, Kevin
and Aragam, Bryon and Ravikumar, Pradeep, 2022). For example, within this domain one can
expand the log determinant as k≥1 tr(S k )/(ksk ); its nonnegative cycle terms again explain
                                P

the zero condition. Computing a log absolute determinant outside the domain does not justify
the same conclusion.
532                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The inspected linear DAGMA implementation uses inverse-matrix checks and backtracking
in its optimization. Its documentation explicitly allows the possibility that the finite output is
cyclic and states that requested included edges are not guaranteed to survive. It also centers the
supplied array in place and saves a final residual before thresholding (kevinsbello/dagma, 2026).
These findings motivate copying the input, retaining the full optimization configuration, and
recomputing topology and residual diagnostics on the actual returned graph. They establish a
proposed adapter requirement; they do not establish a measured failure rate.
  A small exact counterexample illustrates why a tolerance cannot replace a topological check.
Set W = ( 0ϵ 0ϵ ) with ϵ = 0.005. This is a two-cycle. Nevertheless,

                          hexp (W ) = 2{cosh(ϵ2 ) − 1} ≃ 6.25 × 10−10 ,                        (27.11)
                                       4                 −10
                          hpoly (W ) = ϵ /2 = 3.125 × 10       ,                               (27.12)
                                                  4                  −10
                         hlog,1 (W ) = − log(1 − ϵ ) ≃ 6.25 × 10           .                   (27.13)

All are below 10−8 . A threshold of 0.001 retains both edges. The reference default threshold
of 0.3 removes both; this example is therefore not a claim that a default solver necessarily
returns this cycle. It shows why the numerical residual, thresholded support and scientific
effect are three distinct objects (Causal banking proposal project, 2026q).


27.7.6    Units and centering can change the selected orientation

In the preceding two-model Gaussian example, the population least-squares loss 12 j var(εj )
                                                                                           P

is 0.82 in both orientations, and the coefficient ℓ1 penalty is 0.6 in both. Both graphs are
acyclic. Thus neither perfect acyclicity nor this matched population objective distinguishes
the two causal effects. Scores that add other model restrictions may distinguish them, but
those restrictions must be declared and defended.
  Now express Y in units ten times as large numerically, Y ′ = 10Y , while leaving X unchanged.
The forward coefficient becomes 6, the reverse coefficient becomes 0.06, and their residual-
variance sums become 65 and 100.64, respectively. The corresponding least-squares losses are
32.5 and 50.32. The physical observational ambiguity is unchanged, but the unweighted loss
and sparsity tradeoff have changed (Causal banking proposal project, 2026q). This matters
when a funding dataset mixes percentage points, currency, duration and account counts.
Standardization is a modeling decision that must be recorded and reversed when reporting
monetary responses; it does not independently supply causal identification.
   CausalNex’s selected unpenalized NOTEARS path applies its squared-error criterion to
the supplied numeric array without the centering performed in the reference NOTEARS
least-squares path. It provides tabu edges and prohibited parent/child nodes as optimization
bounds, and its StructureModel records edge origins. The same graph object has an explicit
operation that repeatedly drops the smallest absolute-weight edge until a DAG remains, with
a warning about different units (mckinsey/causalnex, 2026a). Dropping an edge changes the
model used by an intervention query. It must not be treated as invisible file cleanup, and the
thresholded model should be assessed on its own assumptions.
   The pinned CausalNex package declares Python versions from 3.8 to below 3.11. That
declaration does not prove installation failure in every newer environment, but it is sufficient
to reject an unqualified promise that the current common Python environment can adopt
it directly. An isolated process is a possible design if a consumer values its StructureModel
workflow enough to justify the additional environment. For the simpler linear reference
comparison, wrapping NOTEARS directly is a substantive alternative that avoids introducing
that framework dependency merely to obtain a DAG matrix.
27.7. Python discovery: choosing a computation that preserves the question                     533


27.7.7    Causica connects discovery and effects through a learned model

Causica’s inspected DECI path jointly learns a distribution over graphs, functional relationships
and noise. Its training step samples a relaxed graph, evaluates a data log density, incorporates
the graph distribution’s entropy and a graph prior, and adds an acyclicity penalty. Suppressing
implementation scaling details, the statistical part has the form
                          −Eqϕ (G) log pθ (X | G) + KL{qϕ (G) ∥ p(G)}.                     (27.14)
Here qϕ is an approximating graph distribution, θ parameterizes the structural functions and
noise, and p(G) contains graph preferences. The actual module uses minibatches, relaxed
samples and scaled penalties; this expression explains their statistical roles, not an assertion of
exact posterior computation. The inspected prior includes sparsity and an optional weighted
discrepancy from a supplied expert graph (microsoft/causica, 2026).
   For an assumed structural model, simulation after replacing an intervention equation can
estimate a model-implied ATE. The Causica documentation describes this workflow, while
the inspected test methods separately evaluate graph reconstruction, observational likelihood,
interventional likelihood and effect errors when appropriate reference data are supplied. These
distinctions are useful for the proposed product. A model may predict observed balances well
while choosing the wrong intervention direction in an observationally ambiguous case; graph
uncertainty under qϕ is conditional on the model family, prior and approximation. It is not
automatically a confidence set with frequentist coverage for a bank effect.
   In particular, an expert graph supplied by a language model should retain its origin and
uncertainty. A strong prior favoring a rate-to-balance direction can concentrate a fitted graph
distribution without providing new assignment evidence. A suitable prototype would compare
the same task under an empty prior, a justified restricted prior and a deliberately wrong prior,
preserving the resulting change in intervention conclusions. Such a comparison is a proposed
experiment, not a result of this source review.
   The exact revision also matters for capability claims. Its README states that Rhino and
DDECI were removed from the refactored codebase and points to an older release. Their
historical association with Causica cannot be used to claim that the inspected DECI path
currently implements general temporal or latent-confounded inference. A missingness or
latent-variable claim needs the corresponding implementation and assumptions, examined in
its own right.

27.7.8    A Python wrapper can carry another language’s scientific contract

CDT’s selected PC and GES classes illustrate why language should be recorded at both the
public interface and the computational backend. PC checks for pcalg, kpcalg and RCIT; GES
checks for pcalg. The wrappers construct files, dispatch R templates and read results into
Python graph objects (FenTechSolutions/CausalDiscoveryToolbox, 2026). A Python package
pin alone therefore does not freeze the statistical engine, the R environment or its graph
encoding. A direct R adapter is a serious alternative if it preserves the same semantics with
fewer conversion layers.
   There are two concrete reasons to defer a default CDT recommendation. First, its GES
documentation labels one option as categorical, while the code maps the corresponding int
key to GaussL0penIntScore. The selected Python wrapper does not establish a discrete
likelihood merely because of that prose label. The R template and delegated implementation
need inspection before assigning the option a capability. The wrapper also relabels graph nodes
using sorted column names in a selected path, making a permutation test with deliberately
unsorted columns essential before banking use.
534                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Second, the repository’s saved license text is MIT, while the saved setup metadata names
Apache 2.0. Both observations are retained. Neither is a reason to invent a single reconciled
distribution license or to assume delegated R packages inherit the wrapper’s terms. This is a
local adoption question, not a reason to stop comparisons of unrelated Python implementations.
The other selected primary terms are Apache 2.0 for NOTEARS, DAGMA and the inspected
gCastle root; CausalNex supplies Apache terms and separate trademark text; Causica, LiNGAM
and the pinned pgmpy license supply MIT text. causal-learn’s MIT text was acquired on the
cutoff date from a mutable-main snapshot and should be checked at the technical pin before
distribution. These observations guide dependency review; they do not constitute a complete
transitive-license opinion.


27.7.9     Selection and missingness change what a discovery table means

A funding table may contain only customers who were successfully contacted, retained an
account or completed a follow-up. Treating the remaining rows as a random sample can create
edges even before choosing a discovery algorithm. For an exact generated illustration, let F
and N be independent√standard normal variables
                                             √ and observe only rows satisfying F + N > 0.
Define U = (F + N )/ 2 and V = (F − N )/ 2. Before selection, U and V are independent
standard normals. After selection, U is half-normal with variance 1 − 2/π, while V still has
variance one. It follows that
                                                                              1
         cov(F, N | F + N > 0) = −1/π,         corr(F, N | F + N > 0) = −        .         (27.15)
                                                                             π−1
The selected correlation is about −0.467, despite population independence (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026q). A graph of the selected table can correctly describe its associations
while misleading a population intervention query.
   This example gives practical meaning to the distinction between a missing-value option and an
argument for selection recovery. A package-specific route must state which response mechanism
it handles and what observations identify its correction. Imputation, complete-case analysis and
a generative missing-data model make different commitments. The proposed request should
carry the sampling unit, observation window, selection indicators, and relevant conditioning
events. If these are unavailable, the product can still support exploratory associations and
alternative diagrams, but its intervention conclusion must retain the unresolved selection
assumption.


27.7.10     An adapter contract and an economical prototype choice

The proposed static-discovery boundary first validates the question and data: units, node order,
information timing, row dependence, missingness, allowed interventions and model family. It
then configures one pinned engine and retains its native result. A second step decodes that
result into a typed graph or structural-model object. Only a subsequent identification step
may turn that object into a causal effect or effect set. For a partially directed result, selecting
one completion is an explicit additional assumption; for a neural SEM, reporting simulation
output is conditional on the selected learned model and uncertainty representation.
   Useful deterministic acceptance cases follow directly from the comparison. The funding model
tests a transpose and a deliberate permutation of columns. The two Gaussian orientations
test whether an interface preserves unresolved effects. The weak two-cycle tests support-level
acyclicity independently of a floating-point residual. A coefficient exactly on the threshold
tests the inequality convention. A singular CI input tests refusal, while duplicated rows test
whether the declared sampling unit is preserved. These cases check the proposed boundary;
27.8. Symbolic identification and numerical evaluation                                      535


they are not substitutes for a prospectively designed empirical evaluation of discovery accuracy
or uncertainty.
  The initial prototype should therefore favor a small, interpretable set of mechanisms: one
PC/GES path that preserves equivalence, one functional path with explicit non-Gaussian
assumptions, and separate NOTEARS/DAGMA numerical references. gCastle can test the
cost of a broader algorithm catalog. CausalNex and CDT should enter only when a specific
consumer justifies their additional dependency or conversion burden. Causica supplies a distinct
generative-model experiment, whose contribution should be judged on matched intervention
questions and negative cases rather than an attractive graph alone. Porting a numerical core
becomes worthwhile only when measured deployment constraints or performance needs exceed
the cost of validating a second implementation.
   These choices make the proposal concrete without assigning a fictional bank ROI. Their
economic comparison must include environment maintenance, source and assumption review,
translation errors, failed requests and the cost of resolving consequential graph ambiguity. The
known routes are exact interface tests, scoped primary-source completion and prospectively
designed public or generated comparisons. The unresolved scientific question is whether the
information available for a particular bank decision supports the required intervention claim.
Adding another optimizer does not answer that question.


27.8      Symbolic identification and numerical evaluation
aGrUM’s inspected CausalModel documentation permits a causal DAG with an optional
observational Bayesian network. Structural operations, including backdoor/frontdoor queries
and construction of do-calculus expressions, can be available when conditional probability
tables are absent. Operations that read those tables then raise an unavailable-operation
exception. This is a useful separation: a funding query can be identified relative to a supplied
graph before a distribution has been fitted. It does not follow that the effect can already be
reported numerically.aGrUM contributors (2026b)
   The selected CausalImpact implementation first attempts appropriate backdoor and front-
door paths, then invokes a do-calculus routine. The inspected dispatch supports a comparison
of these routes; it is not a verification of the full ID or IDC algorithm. A particularly con-
sequential detail is the handling of failures. A not-yet-implemented method and a hedge
exception are caught in different branches, but each produces a formula with no expression tree.
Their explanation strings differ. An adapter that reads only the boolean isIdentified would
erase the distinction between an unavailable implementation and a causal nonidentification
result.aGrUM contributors (2026b)
  These outputs should instead be represented as separate states:
536                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


      State                        Required scientific meaning
      Identified expression      A functional has been obtained under the declared graph
                                 and assumptions.
      Numerical result unavail- The expression may exist, but distributions, estimators
      able                       or numerical prerequisites are absent.
      Method unsupported         This implementation cannot perform the requested
                                 method or graph operation.
      Nonidentified in the model The supplied causal model and information do not deter-
                                 mine the requested functional, with the relevant reason
                                 retained.
      Computational failure      The attempted operation failed; the failure supplies no
                                 causal conclusion.

   pgmpy’s guide also separates identification from estimation and uses annotated graph roles.
Its adjustment interface returns a graph or collection of graphs and a success indicator. Source
inspection narrows what the guide alone would suggest: the minimal_variance branch raises
NotImplementedError, despite the guide’s description of variance-optimal adjustment. The
minimal branch rejects multiple exposures or outcomes. The selected implementation contains
a graph-type TODO, so the broad graph-type docstring does not by itself qualify every graph
class.pgmpy contributors (2026b)
   An unsuccessful adjustment search is also narrower than failure of general causal identifica-
tion. The package guide discusses a frontdoor route as a distinct alternative. The proposed
product should retain the method attempted and its applicability rather than mapping every
false adjustment indicator to “causal effect impossible.” For a bank analyst, that distinc-
tion determines whether the next action is to consider another identifying functional, obtain
additional information, or correct an unsupported request.


27.9       Effect candidates, hulls and confidence sets
Tetrad’s inspected IDA constructor requires a legal partially directed acyclic graph and
continuous data. Its total-effect routine produces regression-based candidates across eligible
parent configurations. Candidate-specific exceptions are caught and logged without a typed
failed-candidate object in the returned list. Consequently, the downstream interface needs
enough information to distinguish a genuinely small candidate set from a larger intended
calculation whose members partly failed.tetrad contributors (2026)
   Three numerical objects must remain distinct. A candidate multiset records effects attached
to graph alternatives. Its convex hull fills all values between the smallest and largest candidate.
A confidence set is a random set with a stated coverage interpretation under a sampling law.
Neither the candidate list nor its hull becomes a confidence set merely because it has endpoints.
  The inspected IDA distance helper illustrates the distinction. For project values S = {0, 0.8}
and hypothetical truth θ = 0.4,

                        d(θ, S) = min |θ − s| = 0.4,     d(θ, hull(S)) = 0.
                                  s∈S

The selected helper uses the minimum–maximum interval, so it computes the second quantity.
Its empty-list branch returns the supplied true effect, which could even be negative. These are
static observations about that helper, accompanied by project arithmetic; no Tetrad execution
is claimed. They imply that evaluation and transport must define their set object before
27.9. Effect candidates, hulls and confidence sets                                          537


choosing a distance metric. An empty set of available estimates requires an explicit unavailable
or failed state, not an arbitrary scalar score.tetrad contributors (2026)
   The initial adoption preference is therefore to evaluate the existing Java engine through a
narrow process boundary, with endpoint roundtrips and typed failure handling. Porting an
isolated helper would omit the graph semantics that make its output meaningful. For aGrUM,
the existing C++ core and Python wrapper deserve comparison before any reimplementation.
Its saved build files declare version 3.2.0 and C++20; these are environment requirements to
test, not evidence that the proposed binary or wrapper already works.
Chapter 28

Design-based estimation, weak
information and diagnostics

28.1     An instrument is a scientific claim
Suppose a bank uses a rule-based funding incentive Z as an instrument for an offered rate
A, with retained balances Y as the outcome and baseline controls W . Software can encode a
regression system, but it cannot establish that the incentive has no direct effect on balances
or that its assignment is independent of omitted balance determinants. Those are properties
of the economic setting and information process. The package comparison begins after the
instrument, target population, timing and exclusion claim have been stated.
   The selected ivreg documentation describes ordinary two-stage least squares and robust
M/MM regression choices. Exogenous regressors in the outcome equation must also appear
among the instruments. An adapter should therefore retain explicit endogenous, exogenous and
instrument column roles rather than constructing the formula from a single list of predictors.
The robust regression option is an estimator choice; it does not supply a weak-instrument
confidence guarantee. The inspected package is ivreg 0.6-8. The broader AER family is a
separate source-review obligation.ivreg contributors (2026)
  Weak information changes the result contract. The inspected ivmodel documentation
exposes Anderson–Rubin and conditional-likelihood-ratio routines whose confidence-set outputs
are matrices of interval components. A client that extracts one lower and one upper endpoint
can lose disconnectedness or unboundedness. The appropriate object is
                                               J
                                               [
                                         C=         Ij ,
                                              j=1

where each component Ij retains its endpoints, possible infinite bounds and method-specific in-
terpretation. The number of components is part of the result, not formatting metadata.ivmodel
contributors (2023)
   For illustration, a hypothetical reported set C = (−∞, −2] ∪ [3, ∞) excludes zero while
remaining unbounded in both directions. Its interval hull is the whole real line. Replacing the
set with that hull changes the question “is zero in the set?” and replacing it with a midpoint
invents a finite estimate. Conversely, an empty inversion result is not equivalent to a missing
calculation. The proposed result schema must preserve these distinctions before any banking
decision rule uses the output. This hypothetical set is not a computed result from ivmodel.
  The two R packages are therefore complementary candidates. ivreg supplies a regression

                                             538
28.2. Regression discontinuity is a family of designs                                        539


interface with specific estimation and diagnostic choices; ivmodel supplies selected weak-
information test/inversion interfaces. A matched trial must align instruments, controls, scaling,
sampling assumptions and covariance choices. It must retain weak and zero first stages, singular
designs and unbounded sets. A regression returning quickly on a well-conditioned example
would not qualify the weak-information case, and the presence of an inversion API would not
establish coverage for dependent bank panels.


28.2      Regression discontinuity is a family of designs
A credit policy can change at a score cutoff, but several causal questions can be attached to
that threshold. A sharp design studies a deterministic assignment change. A fuzzy design
uses a discontinuity in treatment probability. A kink design studies a change in slope. These
require different estimands and denominators. Treating them as one generic local regression
would make an apparently comparable benchmark compare different scientific problems.
  The inspected rdrobust 4.0.0 documentation exposes sharp, fuzzy and kink settings, local-
polynomial choices, bias correction, bandwidth choices and variance options. The adapter
should bind the cutoff and running-variable units to the result and export the actual bandwidth
and inference settings. The bandwidth for a point-estimation objective and the choices
underlying a bias-corrected interval cannot be silently conflated. The saved 4.0.0 snapshot
predates the literature cutoff; it is not a claim that this was the latest release on that
date.rdrobust contributors (2026)
   For a fuzzy design, the treatment jump matters as much as the outcome jump. If a local
effect is expressed schematically as τY /τA , a small τA produces an unstable ratio even when
each fitted regression has a clean numerical convergence report. The bank’s first question
should be whether the score rule changes the specified treatment in the relevant population.
The software trial should vary that first-stage jump and preserve weak cases rather than
selecting only a strong demonstration.
   rddensity supplies a different operation: local-polynomial density or manipulation diagnostics
near the cutoff. Such diagnostics can challenge a design, but failure to reject a discontinuity
does not verify the assignment mechanism or continuity of potential outcomes. An interface
that displays “RD valid” after a density test would convert one diagnostic into a much
stronger scientific statement. A useful report instead gives the test, bandwidth, support and
interpretation limit alongside other design evidence. Discrete scores and mass points require
explicit attention.rddensity contributors (2026)
   rdlocrand represents another approach, based on a declared local-randomization window.
Its selected documentation states that a positive polynomial order uses asymptotic inference
and that confidence-set inversion is performed over a supplied grid. Thus a finite grid endpoint
is not automatically a finite confidence bound. If all evaluated values near the boundary
remain accepted, the result should say that the search is truncated. Extending the grid is a
computational remedy; it is not evidence for the local-randomization assumption. Window
selection, assignment probabilities and the intervention must still be recorded.rdlocrand
contributors (2026)
   These packages should be evaluated as a collection of design-specific operations. The
proposed integration uses a common report for the score, cutoff, assignment rule and target,
then separate method records. The product should not expose a single switch called “robust
RD” that hides whether the calculation is continuity-based local-polynomial inference or
local-randomization inference. The alternatives may both be useful, but they answer their
questions under different assumptions.
540                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


28.3     Sensitivity parameters are not missing truth
Two other R interfaces provide useful sensitivity summaries. sensemakr parameterizes omitted-
variable sensitivity through partial R2 quantities and observed-covariate benchmarks. A large
benchmark asks how conclusions would change if an omitted variable had specified residual
associations; it does not measure the actual association of an unobserved variable. The bank
must identify what makes a proposed benchmark plausible, and the report should retain both
the chosen benchmark and the effect scale.sensemakr contributors (2024)
   The selected EValue evalues.RR interface takes a risk ratio and optional confidence limits
and reports E-values for the point and the near-null confidence limit. This is a particular
scale-specific sensitivity operation. A default probability difference, a standardized regression
coefficient and a net present value should not be passed to it as if they were risk ratios.
Any conversion needs an explicit target and assumptions. An E-value does not estimate a
confounding correction or certify an absence of confounding.EValue contributors (2025)
   These tools can make a funding or credit recommendation more intelligible: they expose
how much an assumption would need to change before a conclusion changes. They cannot
supply verified instrument exclusion, known ownership, correct record inclusion or a gold audit
label. Their adoption is therefore conditional on a result contract that separates observed data
summaries, user-supplied sensitivity assumptions and causal conclusions.
Chapter 29

Longitudinal treatment, monitoring
and mediation

29.1      The history is part of the intervention
The servicing problem is naturally sequential. An initial action A0 , such as an early contact,
can change a later financial condition L1 . A second action A1 is then chosen using that
condition, and a later account cost Y is observed. The variable L1 can be both a consequence
of the first action and a determinant of the second. Treating it as an ordinary baseline control
erases that temporal structure. Treating both actions as one binary indicator can erase the
policy being evaluated.
  Consider a finite project mechanism in which A0 , L1 , A1 are binary and
              Pr(L1 = 1 | do(A0 = 0)) = 0.8,               Pr(L1 = 1 | do(A0 = 1)) = 0.4.
Conditional mean cost, in CNY per account over a fixed horizon, is specified as
                           m(a0 , l, a1 ) = 100l − 50a1 l + 20a0 + 10a1 .
The initial action costs 20 and reduces the chance of the adverse condition. The later action
costs 10 and reduces adverse-condition cost by 50 when that condition is present. These
numbers define the example; they are not estimates of actual bank effects.
  For a second-stage rule d, replacing the two action equations gives
                                    1
                                    X
                     V (a0 , d) =         m(a0 , l, d(l)) Pr(L1 = l | do(A0 = a0 )).                  (29.1)
                                    l=0

Equation (29.1) follows by enumerating the two possible conditions under the specified inter-
vention. It yields
                     V (0, 0) = 80,          V (1, l 7→ l) = 44,      V (1, 1) = 50.
The adaptive policy is better than always giving the later action because it avoids paying for
that action in accounts without the adverse condition. No policy-learning or global-optimality
theorem is needed for this comparison of three explicitly specified rules. A proposed general
optimizer would have additional obligations.
   Now hold A0 = 0 and consider an observed logger that gives A1 = 1 with probability 0.9
when L1 = 1, and 0.1 otherwise. The observed treated group contains a disproportionate share
of accounts with the adverse condition. Direct enumeration gives
       E[Y | A1 = 1, A0 = 0] = 58.64865 . . . ,            E[Y | A1 = 0, A0 = 0] = 30.76923 . . . .

                                                     541
542                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


The observational difference is approximately +27.88. Yet the intervention contrast that treats
everyone at the second stage, at A0 = 0, is V (0, 1) − V (0, 0) = 50 − 80 = −30. The sign
reversal is selection by an observed time-varying condition in this mechanism. It shows why
an interface must retain the treatment history and the distribution over which the policy is
valued.
   In an application, evaluating an expression like (29.1) from observations requires substantive
assumptions connecting observed conditional distributions to the intervention model. It
also requires that relevant histories and actions have support. The example supplies its
structural law directly; it does not demonstrate that a bank’s logger, monitoring or missingness
mechanisms satisfy those assumptions.


29.2      Point treatment and sequential software have different
          contracts
The selected tmle interface concerns binary point-treatment effects with missingness and
subject-ID options. It is a candidate for a suitable static effect question; that does not make
it an arbitrary longitudinal policy engine. The versioned documentation also contains a
treatment-missingness wording difference between DESCRIPTION and the selected Delta
argument. That feature needs implementation review before it is enabled in an adapter. A
convenient argument name cannot settle what missingness pattern the procedure supports.
tmle contributors (2025)
   stremr’s selected sequential g-computation and TMLE documentation is closer to the
servicing problem. It accepts time points, sequential outcome-model formulas, treatment
intervention probabilities, monitoring intervention probabilities and related weighting choices.
Treatment and monitoring are separate intervention components. A bank that increases
contact may also increase the chance that financial stress is recorded; holding monitoring fixed
and changing it are different policy questions. The interface should name which of these is
being evaluated.stremr contributors (2017)
   The same documentation makes several operational qualifications explicit. The Qstratify
option is labeled nonfunctional and an error source. Weight truncation and stabilization are
choices. Iterative targeting has stopping and iteration controls. A wrapper should reject
the documented nonfunctional option before execution and report the actual truncation and
stopping behavior after execution. A truncated weight or stopped numerical iteration is
not evidence that positivity or statistical accuracy has been established. It is part of the
approximation and diagnostic record.
   survtmle addresses another closely related but distinct problem: right censoring, competing
failures and cumulative incidence. Its selected interface supports two treatment values. A
competing failure must not be recoded as ordinary censoring simply to fit a common input
schema. In a banking setting, default, repayment, restructuring and account closure can
correspond to different outcome or observation events, depending on the question. The
adapter must preserve the cause, horizon and target, and the analyst must justify their
interpretation.survtmle contributors (2019)
   The initial software decision is to evaluate separate R operations for static TMLE, sequential
g-computation/TMLE, and competing-risk cumulative incidence. One common transport
envelope can contain their inputs and outputs, but it should not imply scientific substitutability.
The proposed tests include treatment-confounder feedback, monitoring-dependent recording,
administrative censoring, absent action support, and the distinction between a failure event
and a missing observation. These trials must assess the specific estimand and sampling law; a
29.3. Mediation changes the target again                                                     543


successful fit on complete independent records does not qualify a dynamic bank panel.
   The age of a saved distribution is recorded as evidence about that distribution, not as a
verdict on project maintenance. In particular, older stremr and survtmle snapshots do not
prove abandonment. Conversely, a recent version string does not demonstrate correctness
of every documented feature. Build compatibility and method validity require their own
observations.


29.3     Mediation changes the target again
A servicing team may want to decompose an action’s effect into a part operating through
customer engagement and a part operating through other channels. This is a different question
from the total effect of an adaptive policy. The mediator’s definition and observation time
matter, and a missing engagement record may itself be affected by contact intensity.
   medflex supplies a natural-effect-model interface based on expanded data. Its selected
documentation explains that the original mediator is excluded from the final natural-effect
formula and that a full bootstrap refits working models. Both details affect integration.
Expanded records must retain their link to the original account, and a bootstrap operating
on those records independently would not generally reproduce a bootstrap of the original
subjects and fitting procedure. Reusing a fixed first-stage fit would also change the documented
full-bootstrap operation.medflex contributors (2025)
   The proposed adapter should therefore export an expansion identity, the original sampling
unit, the effect scale, the mediator definition and the models refitted in each resample. It
should not market data expansion as a solution to unmeasured mediator–outcome confounding.
Sensitivity summaries can accompany the decomposition, but they remain conditional analyses
of assumptions. A total-effect engine and a mediation engine can both be useful without their
outputs being interchangeable.


29.4     What an R boundary must preserve
An R process boundary is a plausible first integration route because it permits evaluation
of the existing estimator with its native dependencies. It is not yet a selected or qualified
deployment. The input should contain a stable account identifier, the information and action
clock, event/availability times, the observation convention, the intervention specification and
the target’s units. Serialization must distinguish absent values from absent records and preserve
factor levels, censoring codes and repeated-subject structure.
   The output needs more than an estimate. It must identify the exact target, weights and
truncations, nuisance-model choices, fitted sample, uncertainty procedure and unavailable
quantities. A bridge may fail before the estimator runs, during fitting, or while translating
a result. These failures require different remedies. The first remedy is an environment or
transport repair; the second may require numerical diagnostics or revised assumptions; the
third requires correction of the adapter. None is a causal conclusion about the underlying
servicing policy.
   Porting is an alternative only after the complete method boundary is clear. Reimplementing
a final regression while omitting its expansion, sequential weighting, model-refitting bootstrap
or stopping conditions would create a different procedure. The advantage of a native port
must be demonstrated on the full workflow, including data transfer, model fitting, uncertainty
and failure handling. A faster final matrix multiplication is not enough.

Panel effects, event studies and
synthetic controls

30.1     Population averages and treated-group averages
A bank-wide policy evaluation can target all eligible accounts, the accounts actually treated,
or a particular rollout cohort at a particular horizon. Even perfectly computed effects can
support opposite decisions when the target population is silently changed.
  In a project example, half the eligible accounts belong to a high-response baseline stratum
H. Treatment is given with probability 0.8 in H and 0.2 outside it. Suppose the incremental
gross contribution of treatment over the declared horizon is CNY 400 in H and CNY 100
outside it. These are stipulated stratum effects, with no estimation noise. The population
average treatment effect is

                              ATE = 0.5(400) + 0.5(100) = 250.

Bayes’ rule gives
                                                 0.5(0.8)
                          Pr(H | A = 1) =                       = 0.8,
                                            0.5(0.8) + 0.5(0.2)
so the average effect in the treated group is

                              ATT = 0.8(400) + 0.2(100) = 340.

At a hypothetical CNY 300 treatment cost, average net benefit is −50 for the eligible population
and +40 for a group with the treated-group composition. The example does not authorize
future targeting using an observed treatment label; it shows why a result’s population is a
necessary part of its meaning.
   DRDID’s selected documentation explicitly targets ATT and distinguishes panel data from
stationary repeated cross sections. A shared API must retain both facts. A repeated cross
section does not supply the same account-level changes as a panel, even if its columns have
the same names. A result labeled only “average effect” would hide the target distinction
illustrated above. Double robustness also operates within the procedure’s identification and
nuisance-model framework; it does not establish parallel trends or assignment truth.DRDID
contributors (2026b)

30.2. Staggered timing and generated outcomes                                               545


30.2     Staggered timing and generated outcomes
A rollout across branches or customer groups creates treatment cohorts and relative event times.
A useful request must state the first treatment time, whether treatment is absorbing, which
units serve as controls, which relative times are supported, and how effects are aggregated.
Otherwise two event-study plots can represent different populations at the same displayed lag.
   did2s documents a first stage fitted on untreated observations and a second stage using the
full sample. The standard-error calculation is adjusted for that procedure and its clustering
contract. Passing the residualized outcome to an ordinary second regression and reporting that
regression’s default standard error would not preserve the documented method. The proposed
adapter must retain the first-stage sample, generated outcome, omitted periods, treatment
timing and inference settings.did2s contributors (2026b)
   eventstudyinteract is community Stata code. Its selected help file describes an interaction-
weighted estimator: estimate cohort-by-relative-time effects, estimate cohort shares, then
aggregate with those shares. It permits never-treated or last-treated control cohorts; when the
last-treated cohort is used, periods in which that cohort receives treatment must be excluded.
The help file warns that the cited validity result covers balanced panels without covariates,
while the implementation also accepts unbalanced data. Software acceptance of that input is
therefore not the same as an inspected validity argument for it.EventStudyInteract contributors
(2023)
   The package stores the interaction-weighted estimates and covariance in e(b_iw) and
e(V_iw). The ordinary e(b) and e(V) entries belong to the underlying interacted regression.
An adapter exporting the familiar default slots would risk returning the wrong object. This
is a concrete reason to qualify the statistical handoff rather than merely test that Stata can
launch.
   The same documentation describes pointwise intervals. Simultaneous coverage of an entire
event path is a different property. As a project probability calculation, ten independent
intervals each with exactly 0.95 coverage cover all ten targets with probability

                                    0.9510 = 0.5987369 . . . .

Actual event-study estimates need not be independent, and this number is not a measurement
of eventstudyinteract. It demonstrates that a collection of pointwise labels cannot itself
establish a simultaneous guarantee. A report must identify the family of targets and the
inference method supporting any joint statement.
   The Stata runtime introduces a commercial dependency, but it does not make eventstudyin-
teract a built-in vendor capability. The inspected community files also do not establish their
complete redistribution license. A prospective Stata bridge consequently needs both a licensed
runtime and a package/ dependency license review. Comparing that bridge with a vendor’s
own estimator requires the vendor’s dated technical documentation, not inference from this
community package.


30.3     Synthetic controls and the source of uncertainty
When a policy changes for one region, branch group or business line, a donor combination can
form a counterfactual trajectory. The donor definition, pre-treatment period, scaling, fitting
criterion and post-treatment horizon are part of the scientific design. The weight optimizer is
one component of that design. A small fitting loss does not by itself explain why post-treatment
prediction error should have a particular distribution.
546                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The inspected Synth interface takes preprocessed predictor and outcome matrices and
reports donor/predictor weights and optimization losses. This makes it a candidate for a
controlled weight-construction operation. The selected passages do not supply a universal
placebo or confidence-coverage guarantee. The product should report fitting loss and donor
dependence as diagnostics and attach only an uncertainty procedure whose assumptions and
target have been separately stated.Synth contributors (2026)
   augsynth’s selected dispatcher distinguishes single-outcome, multiple-outcome and staggered
settings, with distinct balance and regularization controls. Selecting the family name is
therefore insufficient to select a method. The downstream path and its inference procedure
must be inspected for the particular request. The author-repository snapshot was available
after a CRAN mirror lookup failed; that establishes source access for the inspected revision,
not a CRAN release history.augsynth contributors (2026)
   scpi’s selected documentation explicitly distinguishes in-sample and out-of-sample uncer-
tainty and exposes donor constraint sets, solvers and simulation choices. A generic scalar
“standard error” field would compress these components into a misleadingly uniform object.
The proposed integration retains the constraint set, solver outcome, simulation identity and
the assumptions used for prediction error. It also records failures: an infeasible or numerically
failed solve does not become a zero effect, and changing the constraint set to obtain a solution
changes the reported procedure. scpi contributors (2026)
   For banking examples, donor contamination is a substantive concern to assess: a nominally
untreated branch may be affected by shared pricing, national communications or customer
movement. This is a proposed design diagnostic, not an observed defect in a package or dataset.
The software should make donor membership and exclusions reviewable. It cannot verify lack
of spillovers solely from a donor weight vector.


30.4      Bayesian intervention analysis for branch campaigns
A bank that launches a campaign in one branch group may want the daily path of additional
applications, rather than a single coefficient pooled over all branches. Google CausalImpact is
a substantive candidate for this question. Its Bayesian structural time-series approach models
how the treated series would have evolved without the intervention, using its earlier history
and, when available, contemporaneous control series. The proposed reuse decision is to retain
the R implementation as a reference and prospective baseline, with an isolated R adapter
conditional on a compatible environment and reviewed behavior. No such adapter or fitted
package comparison has been executed here. This disposition preserves a useful alternative
without turning a forecasting model into a general identification engine. Causal banking
research proposal project (2026a); Google CausalImpact maintainers (2026a)
   Here the package name denotes google/CausalImpact. It does not denote the aGrUM
symbolic object discussed in the identification survey. The selected R source is version 1.4.1
at the commit beginning 0f5bf8d97cfb, committed on 31 March 2026. Its DESCRIPTION
retains a 24 September 2025 package date, but the later commit raises the required R version to
4.5.0. An unchanged package version is consequently insufficient to reproduce the environment.
The repository contains a three-platform release-R check workflow and substantive input,
model and inference tests; inspection of those files establishes intended checks, not that the
checks passed on the proposed platform.Google CausalImpact maintainers (2026a,b)
30.4. Bayesian intervention analysis for branch campaigns                                   547


30.4.1    The target and the identifying restriction

Let the intervention begin after date T0 , let H be the declared post-intervention horizon, and
write Yt (0) for the outcome that the treated branch group would have produced without the
campaign. The realized path contrast is ∆t = Yt − Yt (0). A posterior for this missing path uses
the observed pre-intervention response and the control history X1:T0 +H . In the state-space
formulation of Brodersen and colleagues,

                                      Yt (0) = ZtT αt + εt ,                              (30.1)
                                       αt+1 = Tt αt + Rt ηt .                             (30.2)

Here αt is a latent state, Zt maps it to the scalar response, Tt evolves that state, and Rt
maps state innovations into it. The observation and state innovations have the specified
Gaussian laws; trend, seasonality and regression components determine the matrices and their
parameters. Posterior simulation integrates over the stated parameter, state and variable-
selection uncertainty. The inherited method supplies a joint predictive law for the entire
missing response path, not merely separate forecasts at each date.Brodersen et al. (2015)
    For causal attribution, the control series must remain unaffected by the intervention, and
the pre-period relationship must continue to describe the untreated post-period response.
Neither an accurate pre-period fit nor a posterior excluding zero proves these restrictions.
National advertising, shared customer acquisition channels, a branch closure or a simultaneous
pricing change can make the proposed donor history inappropriate. A post-period control
may be available for retrospective analysis while being unavailable when a campaign is first
planned. The proposal must distinguish these two information sets before using retrospective
fit to justify a prospective decision.Google CausalImpact maintainers (2026a); Brodersen et al.
(2015)
  An exact construction shows the consequence. Let At = 0 for eight pre-period days and
At = 1 for four campaign days. Set x0t = 10 + t and suppose the observed daily application
count and control index satisfy

                         Xt = x0t + 15At ,      Yt = 100 + 2x0t + 20At .

In this first law, the campaign increases applications by 20 per day and also changes the
control index by 15. The pre-period relationship is exactly Yt = 100 + 2Xt . Continuing that
relationship into the post-period gives

                             Yt − (100 + 2Xt ) = 20 − 2(15) = −10.

The same twelve observed rows arise under a second law in which the exogenous control
path is the observed Xt , the campaign leaves it unchanged, and the response equation is
Yt = 100 + 2Xt − 10At . Under that law the effect is genuinely negative. The exogenous control
path is allowed to shift on the campaign date; no random timing assumption excludes that
possibility in this construction. Thus the identical observations, including perfect pre-period
fit, support opposite effects under different control-invariance assumptions. This is a project
counterexample to automatic attribution, not a fitted CausalImpact result or a claim that its
algorithm returns the exact linear forecast. Causal banking research proposal project (2026b)
   More generally, with pre-period slope β, donor contamination γAt and response effect τ At ,
the continued linear contrast is τ − βγ. This decomposition makes a sensitivity analysis
interpretable: an owner can state a plausible range for donor spillover and inspect when the
sign changes. It does not estimate that range from the same ambiguous history. Similarly,
an unmodeled untreated post-period shift δ would enter the contrast as τ + δ − βγ. A richer
548                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


state model can represent some changes, but cannot learn from missing untreated outcomes
which part of a coincident break was caused by the campaign.
   For an investment illustration, stipulate a net value of USD 1 per additional application and a
four-day campaign cost of USD 20. The two laws imply 4(20) − 20 = 60 and 4(−10) − 20 = −60
dollars. These are deliberately specified values, not measured bank economics. Their role is to
show why obtaining a defensible unaffected control or a randomized comparison can matter
more than reducing Monte Carlo error around the wrong counterfactual. Causal banking
research proposal project (2026b)


30.4.2    What the selected implementation actually summarizes

The R data path takes the response in its first column and controls in later columns. It
checks numeric input, requires more than three total rows and a pre-period spanning at least
three row positions, and rejects missing covariates. Some out-of-range period endpoints are
clipped with warnings. The automatic path standardizes using pre-period moments and masks
the response after the pre-period before fitting. The supplied-model path instead requires a
separately fitted bsts model with the post-treatment response missing. These details are part
of the computation’s information boundary; an adapter must not silently train on the response
it is supposed to predict counterfactually.Google CausalImpact maintainers (2026b)
   The automatic model includes a local level and optionally seasonality and regression. The
inspected defaults include 1,000 iterations, standardization, local-level prior scale 0.01, no
seasonal component and static regression. The static regression construction also supplies an
expected model size of three, expected R2 = 0.8, and prior degrees of freedom 50. These are
modeling choices to expose and examine, rather than bank-independent constants that need
no justification. The source passes seed=1 to its bsts calls, while predictive observation-noise
simulation uses R random generation. Reproducibility therefore needs the full runtime and
random-state contract; preserving only a displayed seed is insufficient. The number of iterations
is not a convergence certificate. Google CausalImpact maintainers (2026b)
   The distinction between latent-state means and predictive draws matters. The implementa-
tion averages state contributions for point predictions, but uses trajectories including simulated
observation noise for predictive quantiles. For draw b, the reported effect transformation is

                         (80, 120),   (120, 80),   (80, 120),   (120, 80).

  Relative effects require another distinction. The inspected summary computes draw-wise
