                        ψ = µ1 (W ) − µ0 (W )
                                D{Y − µ1 (W )} (1 − D){Y − µ0 (W )}
                            +                 −                     .
                                     e(W )           1 − e(W )

With the true conditional functions and exchangeability, each residual term has conditional
expectation zero. Hence E[ψ] = E[τ (W )] = 4. Conditioning the same score on a coarser pre-
action characteristic X gives E[ψ | X] = E[τ (W ) | X] when X is included in the conditioning
information. Estimating those functions, fitting a conditional mean and obtaining valid
uncertainty require additional regularity and sampling arguments. The exact score calculation
alone establishes neither finite-sample calibration nor robustness to arbitrary learner errors
Causal banking research project (2026a).
   This example motivates a concrete proposal requirement: record the eligible population,
treated subpopulation, effect modifiers, nuisance-only variables and weighting target separately.
A coarse risk-band request must not inherit an estimand merely because the nuisance model
uses many variables. Model specification, target aggregation and source-population weights
are part of the scientific contract. They must survive export to a library result, a CLI artifact
and an MCP response.


32.13.2     Stata: a developed conditional-effect workflow

The inspected cate documentation describes continuous outcomes and binary treatment, with
partialing-out and augmented inverse-probability weighting paths. Outcome and treatment
nuisance functions can use lasso, random forests or documented parametric alternatives; the
conditional effect can use a forest or linear regression. It distinguishes IATEs, prespecified group
average effects, and sorted groups constructed from estimated IATE quantiles. The distinction
matters operationally: a regulator-defined risk band is a different grouping mechanism from a
band discovered after fitting the same sample StataCorp (2025).
680                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The default cross-fitting specification randomly divides observations into ten folds. Default
honest forests split the tree-building sample between split selection and leaf estimation. The
manual explains that disabling honesty disables the corresponding forest standard errors
and confidence intervals. These are useful documented controls, but their purposes should
remain distinct. Cross-fitting separates nuisance estimation from the observation scored;
honesty separates tree partitioning from leaf labeling. Neither operation, by its name alone,
demonstrates validity when accounts repeat within households or outcomes share calendar
shocks. The inspected random-observation algorithm does not establish a household- or
time-dependent inference result; that comparison remains open rather than being converted
into a claim about every Stata command StataCorp (2025).
   The out-of-bag alternative requires forest outcome and treatment models. It cannot be
combined with the documented sorted-group option, and it is an alternative to the cross-fitting
setting. A proposed wrapper must validate these combinations before launching a job. It should
not expose cross-fitting, out-of-bag prediction and arbitrary grouping as freely composable
switches. The default propensity tolerance is 10−5 ; the manual describes an error for estimated
propensities below that tolerance and an option identifying offending observations. This is
a documented computational safeguard, not a certificate of scientific positivity StataCorp
(2025).
   Missingness is similarly method-specific. The documentation permits missing covariates
when all three models use forests, whereas other configurations omit affected observations; an
explicit option forces listwise omission. Changing learner settings can therefore change the
analyzed population. For servicing, the disappearance of accounts with incomplete contact
history may alter both estimated response and the operational population. A wrapper needs
input and retained-row counts, reasons for exclusions, and a clear distinction between a model’s
missing-value routing and a causal assumption about the missingness process StataCorp (2025).
  Postestimation includes conditional predictions, heterogeneity tests, group comparisons,
projections and evaluation of a prespecified treatment rule. Forest prediction standard errors
use a bootstrap of little bags; the linear-regression prediction path uses a delta method. The
policy command computes the value of a specified rule and can compare two rules. These
are concrete comparison requirements for the proposed library: a point estimate without a
target, prediction method, uncertainty convention and policy-selection history would be a
weaker deliverable. At the same time, documentation of a prespecified-policy command is not
proof that a policy chosen to maximize the same evaluation outcomes has valid uncertainty
StataCorp (2025).
   Stata is therefore a candidate for a licensed external reference execution, subject to edition,
automation and runtime rights. The proposal should seek matched generated-data comparisons
for ATE, conditional means and prespecified policy value, with identical samples and effect
modifiers. It should not propose copying proprietary implementation code or equate a CLI
wrapper with validated cross-language statistical equivalence. Exact version, seeds, defaults,
retained sample and inference method would need to accompany each result. Runtime and
entitlement verification remain open in this survey Causal banking research project (2026b).


32.13.3     JMP Uplift and JMP Pro Causal Treatment answer different ques-
            tions

The JMP Uplift overview describes partition models whose splits maximize treatment differ-
ences. For a continuous outcome, candidate splits enter a linear model through split, treatment
and their interaction. For a categorical response, the corresponding comparison uses a logistic
model. Predictor selection uses interaction significance with a Monte Carlo adjustment for the
32.13. Commercial heterogeneity tools: from a conditional effect to a servicing decision     681


number of candidate levels or models. This documented adjustment addresses a predictor-
selection mechanism; it is not a general proof of causal identification or uncertainty after all
possible model and policy searches JMP (2025).
   The separately versioned JMP 16 guide makes two particularly consequential interface
details explicit. Treatment value ordering determines the comparison, and more than two
treatment levels are reduced to the first level against all remaining levels combined. Validation
data help choose the split sequence. Those older-guide details must be rechecked in a chosen
contemporary runtime; they are not automatically a JMP 19 guarantee. Their architectural
lesson already applies: an adapter accepting three servicing actions must not silently turn
a three-action decision into a binary first-versus-rest contrast. Likewise, validation used for
selecting a tree is not a fresh final policy-evaluation sample. A node’s displayed treatment
difference or test statistic does not by itself settle that selection issue JMP (2025).
   JMP Pro’s Causal Treatment personality is a different pathway. The inspected 19.2
documentation describes binary or continuous treatment, binary or continuous outcome, and
average-effect summaries. For binary treatment, the report distinguishes population ATE
from ATET and documents inverse-probability weighting with ratio adjustment, regression
adjustment and augmented weighting. The specified propensity model is logistic regression,
with linear or logistic outcome regression according to outcome scale. These claims concern
those documented model paths, not an inferred native conditional-effect forest or arbitrary
machine-learning interface JMP (2026).
   For continuous treatment, the prose specifies a normal conditional treatment density with
parameters fitted by linear regression. It presents a stabilized-weight marginal structural
model and a generalized propensity score route to mean potential outcomes at specified doses.
Thus a continuous contact intensity or price change needs a dose and support definition, not a
reinterpretation of a binary-treatment coefficient. The displayed report discusses a treatment
and squared-treatment regression; its image-rendered equations were not transcribed into this
comparison. Only inspected prose supports the implementation description JMP (2026).
   The same documentation states consistency, conditional exchangeability and positivity
as identification assumptions. Empirical overlap plots can reveal severe support problems
in observed data; they cannot establish the absence of unmeasured confounding, a well-
defined intervention or population positivity everywhere. An attractive diagnostic plot must
therefore be stored with its interpretation and limitations. The proposal should compare
JMP’s documented reports as a user-facing baseline while retaining explicit assumption and
target records JMP (2026).
   The practical reuse choices differ by pathway. Uplift is a candidate benchmark for transparent
treatment-response segmentation under a suitable experimental design. Causal Treatment
is a candidate comparator for the specified average and dose-response models. Neither
choice establishes availability of an unattended server interface, MCP service or permitted
redistribution. Product edition and rights must be reviewed before an execution adapter is
approved. A file-based result import can be designed now, with an explicit unresolved-runtime
disposition Causal banking research project (2026b).

32.13.5    Overlap, selection and the economics of a policy

Overlap policy is not a minor numerical option. Consider a generated population with true
propensity 1/20, Y (1) = 10 and Y (0) = 0. If an unnormalized IPW expression replaces the
propensity by a floor of 1/10, its expected treated contribution is (1/20)10/(1/10) = 5, although
the true ATE is 10. This deliberately narrow counterexample concerns that unnormalized
formula. It does not assert the same bias for a ratio-normalized estimator, a correctly specified
augmented estimator or a separately defined overlap target. It shows why the adapter must
preserve the exact weighting and normalization rule, not just a boolean clipping flag Causal
banking research project (2026a).
  Policy value introduces costs and selection. Let π(G) be a fixed binary contact rule and
c(G) its per-contact cost. Its incremental net value per eligible account in the constructed
example is
                                 V (π) = E[π(G){τG − c(G)}].
Treating no one yields zero; treating only lower-risk accounts yields 3/4 dollars; treating only
higher-risk accounts yields −1/2 dollars; treating both yields 1/4 dollar. The highest-effect
group is not the highest-net-benefit group because its stipulated delivery cost is larger. These
are exact scenario values under fixed effects, costs and population shares. Capacity, customer
harm, uncertainty, interference and treatment feasibility would require additional constraints
before a bank decision Causal banking research project (2026a).
   Even without those complications, choosing a policy on its evaluation noise can inflate the
apparent benefit. Suppose two equal true effects are observed with independent errors taking
−1 and 1 with equal probability. The expected larger reported effect is 1/2. Selecting with
these observations and evaluating with fresh independent zero-mean errors gives expected
evaluation error zero. This elementary construction does not accuse a vendor of using an
invalid procedure. It explains why the proposed workflow must distinguish policy training,
tuning and final evaluation, and why a prespecified-rule command cannot automatically certify
an adaptively chosen portfolio Causal banking research project (2026a).
32.14. Commercial instruments and credit eligibility thresholds                              683

The inspected alternatives make the required comparison concrete. A credible proposed

  A first implementation should use a small declared set of targets and sampling laws. An

   The recommended comparison sequence is to reproduce the exact target examples, then use

Vendor execution is conditional on a licensed, versioned runtime. Code porting requires an

32.14       Commercial instruments and credit eligibility thresholds
A credit committee changes an eligibility rule at a score threshold. Approval increases above
the threshold, but some eligible borrowers decline the loan, some ineligible borrowers receive an
exception, and a second benefit may change at the same score. The committee wants the value
of extending credit, not merely the difference in outcomes between score groups. This example
connects instrumental variables (IV) and regression discontinuity (RD), while showing why
selecting a familiar command does not settle identification. The software must represent the
assignment rule, actual action, running variable, cutoff, observation horizon and uncertainty in
the local first stage. The analyst must defend what the assignment changes besides the action.
   Commercial software already provides substantial parts of this workflow. Stata documents
weak-instrument test inversion with disconnected, unbounded and empty sets. SAS and RATS
provide systems and instrument specifications; EViews provides several distinct instrument
diagnostics; SPSS exposes a two-stage least-squares procedure; and JMP documents equation-
specific model-implied instruments. A proposal that compares only conventional least squares
with its own set-valued interface would miss these alternatives. The relevant comparison
concerns the target, assumptions, numerical boundary, licensed execution and preservation of
the result between applications.
  The comparison below uses inspected official technical text for six commercial families and
pinned upstream Stata RD packages. MATLAB, PcGive and LIMDEP remain candidates
with unavailable essential originals in this bounded review. They are not classified as lacking
684                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


IV or RD. Documentation identifies the available operation in its stated edition; it does not
establish runtime performance or a successful integration here. Mutable manuals acquired
on 13 October 2026 do not prove their exact bytes existed at the 7 October literature cutoff.
Dated editions and pinned package commits narrow that uncertainty, and unresolved edition
and execution rights remain explicit (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026f).


32.14.1         A threshold jump is a target with assumptions

Write S for the score, c for the eligibility threshold, Z = 1{S ≥ c} for eligibility, A for actual
credit extension and Y for subsequent value. Where the relevant limits exist and are identified
by the score support, define

  ∆Y = lim E[Y | S = s] − lim E[Y | S = s],        ∆A = lim E[A | S = s] − lim E[A | S = s].
          s↓c                s↑c                          s↓c                   s↑c

The ratio ∆Y /∆A is a local observed contrast when ∆A ̸= 0. Its causal interpretation needs a
model. Under continuity of the relevant potential-outcome and compliance laws, an exclusion
restriction, a nonzero first-stage jump and local monotonicity, a binary action can give a local
complier target. Monotonicity rules out borrowers whose treatment response moves in the
opposite direction to eligibility. It does not follow from observing a positive aggregate first
stage. A constant structural-effect model instead supplies its own stronger interpretation.
Neither target is automatically the bank-wide effect of extending credit to every applicant.
   The local complier calculation can be seen directly in a stipulated limiting population
whose potential outcomes and treatment responses have the same distribution on both sides
of the cutoff. Under exclusion and consistency, write A(1), A(0) for eligibility responses and
Y (1), Y (0) for action outcomes. Monotonicity gives A(1) − A(0) = 1{C}, where C denotes
a complier. Consequently ∆A = P (C) and ∆Y = E[(Y (1) − Y (0))1{C}]; their ratio is
E[Y (1) − Y (0) | C] when P (C) > 0. The common limiting population is the scientific premise.
If eligibility itself changes the outcome or the two sides approach different potential-outcome
laws, this decomposition does not identify the proposed action effect.
   A finite authored construction exposes the exclusion issue without relying on a fitted
estimator. Let action probabilities below and above the threshold be .2 and .6, and mean
outcomes be USD 90 and USD 110. In one model, the outcome mean is 80 + 50E[A | Z], so
the causal coefficient is USD 50 and the reduced-form ratio is also 50. In another, the mean is
84 + 30E[A | Z] + 8Z. It has exactly the same two action probabilities and outcome means,
but a causal coefficient of USD 30 and a direct eligibility benefit of USD 8. With an expressly
stipulated incremental cost of USD 40, the implied value of the action is +10 or −10. These
equal summary moments are not asserted to be equal full distributions. They demonstrate
which additional restriction the ratio uses (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026e).
   More instruments do not automatically validate exclusion. Consider independent fair signs
Z1 , Z2 , V, U and the structural equations

                      A = Z1 + 2Z2 + V,      Y = 30A + 10(Z1 + 2Z2 ) + U.

An intervention changing A while holding its causes fixed has coefficient 30. Nevertheless
Y − 40A = U − 10V , so both population instrument moments E[Zj (Y − 40A)] equal zero.
Instrument direct effects proportional to their first-stage contributions escape this population
overidentification comparison. The exact sixteen-state enumeration checks the calculation;
it is not a vendor test run or a claim about a particular finite-sample rejection probability.
First-stage relevance, overidentifying restrictions and causal instrument validity therefore need
separate fields and explanations (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026e).
32.14. Commercial instruments and credit eligibility thresholds                                685


32.14.2     Stata already provides weak-instrument sets

The inspected ivregress manual documents two-stage least squares, limited-information
maximum likelihood and generalized method of moments. The postestimation manual distin-
guishes endogeneity tests, first-stage statistics, overidentification tests and estat weakrobust.
For just-identified models the latter defaults to an Anderson–Rubin test; for overidentified
models it defaults to a conditional likelihood-ratio test, with the documented generalization
for a nonhomoskedastic covariance estimate. The requested null concerns coefficients of the
endogenous regressors. Confidence-set output through ci is restricted to a single endogenous
regressor. A multiple-coefficient hypothesis test must not be exported as though it were a fully
computed joint confidence region (StataCorp, 2026g).
   The manual explicitly describes five confidence-set forms: a finite interval, a union of finite
intervals, a union that can include infinite intervals, the whole real line and the empty set. Thus
preserving disconnected or unbounded answers is already part of a documented commercial
alternative. The proposed library’s general quadratic-set operation does not by itself establish
a statistical advance over these procedures. Its potential contribution is a common scientific
contract across tools, complete request accounting and a decision layer that preserves the
uncertainty and its construction.
   The numerical distinction matters. For some cases Stata computes the inversion directly; for
nonhomoskedastic overidentified CLR inference it uses a grid. The inspected documentation
specifies an initial grid of 500 points, default bounds five conventional standard errors around
the estimated coefficient, adaptive expansion, a default maximum of 20 iterations, and options
controlling bounds and adaptation. Where critical values require simulation, the default is
25,000 draws and a seed can be supplied. These are documented controls, not measured
execution costs. An adapter should retain the requested and final bounds, grid size, simulation
seed/state, replications, covariance specification and all interval components (StataCorp,
2026g).
   The manual distinguishes a model-rejecting empty Anderson–Rubin set in an overidentified
model from an apparent empty answer produced by insufficient grid bounds in other cases.
This prevents a downstream agent from reading every empty set as scientific rejection. A
simple authored rectangle makes the danger concrete: M ∈ [1, 2] and Q ∈ [−1/2, 1/2] imply
the ratio relation set (−∞, −2] ∪ [2, ∞). A grid confined to [−1, 1] finds no accepted points
despite a nonempty set. This is an exact geometry example, not a reproduction of Stata’s AR
or CLR algorithm. It motivates recording whether the numerical search actually resolved the
declared domain (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026e).
   The official feature pages associate weak-instrument inference with Stata 19 and identify its
earlier StataNow availability in the Stata 18 feature listing. That evidence does not imply
that every fixed Stata 18 installation contains the same command or that the mutable manual
is identical across updates. The deployment manifest must bind the actual installed edition,
update and command help. The inspected licensing page distinguishes an identified single
user from a specified number of concurrent network users. It does not settle unattended
service accounts, embedding, redistribution or the commercial terms of a proposed MCP
service. Those rights and prices need a relevant license review before a licensed integration
trial (StataCorp, 2026g,f).
686                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


32.14.3     Systems, diagnostics and model-implied instruments are different
            alternatives

SAS/ETS 14.1’s PROC SYSLIN documentation supplies a useful systems-oriented comparison.
It documents 2SLS, LIML, K-class, MELO, SUR, 3SLS and full-information alternatives.
Its technical discussion states the instrument correlation and orthogonality requirements.
The INSTRUMENTS statement supplies all listed instruments to each first-stage regression; an
endogenous variable used as a regressor is declared in ENDOGENOUS. The worked 2SLS example
explains the FIRST option and warns that its ANOVA and R2 need a different interpretation
from ordinary least squares. A consumer therefore needs the equation system, restrictions,
instrument lists and actual estimation sample, not just a coefficient table. These inspected
pages establish documented operations; they do not settle weak-IV set inversion or RD support
in every SAS edition. The incomplete download of a later manual is excluded from technical
evidence (SAS Institute, 2015a).
   EViews’ instrument-diagnostic documentation distinguishes instrument summary, subset
orthogonality, regressor endogeneity, weak-instrument diagnostics and a GMM breakpoint
test. The summary can expose instruments dropped for collinearity. Its weak-instrument view
reports Cragg–Donald statistics, available Stock–Yogo critical values and moment-selection
criteria for the stated estimation methods. The manual itself qualifies the Cragg–Donald
statistic as applicable to TSLS and other K-class estimators while also displaying it for GMM
comparison. The proposed interface should carry that diagnostic qualification. A relevance
screen is neither a confidence set robust to weak identification nor verification of exclusion.
The extracted document’s equations contain image elements; only inspected textual definitions
and scope are used here, without reconstructing unread formulas (EViews, 2025a).
   IBM SPSS Statistics 30 documents a 2SLS procedure requiring the Standard edition or
Regression option. It exposes explanatory and instrumental variable lists, coefficient/covariance
output and command syntax. A regressor omitted from the instrument list is treated as
endogenous; the documentation normally includes the exogenous explanatory variables in both
lists. This is useful for a guided analysis interface, but a generic menu explanation calling
a fitted proxy optimal cannot replace the identifying assumptions, rank conditions or the
appropriate covariance argument. The inspected procedure page does not establish all-version
weak-IV or RD coverage. Its listed model-based intervals must retain their own assumptions
when exported (IBM, 2026b).
   RATS 11 provides a programmable alternative. Section 2.5 of its 2025 user’s guide specifies
the INSTRUMENTS list and INST option across its regression procedures, with system operations
using the documented GMM route. It writes the orthogonality condition explicitly and
distinguishes the covariance choice through ROBUSTERRORS and other options. No variable,
including the constant, is automatically included in the instrument list. This small semantic
difference can change a translated model. A generated command file must therefore declare the
constant, included exogenous variables, excluded instruments, sample window and covariance
options explicitly. The source does not support a claim that an arbitrary RATS program is a
valid IV design, or that every inference extension has been inspected (Estima, 2025).
   JMP 19’s September 2025 multivariate manual documents model-implied instrumental-
variable 2SLS inside its structural-equation modeling platform. It estimates equations sepa-
rately and reports equation-level Sargan diagnostics and the instrument set for each equation.
This is a valuable alternative when the analyst begins with a supplied structural model. The
instruments are implied by that model; discovering a valid credit encouragement from an unre-
stricted business brief is a different task. The documented local-misspecification advantages are
not a theorem that every structural misspecification or invalid instrument is harmless. Edition
entitlement and an actual scripted export remain to be checked for the intended installation. A
32.14. Commercial instruments and credit eligibility thresholds                              687


model-implied instrument should be identified as such in the shared contract (JMP Statistical
Discovery, 2025).
   MATLAB’s ivx/iv4, PcGive’s instrument-estimation path, and LIMDEP/NLOGIT remain
named acquisition leads. Their essential technical pages were inaccessible through the bounded
official routes used here. Consequently this comparison makes no technical equivalence, absence,
performance or deployment-rights claim for them. The concrete follow-up is an edition-matched
original manual and license record, followed by the same instrument, covariance, numerical-set
and export comparison. This omission limits commercial coverage; it does not invalidate the
supported findings for the acquired sources (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026f).


32.14.4     An open RD package on a commercial host has two reuse decisions

The pinned upstream Stata rdrobust help and source identify version 11.1.1, dated 1 October
2026. They document local-polynomial point estimation, robust bias-corrected inference,
sharp and fuzzy designs, distinct estimation and bias bandwidths, covariates and several
variance options. The help distinguishes conventional inference, bias-corrected estimates with
conventional variance, and bias-corrected estimates with robust variance. A result containing
only one coefficient and standard error loses that distinction. Its MSE and coverage-error
bandwidth choices also need their labels retained. The inspected source requires Stata version 16
semantics; this is a declared source requirement, not a completed compatibility trial (RD
Packages developers, 2026b).
   The masspoints options inspect repeated running-variable values. The default adjustment
enlarges preliminary bandwidths to include a minimum number of distinct values, with ten as
the documented default and an explicit override. The source computes unique-score counts on
both sides for manual as well as automatically chosen bandwidths. Its fuzzy branch rejects
the fully degenerate constant treatment case with no jump. That exact guard does not by
itself establish coverage when the first stage is merely small. Nor is robust bias correction
synonymous with weak-IV robustness. A matched trial must retain both bandwidth uncertainty
and weak local treatment uptake in its design (RD Packages developers, 2026b).
   The companion pinned rddensity help describes local-polynomial density manipulation
tests, bias-corrected and conventional statistics, mass-point adjustment and complementary
binomial testing. Its graphical path requires lpdensity. Those are useful diagnostics, not
a certificate that applicants could not manipulate scores or that all potential outcomes are
continuous. A nondetectable density change can coexist with another discontinuous policy;
a density rejection can reflect a measurement or design issue that needs investigation. The
proposal should retain test statistic, bandwidth, cutoff, support counts, test family and
qualification instead of converting a p-value into a Boolean “causal design verified” field (RD
Packages developers, 2026a).
   Discrete scores show the remaining information problem. Suppose the observed support
is {−2, −1, 1, 2}, eligibility starts at zero, and observed means are 80, 90, 130, 140. Let the
treated response function be 120 + 10s. Two smooth untreated functions are
                                          δ
                    µ0,δ (s) = 100 + 10s + (s + 1)(s + 2),        δ ∈ {0, 40}.
                                          2
Both agree with the observed untreated values at −2 and −1. Under sharp assignment the
treated observations agree as well. Yet the causal discontinuity at the unobserved cutoff
is 20 − δ, which is +20 or −20. Repeating these same scores indefinitely does not supply
observations tending to zero. Smoothness without a quantitative shape restriction does not
choose between these laws. A justified curvature bound, prespecified response model, local
688                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


randomization law or new score resolution is additional information. Counting mass points is
useful; it cannot create the missing support (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026e).
   The two upstream license files declare GPL version 3. The proposed default is a reviewed
adapter to a pinned distribution, with the applicable license obligations assessed for the actual
distribution and use. Stata’s host license is a separate issue. A port would need to preserve
the polynomial basis, kernel, bandwidth selection, bias variance, cluster corrections, support
accounting and missing-data rules, with independent reference comparisons and an appropriate
license decision. Rewriting a few coefficient formulas would not reproduce the package. Direct
adoption inside a licensed Stata workflow may be preferable for an existing user; a native
R/Python path may be preferable for another consumer, but cross-language equivalence is an
empirical obligation (RD Packages developers, 2026b,a).


32.14.5     The proposed product must compare complete decisions

A useful IV/RD request carries the business decision, target population, action and outcome
units, decision and outcome clocks, cutoff rule, running-variable precision, instrument origin,
exclusion and compliance assumptions, estimation sample and covariance design. The result
retains the target actually estimated, first-stage and support diagnostics, every interval
component, numerical search status, all failed requests and the source/engine identities. A
report must distinguish a nonidentified effect, an unsupported operation, a scientifically refused
request and an unfinished numerical search.
   The current local reference service can preserve generic supplied moment and sensitivity sets,
but it does not implement the acquired commercial procedures or the pinned RD packages.
The proposed integration should begin with one licensed IV path and one pinned RD adapter,
each compared with a separate exact or small numerical reference. The trial should include
strong, weak and zero first stages; valid and invalid exclusion; correlated and heteroskedastic
observations; coarse scores; manipulated cutoffs; alternative bandwidths; empty, disconnected
and whole-line sets; and grid exhaustion. It should record all model fitting, conversion,
failed-request and review costs. These are proposed comparison cases, not completed vendor
experiments.
   The investment decision is whether those paths reduce errors and repeated manual work
enough to justify the integration. It is not established by a longer list of estimator names.
Stata’s existing weak-IV sets are a substantive baseline; SAS, RATS, EViews, SPSS and
JMP supply different supported entry points. The near-term opportunity is to preserve their
scientific meaning, expose their limits, and connect a locally justified effect to a decision with
explicit costs. Measured savings and bank returns remain later empirical questions (Causal
banking research proposal project, 2026f,e).


32.15      R instruments and credit thresholds: preserving the
           design and its limits
A credit eligibility threshold can change access to a product without forcing every eligible
customer to take it. A bank comparing losses above and below the threshold must decide
whether its question concerns eligibility, actual take-up, the customers whose take-up changes,
or universal provision of the product. These are different interventions and populations. An
R interface that returns one coefficient under the label “causal effect” can conceal the most
consequential choice in the analysis. The useful comparison is therefore between complete
designs: the assumptions, target, statistical procedure and information that must survive a
32.15. R instruments and credit thresholds: preserving the design and its limits             689


library, CLI or MCP request.
  Six concrete package profiles supply complementary pieces. AER 1.2-17 and ivreg 0.6-8
provide separately implemented instrumental-variable regression interfaces. ivmodel 1.9.1 adds
weak-instrument tests and sensitivity procedures for a specified linear model. rdrobust 4.0.0
supplies local-polynomial estimation and bias-corrected inference at a cutoff; rddensity 3.0
supplies density diagnostics; rdlocrand 3.0 supplies methods under local randomization. AER
remains relevant both as a comparison and as a declared dependency of rdlocrand. The shared
ivreg function and class names do not make the first two packages the same engine.(AER
package contributors, 2026; ivreg package contributors, 2026; ivmodel package contributors,
2026; rdrobust package contributors, 2026; rddensity package contributors, 2026; rdlocrand
package contributors, 2026)
   The release date also matters. rdrobust 4.1.1 carries the package date 7 October 2026, but its
CRAN publication field is 23:20:02 UTC on that date, after the client cutoff of 15:59:59 UTC.
The cutoff comparison therefore retains the earlier authenticated 4.0.0 distribution. This
resolves the CRAN distribution question without asserting that every possible upstream
channel had the same publication history. Current manuals cannot silently supply capabilities
to an earlier version.(rdrobust package contributors, 2026)


32.15.1     What the instrument identifies, and which policy it values

Let Z ∈ {0, 1} denote eligibility or a randomized encouragement, D(z) actual take-up under
eligibility z, and Y (d) a fixed-horizon monetary loss under treatment d. Loss is positive when
it costs the bank money. In an independent-encouragement design, assume consistency, no
interference, independence of Z from the potential variables, exclusion of a direct Z effect on
loss, monotonicity D(1) ≥ D(0), and a positive first stage. Write C = {D(1) > D(0)} for the
complier group. Independence and exclusion give

                ∆D = E[D | Z = 1] − E[D | Z = 0] = P (C),
                ∆Y = E[Y | Z = 1] − E[Y | Z = 0] = P (C)E[Y (1) − Y (0) | C],
                 θC = ∆Y /∆D .                                                            (32.1)

The second equality follows because always-takers and never-takers do not change treatment,
while every complier changes from zero to one. It does not identify their unobserved treatment
contrasts, and therefore does not generally identify the population average effect. With a
deterministic score cutoff, global independence of eligibility is unavailable: an appropriate
continuity argument at the cutoff, or an explicitly justified local-randomization window, must
supply the corresponding design. Calling eligibility an instrument does not supply that
argument.
  Consider the following complete, project-authored population. The encouragement is
independent of type and has probability 1/2. All monetary values are hypothetical dollars
over the same horizon.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bk)

                            type     mass D(0) D(1) Y (0) Y (1)
                          complier   2/5   0    1    200     50
                                                                                          (32.2)
                        always-taker 1/5   1    1    200 150
                         never-taker 2/5   0    0    200 200

Mean take-up is 1/5 without encouragement and 3/5 with it. Mean loss changes from USD 190
to USD 130. Thus ∆D = 2/5, ∆Y = −60 and θC = −150, while the full population effect is
−70. If treatment costs USD 100, the stipulated complier treatment margin is USD 50, but
690                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


treating everyone instead of no one has margin USD −30. Complier membership is a latent
response type, so the first margin does not imply an implementable policy that identifies and
treats only compliers.
  The encouragement itself is an implementable alternative under this law. If it costs USD 10
per customer and changes treatment costs only through the extra take-up, its incremental
margin relative to no encouragement is

                            VZ = −∆Y − 100∆D − 10 = 10 USD.                                (32.3)

This calculation explains why the proposed service should return the reduced form and first
stage together with their ratio. A business request about changing eligibility may be answered
by the eligibility effect without extrapolating a complier effect to universal treatment. In
actual estimates, uncertainty in both components and their covariance must enter the policy
calculation.
   Two violations show what software cannot repair by fitting more accurately. If encouragement
directly lowers every customer’s loss by USD 20, holding the treatment law fixed, the observed
ratio becomes (−60 − 20)/(2/5) = −200 although the treatment contrast among compliers
remains −150. Alternatively, let compliers have mass 2/5 and effect −150, defiers have
mass 1/5 and effect −50, and the remaining customers never take treatment. Independence
and exclusion then imply a first stage 1/5, reduced form −50 and ratio −250. The ratio is
outside the two changing groups’ effects because the defier weight is negative. Neither an
overidentification test nor a first-stage statistic establishes the exclusion and monotonicity
assumptions used in equation (32.1). These finite examples isolate the failure; they are not
empirical evidence of either violation at a bank.


32.15.2    Regression interfaces and weak-instrument sets

AER documents a two-part regressor/instrument formula, with exogenous regressors also
included as instruments. Its summary method defaults to diagnostics being off; when requested
it reports first-stage, endogeneity and overidentification diagnostics. The dedicated ivreg
package offers additional formula conventions, including separate exogenous, endogenous and
excluded-instrument parts, and ordinary two-stage least squares or M/MM robust regression.
Its summary defaults to diagnostic reporting, and an alternative covariance must be supplied
as a function when auxiliary diagnostic regressions also require it. A saved matrix for the final
regression does not specify covariance for those auxiliary fits. (AER package contributors,
2026; ivreg package contributors, 2026)
   The integration should therefore name the package and version, construct an allowed formula
from typed variable roles, and record the realized design matrices, row mask, contrasts, weights,
intercept, numerical ranks and covariance method. It should retain aliased or unavailable
coefficients with their reasons. Automatically dropping an absorbed or collinear treatment and
reporting zero would change an unavailable target into a false scientific result. The M/MM
options address outlier-resistant regression; heteroskedastic or cluster covariance addresses
other uncertainty issues. Neither label by itself supplies inference valid under a weak first
stage.
   ivmodel describes a continuous-outcome model with one endogenous variable, Y = Xα +
Dβ + ϵ, and E[ϵ | X, Z] = 0. Some procedures, including its conditional likelihood ratio
path, add a linear first-stage model. The Anderson–Rubin and conditional likelihood ratio
interfaces return a matrix whose rows are interval components, together with a human-readable
description. The pinned source explicitly constructs whole-line and disconnected outputs.
Those are substantive answers, not serialization defects. (ivmodel package contributors, 2026)
32.15. R instruments and credit thresholds: preserving the design and its limits             691

   For the first row, searching only [−1/2, 1/2] finds no accepted value even though the true
inverted set contains two infinite rays. An interface must distinguish “empty on the searched
grid” from a globally empty set. It must also distinguish an infinite endpoint from missing
information and from an unfinished numerical search. Replacing the two components by their
convex hull would insert all the rejected values between −1 and 1; replacing them by a finite
interval would remove supported tail values. A monetary decision can change under either
alteration.
   Static inspection adds a specific implementation concern. In the pinned ivmodel CLR
routine, a numerical error during conditional p-value evaluation is caught and replaced with
zero; a root-search error similarly substitutes zero for an intermediate quantity. The AR routine
uses a projection F statistic, while CLR constructs a residual cross-product covariance. The
parent object’s generic heteroskedastic or cluster standard-error options do not establish that
these paths implement the corresponding robust tests.(ivmodel package contributors, 2026) A
proposed worker must expose or independently detect the numerical failure before accepting
the result. An explicit zero p-value is otherwise indistinguishable from the substituted failure
value at that field alone. The source establishes the branch; its frequency and native triggering
cases remain to be measured in a controlled prototype. This is a reason to retain the package
as a reference while withholding runtime admission for that path.


32.15.3     A local polynomial cannot fill a gap in the score support

rdrobust’s continuity-based profile distinguishes sharp, fuzzy and kink designs, the degree
used for estimation and bias correction, left/right estimation bandwidths h, bias bandwidths
b, kernel, variance procedure and clustering. Its outputs distinguish conventional estimates,
bias-corrected estimates and the associated uncertainty rows. The adapter must preserve
these associations; a corrected estimate with the wrong standard error is a different procedure.
Effective sample sizes, unique score counts and warnings are part of the result. (rdrobust
package contributors, 2026)
692                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


  Rounded credit scores make the support issue concrete. Suppose the only score values are
R = −1 and R = 1, eligibility is D = 1{R ≥ 0}, and observed mean losses are USD 100 and
USD 80 respectively. Two continuous potential-mean models agree at every observed score:

                               A: m0 (r) = 100,       m1 (r) = 80,
                                B: m0 (r) = m1 (r) = 90 − 10r.                              (32.7)

Model A has treatment effect USD −20 at zero, while model B has effect zero. There are no
observations approaching the cutoff from either side, so continuity alone cannot select between
the models. More customers at the same two scores reduce uncertainty about the observed
means but do not identify the unobserved limits. A mass-point option can alter estimation
behavior; it cannot create missing score support.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bk;
rdrobust package contributors, 2026)
   If additional substantive information bounds each potential-mean slope in absolute value by
L, and the nearest observations are distance δ from the cutoff, each extrapolation contributes
at most Lδ. In this two-point law the cutoff effect belongs to

                                θ(0) ∈ [−20 − 2Lδ, −20 + 2Lδ].                              (32.8)

The endpoints are attainable by choosing the two potential-mean slopes within the declared
bound. With L = 10 and δ = 1, the effect set is [−40, 0] dollars. At an assumed treatment
cost USD 10, the net-margin set is [−10, 30] dollars, and it does not justify a uniformly
positive-margin claim. These are identification bounds with known observed means; sampling
uncertainty would need to be added rather than silently absorbed into the slope restriction.
   rddensity supplies a different diagnostic: local-polynomial density estimates and tests for
a discontinuity in the running-variable distribution, with explicit bandwidth, variance and
mass-point options. Its documentation distinguishes a conventional statistic from robust bias
correction and warns about conventional inference with an MSE-selected bandwidth.(rddensity
package contributors, 2026) Even exact equality of the score density on both sides would not
prove continuity of potential losses. For example, a continuously uniform score can coexist
with another policy that changes at zero and affects loss, even when the treatment being
studied has no effect. A density test examines the score law, not that competing intervention.
Conversely, rounded scores need their own support and measurement discussion before a
continuous-density interpretation is applied.


32.15.4     Local randomization is an alternative design with its own obligations

rdlocrand assumes local randomization within a supplied or selected window. The window-
selection routine considers nested windows and covariate balance tests. That procedure is
useful evidence for design assessment, but a favorable balance p-value cannot prove assignment
independence. Outcome-driven window search also changes the inference problem. The
proposed request must retain whether the window was fixed before outcome inspection,
selected with pre-treatment covariates, or chosen through a procedure requiring additional
selection analysis. (rdlocrand package contributors, 2026)
   The distinction is visible in a finite reference. Fix six customers’ losses under the sharp null
at (0, 0, 0, 100, 100, 100) dollars. Assume exactly three are assigned treatment, uniformly over
the 63 = 20 allocations, in a window fixed in advance. If the first three receive treatment, the
difference in mean loss is −100. Exactly two allocations have an absolute difference at least
this large, so the two-sided randomization p-value is 2/20 = 0.1. This is complete enumeration
under a Fisher sharp null of no effect for any customer. It does not supply a general test of
32.15. R instruments and credit thresholds: preserving the design and its limits             693


zero population average effect under arbitrary heterogeneous effects.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026bk)
   The pinned rdlocrand documentation also distinguishes requested from effective polynomial
degree. For the documented mean contrasts and fuzzy procedures, positive degree invokes
large-sample normal inference; a randomization p-value is not computed. Some statistic/degree
combinations revert to degree zero with a warning. Fuzzy test inversion can require an explicit
effect grid. Consequently, the adapter must export the effective method, degree, variance choice,
assignment law, seed, repetitions, window and grid, not just the originally requested options.
HC3 standard errors do not confer finite-sample randomization validity, and a TSLS/Wald
label does not remove weak-first-stage concerns. (rdlocrand package contributors, 2026)


32.15.5     Reuse choices, rights and a prototype that can change the decision

The immediate recommendation is reference reuse with conditional plans for original R workers.
The dedicated ivreg interface is the natural initial ordinary-2SLS candidate; AER remains a
distinct baseline and dependency. ivmodel is valuable for documenting sets and sensitivity, with
CLR admission conditional on a qualified failure path. rdrobust serves an explicit continuity
profile, rddensity a supplementary diagnostic, and rdlocrand a separate local-randomization
profile. A direct port adds numerical and maintenance duties and should follow an identified
operational need. Existing grf effect-estimation and fixest panel-worker proposals do not
automatically qualify an IV target or this threshold design merely because they share an R
execution path.
   The pinned metadata declares GPL version alternatives for AER, GPL version 2 or later for
ivreg, and GPL 3 for the three RD packages. ivmodel declares GPL 2 or its local license file,
whose inspected text supplies an MIT alternative with copyright/permission-notice conditions
and a warranty disclaimer. These facts improve the package-level comparison but do not clear
the full dependency tree. rdlocrand imports AER and sandwich; other profiles also depend on
statistical, formula, matrix or plotting packages. Exact installed versions and their notices
must be included in the selected distribution.(AER package contributors, 2026; ivreg package
contributors, 2026; ivmodel package contributors, 2026; rdrobust package contributors, 2026;
rddensity package contributors, 2026; rdlocrand package contributors, 2026)
   The GPL texts distinguish running a program from copying, modifying and conveying
it, and impose applicable notice and corresponding-source conditions. Moving an engine
behind a process boundary does not itself decide all obligations of a particular distributed
product. Original-worker integration and porting therefore need a review of the actual
distribution, including third-party material. No current package recommendation grants that
implementation clearance. (Free Software Foundation, 1991, 2007)
   A useful public prototype would first compare typed requests with independent projection
and set-inversion references, then test the complete native workflow. The ordinary-IV cases
should vary rank, weights, missingness and covariance conventions while preserving the target.
Weak-IV cases should stress a vanishing first stage, disconnected sets, numerical integration
and root-search failures. Threshold cases should distinguish smooth support approaching zero,
a small take-up discontinuity, rounded scores and competing policies. The local-randomization
path should reproduce the twenty-allocation example before larger simulations, and analyze
selected-window behavior separately.
  Before final simulation, freeze the data laws, target, package/dependency versions, seeds,
replication budget, tolerances and stopping rule. Keep failed fits in the denominator and
report Monte Carlo uncertainty. Native execution, serialization fidelity, statistical calibration
and decision value answer different questions; passing one must not silently mark the others
694                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


complete. An LLM can help translate the business question, propose alternative eligibility
graphs and assemble these typed requests. It must preserve unresolved exclusion, compliance
and score-support questions, and must not convert a failed search or a diagnostic p-value into
a causal certificate. This design makes a bounded prototype informative before an expensive
experiment with bank data.


32.16       Commercial survival software and repeated banking in-
            terventions
A servicing team observes default, prepayment, hardship contact and changing arrears over
a loan’s life. It asks whether repeated assistance will improve customer outcomes and the
value of the portfolio. Several familiar software operations sound relevant: a survival curve,
a Cox regression with changing covariates, an average treatment effect on survival time, a
competing-event model and a latent growth model. They do not answer the same question.
An adequate comparison begins with the decision, eligible population, common time origin,
event definitions and intervention history. Only then can the proposed library decide which
commercial operation is a valid comparator.
   This bounded review develops eight families from official technical text: Stata, SAS/STAT,
IBM SPSS, JMP, Minitab, NCSS, Statistica and Mplus. MATLAB remains a ninth candidate
because both attempted official method pages were unavailable. Several sources identify an
edition; the exact NCSS and Mplus editions and the Minitab update remain unresolved. A
mutable manual acquired after 7 October 2026 does not establish its exact content at that
literature cutoff. Consequently the comparison supports its inspected method claims, not an
exhaustive historical market census or installed-product qualification. No commercial engine
was executed, and no price, deployment entitlement or performance advantage is inferred from
documentation (Causal banking proposal, 2026aq).


32.16.1     Time, events and causal targets belong in the interface

Let T g be the first terminal-event time under a declared feasible policy g, and J g the event
type, such as default or prepayment. A first-event survival probability P (T g > t) differs from
the default cumulative incidence FDg (t) = P (T g ≤ t, J g = D). The restricted mean time
without either event is E[min(T g , τ )], for a specified horizon τ . It is neither the unrestricted
mean default time nor a ratio of conditional hazards. A policy may change prepayment as
well as default, so changing the target can change the apparent benefit. These objects are
proposed contract fields, not automatically identified quantities.
   For a discrete two-period construction, write dgk and pgk for the conditional probabilities
of default and prepayment during period k among loans still active at its start. They are
mutually exclusive, with dgk + pgk ≤ 1. Set S0g = 1. Direct conditioning gives
                                                                  K
                      Skg = Sk−1
                             g
                                 (1 − dgk − pgk ),    FDg (K) =     g

The analogous sum with pgk gives prepayment incidence. The recursion is an accounting
identity within the stipulated policy law. Identification of that law from bank observations
requires additional causal and observation assumptions. In particular, replacing the recursion
by 1 − k (1 − dgk ) removes prepayment while retaining the same default hazards. That is
        Q

a different construction; the unchanged-hazard premise does not follow from observing the
original competing-event process (Causal banking proposal, 2026ap).

  Suppose both periods have default probability 1/10 under two generated policies. Policy
A has prepayment probability 2/5, while B has probability 1/10. After two periods A has
default incidence .15, prepayment incidence .60 and active probability .25. B has corresponding
probabilities .18, .18 and .64. Removing prepayment and retaining the default hazard gives .19
under either policy. All three default numbers answer different questions. A lower observed
default incidence under A can arise because more loans leave through prepayment, even though
the conditional default hazard is identical. Full enumeration of both period outcomes agrees
with the recursion (Causal banking proposal, 2026ap).
   Value need not rank the policies by default incidence. Stipulate USD 10 per active loan at
the start of each period, USD 100 lost at default and USD 20 lost at prepayment, with no
discounting. Expected active periods are 1.5 and 1.8, so values are

  VA = 10(1.5) − 100(.15) − 20(.60) = −12,        VB = 10(1.8) − 100(.18) − 20(.18) = −3.6.

The policy with fewer defaults has lower value under these exposed prices. These are authored
scenarios, not estimated bank effects or claims that prepayment always causes a loss. The
interface should return the joint event accounting and the declared value map, allowing different
accepted prices without changing the scientific target (Causal banking proposal, 2026ap).


32.16.2     Stata offers causal survival comparators with explicit limits

The inspected stteffects manuals document ATEs, effects on the treated and potential-
outcome mean survival times through regression adjustment, inverse-probability weighting and
combined methods. These are substantial existing causal-estimation capabilities. Comparing
the proposed library only with an unadjusted survival plot would understate the commercial
alternative. The manuals also expressly exclude delayed entry, time-varying covariates and
multiple-record data from this command family. A documented baseline-treatment survival
estimator therefore cannot be silently relabeled as an estimator of a repeated collections policy
(StataCorp, 2026i).
   Three scientific conditions remain distinct: conditional independence of treatment and
potential outcomes given the supplied covariates, treatment overlap and correct adjustment
for censoring. The documentation distinguishes likelihood-adjusted censoring in LAC-IPWRA
from weighted-adjusted censoring in WAC-IPWRA. In the inspected implementation, weighted
censoring requires random, correctly modeled censoring and a censoring process that does not
vary by treatment level. The choice is consequential for a servicing example where treatment
changes the chance that records disappear. Calling an estimator doubly robust does not remove
an identification premise or extend the documented censoring regime (StataCorp, 2026i).
   The proposed adapter should retain the chosen estimand, treatment/control labels, outcome
distribution, treatment model and censoring adjustment as separate fields. It should export
propensity scores, censor-survival probabilities, conditional means, covariance type and the
actual estimation sample. The manual documents an overlap tolerance that can stop estimation
and an option identifying offending observations. It also distinguishes robust, clustered,
bootstrap and jackknife uncertainty. A refusal at an overlap boundary belongs in the result,
not in an omitted request. Balance and overlap diagnostics examine supplied observed
covariates; they do not authenticate an unmeasured-confounding assumption (StataCorp,
2026i).
   Stata’s separate stcrreg command models the subhazard of a selected event with specified
competing events. It permits single or multiple records but not multiple failures per subject.
Its event codes, time interactions, cluster settings and cumulative-incidence interpretation
require a different conversion contract from stteffects. Recurrent missed payments and
696                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


terminal default are different event structures even when the raw table has the same number
of rows. The first proposed commercial trial should use a supported fixed-treatment case
and a separately specified competing-event case; it should not claim that either demonstrates
arbitrary dynamic-policy evaluation (StataCorp, 2026j).


32.16.3     SAS and JMP illustrate why competing-event outputs differ

SAS/STAT 14.1 PHREG documents counting-process input in intervals (T1 , T2 ], with covariates
held fixed within each record and event status at the end. Its examples cover repeated events
and delayed entry. This is useful for representing servicing records faithfully, provided subject
identity, actual entry time and covariate availability are preserved. The input representation
does not itself identify the effect of intervening on a history. It specifies who belongs in a
model’s risk set (SAS Institute, 2015b).
   The same edition documents a distinct subdistribution-hazard pathway through EVENTCODE.
Subjects with competing events remain in modified risk sets with weights; they should not
be exported as ordinary event-free subjects. The manual specifies a sandwich covariance, an
explicit cluster-ID route, cumulative-incidence predictions and pointwise interval settings. It
also states that several options and statements are ignored in this mode, including ASSESS,
BAYES and RANDOM. A generic wrapper that accepts every option and labels it effective would
misdescribe the analysis. The adapter must preserve the effective procedure configuration and
distinguish a pointwise band from a simultaneous or policy-value guarantee (SAS Institute,
2015b).
   JMP 18.1’s inspected Competing Causes page describes cause-specific survival estimation by
censoring events from other causes and states independence for its cause-wise interpretation.
Its Omit Causes control recalculates the display to illustrate removal of selected causes.
In the banking construction, removing prepayment and holding default hazards unchanged
yields .19, while actual default incidences are .15 and .18. Thus a cause-removal display is
not interchangeable with the observed cumulative default probability. Nor does the control
establish that a bank can remove prepayment without changing default mechanisms. This is
a scoped comparison of the documented platform, not an assertion that every JMP survival
capability shares that interpretation (JMP Statistical Discovery, 2024; Causal banking proposal,
2026ap).
   The proposal should therefore avoid importing a column merely named “survival” or
“risk.” Its descriptor needs the event set, horizon, conditional population, risk-set convention,
cause-removal premise where used, and uncertainty definition. SAS’s subdistribution output
and the inspected JMP cause-wise display are useful alternatives for different questions. A
matched experiment first harmonizes the question and only then compares numerical estimates,
diagnostics and workflow cost.


32.16.4     Time-dependent regression must preserve the decision clock

IBM SPSS Statistics 30 documents the system time variable T_, both for explicit time
interactions and for segmented measured covariates. Its weekly example combines logical
interval indicators with measurements. Statistica 14.2 separately offers survival-time inputs,
explicit time-function covariates and counting-process start/stop inputs. These are useful
ways to represent changing records, but a change of input form is not evidence of a causal
dynamic-regime estimator. Measurement time, availability time and the action time must still
be checked independently (IBM, 2025; Cloud Software Group, 2024).
  Consider 100 stipulated loans at a common initial eligibility date. Twenty default before
32.16. Commercial survival software and repeated banking interventions                      697


day two. Among the 80 survivors, 40 receive assistance at day two and 40 do not; ten in each
group subsequently default. Labeling exposure from the initial date by whether assistance ever
occurs gives risks 10/40 and 30/60, an apparent difference of minus 25 percentage points. The
future-treated category necessarily excludes the twenty early defaults. A day-two landmark
comparison gives 10/40 in each arm, but now concerns the survivor population. Neither
rewriting the label nor dropping early events recovers a baseline assignment-policy effect. The
construction diagnoses a clock and denominator error; it is not an estimate of Cox-regression
bias (Causal banking proposal, 2026ap).
   A converter should split records at declared changes while preserving which covariate value
was known immediately before the decision. In a (s, t] record, the end event and any new
information at t must follow an explicit ordering convention. A measurement collected after
an event cannot be carried back into its risk interval. A policy scheduled for day two needs
a definition for loans that default earlier. These are scientific design choices, not formatting
repairs; the software should reject ambiguity rather than choose an ordering from the row sort.
   Minitab’s inspected counting-process method table makes several conversion checks concrete.
It distinguishes fixed predictors from time-dependent repeated measures, records categorical
coding and tie adjustment, distinguishes robust from model covariance, and describes stratifi-
cation and proportional hazards diagnostics. It also documents excluded rows with missing
or nonpositive response times and an error when entry exceeds exit. Consequently the input
row count is insufficient: a proposed adapter should reconcile subjects, intervals, events and
exclusions, and preserve the effective covariance and tie method. This is documentation-based
design; exact edition and runtime parity still need qualification (Minitab, 2026).


32.16.5     Sequential confounding is not removed by a time column

An exact two-decision construction shows the additional causal work. Let A0 be an early
assistance action randomized with probability 1/2. Let L be later arrears, with probabilities
.8 under A0 = 0 and .2 under A0 = 1. The later action A1 has probability .8 when L = 1 and
.2 when L = 0. Define final default probability by

                          P (Y = 1 | L = l, A1 = a) = .1 + .4l − .05a.

Independent randomizers generate the stated conditional probabilities. This fully specified
law supplies consistency, sequential exchangeability and positive treatment support for this
example. None is inferred from a fitted hazard model or a software diagnostic (Causal banking
proposal, 2026ap).
   Marginally P (L = 1) = 1/2. Later assistance selects higher-risk histories: P (L = 1 | A1 =
1) = .8 and P (L = 1 | A1 = 0) = .2. Hence observed default risks are .37 with A1 = 1 and
.18 with A1 = 0, despite the negative conditional action effect. Under fixed policies, direct
summation instead gives
                             P (Y 0,0 = 1) = .2(.1) + .8(.5) = .42,
                             P (Y 1,1 = 1) = .8(.05) + .2(.45) = .13.
Their difference is −.29, while the observed late-action difference is +.19. The two policy
values are also reproduced by averaging the default indicator Y over the complete sixteen-state
law with weights
                                    1{A0 = a0 , A1 = a1 }
                                                             .
                                 P (A0 = a0 )P (A1 = a1 | L)
This is a population identity for the authored law, not a fitted weighting study or an asserted
finite-sample coverage result (Causal banking proposal, 2026ap).
698                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Conditioning on L can remove confounding of the later action while also holding fixed
a variable changed by the earlier action. In this construction, the controlled A0 difference
at fixed (L, A1 ) is zero, although the two-regime contrast is not. A single coefficient from
a regression containing A0 , L, A1 cannot be interpreted as the total effect of the repeated
policy without further calculation and assumptions. The proposed library needs an explicit
longitudinal target, history-indexed assignment/observation laws and a valid standardization
or other justified procedure. A counting-process adapter can supply faithful data to such work;
it is not a substitute for it.
   Mplus’s inspected Chapter 6 offers distinct discrete-time survival, Cox, parametric baseline-
hazard and latent-factor survival examples. In the discrete example, post-event periods
and dropout can share a missing-value code. A bank adapter should retain their different
reasons before conversion. The latent-factor example makes numerical integration and its
computational burden explicit. Its measurement model is a substantive alternative when
supported, but fitting a latent factor does not authenticate causal confounding control. These
examples justify a narrow model-and-output comparator, while the chapter’s exact edition,
intended runtime and rights remain unresolved (Muthen and Muthen, 2026c).


32.16.6     Censoring and failed uncertainty calculations remain outcomes

A small horizon-observation example separates an outcome model from its observed cases.
Half the population is low risk with default probability .1; half is high risk with probability
.6. All low-risk outcomes and one quarter of high-risk outcomes are observed. Observation
is stipulated independent of default conditional on this recorded stratum. Full-cohort risk is
.5(.1) + .5(.6) = .35, while complete-case risk is

                                   .5(.1) + .5(.25)(.6)
                                                        = .20.
                                       .5 + .5(.25)

Inverse observation weighting restores .35 under the known probabilities. It cannot do so
by arithmetic alone if the stratum is unavailable, the probabilities are wrong or observation
depends on unrecorded future outcomes. This finite missingness construction motivates the
analogous checks for a time-indexed censoring model; it does not establish a continuous-time
estimator (Causal banking proposal, 2026ap).
   NCSS’s Cox manual supplies a useful reporting comparator even without a qualified in-
tegration. Its run summary contains processed and estimation rows, likelihood iterations,
achieved convergence and completion status. The described stopping statistic is the maximum
relative coefficient change on the last iteration. A finite number in a coefficient table is
therefore not enough to classify a run as converged. The proposal should preserve these
diagnostics and distinguish numerical nonconvergence, a scientifically unidentified target and
an unsupported method. The source is an undated official chapter; it supports the inspected
reporting semantics, not a claim about a particular installed NCSS release (NCSS LLC, 2026).
   Uncertainty calculations need their own failure denominator. Suppose eight subjects include
only one with a required rare treatment history. An ordinary eight-draw subject bootstrap
omits that subject with probability (7/8)8 ≃ .3436. An unregularized mean for that history is
undefined in those resamples. Discarding them and silently drawing replacements conditions
the replication distribution on containing the history. It is not the unconditional bootstrap
originally declared. This exact occupancy calculation does not claim a 34.36% failure rate for
any vendor command: it specifies a stress case for the proposed wrapper. A cluster bootstrap,
stratified design, regularization or a restricted target is a substantive alternative with its own
assumptions, not a license to hide failures (Causal banking proposal, 2026ap).
32.17. Commercial survival options against the proposed service                                 699


32.16.7     Build a target-preserving comparator before a product claim

The current six-operation reference service handles declared graph syntax, a supplied-DAG
backdoor case, supplied-moment inversion, deterministic sensitivity sets and declared observa-
tion clocks. It does not expose fitted survival, competing-risk or dynamic-regime estimation.
Research derivations elsewhere in this proposal do not enlarge that service contract. The
inspected commercial procedures already supply serious estimation, diagnostics and reporting
alternatives; the proposed differentiator must be demonstrated in target preservation, sup-
ported causal scope and transparent uncertainty, rather than assumed from having an agent
interface (Causal banking proposal, 2026aq).
   The immediate route is a public/generated comparator contract. Begin with a fixed-
treatment survival target supported by the chosen procedure; add a competing-event case with
separately declared incidence and cause-removal targets. Verify subject identity, time units,
entry/exit boundaries, event codes, treatment levels, selected rows and output units. Then
inspect complete failure trajectories, censoring diagnostics and uncertainty settings. Repeated
policies enter a separate experiment with an explicit sequential identification argument and
exact reference law. No unsupported request should be routed to the nearest command by
name.
   Stata and SAS warrant consideration as licensed numerical comparators; IBM, Statistica
and Minitab supply useful clock, representation and diagnostic comparisons; JMP clari-
fies cause-removal semantics; NCSS exposes convergence reporting; and Mplus supplies
survival/measurement-model alternatives. These are proposed uses of documented paths.
Proprietary code should not be ported under an assumed license. A future adapter or direct-
use decision requires the selected edition, authorized execution mode, permitted exports
and applicable redistribution and benchmark-publication terms. MATLAB and uninspected
extensions stay unresolved. Missing evidence is not a negative feature finding (Causal banking
proposal, 2026aq).
   Only after the public/generated prototype preserves these targets and makes the intended
comparison useful should a paid runtime study or authentic bank experiment be commissioned.
Its cost includes the license, conversion, fitting, uncertainty replication, failed attempts, review
and maintenance. No current quotation or bank ROI is available from this review. That is a
specific later input, while the present proposal can already specify the scientific comparisons,
acceptance cases and unsupported uses.

The preceding survival analysis compares several procedures on their own terms. A procurement

is not evidence that its reference service computes it. The existing local service implements
a bounded supplied-moment residual inversion, a supplied DAG back-door construction for

method dispatcher returns unsupported for the three authored fixed-treatment survival,
competing-incidence and sequential-policy identifiers. This observation is a test of the local
dispatcher, not a vendor execution or an attempted encoding of every survival target. The

32.18      Commercial policy evaluation: what an offline score
           permits
A servicing manager comparing a contact policy with the existing workflow needs a value for a
specified action rule, population and horizon. Several commercial tools expose quantities called
policy value, reward, uplift or expected utility. These quantities support different decisions.
A static treatment-assignment rule, a learning procedure that changes after each event, a
sequence of servicing actions, and an optimum within a supplied decision model are distinct
objects. The proposal should compare them at those boundaries before deciding whether to
buy a license, integrate an engine or build a missing component.
   The documented landscape already contains useful capabilities. Stata’s cate postestimation
evaluates prespecified treatment-assignment policies. The historical Azure Personalizer service
documents offline comparisons of learning policies. GeNIe and its SMILE engine provide
decision analysis and expected utilities in supplied influence diagrams. Amazon Personalize
documents held-out recommendation metrics. JMP’s uplift platform provides a separate
targeting alternative. These are substantive comparators, but they do not jointly establish
a generally valid sequential causal-policy service. The following comparison uses inspected
official technical text; none of these vendor engines was executed for this review. (StataCorp,
2025; Microsoft, 2026a; BayesFusion, LLC, 2024n; Amazon Web Services, 2026a; JMP, 2025)


32.18.1     Four policy questions and one declared information clock

For one binary treatment, let X denote information available before treatment, Y (a) the
potential outcome, and π(x) ∈ [0, 1] a prespecified probability of assigning treatment. The
static value is
                        V (π) = E{π(X)Y (1) + [1 − π(X)]Y (0)}.
This is the target displayed in Stata’s policy-evaluation methods. The command also compares
two policies and accepts probability-valued policy variables. Its synonym estat tassigneval
should not be counted as a separate method. The premises of the underlying treatment-effect
analysis still apply. A rule chosen by maximizing this same evaluation sample is a different
inferential target from a prespecified rule; a changing sequence of actions is not represented
merely by placing its last action in the treatment column. (StataCorp, 2025)
  For sequential servicing, let Ht be the observed history immediately before action At , Rt
the subsequent net cash flow, bt (a | h) the logging probability, and πt (a | h) the proposed

The change-of-law argument needs consistent actions and outcomes, sufficient histories for
sequential assignment, positive logging probability wherever the target policy acts, and an
appropriate initial population and observation law. Under a correctly specified observed-
state experiment, the likelihood ratios change the action distribution while leaving the shared
environmental mechanisms unchanged. Jiang and Li develop trajectory and stepwise importance
sampling and a sequential doubly robust construction; their discussion also requires separating
a data-derived target policy from the sample used for evaluation. That result does not grant
causal validity to arbitrary hidden servicing states or misrecorded logging probabilities. (Jiang
and Li, 2016)
   A supplied-model decision engine answers a third question: what action has the highest
expected utility if its probability tables, information sets and utilities are correct? A recom-
