Matched qualification and build, buy
or integrate decisions

39.1     An admissible route before a preferred supplier
A bank selecting causal software is choosing a procedure for a specified decision, together with
the means of maintaining and operating that procedure. Discovery for a supplied independent
sample, identification in a latent graph, and evaluation of a repeated servicing policy are
different services. The software survey establishes candidate routes and their restrictions. This
chapter asks how those routes should be compared once a bounded use has been chosen, and
what evidence could justify direct adoption, a process bridge, a port, an internal implementation,
a commercial purchase, or reference-only use.
  Let q denote the complete requested scientific operation and s a declared workload scenario.
For candidate route j, write

              aj (q, s) = amethod
                           j      (q, s) arepresentation
                                          j              (q, s) aoperating
                                                                 j         (q, s) arights
                                                                                   j      (q, s),

where each factor is one only when the corresponding necessary condition has been established
in the declared scope. The factors describe compatibility with the causal method, preservation
of its objects, the required runtime behavior, and the intended reuse arrangement. An unknown
condition remains unresolved; it is not a passing value. This is an admission rule for a proposed
comparison, not a probability model or a weighted capability score. A low price cannot
compensate for a method that answers a different intervention query, and a favorable license
cannot supply missing uncertainty. (Causal banking research project, 2026as)
    Admission should distinguish hard scientific restrictions from tunable engineering require-
ments. If the selected routine only handles independent units, declaring a panel identifier does
not make it a dependent-data method. If the issue is process startup, an alternative process
lifecycle may resolve it without changing the target. If the issue is an unsupported counterfac-
tual, an adapter cannot resolve it by relabelling an associational prediction. This classification
tells the proposal whether to restrict the supported domain, implement a conversion, select
another scientific method, or commission research. It prevents an implementation task from
carrying an implicit promise to solve nonidentification.
   The inspected candidates illustrate why a route is more specific than a package name. The
pinned pgmpy review finds an advertised adjustment option whose selected implementation
raises NotImplementedError; that option cannot enter the executable comparison merely
because it appears in a guide. The selected Tetrad review supports a restricted Java PC
prototype subject to runtime, conversion and reuse conditions, not an unrestricted Java

                                                     745
746                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


discovery service. The CausalNex review treats the inspected discontinued source as an
archival comparison; maintenance and unreported solver behavior remain part of the decision.
These are findings for inspected revisions. They do not establish that another release, method
or supplier has the same restriction. (pgmpy contributors, 2026a; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026r; mckinsey/causalnex, 2026b)


39.2     Matching the experiment and its denominator
A comparison requires a common request population before it requires a common timer. Let
Q be the prespecified distribution of requested cases, including difficult and unsupported
cases relevant to the proposed service. For each route, retain a disposition Rj (q) such as
computed, unsupported, unavailable, or invalid input, together with the target and uncertainty
object actually returned. The intended denominator is the requested workload. A conditional
accuracy figure among successful outputs remains useful, but it answers a different question
from the probability of receiving a correct, usable result for an arbitrary requested case.
   For estimator comparisons, a matched case must bind the population measure, intervention,
horizon, information clock and uncertainty meaning. The two procedures may legitimately
use different computational strategies. They may also use different statistical methods if the
purpose is a method comparison, provided the target and admissible information are held
fixed and each method’s assumptions are exposed. A port-equivalence study has a narrower
objective: it tests whether the intended procedure survives translation, including defaults,
failure behavior, randomness and diagnostic outputs. Mixing these objectives would make a
better result ambiguous between a scientific change and a faithful implementation.
   The first prototype should contain three complementary groups. Exact finite or analytic
constructions test meanings and numerical identities. Generated sampling experiments test
operating characteristics under explicit truth. Documented public datasets test preparation,
interfaces, and useful questions within their evidence limits. Agreement on public observational
data is not itself a causal-truth label. A benchmark with known intervention assignments
supports a stronger comparison only for its documented population and design. The proposal
can therefore establish the merit and practicality of a later bank experiment without pretending
that public data reproduces private bank assignment, identity or operational truth. (Causal
banking research project, 2026as)
   Workload matching also includes resource and information budgets. Both routes should
receive the same permitted data and expert restrictions; preprocessing, search, tuning and
human repair must be charged consistently. If one candidate uses a larger graph-search
budget, report both a fixed-budget comparison and the declared cost–quality tradeoff. For a
bridge, include serialization, data movement, environment startup, numerical work, uncertainty
construction and publication. Warm and cold executions are distinct operating scenarios.
Reuse of a fitted model or cached result is valid only when the identity and invalidation rule
agree with the intended service.


39.3     A paired comparison can reverse a preferred route
Consider an authored workload law with 1,000 equally weighted request slots. Each route
produces a correct usable answer, a wrong answer, or an unavailable answer. The following
table specifies the entire paired law; it is not an observed package trial. A row refers to route
39.4. What a failure-free prototype establishes                                             747


A, and a column to route B.

                               B : correct B : wrong B : unavailable total
                 A : correct          600         20              10  630
                 A : wrong              10         5               5   20
               A : unavailable        190         75              85  350
                    total             800        100             100 1000

Among available answers, A is correct in 630/650 = 126/130 cases and B in 800/900 = 8/9.
On the requested denominator, their correct-answer rates are 0.63 and 0.80. Thus A has higher
conditional correctness while B supplies more correct answers overall. Neither statement alone
selects the preferred banking workflow. (Causal banking research project, 2026at)
  Suppose a correct answer has stipulated gross value USD 10, a wrong answer causes loss ℓ,
unavailable answers have zero gross value, and the complete per-request costs are USD 1 for A
and USD 2 for B, charged on all requests. Their total values are

                 VA = 630(10) − 20ℓ − 1000,       VB = 800(10) − 100ℓ − 2000.

The difference is VB − VA = 700 − 80ℓ. Route B is preferred only when ℓ < 8.75. At ℓ = 40,
the totals are USD 4,500 and USD 2,000, respectively. This threshold is a sensitivity result
under a specified loss and fallback convention. It is not a market price or a claim about a
bank’s actual error cost. If unavailable answers require manual review, that fallback has its
own value, delay and cost and must be incorporated in both workflows. (Causal banking
research project, 2026at)
  Pairing provides information that two separate success percentages lose. Let Xj be the
indicator of a correct usable answer from route j, and let D = XB − XA . In the stipulated
law, D = 1 on 200 slots, D = −1 on 30, and D = 0 on 770. Hence

                      E(D) = 0.17,        Var(D) = 0.23 − 0.172 = 0.2011.

Equivalently, the covariance of the two correctness indicators is 0.600 − (0.63)(0.80) = 0.096,
and
                        Var(D) = 0.63(0.37) + 0.80(0.20) − 2(0.096).
If independent paired requests were drawn from this law, the sample mean difference would have
variance 0.2011/n. Treating the two outcomes as independent instead gives 0.3931/n. These
expressions describe the stipulated sampling experiment; they are not confidence statements
for a fixed benchmark table. Repeated variants from one customer, graph or source document
require their actual group dependence to be retained. (Causal banking research project, 2026at)
   The paired table also makes disagreement review efficient. The 200 cases on which only B
is correct and the 30 on which only A is correct are natural targets for diagnosing method
domain, conversion or failure handling. They should remain in the final outcome accounting
after investigation. Correcting a test oracle or an adapter creates a successor comparison with
explicit changes; removing disagreeing cases until the routes agree would change the workload
and obscure the reason for the improvement.


39.4      What a failure-free prototype establishes
A set of successful fixtures proves the stated examples, not universal compatibility. A small
stochastic qualification experiment supplies a different, conditional statement. Suppose a fixed
workload distribution has independent Bernoulli failures with probability p, and the evaluation
748                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


contains n prespecified requests. If zero failures occur, the probability of that observation is
(1 − p)n . Inverting the one-sided test at error probability α gives the upper bound

                                         pU = 1 − α1/n .

With n = 100 and α = 0.05, this is approximately 0.0295. Zero failures among a hundred
independent requests therefore does not establish a one-percent failure ceiling at this level.
The exact inequality
                                     (0.99)n ≤ 0.05
first holds at n = 299. This is a prospective sample-size implication if that design and ceiling
are appropriate, not a claim that the prototype has passed it. (Causal banking research project,
2026at)
   For eight separately declared profiles, a simultaneous statement needs its own error allocation.
Assigning α/8 to each and applying the union bound yields joint error at most α without
requiring independence between profiles. Each within-profile zero-failure calculation still
requires its stated independent Bernoulli experiment. At a common one-percent ceiling,
(0.99)n ≤ 0.05/8 first holds at n = 505 requests per profile. A single pooled bound would
answer a different question and could hide a bad rare profile. Conversely, infinitely many graph
families or deployment regimes cannot be qualified by calling eight chosen profiles exhaustive.
(Causal banking research project, 2026at)
   These calculations motivate a bounded qualification protocol rather than a large unstructured
test collection. Define the admitted profile, failure event, request distribution, denominator,
sample size, simultaneous statement and stopping rule before evaluation. A crash, timeout,
missing interval or wrong target is not automatically the same event; retain their separate
frequencies and any combined service failure used for acceptance. If a generated experiment
tests confidence-set coverage, its event is whether the known fixed target is contained, together
with declared availability and precision requirements. Statistical coverage, computation
completion and useful decision resolution need separate criteria. Adaptive test selection or
optional stopping requires a design that justifies it; repeatedly adding cases until the displayed
bound passes does not preserve this fixed-sample argument.
   An exact finite-domain test can offer stronger evidence within a smaller domain. Exhausting
all supported endpoint pairs or all three-node graphs may settle the declared finite conversion
behavior. It does not become a sampling confidence claim, nor does it establish arbitrary-
dimensional algorithm correctness. The topology examples show how exact counterexamples
and actual codecs complement rather than replace a generated performance study. The
proposal should state which of these evidence forms closes each acceptance condition. (Causal
banking research project, 2026aw,au)


39.5      A port must preserve the full procedure
Porting has several possible meanings. A mathematical reimplementation may reproduce
a functional using a different algorithm. A compatibility port may seek the same defaults,
accepted inputs, warnings and output semantics as a specified release. A new method may
deliberately improve an estimator or uncertainty construction. Each can be useful, but each
requires a different comparison. The product should not retain an upstream method name
while changing its weighting measure, policy target or interval construction without declaring
that change. Source-level agreement is particularly weak when a caller changes the meaning of
an otherwise correctly translated routine.
39.6. Lifecycle cost conditional on qualified behavior                                       749


   For the inspected CausalPy route, the proposed sharp-discontinuity contract distinguishes a
finite-epsilon prediction contrast from a threshold estimand, and a point backend from posterior
draws and predictive responses. A port that reproduces a plotted difference while discarding
epsilon, treatment direction or left/right support has not reproduced the causal operation. For
the d3rlpy route, the proposed contract separates episode termination, administrative cutoff,
missing continuation, initial-state population, policy identity and the physical discount clock.
Reproducing an optimizer while averaging the wrong initial states can produce a different
policy value. These source-grounded contracts specify tests to execute before enabling the
proposed integrations; they are not records of native acceptance trials. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026c,at)
   Numerical acceptance should be stated in the coordinates of the decision. Let θe approximate
an independently defined reference θ, with justified deterministic bounds |θei − θi | ≤ εi . For
fixed weights wi and cost c, the triangle inequality gives
                                                                !
                            X                     X                     X
                                 wi θei − c −          wi θ i − c   ≤       |wi |εi .
                             i                     i                    i

This transports certified numerical error; it does not certify the reference’s causal validity or
its sampling uncertainty. Relative-error tolerances alone are unsuitable near a zero-valued
target, and coordinate tolerances that look small can still reverse a near-threshold decision.
   For a stipulated example, let w = (3/4, 1/4), θe = (24, −8) USD, c = 15 USD and ε = (2, 4)
USD. The approximate net value is USD 1, but its numerical error allowance is USD 2.5,
giving the enclosure [−1.5, 3.5]. The permitted reference θ = (23, −10) yields USD −0.25.
Declaring a profitable action from the approximate point would exceed the available numerical
evidence. Reducing the numerical budget, retaining an unresolved decision, or changing the
information/design are distinct responses. If sampling uncertainty is also present, the numerical
enclosure must be combined with that construction under its actual guarantee, not relabelled
as another confidence level. (Causal banking research project, 2026at)
   Port acceptance should consequently include independent algebraic references, metamorphic
transformations with known consequences, adverse inputs, and method-specific numerical
error checks. Graph and set outputs need structural and containment criteria, not only a
mean squared difference. Seeds, thread counts, solver versions, hardware-dependent arithmetic
and stopping conditions belong in the tested procedure. An upstream test suite is valuable
inherited evidence, but common implementation mistakes can survive a direct translation
of both code and tests. Independent references should target the scientific properties the
proposed product promises.


39.6      Lifecycle cost conditional on qualified behavior
Only admitted routes should enter a procurement comparison. For route j, a transparent
planning quantity over T periods is
                                         T
                                         X
                            Cj = F j +          dt {Ljt + Mjt + Nt cjt + Ijt },
                                         t=1

where Fj is initial engineering and qualification cost, Ljt license or subscription expense, Mjt
maintenance and compatibility work, Nt cjt workload-dependent cost, and Ijt the expected
incident or recovery cost under an explicitly stated model. The dt are the chosen discount
factors. These terms need not be known at proposal time. Ranges and break-even conditions
are more informative than an invented precise total, and omitted costs must remain visible.
750                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


  Suppose, purely for planning, a bridge costs USD 100,000 initially, USD 20,000 per year to
maintain and USD 3 per request. A port costs USD 300,000 initially, USD 80,000 per year
and USD 1 per request. Ignore discounting over three years and assume both routes meet
exactly the same service requirements. Ignoring maintenance suggests a break-even volume of
                                  300000 − 100000
                                                  = 100000
                                       3−1
requests. Including the three years of maintenance gives
                       300000 − 100000 + 3(80000 − 20000)
                                                          = 190000.
                                     3−1
At 150,000 total requests the bridge costs USD 610,000 and the port USD 690,000. The
cheaper numerical kernel does not establish the cheaper full route. These are exact hypothetical
calculations, not measured costs, vendor quotes or return on investment. Their practical use
is to identify which workload and maintenance estimates could change the decision. (Causal
banking research project, 2026at)
   The same decomposition organizes substantive alternatives. Direct adoption can minimize
translation work when the upstream environment and result contract fit, but it retains
dependency and upgrade obligations. A process bridge can isolate an environment and preserve
the upstream implementation, at the cost of conversion, lifecycle and operational work. A
port may serve an unavailable deployment environment or a demonstrated bottleneck, but
incurs full-procedure equivalence and maintenance responsibilities. An internal implementation
is justified when the required scientific construction or result type is absent from suitable
existing routes; its comparison should include the continuing cost of independent verification.
Reference-only use is appropriate when an implementation clarifies a method but its runtime,
rights, maintenance or scientific domain is unsuitable for the proposed service.
   A commercial purchase is evaluated through the same admitted operation and whole-
workflow cost. The exact edition, automation route, technical method, diagnostics, export
semantics and intended deployment terms matter. Community extensions should not be
attributed to the vendor’s supported core without evidence. Missing technical documentation
leaves a capability unresolved; it does not establish absence. Unquoted prices remain unknown.
The commercial comparison therefore supports a request for a matched evaluation or a bounded
purchase decision when its evidence permits one, rather than an unsupported claim of product
superiority. (Causal banking research project, 2026as)


39.7     A proposal decision that can be executed
The immediate deliverable should be a conditional route decision, with a specific supported
profile and a finite acceptance experiment. A useful decision identifies the candidate revision
and environment, the exact causal operation, the alternative route, the information and
compute budget, the correctness and failure events, the required numerical or uncertainty
guarantee, and the cost quantities that remain to be measured. It also states what outcome
would change the choice. A preferred prototype candidate is therefore compatible with deferred
integration; it expresses where the next evidence is most valuable without asserting that the
evidence exists. (Causal banking research project, 2026as)
  For a discovery prototype, a restricted supplied regime and independently checked graph
conversions precede an effect claim. For a threshold design, the treatment direction, support
and requested limit precede a comparison of predictions. For servicing, the complete policy
and episode population precede offline value comparison. For funding, weak information and
39.8. Commercial orchestration and the recovery of a causal batch                             751


the topology of the effect set precede a monetary recommendation. These conditions let
independent prototype routes advance while another method remains unsupported. They also
make rejection useful: a documented mismatch removes a route from the admitted domain
and identifies whether new information, another method or engineering work could restore it.
   No proposed acceptance test can make observationally indistinguishable causal models
distinguishable by computation alone. Nor can it invent bank precision targets, authentic
identity and assignment records, supplier commitments or independent approval. Those limits
should govern the claim made by the proposal, while public/generated prototype comparisons
establish what can be learned now. A later bank trial is justified by a credible scoped method,
demonstrated semantic and numerical behavior, and a decision-relevant uncertainty and cost
question. The resulting build, buy or integrate decision is conditional on that evidence, with
an explicit fallback when qualification fails.


39.8     Commercial orchestration and the recovery of a causal
         batch
A recovered causal batch is useful only if its result answers the declared question for the
declared population and information set. Consider a nightly offer analysis that fails after
writing some cohort effects. Restarting the job can save computation, but it can also duplicate
customers, reuse an outdated estimate or execute a changed procedure. The relevant product
requirement joins execution recovery to preservation of the scientific request. This motivates
comparing available orchestration before building another scheduler.
   The six selected official manuals cover Databricks Lakeflow Jobs on AWS, Snowflake task
graphs, Azure Machine Learning API-v2 pipeline reuse, Dataiku DSS scenarios and AWS Step
Functions. They provide current technical observations retrieved on 22 October 2026. They
do not establish an unchanged capability at the literature cutoff, 7 October 2026. Databricks’
repair and monitoring pages display 9 and 15 October updates. Azure displays a 30 March date
while its HTML repository metadata records a 19 October update. The remaining mutable
manuals lack an authenticated historical revision. These observations supplement the cutoff
survey; historical coverage remains open. (Databricks, 2026d,c; Microsoft, 2026b; Snowflake,
2026c; Dataiku, 2026a; Amazon Web Services, 2026c)

39.8.1    Partial repair must preserve both writes and meaning

The inspected Databricks repair manual describes rerunning unsuccessful tasks and their
dependents using current job and task settings. Each unsuccessful task starts again from
the beginning. The text explicitly warns that Jobs does not make task writes idempotent:
a partially completed append can duplicate data when repaired. A shared job cluster is
recreated using current settings, and repair parameters can override earlier values. These
mechanisms can support efficient recovery; they make the application’s output-commit and
version contracts material to a causal result. They do not establish that the platform cannot
implement those contracts.(Databricks, 2026d)
    Let the finite target population be U, and let τi be its stipulated potential-outcome contrast
Yi (1) − Yi (0). The equal-unit target is
                                                 1 X
                                          τU =         τi .                                 (39.1)
                                               |U| i∈U
For an exact constructed example, three units have contrast 6 and one has contrast −2, in
hypothetical dollars per unit. Their effect is 4. If the first two positive-contrast units are
752                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


written before interruption, and all four units are appended on repair, the stored-row average
becomes
                               5(6) + 1(−2)      14                     2
                     τappend =                = ,       τappend − τU = .                 (39.2)
                                      6          3                      3
The batch is computationally complete but its implicit positive-group weight has changed from
3/4 to 5/6. At stipulated per-unit cost 1, the intended net value 3 becomes the misleading
value 11/3. No statistical noise is needed for this error. These are exact authored values,
rather than bank observations or measured vendor behavior.(Causal banking proposal project,
2026bn)
   A final output keyed by unit identifier can recover four unique units, provided the values
belong to the same semantic request and the final commit is atomic or otherwise conflict
checked. The history still contains six write attempts. Deduplicating the result must not erase
the partial attempt, its cost or its failure. Conversely, overwriting a key with a result from a
different target or data vintage is not valid idempotency. Identifier equality alone does not
establish scientific equality. The proposed adapter must distinguish a repeated delivery of the
same result from a conflicting new result.


39.8.2    Job status and request status answer different questions

The current Databricks monitoring manual distinguishes “Succeeded with failures” from
ordinary success and explains job outcomes in terms of leaf tasks. A final task that tolerates
an upstream failure can complete without establishing that every requested customer cohort
or sensitivity scenario was evaluated. A causal batch therefore needs a request-level ledger
alongside the scheduler’s result: completed, refused, failed, skipped and reused requests remain
distinguishable.(Databricks, 2026c)
   The same manual describes a 48-hour finished-run graph and a 60-day run-history window. It
also explains that one-time API submissions have no saved job name, so searching by that name
does not find them. A durable scientific record should bind the actual run identifier and export
the relevant lineage before its operating display expires. Retention and search convenience
are useful platform features; neither determines the validity of the causal assumptions or the
completeness of the requested workload. (Databricks, 2026c)
   For a declared request set Q, report the requested count together with each disposition
count. Accuracy among returned results and the fraction of requests receiving an admissible
result are different quantities. Retry success must not silently remove difficult requests from
the denominator. An unsupported intervention is a scientific refusal; a transient storage failure
is an operating failure. Treating them identically would hide the appropriate remedy and
distort the comparison with another route.


39.8.3    Version the scientific dependencies behind an execution DAG

Snowflake’s inspected task-graph manual describes dependent SQL execution, retries, finalizers
and overlap controls. Its graph is a scheduling DAG. An edge that says one job must finish
before another does not imply a causal arrow or identify an intervention. This distinction
matters when an agent translates the same word “graph” across workflow and causal APIs.
(Snowflake, 2026c)
   The manual says that graph versions include task properties, but not the definitions of
stored procedures called by those tasks. If a called procedure changes during execution, its
new definition can run within the current graph run. Scientific replay must therefore pin
39.8. Commercial orchestration and the recovery of a causal batch                          753


procedure definitions and their relevant dependencies separately. A stable task-graph version
is insufficient to infer unchanged estimator code. (Snowflake, 2026c)
   The same text says that a suspended child can be treated as though it succeeded, while a
finalizer does not start when the root task is skipped. Overlap can be allowed where read/write
operations tolerate it. These are documented execution choices whose compatibility with
the proposed experiment must be assessed. A manifest and commit protocol should make
incompatible concurrent writes detectable and should retain skipped scientific requests. This
is a design requirement, not a demonstrated Snowflake adapter or an absence claim about
other product features. (Snowflake, 2026c)


39.8.4    A reusable output must still answer the same target

Azure Machine Learning’s inspected API-v2 description requires a deterministic component,
ForceReRun=false and matching code, environment, inputs, parameters, output settings and
run settings for reuse. The reused component displays the earlier status, output, logs and
metrics. Force-rerun children cannot be reused by other jobs. These controls offer a useful
starting point for lineage and reproducibility, with the historical-edition limitation stated
above. (Microsoft, 2026b)
   The scientific application must express its dependencies through the declared artifacts. An
unchanged URI need not establish an unchanged table behind it; an undeclared population
revision can change the question even if the code is identical. The determinism flag is a
declaration about the component, not an independent validation of determinism or causal
assumptions. The manual’s code-snapshot and environment comparisons help diagnose execu-
tion reuse; the library must add the estimand and information clock to the meaning of reuse.
(Microsoft, 2026b)
   In the finite example, keeping group effects (6, −2) but changing population weights from
(3/4, 1/4) to (1/4, 3/4) changes the effect from 4 to 0 and net value from 3 to −1. Retaining
the original weights but revising the last unit’s contrast from −2 to −10 changes the effect to
2 and net value to 1. The first change is a target change; the second is a data-vintage change.
A cached number may be exactly equal to an earlier output and still answer the wrong current
question.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bn)


39.8.5    Retries need a budget that survives redrive

The current AWS Step Functions manual describes ordered retriers and catchers, backoff,
jitter and bounded retry counts. Catchers apply to Task, Parallel and Map states, rather than
top-level execution failures. Eligible states can have their retry counts reset on redrive. A
library request that requires a total budget must retain attempts across these boundaries, as
well as configure each state’s retry policy. A new execution identifier must not erase earlier
time, resource use or failed scientific requests. (Amazon Web Services, 2026c)
   Error classes require the exact documented meaning. In the inspected current text, the
States.ALL wildcard excludes DataLimitExceeded and Runtime. The manual explicitly permits
a named DataLimitExceeded retry or catch, whereas Runtime remains non-retryable. It would
be inaccurate to infer from the wildcard exclusion that every explicit payload-limit handler is
unavailable. The historical revision must be recovered before attributing these semantics to
the cutoff edition.(Amazon Web Services, 2026c)
 The manual states that retries are billed as state transitions. Actual comparison requires
more than the number of successful final tasks. For a common workload, define a proposed
754                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


accounting identity

       Cworkflow = Ctransitions + Ccompute + Cstorage + Ctransfer + Chuman + Clicense .      (39.3)

Each term includes failed and recovery attempts within the declared horizon; overlapping
charges must not be counted twice. Rates, region, service edition, retention and staff time need
authentic evidence before evaluating this identity numerically. No observed prices, runtime
advantage or bank return are supplied by the exact arithmetic example.


39.8.6    What remains unresolved in the commercial comparison

Dataiku’s retrieved page identifies DSS 15 and indexes automation scenarios, build/check/-
metrics/code steps, trigger categories and failure/conditional execution. It is primarily an
index. Those headings establish the scope of linked topics, not detailed transaction, retry or
concurrency semantics. The technical pages and historical DSS edition must be inspected
before a stronger comparison.(Dataiku, 2026a)
   SAS Viya orchestration, Domino and Posit Workbench/Connect remain candidates for this
bounded frame. Their presence here grants no capability or absence finding. Complementary
market discovery, product aliases, deployment editions, licensing and actual prices remain
necessary. For the five inspected families, current manuals support specific mechanisms
and application obligations; none completes historical coverage or native qualification. This
comparison therefore motivates an architecture that reuses suitable orchestration while adding
scientific semantics. Whether each adapter preserves those semantics remains a proposition to
test.


39.8.7    A common manifest across the library, CLI and MCP

Let m(q) serialize the full declared meaning of scientific request q:

                  m(q) = (D, T, I, G, A, E, S, N, O),       k(q) = hash(m(q)).               (39.4)

Here D identifies input snapshots and availability, T the population and estimand, I the
information clock, G graph/identification assumptions, A the estimator and covariance settings,
E code and environment, S seeds or randomness coupling, N numerical tolerances, and O
the output schema. The serialization must be canonical and must include the dependencies
needed for that method; the tuple is a proposed contract, not a proof of completeness. Equal
hashes bind specified bytes and declarations. They do not establish truthful provenance, valid
assumptions or an identified causal effect.
   The reference program constructs a finite manifest and verifies that changes to the data,
target weights or environment change its key. It also verifies the append bias and keyed recovery
using exact rational arithmetic. This is a local authored reference, not a vendor adapter or
a fault-injected deployment. The CLI and MCP should transport the same manifest and
return lineage, the target, uncertainty meaning and request disposition. A refused unidentified
effect must not be converted into an ordinary numerical answer by either entry point.(Causal
banking proposal project, 2026bn)


39.8.8    Demonstrate merit on public fixtures before a costly trial

A first frozen experiment should combine a public dataset with a separately generated potential-
outcome fixture. The public source exercises realistic schema, scale and custody; generated
39.9. Scenario controls must preserve a fixed scientific workload                             755


outcomes supply known causal truth under declared assumptions. Public observational
agreement alone supplies no such truth label. Compare uninterrupted and interrupted execution
with the same targets, data, methods, randomization and resource envelope.
  Prespecify partial writes, lost responses after commit, changed tables or procedures, stale
cache, skipped children, payload limits and exhausted redrive budgets. Every requested case
remains in the denominator. Deterministic exact cases require identical results and statuses.
Floating or randomized cases need predeclared tolerances and appropriate coupled randomness.
Incompatible manifests must be refused; commits must be unique and the attempt/cost ledger
complete. A statistical estimator retains a separate calibration protocol. Computational
equivalence does not itself establish coverage or identification.
   This experiment can justify whether a native trial is worth its cost. Later commercial
qualification needs the chosen edition, licensed environment, actual execution and complete
prices; later bank acceptance needs authentic bank questions, truth and owners. The proposed
contract supplies a concrete route for those stages while preserving uncertainty about their
outcomes. It does not establish that any sibling repository or commercial platform has already
adopted the causal library.


39.9      Scenario controls must preserve a fixed scientific workload
The previous orchestration comparison motivates a closer question for a nightly bank offer
analysis: which requested effects survive a partly failed scenario? Dataiku’s detailed official
manuals describe useful controls for handling failures, testing a flow and initiating another run.
Their current technical text supports a more precise comparison than an index of scenario
features. The observations below concern the saved DSS 15 and DSS 14 manuals acquired
after the 7 October 2026 cutoff. They establish documented mechanisms, with the historical
qualification developed below; they do not establish an executed adapter or an exhaustive
account of the product. (Dataiku, 2026d,g,f,b)


39.9.1     A tolerated operating error leaves a scientific question

The step-control manual specifies sequential execution until the first failure or completion
of all steps. Some steps, including Build/train, can downgrade an error to a warning and
let later steps run. An example uses Ignore failure when attempting to kill another scenario.
Individual steps can be disabled with Never, run with Always regardless of previous failures, or
use conditions on earlier failures, the current outcome or variables. The documented scenario
outcomes are SUCCESS, WARNING, FAILED and ABORTED. These distinctions are useful:
cleanup can still run after a failure, and a later diagnostic need not be lost. They leave the
application responsible for deciding whether its requested causal effects have actually been
returned. (Dataiku, 2026d,b)
   Let Q be the declared set of cohort requests, wq their fixed population weights with
P
  q∈Q wq = 1, τq the cohort’s mean potential-outcome contrast between contact and no contact,
and cq the incremental cost of contacting a member. The declared all-contact policy has
incremental net value, in dollars per member,
                                              X
                                       VQ =         wq (τq − cq ).                         (39.5)
                                              q∈Q

For the following exact authored construction, cohort effects are stipulated truth, not estimates
whose identification or precision has been established. There are two equal-weight cohorts,
756                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


with τA = 10, τB = −30 and cA = cB = 1. No contact has zero incremental value and cost.
Thus
                         VQ = 21 (10 − 1) + 12 (−30 − 1) = −11.                  (39.6)
If the effect for cohort B is missing after a failed or skipped step, averaging the available cohort
instead reports Vavailable = 9. The apparent improvement of 20 dollars comes from changing
the population. It reverses the financial sign without any sampling noise. A tolerated error
that leaves the same effect missing creates the same arithmetic problem. These are constructed
missing-output illustrations; they are not recorded Dataiku run outcomes. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026bs)
  The proposed scientific ledger keeps two requested effects and one returned effect in every
such illustration. It retains the failure, skip or tolerated error as a distinct disposition, the
declared weights and the missing result. It can describe the available cohort’s value for that
cohort, but cannot rename it the original population value. Assigning zero to a missing effect
would add a substantive assumption. Even renormalizing costs to the returned cohort would
change the all-contact policy being evaluated.
   An explicit range can communicate a limited answer. If a separate substantive argument
justifies τB ∈ [−50, 50], with cohort A’s effect and the costs still stipulated, the original target
obeys
                                   VQ = 4 + 21 τB ∈ [−21, 29].                                (39.7)
This identified set follows from assumed bounds, rather than statistical confidence. It gives no
guarantee of a positive net return. The route to a sharper answer is to recover the missing
effect, defend tighter bounds or declare a different policy and population explicitly. Reporting
only the successful cohort cannot supply the lost information. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026bs)

39.9.2    A trigger observes its rule, not a complete causal snapshot

The trigger manual distinguishes initiation from execution. Several active triggers are evaluated
independently; any true condition can promote a scenario for execution, which need not start
immediately. For filesystem datasets, change detection uses filenames, lengths and modification
times, with an optional marker file. A dataset-change trigger does not detect SQL data changes;
a SQL-query trigger compares the query’s output. The suggested row count or maximum-
column query is a useful proxy, whose adequacy depends on the scientific request.(Dataiku,
2026g)
  For example, two fixed records can retain both row count and maximum date while cohort
B’s stored contrast changes from −30 to 30. In the same stipulated equal-weight population,
net value then changes from −11 to 19. A count-and-maximum-date proxy cannot distinguish
these two tables. This is a logical counterexample for that chosen query, rather than a claim
that SQL triggers cannot use a stronger query or that the platform loses changes. The proposed
adapter should bind the relevant data snapshot and information clock, with a change rule
appropriate to those dependencies. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026bs)
  By default, Suppress triggers while running is enabled: a second trigger can go unevaluated
during a long run. If suppression is disabled, an evaluation finishing while the scenario is still
running is ignored. For eligible tracked events, the manual describes disabling suppression,
enabling Delay runs and disabling Squash delayed runs to retain a run per trigger. It also warns
that serial scenarios accumulate delayed runs if arrival throughput exceeds service throughput.
Squashing limits the delayed queue to at most one run and can cancel an intermediate run.
Time-based, manual and hidden Run another scenario triggers are excluded from run delaying.
(Dataiku, 2026g)
39.9. Scenario controls must preserve a fixed scientific workload                            757


  These controls support different operational objectives. A latest-snapshot analysis may
deliberately combine changes, whereas a predeclared event study may need every eligible event
and its clock. The latter requires a durable event/request record and reconciliation against
the declared workload. Trigger counts alone cannot certify that denominator, and every raw
data change need not be a scientific event. The application must define the relationship
before choosing suppression or squashing. This is a proposed contract to qualify, rather than
demonstrated event completeness.


39.9.3     Existing tests help define a bounded integration experiment

The scenario-step manual documents checks and data-quality rules: the step fails when at
least one selected check fails, and rule outcomes become variables for later steps. It also
documents project pytest selection and a flow integration test that swaps in stable reference
inputs, rebuilds outputs and compares them with reference datasets. These mechanisms
could support a prototype comparison using public or generated data. A causal extension
would need reference targets, weights, information clocks, refusals and uncertainty alongside
ordinary output comparisons; the documentation does not show that such an extension has
been executed. (Dataiku, 2026f)
   Run another scenario waits for completion and takes the child’s outcome. The manual says
the initiating step’s user is used regardless of the child scenario’s Run as setting. A proposed
adapter must therefore preserve the observed run identity together with the scientific request,
then test the relevant configuration. This narrow documented behavior does not establish the
whole authorization model. Similarly, a Clear step deletes dataset or folder contents; persistent
scientific evidence must have its own deliberate retention arrangement.(Dataiku, 2026f)
   The economical next experiment is a small fixed manifest containing complete, failed,
skipped and tolerated-without-effect requests. Check the returned scientific ledger, weights
and source identities before measuring retries or runtime. Pair this with two data versions
that share a selected trigger proxy but differ in a scientific dependency. A successful native
experiment would support only its frozen release, configuration and manifest. Its merit should
be established with public/generated inputs before purchasing a large bank study. No native
execution, licensed entitlement or measured commercial cost is asserted here.


39.9.4     The cutoff requires a patch identity, not just a major version

The current release index lists DSS 15.0.0 on 14 August 2026 and DSS 15.0.2 on 24 September
2026, both before the client cutoff. It lists DSS 15.1.0 on 8 October and DSS 15.2.0 on 15
October, both later. DSS 15 therefore cannot be dismissed as entirely post-cutoff. Equally, its
current major-version manual cannot silently stand for the exact 15.0.2 technical bytes. The
DSS 14 release index lists 14.7.5 on 24 September. Its inspected step-control body matches
the DSS 15 body, which supports a current textual comparison but does not authenticate the
historical patch revision. (Dataiku, 2026e,c,d,b)
   Release-index headings for Agent Skills and MCP server do not establish their detailed
behavior. Those claims need the relevant primary technical text and edition. The detailed
scenario review narrows one earlier source omission; exact cutoff originals for the selected
commercial manuals, SAS Viya, Domino, Posit and complementary market coverage remain
to be investigated. Rights, prices and native qualification remain separate questions. This
comparison supports reuse of documented orchestration mechanisms as candidates, while
requiring an explicit scientific workload before an integration is accepted.
758                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


39.10      Commercial execution platforms and open client con-
           tracts
A bank’s overnight causal analysis may run in an established execution platform while its
scientific meaning remains the responsibility of the proposed library. A useful commercial
comparison therefore follows the actual boundary: submission, observation of a remote job,
interpretation of its terminal state, recovery and custody of its outputs. The open clients
supplied by SAS, Domino and Posit reveal concrete integration choices. Their selected source
revisions precede 7 October 2026. They authenticate client and SDK behavior visible in source,
not every feature of a licensed server, a supported deployment combination, or a successful
native trial. (SAS Institute, 2026i; Domino Data Lab, 2026b; Posit PBC, 2026a,c)


39.10.1    Completion is one coordinate of a scientific result

Let q denote an immutable scientific request, a a run attempt, v a code revision, d a data
snapshot and e an execution environment. The requested result has a declared estimand,
population, information time and assumptions. An execution record is a different object: it
says which attempt ran which inputs, whether it terminated, and which artifacts it produced.
A proposed acceptance rule can make these requirements explicit:

                       A(q, a) = T (a) S(a) B(q, a, v, d, e) E(a) C(q, ra ),                 (39.8)

where each factor is a zero–one indicator. Here T means terminal, S means an allowed
successful execution state, B means a verified binding between request and execution identities,
E means the required result artifacts ra exist, and C means the result passes the stated
scientific contract. The last factor may require an explicit nonidentification or refusal result;
a numerical effect need not exist for every valid request. These are proposed application
semantics, not a claim that a vendor implements this particular rule. A successful process exit
supplies evidence for only part of the conjunction.
   This distinction matters even when all arithmetic is exact. Suppose a funding decision has
a stipulated incremental response coefficient bv , capital exposure of USD 1,000 and cost of
USD 20. For two revisions that encode different supplied assumptions, take b0 = 3/100 and
b1 = 4/100. Their net values are

                V0 = 1000(3/100) − 20 = 10,         V1 = 1000(4/100) − 20 = 20.              (39.9)

Both calculations can exit successfully. Substituting the second revision while describing the
run as a replay of the first changes the answer by USD 10. This is an authored identity
example with stipulated coefficients, not an estimated causal effect or a measured vendor
failure. Recording a code commit alone also leaves the data snapshot, configuration, dependency
versions and randomization state to be specified. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026cp)


39.10.2    Domino: versioned restart and distinct polling predicates

The selected Domino Python client exposes useful controls for this boundary. Its job submission
payload includes a commit identifier, main-repository Git reference, environment identifier
and hardware selection. Its restart method defaults to requesting the original input commit;
the alternative requests the current version. The stop method separately accepts a flag asking
to commit results. These are meaningful strengths for controlled experimentation, but the
selected client source does not establish complete data and environment immutability or the
licensed server’s interpretation of every field. (Domino Data Lab, 2026b)
39.10. Commercial execution platforms and open client contracts                               759


   Two polling interfaces in the same source have different visible predicates. The legacy
blocking run helper resets its consecutive status-read retry count after a successful read. It
waits for an output commit and then requires the reported status to be Succeeded. The
newer blocking job helper raises on executionStatus == Failed and passes isCompleted
to the polling library as its success predicate. Its defaults specify a five-second poll interval
and a 6,000-second polling timeout, with selected request exceptions ignored during polling.
(Domino Data Lab, 2026b)
   These observations justify a precise question rather than an accusation of a product defect.
A supplied hypothetical response whose completion flag is true and whose execution status
is neither Failed nor Succeeded satisfies the newer local predicate. It would fail a proposed
explicit Succeeded allowlist. This is a logical witness about the inspected expression; it does
not show that the server actually emits such a response. Resolving that question needs the
supported server state schema and its version. An adapter should preserve both fields, the
raw response, job identity and output binding until the mapping is justified. It must also
distinguish failure to observe a job before the deadline from proof that the remote job has
stopped. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026cp; Domino Data Lab, 2026b)
  For the proposal, the preferred route is a narrow client wrapper that keeps Domino’s
execution and revision controls and adds the scientific request contract. Reimplementing the
entire scheduler has no demonstrated advantage. The wrapper remains a proposed integration:
supported API routes, exception mapping, actual terminal states, output custody and fault
behavior still need their own inspection and registered public or synthetic trials.


39.10.3     Posit Connect: tasks, jobs and schedules have different meanings

The inspected R client declares development version 0.12.1.9000. Its task object normalizes
an incoming identifier when necessary. The poll_task implementation waits for the task’s
finished field, checks the final numeric code, raises on nonzero code and attaches an optional
result to the task object. The function exposes a wait interval but no overall deadline parameter.
This describes the local function signature and loop, not the absence of time limits elsewhere
in the server or transport. An integrating worker should impose an explicit observation budget
and retain the remote task identity for reconciliation. (Posit PBC, 2026a)
   Job records carry additional context: content and bundle identifiers, start and end times,
execution status, exit code and, where available, cluster and image information. The selected
documentation distinguishes Active, Finished and Finalized on newer servers and identifies
missing fields on versions earlier than 2022.10.0. The implementation also normalizes older
timestamp and identifier representations. A consumer must not treat missing historical fields
as verified empty values or infer a successful scientific result from the label Finished. A bundle
identifier is useful provenance, but its mapping to the request’s code, data and configuration
still needs evidence. (Posit PBC, 2026a)
   Scheduling adds another boundary. The inspected schedule-update method is marked
experimental, converts start and next-run times and calls unversioned schedule endpoints.
Thus the R package’s source commit, the server API behavior and the schedule’s information
clock are separate versioning questions. In banking, a job scheduled after a ledger cutoff must
not quietly use records first available after the intended decision time. The proposed adapter
should preserve that time explicitly and reject ambiguous timestamp conversion. This is an
application requirement, not a finding that Posit violates it. (Posit PBC, 2026a)
   The R client is therefore a plausible integration route for R-based estimation and reporting.
Its task, job and schedule objects should remain distinct in the library/CLI/MCP contract.
Porting the client wholesale to another language would add an API-maintenance obligation
760                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


without yet proving better scientific fidelity. A worker boundary with typed results is the more
limited candidate to test first.


39.10.4     Posit Launcher: reuse the scheduler boundary with explicit state

The Launcher Go SDK addresses a different layer. Its official guide describes a plugin connecting
Workbench or Connect to a scheduler using length-prefixed JSON over standard input and
output. Bootstrap reconciles current jobs, heartbeats detect an unresponsive plugin, and
multiple Launcher instances require a common view of job state. The guide gives Go and
product-version prerequisites. These are documented design contracts of the pinned SDK;
they are not a measured availability or recovery guarantee. (Posit PBC, 2026c)
   The testing guide offers a useful structure for proposed qualification. It separates universal
invariants, product request sequences and individual control scenarios. Examples cover
nonempty job identifiers, distinct IDs for two submissions, retrieval and filtering, terminal-state
nonregression, launch, stop, kill and cancel. Profiles allow scheduler-specific terminal states
and exit codes; unsupported suspend/resume can be skipped. An integration must interpret
the selected profile and skipped cases rather than collapse the entire suite to one portable
success claim. These tests are documented upstream facilities; no passing execution is asserted
here. (Posit PBC, 2026c)
   For a bank with an accepted scheduler, adopting this bridge boundary is more plausible than
reproducing an execution platform inside a causal library. The library would still own causal
request identity and result validation. The platform would own job dispatch and resource
management. A prototype comparison should test stale state after restart, duplicate submission,
status-stream interruption and missing output, including the cost of state reconciliation. A
failed bootstrap or missing shared state must remain visible as an operating failure, not be
translated into a zero causal effect.


39.10.5     SAS: preserve experimental scope and explicit timeout outcomes

The sasctl project exposes Python module and command-line access to SAS Viya. Its selected
Workflow class states that its partial implementation is experimental and can change without
notice. The comment refers to the documentation situation in September 2022; it does not
establish whether public workflow documentation exists at the proposal cutoff. Submission
selects an enabled definition, maps supplied values to declared prompts and includes their
declared types and versions. Naive datetime values are converted using local timezone when
possible, with a UTC fallback if they remain naive. A banking adapter should require an explicit
timezone before submission rather than let the worker host silently define the information
clock. (SAS Institute, 2026i)
   A separate score-execution method exposes another concrete control issue. It returns the
strings completed or failed on those reported states. Its timeout test is inside the polling loop,
while the loop guard itself limits elapsed time; there is no explicit return after the loop. A
supplied zero timeout therefore skips the body and reaches Python’s implicit None return. For
a positive budget, the timeout branch can be reached if time crosses the threshold during an
iteration, but a later failed loop guard can also end the loop without that explicit timeout
result. This is source-level control-flow reasoning, not a timed experiment against SAS. (SAS
Institute, 2026i; Causal banking proposal project, 2026cp)
   The proposed wrapper should validate a positive observation budget, normalize all completion
paths into typed states, retain execution identity and logs, and require a separately verified
result binding. An unrecognized or absent polling return is an unresolved observation, not
39.11. Following commercial workflow requests into their delegates                            761


permission to use stale scores. Reusing the open client selectively is a candidate; depending
on its experimental workflow service without versioned qualification is not yet a supported
product commitment.


39.10.6     Retries, rights and a costed prototype choice

Recovery can change value when a retry repeats a charge or an externally visible action. In an
exact illustrative servicing example, suppose one useful contact produces a stipulated USD 12
gain and every attempted delivery incurs USD 7. If there is at most one useful gain, net value
after n charged attempts is

                        V (n) = 12 − 7n,       V (1) = 5,     V (2) = −2.                 (39.10)

The sign changes solely because of the assumed duplicate cost. A repeated analysis job need
not incur this contact cost; the example concerns a workflow that crosses into a paid or
externally visible action. It motivates separate request and attempt identities, reconciliation
before resubmission and an idempotency key at the side-effect boundary. It establishes no
vendor failure rate, bank return or economic superiority. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026cp)
   The selected connectapi license is MIT; the Launcher root license provides an MIT-style
grant unless supplied under a commercial agreement. The Domino and sasctl client roots
include Apache 2.0 texts. These source licenses are relevant to proposed client reuse. They do
not supply an entitlement to a commercial server, a supported edition, a complete dependency-
rights review or a price. Consequently the commercial comparison should price an actual
deployment and support arrangement separately from the open wrapper. (Posit PBC, 2026a,c;
Domino Data Lab, 2026b; SAS Institute, 2026i)
   The practical proposal is to compare narrow wrappers around established execution services
using the same public or synthetic scientific workload. Record installation and maintenance
effort, queue and compute time, output validation, failed attempts, recovery and any billed
actions. Preserve every requested case in the denominator. Qualify client and server versions,
explicit failure states, output custody and clock semantics before drawing an economic conclu-
sion. Historical Dataiku technical-version gaps and wider market coverage remain separate
survey obligations; these four inspected profiles neither establish market completeness nor
erase those limits.

An overnight funding estimate is usable only if its execution record still refers to the requested
population, information date and model. The boundary between a causal library and an
execution platform therefore includes more than a submission endpoint. Transport retries,

a consumer believes happened. Following the pinned SAS, Domino and Posit clients into their
delegates makes the comparison more precise. These are selected primary files from source

compatibility matrix. The preceding client comparison remains applicable in its stated scope.

39.11.1     SAS: separate refresh counts, transport time and sampling mem-
            bership

The SAS service boundary is concrete. Service.request prefixes its service root and forwards
the request and keyword arguments to core.request; the latter calls the selected session and
raises an HTTP error for response codes 400 through 599 before converting the response. The
session exposes timeout=None and forwards the value to its underlying request implementation.
When a 401 challenge specifically reports an expired access token, successful refresh can cause
the request to be issued again. This supports a wrapper using the existing client while making
request identity, authentication events and transport policy explicit. It does not demonstrate
that every failed submission is safe to repeat or that a remote side effect occurred twice. (SAS
Institute, 2026h)
   The generic Service._monitor_job helper illustrates a second boundary. It treats both
completed and failed as terminal, sleeps half a second before each refresh, and limits the
number of refreshes. On a terminal response it returns the job, including a failed job; otherwise
it raises JobTimeoutError. That is a count-limited observation procedure. It does not itself
establish a wall-clock deadline for a request that stalls. The inspected workflow-submission
method is not shown to call this generic helper, so this finding must not be projected onto
every workflow execution path. The workflow unit tests mock definition lookup and POST:
they establish intended URL and prompt formatting, including conversion of datetime prompts
to strings, rather than actual server completion. (SAS Institute, 2026h)
   For a supplied timing example, let m be the number of nonterminal refreshes, h their sleep
interval and ri the duration of refresh i. Ignoring fixed overhead, the observation time is
                                                     m
                                                     X
                                        tm = mh +          ri .                               (39.11)
                                                     i=1

With three refreshes, h = 1/2 second and every ri = 2 seconds, the sleep budget is 3/2
seconds while the actual supplied duration is 15/2 seconds. An upper bound on m alone
cannot bound the sum if request durations are unrestricted. These are exact authored timings,
not measured SAS latency. A proposed worker should combine a monotonic observation
deadline with bounded transport requests and retain the remote job identity when the deadline
expires. Expiration establishes that observation stopped; remote termination requires separate
reconciliation. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026cq)
   Pagination also matters to scientific meaning. The selected PageIterator extracts start
and limit from a next link and schedules offset requests through a thread pool. It stops after an
empty result. The item iterator explicitly calls its length an approximate count and notes that
permissions can affect accessible membership. This offers convenient client iteration without
proving a frozen population, stable ordering or snapshot consistency. It would be incorrect to
infer that the server lacks such facilities merely because the selected iterator does not establish
them; the server contract must supply the missing evidence. (SAS Institute, 2026h)
   Consider an authored frame with identifiers (1, 2, 3, 4), page size two and binary outcomes
(1, 0, 1, 0). The first page returns (1, 2). If identifier 1 is removed before a second request with
offset two, the current frame is (2, 3, 4) and the second page returns (4). The consumer observes
(1, 2, 4) and estimates 1/3, whereas the initial-frame mean is 1/2. This is a changing-offset
counterexample, not a reproduced SAS defect. Deduplicating returned IDs would not recover
the missing initial identifier 3. A causal audit that samples workflow records must therefore
bind the membership and permission law to an immutable snapshot, a reconciled ID manifest
or a justified server cursor contract. More parallel requests do not by themselves identify that
law. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026cq)
39.11. Following commercial workflow requests into their delegates                             763


   The preferred SAS route remains a narrow Python/CLI worker over declared service versions.
Reusing the request and prompt machinery avoids creating another partial REST client.
Wholesale porting would still require the server schemas, time conventions, authentication and
supported edition contracts that are currently unresolved. A future registered prototype should
distinguish an accepted submission, an authentication refresh, a failed job, an observation
deadline and a confirmed cancellation. No native trial or server entitlement follows from the
open client source.


39.11.2     Domino: preserve method policy and exception identity

The Domino route delegate distinguishes legacy run endpoints from the v4 job endpoints for
start, stop, status, restart and execution details. Its HTTP manager mounts an HTTPS retry
adapter with a configured total whose default is four, backoff factor one and status list 408,
502, 503 and 504. It does not explicitly override the retry library’s allowed-method policy.
Consequently, the presence of this adapter is insufficient evidence that a job-submission POST
is automatically retried on those statuses. That claim needs the exact HTTP dependencies
and their policy. The wrapper forwards request keywords without setting an overall deadline
in these methods; the blocking helper’s polling timeout is a separate layer. (Domino Data Lab,
2026a)
   Exception classes also affect what the polling loop does. The manager converts
HTTP 409 into ReloginRequiredException; other HTTP errors are re-raised. The
selected exception inherits DominoException, whose base is Exception. It is not the
requests.exceptions.RequestException listed in the blocking helper’s default ignored
exceptions. Thus the statement that this helper ignores intermediate request exceptions must
retain its declared class boundary. It cannot be expanded into a claim that authentication-
expiry exceptions, every HTTP conflict or every failure is silently retried. The 409 mapping is
a client interpretation; an authoritative server error contract is still needed before assigning
the same meaning to every supported deployment. (Domino Data Lab, 2026a,b)
   The job tests clarify intent without closing that deployment question. Unit fixtures provide
Queued and Succeeded responses, an isCompleted flag and a mock server version 9.9.9.
Other unit tests specify a polling timeout when RequestException is ignored, and immediate
propagation when the ignored-exception tuple is empty. Live tests are conditional on a reachable
Domino deployment. Reading these sources is neither running the tests nor authenticating
9.9.9 as a real supported server. The earlier question about a complete terminal-state schema
remains open: a successful mock does not enumerate every server terminal state. (Domino
Data Lab, 2026a)
   For the proposal, preserve the client’s useful restart and revision controls and add an explicit
result contract at the worker boundary. Keep transport retry, reauthentication, remote restart
and a new scientific attempt as different events. Before any resubmission with external effects,
reconcile the remote attempt and use an application identity whose idempotency semantics
are actually supported. This is a proposed protocol, not a claim that Domino duplicates jobs
or lacks an idempotency facility. Porting the whole client would reproduce the unresolved
schema and dependency questions without yet demonstrating better causal fidelity.


39.11.3     Posit: terminal state, exit code and conformance coverage

The Launcher SDK gives a particularly useful typed distinction. Its Failed status means the
job could not be launched; its Finished status includes a process that launched and exited
with a nonzero exit code. Canceled, Failed, Finished and Killed are terminal. The job object
764                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


carries status, optional reason/code and a separate optional process exit code. A causal CLI or
MCP consumer should preserve these fields instead of translating every terminal or Finished
record into scientific success. A successful refusal artifact may be an acceptable scientific
answer, but that acceptance must be explicitly bound to its request and contract. (Posit PBC,
2026b)
   To expose the accounting consequence, suppose four supplied attempts yield Finished with
exit zero and a valid bound artifact; Finished with exit seven; launch failure; and cancellation.
All four are terminal. Only the first satisfies a stipulated acceptance predicate requiring the
allowed state, allowed exit and artifact binding. At a supplied cost of USD 3 per attempt, USD
12 has been spent. Reporting USD 3 per terminal event and USD 12 per accepted artifact
answers different questions. Neither number proves causal validity, which remains another
contract, and neither is a Posit price or a bank ROI estimate. This exact example shows
why a proposal comparison must use the same accepted-output definition and failed-request
denominator for every execution alternative. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026cq)
   The scheduler example offers a reusable separation between Launcher protocol handling
and a SchedulerClient backend that submits, observes, cancels, kills and retrieves output.
Its illustrative state mapper sends unrecognized native values to Pending. That default is
an example, not evidence that all scheduler states are known or that a supplied plugin is
production ready. A bank worker should retain the native value and use an explicit unresolved
mapping until the chosen backend profile justifies it. Reusing the SDK boundary is a narrower
candidate than reimplementing the execution service, but the backend and supported product
versions must be selected before qualification. (Posit PBC, 2026b)
   The source conformance facilities strengthen the proposed qualification design when their
coverage is kept explicit. A profile requires job factories and expected stop/kill states and exit
codes. Network, output and suspend switches determine which workflow assertions run. The
NetworkAvailable comment says default true, while the inspected applyDefaults function
sets only durations. An omitted Go boolean remains false. A prototype must therefore record
the actual profile and set the required switch explicitly, instead of assuming that a documented
default caused a network check to execute. This is a discrepancy between selected source
comments and defaults, not an observed deployment failure. (Posit PBC, 2026b)
   Two further qualifications prevent overstatement. The terminal-regression invariant compares
a terminal result with one revisit 200 milliseconds later. Agreement at those times is useful
evidence for that run, not a proof of permanent stability: an authored history can agree at
times zero and one fifth second and change at one second. The cancellation scenario skips
when the API returns an error, explaining that the job may already have started. That branch
does not first demonstrate the proposed start race. A registered adaptation should inspect
state and error identity before classifying a race, retain every skipped or unsupported case,
and avoid counting a skip as successful cancellation. No upstream conformance suite has been
executed here. (Posit PBC, 2026b; Causal banking proposal project, 2026cq)


39.11.4     A bounded integration choice and the remaining comparison

These delegates support a coherent prototype choice. Preserve vendor job dispatch and resource
management behind typed workers, with a common causal request and result contract above
them. Record request, attempt, code, dataset, environment, information date and native
state separately. Bound observation and transport time; reconcile a remote attempt after a
timeout; freeze audit membership; and validate the expected artifact and its scientific meaning
independently of process completion. This is a proposed integration architecture. The exact
authored timing, sampling and cost witnesses explain why its contracts are needed; they do
39.12. From workflow submission to a scientifically acceptable artifact                         765


not qualify the implementation.
   The remaining market comparison has specific inputs. SAS needs a versioned public
REST/workflow contract; Domino needs its supported terminal and error schema; Posit needs
a concrete backend, product versions and an explicit conformance profile. Immutable Dataiku
15.0.2 cutoff technical bytes remain a separate historical-source omission. Client licensing,
commercial server rights, dependency notices and actual prices must be assessed separately.
Public or synthetic fault trials can justify a later costly prototype study once its environment is
fixed. Until then, these are source-based comparison and integration choices; native capability,
whole-market coverage and bank acceptance remain open.


39.12       From workflow submission to a scientifically acceptable
            artifact
A restarted causal batch needs an account of what was requested, what actually ran and
which result answers the banking question. A collections team might request a monthly
policy comparison, receive a trigger acknowledgement, and later find either a completed
simulation or no run at all. A funding analyst might receive a Finished job whose process
exited unsuccessfully. Neither an acknowledgement nor a terminal state establishes that the
requested intervention contrast, population and information date survived execution. The
following historical source profiles supplement the earlier client comparisons with immutable
Dataiku client text, SAS REST examples, a declared-range HTTP dependency profile and a
concrete Posit Local backend. They establish source contracts, not observed performance of
licensed installations.(Dataiku SAS, 2026; SAS Institute, 2026j; Domino Data Lab and HTTP
