39.50       Java survival components: event clocks and defensible
            intervention services
Java survival components answer different parts of a banking problem. A collections manager
needs to compare action sequences for an eligible borrower population; a capital analyst may
first need event-time prediction. Combining records held by several institutions introduces
a confidentiality problem. These requirements should not collapse into whether a package
implements Cox regression. Selected primary sources establish four candidates: H2O-3’s
distributed fitting and portable scoring, BioJava’s survival module, FRESCO-stat’s secure
computation, and the distinct repository robbyjo/JLinAlg. They do not establish exhaustive
Java coverage, qualified integration or a longitudinal causal estimator simply because a survival
routine exists. (H2O-3 contributors, 2026; BioJava survival contributors, 2026; FRESCO-stat
contributors, 2026; robbyjo/JLinAlg contributors, 2026)


39.50.1     Specify the event, clock and target first

Let Li be entry time, Ti the end of an observed interval, Di its event indicator, and Xi (t)
information available before a decision at t. In stratum s, stipulate the working model
λi (t) = λ0s (t) exp{Xi (t)⊤ β + oi (t)}, where oi is a declared offset. Its risk set uses Li < t ≤ Ti .
Neither a fitted coefficient nor concordance identifies the consequence of changing collections
policy. A causal use still needs the treatment rule, population, observation mechanism,
sequential support and identification assumptions developed earlier. A confounder affected
by earlier treatment does not become a valid ordinary adjustment variable merely because
a start–stop row can be supplied. The comparison separates the event-time computational
component from the intervention argument. The clock convention is explicit in the selected
H2O and JLinAlg source. (H2O-3 contributors, 2026; robbyjo/JLinAlg contributors, 2026)
   For a fixed baseline profile, write r = exp(X ⊤ β + o). Integrating the stipulated hazard gives
S(t | X) = S0 (t)r . A log score, relative score and probability have different units. With r = 2,
baseline survivals 1/2 and 3/4 imply risks 3/4 and 7/16. Under a stipulated USD 1,000 loss
and USD 600 premium, margins are −150 and 162.50 dollars. The same relative score permits
opposite decisions. These are exact authored laws, not bank observations or fitted package
outputs. A CLI or MCP response must bind horizon, baseline, stratum and centering before
returning monetary consequences. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026dr)
   Event coding matters too. In a designed ten-borrower cohort, one default and four prepay-
ments give observed default fraction 1/10; collapsing the events gives 1/2. Applying the same
stipulated USD 1,000 default loss yields USD 100 versus USD 500 per borrower. This coding
witness is not a counterfactual estimator. Prepayment as a competing event, censoring under
an observation model, and hypothetical elimination of prepayment remain distinct targets.
The earlier R and Python comparisons provide alternatives for repeated-treatment requests.
(Causal banking proposal project, 2026dr)

39.50.2     H2O-3: separate fitting, baseline and scoring contracts

The selected H2O commit is dated 20 September 2026; its build property says 3.47.0 and
bleeding_edge. This is a pinned development profile, not a supported-release claim. Its Cox
implementation accepts start and stop columns, strata, offsets and observation weights, with
Efron or Breslow ties. The introductory document calls time columns integer-valued, but
inspected validation requires numeric columns and maps distinct stop times to indices. The
per-row discretizer rejects Li ≥ Ti ; the preliminary global check alone is not the full validation
path. The common task skips bad or zero-weight rows, while the processing routine rejects
nonpositive weights that reach it. A wrapper must report exclusions and resolved weights.
(H2O-3 contributors, 2026)
   The event routine subtracts the minimum observed event value and treats a positive
difference as an event. Multilevel codes are therefore not an automatic competing-risk model.
Require an explicit binary event mapping. Coefficient covariance in the inspected path is the
negative inverse Hessian; the R summary bridge explicitly says robust variance was not used.
Supplying inverse-probability weights alone does not supply uncertainty for estimated weights,
repeated histories or branch shocks. (H2O-3 contributors, 2026)
   The documentation has a weighted-likelihood discrepancy. Its displayed no-tie contribution
               P
is exp(wi ηi )/ j∈Ri wj exp(ηj ), whereas its Breslow expression and inspected Breslow code
raise the denominator to the event weight. With event weight two, another weight one, and
relative risks one and two, these expressions are 1/4 and 1/16. At covariates zero and one
with coefficient log 2, the corresponding log-likelihood derivatives are −1/2 and −1. This is
not an ignorable constant. Specify the implementation and tie/weight semantics, retain the
discrepancy, and require an independent fixture before native use. (H2O-3 contributors, 2026;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026dr)
   Baseline outputs require another check. One cumulative-hazard array uses tie-specific
risk-set denominators. Named baseline frames use a separate loop starting with total risk and
subtracting rows at stop times; that loop does not apply the Efron correction or add delayed
entrants at entry times. An abstract witness fixes unit risks: A fails at time one, B enters at
one and stops at two, and C is followed from zero to two. The declared risk set at time one is
A and C, giving increment 1/2; an all-row initial total gives 1/3. Two tied events among three
unit-risk rows separately give Breslow 2/3 and Efron 1/3 + 1/2 = 5/6. These are source-path
implications at supplied risks, not observed H2O runtime failures. Test the exact exported
baseline rather than treating similarly named outputs as interchangeable. (H2O-3 contributors,
2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026dr)
   The scoring frame is named lp and returns a centered linear predictor. The MOJO scorer
likewise returns a linear combination with stratum centering and offset, not an absolute survival
probability. Its reader loads coefficients, means, strata and interactions; this score alone does
not provide a horizon-specific baseline. The source includes parity tests for optional columns.
One categorical/stratified test deliberately uses Breslow because of a documented Java 11-plus
Efron issue. That comment identifies a qualification question, not failure in every current
environment. An original H2O fitting service and separately qualified portable scorer are
plausible choices; a whole-library port has no demonstrated benefit here. (H2O-3 contributors,

39.50.3     BioJava: an existing port still needs semantic review

The survival module belongs to a 7.3.1-SNAPSHOT parent. Source describes a port of portions
of R survival and explicitly says not all variants were implemented. The selected helper accepts
904                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


one event/censoring time, weights, strata and clusters. Its row object stores one time; this path

retained-row identities and convert null into a typed failure, never a zero coefficient. (BioJava

   The robust path saves naive variance, obtains score or dfbeta residuals, groups by cluster
when supplied and forms a cross-product. Strata conversion still needs care: the fitting arrays
describe terminal-row indicators, whereas the helper reads integers and the comparator sorts

need repair or refusal before reliance. A conjunction in the cluster guard can dereference

39.50.4     FRESCO-stat: confidentiality is a separate contract

At the pinned March 2023 commit, FRESCO-stat declares 0.6-SNAPSHOT, FRESCO 1.3.3

a field named censored. The gradient multiplies contributions by that field as an event-status

rather than guessing its encoding. (FRESCO-stat contributors, 2026)
   The public class comment says gradient descent, but the optimizer computes a Hessian
pseudoinverse, multiplies it by the gradient, and subtracts a scaled step for a fixed iteration
count. The result has coefficients, standard errors and a partial-likelihood-ratio statistic; the
inspected loop has no further convergence criterion. Fixed-point exponentials, inverses and
square roots add numerical obligations. The README warns that overflow can produce very

disclosure contract must name it. This inspection proves no complete security theorem or

proposal project, 2026dr)
  A separately qualified secure worker is a candidate when cross-custodian analysis justifies its

39.50.5     JLinAlg: explicit diagnostics and a narrower CLI

preserve the workflow chapter’s request, cancellation and artifact rules rather than silently

39.51      C++ survival components: preserving the event, clock
           and output
C++ survival components answer several different questions inside a banking workflow. A
collections team may want the observed probability of default by month twelve, the default
probability in a hypothetical world without prepayment, or the effect of a sequence of contact
decisions. These are different targets. A fast predictor of recorded survival time does not
choose among them. The proposed product must preserve the event dictionary, observation
and treatment clocks, competing transitions, selection law and uncertainty target before it
chooses a computational engine. This comparison examines four pinned lineages: XGBoost,
CatBoost, ranger and aorsf. The evidence consists of authenticated primary source and
documentation, not execution of these packages or their tests. Discovery remains bounded;
neither four candidates nor a repository search establishes exhaustive C++ coverage.(XGBoost
contributors, 2026; CatBoost contributors, 2026; ranger contributors, 2026; aorsf contributors,
2026)


39.51.1     The estimand precedes the software label

Let T be the first transition time and J its type, with J = D for default and J = P for
prepayment. The default cumulative incidence is FD (t) = Pr(T ≤ t, J = D). It is not generally
the complement of survival obtained by treating prepayments as ordinary censoring. In an
authored finite cohort of ten accounts, four prepay at time one, two default at time two and four
remain open. With these complete observations, the default incidence is 2/10. The product
of surviving all earlier transitions and the conditional default fraction is (6/10)(2/6) = 1/5.
Treating the four prepayments as censored instead gives the default-only complement 2/6 = 1/3.
This is a different functional, not an arithmetic refinement of the same answer. At a stipulated
USD 1,000 default loss, the two expected-loss calculations are USD 200 and USD 1,000/3.
Neither a different language nor more trees resolves the target substitution. A hypothetical
intervention eliminating prepayment also needs its own scientific assumptions; censoring a
record is not such an intervention.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026dq)
  Observation intervals need equally careful interpretation. If account i enters observation at
Li and exits at Ui , the risk indicator for a counting-process analysis is Yi (t) = 1{Li < t ≤ Ui }.
For the three authored intervals (0, 1], (1, 2] and (0, 2], with a default on the first account at
39.51. C++ survival components: preserving the event, clock and output                         907


time one, the correct risk set contains two accounts. Its unit-risk hazard increment is 1/2,
compared with 1/3 if every terminal-time row is treated as present from zero. Bounds on an
unknown failure time are different from entry and exit times: an interval-censored observation
says that an event occurred within a range, whereas delayed entry says when an account
becomes observable. An adapter must refuse their silent interchange. Repeated rows also do
not by themselves provide sequential exchangeability, positivity or cluster-valid uncertainty for
a treatment policy.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026dq)


39.51.2     Boosted Cox and accelerated failure time objectives

The selected XGBoost commit is c914bd00a946081c96e2f7aaa0e298f38b7b17e1, dated 7
October 2026. Its root build declares version 3.5.0; this identifies inspected development bytes,
not a supported binary release. The Cox objective sorts absolute labels, uses positive labels for
observed events and negative labels for censoring, and exponentiates the margin for prediction.
That exponentiated output is a relative risk score. It does not contain a baseline survival
curve or a monetary default probability. The inspected routine multiplies each final gradient
and Hessian by its row weight, while its risk-set exponential sum is unweighted. This source
contract must not be relabelled as an inverse-probability weighted longitudinal estimator
without a separate derivation.(XGBoost contributors, 2026)
   XGBoost’s AFT documentation instead specifies log T = m(x) + σZ, with normal, logistic
or extreme-value choices for Z. Its ranged labels encode exact, right-, left- or interval-censored
failure times. The examples use zero as a left bound and positive infinity as the right bound
for right censoring. The inspected CPU and CUDA kernels call the same distribution-specific
derivative helpers and apply row weights. The prediction transform returns exp(m(x)), while
the evaluation transform retains the raw margin for the AFT loss. Declared CUDA kernels
are evidence of implementation text, not observed GPU conformance, speed or numerical
parity. The pinned tutorial routes ranged labels through the native training and data-matrix
interfaces and states a limitation for its scikit-learn interface. These statements are tied to the
acquired version.(XGBoost contributors, 2026)
   The AFT output requires its distribution and scale to be useful. Consider an authored
logistic AFT law with exp(m) = 2 and horizon eight. For scale one, the failure probability is
F (log 4) = 4/5; for scale two it is F (log 2) = 2/3, where F (z) = ez /(1+ez ). Both models return
the same exponentiated location. A consumer that interprets that location as a probability
cannot distinguish them. The proposed result therefore carries the raw margin, transformed
location, distribution, scale, time unit and requested horizon as separate fields.(Causal banking
proposal project, 2026dq)
   The CatBoost commit 1ac99c589b54e91a349dd04a049f8ec1e1572326, also dated 7 Oc-
tober 2026, declares Python package version 1.2.10. Its documentation presents Cox and
SurvivalAft objectives and marks their GPU support unavailable in the inspected table. The
displayed Cox expression uses ai inside an exponential, and the AFT helper uses (log t − a)/σ.
These mathematical roles require more precise output typing than the documentation’s com-
mon phrase hazard rates. The raw objective margin is not an absolute hazard or probability.
CatBoost’s inspected AFT routine uses −1 as an unbounded endpoint, with a separate lower-
end branch for left censoring. XGBoost’s documented zero and infinity conventions therefore
cannot simply be copied into a CatBoost target array. End-to-end target validation and the
public prediction transformation still need a frozen wrapper review.(CatBoost contributors,
2026)
  Both projects clip or regularize AFT derivatives and provide limiting branches for numerically
extreme inputs. These choices are part of the computation, not proofs of statistical calibration.
908                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


CatBoost’s selected Cox and AFT derivative signatures leave their weight argument unused, but
the inspected Cox caller also passes weights into subsequent leaf accumulation. The appropriate
finding is that weighted-objective equivalence is unqualified: a local unused argument does
not establish that the entire training system ignores weights. A prototype must compare
the complete selected fitting path with an independently specified weighted target.(XGBoost
contributors, 2026; CatBoost contributors, 2026)


39.51.3     A tie fixture that can falsify silent equivalence

Source review supplies a concrete acceptance question before a costly benchmark. Take three
unit risk scores, with two observed events tied at time one and a third account censored at
time two. For margins fi , the Breslow negative log-likelihood contribution is

                           ℓ(f ) = −f1 − f2 + 2 log{ef1 + ef2 + ef3 }.

At zero margins its gradient is (−1/3, −1/3, 2/3). Its components sum to zero, as required
by invariance to a common additive margin. An independent rational trace of the inspected
XGBoost loop, in event/event/censor order, gives (−2/3, −1/3, 2/3): the first tied event is
processed before the second event’s reciprocal-risk contribution enters the running accumulator.
The sum is −1/3. The analogous inspected CatBoost loop removes the previous exponential
at each positive event and gives negative-log-likelihood-sign scores (−2/3, −1/6, 5/6). Their
sum is zero, but the two tied events are not symmetric and the vector differs from the stated
Breslow derivative. These are abstract source-loop traces, not native benchmark results or a
claim that every release, wrapper or training regime behaves identically.(XGBoost contributors,
2026; CatBoost contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026dq)
   The next justified experiment is narrow: freeze the complete dispatch path, evaluate
equal-time permutations and event/censor ties, compare finite-difference derivatives with an
independent likelihood, and retain both the returned gradients and row identities. Non-unit
weights and extreme margins form separate fixtures. A failing fixture would justify a restricted
regime, another engine, or a reviewed repair; it would not justify silently changing the scientific
likelihood. Until that experiment is admitted and performed, these findings remain source-level
concerns and acceptance criteria.


39.51.4     Survival forests and transformations that change the decision

ranger is pinned to dafa5db57972dd49c808db881e6e6cd5c4ebdc4a, dated 16 January 2026;
its R description declares 0.18.0. The inspected C++ leaf routine sums dj /nj to construct a
cumulative hazard. The forest averages those hazards, and the inspected R prediction wrapper
returns survival as the exponential of their negative. Its OOB error uses one minus concordance
on summed cumulative hazards for accounts with at least one OOB tree. That is a ranking
diagnostic, not an interval for a causal effect or a certification of horizon calibration. The
wrapper rejects nonbinary event coding in the selected survival path, and its two standard-error
choices explicitly reject survival forests. Case weights are documented as sampling weights for
bootstrap or subsampling selection. These contracts are more specific than the labels weighted
forest or uncertainty available.(ranger contributors, 2026)
   aorsf is pinned to 085db7062d995eeafa4e210481d66af2eb02b8dc, dated 5 February 2026;
its description declares 0.1.6. Its documented accelerated survival control uses a one-iteration
Cox fit to construct split directions. The C++ delegate distinguishes that path from further
iterations. This is a tree-building choice, not a claim that the final forest is a converged
Cox regression. The selected leaf code maintains a product-limit survival estimate and an
39.51. C++ survival components: preserving the event, clock and output                       909


additive cumulative-hazard estimate separately, with weighted event and risk counts. The
wrapper documents normalization of supplied weights to the number of observations. Risk,
survival, cumulative hazard, mortality and time are distinct prediction types. Predictions
beyond maximum follow-up are documented as constant if boundary checks are disabled; a
flat continuation is not evidence about an unobserved future.(aorsf contributors, 2026)
   For an authored leaf with one event among two at risk, the product-limit survival is 1/2,
whereas the cumulative hazard is 1/2 and its exponential survival is e−1/2 ≃ 0.606531. The
corresponding risks are 0.5 and approximately 0.393469. With a stipulated USD 450 premium
and USD 1,000 loss, the margins are USD −50 and approximately USD 56.53. These are
deliberately simple constructed outputs; they are not observed errors or bank estimates. They
show why a consumer must retain the estimator and transformation, even when both fields are
called survival. Aggregation creates another distinction: for two authored hazards (0, log 4),
exponentiating the negative average gives 1/2, while averaging their exponentiated negatives
gives 5/8. An adapter must reproduce the declared aggregation order rather than substitute a
familiar formula.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026dq)


39.51.5    Integration, adoption and justified rejection

The proposed first route retains original engines behind typed workers. XGBoost and CatBoost
are conditional boosted-prediction alternatives once their objective, endpoint, margin, weight,
tie and environment contracts pass selected fixtures. ranger’s standalone C++ library or CLI
and its R wrapper are separate packaging choices; the inspected build declares C++14 and
library/CLI targets. Its primary headers explicitly distinguish the MIT C++ core from the
GPL-3 R package. XGBoost and CatBoost have Apache-2.0 root declarations. aorsf declares
MIT and R/Rcpp/RcppArmadillo dependencies. These direct declarations do not clear every
dependency, model artifact or redistribution. Rights review must bind the actual chosen
distribution.(XGBoost contributors, 2026; CatBoost contributors, 2026; ranger contributors,
2026; aorsf contributors, 2026)
   For aorsf, an original R worker preserves the formula, validation and prediction semantics
while using its C++ core. Extracting that core into a new standalone port would require
recreating the R-side contract and numeric dependencies; the proposal has not demonstrated a
benefit sufficient to justify that work. For ranger, direct C++ embedding remains an alternative
to an R worker when deployment requirements and rights justify the separate interface. Whole-
library rewrites are rejected for the present proposal because they add parity and maintenance
obligations without demonstrated need. Native workers, a dedicated longitudinal R/Python
estimator and an independent finite-law reference remain substantive alternatives, selected
according to the target rather than language preference.(aorsf contributors, 2026; ranger
contributors, 2026)
   The CLI and MCP proposal should expose a versioned request containing population,
time zero, availability clock, event dictionary, competing-event interpretation, entry/censoring
representation, treatment history, weights and their meaning, sampling units, horizons, options
and artifact hashes. The result must preserve accepted and rejected row identities, objective and
output type, baseline or distribution parameters, convergence/numerical warnings, uncertainty
method, timing and complete request costs. Refusal is a typed result. A finite output, successful
process exit or replayed artifact must not be promoted to causal identification or qualified
uncertainty. These are proposed interfaces; no new native adapter or sibling integration is
implemented by this review.
  The method owner must first decide whether a public or generated study can identify the
proposed target. The adapter owner then freezes version, wrapper and conversion fixtures;
910                                                                 Causal analysis for a universal bank


the rights owner resolves the actual distribution; the evaluation owner preregisters held-out
targets, ties, censoring and competing events, row permutations, dependent units, failure
denominators and full costs. No purchase, vendor trial or expensive bank experiment is
necessary to write those contracts. Candidate aliases, unreturned discovery tails, uninspected
delegates, cluster-calibrated uncertainty and native performance remain recorded follow-ups.
This bounded comparison improves the proposal’s executable evidence and actions without
declaring C++ longitudinal coverage complete.


39.52      Julia and Rust survival components: preserving the clock
           and the estimand
A collections decision is defined by its clock before it is defined by its software language.
Consider accounts eligible for a payment holiday at the start of a month. The bank may
compare initiation within a grace period against continued ordinary servicing, follow default
and prepayment, and value interest receipts during a fixed horizon. A program that returns a
survival curve has solved only one part of this problem. The eligibility date, treatment strategy,
event definition, observation mechanism and sampling unit must survive the translation from
the business request to the estimator. This section examines six concrete Julia and Rust
alternatives at commits preceding the client cutoff of 7 October 2026. Their role is conditional
reuse or reference, not evidence that a native causal product has already been qualified.


39.52.1     A target and an observation contract

Let T a denote event time under strategy a, measured from eligibility, and let Sa (t) = Pr(T a > t).
Two possible targets are the event-risk contrast
                                                               Z τ
                       1              0
        ∆F (τ ) = Pr(T ≤ τ ) − Pr(T ≤ τ ),         ∆M (τ ) =         {S1 (t) − S0 (t)} dt.      (39.23)
                                                                0

The first is a probability difference; the second is a restricted-mean survival-time difference
and has time units. If the event is default, prepayment needs an explicit competing-event
or hypothetical-intervention interpretation. Treating prepayment as ordinary independent
censoring changes the question unless the necessary assumptions are supplied. These definitions
do not by themselves identify either counterfactual curve. Consistency, treatment and censoring
exchangeability under the specified history, positivity and an appropriate observation law
remain substantive conditions.
   Write Li for entry, Ci for right censoring and Tei for observed exit. For a continuous clock
with a declared boundary convention, a risk indicator might be Yi (t) = 1{Li < t ≤ Tei }. By
contrast, an interval-censored record (ui , vi ] says that the event occurred somewhere in that
interval; it does not say that observation began at ui . Three otherwise eligible accounts, one
entering after the first observed event, give a first-event increment 1/2, while ignoring entry
gives 1/3. This exact example concerns data meaning, not numerical speed. The independent
reference also constructs two deterministic event times, four and two months, with horizon
five. Their restricted means differ by two months while their event risks at the horizon are
both one, so the risk difference is zero. Multiplying the time scale by thirty changes the mean
contrast to sixty days and leaves the probability contrast unchanged.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026er)
   The proposed command and MCP request must therefore bind population, eligibility clock,
intervention strategy, history availability, entry, censoring, competing events, horizon, output
39.52. Julia and Rust survival components: preserving the clock and the estimand                911


units and sampling unit before selecting an engine. A convenient two-column schema is
insufficient evidence that two engines implement the same target.


39.52.2     Julia alternatives and their distinct contracts

The JuliaStats Survival.jl snapshot declares version 0.3.3 and Julia 1.10 compatibility, with a
direct MIT licence. Its exported event type contains a time and a Boolean event/right-censoring
indicator. The event-table constructors, Kaplan–Meier component and Cox fitting component
provide useful building blocks for a narrow right-censored worker. They do not, through that
response type alone, encode entry or a treatment history. The inspected Cox objective uses
fractional removal of tied event risk scores, an Efron-style convention.(JuliaStats Survival.jl
contributors, 2026)
   Even this narrow candidate needs explicit boundary fixtures. In the inspected zero-time
helper, the first nonzero index is i and the deletion interval is start : (start + i − 1). For a
conventional one-based vector with times (0, 1, 2), the abstract trace removes indices one and
two, leaving only time two. If all times are zero, the first-nonzero search has no result and
the deletion branch is not entered. The already-sorted event-vector constructor also passes
its vector into this mutating helper; its comment that the input is unaffected does not settle
aliasing. These are source-local concerns with inspected constructor and export paths, not
reported outcomes from a Julia execution. The safe proposal route is to reject unsupported
zero-time inputs until the intended rule and a native regression fixture are agreed; silently
adding a small epsilon would change the clock and conceal the question.(JuliaStats Survival.jl
contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026er)
   SurvivalAnalysis.jl supplies another architecture. Its pinned version 0.1.0 declares Julia
compatibility ˆ1.2 and MIT licensing. Its response hierarchy contains right-, left- and interval-
censored forms, but the inspected documentation explicitly says that only right-censoring
methods are included. In particular, Surv(start,stop) represents interval censoring. The
parametric fitting dispatch takes a right-censored response and admits Weibull or exponential
baselines. The Hessian inverse and standard-error calculation have exception paths producing
NaNs. An adapter must report those outcomes as unavailable uncertainty, not replace them
with zero standard errors. PH prediction distinguishes a linear predictor from a transformed
survival distribution, which is useful for a typed output contract. The stated candidate role is
an original Julia parametric worker, subject to baseline, optimisation and uncertainty checks;
its response classes do not justify a universal censoring claim.(SurvivalAnalysis.jl contributors,
2022)
   SurvivalModels.jl, at its pinned 0.1.6 declaration with Julia 1.11 compatibility and MIT
licensing, develops parametric general-hazard alternatives and Cox and nonparametric compo-
nents. The inspected CoxDefault implementation groups tied times before subtracting d log R
from the log likelihood: this is a Breslow-style tied denominator. It should not be expected to
agree numerically with the preceding Efron-style path for every tied data set. With risk scores
(1, 2, 3) and the first two subjects failing together, the numerator is two and the total risk score
is six. The Breslow partial-likelihood contribution is 2/62 = 1/18, whereas fractional removal
gives 2/[6(6 − 3/2)] = 2/27. A parity fixture must name its tie convention before classifying a
difference as a failure.(SurvivalModels.jl contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026er)
   Its Kaplan–Meier constructor forms event increments at stored event/censor times. The
vector survival prediction takes their cumulative product; scalar prediction uses only times
strictly less than the requested time. For one event at time two among two accounts, with
the other censored at four, the abstract boundary values are S(2−) = 1 and S(2) = 1/2.
912                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


The inspected scalar and stored-grid routes thus encode different sides of the jump, despite
documentation describing the usual less-than-or-equal product. The proposed wrapper must
explicitly distinguish left limits from survival after the event and test scalar/vector agreement
under the chosen meaning. A package name or a successful fit cannot resolve this discrepancy.
Delegated SurvivalBase and SurvivalDistributions behaviour remains a separate inspection
obligation. (SurvivalModels.jl contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026er)
   JointSurvivalModels.jl offers a different reuse candidate: constructing distributions from
hazards linked to a longitudinal process. Its version 1.0.0 snapshot declares Julia 1 compatibility
and MIT licensing. The inspected structure combines a baseline hazard with covariate and
linked-process effects. This can help formulate a stipulated joint model of servicing history
and event time, but a model of association does not identify a payment-holiday intervention.
Numerical support defaults to a positive lower endpoint 10−4 and upper endpoint 104 ; hazard
integration begins at the configured lower endpoint. The sampling method accepts a random
generator but the inspected uniform draw calls the unqualified global random function.
Integration tolerance, tail support and generator routing must therefore be inspected and tested
before reproducibility or distributional accuracy is claimed. A conditional modelling worker is
plausible; a blanket port would import these unresolved semantics. (JointSurvivalModels.jl
contributors, 2024)


39.52.3     Rust causal labels require method-level inspection

The Cameron-Lyons survival repository declares version 2.0.0, edition 2024, Rust 1.94 and MIT
licensing at the pinned commit. These are declarations in the snapshot, not evidence of a tested
toolchain or supported release. Its public Rust module path re-exports target-trial, marginal-
structural-model and TMLE-named functions. Python registration is delegated and is not
established merely by a Rust export. This explicit distinction matters because an integration
proposal must name the entrypoint whose behaviour is being assessed.(Cameron-Lyons survival
contributors, 2026)
   In the inspected target-trial function, a treated clone initiating within the grace period
receives follow-up min(Te − tA , τ ), while the control clone uses a clock censored at treatment
initiation. With eligibility zero, treatment at month two, event at month ten and grace period
three, the untruncated treated duration is eight rather than ten months from eligibility. With
maximum follow-up five, the treated duration becomes five but its event flag retains the original
event status. The authored trace is (5, 1), while an origin-clock observation administratively
censored at five would be (5, 0). This does not establish runtime behaviour of every wrapper;
it establishes why a native admission fixture must bind origin, grace-period strategy, censoring
time and event status jointly. (Cameron-Lyons survival contributors, 2026; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026er)
   The inspected censoring-weight routine ignores its censoring-covariate arguments, assigns
protocol-censored clones a constant based on the trimming option and can then normalise
the weights to mean one. It is not a fitted conditional censoring model in this path. If two
hypothetical conditional observation probabilities are 1/2 and 1/4, their inverse weights are
two and four and their mean-normalised weights are 2/3 and 4/3. Giving both records ten
and normalising yields one and one; normalisation cannot create the missing conditioning
information. Likewise, a longitudinal weight’s numerator model has a meaning distinct from
mean normalisation. Two treatment probabilities 1/4 and 1/2 give an unstabilised weight eight;
numerator probabilities 1/2 and 1/2 give a stabilised weight two, whereas mean normalisation
of a single weight gives one. (Cameron-Lyons survival contributors, 2026; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026er)
39.52. Julia and Rust survival components: preserving the clock and the estimand               913


   Output and uncertainty contracts need equally close attention.                  The inspected
risk_difference field is assigned the difference between restricted means, which has
time units. The main calculation weights clones and uses one hundred grid points; its
subject-resampling bootstrap recreates clones without the inspected censoring-weight call and
uses fifty grid points. Fewer than two bootstrap results trigger a fixed pair of 0.5 standard
errors. The sequential-trial helper skips small eligible sets and retains successful results from a
conditional call, so a delivery wrapper must preserve attempted, skipped, failed and returned
trial counts. These findings motivate rejection of direct causal admission for these entrypoints
at this snapshot, not rejection of every component in the repository. (Cameron-Lyons survival
contributors, 2026)
   The inspected survival-TMLE function assigns outcome one to observations surviving beyond
a horizon, zero to prior observed events and one half to observations censored before that
horizon. A half is an assumption about an unresolved outcome. With one known survivor, one
known event and two unresolved records among four subjects, the finite-cohort survival fraction
can range from 1/4 to 3/4; imputing one half for each unresolved record chooses 1/2. It does
not identify that value. The inspected function fits a propensity and an outcome regression
but contains no explicit censoring-model adjustment for that assignment. Its restricted-mean
integration starts at the first supplied horizon, while its reported mean-time standard error is an
unweighted combination of pointwise errors without time widths or cross-horizon covariances.
Rescaling months to days must rescale a time-valued standard error; the abstract expression
without time widths does not do so. A method name cannot substitute for these checks, and
no conclusion here extends to uninspected censoring or TMLE alternatives elsewhere in the
repository. (Cameron-Lyons survival contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026er)

39.52.4     An interval-data candidate and a justified refusal

The small Rust turnbull snapshot declares version 0.1.0 and edition 2021. No licence grant was
located in the inspected Cargo declaration or complete root tree, so adoption or redistribution
cannot be presumed. Its response type includes interval and entry information, but the
inspected estimator constructs support only from uncensored exact-event times and an infinity
point; handling truncation and variance is marked unfinished. With only finite intervals (1, 2]
and (2, 3], this abstract support construction supplies only infinity. Neither interval contains
that point, so both membership rows have zero sum. The normalisation step then has no
positive denominator. This is a reproducible support witness, not a native Rust test result. The
visible convergence loop also lacks an explicit iteration cap. (mwklose turnbull contributors,
2024; Causal banking proposal project, 2026er)
   The defensible proposal disposition is reference-only pending source, rights and algorithmic
repairs. A qualified interval-censoring worker would need an appropriate support construction, a
declared truncation likelihood, finite-iteration and nonfinite-value handling, and an uncertainty
contract. A zero variance placeholder must not become a claim of certainty. An interval-only
fixture is especially valuable because ordinary exact-event examples can succeed without
exercising the capability named by the package.

39.52.5     Adoption choices, public prototypes and full costs

The preferred architecture preserves selected original engines behind typed, versioned workers.
JuliaStats is a candidate for narrowly specified right-censored estimation after boundary
qualification; SurvivalAnalysis for its declared parametric response family; SurvivalModels for
explicit tie and prediction contracts; and JointSurvivalModels for a stipulated joint distribution
914                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


after numerical and random generator checks. Rust components can be reference or future
worker candidates, but the inspected causal entrypoints require semantic repair before admission.
The interval-data prototype remains reference-only while its licence and support questions are
unresolved. Whole-library ports are not justified by language preference alone: a port transfers
maintenance, rights, numerical and semantic obligations without supplying identification.
   A generated/public prototype can test the merit of this architecture before an expensive
bank experiment. Register exact-event, all-censored, zero-time, delayed-entry, interval-only,
tied-event, competing-event, administrative-censoring and malformed-input fixtures; match
each fixture to a target-specific oracle. Compare scalar and vector outputs, time-unit rescaling,
row permutations, random-seed routing and complete estimator resampling. Separately
evaluate uncertainty under a declared independent or clustered sampling law. Finite-law
examples establish those exact laws; public data establish only the observable behaviours and
assumptions they actually support. Neither silently supplies counterfactual bank truth.
   The CLI/MCP result should carry the source snapshot, environment and rights profile,
original row and subject identities, target and clock, tie/boundary options, diagnostics, refusal
reason, uncertainty method and complete costs. Preserve unsuccessful requests and human
repairs in the denominator. In a stipulated accounting example, twelve initiated requests
costing USD 36 and producing three accepted numeric deliveries cost USD 3 per initiation
but USD 12 per accepted delivery. Correct refusals should be scored separately from accepted
numeric results; deleting them would distort both reliability and cost. These amounts are
authored examples, not vendor prices or measured performance.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026er)
  The six selected profiles constitute a contrastive review, not exhaustive other-language
coverage. The Julia discovery tail, Rust alternatives, failed target-trial search and uninspected
delegates remain explicit follow-ups. The method owner must approve the target and obser-
vation law; the adapter owner must preserve units, failures and identities; the rights owner
must clear the exact distribution; and the evaluation owner must preregister public/generated
comparisons. This gives concrete next actions while leaving native, exhaustive and bank
acceptance unestablished.


39.53      R policy learning: what is optimised, what is evaluated,
           and what remains unknown
A servicing policy should be judged by the value of the decisions it will make after selection.
Consider a bank choosing between a reminder, a payment holiday and ordinary servicing at
successive monthly decisions. A shallow decision tree can describe an interpretable allocation;
a backward regression can construct a sequence of actions; and a policy evaluator can estimate
the value of a supplied rule. These are related services, but they have different targets and
failure modes. This section compares policytree, DynTxRegime, DTRreg and polle at pinned
commits preceding 7 October 2026. It develops conditional original-R-worker choices from
inspected technical sources. Native behaviour, the original methodological papers referenced
by those packages, complete rights and exhaustive R coverage remain separate obligations.


39.53.1    Three targets that an interface must distinguish

Let Ht be the information available before the stage-t action At , and let d = (d1 , . . . , dK )
be a policy with At = dt (Ht ). For a stipulated utility U , write V (d) = E[U d ]. The value
of a fixed rule d, the value of a data-selected rule d,
                                                     b and the best value sup
                                                                              d∈D V (d) over a
39.53. R policy learning: what is optimised, what is evaluated, and what remains unknown      915


declared policy class D are different objects. Exact empirical optimisation within shallow
trees establishes neither population optimality nor optimality over unrestricted policies. An
estimated value for rules trained on subsets also need not be the value of the final rule refitted
on all observations. The request must identify which of these is intended.
  Selection alone can create apparent value. Suppose two policies each have true value zero,
and their independent development-value errors are equally likely to be minus one or plus
one dollar. Selecting the larger estimate has development expectation E[max(ϵ1 , ϵ2 )] = 1/2
dollar: the maximum is minus one only when both errors are negative, with probability 1/4.
The selected policy’s fresh expected value is still zero in this stipulated law. No defect in the
optimiser is needed. A held-out evaluation or a justified design for adaptive-policy evaluation
addresses a different question from improving the empirical search. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ed)
  The familiar one-stage augmented score also exposes the assumptions that a software label
can hide. For action a, define

                                            1{A = a}
                           Γa = ma (X) +             {Y − ma (X)}.                         (39.24)
                                             eba (X)

Conditional on X and fixed fitted nuisance functions, let ea = Pr(A = a | X) and µa = E[Y |
A = a, X]. Direct conditioning gives
                                                 ea
                                                      
                            E[Γa | X] − µa = 1 −     (ma − µa ).                           (39.25)
                                                 eba
Thus either correct nuisance function removes this conditional mean error, where the propensity
denominator is positive and the expectations exist. Interpreting µa causally still requires the
relevant consistency and exchangeability conditions. Conditioning on fixed nuisance fits is
also not a licence to reuse the same observations adaptively without further analysis. With
µa = 10, ma = 8, ea = 1/4 and eba = 1/2, the expected score is nine, not ten; correcting either
nuisance gives ten in this exact example. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ed)
   When an action has no logging support, neither optimisation nor a fitted propensity creates
evidence for its reward. A logger that always takes action zero with reward zero is compatible
with both minus ten and plus ten dollars under action one. These worlds have the same
observed data but different optimal decisions. A bank must supply additional justified structure,
new information or an experiment; there is no universal software repair for this unrestricted
gap.


39.53.2     policytree: a useful optimiser with an upstream score obligation

The inspected policytree declaration is version 1.2.5, requiring R at least 3.5.0, with MIT
plus its licence file and dependencies including grf and Rcpp. Its main interface accepts a
feature matrix X and an action-reward matrix Γ. The documentation describes exhaustive
shallow-tree search and explains the substantial dependence on depth, feature count and
distinct feature values. The optional split.step skips candidate splits; hybrid search builds
a deeper tree using limited lookahead. The latter is a different optimisation procedure, not an
unqualified certificate of the same global optimum. (policytree contributors, 2026)
   The inspected R wrapper checks numeric matrix/data-frame inputs, missing entries, match-
ing row counts, nonnegative depth and positive integer split and node-size controls. It passes
the matrices to an Rcpp binding, which invokes the C++ tree search. The inspected leaf
routine maximises sums of supplied rewards, retaining the earlier action on exact reward ties
because its update uses a strict greater-than comparison. Recursive paths check interrupt
916                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


requests and split eligibility. These details make an original R worker a plausible proposal
choice, but they do not establish runtime bounds on an arbitrary input or causal validity of the
supplied reward matrix. The wrapper needs explicit finite-value, depth/resource and action-ID
policies, with native tests of the exact entrypoint before admission. (policytree contributors,
2026)
   The binary causal-forest score adapter constructs the two conditional mean estimates from
forest predictions and forms the augmented scores using observed treatment propensities.
In the inspected function, the inverse propensity is calculated directly; support and any
upstream grf safeguards therefore need to be matched explicitly. An adapter should record
whether the supplied scores are out-of-sample, which nuisance version produced them and
which observations were used to select the policy. It should not label an arbitrary matrix as
doubly robust evidence. The package’s train/test example is useful documentation, but a
complete learning procedure must also account for nuisance and feature-selection dependencies.
(policytree contributors, 2026)
   Prediction adds a mundane but material banking risk: feature meaning can change without
changing matrix dimensions. The R method checks the column count, while its documentation
requires the training order. The C++ prediction path follows numeric split-column positions. A
CLI/MCP worker should bind names, order, units and preprocessing to the fitted artifact, and
refuse a schema mismatch. Action indices similarly need a stable mapping to reminder, holiday
and ordinary servicing. The proposed choice is to integrate the original optimiser behind
a schema-aware worker and an independently qualified scoring/evaluation layer. A whole
C++ port is unnecessary unless a measured deployment constraint justifies its maintenance.
(policytree contributors, 2026)


39.53.3    DynTxRegime and DTRreg: sequential structure is an explicit
           modelling choice

DynTxRegime’s pinned 4.16 declaration identifies Q-learning, interactive Q-learning, weighted
learning and value-search families, with GPL-2 licensing and dependencies including modelObj,
kernlab and optimisation packages. Its qLearn interface performs a single backward step. A
numeric response starts the recursion; a prior QLearn object passes the preceding estimated
value into the next step. The inspected dispatch verifies model objects, the data frame,
response and feasible action-set interface, then delegates regression and prediction. A sequence
of calls therefore needs a declared stage order, available histories and reward convention; the
existence of the object hierarchy does not prove that the chosen regression models identify the
bank’s optimal strategy. The documented training-set value must be kept distinct from an
external evaluation of the resulting rule. (DynTxRegime contributors, 2025)
   This is a reasonable original-R-worker candidate where its model and action-set interfaces
match the question. The alternatives are to use a different qualified sequential estimator,
to retain it as a mathematical/design reference, or to defer a family whose delegates and
assumptions have not been inspected. The package-level listing of methods must not close
every method-specific coverage cell. In particular, the selected Q-learning dispatch does not
establish a universal outcome-weighted, value-search or hidden-state capability.
   DTRreg version 2.4 declares GPL-2 and provides dynamic weighted least squares, G-
estimation, Q-learning and survival-related families. The inspected DTRreg documentation
specifies treatment, treatment-free and blip models at each stage; it restricts continuous-
treatment blips to a quadratic form. Its direct consistency claims depend on model conditions
and should be assessed against the methodological originals before inheritance as a theorem.
In the inspected dispatcher, multinomial G-estimation is explicitly rejected. Backward stage
39.53. R policy learning: what is optimised, what is evaluated, and what remains unknown      917


fitting is followed by forward recalculation of selected treatments and renewed pseudo-outcome
construction. That is a substantive sequential algorithm, not a collection of unrelated stagewise
regressions.(DTRreg contributors, 2026)
   The continuous-action domain illustrates why an apparently precise optimum can exceed
the evidence. For a stipulated benefit u(a) = 8a − 2a2 , the nonnegative unrestricted optimum
is a = 2 with value eight. If observed actions cover only [0, 1], the supported optimum is a = 1
with value six. A second response curve can equal this quadratic on [0, 1] and continue as
6 − 100(a − 1) beyond one; the observed action range cannot distinguish it, but its optimum
remains one. Choosing the first curve’s extrapolated optimum requires the quadratic restriction
outside support. Clipping a recommendation is a policy constraint, whereas asserting the
extrapolated optimum is an identification claim.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ed)
  DTRreg’s inspected weight dispatcher distinguishes inverse probability, capped inverse
probability, overlap and other paths. The capped path uses the empirical 99th percentile.
Trimming can control extremes, but it changes the estimating expression and does not restore
unsupported actions. In an exact four-stage example with probability 1/10 of the required
action at each stage, the target path occurs with probability 1/10,000 and has inverse weight
10,000. With unit reward and a cap of one hundred, the expectation of the capped path
contribution is 1/100 instead of one. This is an authored illustration of the tradeoff, not a
benchmark of DTRreg’s default settings.(DTRreg contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ed)
   Its selected bootstrap resamples participant rows, reconstructs the object and reruns the
stage procedure. An interruption returns an explicit aborted result; NA parameter draws
trigger an error before covariance construction. An optional tail replacement modifies bootstrap
draws before variance calculation. These are observable source contracts that a worker should
preserve. They do not establish finite-sample coverage, justify treating correlated bank accounts
as independent, or remove nonregularity near tied optimal actions. The documentation warns
about nonunique optimal treatment only when a variance-estimation option is selected; absence
of that warning otherwise is not evidence of a unique optimum. (DTRreg contributors, 2026)


39.53.4     polle: separating training, evaluation and history restrictions

The pinned polle 1.6.5 declaration describes policy learning and evaluation, requires R at
least 4.1 and lists an Apache License at version two or later. Its dependencies include
policytree, DynTxRegime, survival and targeted; this declaration is not transitive rights
clearance. The inspected evaluator accepts either a fixed policy or a learner, and distinguishes
value evaluation from a restricted single-stage, binary-action subgroup effect. It accepts
separate action, outcome, censoring and terminal-outcome models. Source checks request
censoring models when relevant censoring events occur and a terminal-outcome model for
the specified missing terminal-utility case. These are useful refusal semantics for a proposed
worker. (polle contributors, 2026)
   The default evaluator has M=1. In that branch, training and validation objects are the same.
For M>1, the inspected routine constructs folds, splits by the policy-data IDs and passes distinct
training and validation objects to the evaluation function. That function sends the training
object to fit_functions; when no fixed policy is supplied, the inspected delegate invokes
the learner on that training object before evaluating on validation data. This establishes a
concrete source path for outer evaluation separation. It does not by itself prove independence
of related accounts, prevent leakage through externally supplied fitted nuisance objects, or
validate every delegated learner. The choice of a fixed policy, training algorithm, training
sample size and final refit must appear in the reported target.(polle contributors, 2026)
918                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   History compression is another explicit restriction. The inspected interfaces have separate
full-history flags for action, outcome and censoring models and for the policy itself, with
state-like histories as defaults. In a stipulated example, an earlier binary observation H is
fair, the present state is constant, and utility is 1{A = H}. A rule retaining H achieves
value one; every fixed action using only the constant state achieves one half. A smaller state
representation is not harmless merely because an API accepts it. The bank must explain why
the retained state suffices for the causal and decision questions, or preserve the history and
evaluate the larger model.(polle contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ed)
   The learning interface offers distinct Q-learning, doubly robust Q-learning, tree and weighted-
learning choices, with method-specific restrictions and delegates. Nested nuisance-fitting folds
and outer policy-evaluation folds are different controls. An adapter must preserve both, record
any supplied prefit models and avoid translating a method name into a blanket calibration claim.
Source comments about the orientation of one weighted-learning solver require inspection of
that delegate before they are inherited as established behaviour. For the present proposal,
polle is a conditional original-R-worker candidate with named method, history, support and
evaluation contracts.(polle contributors, 2026)


39.53.5     Qualification through public and generated tasks

The package comparisons lead to a practical prototype rather than an immediate whole-library
rewrite. Use a small finite-state servicing generator with known policy values and action
probabilities; add public longitudinal data only for properties its observed records can support.
Compare fixed-policy value, selected policy value and constrained empirical optimisation
separately. Include zero and small support, tied best actions, history loss, continuous-action
extrapolation, censoring and wrong-schema fixtures. Evaluation should retain failed fits,
aborted bootstraps, correct refusals and repair costs, rather than reporting only returned
numeric estimates. The exact logger, task and policy versions must survive through CLI and
MCP artifacts.
   Sampling units are part of this contract. Suppose two independent borrower groups each
produce one Bernoulli-half outcome, copied across one hundred linked accounts. The variance
of the overall mean is 1/8; falsely treating two hundred rows as independent gives 1/800, a
factor of one hundred smaller. Subject IDs and ordinary cross-fitting do not automatically
solve dependence between distinct IDs. The appropriate grouping and uncertainty design must
follow the declared sampling law. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ed)
   Each worker should return policy-class and action-domain restrictions, feature and history
schemas, training/evaluation membership, logger/support diagnostics, utility units and costs,
uncertainty method and refusal reasons. With twenty initiated requests costing USD 100 and
five accepted numeric results, the cost is USD 20 per accepted numeric delivery, compared
with USD 5 per initiation. Four correct refusals can be reported as useful safety outcomes
without relabelling them as numeric deliveries. These are stipulated accounting quantities;
vendor charges, bank value and production throughput remain unmeasured.(Causal banking
proposal project, 2026ed)
  The preferred choices are conditional integration of original R workers, direct use of the
authored finite-law oracles, and refusal of unsupported conversions. A port needs a specific
performance or platform case and must preserve statistical meaning, rights, diagnostics and
maintenance responsibilities. The four profiles leave other R families, delegated methods
and original theoretical results to be inspected. Unknown logging, unsupported actions and
unrestricted hidden state still require new information or justified restrictions. This bounded
comparison supplies a route without claiming exhaustive policy coverage or native acceptance.

39.54      Choosing a Python policy component by the question it
           can answer
A bank comparing Python policy tools must first decide whether it is evaluating a single offer,
a sequence of servicing decisions, a newly learned rule, or a plan conditional on a supplied
hidden-state model. These questions need different information and different validation. The
preceding original-source profiles provide four contrastive choices: Open Bandit Pipeline
(OBP), SCOPE-RL, d3rlpy and POMDP-Py. Their common Python interface does not make
their policy-value outputs interchangeable. This synthesis uses the exact previously inspected
revisions and their original source records; it adds no assertion of a newer release or a native
comparison.(Yuta Saito and Open Bandit Pipeline contributors, 2022; Haruka Kiyohara and
SCOPE-RL contributors, 2023; d3rlpy contributors, 2025b; Kaiyu Zheng and POMDP-Py
contributors, 2025)

   POMDP-Py occupies a different role. Its belief update consumes a transition law, observation
law and prior belief; its planner searches within that supplied model. It can support an
architectural or numerical comparison when those laws are specified, but cannot by itself
identify them from partially observed logs. The inspected histogram update normalizes only
when its total mass is positive. An impossible observation must be exposed as such, rather
than relabeling a zero-mass output as a valid posterior. Belief, model and planner errors
require different diagnostics.(Kaiyu Zheng and POMDP-Py contributors, 2025)
   This gives a practical selection rule. Use a contextual estimator for a justified single-decision
target; use sequential scores for a supported logged trajectory target; consider a learner and its
matching evaluator for a frozen learned policy; and use a hidden-state planner for a justified
supplied-model planning target. When the substantive assumptions fail, switching packages is
not a repair. The request should instead return an identified set, a sensitivity result, a need
for additional information, or a refusal with its reason.


39.54.2     Evaluation of a learned rule differs from learning its value

Let Dtrain be the data used to choose π   b , and let Deval be an evaluation sample under a
justified logging and sampling law. Conditional evaluation asks for J(π  b ) given the trained
rule. Assessment of the learning algorithm averages over possible training samples. The value
supπ∈Π J(π) of a policy class, or an unrestricted optimum, is a third target. Neither a large
fitted value nor a winner among estimated values equates these objects. A comparison must
freeze which target it reports, including the policy’s randomness, constraints, postprocessing
and version.
   This matters when combining the libraries. SCOPE-RL’s selected input machinery delegates
fitted-Q work and caches models by policy name. The standalone d3rlpy revision reviewed here
is not automatically the exact delegate imported by that SCOPE-RL environment. Matching
a package name is insufficient: the dependency version, artifact and selected calling path
need their own binding. The policy name should also not be the sole identity of a retrained
rule. A proposed value artifact should bind policy bytes, preprocessing, feature order, fitting
data, hyperparameters, stochastic deployment rule, evaluator and target population. (Haruka
Kiyohara and SCOPE-RL contributors, 2023; Causal banking proposal, 2026at)
   Uncertainty needs the same precision. The selected OBP and SCOPE-RL interval paths
resample already calculated scores. They do not thereby repeat all nuisance fitting, normaliza-
tion and policy selection. Conditioning on fitted functions can be valid in a justified design, but
must be the actual scientific claim. In the earlier exact self-normalization example, fixed-score
bootstrap means are (0, 3, 3, 6) while recalculated weighted ratios are (0, 3, 3, 4). These define
different resampling distributions. Neither list alone establishes coverage. The source-specific
distinctions among one-sided and symmetric bounds also prevent copying a criticism or guar-
antee between packages merely because the helpers share a statistical name.(Yuta Saito and
Open Bandit Pipeline contributors, 2022; Haruka Kiyohara and SCOPE-RL contributors, 2023;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026ch)
  For banking data, customer clustering and shared calendar shocks additionally govern valid
splits and uncertainty. Shuffled rows can place the same customer’s history in training and
evaluation, or mix earlier and later information. A target-specific comparison should preserve
units and clocks, define whether training is external or refitted, and justify its dependence
assumptions. The reviewed software is useful for implementing selected calculations, not for
manufacturing these missing premises.

39.54.3    A shared data adapter must preserve money and endings

A single adapter that flattens histories and passes arrays to each package is insufficient.
SCOPE-RL’s inspected done mask includes the current transition, whereas a dataset may
attach the terminal reward to that same transition. The earlier (2, 8) reward example then
changes retained value from USD 10 to USD 2. d3rlpy distinguishes termination, truncation
and an unclosed tail, with different transition counts. POMDP options can consume multiple
primitive time steps and need a consistent convention for internal rewards and continuation
discounts. These are distinct contracts to test, not evidence that one package is globally
better.(Haruka Kiyohara and SCOPE-RL contributors, 2023; Causal banking proposal project,
2026ch; d3rlpy contributors, 2025a; Kaiyu Zheng and POMDP-Py contributors, 2025)
   Money also survives only if its transformation is preserved. Under an affine reward transform
r′ = ar + b, a cumulative value obeys
                                                         −1
                                                        TX
                                   V ′π = aV π + bE π         γt.
                                                        t=0

A one-step inverse is generally insufficient, particularly when the policy changes the horizon.
The previously derived two-period example converts a transformed value 3.7 back to USD 28
with the correct discounted shift, but only USD 23.50 with a one-step inverse. Clipping can
destroy invertibility altogether. Preserve original cash flows and declare the objective used
for learning separately from the monetary objective used for evaluation. (d3rlpy contributors,
2025c; Causal banking proposal, 2026au)
   The common CLI/MCP request can therefore bind the population, history and action
schemas, assignment mechanism, policy identity, observation and reward clocks, ending
conventions, monetary transformation and scientific target. Each worker then applies a
package-specific conversion with a reversible provenance record where reversibility is possible.
Its result should include accepted units, excluded and unresolved tails, failures and refusals,
support diagnostics, uncertainty scope and actual computational cost. A returned scalar
cannot substitute for this contract.


39.54.4    Reuse choices and the remaining search

The four prior decisions favor source-qualified references and conditional original workers, not
unconditional adoption. OBP and SCOPE-RL declare Apache 2.0 licenses in the inspected
roots; d3rlpy and POMDP-Py have inspected MIT declarations. Full dependency, data,
compiler and distribution obligations remain specific to the chosen artifacts. POMDP-Py’s
Cython components require native-binary and ABI custody; Python packaging alone does
not remove that duty. The existing conversion contracts explain why a wholesale cross-
language port would duplicate scientific, numerical and maintenance responsibilities without
an established benefit. Small independent oracles remain valuable because they can expose
semantic disagreement without inheriting the same implementation. (Yuta Saito and Open
Bandit Pipeline contributors, 2022; Haruka Kiyohara and SCOPE-RL contributors, 2023;
d3rlpy contributors, 2025b; Causal banking proposal, 2026at; Kaiyu Zheng and POMDP-Py
contributors, 2025)
   The next inexpensive comparison should use finite generated laws with known policy values
and public logged tasks whose provenance and rights are inspected. It should distinguish
genuine propensities from fitted or invented ones, supported from unsupported actions, greedy
from stochastic deployment, pre-terminal from post-terminal reward flags, and fixed-policy
from selected-policy uncertainty. Retain zero-match replay, impossible observations, nonfinite
922                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


inputs, timeouts and unresolved tails in the request denominator. Measure conversion, fitting,
search, evaluation, repair and review costs per scientifically accepted artifact, with correct
refusals separate. No such native comparison is claimed here.
   Coverage is still incomplete. The inherited cutoff-filtered bibliographic query returned ten
records from 2,527 reported matches, and is not an exhaustive software or alias census. Its
methodological leads need genuine originals before their technical results enter this proposal.
Broader continuous-action, distributional, slate and multiple-logger families, complete learning
delegates, and alternative implementations remain explicit follow-up. The justified contribution
of this comparison is a coherent selection and qualification route across four inspected families.
It does not close Python policy coverage, unrestricted hidden-state identification, calibrated
optimal-policy inference or bank adoption. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ec)


39.55      Java policy systems: planning, fitted control and the
           missing evaluation contract
A bank comparing Java policy tools must first decide whether its question is about a supplied
model, a policy learned from experience, or the value of an intervention in the population
represented by a logging process. The same customer-servicing action can occur in all three
problems, but the evidence supporting its value changes. Consider a loan account for which the
bank can wait, offer a restructuring or obtain additional information. The observed balance is
not automatically a Markov state: unrecorded affordability, previous contact, calendar shocks
and the timing of a consent response may matter. A simulator can accept a proposed state
and action without establishing that these are the variables on which the bank’s historical
assignment was conditionally unconfounded. This distinction governs the following comparison
of BURLAP, Chen’s Java reinforcement-learning library and an explicitly historical RL4J
artifact. It also explains why an off-policy learning label is insufficient for causal off-policy
evaluation.(BURLAP contributors, 2017; Chen Java reinforcement-learning contributors, 2017;
Eclipse Deeplearning4j contributors, 2022; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ef)


39.55.1     A bounded inventory with explicit historical identity

The inspected BURLAP repository revision is dated 27 November 2017. Its build declaration is
3.0.2-SNAPSHOT, whereas its README installation example names 3.0.1; these are distinct
declarations, not evidence of an installed artifact. The POM targets Java 1.7 and names
numerical and logging dependencies whose installed versions and transitive rights would need
a separate build qualification. Its direct license is Apache 2.0. The selected paths cover
supplied-model policy evaluation and iteration, least-squares policy iteration, tabular temporal-
difference learning, episode representation and a partially observed planning approximation.
These roles are materially broader than a single policy scorer, but breadth does not establish
inferential coverage.(BURLAP contributors, 2017)
   Chen’s repository revision is dated 16 December 2017. The POM declares 1.0.6 and Java
1.8; the README example uses 1.0.5. Its direct license is MIT. The inspected interfaces use
integer states and actions and mutable value tables; they include Q-learning, Sarsa and an
actor-update path. They are useful compact references for the arithmetic of learning, but none
of the selected update signatures supplies a causal logging law, an evaluation population or
a confidence construction. That statement concerns the inspected paths, not an exhaustive
absence claim about all Java software.(Chen Java reinforcement-learning contributors, 2017)
  RL4J requires a more careful identity boundary. A complete tree for the selected February

39.55.2     What a small Bellman residual actually establishes

Write a supplied finite discounted model as (S, A, P, r, γ), with 0 ≤ γ < 1. For a fixed
randomized policy π, its Bellman operator is
                                             (                                     )
                                                                      ′        ′
                                X                           X
                      π
                   (T v)(s) =        π(a | s) r(s, a) + γ        P (s | s, a)v(s ) .
                                 a                          s′

BURLAP’s selected evaluator discovers reachable states using the supplied full model and
updates their values using the fixed policy’s action probabilities. It stops after a configured
iteration limit or a sufficiently small observed change. Its reachability cache depends on state
identity and prior expansion. A changed transition model or meaning of state identifiers
therefore requires deliberate reset and re-enumeration. A changing customer population cannot
silently inherit an old graph of reachable states.(BURLAP contributors, 2017)
  Under the declared discounted finite model, the contraction inequality yields
                                                     ∥T π v − v∥∞
                                     ∥v − V π ∥∞ ≤                .

Indeed, add and subtract T π v in v − T π V π and move the term γ∥v − V π ∥∞ to the left.
This is a project derivation about a residual computed over the required state space. The
implementation’s in-place iteration change is not automatically that full residual, and reaching
an iteration cap does not prove either quantity small. More fundamentally, the bound concerns
the supplied P, r. In an authored one-state example, r = 1 USD and γ = 0.9 give v = 10
USD with zero nominal residual. If the true reward is 2 USD, the true value is 20 USD. Exact
solution of the declared equations leaves a 10 USD model error.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ef)
   State identity is part of this contract. The selected hashing factory defaults to object-
identifier independence and documents identifier-dependent treatment for relational domains.
Two records with equal displayed balances need not be equivalent when their links to a
household, guarantor or intervention history change feasible actions or transitions. The
adapter must justify the equivalence relation it uses; an ordinary hash collision and a deliberate
