40.7.4    An answer key is another measured object

Let Z be a benchmark’s recorded label, T the scientifically intended answer and Tb the system
output. For exact-match correctness,

                             1{Tb = T } − 1{Tb = Z} ≤ 1{T ̸= Z}.                           (40.6)

Whenever the label is correct, both correctness indicators are equal; otherwise their difference
is at most one. Taking expectations therefore bounds the difference between scientific accuracy
and label agreement by the answer-key error probability. If a defensible upper bound is ϵ,
reported agreement a implies only max(0, a − ϵ) ≤ P (Tb = T ) ≤ min(1, a + ϵ). This statement
assumes a meaningful common answer space; set-valued and ambiguous tasks require an
explicitly defined acceptance relation.
   With agreement .9 and a stipulated label error .1, truth accuracy can be .8 or 1 in two
simple 100-case constructions. Errors in the key can either conceal wrong outputs or penalize
correct ones. This is an exact example, not an allegation that any inspected benchmark has
a ten-percent error rate Causal banking proposal project (2026i). The practical lesson is to
audit the generator, label rule and edge cases before using a score as product evidence. An
incorrect IV-to-population-ATE oracle cannot be repaired by making an agent match that
oracle more reliably. Likewise, model-generated labels and model-generated answers can share
errors even when their agreement is high.
   For public observations without known causal truth, use the information that is actually
available: variable definitions, temporal admissibility, numerical reproduction, sensitivity to
assumptions and agreement with a justified design. Do not silently promote a published
observational point estimate into ground truth. For generated mechanisms, keep generator
truth outside the analysis interface and verify the reference calculation independently. An
intentional nonidentified case must accept appropriate refusal or a valid set, rather than reward
a precise but unjustified number.


40.7.5    Causal uncertainty matters through the decision

Return to a bank choosing an action a ∈ {0, 1}. Let V (a, M ) be its net value under causal
model M . When the evidence retains class M, one way to display the decision consequence is
regret
                         R(a, M ) = max V (b, M ) − V (a, M ).                        (40.7)
                                        b∈{0,1}

A model’s graph accuracy and its decision regret can order systems differently. An edge
irrelevant to the intervention query may contribute graph loss without changing the decision;
a single uncertain edge on the treatment-outcome path can reverse the preferred action. A
credible evaluation reports both the scientific object and the loss appropriate to the decision.
  The architecture chapter gives two Gaussian worlds with an identical observed distribution
but effects of 0 and1/2. Rescale the effect to dollars so that the two candidate gains from
acting are 0 and 500, and set action cost to 250. Not acting has value zero in both worlds.
Acting has value −250 or 250. Because the available information has the same law in both
worlds, any randomized rule acts with the same marginal probability p. Its expected regrets
are 250p and 250(1 − p), so

                               inf max{250p, 250(1 − p)} = 125.                            (40.8)
                             0≤p≤1

Equality holds at p = 1/2; either deterministic rule has worst regret 250. This restricted
two-world calculation illustrates the cost of unresolved information. It is not a recommendation
40.8. From a coherent answer to a defensible causal decision                                1081


to randomize real banking actions, and the world class and loss are authored. It explains why
a request for an informative experiment can be more valuable than another confident narrative
Causal banking proposal project (2026c,i).
   The next experiment should target information capable of distinguishing models with
different preferred actions. A public simulator can check that the proposed procedure chooses
such an experiment under known truth. Public observations can establish feasibility of a
data pipeline or stress an assumption. Neither proves that the same model class, costs or
experiment availability holds at a particular bank. Those transport questions belong to a later
study justified by the prototype’s findings.


40.7.6    A public-evidence portfolio with explicit transfer limits

An affordable portfolio follows the four banking journeys already developed. For funding,
public panel and macro records support data-clock, aggregation and reproducibility checks,
while declared generated laws supply causal truth for uncertainty tests. For servicing, a
controlled history/action generator tests positivity failures, feedback, policy definitions and
the effect of withheld state information. For discovery, known mechanisms should include
observationally equivalent graphs whose effects differ, so a confident single graph is not always
rewarded. For observation construction, public or generated documents can test extraction
and linkage while preserving the difference between a faithfully extracted assertion and a true
causal statement.
   Each journey should compare a deterministic reference, an established statistical route
and the proposed assistance where its role is relevant. Give all arms the same admissible
information and account separately for training labels, retrieval, tool use and human repair.
Freeze mechanisms, splits, budgets and scoring before final evaluation. A fixed held-out set
can be used for that registered comparison; repeated development against its answers creates
a new dependence and requires a new final evaluation design. An unavailable or malformed
answer remains in the assigned-request denominator.
   The interpretation should stay attached to the actual evidence. A document review can
justify an integration candidate. A local exact example can expose a failure mechanism. A
controlled prototype study can compare methods under its declared law. A live-model study
adds evidence about a particular model revision and task distribution. A bank study adds
evidence about the target process and its decision consequences. These are useful, different
claims; their separation allows the proposal to advance now without purchasing an expensive
experiment merely to satisfy a deployment gate.
   The current research frontier therefore supports a concrete proposal: build typed formulation
and evidence assistance around an auditable causal core; retain supervised, deterministic
and formal alternatives; measure composition and review costs; and direct new information
acquisition toward consequential ambiguity. It leaves open the reliability of language-mediated
assumptions, performance outside benchmark support, annotation validity and the economics
of sustained human review. Those are falsifiable next questions. A count of papers, agents or
completed reports does not answer them.


40.8      From a coherent answer to a defensible causal decision
Three recent systems clarify different meanings of assistance. A verifier can check whether
an answer follows from the reasoning presented to it; an orchestrator can choose and run a
sequence of causal tools; a literature agent can extract candidate relations and draw a diagram.
1082                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


These are valuable but different contributions. A bank considering a retention offer needs an
answer to a further question: under which assumptions would that offer change a specified
outcome for a specified population? We compare the mechanisms of Recursive Causal Audit,
OrcheCause and EpiCausalX against this decision, keeping reported demonstrations distinct
from a proposed banking implementation. (Chang, 2026; Yang et al., 2026a; Liu et al., 2026a)


40.8.1    Process consistency and the scientific oracle

Chang’s Recursive Causal Audit, or RCA, addresses a specific failure: a model can describe a
problem in one way and then emit a contradictory final label, particularly when challenged
by a user. Its judge has no gold labels. It checks the output schema, consistency among
fields, whether the conclusion follows from the structured reasoning, and whether a user
hint dominates contrary reasoning. Staged prompts demand more explicit variables, causal
sketches and assumptions when the earlier output fails. The paper explicitly recognizes that a
consistently incorrect argument can pass the judge. That limitation is part of the mechanism’s
definition, rather than an accidental omission that another formatting check can repair.(Chang,
2026)
  In a retention analysis, the agent might state that adviser discretion creates confounding
and then report the treated-minus-untreated retention difference as an identified offer effect. A
consistency judge could catch the conflict. It would not necessarily catch a different response
that consistently asserts random assignment throughout, when advisers actually selected
customers using unrecorded risk. The latter response needs evidence about the assignment
process. Agreement between a rationale and a number is a necessary internal check for a
well-formed report, but does not supply that evidence.
   The study uses a curated 454-vignette diagnostic suite and standardized pressure protocols.
Its limitations include subjective annotations, prompt dependence, black-box explanations
of model behavior and the absence of a component-level ablation of RCA. The historical
calls run through January 2026; they are not a ranking of models available at the time of
this proposal. There is also a specific unresolved denominator issue: the statistical-analysis
paragraph describes L1 with 50 cases per class and 100 overall, while Table 7 totals 50 L1, 304
L2 and 100 L3 cases. We therefore do not reconstruct a pooled confidence interval or repair
the denominator by assumption.(Chang, 2026)
   The answer-transition metric requires equally careful scope. In the paper’s Table 4, the L2
labels are binary, VALID and FLAWED. For a fixed gold label, changing an incorrect binary
answer necessarily corrects it. Let p denote initial accuracy, b the probability of becoming
wrong conditional on an initially correct answer, and c the probability of becoming correct
conditional on an initially wrong answer. Then

                                  pfinal = p(1 − b) + (1 − p)c.                                (40.9)

This is a partition by initial correctness, not a model of independence between the two answers.
Substitution for three selected rounded rows in Table 4 agrees with their reported final
accuracies to within 0.1 percentage point. It is therefore unwarranted to call this particular
binary table erroneous merely because a more general answer vocabulary exists elsewhere in
the paper.(Chang, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026bu)
   For a banking assistant that also permits an answer of not identified, a change from one
wrong answer to another wrong answer is possible. To see the difference, fix a task with true
label C and two wrong labels W1 , W2 . The following project-authored law specifies initial
probabilities π and transition matrix P , with rows indexed by the initial answer and columns
40.8. From a coherent answer to a defensible causal decision                                    1083


by the final answer:
                                                                          
                                                     9/10 1/20 1/20
                       π = (3/5, 1/5, 1/5),     P =  1/5 3/10 1/2  .                       (40.10)
                                                                  
                                                     1/10 3/5 3/10

All rows sum to one. Among initially wrong answers, the probability of any label change
is 7/10, whereas the probability of correction is only 3/20. The bad-flip probability is 1/10.
Equation 40.9 therefore gives final accuracy 3/5; incorrectly substituting the switch rate for
c would report 41/50. Direct multiplication gives πP = (3/5, 21/100, 19/100) and confirms
the first result. These are exact constructed probabilities, not measured model performance.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026bu)
   The practical implication is to preserve a full answer transition table, including refusal and
tool failure, with a fixed target-specific gold label. Whether refusal is correct depends on whether
the question is identified under the supplied assumptions. A pressure test should separately
expose unsupported endorsement, inappropriate rejection and appropriate withholding. Its
denominator must include the same assigned questions before and after review; deleting failed
or abstaining requests can change the apparent benefit.


40.8.2     Confounding is not a proof of a zero effect

A vignette in Chang’s appendix describes treatment given to more severely ill patients. It labels
the positive causal assertion NO and describes the association as spurious. The defensible
lesson is that the supplied association does not establish the asserted effect. Confounding
by itself does not establish that the treatment has no effect. A gold-label protocol must
distinguish an unjustified assertion from a false effect assertion. (Chang, 2026)
   Consider the following authored banking construction. Let A indicate a retention offer, Y
indicate retention over a fixed horizon, and U be an unrecorded customer characteristic. Draw
U as Bernoulli with probability 1/2. Independent exogenous uniform variables generate the
offer and outcome using the conditional probabilities

      Pr(A = 1 | U = u) = 14 + 12 u,      Pr(Y = 1 | U = u, A = a) = α + βu + τ a.           (40.11)

The outcome equation is retained under intervention; only the offer equation is replaced. All
conditional probabilities below lie strictly between zero and one, so the comparison does not
depend on deterministic treatment or an empty observed treatment stratum.(Causal banking
proposal, 2026bu)


                       World              α     β        τ E[Y (0)] E[Y (1)]
                       Positive effect 7/20 1/5 1/10            9/20    11/20
                       Zero effect     3/10 2/5    0             1/2      1/2
                       Negative effect 1/4 3/5 −1/10           11/20     9/20

  Each world has Pr(U = 1 | A = 1) = 3/4 and Pr(U = 1 | A = 0) = 1/4. Consequently the
observed conditional means are

         E[Y | A = 0] = α + β/4 = 2/5,         E[Y | A = 1] = α + 3β/4 + τ = 3/5             (40.12)

in all three worlds. The complete observed joint law of (A, Y ), not only its two means,
is identical: the cells (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1) have probabilities 3/10, 1/5, 1/5, 3/10. Under
1084                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


intervention, E[Y (a)] = α + β/2 + τ a, so the causal difference is τ . Thus the same positive
observed difference of 1/5 coexists with a positive, zero or negative effect. Independent finite
enumeration of the threshold construction reproduces both the observed and intervention laws.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026bu)
   For a stipulated USD 100 value per additional retained customer and USD 5 cost per offer,
incremental value is 100τ − 5: USD 5, minus USD 5 or minus USD 15 in the respective worlds.
These assumed amounts illustrate why an unjustified zero-effect conclusion and an unjustified
positive-effect conclusion can both mislead a decision. They are not estimates of bank prices or
returns. Even unlimited observations of (A, Y ) would leave these three worlds observationally
indistinguishable. The next investment must supply defensible restrictions or new information,
such as an appropriately designed public or synthetic randomized demonstration before
proposing an expensive bank trial.(Causal banking proposal, 2026bu)


40.8.3    Text constraints and the limits of graph-score tuning

OrcheCause offers a complementary mechanism: task orchestration across causal discovery,
structural causal modeling, root-cause analysis and causal-effect estimation. Its paper describes
causal-learn, DoWhy, pgmpy and causalml as underlying libraries. User text yields hard cause–
effect constraints, while external database text yields soft constraints. Preprocessing includes
imputation and removal of highly correlated features; hyperparameter search can use BIC
when a ground-truth graph is unavailable. (Yang et al., 2026a)
   This distinction between hard and soft text makes a concrete design choice visible. A hard
requirement A → Y excludes every graph without that edge. If the sentence actually describes
a historical association, a mediated effect, an intended policy or a different time scale, the true
explanation may already have been removed before a statistical test runs. A soft constraint
can permit disagreement with the data, but its weight is still a modeling choice; an LLM’s
linguistic confidence is not automatically a calibrated probability that the edge is true. In the
proposed bank interface, each relation therefore needs an explicit role: observed association,
mechanistic hypothesis, temporal prohibition, intervention definition or accepted scientific
restriction. The strength of a constraint must follow its accepted meaning and scope.
   The paper’s table also argues against a single undifferentiated improvement score. The
following are the reported PC demonstrations; HPO denotes hyperparameter optimization,
DK domain knowledge from the original dataset papers, and EK external knowledge. Lower
structural Hamming distance (SHD) and higher F1 are favorable under the paper’s respective
metrics. (Yang et al., 2026a)


               Dataset    Metric Baseline HPO DK+HPO DK+EK+HPO
               ALARM SHD                  13     13           10                10
                     F1                 .927   .927         .940              .940
               Sachs SHD                  21     23           14                10
                     F1                 .323   .343         .611              .688

   HPO alone makes Sachs SHD worse, from 21 to 23, while F1 improves. Thus the paper’s
general statement of progressive improvement is too broad if read as improvement of every
metric at every stage. Nor does knowledge drawn from the dataset’s own original paper simulate
a previously unknown bank mechanism. The demonstration supports the value of investigating
knowledge-assisted discovery; it does not estimate deployment accuracy, causal-effect coverage
or the incremental value of each component on new banking questions. Time-series analysis,
40.8. From a coherent answer to a defensible causal decision                                   1085


high-dimensional low-sample robustness and improved extraction from real documents are
future directions in this paper.(Yang et al., 2026a)
   Observed fit cannot by itself solve this last step. The three complete laws in Equation 40.12
give the same likelihood for every sample of the observed variables, while their intervention
values differ. No criterion computed solely from that observed distribution can select the
correct intervention value without additional restrictions. A graph score may guide a search
inside an assumed family; the product must still expose the family and its exclusions. Similarly,
removing a highly correlated variable needs a causal-role review: predictive redundancy does
not prove that an adjustment variable or measurement proxy can be discarded. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026bu)
   For a prototype, the useful adoption is the modular orchestration idea and the explicit
distinction between text sources. Reproducing the reported implementation requires a separate
pinned-code and dependency review. A first comparison would hold the dataset, target and
compute budget fixed, then compare no text, verified constraints, erroneous constraints and
contradictory documents. The outcome is not merely graph similarity: it includes whether the
effect is identified, whether a wrong constraint changes the decision, and whether the system
discloses the conflict.


40.8.4    Literature extraction, diagrams and query-relative roles

Liu and colleagues’ EpiCausalX preprint describes a literature-driven workflow with natural-
language initiation and diagram construction. Its methods extract relationship terms with
regular expressions and infer directions through heuristics informed by text and epidemiological
theory. The diagram tool checks acyclicity and uses topology to label exposures as nodes
without incoming edges and outcomes as nodes without outgoing edges. The reported usability
exercise includes 12 participants, split into two groups of 6, and an average task initiation
within two dialogue rounds. These are workflow observations; they are not measurements of
causal-effect accuracy or coverage.(Liu et al., 2026a)
   The topology rule illustrates an important boundary for business translation. In the graph
U → A, U → Y , A → Y , the offer A is still the exposure of interest despite having an incoming
edge. If retention Y subsequently affects account value V , then Y remains the outcome for
a retention question despite having an outgoing edge. Roles are relative to the query and
intervention, whereas root and sink status are graph properties. The authored worlds above
instantiate the first graph with explicit positive probabilities. A drawing tool can validate that
this representation is acyclic; it cannot thereby prove the absence of omitted common causes
or identify the effect from observed (A, Y ) alone. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bu)
   Literature extraction can nevertheless lower the cost of preparing a review. A useful output
is a candidate relation with its original passage, population, time ordering, measurement
definition and study design. An observational association should remain an association until
the proposed causal argument and its assumptions have been checked. Negation, hypothetical
wording, direction reversal, selection and population mismatch deserve explicit adversarial
examples. The agent can propose a diagram and alternatives, then pass a well-specified query
to a separately reviewed identification routine. The diagram is an argument to inspect.
   The preprint itself places systematic expert review, real-world validation, larger user studies
and comparisons with manual work in its future program. It also describes open-source release
as a future step after initial validation. Its displayed rights notice and the absence of a reviewed
software release prevent a direct-adoption decision here. The appropriate proposal is to assess
the documented workflow and develop independent query-typing tests; the paper’s usability
result does not justify porting an uninspected implementation or claiming current software
1086                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


availability. (Liu et al., 2026a)


40.8.5    A public-evidence prototype that distinguishes these contributions

The three mechanisms lead to a staged, falsifiable prototype. Its first component is a collection
of stipulated causal worlds and business questions, including the equal-observation example,
query-relative variable roles, binary and three-label review tasks, and deliberately false textual
constraints. These fixtures have known answers because their laws are specified. A second
component uses public datasets and documented assumptions to test tool invocation, prove-
nance and the treatment of missing identification information. Public observational data need
not have known effects: the expected response may be an identified set, sensitivity analysis or
an explicit inability to decide.
   The comparison separates the three interventions. Adding a consistency judge tests whether
contradictory conclusions decrease at a declared review cost. Adding text constraints tests
whether correct information helps and wrong information is exposed. Adding literature
extraction tests whether supported relations, populations and temporal definitions are preserved.
Requests, failed calls, refusals, changed assumptions and review time must remain in the
evaluation record. For generated mechanisms, replicate mechanisms rather than treating
repeated prompts about the same mechanism as independent scientific evidence. Predeclared
tolerances and held-out problem families would be needed before estimating an improvement.
   The resulting investment case would establish whether these separate contributions merit a
larger experiment. It would preserve the distinction between coherent reasoning, a diagram, a
successful tool call, a better graph score and a justified banking decision. The attainable next
step is a narrowly specified prototype with known failures and honest uncertainty, followed by
bank-specific validation if that evidence warrants the cost.
Chapter 41

Translating a banking decision into a
causal question

41.1      A business sentence can contain several questions
“Should we increase the deposit offer?” sounds like a single question, but it leaves several
choices unresolved. The intended action could be a change in the quoted rate, the eligibility
rule, the message shown to a customer or the allocation of a fixed promotional budget. The
outcome could be a new deposit, retained balances, funding cost or total relationship value.
The population could be existing customers, applicants who received an offer or everyone
eligible under a proposed rule. Each choice defines a different causal problem.
   A language assistant can expose these alternatives and organize the evidence needed to
resolve them. It should not choose the easiest target to estimate and silently treat that target
as the owner’s decision. In the project funding case, the response of balances to a 25-basis-point
increase and the change in net funding cost over thirty days are retained as separate candidates.
Their business motivation is shared; their outcomes and decision consequences are not identical.
The unresolved choice is useful information, not a failure that must be hidden by returning a
number.
   The co-pilot roadmap discussed by Alaa and colleagues motivates this progression from a
scientific question through assumptions, statistical targets and interpretation. Their illustrative
medical examples attend to eligibility, baseline time, treatment and follow-up. The inspected
paper also reports that generic uncued answers can omit relevant design concerns. Applying
those principles to banking is a project proposal; the medical examples do not validate banking
clocks or interventions.Alaa et al. (2024)


41.2      A question as a collection of commitments
The project represents a question as

                                Q = (U, P, A, π, π0 , Y, H, ν, ℓ, I).                        (41.1)

Here U is the unit of analysis; P is the target population; A is the feasible action set; π and
π0 are the policy and comparator; Y is the outcome; H is the horizon; ν is the measure used
to average over the population; ℓ is the loss, including its units; and I specifies information
available at each action. This notation defines the project’s declaration contract. It is not an
identification theorem.

                                               1087
1088                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The unit needs particular care. An account can be an observation while a customer is the
decision unit and a household is the unit within which actions interact. An assistant can ask
which role each identifier plays, but a column called customer ID does not certify ownership or
stable linkage. If several accounts share a budget or pricing rule, an account-level action may
also be an infeasible description of the intervention. The feasible action set should reflect what
the responsible institution can actually change.
   The comparator must be as explicit as the intervention. “No treatment” might mean no
new contact, continuation of the current contact policy, no rate increase, or a different offer
under a fixed budget. A dynamic policy can include future actions conditional on history, so
its comparator is also a history-dependent rule. An effect relative to one comparator cannot
be reused for another solely because the same treatment variable appears in the dataset.
  The outcome and loss should also remain separate. A change in balances has units of
currency held over a horizon; funding expense combines balances, rates and time. A larger
deposit balance can have a positive acquisition interpretation and an unfavorable net-cost
implication. If g(a) is a specified gross benefit and c(a) is a specified cost, the decision may
depend on E[g(a) − c(a)], not on E[g(a)] alone. The definitions and valuation assumptions
must be supplied before that subtraction is meaningful. The assistant should make missing
costs visible rather than invent prices.


41.3      Changing a population measure changes the answer
Let X denote baseline features and let τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x]. A weighted target can
be written
                                 E[w(X)τ (X)]
                           θw =                ,     E[w(X)] > 0.                       (41.2)
                                   E[w(X)]
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different weights. Under the
conditions that make a propensity e(x) = Pr(A = 1 | X = x) appropriate for the intended
population, familiar choices are 1, e(x), e(x)(1 − e(x)) and 1{a ≤ e(x) ≤ b}, respectively.
The formula records which average is wanted. It does not establish exchangeability, support,
estimation rates or coverage.
  An exact project example makes the distinction visible. Let two strata have equal population
probability, with propensities 0.2 and 0.5, and effects 0 and 10. Trimming to [0.1, 0.9] keeps
both strata, so the trimmed-population effect is 5. Overlap weights are 0.16 and 0.25, giving
                                   0.16(0) + 0.25(10)   250
                      θoverlap =                      =     = 6.09756 . . . .
                                       0.16 + 0.25      41
Both calculations can be exact and still answer different questions. A label such as “overlap
population” is insufficient if its underlying weighting rule is not retained.
   This issue is directly relevant to the inspected OCI agent paper. Chou and colleagues
describe a principal/actor/critic workflow, reproducible notebooks, point-in-time estimation
and overlap diagnostics. The inspected trimming passage uses a target label that must be
reconciled with the actual weighting rule before mapping it to conventional overlap weighting.
The proposed architecture is informative, but an assistant should not inherit a target label
without checking its definition.Chou et al. (2026)
   Changing the target to remove unsupported accounts can be scientifically reasonable, but it
is a new decision question. A bank owner may care about precisely those accounts for which
treatment support is weak. An honest report can say that a narrower target is estimable under
the supplied assumptions while the original target remains unresolved. It should show the
excluded population, the new averaging rule and the implications for the decision.
41.4. Information is governed by an availability clock                                      1089


41.4      Information is governed by an availability clock
The date on which an event occurred differs from the date on which an analyst or policy could
observe it. For a recorded variable V , write eV for event time and aV for availability time.
The finite project fixtures require eV ≤ aV , and a policy acting at time t can use the value
only if aV ≤ t. A derived feature becomes available no earlier than its required inputs. These
rules prevent an apparently historical feature from leaking future information into a decision.
   In the servicing fixture, an account condition occurs at day ten but becomes available
at day eleven. A rule acting on day eleven may use it; a rule acting on day ten may not.
The distinction matters even when both values later appear in the same warehouse table. A
language assistant should request the recording and availability convention, rather than infer
it from a field name or a sorted timestamp.
   Advance announcements and forecasts require different variable definitions. A forecast
observed today of next month’s condition is a current forecast variable, not a measurement of a
future realized condition with an impossible availability time. Revised historical data similarly
require a vintage or revision convention. The project’s finite validator does not implement
every revision protocol. It checks the stated recorded-value contract and leaves more complex
clocks as explicit extensions.
  Equal timestamps do not determine direction. Two columns aggregated to the same day
may hide a finer action sequence or a common cause. The assistant can propose a finer clock
and identify the evidence needed to support it. It cannot establish temporal precedence by
placing one variable first in a diagram. When the granularity is insufficient, the ambiguity
should survive into the model class.


41.5      An available covariate is not automatically an adjustment
          variable
In a sequential servicing model, A0 changes an intermediate condition L1 , which affects both
a later action A1 and the outcome Y . The same L1 is a mediator for the first action and a
common cause of the second action–outcome relation. Its appropriate use depends on the
target. Including every available column in one regression does not preserve all possible total,
direct and policy effects.
   The project declaration therefore distinguishes a policy-history purpose from an ordinary
adjustment purpose. A simple directed-path diagnostic flags a post-treatment descendant
proposed as an ordinary total-effect control. It does not declare all post-treatment conditioning
invalid. Controlled direct effects and longitudinal procedures need their own question and
formal analysis. A warning from a declaration validator is not a replacement for an adjustment
criterion or an identification algorithm.
   Observation processes can alter the target in a similar way. Suppose only successfully
linked records enter an analysis and both action and repayment affect successful linkage. The
selection indicator is part of the causal problem, and an effect among linked records may differ
from an effect in the original population. A record-link score is an observed proxy; it is not
verified ownership. The observation fixture deliberately retains a latent ownership variable, a
selection node and an unresolved population choice.
  CausalDS provides a useful literature distinction here: its conceptual SCM variables and its
separate observation model are not interchangeable. The paper’s narrated synthetic scenes
can test how an agent handles that distinction, but they do not supply authentic banking
1090                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


semantic or assignment truth.Leban and Sun (2026)


41.6     The handoff to formal analysis
The assistant’s useful output is a reviewable declaration and a record of what remains unresolved.
A selected declaration contains one explicit target, its population measure, the intervention
and comparator, clocks, feasible actions, outcome and loss. An ambiguous declaration retains
candidate targets without covertly selecting one. A contradicted assumption cannot be left as
an inconsequential note while the calculation proceeds as if it held.
  The local project validator exercises these distinctions with four synthetic banking cases and
adverse contract tests. It checks declared identities, types, references and selected clock/graph
conditions. It does not authenticate an institution, certify a reviewer, determine whether a
causal assumption is true, or implement every MAG/PAG/CPDAG validity condition. A
declaration ready for formal analysis is ready for the next conditional operation, not a qualified
bank recommendation.
   This boundary also explains the limited scope of the current executable prototype. A
declaration can describe a dynamic regime while the selected operation supports only a
static binary population ATE. The correct handoff then reports unsupported target mapping.
Translating that request into a static regression would produce a result at the cost of changing
the user’s question. The appropriate remedy is to qualify a longitudinal operation or obtain
an explicit new target decision, with the original question preserved.


41.7     A complete translation example: the incentive question
Suppose a manager asks an agent to “find the incentive uplift and choose the best offer.” The
sentence leaves at least three mathematical objects open: a binary offer effect, a continuous
local slope, and a finite-dose policy value. The agent can help by presenting these alternatives
with their populations, units and action constraints. It should not select whichever object
happens to be exposed by the first available package.
   Let A be incentive intensity in a declared unit and let Y be retained net value over a fixed
horizon. The finite question is ∆(a1 , a0 ) = E{Y (a1 ) − Y (a0 )}. A local derivative, where
it exists, is µ′ (a). A covariance slope averages features of the response under an exposure
distribution and need not equal either object. The inspected grf and dose-response interfaces
make this a practical interoperability issue, not merely a linguistic distinction.grf project
(2026b); causaldrf project (2026b)
   For the stipulated curve µ(a) = 20a − 3a2 , a uniform exposure on [0, 2] gives covariance
slope 14, while moving from dose one to dose two changes the mean by 11 CNY. An agent
that labels 14 as the value of the specified change has mistranslated the problem even if it
calls its numerical tool correctly. The exact project calculation makes the error detectable
without a live model experiment.Causal banking research project (2026bk)
   A useful translation record would therefore state: eligible existing customers; the information
available before the offer; current dose one and feasible dose two; a fixed retention horizon;
treatment and outcome currency units; and whether incentive expense is already included
in Y . If expense is excluded, the decision value is ∆(a1 , a0 ) − {c(a1 ) − c(a0 )}. Subtracting
it again when Y already measures net value would double-count cost. The record also needs
account closure/default definitions and a sampling unit for uncertainty.
  The agent’s role can be useful at each handoff. It can flag unspecified units, find source
41.8. A servicing policy is a rule with an information boundary                               1091


definitions, propose alternative causal questions and generate typed requests. Formal checks
can verify that a numerical result matches the declared query. Domain owners must still
confirm the feasible intervention and measurement meanings; neither fluent prose nor a schema
establishes them.


41.8      A servicing policy is a rule with an information boundary
For sequential servicing, an action rule uses Ht , the information actually available at decision
time. A data field recorded later may describe an earlier event while remaining unavailable
to the operating policy. An agent assembling history features must preserve both event and
availability times. Otherwise the proposed policy uses information the bank would not possess
when acting.
   The causal query should distinguish evaluating a specified rule, choosing among rules and
claiming an optimal hidden-state policy. A longitudinal simulator can evaluate supplied regimes
under its assumptions. Its ability to accept a custom history function does not identify private
customer states or make an unknown logger known. The inspected pygformula class exposes
useful histories, event and regime options, but its source interface alone establishes neither
policy optimality nor uncertainty under arbitrary dependence.pygformula project (2026b)
   A concrete policy-selection hazard can be shown without an asymptotic argument. Suppose
two equally valuable policies each have independent evaluation error equal to minus one or
plus one with equal probability. The maximum of the two errors is minus one only when both
are minus one, and plus one otherwise. Its expectation is therefore 34 − 41 = 12 . Reporting the
selected policy’s same-data evaluation is optimistic. If the selected policy is evaluated with a
fresh independent error of mean zero, the evaluation error has mean zero conditional on the
selection. Exact enumeration verifies both claims.Causal banking research project (2026bk)
   This example does not prove that a particular split is sufficient for a dependent servicing
panel. It explains why the selection and evaluation laws must be specified. An agent can
preserve the split, freeze candidate rules and refuse reuse of a held-out set for tuning. A
scientific argument must still justify independence or the required dependence control. Training
a policy and then narrating its favorable development score is not an independent evaluation.


41.9      Translation outputs that deserve abstention
Some business questions should produce a request for more information or a set of alternatives.
If “the customer” may mean the legal entity, the beneficial owner or a linked household,
choosing one silently changes both the population and interference structure. If the intended
action is not operationally feasible, the mathematically optimal action is irrelevant. If the loss
function and costs are unknown, the agent can compare statistical targets but cannot assert
an investment recommendation.
   Abstention should be specific. It should identify the missing definition, record the alternative
interpretations and explain which downstream operation depends on the answer. That is
different from a generic refusal to analyze. For an incentive query, the missing item may be
treatment units or whether cost is already included. For servicing it may be the information
clock or the policy class. For interference it may be network direction or the allocation
policy. These are concrete commitments that owners can resolve and numerical tools can then
preserve.
1092                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


41.10      From a literature graph to a testable banking hypothesis
A bank translating a business question into a causal analysis needs more than a plausible arrow.
Suppose a servicing team asks whether a digital reminder reduces missed payments among
customers whose income has become irregular. Literature can suggest mechanisms involving
attention, financial stress, access and payment timing. A useful assistant should expose those
possibilities and their sources, then help specify an intervention, eligible population, outcome
horizon and decision clock. It should not quietly turn a sentence about association into an
identified effect of sending a reminder. Tong and colleagues provide a concrete design for using
language models and a literature graph to generate research hypotheses. Their psychological
setting is informative about the design of that assistance, while supplying no validation of the
banking intervention.(Tong et al., 2024)


41.10.1     What the literature graph represents

The inspected July 2024 article describes three stages: retrieve literature, extract relation pairs
and generate hypotheses from predicted links. From a wider psychological and neuroscience
collection, the authors select 43,312 articles using a journal-title criterion; 35,797 come from
Frontiers in Psychology. That concentration is a property of the selected evidence, not a
census of psychological knowledge. PDF cleaning and chunks of at most 4,000 tokens precede
GPT-4 extraction. The prompt explicitly requests both causal and correlational relations, their
concepts, and the sign of causal relations. Model filtering and periodic expert feedback follow.
The resulting graph is reported to contain about 197,000 concepts and 235,000 connections.
Neo4j supplies storage; node2vec embeddings and neighbor Jaccard similarity guide candidate-
link selection. GPT-4 then turns selected concept pairs into hypotheses. These are the authors’
reported components and counts, not a reproduced implementation.(Tong et al., 2024)
   A bank-facing evidence object should retain more information than the concept pair. Let q
identify a source claim, dq its document and version, sq the inspected passage, rq its asserted
relation type, and cq its population, timing and study-design context. A useful proposed
representation is

                      eq = (dq , sq , rq , cq , extraction status, review status).              (41.3)

The claim graph constructed from these objects need not be an acyclic structural causal
model. Different studies can use different populations, variable definitions and time resolutions;
an article can report a causal interpretation whose identifying assumptions remain disputed.
Deduplication must preserve disagreement and source independence. A collection of paraphrases
of one study cannot acquire the status of several replications. Model confidence and an expert’s
agreement that the text contains a claim are also different quantities from evidence that the
claim is true in the proposed bank population.
   The paper’s extraction check makes this distinction measurable. Among 238 pairs classified
as causal by GPT-4, the main article reports 156 agreed causal labels and 31 pairs not
recognized as relationships. The complementary 51 therefore have a different recognized
relation label under that classification. Consequently,
                    156                    207                     31
                        ≃ 65.55%,              ≃ 86.97%,              ≃ 13.03%.                 (41.4)
                    238                    238                    238
The small rounding differences from the article’s displayed percentages do not change the
substantive point: relation-existence agreement is a different endpoint from causal-label
agreement. Neither denominator measures an intervention’s ground-truth effect. The authors’
41.10. From a literature graph to a testable banking hypothesis                           1093


familiar-paper evaluation and feedback process supplies useful exploratory evidence; it does
not establish performance on previously unseen banking mechanisms.(Tong et al., 2024; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026ap)


41.10.2     Why a predicted link remains a hypothesis

For neighbor sets N (a) and N (b), the usual Jaccard score is
                                                |N (a) ∩ N (b)|
                                    J(a, b) =                   .                       (41.5)
                                                |N (a) ∪ N (b)|
This expresses shared graph context under a chosen neighbor convention. A denominator
of zero needs an explicit implementation policy. Direction, edge types, duplicate claims and
temporal aggregation also affect what a neighborhood means. A score in [0, 1] is not thereby a
probability of causation, a confidence level or an effect magnitude.
   An authored counterexample illustrates the missing implication. Take mutually independent
zero-mean Z, εA , εB , εP and the structural equations

                     A = Z + εA ,       B = Z + εB ,         P = A + B + εP .           (41.6)

The DAG has Z → A, Z → B, A → P and B → P . Using undirected adjacency neighborhoods,
N (A) = N (B) = {Z, P }, so J(A, B) = 1. Yet intervening on A changes neither Z nor the
equation for B: the derivative of E[B | do(A = a)] with respect to a is zero. Shared cause
and shared consequence create identical neighborhoods without a direct or total effect of A on
B. This is a statement about the displayed construction; the uninspected package’s neighbor
convention is not assumed.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ap)
   For a banking interpretation, let A encode a reminder policy, B a repayment response, and
Z a common predisposition in a hypothetical observational population. If a planner wrongly
treats similarity one as a success probability for an intervention worth USD 100 at cost USD
20, the apparent margin is USD 80. Under the stipulated zero-effect law, the incremental
margin is USD -20. No bank profit or package failure is measured here. The construction
shows why a candidate generator must return a proposed relation with its evidence, while a
subsequent identification step supplies any admissible causal effect or refusal.


41.10.3     What the reported evaluation can establish

The authors focus on well-being and generate 130 hypotheses. The principal comparison uses 30
randomly selected model-and-graph hypotheses, 30 expert-selected hypotheses, 30 hypotheses
sampled from 41 ideas supplied by 13 responding doctoral students, and 30 Claude-2 hypotheses
selected by GPT-4 from 50 generated ideas. Three experts rate novelty and usefulness, with
hypotheses presented in randomized order. These pipelines differ in generation and selection.
The comparison therefore concerns the resulting pipelines and selected ideas, rather than
isolating one graph component under identical resources. Reported reviewer correlations vary,
including a novelty correlation of 0.069 for one reviewer pair; an average rating cannot erase
that disagreement.(Tong et al., 2024)
   The paper reports higher novelty for its randomly selected graph-assisted ideas than for
the Claude comparison. The expert-selected arm is not uniformly significant: Table 5 gives
mean-comparison p = 0.085 and median-comparison p = 0.550 against Claude. A later
60-versus-60 GPT-4 ablation reports a novelty advantage but a usefulness comparison of
p = 0.1937. Nonsignificance does not prove equal usefulness, nor does an insignificant human-
versus-model comparison establish equivalence to experts without a justified equivalence margin
1094                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


and suitable design. These endpoints are judgments of ideas; the proposed mechanisms were
not validated by the reported rating experiment. BERT representations and t-SNE plots
describe semantic structure and require their own interpretation. They do not replace an
intervention experiment.(Tong et al., 2024)
  Several printed numerical statements also require reconciliation before the proposal inherits
their inferential force. The usefulness paragraph pairs F (3, 116) = 5.25 with p = 0.553.
Independent evaluation of the ordinary F upper tail gives approximately 0.001967. In the
semantic-distance analysis, the printed F (3, 1652) = 84.1611 is paired with explained variance
86.96%. Under ordinary one-factor ANOVA with the printed degrees of freedom,

                                d1 F        3(84.1611)
                      R2 =             =                   ≃ 0.132573.                    (41.7)
                             d1 F + d2   3(84.1611) + 1652

These are arithmetic checks conditional on the stated conventional model, not a reconstruction
of unavailable raw ratings. The correct repair is to obtain the analysis and resolve which
printed quantities or definitions need correction. The prose also varies from its table for a
human-comparison t value and calls a median comparison significant where the table gives
p = 0.550. Hypotheses contributed by the same person, repeated ratings and distances
sharing the same hypothesis create dependence questions; their inferential treatment cannot be
recovered from a significance label alone.(Tong et al., 2024; Causal banking proposal project,
2026ap)


41.10.4    A public evaluation before a bank prototype trial

The proposed library can adopt the separation of literature extraction, graph-assisted candidate
generation and expert evaluation as a design hypothesis. Direct code adoption remains
premature: the selected article does not itself qualify immutable implementation identities,
exact model snapshots, full prompts and thresholds, dependency licenses, or complete corpus
redistribution rights. Its data statement makes only part of the evidence available with
supplementary material and offers additional data on request. The earlier preprint’s appendices
are a different version and cannot silently substitute for the revised supplement. The article’s
own limitations acknowledge extraction error, synonymous concepts, a restricted hypothesis
sample and a shift in scarce expert work from generation to evaluation.(Tong et al., 2024)
   A first public experiment should freeze a licensed corpus and evaluate four linked but
separate questions. Can extraction recover source-supported claims, relation type, direction,
sign and uncertainty on held-out documents? Can an assistant translate a business description
into an operational population, intervention and outcome without inventing assignment or ob-
servability? Does graph-assisted generation improve blind ratings of useful, testable hypotheses
relative to retrieval-only, language-model-only and human-assisted baselines under matched
budgets? Finally, do proposals survive identification and intervention checks in generated
banking mechanisms with known truth and in suitable publicly documented experiments?
Novelty and semantic diversity remain secondary to correctness and decision loss when an
action is proposed.
   Document families, shared studies and generated mechanism families should be separated
across development and evaluation to reduce leakage. The public protocol should retain contra-
dicted claims, extraction failures, unavailable answers and refusal. Human evaluation needs a
declared sampling unit, a predeclared treatment of reviewer disagreement and dependence, and
a held-out adjudication process. Actual calls, retries, tokens, expert minutes and component
compute should be recorded. The comparison should price the full review workflow rather
than assume that automatic hypothesis production removes expert work.
41.11. A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alternatives                         1095


   Across library, CLI and MCP, the proposed output should distinguish extracted_claim,
hypothesis, reviewed_assumption and identified_query. It should carry immutable
source anchors, event-time definitions, unresolved conflicts and the checks still required
for promotion. A client requesting an effect must not receive a link score under an effect field.
These contracts are a concrete route to a useful public prototype; qualification of a banking
intervention still requires evidence about that intervention.


41.11      A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alter-
           natives
A language model can make a business question more precise by exposing the decisions that its
wording leaves open. Its useful output is a set of explicit candidate questions, with evidence
for their variables and clocks, followed by a reasoned choice of a supported analysis. Fluency
alone does not determine which candidate the bank intended. A formal causal engine also
cannot repair a mistake that was made before the graph, intervention and target reached the
engine.
   Consider a manager who asks, “Which customers should receive a retention invitation next
month, and how much value will it create?” One interpretation is the effect of offering the
invitation to every currently eligible customer. Another is the effect among customers who
historically received it. A third is the value of a targeting rule under a fixed contact budget.
The first two are averages over different populations. The third also requires a feasible policy
class, the information available when the rule acts, a comparator policy and a cost definition.
A model that estimates historical recipients’ average effect and calls it the expected value of
the new targeting rule has changed the question.
   The formulation record should therefore contain the eligible population and exclusions,
the sampling unit, invitation and comparator, actual receipt if distinct, the decision time,
permissible information, outcome horizon, monetary units and accounting treatment of contact
cost. It should distinguish invitation from successful contact and from subsequent product use.
Those variables may be causally related, but they are different interventions. It should also
retain alternatives that remain unresolved: all eligible customers versus historical recipients, a
single action versus a sequence, and gross revenue versus net value.
  For a binary invitation A, a baseline record W available at time zero, and a fixed-horizon
outcome Y , an initial target may be

                                     ψ = Eν {Y (1) − Y (0)},

  where ν names the eligible population. The adjustment expression
                  Z
             ψ=       {m1 (w) − m0 (w)} dν(w),      ma (w) = E[Y | A = a, W = w],

   requires consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, suitable sampling and the
declared interference restriction. The model may help elicit and document those assumptions.
It cannot infer their truth from a plausible explanation or from a successful estimator call. In a
generated development example, the project can stipulate and inspect the complete assignment
law. In a later bank application, the assignment mechanism and measurement meanings need
accountable scientific ownership.

41.11.1     What the frontier evidence supports

The knowledge-assisted perspective of Kıcıman and colleagues motivates graph drafts, critique
and connections to formal tools. Its own memorization probes and discussion of novel scenarios
limit what benchmark success establishes. The inspected original distinguishes knowledge-
based graph generation from conventional discovery from observations. For this proposal, a
directional suggestion is a hypothesis with source provenance, not a discovered bank fact. A
model can suggest that financial distress confounds retention contact and subsequent deposits;
the analysis still needs to determine what was measured, when staff observed it and how it
affected assignment. (Kıcıman et al., 2023)
   The medical co-pilot proposal develops a causal roadmap from a scientific question through
study design and interpretation. Its examples of prevalent versus incident users are directly
relevant to the distinction between existing account holders and newly eligible customers. That
transfer is a project design proposal, not evidence that a medical demonstration validates
banking workflows. The paper’s evaluation discussion also makes clear that medical question-
answering ability and causal study-design quality are different evaluation targets. Carefully
cued illustrative responses do not establish reliable autonomous formulation. (Alaa et al.,
2024)
  CLadder provides formally generated causal questions and explicitly separates levels of
causal reasoning. Its results and limitations support using a formal reference to evaluate
whether verbalized information was translated into the right query. Binary answer accuracy
on its selected query families does not measure effect calibration, correct bank populations or
decision loss. The paper also identifies the language-to-formal-tool interface as a remaining
problem. The proposed baseline therefore checks the structured query before it scores a
numerical answer. (Jin et al., 2023)
   The 2026 CausalDS paper adds narrated synthetic structural models, data files, an observa-
tion layer and separate private scoring information. It distinguishes the conceptual variables
used for identification from their noisy observed proxies. Its reported results separate symbolic
reasoning, estimation, interval quality, abstention and tool cost. This is useful evidence for a
multidimensional evaluation: correctly extracting a story’s graph does not guarantee that the
observed data identify or precisely estimate the stated effect. The paper’s historical model
results are author-reported; they have not been reproduced in this project. (Leban and Sun,
2026)
   The 2026 observational causal-inference agent paper provides a concrete principal, actor and
critic workflow built around deterministic analysis tools and reproducible notebooks. It reports
favorable comparisons under its evaluated settings, while its disguised observational-study
examples retain important overlap-related refusals. This supports investigating constrained
analytical workflows with explicit diagnostics. It does not establish unmeasured-confounding
control, longitudinal-policy identification or valid conditional coverage after the critic selects
which estimates to report. Its point-in-time scope must survive transfer to the banking proposal.
(Chou et al., 2026)
   Two additional primary studies sharpen the boundary between an effective workflow and
causal truth. Sng and colleagues study inconsistencies in causal-edge ratings and compare
retrieval augmentation with a debate-and-arbiter design. Their retrieval experiment supplies a
mocked true causal graph. The authors explicitly state that reduced inconsistency does not
imply accurate causal prediction and call for true-graph validation. The title’s language about
eliminating hallucinations should therefore not become a guarantee in this product proposal.
Consistent agents can agree on an incorrect edge, and a retrieval corpus can encode the same
incorrect premise. (Sng et al., 2024)
41.11. A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alternatives                         1097


   CausalPulse describes query planning, semantic descriptions, process constraints, agent cards
and MCP/A2A coordination for manufacturing diagnostics. Its reported operational success is
a useful architecture comparison. The paper separately reports root-cause attribution, with a
PSE Hits@1 of 0.44 and F1 of 0.39, using annotations of variables that changed at the anomaly
time. Such annotations and tool-invocation success are different from interventional causal
truth. The paper’s local timing setup and manufacturing deployment discussion likewise do
not establish banking runtime or treatment-effect performance. We can adapt its separation
of semantic services, deterministic tools and workflow state as a design pattern while retaining
those scientific limits. (Shyalika et al., 2026)
   These studies suggest complementary roles: retrieve definitions, draft alternatives, check
logical consistency, construct typed calls, retain execution artifacts and explain formal results.
The adverse findings point to the same missing link: a linguistic interpretation must be checked
against the intended population, intervention, measurement model and information clock.
An additional critic can help find mistakes, but agreement between related models is not
independent validation of an assumption.


41.11.2     A worked failure: an overlap remedy changes the population

Suppose the bank initially asks for the average invitation effect among all eligible customers.
A diagnostic finds weak overlap for one customer stratum. An agent proposes trimming that
stratum and continues to report the result as if it answered the original question. Even with
perfect estimation, that continuation can be wrong.
   To isolate the target issue, stipulate a three-stratum population with known masses, propen-
sities and conditional effects. These are generated numerical assumptions; the units of the
conditional effect are thousands of currency units per customer.

               Population mass p(w), invitation propensity
 Stratum w     e(w)                                        Conditional effect τ (w)
0              0.5, 0.05                                         0
1              0.3, 0.50                                         2
2              0.2, 0.80                                         8


   The full-population ATE is 0.5(0) + 0.3(2) + 0.2(8) = 2.2. Trimming to true propensities in
[0.1, 0.9] retains half the population and gives 2.2/0.5 = 4.4. The conventional overlap-weighted
target instead uses the measure proportional to p(w)e(w){1 − e(w)}:

                           w p(w)e(w){1 − e(w)}τ (w)
                      P
                                                            0.406    1624
              ψOW =                                    =           =      ≃ 3.1052.
                             w p(w)e(w){1 − e(w)}
                           P
                                                           0.13075    523

   The effect among treated customers is different again: ψATT = 316/67 ≃ 4.7164. Exact
rational calculations reproduce all four values. None is an empirical estimate from a package
or a live language model. Their disagreement arises entirely from the population measure.
(Causal banking research project, 2026h)
  This distinction is visible in a real proposed reuse path. The inspected oci-agent notebook
applies a propensity-based keep mask and averages AIPW pseudo-outcomes over that subset
while labeling the output “ATO.” The accompanying paper describes the trimming remedy in
the same terminology. A hard-trimmed average and an e(W ){1−e(W )}-weighted overlap effect
are not generally equal. The integration must either label the result as a trimmed-population
ATE, with its actual eligibility rule, or implement and validate the intended weighting operation.
1098                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


It must also retain the original all-eligible request and the excluded population. Estimated
propensities add randomness to selection; the simple known-law calculation above does not
validate that further inference step. (oci-agent contributors, 2026; Chou et al., 2026)
   The correct translation response is therefore a revised analysis proposal: the original target
is unresolved under the current information or diagnostics; a specified restricted-population
target may be feasible; and the bank must assess whether that restricted target still informs its
decision. In a public or generated prototype, this branch can be evaluated without bank data
by stipulating both populations and checking that the system preserves their difference. It is
not necessary to obtain expensive authentic evidence merely to detect a target substitution.


41.11.3    Concrete package choices and the formal baseline

The inspected pywhy-llm path is a candidate for eliciting hypotheses and candidate variables. Its
IdentificationSuggester.suggest_backdoor delegates to a language-model confounder sug-
gester. That class’s front-door method is a stub, whereas SimpleIdentificationSuggester
has a front-door method that generates text suggestions. Neither fact establishes a formal
identification algorithm. The proposal should reuse the suggestion pattern selectively and
send the resulting explicit graph and query to a separately admitted causal engine. It should
preserve cited source passages and unresolved alternatives instead of interpreting a generated
factor list as an approved adjustment set. (pywhy-llm contributors, 2026)
   For oci-agent, the useful candidate is the separation of a specification, a deterministic
analysis notebook and a critic report. The selected source has a general notebook runner and
a target-label issue requiring correction. A bounded banking interface should expose fixed
reviewed operations with resource limits and typed outputs. The proposal does not adopt a
general notebook executor as the causal MCP surface. Dependency resolution, failure handling
and executable parity remain separate implementation tasks; the source’s research status is
not a reason to infer a deployed bank service. (oci-agent contributors, 2026)
   CausalDS is a candidate for generated scene and task design, but its grader needs a semantic
review before direct adoption. The inspected identification/scoring helpers distinguish several
genuine states, yet some missing metadata defaults and finite-interval checks require attention.
Unknown identification due to a missing backend is not scientific nonidentification. A malformed
answer is not a justified abstention. A capped score can conceal severe tail losses unless the
uncapped losses and coverage are also reported. The proposal therefore takes the task separation
and private-reference design while requiring explicit metadata and failure validation. (causalds
contributors, 2026)
   The deterministic formulation baseline has three layers. A schema check verifies that
population, unit, intervention, comparator, horizon, clock and scale are present. A semantic
check compares these fields with the supplied brief and dictionary: a post-contact duration
cannot become a pre-contact covariate, an invitation cannot silently become actual uptake, and
a requested all-eligible effect cannot become a recipients-only effect. A formal check evaluates
identification under the explicitly supplied candidate graph and returns an expression, model-
relative nonidentification, unsupported scope or an unresolved input. These checks validate
different things. A well-formed schema does not prove the story is true, and a correctly
evaluated graph does not prove its edges.
   For a generated benchmark, the reference can enumerate a finite set of admissible formu-
lations Q(b) for brief b. An explicitly resolved brief may have one acceptable target. An
ambiguous brief may have several and require the system to request or retain the missing
distinction. A baseline can return those alternatives directly from the supplied reference
fields and use exact calculations such as the example above. This establishes a transparent
41.12. Whose effect is the assistant being asked to estimate?                                 1099


lower-cost comparator and exposes what a language model is expected to add: interpretation
of unstructured language, evidence retrieval and useful clarification, rather than numerical
work already handled by a deterministic engine.


41.11.4     Evaluation before a costly bank study

The initial evaluation can use public data dictionaries and openly documented financial
examples alongside generated causal mechanisms. Public data support questions about
available variables and clocks; they usually do not supply intervention truth. Generated
mechanisms can supply that truth for the declared model. A reference author should create
matched examples that vary one decisive feature: invitation versus uptake, all eligible versus
treated population, pre-decision versus post-decision measurement, complete variables versus
noisy proxies, or a single action versus repeated treatment. The target-change example supplies
one exact reference family. This is a proposed evaluation design; it is not a reported live-agent
comparison.
   Train/development and final evaluation should be split by the underlying scenario or
structural model, not merely by paraphrases of the same question. Otherwise a system can
learn the reference target from exposed near-duplicates. All requests should remain in the
evaluation denominator, including ambiguous requests, timeouts, unsupported estimands,
malformed answers and justified nonidentification. Report target and clock fidelity, unjustified
resolution of ambiguity, false causal answers, valid abstention, numerical error where a target
is actually identified, interval availability and coverage where ground truth permits them, and
total resource use. A high completion rate alone rewards an agent for confidently answering
questions that should remain unresolved.
   Retrieval, structured prompting and an actor/critic loop should be compared against the
same deterministic baseline and fixed task families. A retrieval ablation tests whether source
passages improve interpretation. A critic ablation tests whether additional review catches errors,
while reporting the added calls, time and newly introduced mistakes. A graph-perturbation
comparison tests whether a system notices that an assumption changed. Repeated runs
reveal stability. These studies need their actual model, tool, prompt, data and stopping-rule
identities frozen before final evaluation. Agreement across repeated runs is useful evidence
about stability; it is not evidence that the agreed answer is causally correct.
   Several gaps remain scientific. A general method for recovering stakeholder intent from
incomplete language is not established. The immediate remedy is to preserve admissible
alternatives and make the missing decision explicit. A general guarantee that retrieval or
debate validates causal edges is also absent; the current studies justify investigating those tools
with factual and graph-specific references, not treating consensus as truth. Identification from
noisy proxies, dependent observations or repeated interventions requires the corresponding
statistical model and method. Finally, whether an assisted workflow saves bank analyst time
or changes an investment decision requires a later workflow study after a bounded prototype
shows merit. Those gaps narrow the claims and motivate specific experiments; they do not
prevent writing or testing the proposal’s public/generated formulation contract.


41.12       Whose effect is the assistant being asked to estimate?
A banking assistant translating an offer proposal must specify whose outcome the offer is
intended to improve. “The average effect is positive” leaves open whether the average describes
existing customers, a new acquisition population, an equal mix of branches, or a precision-
weighted statistical summary. These choices can lead to different actions even when every
1100                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


group effect is known. Vilfort’s Robust Inference for Weighted Estimands provides a useful
statistical treatment of this ambiguity Vilfort (2026). It is an econometric contribution to
specifying and checking targets, rather than an algorithm for language-model discovery. Its
value for a causal assistant begins after the group effects have a defensible interpretation.


41.12.1     Separate identification, aggregation and sampling uncertainty

Let θ = (θ1 , . . . , θK )′ contain effects for K customer groups, with each entry measured in the
same units and over the same horizon. A weight vector w defines

                                    τw = w′ θ,       1′ w = 1.                                (41.8)

Normalization alone permits negative entries. If the question concerns an actual customer
mixture, require the simplex ∆K = {w : w ≥ 0, 1′ w = 1}. A signed regression contrast may
be a legitimate statistical target, but it should not be described as the mean outcome of an
unspecified population. Group definitions, treatment regimes, calendar times and horizons must
be compatible before aggregation. A weight change cannot repair an effect whose identification
assumptions have failed.
  The exact experiment studied in the paper assumes

                                    θb ∼ N (θ, Σ),     Σ ≻ 0,                                 (41.9)

where K is fixed, Σ is known, and the baseline weights and alternative class are fixed and
known. The full joint covariance matters; separate group standard errors do not supply it. Let
Λ be a nonempty compact convex class of alternative normalized weights. It represents stated
ambiguity or disagreement about the target, rather than an automatically identified set of
possible bank populations. A target outside this class receives no protection from robustness
calculated inside it. Choosing the class after inspecting estimated effects also changes the
statistical problem.
   Consider an authored two-group illustration with stipulated effects θ = (6, −2)′ USD per
customer and baseline w = (3/4, 1/4)′ . Its contribution is 4. The alternative population
λ = (1/4, 3/4)′ has contribution 0. At a stipulated cost of USD 1 per customer, the respective
net values are 3 and −1. Nothing about this disagreement requires a hallucination or an
inaccurate group-effect estimate. The populations answer different questions. These are exact
project examples, not observations from a bank or replications of the paper’s applications
Causal banking proposal project (2026bm).
   One transparent ambiguity class moves a fraction ϵ of baseline weight to any simplex
distribution:
                          Λϵ = (1 − ϵ)w + ϵ∆2 ,    0 ≤ ϵ ≤ 1.                    (41.10)
Because the smallest and largest group contributions are −2 and 6, its effect and net-value
ranges are
                {λ′ θ : λ ∈ Λϵ } = [4 − 6ϵ, 4 + 2ϵ], Vϵ = [3 − 6ϵ, 3 + 2ϵ].         (41.11)
The worst-case net value is strictly positive only for ϵ < 1/2. The alternative population above
first enters the class at ϵ = 2/3: its first coordinate requires 1/4 ≥ (1 − ϵ)3/4. The break-even
ambiguity level therefore has a clear business meaning. It states how much customer-mix
uncertainty the proposed decision tolerates under stipulated effects. It does not estimate how
uncertain the true mix actually is.
  Even a correctly calibrated interval for the baseline need not protect the other population.
Under the additional stipulated model θb ∼ N ((6, −2)′ , I2 ), the baseline estimator has variance
