42.7     From a balance response to a monetary decision
The deposit example exposes a difficulty that arises before any estimator is chosen. A balance
is a stock, its accumulation over time is an exposure, and the financial benefit of that exposure
depends on a valuation convention. These quantities cannot be interchanged because they
all contain a currency unit. The assistant must obtain a complete statement of the business
target: does treasury want additional deposits, lower expense for a fixed funding requirement,
or a relationship-value objective that includes services beyond funding? Each question can be
legitimate. Only the second is answered by the funding-cost construction developed here. The
construction and all numerical values in this section are authored, exact illustrations. They
supply a reference for testing a proposed translator, not observed bank economics (Causal
banking research project, 2026ba).
  Let Bd (a) be end-of-day eligible balance under offer a on day d, where a = 0 is the stated
existing offer and a = 1 is the proposed offer. Fix a horizon of H days and a day-count
denominator D. Define
                              H                         H
                           1 X                          X
                    B(a) =       Bd (a),       S(a) =         Bd (a) = HB(a).                (42.4)
                           H d=1                        d=1

The units are dollars and dollar-days respectively. With a constant annual valuation rate q,
the monetary amount assigned to the balance-time is qS(a)/D dollars. The rate, denominator,
daily measurement convention and horizon are part of this definition. For example, substituting
a last-day balance for an average balance changes the outcome even if the two amounts happen
to agree in a stable illustrative account. A genuine proposal needs the product’s actual accrual
convention; the example fixes D = 365 without claiming that this convention applies to every
deposit contract.
   Suppose, for the moment, that treasury has the same exogenous daily funding requirement
Fd under either offer and can cover the residual Fd − Bd (a) at a supplied rate qd . This
construction assumes 0 ≤ Bd (a) ≤ Fd ; excess deposits would require a separately specified
investment or disposal rule. Let rd (a) be the deposit rate, and let K(a) be the monetary
expense outside interest: for example a stipulated communication charge. Ignoring discounting
in this short-horizon construction, define
                                 H
                              1 X
                    N (a) =        {rd (a)Bd (a) + qd [Fd − Bd (a)]} + K(a),                 (42.5)
                              D d=1
                                H
                             1 X
                     V (a) =      [qd − rd (a)]Bd (a) − K(a).                                (42.6)
                             D d=1

Here N is net funding cost and V is the saving relative to funding the entire requirement at
qd . Their sum is the common reference cost D−1 d qd Fd . Therefore the offer’s incremental
                                                 P

value is exactly ∆V = E[V (1) − V (0)] = −E[N (1) − N (0)]. Maximizing V and minimizing
N agree. Neither convention licenses maximizing the increase in funding cost. A separate
expense must be netted as K(1) − K(0), not automatically as K(1): the comparator itself
may incur expense, and cancelling a campaign may save it.
  This identity depends on the reference funding requirement and valuation path being
common. If the offer changes lending volumes, the institution’s marginal funding rate, or the
capacity to raise substitute funds, those objects acquire potential-outcome indices and the
common-reference term no longer cancels. An assistant cannot preserve the simple identity
while quietly adding those effects to its narrative. It must expand the target, state the
additional intervention and equilibrium assumptions, or present the fixed-requirement result
42.7. From a balance response to a monetary decision                                       1113


as a narrower answer. Likewise, relationship benefits should be represented by a separately
specified monetary outcome, not attached to a balance effect through an unexplained positive
adjective.


42.7.1    Repricing existing balances can reverse the conclusion

Under constant rates, write r1 = r0 + δr and ∆S = S(1) − S(0). Subtracting the two value
definitions gives the pathwise identity
                                      (q − r0 )∆S − δrS(1)
                    V (1) − V (0) =                        − [K(1) − K(0)].              (42.7)
                                                D
The first term values additional balance-time at the old spread. The second charges the higher
deposit rate to all balances receiving it, including balances that would have remained without
the offer. It is not restricted to newly attracted deposits. An equivalent decomposition uses
the new spread on ∆S and the rate increase on S(0). Both produce the same cash difference;
adding both repricing terms would count part of the cost twice. These identities hold for each
pair of potential balance paths, so taking expectations requires no independence between the
two paths.
   Consider an exact thirty-day example. The comparator holds USD100,000 every day at
a 2% annual rate; the offered rate is 2.25%, and its balance is USD110,000 every day. The
stipulated substitute funding rate is 5%. Operating expenses are USD4 under the comparator
and USD8 under the offer. Thus ∆S = 300,000 dollar-days and the added average balance is
USD10,000. The additional old-spread value is 1800/73 dollars and the repricing charge is
1650/73 dollars. Their difference is only 150/73 dollars. Subtracting the incremental USD4
expense gives
                               1800 − 1650           142
                        ∆V =                 −4=−         ≃ −USD 1.95.                    (42.8)
                                    73                73
The offer attracts balances while increasing net funding cost. The reference also constructs the
complete daily ledger for a stipulated USD150,000 funding requirement and reproduces the
opposite-signed cost difference by summation. That second calculation checks the accounting
identity instead of merely repeating the printed formula. Treating the USD10,000 stock
increase as a USD10,000 benefit, forgetting existing-balance repricing, or subtracting USD8
instead of the incremental USD4 each answers a different question.
   The all-eligible mean effect remains a population target. A deterministic balance path here
makes the arithmetic transparent; a causal analysis must identify or bound the distribution
of paths under both offers. Identifying the mean balance contrast alone is sufficient for this
linear, fixed-rate valuation only when the other required expectations and costs are supplied.
It is not a claim that a regression coefficient identifies the complete financial response of a
deposit portfolio.


42.7.2    Marginal funding cost and an explicit valuation boundary

Another reasonable business question is the annualized incremental expense per unit of extra
balance-time. For a positive expected balance-time change, under the same constant-rate
convention define
                               r1 E[S(1)] − r0 E[S(0)] + DE[K(1) − K(0)]
                      rinc =                                             .               (42.9)
                                              E[S(1) − S(0)]
This is a ratio of portfolio expectations, not the mean of customer-level ratios. The latter can
be undefined for accounts with no balance response, give large influence to tiny denominators,
1114                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


and change the aggregation question. The incremental cost rate also differs from the offered
deposit rate. In the example it is 1571/30000, or about 5.237%, despite the 2.25% offered
rate. It includes paying more on existing balances and spreading the incremental operating
expense over the new balance-time. With positive expected ∆S, ∆V is positive precisely when
q > rinc . If that denominator is zero or negative, the displayed ratio is unavailable or loses this
comparison interpretation; the original monetary difference remains the appropriate object to
inspect.
   This comparison is useful even when a bank has not yet supplied a valuation rate. Instead
of inventing a price, the proposal can report the break-even rate or a sensitivity interval. If
the same example permits q between 4% and 6%, its value ranges from −742/73 to 458/73
dollars, roughly minus USD10.16 to plus USD6.27. There is no uniformly preferred offer over
that stipulated set. An owner who accepts the funding model can resolve the economic choice
by supplying the relevant rate and cost convention. This is a missing business input, distinct
from an unidentified balance response. Uncertainty about both should be kept visible rather
than folded into one unexplained error bar.
  For a set of admissible causal laws P and valuation specifications Q, the corresponding
proposal can report

                    V = {EP [Vq (1) − Vq (0)] : (P, q) ∈ A},      A ⊆ P × Q.                (42.10)

The joint admissible set A matters. If liquidity conditions affect both the response and the
marginal rate, independently combining marginal endpoints may create impossible scenarios or
omit admissible dependence. The interval above deliberately varies only a deterministic rate
while holding the response law fixed. It is an economic sensitivity calculation, not a confidence
interval, a Bayesian posterior, or a general sharp bound. The formulation should state which
of those objects the user is requesting before selecting a downstream numerical tool.


42.7.3    Timing and nonlinear valuation require more than a mean

Balance-time suffices only for a constant linear valuation. With a supplied time-varying path
qd , the gross monetary effect is D−1 d qd E[Bd (1) − Bd (0)]. As an exact two-day example,
                                      P

compare additional balances of (200, 0) with (0, 200) dollars. Both have average additional
balance USD100 and exposure 200 dollar-days. At rates (0.10, 0.01) their gross values are
20/365 and 2/365 dollars. A translator that passes only the mean balance to the valuation
engine loses the information needed to distinguish these cases. Discount factors, when required,
must similarly attach to the appropriate cash-flow dates; they cannot be appended after
aggregation if the timing information was dropped.
   A nonlinear valuation needs still more information. Suppose a hypothetical gross value rule
is m(B) = 0.01 min(B, 100) dollars and a comparator has zero gross value. A balance fixed at
USD100 has expected gross value USD1. A balance of zero or USD200 with equal probabilities
has the same mean balance but expected gross value USD0.50. With incremental expense
USD0.75, their net values are USD0.25 and minus USD0.25. The mean balance response does
not identify which decision is favorable. This example is deliberately stylized; its purpose is to
distinguish E[m(B)] from m(E[B]), not to suggest a bank’s valuation schedule.
  Where costs depend on utilization, default, or other post-offer quantities, those quantities
belong in the monetary potential outcome. Their joint distribution can matter. Using the
realized balance to calculate interest is legitimate outcome construction; using that same
post-offer balance as a pre-offer targeting feature is a clock violation. Similarly, conditioning
on it to estimate an ordinary total effect generally changes the question. The declaration
must identify the role a variable plays, rather than labelling a field universally permitted or
42.8. Measurement and selective notes can change the target                                1115


forbidden. The target-trial and time-varying treatment distinctions already developed from
Hernán and Robins (2020) provide the inherited framework; the cash-flow mappings here are
project-specific definitions.


42.7.4    Consolidation and feasibility are part of the intervention

The business unit determines what counts as additional funding. If an offer moves USD10,000
from one account to another account at the same bank, the receiving account’s effect is positive
while the consolidated balance change is zero. Repricing the receiving account can nevertheless
increase expense. For mutually exclusive account balances under a fixed consolidation map, the
bank-level outcome sums the account paths before applying the bank-level valuation. Shared
accounts must not be counted once for each linked owner. When the intervention changes
ownership, currency composition or legal availability, a fixed consolidation map itself becomes
an assumption to reconsider. An identifier matching exercise cannot choose the economic
boundary on the owner’s behalf.
   This also changes treatment definition. A rate offered to one account may alter another
account’s balance or a household’s other offers. The potential outcome may then depend on
an allocation vector, not just an account’s own binary action. A feasible policy must respect
the shared budget and the permitted unit of allocation. Account-level exchangeability and
a no-interference assumption are substantive restrictions on that target, not conveniences a
language model can infer from a rectangular dataset. If these restrictions are not defensible,
the proposal can retain a cluster or portfolio question with its additional requirements.
   A budget needs an equally clear comparator. An absolute expense constraint E[K(π)] ≤ B
differs from an incremental constraint E[K(π) − K(π0 )] ≤ B. A capacity constraint on the
number of contacts is a third object and may not be expressible as either monetary constraint.
The policy π can use only the declared predecision history; the comparator π0 must satisfy its
own declared feasibility conditions. The proposed assistant should present these alternatives
in the business brief and carry the accepted choice into the formal query. Optimization before
that choice can produce a precise answer to an unstated problem.


42.8     Measurement and selective notes can change the target
The cash-flow argument generalizes to language-derived outcomes. A rule g that converts a
servicing note into a distress indicator defines an observed measurement, not automatically
the underlying distress variable. The inspected discussions by Keith and colleagues and Egami
and colleagues separate measurement from causal identification and distinguish a learned text
representation from the scientific target (Keith et al., 2020; Egami et al., 2018). The proposed
translator must say whether the owner wants the effect on recorded distress, on a fixed coding
rule’s output, or on latent distress. Those outcomes can differ even when the extraction system
executes exactly as specified.
   Let a binary underlying outcome have intervention-specific mean µa = Pr(Y (a) = 1). For a
fixed binary measurement rule, define its sensitivity sa = Pr(Y ∗ = 1 | Y = 1, do(A = a)) and
specificity ca = Pr(Y ∗ = 0 | Y = 0, do(A = a)). By the law of total probability, when these
conditional rates are defined,

                   µ∗a = sa µa + (1 − ca )(1 − µa ) = (sa + ca − 1)µa + 1 − ca .        (42.11)

This is an exact project derivation, not an imported guarantee for an LLM. If sensitivity and
specificity are common across interventions, the measured contrast equals (s + c − 1)(µ1 −
1116                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


µ0 ). Recovering the underlying contrast by division requires those error rates to be known,
transportable and s + c − 1 ̸= 0. If the sum is one, the measurement contains no marginal
information about the binary outcome through this channel. If it is less than one, its direction is
reversed. Assuming ordinary attenuation without checking the channel is therefore unjustified.
   For example, set true outcome risks to 2/5 and 1/2, a true effect of 1/10. With common
sensitivity 4/5 and specificity 9/10, the measured effect is 7/100. Now retain those control
error rates but use treated sensitivity 1/2 and specificity 19/20. The measured effect becomes
−21/200, reversing the sign. All probabilities remain valid. The change could represent
different document content or extraction errors after the offer; the example makes no claim
that this occurs in a bank. Its implication is that pooled classification accuracy cannot
determine the causal error. A validation design needs outcome truth and enough treatment-
specific information to support the proposed correction, including the population and document
mechanism to which the rates are transported.
   Missing notes introduce a separate problem even when every available note is coded perfectly.
Let A and predecision distress U be independent Bernoulli variables with probability 1/2,
and define Y (a) = U for either action. The intervention has zero effect. Let R indicate
a note available for analysis, with probability 3/4 when A = U and 1/4 otherwise. Every
action–distress combination has positive note availability, so this example does not depend on
a cell with zero support. Exact enumeration gives
                                        3                                    1
              Pr(Y = 1 | A = 1, R = 1) = ,         Pr(Y = 1 | A = 0, R = 1) = .            (42.12)
                                        4                                    4
The observed-note contrast is 1/2 despite random assignment and a zero effect in the full
population. Selecting notes conditions on a common effect of action and distress. A correct
event timestamp, perfect extraction and randomized treatment do not remove that selection
mechanism.
   An oracle that knows U and the note probabilities can reweight each selected cell by the
inverse of its selection probability and recover mean distress 1/2 in each arm. This verifies
the construction; it is not a proposed correction when distress is precisely the unobserved
quantity the notes were meant to measure. The useful handoff identifies what is missing: a
justified observation model, independent validation measurements, or a narrower target that
the owner actually accepts. It must not quietly replace the eligible population by customers
with convenient documentation.
   These examples distinguish three repairs. Correcting a unit or comparator is a specification
repair. Estimating a measurement channel needs suitable validation information. Correcting
selective availability needs a defensible observation law and support. A language model can
locate definitions, propose alternatives and flag contradictions in each case, but those actions
do not provide the missing scientific information. Multiple defensible diagrams and their
different identifying consequences should survive the formulation stage, consistent with the
inspected argument for explicit assumption-based modelling in Geraldo Bastías (2024).


42.8.1    A proposal evaluation that isolates the translation error

A useful public and generated evaluation can freeze a set of business briefs that share language
while differing in one decision-relevant fact. For funding, pair a balance target with a net-cost
target; then vary whether the comparator incurs expense, whether repricing covers old balances,
and whether valuation is time-varying or nonlinear. For measurement, vary common versus
differential error and complete versus selective notes. The exact mechanisms above supply the
expected mathematical answer, while public dictionaries can supply realistic field names and
42.9. Which servicing policy does the business sentence describe?                                   1117


documented units. Public text alone supplies neither assignment truth nor a bank’s marginal
funding rate. An evaluation should preserve that distinction explicitly.
   The reference response should contain the target, the necessary outcome components, the
sign convention, the information that is absent, and the reason an alternative interpretation
would change the answer. A numerical score is appropriate only when the brief supplies enough
information to determine it. For an unspecified q, reporting the break-even rate and the
unresolved valuation choice can be correct; inventing a rate to produce a confident investment
recommendation is an error. For selective notes with unknown selection probabilities, reporting
the selected contrast as the full-population effect is an error even when the subtraction is
exact.
   The comparison should use the same briefs, dictionaries, permissible source material and
answer schema for a structured analyst baseline and an assisted workflow. Separate the
underlying mechanisms used for development from those used for final evaluation, and keep
ambiguous, unsupported and failed requests in the denominator. This section provides exact
authored reference families, not a completed provider comparison. A useful prototype result
would identify which translation failures become less frequent and at what review cost. That
result can support a later decision to purchase authentic banking validation; it cannot supply
such validation in advance.


42.9      Which servicing policy does the business sentence de-
          scribe?
A request to improve early servicing can leave the later action rule unspecified. That omission
is more consequential than a missing estimator option. An initial review may change a
later condition, and a subsequent contact may respond to that condition. Comparing first-
stage actions while holding the later action fixed therefore differs from comparing complete
operating policies. The longitudinal formula developed earlier makes this distinction precise;
the following finite construction shows the numerical consequence. It specializes the inherited
sequential-intervention framework of Hernán and Robins (2020) to an authored example, with
no empirical claim about how an actual servicing review affects hardship.
   Let A0 denote an initial action, L1 a later adverse-state indicator, and A1 a follow-up action
taken after observing L1 . Stipulate Pr(L1 = 1 | do(A0 = 0)) = 1/4 and Pr(L1 = 1 | do(A0 =
1)) = 3/4. The initial action has a direct benefit but increases the chance of the costly later
state in this deliberately adverse model. Define net recovery, in hypothetical dollars, by

                                 Y (a, l, b) = 100 + 20a − 40l + 30bl − 10b.                      (42.13)

The last term is the follow-up cost and is already included in the outcome. There is no
additional initial cost in this construction. The structural model uses an independent uniform
disturbance to generate L1 at the stated probabilities, and the outcome is then deterministic
given the actions and state. These declarations supply the causal law for the example; observed
historical conditional frequencies would not by themselves supply the same law.
   For a fixed initial action a, let g a take the follow-up action precisely when L1 = 1. In that
state, follow-up adds USD20 net; when L1 = 0 it subtracts USD10. The adaptive rule is
consequently optimal within this specified two-action second-stage class when the state is fully
observed and there is no shared capacity constraint. Its value is
                 1
                 X
    V (g a ) =         Y (a, l, l) Pr(L1 = l | do(A0 = a)),    V (g 0 ) = 95,   V (g 1 ) = 105.   (42.14)
                 l=0
1118                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


The complete-policy contrast is USD10. If follow-up is prohibited under both initial actions,
both values are USD90 and the first-action contrast is zero. If the state is held fixed and the
same follow-up action is used, the direct contrast in the reward expression is USD20. Finally,
comparing g 1 with never taking either action yields USD15. All four calculations are correct
for their own interventions. A translator that reports one without stating which subsequent
policy is held fixed has not resolved the business question. Subtracting the follow-up expense
again would introduce a separate accounting error.
   The value comparison can be independently checked under a fully supported generated logger.
Let the logger randomize each action with probability 1/2, using an independent randomization
at the second stage after observing the state. Its eight possible histories have probabilities
1                                             a
4 Pr(L1 = l | do(A0 = a)). For the target g , retain histories with A0 = a and A1 = L1 and
multiply their logger probabilities by four. Summing the weighted rewards reproduces 95 and
105. This finite enumeration and the direct policy calculation are implemented separately in
the exact reference (Causal banking research project, 2026bb). The agreement checks this
particular known law. It does not show that a real logger is known, that hidden hardship is
observed, or that weights fitted to dependent customer histories have calibrated uncertainty.
   The availability clock gives the rule an operational interpretation. If L1 is available before the
second decision, A1 = L1 is admissible. If the note describing it arrives after that decision, the
same expression uses unavailable information. A fixed always-contact rule has values USD87.50
and USD102.50 for initial actions zero and one; a fixed never-contact rule has values USD90
and USD90. The best fixed rule is never-contact for initial action zero and always-contact for
initial action one under this stipulated law. These rules illustrate a value difference caused by
changing the permitted information, not by switching estimators. A forecast available earlier is
another candidate input with its own joint law; it cannot be substituted for the later realized
state without a new calculation.
   The formulation should accordingly distinguish three requests: evaluation of a supplied
policy, selection from a declared feasible policy class, and an unrestricted optimal-policy
claim. The example resolves only a tiny known-law class. Adding hidden state, nonbinary
actions, capacity constraints or an unknown behavior policy creates additional research and
implementation requirements. The assistant can preserve these requirements in a formal query
and explain why the static effect is insufficient. It cannot convert the finite optimum into a
guarantee for general private-state servicing.


42.10       A threshold change is an applicant-population decision
Credit approval introduces a different translation failure: observing a good outcome among
accepted applicants does not establish the value of expanding acceptance. Let Dz (S) be a
deterministic approval rule at score S under policy z. Define R(1) as net monetary contribution
if a specified loan is offered and R(0) as the contribution under the specified alternative, such
as declining this product while retaining other services. On a common applicant population,
the policy value is
                             V (z) = E[Dz (S)R(1) + {1 − Dz (S)}R(0)].                    (42.15)
This definition needs the loan terms, horizon, default and recovery treatment, capital charges
and the decline alternative fixed. Repayment probability alone does not supply R. Nor is the
mean contribution among approved applications equal to V (z): its denominator changes with
the threshold.
  Suppose the new rule expands approval monotonically and changes no loan terms for already
approved applicants. Under a common potential-outcome law without capacity spillovers,
42.10. A threshold change is an applicant-population decision                               1119


subtracting the policy values gives

                      V (1) − V (0) = E[{D1 (S) − D0 (S)}{R(1) − R(0)}].                 (42.16)

Only the newly approved band contributes. If repricing or other changes also affect incumbent
approvals, this simplification fails and their contribution must remain in the target. If
actions interact through a capital or staffing constraint, the individual response law also needs
revision. The equation is an accounting consequence of the specified potential outcomes, not
an identification result from historical approvals.
   For an exact counterexample, let the old rule approve one fifth of applicants, each with
USD100 expected net contribution, and let the new rule admit an additional one tenth. Set the
decline contribution to zero. In one admissible law the new band would contribute USD50 each
if offered the loan; in another it would contribute minus USD50. The historical data under
the old rule can be identical because this band received no loans. Its loan outcomes remain
unobserved. The old policy value is USD20 per applicant in either law, while the expanded
policy has values USD25 and USD15. The incremental values are therefore USD5 and minus
USD5. Exact enumeration verifies the result (Causal banking research project, 2026bb).
   Meanwhile, mean contribution per approved applicant falls from USD100 to USD250/3 in
the favorable law, and to USD50 in the adverse law. Thus even an observed reduction in the
approved-group average does not alone show that expansion reduces total applicant-population
value. It can reflect adding a positive but less profitable group. The proposal should carry the
common applicant denominator, the new approval mass and the net contribution convention
through the analysis. A question about whether loan quality falls should retain portfolio
value and conditional credit quality as different questions until the owner chooses the intended
objective.
   Suppose only the scientific range −200 ≤ R(1) − R(0) ≤ 100 is supplied for the new band.
Its known mass of one tenth then yields the incremental value range [−20, 10] dollars per
applicant. Both endpoints are attained by assigning the corresponding constant contribution
throughout the unobserved band, without changing the old-policy observations. This is a
sharp range within the stipulated class, not a sampling interval or a calibrated statement
about a bank’s loss distribution. A more restrictive response model, credible experimental
information or justified transport restriction can narrow it. A prediction for the unobserved
band merely names one extrapolation unless its scientific basis is established.
   A discontinuity at the old threshold can, under its design assumptions, answer a local
question about applicants near that threshold. It does not automatically supply the response
throughout a finite newly admitted band. The assistant must distinguish moving the cutoff by
a specified amount from estimating a local effect at the existing cutoff, and retain the support
or transport argument required to connect them. Public threshold mechanisms and generated
response laws can test this distinction before a bank considers a costly pilot. The relevant
prototype success is correct translation, appropriate bounds and justified abstention under
absent information, not confident completion of every numerical request.
Chapter 43

Variable meaning, ontology and the
observation that a causal claim needs

A servicing proposal may ask whether an early support offer reduces financial distress over the
next thirty days. The bank can observe payment events, balances, customer messages and
employees’ notes, but none of these is simply the construct of financial distress. A payment
can be made by drawing on another account; a note can describe anticipated hardship rather
than a realized missed payment; an employee can write more carefully after making an offer.
An assistant that assigns all these records the same variable name changes the observation on
which the causal question depends.
  The proposed ontology layer has a specific purpose: make the relationship between a
construct, its operational measure and its original observation explicit enough to challenge. This
can help a scientist formulate a question, a data engineer construct a reproducible observation
and a reviewer locate a disputed assumption. It does not determine which construct the
bank should value, establish the truth of a causal relation, or make an unobserved confounder
observable. The distinction has consequences even when the intervention itself is randomized.


43.1     From a business construct to a defined estimand
Let Ai ∈ {0, 1} denote a support offer at decision time zero for eligible account i. Define Yi (a)
as the indicator of a specified missed-payment event by day thirty under intervention a. With
a fixed eligible population and account weighting, the target is

                                    τY = E{Yi (1) − Yi (0)}.

Consistency requires a sufficiently specified offer, comparator and event; random assignment
and appropriate handling of interference would justify a simple experimental comparison.
An observational proposal additionally needs a defensible adjustment or other identification
argument. Calling a field a confounder does not supply that argument.
   Now let Ti (a) be a service note and Li (a) = gθ (Ti (a)) its binary label under a frozen
extraction rule gθ . Even if the label is named after missed payments, the experiment on labels
targets
                                  τL = E{gθ (Ti (1)) − gθ (Ti (0))}.
This is a defined effect of the offer on a coded textual outcome. Equating it with τY requires
an additional measurement argument. If the desired target is latent hardship Ui (a), neither an
observed payment nor a plausible description of it automatically identifies that target.

                                              1120
43.2. What formal ontologies and language models can contribute                              1121


   Egami and colleagues develop this distinction through a learned text mapping: the repre-
sentation helps define the causal outcome, and learning it from the same treatment-assigned
evaluation documents can induce dependence and overfitting. Their train/test separation holds
the learned mapping fixed for effect estimation on the evaluation sample.(Egami et al., 2018)
That remedy addresses reuse of evaluation information; it does not establish that a learned
category measures hardship without error. The earlier measurement discussion’s residual-
confounding example makes a different point: even a useful proxy can leave confounding and
reverse a coefficient’s sign. Both problems survive a syntactically valid ontology.
   Keith, Jensen and O’Connor explain why the causal role of text also matters: text may
measure confounding, mediate a treatment or be selected by a collider mechanism.(Keith et al.,
2020) A note written after the offer cannot be admitted as a baseline covariate merely because
it mentions a pre-existing condition. Its information might have been elicited by the offer.
The proposal must distinguish the underlying condition’s event time, the record’s availability
and the process that produced the record.
   For each variable, the proposed representation retains five linked objects: the business
construct, the operational definition, the observation or transformation, the role in a particular
causal model, and the target population’s unit and weighting. These links can have different
epistemic statuses. A schema can verify that a payment record has a date and amount; a
reviewer can accept a definition for a study; a causal analyst can still leave the identification
assumptions unresolved. A single confidence score cannot substitute for these separate decisions.


43.2     What formal ontologies and language models can con-
         tribute
Pressat-Laffouilhere’s OntoBioStat thesis treats variable selection as a problem of formal
representation and supplied relations. Its account of recoding is particularly relevant: changing
a variable’s categories creates a different variable, whose context, possible values, missingness
and transformation must be represented. It also distinguishes hypothetical causal relations
from relations under validation and illustrates sensitivity analysis by retaining or removing un-
certain links before rerunning a reasoner.(Pressat-Laffouilhere, 2023) For a bank, an analogous
distinction would separate a note mentioning hardship, a customer reporting hardship and
reviewed evidence supporting an effect of hardship on payment. An inference explanation can
show which supplied relations were used. It cannot establish that those relations are true, or
guarantee a valid adjustment set for every causal graph.
   The two knowledge-graph surveys offer complementary architectural choices. Jeff Z. Pan
and colleagues contrast explicit-knowledge-first with parametric-knowledge-first approaches.
The former can expose a curated vocabulary and links for the assistant to retrieve; the latter
can propose entities and relations that subsequently need canonicalization and review.(Pan
et al., 2023) Shirui Pan and colleagues organize the broader interaction into knowledge-graph-
enhanced language models, language-model-augmented graphs and synergized systems. Their
retrieval, representation and graph/text fusion mechanisms explain how an assistant might
find a definition or propose a relation.(Pan et al., 2024) The question-answering paths and
attention scores in these architectures do not identify the effect of an intervention.
   A useful design keeps relation types separate. A type-of relation belongs to a taxonomy;
derivation describes data lineage; association records an observed relationship; a hypothesized
cause belongs to a candidate causal model. A household owns accounts, but the ownership
edge is not a causal arrow from a household variable to an account outcome. A synonym
link can support a search without authorizing the merger of two measurements. An ontology
1122                                                                  Causal analysis for a universal bank


reasoner checks implications of its formal premises; a causal identification procedure has
different premises and a different output.
   Tan and colleagues’ annotation survey separates generation, assessment and utilization
of annotations, and discusses hallucination, feedback from synthetic data and manual or
automatic validation.(Tan et al., 2024) This separation suggests a staged bank workflow: an
extractor proposes a field and cites the passage; a typed validator checks identity, unit and
clock; a reviewer adjudicates meaning; a causal analysis uses the resulting measurement under
explicit assumptions. Agreement among model-generated labels is evidence about agreement,
not independent evidence about the underlying construct. Generated respondents are especially
unsuitable as substitutes for observed customers in an effect estimate.
   Schwitter, Bach and Klamm distinguish text as outcome, treatment and control and illustrate
substantive measurement decisions in sociological applications. In one reported annotation
example, zero-shot kappa is 0.63 ± 0.01, compared with 0.78 ± 0.01 under three-shot prompting,
across three reruns. These are agreement results in the authors’ setting, not calibrated bank
measurement errors or causal confidence intervals. Their distinction between annotating real
respondents and generating respondent simulations is directly relevant here. Their illustrated
noise experiment discusses a tendency toward type-II error; differential measurement need not
behave that way.(Schwitter et al., 2026)


43.3     High label accuracy can coexist with a false monetary
         conclusion
Consider an exact authored population with randomized, equally sized offer and control arms.
The true adverse-event risk is p0 = p1 = 1/5. Write

              sa = P (L = 1 | Y = 1, A = a),            fa = P (L = 1 | Y = 0, A = a).

The observed label risk is

               qa = P (L = 1 | A = a) = sa pa + fa (1 − pa ) = (sa − fa )pa + fa .

This identity follows by partitioning on the true outcome. It does not assume that an observed
label is the true outcome. Suppose the control arm has (s0 , f0 ) = (4/5, 1/20), while the
offered arm has (s1 , f1 ) = (9/10, 3/20). For instance, the intervention may change employees’
documentation and the terms customers use. The stipulated numbers imply
                       1               3                       1
                   q0 = ,       q1 =      ,      q1 − q0 =        ,     p1 − p0 = 0.
                       5               10                      10
Control accuracy is 0.92, offered-arm accuracy is 0.86, and pooled accuracy is 0.89. Despite that
apparently respectable aggregate accuracy, the label comparison reports a ten-percentage-point
adverse effect under a true null. At a stipulated loss of USD 1,000 per true event, treating
labels as events invents USD 100 of additional loss per account. These are illustrative exact
values, not estimates from customers or model calls.(Causal banking proposal, 2026bw)
  If valid arm-specific measurement rates were known and sa ̸= fa , the algebraic correction
                                                     qa − fa
                                              pa =
                                                     sa − fa

would recover 1/5 in each arm in this example. The rates must describe the actual measurement
process and target population. A representative validation sample would introduce estimation
43.4. Entity, unit and time are part of the variable                                            1123


uncertainty; small sa − fa amplifies that uncertainty; shifts in language or workflow can
invalidate the calibration. Prompt confidence is not a supplied value of sa or fa .
  Without measurement information the problem is one of identification, not just classifier
improvement. The same observed pair (q0 , q1 ) = (1/5, 3/10) also arises under perfect measure-
ment and true risks (p0 , p1 ) = (1/5, 3/10). Thus the observed treatment-label law is compatible
with true effects zero and 1/10. More copies of that law cannot choose between these worlds. A
useful proposal can compare sensitivity ranges, identify an additional validation measurement,
or explicitly target the effect on coded notes. It cannot recover a unique latent effect by
renaming the label.
   This example explains why validation must be stratified by scientifically relevant circum-
stances: treatment arm, language, document source and time can alter error rates. The
eventual sample design must justify how adjudicated observations represent the target popula-
tion. Such expensive validation follows a promising prototype; the proposal can establish the
failure mechanism and candidate remedies using generated laws now.


43.4      Entity, unit and time are part of the variable
Aggregation can change the question while preserving every individual number. Suppose two
households have stipulated household effects of USD 10 and USD −10, but nine and one
accounts respectively. The equal-household mean is zero. Replicating each household’s value
once per account gives
                                    9(10) + 1(−10)
                                                     = 8.
                                         9+1
This is an account-weighted household effect, not proof of an account-level causal mechanism.
Ten rows still refer to two households. The representation must retain entity identifiers,
grouping links, the level of treatment assignment and the target weighting. A precision
calculation cannot treat repeated household records as independent households. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026bw)
   Units require more than a monetary label. Monthly debt service of USD 1,500 and monthly
income of USD 3,000 imply a debt-service ratio of 1/2. Dividing the same monthly obligation
by annual income of USD 36,000 gives 1/24. Converting annual income to monthly income
restores 1/2. The conversion is justified by an explicit common-period definition in this
example. It would not reconcile gross with net income, household with individual income,
a stock with a flow, or average with end-period balances. Those are different constructs or
aggregation rules. Currency conversion would additionally require the rate and valuation date.
   An observation’s event time and usable time also differ. A fact about day one that becomes
available on day five cannot inform a day-three decision. For a derived value computed from
inputs with availability times two and five, availability cannot precede five. A declared time
of four fails even when the input events occurred earlier. Actual production delay may make
availability later still. These examples define a historical information constraint; they do not
prohibit outcomes from becoming observable after the treatment decision.(Causal banking
proposal, 2026bw)
   The local proposal implementation already checks declared measured/latent types, derived
lineage, event-before-availability order, input availability and information at a decision. Its
restricted static-effect projection retains variable identity, role and unit, keeps full declarations
as evidence and refuses a mismatch between outcome and loss units because it has no utility
transformation. These are useful declaration checks. They neither audit individual rows nor
supply a verified extraction, household linkage or currency-conversion service.(Causal banking
1124                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


proposal, 2026bx) The proposed next layer must carry record-specific clocks and provenance
through the conversion, and preserve an explicit unresolved state when availability or identity
cannot be established.


43.5     Missing notes and imputed values need an observation
         model
Even perfect annotation of the notes that exist can mislead. Let Ri = 1 indicate that a note is
observed. In another exact authored law, the true adverse-event risk is 1/5 in both randomized
arms. All control notes are observed. In the offered arm, all adverse events have a note, but
only one quarter of non-events do. Then

                               1 41  2                                       1/5  1
         P (R = 1 | A = 1) =    +   = ,         P (Y = 1 | A = 1, R = 1) =       = .
                               5 54  5                                       2/5  2

Comparing observed notes gives an apparent contrast 1/2 − 1/5 = 3/10 under a true null.
Selection depends jointly on treatment and outcome. Annotation accuracy among observed
notes cannot repair the missing population.(Causal banking proposal, 2026bw)
   Known positive observation probabilities would permit the illustrated weighted population
calculation to recover 1/5; those probabilities are stipulated in this reference, not estimated
from notes with unobserved outcomes. If the relevant selection law is unknown, collecting
representative outcomes or adding justified assumptions is necessary. An assistant can expose
the missingness mechanism, propose a sensitivity analysis and keep a value marked missing.
Filling it with a plausible sentence does not reveal what the customer would have reported.
   This caution is consistent with the primary quantitative-knowledge study reviewed earlier.
Its imputation comparisons report that KNN and random forest methods outperform the
examined LLM alternatives in the stated settings; ambiguous descriptions and units are
discussed as contributors to error. Recognition of familiar datasets also raises contamination
concerns. (Selby et al., 2024) These findings support retaining ordinary imputation and
dictionary baselines. They do not imply that all LLM extraction fails, or that improved
prediction identifies the causal effect when observation depends on an unobserved outcome.
   The ontology should represent missing, not applicable, not collected, redacted, delayed and
model-imputed values distinctly. It should retain the original observation indicator even if
an imputation is created. A changed imputation model creates a new derived measurement
revision; it does not rewrite the original record or convert a latent quantity into an observed
fact. Inference about imputed values needs a separate justification of the imputation and
sampling laws.


43.6     Benchmark evidence and a concrete package decision
OntoURL makes the distinction between understanding, reasoning and generation testable
through fifteen ontology tasks. Its construction uses rule extraction, a reasoner for reasoning
tasks, distractors and quality review. The inspected preprint reports strong performance on
some recognition tasks and weak performance on several structured generation tasks. For
example, its Qwen2.5-72B row gives class-definition and class-relation understanding (U1 and
U2) accuracies of 89.1% and 92.6%, and rule-based and description-logic reasoning (R4 and R5)
accuracies of 75.6% and 68.4%. Class-hierarchy, property-relation and constraint construction
(L2–L4) have Triple-F1 scores of 0.1, 0.0 and 1.0; ontology alignment (L5) has Tuple-F1 of
43.7. A bounded public and generated comparison before bank validation                      1125


21.6, on the table’s percentage scale. These are different tasks and metrics, not a causal-graph
accuracy scale.(Zhang et al., 2025)
   The same version contains a material reporting inconsistency: Table 2 gives L1 BERTScores
around 79–83, while nearby prose says they are typically below 10 and Table 3 uses another
apparent scale. No aggregate comparison should silently reconcile these numbers. The three
PhD-level human participants answer thirty sampled questions per task, while the table’s model
results cover the full dataset. This also limits a simple human-versus-model ranking. Prompting
effects vary across tasks, and the authors acknowledge restricted domains, incomplete task
coverage and an English-only scope. The usable lesson is to evaluate the actual task and
output semantics; the disputed scale and sampling differences require separate resolution.
   OntoLearner offers a more concrete reuse opportunity: a Python framework with task-specific
data and evaluation paths. Its paper reports domain-dependent error patterns and calibration
behavior, and itself argues that F1 alone misses important failure modes.(Giglou et al., 2026)
The inspected revision’s document loader retains document identifiers and extraction methods,
its evaluator dispatches among four task metrics, and its non-taxonomic metric only treats
three declared relation names as symmetric. In particular, the code does not symmetrize every
relation: reversing a causal triple is different from reversing a sameas triple.(Causal banking
proposal, 2026bx)
   There is a specific reason to adapt its evaluation interface before any causal use. Its text-
to-ontology metric concatenates the document identifier and extracted value, then greedily
matches token sets using a Jaccard threshold of 0.8. Take two different document identifiers
and the same nine-word phrase, monthly household income before tax during the reporting
period. The token intersection has size nine and the union eleven, so similarity is 9/11 > 0.8
even though the document link is wrong. This is an exact authored counterexample to
the inspected scoring definition, not an executed upstream-package result. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026bx,bw)
  A causal observation contract should first require exact document identity, then compare
meaning within that document; source-span identity, units and clocks need their own checks.
Lexical similarity can remain a useful diagnostic after those requirements. Similarly, a taxonomy
metric can measure hierarchical agreement without validating an intervention graph, and
deduplication can alter denominators if the intended unit is an observation rather than a
unique term.
  The package decision is to use OntoLearner as a reference and candidate benchmark
component, with an adapter proposed for typed observations and separate semantic scoring.
Direct adoption of the inspected metrics as a causal acceptance gate is rejected. The inspected
downloads do not pin dataset revisions; enabled ontology-import failures can be logged while
processing continues; missing dataset splits can also continue with warnings. A reproducible
evaluation must freeze required dependencies and splits and explicitly fail or mark incomplete
required missing inputs. The base learner’s formatting path does not establish all concrete
subclass behavior. Its MIT license permits relevant code reuse subject to the notice, but does
not establish rights to each external ontology, dataset, model or dependency. Full runtime
qualification remains a separate proposed step. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bx)


43.7     A bounded public and generated comparison before bank
         validation
The proposed prototype takes a document or record, a vocabulary revision, a business question
and its decision clock. It returns candidate observations with the original record and span,
1126                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


entity and aggregation level, construct and operational definition, value domain and unit, event
and availability clocks, transformation lineage, extraction revision, and an explicit evidence
status. Candidate causal roles and relations are separate objects linked to the model in which
they are proposed. Unresolved meaning remains unresolved. An assistant’s numeric confidence
may be stored as a model output, but is not interpreted as a calibrated measurement-error
probability. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bv)
   The initial comparison should contain a deterministic dictionary/schema baseline, an
ontology-assisted mapping alternative, and a constrained language-model extractor if a later
permitted model trial is warranted. The six exact families above supply tractable semantic
reference cases. Additional generated variants should include ambiguous entities, negation,
incompatible definitions, conflicting passages, renamed identifiers and unavailable facts. Positive
cases establish what a valid conversion must retain; negative cases establish the appropriate
refusal or unresolved output. A case with observationally equivalent causal worlds should
reward preserved ambiguity, not a lucky choice of the generator’s hidden world.
   Public ontology benchmarks can test recognition and formal relation tasks; their distributions,
rights and score definitions must be inspected before use. Public treatment text and code
identified by the sociology article are possible comparison materials, whereas the article’s
onsite-only respondent text is not a public dataset. None supplies bank causal truth. Generated
banking records can isolate known unit, clock, grouping and selection mechanisms without
pretending to be authentic bank observations. They also allow newly constructed combinations
that reduce straightforward lookup, although they do not establish absence of contamination
or real-world generalization.
   Before model comparison, freeze the case-generating rules, development and evaluation split,
document families, source revisions, permitted tools, prompts, model identity, budgets and
stopping rule. Keep paraphrases and records from the same entity together when defining
evaluation units. Freeze the measurement mapping before effect evaluation. Report exact
identity, unit and clock preservation; typed relation direction; correctness of acceptance,
refusal and unresolved dispositions; performance on all requests and on accepted outputs; and
effects on the downstream target. Retain malformed responses and missing documents in the
denominator. Human adjudication of meaning, if introduced later, needs an independent label
procedure and disagreements must remain visible.
   Passing all stipulated semantic cases is a bounded engineering criterion, not a guarantee of
future causal validity. The comparison should separately measure whether assistance saves
review effort after retrieval, correction, adjudication, retries and maintenance. A proposed
economic calculation can compare avoided review and error loss with these additional costs; it
cannot assign actual bank savings before the relevant error frequencies, prices and consequences
are measured. The next investment decision is whether a permitted prototype demonstrates
enough benefit to justify expensive representative measurement validation.
   The remaining research is specific. Historical availability and entity matching need evi-
dence for actual records; latent constructs need measurement assumptions and representative
validation; selection and imputation need a defensible observation law; causal sufficiency
needs additional scientific assumptions or information. Better extraction can reduce some
implementation errors, but observationally equivalent measurement mechanisms require new
information or an explicitly broader answer. The proposed program can develop and compare
these remedies now without claiming that an ontology, benchmark score or language model
has settled them.
43.8. Expert evidence, disagreement and causal refusal                                      1127


43.8      Expert evidence, disagreement and causal refusal
A collections manager asks whether a new contact offer will increase repayment within thirty
days. An experienced officer says that offers are allocated to accounts thought most likely
to respond. Another describes assignment as effectively random within the day’s queue.
A retrieved operational note describes the standard queue but predates a change in the
assignment system. An assistant can locate those accounts, identify the disagreement and
make its consequences explicit. Counting two statements in favor of one story does not
resolve which assignment mechanism operated for the accounts under study. This distinction
determines what the proposed product should accept from experts, documents and language
models.
   The useful output is a collection of inspectable claims with their supporting and opposing
evidence, the assumptions still being made, and the decisions that depend on them. A causal
diagram becomes one representation of those claims. The central design problem is how to
retain a plausible alternative when a passage is missing, an expert account conflicts with
a log, or two documents repeat the same original assertion. The literature supplies useful
components for this task, with different evidence boundaries.


43.8.1    What retrieval, elicitation and interactive auditing establish

Zhang et al.’s LACR constructs a skeleton using model background knowledge, retrieved
documents and optionally statistical discovery output, before orienting the retained edges. Its
experiments support a conditional role for retrieval: the ASIA background-only skeleton has
reported F1 of 1, while adding documents lowers it to approximately 0.727; other benchmark
cells improve. The orientation score conditions on true-positive skeleton edges and must not be
presented as whole-graph accuracy. More retrieved text is therefore an input whose relevance
and reliability need evaluation. (Zhang et al., 2024b)
   The algorithm also reveals an uncertainty problem that a superficial reading of its prompts
would miss. Individual responses may be UNKNOWN and contribute zero to an aggregation
score. Nevertheless, the final rule deletes an edge when that score is nonpositive. If every
response is unknown, the edge is deleted. Retaining an unknown token in a prompt is thus
insufficient: the aggregation and graph-conversion stages must preserve its meaning. The
banking proposal should retain an unresolved adjacency when evidence was not located, unless
a separately justified statistical or structural argument excludes it. (Zhang et al., 2024b)
   Soft elicitation offers a different route. Darvariu et al. query both variable orders, average
the corresponding judgments and use the resulting priors to bias graph search. Combined
mutual-information and LLM priors improve selected benchmark comparisons, but LLM-only
priors are not consistently beneficial; mutual information alone is strongest on the specialized
Child benchmark. This motivates sensitivity to the influence assigned to elicited knowledge. It
does not convert the model’s stated probability into a calibrated probability of a banking edge.
Selby et al. provide complementary adverse evidence: some elicited priors conflict with data,
and ordinary nearest-neighbor and random-forest imputations provide strong alternatives.
Their discussion of ambiguous units and recognizable public datasets is directly relevant to
financial data dictionaries and evaluation contamination. (Darvariu et al., 2024; Selby et al.,
2024)
   Interactive auditing can make suggestions easier to inspect. The early Causal Auditor
organizes ratings, proposed confounders and mediators into visual summaries. It reports 103
correct directions out of 110 queries in its selected setting. That is a literature observation
from early cases, with no new evidence about collection offers. Its reported BIC change also
1128                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


needs caution: the text calls a change from -3673.4 to -6270.3 an improvement while the
captions say higher scores are better. Without a reconciled convention and reproduction, the
claimed percentage should not support the product’s value case. In any event, a change in
model fit alone would not validate a causal direction. (Zhang et al., 2023)
   The later CausalChat study reports incorrect-edge counts of 5/18 with BIC feedback, 7/18
with LLM text, and 1/18 with its integrated interface. Six students completed the stages in a
fixed sequence and selected different edges as they proceeded. These observations motivate
usability hypotheses but do not isolate the causal effect of assistance under randomized task
allocation. Expert feedback explicitly identifies missing citations and uncertainty about the
scientific evidence behind the model’s explanations. A persuasive display must therefore
preserve a route back to the primary passage and its limits. (Zhang, 2024)
   Sng et al. show why a metric also needs a precise interpretation. Their hallucination criterion
concerns contradictions across causal-rating prompts. The retrieval experiment supplies a
textual, mocked true graph, and the paper explicitly cautions that reduced contradiction does
not establish accurate causal prediction. The proposed banking evaluation should separately
measure retrieval, statement support, graph admissibility and intervention error; success on
one cannot silently substitute for the others. (Sng et al., 2024)


43.8.2    Formal disagreement handling still depends on its premises

Li and Russo’s 2026 ABAPC-LLM supplies a more explicit combination of semantic and
statistical constraints. It elicits required and forbidden directions, parses them into a schema,
and retains their intersection across five model responses. Conditional-independence results
enter a causal argumentation framework; its solver seeks an admissible extension after relaxing
selected constraints. This makes the provenance and consequences of a conflict more visible
than an unrecorded majority vote. (Li and Russo, 2026)
   The implementation described by the paper is more restrictive than the general idea
of defeasible knowledge. A preliminary skeleton reduction removes edges that are never
reintroduced. Required LLM arrows are discarded when their adjacencies have already been
removed; the remaining required and forbidden directions are enforced as hard constraints. A
stable output therefore establishes consistency relative to the surviving restrictions. It cannot
recover an edge excluded by an erroneous preliminary decision, nor guarantee that a repeatedly
suggested hard constraint is true. The paper acknowledges this tradeoff between tractability
and reconsideration of the hard constraints. (Li and Russo, 2026)
   The study uses 54 generated graphs with five, ten or fifteen nodes and repeated samples
from their stipulated distributions. It reports structural gains over several statistical and
language-model alternatives. The evaluation is useful because it exposes both data constraints
and semantic constraints, but its metadata construction must accompany the result: variable
descriptions are generated with access to the true graph, although prompts request descriptions
that do not explicitly state the links. The same elicited constraint set is reused across data
repetitions for a dataset. Such repetitions assess sampling variation conditional on that set;
they are not independent replications of the full elicitation process. Neutral descriptions,
alternative descriptions and misleading semantic controls remain necessary in a banking
prototype. (Li and Russo, 2026)
   Other qualifications affect the comparison. The consensus procedure can return no con-
straints and sacrifices recall for precision. Runtime tables omit external model latency.
Hidden-confounder extensions and calibrated adaptive weights are proposed future work. The
appendix’s statistical-test description also uses inconsistent observation and degrees-of-freedom
descriptions, so its significance calculations are not independently reconstructed here. The
43.8. Expert evidence, disagreement and causal refusal                                     1129


proposal can adopt the idea of explicit conflict traces while keeping the reported gains as
bounded literature evidence and leaving runtime adoption subject to a separate code, license
and environment review. (Li and Russo, 2026)


43.8.3    Evidence adequacy differs from the truth of an assumption

ARGUS audits whether a paper reports evidence supporting difference-in-differences assump-
tions. It expressly does not adjudicate causal truth. Its bounded retrieval and assessment
stages can locate design flaws that a keyword baseline misses, but retrieval gating trades some
omission detection for abstention. In the five-paper pilot, it abstains on 22 of 55 cells; among
the 33 answered cells, 25 judgments are more severe than the reconciled human labels. The
subsequent calibration is evaluated on the same small pilot and does not establish performance
on unseen papers. (Zhang et al., 2026a)
   This evidence suggests three separate unknown states for the banking workflow. First, the
source may not be accessible or the retrieval procedure may fail. Second, an inspected source
may simply not discuss the needed assumption. Third, it may state an assumption without
evidence that establishes its applicability to the current accounts, dates or intervention. An
operational manual can support the claim that a randomization procedure was prescribed;
assignment logs and an appropriate design are still needed to establish which procedure actually
occurred. A paper’s favorable finding in another population does not settle transport to the
proposed collection policy.
   A claim record should identify the source version and passage, the population, time and
intervention it concerns, what the passage supports, the contrary evidence and the remaining
inference. It should distinguish direct observation, reported procedure, expert assertion,
mathematical implication and hypothesis. Repeated copies should point to a common source
family. An expert should be able to correct the extracted claim without silently replacing
the original text. The system should retain both interpretations when the disagreement is
substantive, then show which graph restrictions and estimands each would permit. These are
proposed product requirements; this synthesis does not claim that an agent already performs
them reliably.


43.8.4    A banking contrast that documents alone cannot identify

Let A indicate receipt of a contact offer at decision time zero, and let Y indicate a repayment
by day thirty. The eligible population is fixed before assignment. Suppose the value of
repayment is USD 100 and each offer costs USD 20. The target is the incremental expected
value per eligible account, 100{E[Y (1)] − E[Y (0)]} − 20. Both the intervention and the cost
are stipulated for this illustrative calculation; there is no observed bank experiment.
  Consider two mechanisms. In the first, A is an independent fair coin and Y = A ⊕ E, where
E is an independent Bernoulli variable with probability 1/4 and ⊕ denotes exclusive-or. In
the second, a latent pre-offer state U is a fair coin, A = U ⊕ E, and Y = U . Both mechanisms
produce exactly the same observed distribution:

                                         Y =0 Y =1
                                     A=0  3/8  1/8 .
                                     A=1  1/8  3/8

  They therefore have the same observed repayment contrast of 1/2. Under an intervention,
however, the first mechanism gives repayment probabilities 1/4 and 3/4, whereas the second
1130                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


gives 1/2 under either action. The causal risk differences are 1/2 and zero, and the net values
are USD 30 and minus USD 20. In the restricted class containing just these two mechanisms,
the effect set is {0, 1/2} and the net-value set is {−20, 30}. These sets are not advertised as
sharp bounds over every possible structural model. (Causal banking proposal, 2026r)
   An assistant that selects the first diagram because several sources call the offer effective
would authorize a different decision from one retaining the latent-selection explanation. More
rows from the same observed law cannot distinguish these two mechanisms. A useful expert
question concerns the actual assignment rule and the information available at assignment,
rather than a generic opinion about whether contact helps. A verified randomized assignment
or defensible additional measurement and assumptions can change the inference. Until then,
retaining both models and refusing a uniquely identified benefit is an informative result.
  This example also supplies an inexpensive formal baseline for a prototype. Enumerate both
candidate mechanisms, verify their observational equality and compare the assistant’s admitted
graph and effect claim with the declared information. The correct behavior under ambiguous
evidence is to retain the distinction between observational fit and intervention value. The
exercise evaluates consistency with stipulated truth, not whether a public document accurately
describes an actual bank.


43.8.5    Why repeated agreement can exaggerate evidence

Suppose an illustrative hypothesis has prior probability 1/2 and one independent source has
a known likelihood ratio of four. The posterior is 4/5. Five copies of the same source still
supply that same evidence. If they are incorrectly multiplied as independent likelihood ratios,
the reported posterior becomes 45 /(1 + 45 ) = 1024/1025. In practice a citation rarely comes
with a defensible numerical likelihood ratio at all. The example demonstrates the need to
track shared provenance rather than prescribing a Bayesian score for every passage. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026r)
   The analogous issue arises with repeated model calls. For a binary judgment with indepen-
dent error probability 1/5, five-call unanimity has probability (4/5)5 + (1/5)5 = 41/125; the
probability of an incorrect answer conditional on unanimity is 1/1025. Now impose perfectly
shared errors with the same marginal error probability. Every call agrees, and the conditional
error remains 1/5. These exact constructed laws show that marginal reliability and agreement
alone do not determine the value of consensus. They do not estimate the dependence or
accuracy of any current model. (Causal banking proposal, 2026r)
   The prototype should accordingly compare individual judgment, consensus, source-family
aggregation and a human-led baseline. It should vary misleading shared evidence, missing
evidence and contradictory passages, while retaining all requests in the denominator. Condi-
tional correctness among returned claims must appear beside availability, false assertions of no
relationship and incorrect refusals. Source-family or task-family dependence also matters for
uncertainty: many paraphrases of one mechanism do not provide the same evidence as many
independent mechanisms.


43.8.6    What a package can contribute, and what must be repaired

The inspected PyWhyLLM revision of 6 January 2026 provides concrete suggestion and retrieval
components under a root MIT notice. Its packaging uses a dynamic version placeholder and
a substantial model, embedding and retrieval dependency stack; that declaration is not a
qualified environment. The selected identification wrapper delegates backdoor suggestions to a
model-based confounder suggester. Its frontdoor method is a placeholder, while a different
43.9. Imperfect advice, joint graph evidence and retention guarantees                        1131


simple class does generate frontdoor names through a prompt. Neither a method name nor a
generated list establishes that a graphical identification theorem has been applied. (PyWhy
Community, 2026)
   The role-based confounder path initializes a treatment-to-outcome edge, asks model personas
for candidate confounders and accumulates counts. Such counts represent agreement across
prompts, with no calibrated probability or source independence attached. Some selected calls
retry a missing-key error without a finite bound in the inspected loop. These findings support
explicit caller budgets and preservation of failure; they are static-source findings, not observed
failures of an executed service. (PyWhy Community, 2026)
   The augmented pairwise path adds a second boundary. It downloads a knowledge resource at
construction, finds a matching pair through lexical and embedding retrieval, and concatenates
selected source sentences into the retrieval context. That concatenation does not carry their
document identity into a structured claim record. When no matching pair is found, it falls back
to model knowledge. The answer parser accepts only the two directions or neither; neither is
not an explicit insufficient-evidence state. The helper also creates its own model client instead
of consistently using the wrapper’s supplied model. These behaviors make direct adoption
inappropriate for the proposed evidence contract. (PyWhy Community, 2026)
  A permissible first integration would be a small, optional elicitation component whose
output remains a proposal for review. It needs explicit model configuration, pre-acquired
versioned source inputs, retained passage identities, bounded calls and retries, and distinct
supported, contradicted, unknown and unavailable outcomes. Graph conversion must keep
negative and unresolved judgments as records, validate clocks and direction restrictions, and
run a separately specified identification procedure. Dataset licenses, transitive dependencies,
provider behavior and the remaining import paths require review before the component is
enabled. The current review enables no adapter.
   The alternatives remain substantive. A manual evidence table with an explicit diagram
may be sufficient for a small proposal. A deterministic retrieval and graph-checking system
can expose evidence without delegating judgment. Soft priors preserve alternative graphs
but require sensitivity to their strength. Argumentation provides explicit conflict traces but
requires a policy for hard and defeasible restrictions. An unqualified hard-constraint pipeline
can produce confident answers efficiently by excluding the correct model.
   The known next step is therefore a public/generated-data prototype comparing these
workflows under declared evidence conditions. It should measure total retrieval and model
cost, expert correction time, failed requests and the effect of evidence handling on the banking
decision. The unresolved research concerns calibration across new domains, dependence among
sources and models, and useful uncertainty when graph and observation assumptions remain
disputed. The truth of an undocumented historical assignment cannot be manufactured by
a better prompt. That boundary is part of the proposed product’s behavior, while bank
experiments and institutional acceptance remain later work.


43.9      Imperfect advice, joint graph evidence and retention guar-
          antees
A banking analyst may know that a diagram remains ambiguous while still having useful
information about the disputed arrows. An account officer can describe which event usually
precedes another; a procedure can explain a permitted action; a language model can suggest
which interpretation to investigate. The difficult question is how much graph uncertainty
this advice can remove without concealing its mistakes. Requiring an adviser to be infallible
1132                                                                  Causal analysis for a universal bank


discards potentially useful information. Treating each confident answer as a causal fact discards
potentially correct graphs. A proposal needs an explicit rule between these extremes, together
with a statement of the probability that the rule actually controls.
   Long and colleagues formulate this problem using language models as imperfect experts.
Their 2023 first version starts from the true Markov equivalence class and uses metadata-based
judgments to orient its ambiguous edges. A prior over legal graphs and an adviser-error
likelihood produce joint posterior probabilities; greedy choices trade a smaller class against
the modeled risk of excluding its true member. This is a useful methodological alternative to
hard acceptance of an elicited diagram. The known starting class and the specified adviser
model are substantive premises, however, rather than consequences of a natural-language
interface.(Long et al., 2023)


43.9.1    The starting class and the experiment that supplies advice

Let G be a directed acyclic graph, and let M0 be a finite class of graphs with the same skeleton
and unshielded colliders. For an ambiguous pair j, write Oj (G) ∈ {0, 1} for its orientation in
G and Ej for the adviser’s proposed orientation. These binary judgments concern an existing
adjacency; they do not decide whether the two variables are the right measurements, whether
an edge is absent, or whether a hidden common cause should replace it. In particular, the
method’s pair question does not provide a general test of the bank’s variable ontology or
latent-variable assumptions.
   Under a uniform prior on M0 and a conditionally independent adviser with constant error
ϵ, the likelihood and posterior are

of each chosen orientation. It does not establish that its greedy rule solves every global
minimum-cardinality retention problem. More fundamentally, the word “probability” in (43.2)
needs its probability model. A posterior over graphs is useful conditional uncertainty; it is not
automatically a confidence statement for every fixed bank graph and every data-dependent
starting class.
