Neither a probability distribution over the two cases nor a sampling confidence level has been
supplied. The midpoint is 10, which is not even a member of this set. Reporting an expected
gain of 10, or a 95% chance of benefit, introduces information that the result object does not
contain. The convex hull [−40, 60] can be displayed as an explicitly labelled outer envelope,
but it also contains values absent from the original object. Under a stipulated worst-case
criterion relative to doing nothing, the minimum gain is negative; under a probability-weighted
criterion, further weights are needed. A useful report explains this decision ambiguity and
the information that would resolve it. The exact calculation is a project reference, not a bank
estimate. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bl)


49.2     Evidence-grounded auditing: useful questions and unfa-
         vorable answers
ARGUS studies whether reported evidence supports identification assumptions in climate-
policy evaluations. Its construct is reported-evidence adequacy, not causal validity. An auditor
can locate an assignment description or an overlap diagnostic without certifying the actual
assignment mechanism or the unobserved outcomes. In its eleven injected-flaw cases, the paper
reports detection rates of .182 for a keyword method, .727 for a two-stage pipeline, .818 for
a single-pass variant and 1.000 for a per-dimension variant, with zero synthetic false alarms
in those headline rows. These are small, constructed cases. Changes in evidence access and
pipeline structure prevent attributing the entire difference to one judging component. (Zhang
et al., 2026a)
   The same paper’s reconciled five-paper pilot is less reassuring. Of 55 assumption cells, the
human labels comprise seven low, forty-six medium and two high cases. ARGUS abstains on
22; among the 33 answered cells, 25 judgments are too severe. Both annotators find relevant
reported evidence in 19 of the 22 abstained cells, and at least one finds it in 21. An abstention
is consequently not interchangeable with a substantive high-risk finding. A rule using retrieval
quality and evidence status increases agreement on answered cells from 8/33 to 25/33 in the
same pilot. Always predicting medium gives 26/33 on that selected subset. Weighted kappa
increases from .08 to .23, with an interval including zero. The alternative abstention rule
reduces answered coverage from 33/55 to 13/55. The improvement is in-sample and does not
qualify future bank monitoring.
   These findings imply a practical remedy. A report should distinguish evidence found and
supportive, evidence found and adverse, inadequate retrieval, conflicting evidence, and an
assumption requiring external facts. Each judgment needs the inspected passage, its source
version, the claim being assessed and the reason for the disposition. Missing retrieval should
trigger a bounded retrieval or human-review route. It should not increase a scientific risk score
by an undocumented convention. Calibration requires held-out examples, a declared labeling
protocol and a reported coverage–error tradeoff.
   The observational causal inference workflow of Chou and colleagues offers a different form of
assistance: a human principal, actor and critic coordinate analysis notebooks, diagnostics and
versioned reports. The authors report 192 satisfactory and 39 unsatisfactory critic judgments
across 231 ACIC datasets. Their smaller scaffolding comparison is favorable, but a disguised
LaLonde evaluation using twenty bootstrap replications has median absolute percentage errors
of 52% for PSID and 19% for CPS; the critic declines the PSID result in all but one replication.
These results motivate both assistance and refusal. They do not make a critic’s acceptance a
new confidence guarantee. Moreover, the inspected notebook’s uniform average after propensity
trimming targets the retained population; calling it ATO does not make it the conventional
49.3. What adjacent monitoring and repair literature contributes                              1297


overlap-weighted estimand. A report must bind the actual population and weighting, even
when a package’s label is familiar. (Chou et al., 2026; oci-agent contributors, 2026)
   For discovery, Causal Discovery in the Era of Agents separates agent suggestions, user
decisions, algorithm settings and graph output. Its proposed benchmarks for method selection,
diagnosis and interpretation remain an evaluation agenda. A reporting assistant should preserve
CPDAG or PAG ambiguity and the restrictions under which an effect query is answered.
The medical causal-copilot paper likewise proposes assistance with target specification and
study design while acknowledging contamination and inadequate study-design benchmarks.
Its discussion of missed or false post-market signals motivates evaluation; it does not supply a
validated alarm procedure. These are substantive design contributions with different evidential
status from completed causal-effect studies. (Zheng, 2026; Alaa et al., 2024)


49.3      What adjacent monitoring and repair literature con-
          tributes
CausalPulse coordinates manufacturing diagnostics through agents, domain rules and tools,
including an MCP utility layer. Its inspected evaluation distinguishes workflow completion
from root-cause attribution: PSE planning and tool-use success are reported at 98.75%, while
root-cause Hits@1 is .44 and F1 is .39. The local hardware and workflow timings are author-
reported manufacturing evidence. A bank report should borrow the separation of stages and
their denominators. Reusing a cached graph also requires its contextual applicability to be
checked; cache availability alone does not settle that question. (Shyalika et al., 2026)
   FlowFixer makes workflow repair more concrete. It converts execution traces to symbolic
descriptions, infers behavioral assertions, attributes failures, proposes edits and verifies candi-
dates. The evaluated collection combines 307 AgentFail logs with 136 n8n failure cases. The
reported repair success is 71.3%, compared with 59.4% for ReCreat, an absolute difference of
11.9 percentage points. Failure-attribution accuracy is 84.4%; the reported 87.9% root-cause
accuracy is conditional on correct failure attribution. These percentages do not share a denom-
inator. Repairs are repeated three times per case and assessed through dynamic verification
on the original inputs. Passing those inputs does not establish generalization to an unseen
incident or preservation of a causal estimand. (Ma et al., 2026a)
   The proposed reuse is methodological: make dependencies explicit, separate symptoms
from an attributed cause, and check an edit against an executable contract. An inferred
assertion that an itinerary respects a budget is not the same kind of statement as sequential
exchangeability. FlowFixer’s pre-execution filter reports 99.7% precision and 84.6% recall for
invalid workflows; some model and tool failures still appear only at execution. For a causal
report, a repair should preserve the frozen target, inputs and uncertainty type, then be tested
on separate adverse cases. Changing the target or deleting failures to obtain a successful
narrative is a scientific change requiring a new analysis. The paper justifies studying this
mechanism; its distribution, dependency rights and actual integration remain to be reviewed.
   PSEBench supplies an adjacent benchmark construction. Human-reviewed clause cards
factor policy conditions, facts, evidence anchors and constraints, then generate complete,
missing-information and uncertain cases. The cutoff-compatible second version contains 3,455,
1,362 and 257 cases in these groups. The authors compare fifteen models and report separate
verdict, evidence-citation, missing-information and uncertainty metrics. For example, the
paper reports 90.2% verdict accuracy and 12.8% uncertainty-detection F1 for its GPT-5
configuration. This is a reported configuration result, not a current model recommendation or
our replication. Its meaning is that classification success can coexist with a large weakness in
1298                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


identifying cases that should remain unresolved. (Han et al., 2026)
   The benchmark reports expert review of ninety generated cases: agreement on 28/30
complete verdicts, 29/30 missing-case indeterminacies and 30/30 uncertain-case ambiguities.
That supports a bounded quality check, not universal correctness of generated labels. The
narratives are synthetic, the Ask tool idealizes retrieval, and the rules are tied to Minnesota’s
framework. For banking, the transferable idea is to author explicit result-and-evidence cards
with separately known failure dispositions. Medical reportability labels should not be imported
as causal truth. Generated cases can test faithful reporting now, while realistic retrieval failures
and different institutional meanings need distinct later evidence.
   The NetOps/AIOps survey adds an operational perspective. Its inspected preprint distin-
guishes freshness and provenance of logs, metrics, traces and change records, and separates
static questions, trace replay, sandbox execution, live testbeds and canary evidence. It rec-
ommends scoring tool costs, abstention, latency, drift and trace quality separately, with
LLM judging as an auxiliary signal. These are helpful contract categories. Proposed service
invariants written using probabilities do not themselves provide calibrated probability models.
The retrieved June preprint is not assumed identical to the journal edition identified in the
original search metadata. (Bilal et al., 2026)
   An economic illustration supplies a caution closer to the application domain. Kim presents
ChatGPT-generated growth and stock-market diagrams and explicitly says that the backdoor
response needs confirmation and that the generated figures should not all be believed correct.
The paper can motivate checking the distinction between a prediction and an intervention
query. It cannot support a claim of verified economic forecasts or calibrated causal alarms. This
negative interpretation is more informative than counting every paper with causal terminology
as affirmative evidence. (Kim, 2026)


49.4      The report object and the actual implementation gap
The proposed report has three linked layers. Its scientific layer binds the target, population,
clocks, graph or graph class, assumptions and exact result type. Its evidence layer binds
the source data, code, environment, diagnostics, source passages and review dispositions.
Its decision layer states the monetary conversion, loss criterion, alternatives and unresolved
obligations. A sentence asserting a number must point to a specific field or a separately
checked derivation. A sentence asserting a premise must identify whether it is stipulated,
supported, contradicted or unknown. These links distinguish faithful transcription from
scientific endorsement. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bk)
   The current local report implementation provides a narrower foundation. It accepts one to
one hundred distinct authorized canonical-response artifacts, checks their schema, binds input
hashes and execution identity, and verifies a completed checkpoint prefix before resumption. Its
summaries retain declared status, disposition, context hash, qualification and source reference.
The verification flag explicitly says that the check is schema-only and is neither causal nor
external review. The inspected worker does not yet copy the full numerical result into a
developed causal narrative or implement an assumption-monitoring service. The agent workflow
also preserves unresolved obligations and denies authorization for a bank action. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026bm,j,t)
   OCI’s pinned notebook runner checks interpreter identity and serializes per-estimand
estimates, intervals and diagnostics. It also accepts a selected notebook and uses an unbounded
notebook timeout. Its artifact concepts can inform the proposed report boundary, but execution
requires separate resource and authority limits. The inspected CausalAgent output parser
49.5. Denominators and uncertainty after a critic selects reports                         1299


extracts text between the first and last braces and returns an empty dictionary on a JSON
decoding error. A consumer must preserve that condition as a typed parse failure; an empty
object must not silently become successful analysis. These are static source observations, with
no new upstream execution. (oci-agent contributors, 2026; CausalAgent contributors, 2026;
Causal banking proposal, 2026bm)
   The proposed CLI and MCP operations should use the same scientific object as the library.
A report request selects immutable result references, an audience, a template revision and
a bounded presentation budget. It does not supply a replacement estimate. The response
includes generated prose, checked claim links, unresolved statements and a reference to
deterministic rendering. A change-review request supplies a versioned event and returns
affected dependencies, reasons and proposed follow-up work. It does not mutate old results.
Both operations distinguish unsupported input, retrieval failure, invalid result structure,
unresolved science and completed presentation. The new fields and monitor remain a proposed
extension; the existing schema-only report is not retroactively described as implementing them.


49.5      Denominators and uncertainty after a critic selects reports
Suppose a generated evaluation contains one hundred requests. Sixty produce computed
answers, of which forty-eight are correct; twenty are ambiguous, ten are unsupported and
ten fail retrieval. Conditional computed-answer accuracy is 48/60 = .80, whereas correct
computed output per submitted request is 48/100 = .48. Neither fraction determines whether
the ambiguous or unsupported dispositions were appropriate. Those require independent
case-level labels, and correct refusals can be useful outcomes. A report should show the
full partition, the scientific status within each group and the corresponding cost. Dropping
an expensive failure changes both the quality and economic comparison. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026bl)
   Selection also changes uncertainty. Let C be the event that an estimated interval covers the
true effect and A the event that a critic accepts the report. Then
                                                   Pr(C ∩ A)
                                     Pr(C | A) =             .
                                                     Pr(A)

Marginal coverage Pr(C) = .95 supplies no equality between this conditional probability and
.95. In an exact constructed law with one hundred equiprobable cases, ninety-five intervals
cover. Let acceptance select five covering and five noncovering cases. Acceptance is 10% and
coverage among accepted cases is 5/10 = .50. The example does not assert that a particular
critic behaves this way. It disproves an unjustified inference.
   A possible remedy is to qualify the complete selection-and-estimation rule, including every
refusal, under a declared joint experiment. Another is to design an appropriate conditional
inference procedure and establish its assumptions. An independent acceptance event would
preserve marginal coverage, but the required independence often fails when a critic reads the
same data, intervals and diagnostics. Adding a second agent, or training the critic elsewhere,
does not establish independence of the acceptance event in the current analysis.


49.6      Monitoring requires a statistical design and an owner
A service can monitor whether an artifact hash changed, whether a response arrived, whether
a measured distribution shifted, or whether a causal claim remains applicable. These are
different events. The first two admit direct engineering checks. Distributional change can
1300                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


sometimes be tested under a specified sampling law. Continued causal applicability depends
also on assignment, measurement, support and target population. The catalog example’s
observationally equivalent worlds demonstrate why an unchanged observed distribution need
not settle an intervention contrast. Repeated queries to the same observations cannot remove
that ambiguity. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bf)
  Even a valid individual test needs a repeated-use design. For twelve independent tests under
their nulls, each with false-alarm probability .05,

                      Pr(at least one false alarm) = 1 − .9512 ≃ .459640.

Independence is required for this exact product formula. A simple alternative allocates the
total budget through
                                             T
                                 .05         X                  T
                         αt =          ,           αt = .05        < .05.
                              t(t + 1)       t=1
                                                              T +1

If each test has a valid null rejection probability bounded by its allocated αt , a union bound
controls the probability of any false rejection; independence is unnecessary for that bound.
For adaptive choice of a test or population, validity must survive that choice, for example
through an appropriate conditional guarantee. Four equally budgeted monitor families would
each receive .0125, rather than independently spending the full .05. The allocation, tested
family, restart policy and observation clock must be explicit. An LLM’s severity label is not a
p-value. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bl)
   This spending construction is a transparent reference, not a recommended high-power
monitor for every dependent banking series. Late thresholds can be stringent, repeated looks
can reuse dependent observations, and weak support can make effects uninformative before
any test rejects. A proposed monitor must state its null, unit, dependence assumptions, delay,
false-alarm criterion, detectable changes and response policy. A scientific owner decides whether
the signal warrants a new design or narrower claim; the data owner explains availability and
assignment changes; the operator owns delivery and recovery. The agent may summarize
signals and prepare the review. No bank-action authority follows from its text.


49.7     Version changes should invalidate the affected argument
Let a dependency graph connect clocks and assignment to a design, the design and cohort
to an estimate, the estimate and prices to economics, and the estimate and economics to the
report. This graph describes provenance and applicability, not causal relationships between
customers. A change in price reopens economics and the report while preserving the stored
statistical estimate. A change in the availability clock reopens the design, estimate, economics
and report. A change to an unrelated cohort reopens its own estimate without invalidating
this entire analysis. The exact reachability example reproduces all three behaviors. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026bl)
   Reachability identifies review obligations, not a verdict that every descendant is wrong. A
source correction may be editorial; an assignment correction may be decisive. Each change
carries its effective time, observation time, affected field, old and new identity, evidence and
responsible reviewer. Historical artifacts stay immutable. A separate applicability state records
current, review-required, superseded, or unknown, with a reason. Revalidation creates a new
linked decision. This prevents an old report from being silently rewritten while also preventing
a stable byte hash from being mistaken for current scientific validity.
49.8. A public and generated prototype can settle the next engineering questions             1301


49.8      A public and generated prototype can settle the next
          engineering questions
The immediate comparison can use frozen public source passages and authored result cards.
Begin with a deterministic renderer that carries all numbers, units, result types and dispositions
exactly. Add a constrained language renderer that may explain those facts, and then an optional
retrieval assistant. The prototype case families should include the finite set and selection
examples above; a conflicting citation; an absent passage; a late feature; a revised price;
an unchanged observed law with unresolved causal meaning; malformed output; a stale
dependency; and an appropriate refusal. Withholding a necessary fact differs from stipulating
that two possibilities remain observationally indistinguishable. (Causal banking proposal,
2026bk)
  Before any optional live-model experiment, freeze the generator, truth fields, source snapshots,
split unit, budgets, prompts, model revision and evaluation rules. Keep related variants on
the same side of a split so that near-duplicate cards do not masquerade as new evidence.
Verify quantitative and structural statements deterministically. Independently review scientific
meaning and explanation quality, with an adjudication rule for disagreement. Report coverage,
wrong numbers or units, lost ambiguity, unsupported claims, correct and incorrect refusals,
provenance defects, delay and full cost. Generation, retrieval, human review, retries, storage
and maintenance belong in that cost. A readability gain is useful only alongside an explicitly
acceptable semantic error profile.
  The exact authored cases have been executed; this comparative model experiment has
not. A first finite conformance gate requires every declared number, unit, result type and
mandatory limitation to survive the selected reference cases. Passing establishes those cases
only. Generalization and alarm calibration require fresh evaluations under their declared laws.
Rights and complete dependency review precede adoption of adjacent packages. A manual
report remains an alternative when automation saves too little review effort.
   The bounded survey leaves three candidate areas outside its inspected evidence: a broad
safety review, marketing context graphs, and traceable agents in bioinformatics. Their technical
claims require original-text and version review. The proposed public and generated comparison
can nevertheless proceed. It can establish faithful handling of declared evidence and known
cases; bank assignment truth, general causal identification, selective calibration and useful
institutional monitoring remain separate questions. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bk)
Chapter 50

Evaluating causal assistance without
changing the question

50.1     The benchmark unit is a causal problem
An agent can produce a plausible report, execute valid code and still answer the wrong causal
question. Evaluation must follow the entire chain from business meaning through assumptions
and identification to uncertainty, availability and decision loss. A benchmark of text fluency,
graph edit distance or successful tool calls measures only part of that chain.
   CLadder demonstrates the value of formal questions with varied verbalizations, including
commonsense and deliberately unfamiliar or conflicting stories. The inspected paper also
identifies language-to-formal-tool formulation as a continuing challenge. Its historical binary-
answer accuracy is evidence about those tasks and models; it is not a measurement of effect
coverage, decision loss or banking readiness.Jin et al. (2023)
  CausalDS expands the evaluation object to narrated synthetic mechanisms, data and a
separate observation model. Its inspected results show why symbolic success, uncertainty
quality, abstention and cost should be reported separately. Its author-reported exam and
repeated runs are useful design evidence, not model evaluations conducted in this project. A
generated world with known truth also remains different from authentic bank data whose
semantic and assignment mechanisms must be established externally. Leban and Sun (2026)
  The proposed experimental unit is therefore an independently generated or independently
adjudicated causal mechanism and question. Several phrasings, label conditions or stochastic
model calls can be nested within that unit. They do not create new independent worlds.
Repeating one problem fifty times can measure response variation for that problem; it does
not provide fifty independent demonstrations of general causal competence.


50.2     Matched information and meaningful alternatives
The prospective design compares a fixed numerical workflow, a language-only workflow, retrieval
assistance, a hybrid of numerical tools and typed model proposals, and structured expert
workflows with and without assistance. Each arm needs a declared information budget. If one
receives the true causal graph and another must discover it, their effect-estimation scores do
not isolate the value of language assistance. If retrieval adds a valid institutional fact, that
information gain should be distinguished from a better inference algorithm.
  Eight strata are proposed: independent sufficient DAGs; latent-variable graph classes;

                                             1302
50.3. A target error can survive perfect arithmetic                                          1303


temporal data with known clocks; treatment-confounder feedback; panel or quasi-experimental
assignment; proxies, linkage and selection; weak or nonidentifying effects; and ambiguous
business targets or monetary loss. Label and evidence conditions cross ordinary descriptions,
unfamiliar labels, misleading or irrelevant material, and conflict between numerical evidence
and text. These strata test different failure mechanisms rather than treating all causal questions
as interchangeable.
   The current planning allocation is 400 mechanisms, with 50 per stratum and three stochastic
repetitions nested within each mechanism. This is an allocation for developing the design,
not a frozen final sample size or a power calculation. For orientation, the worst-case normal
approximation
    p           for one Bernoulli proportion at 400 independent observations has half-width
1.96 0.25/400, approximately 0.049. Paired differences, stratified outcomes and rare severe
errors require their own precision design. A development pilot would inform that design and
must be excluded from the final test.
  Both natural-workflow and matched-budget comparisons can be useful. The first asks what
an analyst can achieve with a realistic workflow, including review. The second asks what
changes when information or computation is controlled. Neither should hide extra expert time,
repeated retrieval or retry costs. The comparison must state which question it answers.


50.3      A target error can survive perfect arithmetic
An exact project IV construction illustrates a benchmark-label hazard. Let a randomized
binary instrument Z affect treatment for half the population, the compliers; the other half
never receives treatment. Set Y (0) = 0 for everyone, Y (1) = 1 for compliers and Y (1) = 3 for
never-takers. Treatment equals Z for compliers and zero otherwise. Randomization, exclusion
and monotonicity hold in this construction.
   The observed outcome difference across instrument values is 0.5 and the treatment-probability
difference is 0.5, so the Wald ratio is one. The population ATE is two. Changing the never-
takers’ unobserved treated outcome changes the population ATE without changing the observed
law. A scorer that calls the unrestricted Wald ratio the population ATE would reward a target
substitution. This is a finite counterexample supporting review of generator assumptions, not
a claim that every IV question in a named benchmark uses this construction.
   The same concern applies to trimming, overlap weighting and selected populations. A
language answer can reproduce the right formula for a different target. Evaluation should
therefore compare the population, measure, action, comparator, horizon and units before
comparing the numeric answer. Critical semantic errors deserve their own count, even when a
numeric discrepancy happens to be small in the test mechanism.


50.4      Graphs, sets and refusals need separate scores
Graph evaluation should compare adjacency and endpoint statements against the appropriate
identifiable class. A justified circle or undirected edge should not be penalized merely because
a simulator internally selected one fully directed graph. Orientation informativeness can
be reported alongside validity. This makes a method that preserves genuine ambiguity
distinguishable from one that returns little information and from one that confidently overorients
the graph.
  Identification outcomes also need separate labels. Scientific nonidentification, unsupported
implementation, malformed output, explicit abstention, timeout and missing input are not the
1304                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


same event. A well-designed agent can correctly identify a missing premise without successfully
computing an effect. A backend can be unable to implement a valid functional. Combining
these into one “incorrect” or “no answer” category would obscure the remedy.
   For identified scalar targets, bias and error can be meaningful. For reported sets, evaluate
coverage, topology, finite availability and size. Whole-line answers can have high coverage and
little decision value. A method that returns short intervals on a selected easy subset needs an
all-request availability denominator. Unbounded and disconnected sets must remain in the
evaluation rather than being replaced by finite plotting limits.
  For an eligible finite interval [l, u], one prospective score at nominal level 1 − α is
                                   2                  2
                       (u − l) +     (l − θ)1{θ < l} + (θ − u)1{θ > u}.
                                   α                  α
The formula balances length with penalties for missing the target. It is not an instruction to
compress a union of intervals into one interval. For unions, coverage and total Lebesgue length
can be reported while retaining infinite lengths. Raw losses should not be capped simply to
make a plot or ranking convenient. The eligible target type must be stated before the score is
selected.


50.5     Contamination, adaptation and selective reporting
An exposed demonstration cannot become a held-out evaluation merely because its variables
are renamed. The local problem fixtures and replay examples have already been used to
develop and debug the prototype. They can continue to test conformance, but they cannot
provide independent estimates of a language model’s causal accuracy.
   The final design needs a frozen development/test split, mechanism identities, prompts,
model/provider revisions, retrieval corpus and ranking rules, numerical baselines, stopping
rules and analysis code. Mechanism families should be separated where family reuse would
reveal the answer. Label novelty and mechanism novelty should be varied independently. An
unfamiliar name attached to a memorized mechanism is not the same test as an unfamiliar
mechanism.
   Test outcomes cannot be used to tune prompt templates, choose the best retriever, strengthen
selected priors or discard difficult cells while retaining a final-test interpretation. A changed
method requires a new reviewed evaluation revision. Failed and unavailable requests remain in
the record. Reporting only the critic-approved subset would confound answer quality with
selection by the critic.
   The inspected OCI paper provides a useful refusal example: its critic declines many
replications when overlap is poor. That can be preferable to an unsupported estimate, but it
makes the denominator essential. The reported successful answers, refused requests, review
effort and remaining target population must all be visible. The external results are author
reports, not a validation of this project’s critic. Chou et al. (2026)


50.6     Decision value and cost
The ultimate question is whether assistance improves feasible decisions at an acceptable total
cost. In a known synthetic mechanism, a policy’s expected loss can be calculated under the
mechanism and compared with the chosen baseline. In a bank, the feasible policy, valuation
model, risk limits, operating costs and outcome truth need authentic inputs. Synthetic decision
loss does not establish institutional return on investment.
50.7. The probability of passing a coverage screen                                            1305


  The prospective cost record includes model calls, input/output/cache tokens, retrieval,
numerical CPU time, wall time, memory, retries and human review and rework. Actual dated
prices are needed to turn these quantities into a currency total. Unknown prices remain
missing; zero live calls in an offline prototype do not imply a free live workflow. A fast answer
that requires substantial correction can have a worse total cost than a slower transparent
analysis.
   No final experiment has been registered or run here. Five prerequisite classes remain: an
exact live backend and custody terms; actual prices and a bounded budget; independent
held-out mechanisms and original benchmark bytes; named business/diagram adjudicators and
a rubric; and qualified numerical baselines. These are missing program inputs. No credentials
were read and no provider endpoint was probed to infer that a service is unavailable. The
design provides a route to evaluation once those inputs are supplied; it provides no current
empirical model-performance claim.


50.7      The probability of passing a coverage screen
Evaluating an agent that recommends inferential procedures requires a clear distinction between
nominal coverage, an argument for coverage and an empirical qualification rule. Suppose a
fixed procedure is tested in n independently generated replications of a declared mechanism.
Let K count requests whose reported sets cover the truth; unavailable or failed requests remain
in the declared denominator. If the per-request coverage is p, then under these simulation
assumptions K has a binomial law.
  For a simultaneous family of m cells and total error budget α, consider the one-sided exact
lower bound
                 L(K, n) = BetaQuantile(α/m; K, n − K + 1),         K > 0,
with L(0, n) = 0. A rule requiring L ≥ 0.95 certifies a minimum in this specific finite experiment.
At true p = 0.95, its probability of passing one cell is at most α/m. This is how a lower-bound
certification test behaves at its boundary, not evidence that the procedure’s true coverage is
zero.
  Before qualification, a designer can compute the smallest integer k∗ that passes and the
operating characteristic
                                  Pr(pass) = Pr(K ≥ k∗ ).
                                      p              p

The project calculation evaluates this exactly for several replication counts, family sizes and
values of p, and independently checks the equivalent binomial-tail threshold. It draws no
random data and does not test a causal estimator. Its purpose is to make the qualification
design interpretable. Causal banking research project (2026bk)
   Increasing replications can distinguish a genuine coverage margin above 95% more sharply.
It cannot make a level-controlled test have high power at the exact boundary. This does
not justify lowering the required minimum after seeing results. The analyst must state what
guarantee is theoretically justified, what empirical screen is being applied and what its power
is. A method may have a plausible asymptotic argument while failing this finite screen; that
should be reported as a qualification shortfall rather than silently recoded as success.
   An agent could otherwise exploit this distinction in two bad ways. It might declare a method
invalid merely because a low-powered boundary screen failed, or widen intervals until they
pass while ignoring decision usefulness. The evaluation should penalize both. Coverage, finite
availability and useful width are separate dimensions. A whole-line interval covers every finite
1306                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


truth but may support no action. Bank width and loss thresholds require actual decision
owners; synthetic thresholds should remain labeled as such.


50.8      A live comparison needs independent mechanisms and
          complete costs
An offline controller can demonstrate request validation, abstention, tool dispatch and preser-
vation of graph/set semantics. It cannot measure how a live model translates a new banking
problem, how often retrieval changes its graph, or what the workflow costs. Zero model calls
means those empirical quantities are unmeasured; it does not mean accuracy is zero or costs
are free.
  A credible live comparison binds the exact backend/revision and inference settings, data-
custody arrangement, actual prices and approved budget, independent held-out mechanisms
or benchmark bytes, adjudicators and rubric, and qualified numerical baselines. The final
prompts, retrieval corpus, tools, retry rules, token/time limits and numerical tolerances should
be frozen before the first final request. Development cases already exposed to the agent cannot
become held-out by receiving different filenames.
  Compare data-only, model-only, retrieval-assisted, hybrid and expert-assisted workflows
under matched information and budgets. A hybrid receives additional information when it
uses a valid domain exclusion; its improvement should not be attributed solely to reasoning.
Conversely, a data-only baseline should not be asked to identify an effect that the observed law
cannot identify. The equal-law counterexamples in Section 44.6 make this boundary testable.
   Metrics should include whether the translated intervention/population is valid, whether
graph output respects equivalence and latent ambiguity, whether the downstream effect is
scientifically supported, and whether abstention occurs for the right reason. Repeated-run
disagreement is relevant even when the average score is favorable. Fluent explanations and
exact string matches to one graph are inadequate substitutes for these criteria.
  Complete costs include unsuccessful calls, retries, retrieval, tool computation, human
review and operating overhead. If an agent frequently produces a request that needs manual
correction, its low token bill can conceal high workflow cost. Decision value should be evaluated
on feasible actions and held-out outcomes or an explicitly justified reference, with uncertainty.
A stipulated arithmetic example explains the accounting but cannot establish provider pricing,
model calibration or bank ROI.


50.9      Testing semantic failures before the expensive study
Several low-cost deterministic cases can be exercised before live qualification. A y0 nonidentifi-
cation response must not become a zero effect. A continuous density must not be interpreted as
a binary probability. A grouped allocation contrast must not become an individual direct effect.
A statsmodels internal covariance option must not be reported as final clustered uncertainty
when the inspected implementation supplies HC0.y0 project (2026b); CausalGPS project
(2026b); inferference project (2026); statsmodels project (2026b)
   These cases test the proposed interface and evaluation rubric. They are useful development
evidence, and their exposure should be recorded. Fresh independent mechanisms are still
necessary to evaluate generalization. Keeping those roles separate allows an agentic workflow
to improve through development while retaining a meaningful final assessment.

50.9.1     Evaluate the claim behind the benchmark score

CausalEval places diverse language tasks in one comparative survey, including commonsense
cause selection, correlation-to-causation questions, graph-based inference and judgments about
described events. This is useful navigation, but the common label “causal reasoning” does not
make their outcomes interchangeable. Correctly classifying a relation mentioned in a sentence,
recovering a graph from observations and identifying a policy value test different information
and assumptions. Yu et al. (2025a)

Relation extraction is a serious baseline, with a narrower claim

Susanti and Holsmoelle compare prompting with fine-tuned models on four relation datasets.
On DDI, Table 1 reports F1 of 67.4 for Single-Prompt C and 87.9 for PubMedBERT: a
20.5-point difference. The paper reports five-fold averages and explicitly limits its evaluation
to binary pairwise causality assessment. It neither demonstrates joint graph verification nor
establishes a universal advantage for fine-tuning under equal annotation costs. The comparison
does establish that a supervised smaller model deserves consideration when the proposed task
is extraction from a stable document domain. Susanti and Holsmoelle (2025)
   For banking notes, evaluate the extraction role on held-out documents with independently
specified labels and timestamps. Track abstention and the treatment of ambiguous or contra-
dictory passages. Then separately evaluate whether extracted statements are admissible graph
evidence. A sentence that says “the waiver caused repayment” is evidence of what the author
claimed; it is not, by itself, evidence that assignment was unconfounded. A useful agent should
retain the quotation, its source and the alternative causal interpretations.
   Sng and colleagues illustrate why agreement is a separate target. Their retrieval experiment
supplies a mocked true causal graph, and their conclusion explicitly says that reducing
inconsistent ratings does not imply accurate causal prediction. A comparison in which one arm
receives such a graph evaluates its use of supplied information. It does not measure whether
retrieval can discover the graph in a bank setting. Registering both correct and misleading
retrieved evidence is necessary to expose that distinction. Sng et al. (2024)

Task-specific gains should remain task-specific

In CausalEval’s Table 3, GPT-4o scores 69 on CLADDER with ordinary chain-of-thought
and 76 with FunctionCall, but its e-CARE scores are 90 and 73, respectively. These are
author-reported pass@1 results for the named versions and samples. The gains and losses
should remain visible rather than being replaced by the claim that tools always improve causal
reasoning. The table is also preferable to silently repeating inconsistent numerical values in
the paper’s surrounding discussion. Yu et al. (2025a)
   The study repeats each question five times with greedy decoding. Repeated calls can reveal
response variation, but five calls to the same question are not five independent causal problems.
For illustration, suppose there are N independent mechanisms, m calls per mechanism, equal
marginal score variance σ 2 , and common within-mechanism correlation ρ. Then

                                            σ2
                                Var(S̄) =      {1 + (m − 1)ρ}.
                                            Nm
  At N = 100, m = 5, ρ = 1, the effective independent count is 100, not 500. This is a
project-derived sampling illustration, not an estimate of the paper’s unreported correlation.
The appropriate prototype analysis clusters calls and paraphrases by underlying mechanism,
reports the number of distinct mechanisms, and uses paired comparisons when methods see
the same cases.
   CausalEval also evaluates some expensive models on 100 cases rather than the usual 500.
Its human row combines scores from original benchmark papers with a study of three graduate
students on 100 questions for remaining datasets. A combined human/model gap therefore is
not one uniform matched experiment. Any investment argument should state the comparison
actually performed, the cost and failure accounting, and the uncertainty that remains.


An affordable, falsifiable evaluation sequence

The proposed sequence starts with fixed causal mechanisms, explicit public document prove-
nance and deterministic numerical answers. It then tests formulation, variable timing, graph
uncertainty, identification, execution and reporting separately, followed by their composition.
Baselines receive the same data, permitted documentation and tools. Model-only reasoning,
retrieval, a typed numerical workflow, and a supervised extractor answer different engineering
questions and should be included where relevant.
   The primary denominator includes every attempted case, with scientific refusals distinguished
from crashes and wrong answers. Numerical accuracy conditional on successful execution is a
secondary outcome. Cost includes failed calls, retrieval, annotation, retries and human review.
Deliberately adverse cases include an accurate quotation supporting a false causal claim, a
timestamp that makes a proposed control post-treatment, alternative graphs with different
effects, a misleading retrieved graph, and an unsupported edit policy.
   Public and generated data can establish that these failure cases are handled as specified and
can compare methods under a known law. They do not establish the frequency of those failures
in a target bank or the value of changing its real decisions. The next expensive experiment
should address a remaining uncertainty that could change the build or adoption decision. Until
such evidence exists, the proposal can recommend a bounded prototype and a testable research
direction while preserving uncertainty about live-model performance, source completeness and
bank transport.
50.9. Testing semantic failures before the expensive study                                    1309


50.9.2    A prospective experiment for causal assistance

The first live comparison should determine whether language assistance improves a specified
causal workflow enough to justify its complete cost. A fluent explanation, a correctly guessed
graph and a correctly identified effect are different outcomes. The design therefore evaluates
formulation, information timing, graph ambiguity, identification, numerical execution and
reporting as separate tasks, followed by their composition. Public documents and generated
mechanisms can support this experiment before a bank funds access to proprietary records.
Model revisions, final sample sizes, acceptance thresholds and prices remain to be selected
from actual inputs; the calculations below are planning examples, not a registered trial or
evidence of live-model performance.
   CausalEval’s inspected experiment repeats each question five times and averages the results
within question. Such repeats can expose output variation, but cannot create additional
independent causal problems (Yu et al., 2025a). The same issue arises in the proposal’s
authored tasks. Its development collection contains 24 variants in twelve template groups; its
reserved collection contains 48 variants in twenty-four groups, with two variants in every group.
These assets support interface and rubric development. Their authorship and generation
history do not establish independent, identically distributed final mechanisms or independently
adjudicated causal truth (Causal proposal project, 2026a).


Mechanisms, information and the reference answer

A final task should begin with a declared scientific information state. For a generated structural
model, the evaluator can retain the full graph, assignment mechanism and intervention outcomes
while the analysis sees only its permitted observations and metadata. The reference must
answer two questions: what is true in the generating world, and what is identified from the
information supplied to the method? They need not have the same answer. An agent that
guesses the hidden true effect in a nonidentifying problem has not correctly solved identification.
   The task portfolio retains six functional families: business formulation; clocks and selection;
graph construction and discovery; identification and estimator choice; evidence tracing; and tool
composition. Across them, stress conditions include hidden confounding, temporal dependence,
treatment– confounder feedback, panel assignment, imperfect linkage and ambiguous monetary
objectives. A selected first experiment need not claim every condition at once. Its included
cells, excluded capabilities and substantive alternatives should be fixed before evaluation rather
than chosen from successful outputs.
   The split should occur at mechanism and template-family level before paraphrases, renamed
variables or translations are created. A new name for a familiar graph does not make its
mechanism unseen. Public benchmarks require their own provenance and label review; public
availability does not establish absence from a model’s training data. A generated final collection
must have its generator, information restrictions and scoring rules checked before the final
draw. Prompts and retrieval settings are chosen on a separate development collection. Any
inspected final case is recorded as exposed, and subsequent method changes require a new
evaluation revision.
  Author-reviewed algebraic references can support a bounded proposal demonstration. Am-
biguous business language, source applicability and multilingual meaning may also require
human judgment. Such judgments should use a frozen rubric, method-blinded presentation
and retained disagreements. Until independent adjudicators actually participate, the result
must remain an author-reviewed study. Neither a generated label nor agreement between two
model responses substitutes for authentic bank assignment evidence.
1310                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The adverse conditions should change both language and information. Useful paired variants
include an unfamiliar variable vocabulary, a unit change, a delayed feature timestamp, a quoted
but scientifically unsupported causal claim, a misleading retrieved graph, and conflict between
text and observed data. Additional languages require a checked translation that preserves
the population, intervention, clock and uncertainty. Language versions and stochastic repeats
stay nested within the original mechanism. At least one primary variant must be chosen
prospectively for the binary comparison derived below; sensitivity results on the other variants
remain visible.


What each comparator is allowed to know

The comparison should hold a backend fixed while changing its information and tool access.
This separates the value of retrieval and numerical composition from a change in the underlying
model. Comparing backends can be a later, explicitly costed dimension. Four proposed live
arms are a frozen prompt alone; the same model with audited retrieval; the same model
with typed numerical tools; and a hybrid with both. A critique step can be ablated within
the hybrid when it fits the same declared total resource budget. It is not free additional
computation.
  The model-only arm receives the same declared task and permitted summaries, but no
hidden graph or numerical-tool result. Retrieval arms use an immutable corpus and a fixed
query/ranking policy, and save the returned passages. Tool arms share pinned algorithms and
the same observations. Constraint proposals must state their evidence and can be refused
by the numerical operation. A proposed restriction cannot silently change the population,
sampling law or model class to make an inconvenient query identifiable.
   Non-model comparators remain essential. A deterministic form/schema workflow tests
whether structured elicitation is sufficient. A data-only estimator tests the numerical stage
on admissible structured inputs. A retrieval-only system tests whether locating a primary
passage suffices. These comparators have different roles: a data-only estimator given a correct
structured estimand is not simultaneously solving free-text business translation. Report stage-
specific results and end-to-end results with the information differences exposed. Human and
human-plus-model workflows are optional additional arms whose time, expertise and reference
independence must be measured rather than inferred from a model benchmark.
   Equal budgets should cover total tokens, model calls, tool calls, elapsed time and retries
per assigned task. If one arm consumes less than its cap, retain that advantage in the cost
account. If an agent uses more calls, compare its benefit against the additional actual cost. A
transport retry and a deliberate internal critique are different events; both belong in the call
ledger. Timeouts, parse failures and exhausted budgets remain assigned outcomes.


Useful abstention and unjustified certainty

Let Ui indicate a useful, scientifically correct resolution of an assigned task, Ei a critical
scientific error, and Ai availability of a usable response. The rubric requires Ui ≤ Ai and
Ui Ei = 0. A useful resolution can be a justified effect set or a specific request for missing
information. It cannot be an unsupported point estimate or a generic refusal unrelated to the
task.

   Operational honesty does not automatically count as a successfully resolved scientific
task. Availability and unsupported-capability rates are reported separately, including among
identifiable tasks. Critical-error rates among answered cases are also reported when their
denominator is nonzero. This prevents a system with no available answers from winning
because it emitted no false causal claims. Final acceptance must jointly constrain useful
resolution, availability, critical errors and cost; the required numerical thresholds are not
supplied by the current proposal.
   Graph scoring compares the returned object with the admitted equivalence class. Unsup-
ported arrowheads count separately from omitted informative orientations, and a justified
circle is not penalized as if a fully directed DAG were identified. Effect scoring first checks
the target and its identification status. Scalar error is meaningful only for the admitted
scalar target; set results retain disconnected components, empty sets and unbounded regions.
Coverage and length are separate outcomes, and infinite length stays infinite. Monetary policy
loss is evaluated only under the declared generated mechanism and feasible actions. It is not a
measurement of bank ROI.


How many independent problems could justify a claim?

Consider an illustrative critical-error indicator for independent, identically distributed mecha-
nism draws in one task family. If no errors are observed in n draws, then the probability of
this event at an error rate p is (1 − p)n . Inverting this probability yields the one-sided upper
confidence bound
                                                      1/n
                                          pU = 1 − α∗ .
With a single 95% bound, zero errors in 48 independent mechanisms still gives pU = 0.06050.
If those forty-eight cases were only twenty-four independent mechanisms with duplicated
observations, substituting 48 for 24 would overstate the evidence; the corresponding bound at
24 is 0.11735. The authored reserved templates do not themselves establish either sampling
law (Causal proposal project, 2026a).
  For K simultaneous one-sided bounds, allocating α∗ = 0.05/K gives a familywise guarantee
1312                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


by the union bound. To obtain pU ≤ 0.05 after zero errors requires

                                         log(0.05/K)
                                                        
                                      n≥             .
                                           log(0.95)

The resulting counts are 59 for one claim, 94 for six, and 107 for twelve. Here 5% is an
illustrative error tolerance, not a bank requirement. Six task-family error bounds and six
improvement tests would together need a joint allocation over twelve claims. Assigning
each collection a separate 5% budget would not provide the same combined guarantee. No
independence between families is needed for this multiplicity argument, although the binomial
model within each family still needs its stated sampling law.
   Improvement also needs prospective power planning. On the designated primary variant
of mechanism i, define Di = Uihybrid − Uicomparator . Let p+ = Pr(Di = 1), p− = Pr(Di = −1),
and q = p+ + p− . Under the stipulated independent common law, the number of discordant
pairs Kn has distribution Bin(n, q), and the number favoring the hybrid given Kn = k has
distribution Bin(k, p+ /q). At the paired null, its success probability is at most one half. Define

                          b∗ (k) = min {b : Pr[Bin(k, 1/2) ≥ b] ≤ α∗ } ,

using k + 1 when rejection is impossible. The exact planning power is
                        n

This is a one-sided paired superiority screen. A statistically detectable positive difference is
not itself proof of an economically useful minimum gain, which requires an additional decision

arithmetic, not a model’s unknown discordance probabilities (Causal proposal project, 2026a).
A development pilot can estimate plausible ranges and request costs, after which the final
design can narrow its claims, increase its sample or decide that the comparison is not worth
funding. The pilot cases must remain outside the final evaluation.


Cost, freezing and the next decision

For each model call, retain input, output and cache-token counts, model revision, chargeable
tool actions and the actual dated price schedule. Add retrieval, numerical computation, storage,
50.10. What published evaluations establish and how to reuse them                                         1313


human review and rework. Unknown prices remain missing; public tasks do not imply free
execution. A useful planning expression is
                  X
       Ctotal =           (rin tin + rout tout + ctools ) + Cretrieval + Ccompute + Creview + Crework ,
                  calls

where token rates and token counts use matching units and cache distinctions are retained
when applicable.
   For illustration, 100 independent mechanisms in each of six disjoint task families, two
variants per mechanism and four live arms give 4,800 assigned arm-variant cases. Three
attempts and up to three internal model calls per attempt yield a conservative envelope of
43,200 calls. If every call is capped at 2,000 input and 500 output tokens, the token envelope is
86.4 million input and 21.6 million output tokens. At prices expressed per million tokens, the
model-only component is 86.4rin +21.6rout , before the other costs above. These are deliberately
explicit caps, not a spend forecast or an approved budget (Causal proposal project, 2026a). A
single-family pilot and fewer justified comparisons can be much cheaper; reducing the study
should also reduce its claims.
   Before any final model calls, the design must bind exact backend revisions, generation
settings, permitted endpoints, prompts, retrieval corpus, numerical algorithms, final mechanism
distribution and draw, reference adjudication, primary contrasts, multiplicity allocation,
numerical thresholds and a priced resource ceiling. A fixed stopping rule retains all assigned
tasks. A global outage or exhausted budget is recorded as an interruption with unexecuted
cases visible, not repaired by silently replacing difficult cases. A materially changed model or
prompt requires a new evaluation identity.
   The recommendation is therefore to fund a bounded prototype comparison only when its
development evidence identifies a consequential uncertainty and its expected information can
change the next investment choice. The proposal can already specify the experiment, expose its
likely precision and resource trade-offs, and reject unsupported universal performance claims.
Authentic bank experiments become worthwhile when the resulting prototype leaves a specific
transport, assignment or operating question that public and generated evidence cannot answer.


50.10      What published evaluations establish and how to reuse
           them

50.10.1     The question a bank must answer

A useful causal assistant must improve the decision made with the available evidence at
an acceptable total cost. Fluent reports, agreement among agents and successful tool calls
are intermediate outcomes. The proposal therefore evaluates the target, assumptions, graph,
identification decision, numerical result and action separately. A correct refusal can be valuable;
an unsupported but precise number can be harmful. This chapter develops a prospective
comparison using public evidence and stipulated mechanisms. It reports no new live-model
experiment, analyst-time observation or bank return on investment.
   Consider the decision to offer a restructuring review at an account’s first qualifying arrears
date. The target is the mean effect of the offer on discounted 180-day net recovery among
accounts eligible at that date. The action is an offer, not eventual acceptance; information
must have been available before the offer, and the offer cost is counted once. The experiment
tests whether a workflow can translate that brief, preserve the clock, decide identification and
return an appropriate estimate or refusal. It does not test whether the bank should deploy the
offer merely because the assistant completed an analysis.
1314                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


50.10.2     What primary evaluations actually establish

CLadder by Jin et al.(Jin et al., 2023) (arXiv:2312.04350v3, Table 2) offers over 10,000 formal
causal questions and deliberately varies commonsense alignment. Its reported historical GPT-4
accuracy rises from 62.03% to 70.40% with CausalCoT, an 8.37 percentage-point improvement.
This is favorable evidence for structuring a language-to-formal-query task. It is not evidence of
discovering an unknown bank graph or calibrating a treatment-effect interval. The benchmark’s
formal answers are valuable only when the generator’s assumptions actually identify the named
target.
   CausalEval by Yu et al.(Yu et al., 2025a) (arXiv:2410.16676v4, Table 3 and Appendix C)
supplies an important counterweight. On its cost-limited GPT-4o subsets, function calling
scores 76 on CLADDER against 69 for CoT, while e-CARE falls from 90 to 73. These
are source-reported percentages, not matched bank performance. Its nine benchmarks have
heterogeneous tasks; some models use 100 examples, and its human row combines previously
published human scores with three trained graduate students on selected datasets. Neither
a universal enhancement ranking nor a matched analyst productivity comparison follows.
The proposal must report results by task and preserve a numerical, ordinary analyst and
single-assistant baseline.
   CausalDS by Leban and Sun(Leban and Sun, 2026) (arXiv:2607.08093v1, Section 5, Figure 3)
brings the evaluation closer to an actual workflow: narrated scenes, files, a distinct observation
layer, private truth and explicit nonidentification. Its 100-scene exam is sampled from 953
scenes, with 28 Rung-1, 51 Rung-2 and 21 Rung-3 tasks and 48/32/20 clean/proxy/proxy-hard
conditions. The paper reports substantially different content, abstention, interval and token
outcomes. However, the 20.0%–71.4% interval coverage figures use only seven eligible ATE
interval tasks per model, five for Qwen. They cannot support a precise population calibration
conclusion. Reasoning effort/settings differ across model groups, and combined prompt-plus-
completion tokens are not dollar costs. The reported failures from excessive tool output also
show why bounded output belongs in the experimental execution contract.
   The study by Feng et al.(Feng, 2024), On the Reliability of Large Language Models for
Causal Discovery (arXiv:2407.19638v2, Sections 2–4) examines accessible OLMo/BLOOM
training corpora, manipulated relation frequencies and contextual variants. Exposure and
context affect responses. These findings motivate separate tests of unfamiliar names, new
mechanism families and misleading evidence. Renaming a familiar graph does not establish
mechanism novelty. Equally, a changed context can legitimately change the causal claim,
so a context-sensitive answer is not automatically an error. An independent target-specific
adjudication is needed.
   CausalChat by Zhang et al.(Zhang, 2024) (arXiv:2410.14146v1, Section 6) is evidence for
useful interaction design and a warning about productivity claims. Six university students
move through BIC feedback, LLM text and the interface in a fixed order, choosing different
remaining edges at each stage. The reported edge errors are 5/18, 7/18 and 1/18. Learning,
order and edge difficulty are not separated by that design. Its expert participants also raise
missing citations. The proposal adopts traceable graph-edit suggestions and measures review
effort; it does not infer a causal labor-saving effect from these counts.
   The study by Le et al.(Le et al., 2024), Multi-Agent Causal Discovery Using Large Language
Models (arXiv:2407.15073v4, ablations and limitations) reports a 16–25-fold token increase
over standard baselines, with coding/debugging taking up to half of the full system’s tokens.
A single-agent variant is competitive on the simpler graphs at approximately half the cost;
full debate improves selected harder examples. The study covers five public graphs with 5–20
nodes and explicitly excludes hidden confounders and cycles. It provides a reason to test
50.10. What published evaluations establish and how to reuse them                             1315


debate against a single assistant, not to make debate mandatory in every task or to infer its
value for latent temporal discovery.
   The study by Murphy et al.(Murphy, 2026), Model Discovery Agent (arXiv:2608.09696v5,
Figure 2 and discussion) combines language proposals with numerical fitting, simulation and
experimental design. Its chemistry comparison retains 115 matched evaluable world–seed cells
from 171 attempted, spanning 54 worlds. A conditional performance curve for those cells is
not all-attempt availability. The comparisons are not compute-matched, its experiments use
open-loop policies, and the paper explicitly says finite held-out predictive tests do not establish
causal identification. The banking design retains attempt counts and numerical computation
costs and separates prediction, experiment choice and effect identification.
   Taken together, these studies support a testable architecture: typed causal tasks, independent
formal/numerical checks, source-grounded human review and selective assistance. They do
not establish one best model, general causal competence or positive bank ROI. The reported
results remain literature evidence from distinct tasks, populations and model settings.


50.10.3     Reusing benchmarks without inheriting their labels blindly

The inspected CLadder source is pinned to commit 3d2d1169b4b9 (2024-05-29), with an
MIT notice. Its query generator contains a Wald-ratio IV template and uses ATE bounds in
constructing answers. An unrestricted IV graph does not identify a population ATE through
the Wald ratio. Additional assumptions may identify a different target or a sign; the full
generator and item assumptions must be checked before admitting a label. Quarantine IV-as-
population-ATE cases and resolve repository/paper dataset-version differences. Retain the
generator as a candidate source of formal fixtures after that review.
   The inspected CausalDS source is pinned to c74671d0a092 (2026-07-17), with Apache-2.0
code and a CC0 data notice. Its separation of conceptual SCM, observed proxy, private truth
and scorer is useful. The inspected grader can default missing identification metadata toward
identifiable and distinguishes intentional abstention from malformed output. It computes both
uncapped and capped normalized interval-score summaries; publish both. Require explicit
identified/nonidentified/unknown states, finite endpoint validation, preserved observation
semantics and raw tail losses before reuse. These are static source findings, not installed-
package results or a completed dependency/license audit.
  The first prototype should import reviewed fixture definitions and expected outputs through
a narrow adapter, then compare the adapter against an independently written oracle on tiny
cases. The trusted scorer must remain outside the agent’s writable task environment. Freeze
hashes of code, data, prompts, retrieval corpus and scoring rules. Impose tool-output and
runtime limits while retaining the failure status and incurred cost. Exposed development
examples are useful for debugging but cannot also be the hidden quality test. Neither upstream
package has been executed for this synthesis.(causalNLP/cladder; andleb/causalds, 2026)


50.10.4     A reproducible evaluation example

For an exact illustration, stipulate a population in which an offer is randomized with probability
one half, independent of binary pre-offer risk X and potential outcomes. Let P (X = 1) = 1/2
and let the potential recovery means be E[Y (0) | X] = 100+20X and E[Y (1) | X] = 105+30X.
The conditional effects are 5 and 15 and the population ATE is 10 monetary units. Consistency,
no interference and the stipulated assignment/observation law identify it. Standardization
over the two known strata is an ordinary numerical baseline. The exact means supply oracle
truth; finite-sample intervals would require a separately specified sampling law and method.
1316                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


In an observational variant with an unmeasured common cause of offer and recovery and no
additional identifying restrictions, the appropriate answer is nonidentification rather than the
randomized formula.
   A second, deliberately hypothetical accounting fixture has 100 requested analyses: 80
identified requests and 20 nonidentified requests. Among the identified requests, 70 return
admissible intervals, 63 cover the true target and 10 fail to return an interval. Among the
nonidentified requests, 16 correctly refuse and four return unsupported numbers. Then

                                     Aid = 70/80 = 87.5%,
                                   Creturned,id = 63/70 = 90%,
                             Creturn and cover,id = 63/80 = 78.75%.

   The correct-refusal rate is 16/20 = 80%. Across all requests, the fraction returning an
admissible covering interval is 63/100 = 63%, but its complement is not an error rate:
principled refusals occupy part of it. The four unsupported numbers do not improve scientific
availability. An overall operational completion count must therefore sit beside identification-
specific outcomes and failure reasons, not replace them. None of these stipulated counts
estimates actual model performance.(Causal banking proposal, 2026p)
  For a finite interval [l, u] at nominal level 1 − α, the interval score is
                                 2                   2
                       (u − l) +   (l − θ)1{θ < l} + (θ − u)1{θ > u}.
                                 α                   α
Report raw scores, coverage, width and availability with their eligible denominators. A
normalized score additionally needs a fixed positive scale. Invalid endpoints are failures, not
zero loss. A disconnected identified set is evaluated as a set, retaining topology and infinite
length; do not replace it with a convenient midpoint or force this finite-interval score onto it.
Graph scores likewise use the declared identifiable equivalence class; unsupported orientation
is not rewarded simply for resembling a fully directed reference graph.


50.11      What an unknown exposure history permits us to con-
           clude
A public benchmark can provide reproducible questions without providing an unexposed test.
These properties answer different questions. The relation frequency and context experiments
of Feng and colleagues motivate recording exposure at the level of a mechanism, its answer,
and its supporting material. Their accessible-corpus analysis does not estimate how much of
an arbitrary closed model’s evaluation was present during training. Nor does the change in an
answer after a context change establish that either answer is wrong: the context can change
the scientific proposition. (Feng, 2024; Causal banking proposal, 2026ad)
  The practical response is to state the inference that remains possible. Let S ∈ {0, 1} indicate
a correct resolution under a fixed rubric, and let E ∈ {0, 1} indicate exposure of the final
mechanism or its answer through the channels declared in the protocol. The definition includes
model development, prompt selection and retrieval when those channels are in scope; it must
not silently count all ordinary domain knowledge as contamination. Write p = Pr(S = 1),
e = Pr(E = 1), p0 = Pr(S = 1 | E = 0), and p1 = Pr(S = 1 | E = 1). When both strata exist,
                                      p = (1 − e)p0 + ep1 .
Here p0 is performance on the unexposed subset of the stated task distribution. It is not the
performance the same model would have if trained again without exposure. Exposed and
50.12. Selective adjudication is an observation mechanism                                    1317


unexposed tasks may differ in difficulty, and retraining can alter answers on both. That causal
effect of changing training requires a different experiment.
   Suppose an independently justified sensitivity assumption is 0 ≤ e ≤ ē < 1, with no
restriction on the exposed score. Then
                                   p − ē                       p
                                                                
                            max 0,              ≤ p0 ≤ min 1,        .
                                   1 − ē                     1 − ē
For a fixed e, solve the mixture identity for p0 and allow p1 to range over [0, 1]. The lower
endpoint decreases and the upper endpoint increases as e increases, before clipping to the unit
interval. This gives the displayed union over all admitted e. The endpoints are attainable by
suitable exposed scores; they are identification bounds for this mixture model, not confidence
intervals.
   If p itself is estimated, a valid interval [L, U ] for the specified score probability can be
mapped through the lower expression at L and the upper expression at U . This statement
inherits the sampling assumptions of that interval and treats ē as valid. An estimated exposure
bound needs its own uncertainty allocation. Without information bounding exposure away
from one, a high public score can leave the unexposed score essentially unrestricted; an entirely
exposed population has no defined unexposed conditional mean.
   Consider a stipulated paired evaluation of 100 mechanisms. Both assistants are correct
on 64, only A on 20, only B on 16, and neither on zero. Their observed scores are 84% and
80%. Assume for sensitivity analysis that at most 20 mechanisms have exposure in either
workflow; this common exposure indicator makes the clean subset comparable. The bounds
for the individual clean scores are [0.80, 1] and [0.75, 1]. More importantly, the same observed
paired table admits opposite rankings:
                         20 exposed cases          p0,A p0,B p0,A − p0,B
                        20 A-only successes        0.80 1.00    −0.20
                   16 B-only and 4 joint successes 1.00 0.75     0.25
Exact enumeration of every feasible allocation to this table gives these same extreme differences.
A four-point observed advantage therefore cannot settle even this descriptive clean-subset
ranking. The twenty-percent exposure bound is an explicit assumption of the example, not a
measured training property of either assistant. No statistical significance test on the original
scores can supply the missing exposure history. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ac)
   For the proposed banking evaluation, disclosure should distinguish known development
exposure, known retrieval access, unknown training exposure and the date of final mechanism
creation. Family-level splits and an exposure ledger reduce controllable leakage; they do not
prove that a generator’s mechanism family is novel to a model. Renaming entities, translating
a prompt and withholding a file hash are useful perturbations but cannot certify unseen causal
structure. A transparent public benchmark can still support conformance and reproducibility.
A performance claim should name that scope, state sensitivity to exposure, and seek a newly
controlled collection when the unresolved ranking would change the investment decision.


50.12      Selective adjudication is an observation mechanism
A second source of uncertainty arises after the assistant answers. Reviewing only low-confidence
outputs, disputed graphs or expensive decisions may be an efficient way to find defects. The
error proportion in that selected set is not automatically the error proportion among all
assigned cases. The review policy is part of the observation model, just as an account-selection
rule is part of a banking data analysis.
1318                                                                    Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Let N frozen outputs have fixed but partly unobserved critical-error labels di ∈ {0, 1}.
If m selected outputs have trustworthy labels and k are errors, the finite-population rate
q = N −1 i di satisfies
         P
                                     k         k+N −m
                                        ≤q≤               .
                                     N              N
The lower completion makes every unreviewed output correct; the upper completion makes
every one erroneous. With ten reviewed outputs, two errors and 100 total outputs, the
admissible range is 2%–92%, even though the selected review reports 20%. This is a missing-
label bound for this fixed collection. It is not a confidence interval for a bank’s future task
population. A confident critic does not remove this missingness.
   One alternative separates defect hunting from measurement. Keep targeted review for
discovery, then use a declared probability audit of the entire frozen output collection. Let
Ri indicate inclusion in the audit and let its known probability be πi > 0. Under truthful
complete adjudication,
                                    N
                                 1 X  Ri di
                          qb =              ,        ER (qb | d1 , . . . , dN ) = q.
