yield mean 3/5 and variance 6/275. This provides a check of both location and spread without
treating an optimizer’s answer as a posterior. A later registered trial can assess chains against
those moments, finite-sample Monte Carlo tolerances and diagnostic behavior. Passing that
trial would qualify this numerical construction under its declared law; it would not identify
a confounded action or validate an unknown causal model.Causal banking proposal project
(2026bx)


50.31.4     Devices, random keys, diagnostics and restart identity

The inspected MCMC interface requests parallel chains by default but falls back to sequential
chains with a warning if too few devices are available. Vectorized chains are another declared
route. Device count, execution method and actual array precision must therefore enter a run
identity; a requested GPU or parallel configuration is insufficient evidence that it was used.
The source utilities expose platform and 64-bit configuration, and the host-device-count helper
carries its own configuration caveat. These are controls to test, not measured throughput or a
general speed advantage over PyMC.NumPyro Contributors (2026)
   Randomness needs equally explicit treatment. The seed handler carries a mutable random
key and documents a closure pattern to avoid leaking this state through JAX transformations.
MCMC splits a single key for multiple chains; it also accepts a supplied batch of keys.
An adapter should preserve how chains and prediction tasks receive keys and check the
intended independence or deliberate coupling. Four exact copies of a Bernoulli(1/2) draw
have average variance 1/4; four independent draws have average variance 1/16. Labelling
copies as independent would understate variance by a factor of four. This is an authored
dependence counterexample, not a finding that NumPyro’s scalar-key splitting duplicates
chains. Deliberately coupled random numbers for a paired comparison can be legitimate, but
their covariance must be represented.NumPyro Contributors (2026); Causal banking proposal
project (2026bx)
   The inspected HMC state includes trajectory and divergence information, while the default
collected fields retain samples and divergences. Further quantities need explicit collection.
Summary functions use split R-hat and effective sample size with declared chain/draw axes and
minimum draw requirements. Their names do not establish identity with another package’s
diagnostic implementation. The proposed worker must distinguish an unavailable diagnostic,
a nonfinite value, an adverse diagnostic and a satisfactory result under predeclared criteria.
None of these outcomes certifies assignment truth, graph identification or repeated-sampling
calibration of a causal policy interval.NumPyro Contributors (2026)
50.31. NumPyro: preserving the experiment through handlers and compiled inference          1365


   For continuation, last_state and post_warmup_state expose more information than saved
posterior draws. The documented continuation route reuses the final state and its random key;
warmup behavior changes when a post-warmup state is supplied. This is a useful interface
for a future recovery design, but not evidence of durable serialization, crash consistency or
compatibility across changed models. A restart contract must bind the complete sampler state,
model/data identities, transformations, adaptation, random-key lineage, numerical environment
and publication boundary. Local fault injection must then show whether uninterrupted and
interrupted executions meet the registered comparison rule. Timing must also account for
JAX’s asynchronous dispatch, which the MCMC documentation expressly notes; elapsed
Python submission time alone is not complete computational cost.NumPyro Contributors
(2026)


50.31.5    A concrete reuse decision and a bounded qualification route

The appropriate disposition is to retain NumPyro as a source-qualified reference for a future
native Python worker. Direct use would preserve its handler, enumeration and numerical
semantics within a pinned environment. A general R, Java or C++ port would duplicate those
semantics and the compiler boundary without demonstrated benefit; a process interface is the
more defensible candidate until conversion costs are measured. PyMC remains a substantive
alternative for graph transformation and posterior prediction, while exact finite and conjugate
calculations remain independent semantic references. Selection between workers should use
matched supported models, accepted uncertainty output, full compilation and warmup costs,
effective sample production, prediction, memory, serialization and recovery. No hardware
performance ranking follows from the source review.NumPyro Contributors (2026); PyMC
Developers (2026); Causal banking proposal project (2026bx)
    Library, CLI and MCP entrypoints should preserve one model and experiment identity:
observation versus intervention, factual versus cross-world target, fixed versus regenerated
sites, posterior averaging versus MAP decoding, units and clock, chain layout, precision
and diagnostic availability. An LLM can propose these declarations, retrieve the supporting
assumptions and explain refused requests; the model owner must justify their scientific meaning.
A maintainer must bind the selected NumPyro, JAX, jaxlib, Funsor and device artifacts and
their rights. An operator must set budgets, verify actual device execution and test durable
recovery. The pinned metadata names a license-file path that differs from the inspected root
filename, so a release trial must inspect the actual distributed notices rather than infer their
custody from a classifier. None of these owner roles is filled by an API response.NumPyro
Contributors (2026)
   Before integration approval, a registered native trial should exercise the finite confound-
ing and cross-world witnesses, compare posterior averaging with discrete decoding, check
deterministic substitution under changed inputs, validate the conjugate moments, inspect
invalid supports and dimensions, verify diagnostic availability and test interrupted continu-
ation. Whole-environment rights, numerical reliability and the causal assumptions remain
separate acceptance questions. The exact examples demonstrate why those experiments have
merit before costly bank validation; general causal identification and bank adoption remain
open.NumPyro Contributors (2026); Causal banking proposal project (2026bx)
1366                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


50.32      Constructed causal labels, semantic refusal and the unit
           of evaluation
A causal assistant can improve the wording of an answer while leaving its decision content
unchanged. It can also repeat a familiar causal story more fluently than an analyst without
establishing that the story applies to the bank’s observations. Evaluation therefore needs to
distinguish recognizing a stipulated mechanism, identifying an effect from supplied information
and choosing a useful action. Two further benchmarks make this distinction concrete: the
published CELLO study by Chen and colleagues and the first Research Square version of
CausalReasonBench by Cherif. The former uses visual scenes and constructed graphs; the
latter uses textual scenarios and automatic reasoning scores. Their results concern their
respective tasks and historical model settings. Neither is a measurement of a causal banking
workflow.(Meiqi Chen and Bo Peng and Yan Zhang and Chaochao Lu, 2024; Ahmed Cherif,
2026)
   Consider the proposed deposit-pricing assistant. A manager asks whether a retention offer
will prevent withdrawals. A useful response must distinguish the association between receiving
an offer and staying with the bank from the effect of offering the same terms to an eligible
customer. It must also state what the information cannot establish. A benchmark that
supplies a complete causal mechanism tests whether the assistant follows that mechanism.
A benchmark that supplies only an observational vignette may instead need an answer that
preserves several possible mechanisms. Those are different questions even when the surface
wording and requested answer are identical. Constructed labels can be valuable for the first
question; their construction does not resolve the second.


50.32.1     What a scene-derived causal answer establishes

CELLO builds causal reasoning questions from Visual Genome relations. The construction
matches subgraphs to graph templates and uses language-model generation to produce questions
and distractors. Its prompting procedure separates entity extraction, graph construction, task
recognition and causal knowledge. This organization is relevant to the proposal because a
banking assistant also needs to turn entities and relationships into an explicit question before
asking a numerical engine to answer it. The distinction is that a relation visible in an image, or
recorded in a customer document, need not determine the intervention semantics assigned by a
template. Static co-occurrence, a plausible physical explanation and a warranted counterfactual
are distinct kinds of information. The benchmark’s annotation and image limitations therefore
constrain the interpretation of its scores, rather than being mere implementation details.(Meiqi
Chen and Bo Peng and Yan Zhang and Chaochao Lu, 2024)
   The paper reports a test set of 1,200 questions, with 100 selected for each of twelve tasks.
Its Appendix B.2 describes a separate validity check of 120 instances, ten per task, by two
annotators: 91.7% were judged valid, with reported Cohen agreement of 84.1%. These
figures describe a question-validity review. They do not turn each template’s intervention or
counterfactual claim into experimentally established truth. For banking, the analogous review
would check that the prompt faithfully expresses an agreed mechanism and information set. It
would still leave open whether that mechanism describes the actual offer assignment, customer
selection and outcome clock. (Meiqi Chen and Bo Peng and Yan Zhang and Chaochao Lu,
2024)
  Table 2 reports GPT-4o overall accuracy increasing from 0.59 to 0.70 with CELLO-CoT,
while confounder identification increases from 0.29 to 0.35. Task-specific behavior matters:
an aggregate improvement does not warrant using a system to select adjustment variables.
50.32. Constructed causal labels, semantic refusal and the unit of evaluation              1367


There is also an unresolved arithmetic boundary in the published table. The twelve displayed
GPT-4o-plus-CELLO-CoT task entries are
            0.83, 0.70, 0.52, 0.50, 0.35, 0.75,    0.81, 0.72, 0.79, 0.77, 0.90, 0.61.
Their equal-task mean is 0.6875. Under conventional rounding to two decimal places, even a
conservative closed envelope for that mean is
                             [0.6825, 0.6925] ∩ [0.695, 0.705] = ∅,                      (50.8)
where the second interval is the corresponding envelope for the reported overall 0.70. With
exactly 100 binary correctness outcomes per task, the displayed entries would sum to 825 correct
answers out of 1,200. This is a conditional aggregation check against the published original.
The cause of the difference is unknown; no sample-level result or alternative aggregation has
been reconstructed. Consequently, the reported improvement remains an author report with
this unresolved qualification, rather than an independently reproduced effect of the prompting
procedure. (Meiqi Chen and Bo Peng and Yan Zhang and Chaochao Lu, 2024; Causal banking
proposal, 2026bq)

50.32.2     Refusal can be correct for the wrong reason

CELLO’s robustness exercise reformulates the questions as requests with additional premises
and binary answers. Section 6.4 states that the correct answer is consistently “No.” This is
a separate distribution from the nearly balanced original binary questions. A constant-No
classifier scores 100% on the reformulated test without inspecting the scene. The paper also
describes GPT-4o declining requests because it is a language model unable to interact with the
physical world, rather than explaining the scene’s causal constraints. Correct answer polarity
can therefore conceal a mismatch between the tested mechanism and the reason for refusal.
(Meiqi Chen and Bo Peng and Yan Zhang and Chaochao Lu, 2024)
  For a banking assistant, “I cannot execute a payment” and “the available evidence does
not identify the effect of this payment policy” have different meanings. The first states an
action limitation; the second states an information limitation. A system could utter either
sentence regardless of whether a proposed comparison is scientifically valid. An evaluation
should therefore record the answer, the asserted reason and the consequence for the requested
decision. It should include supported requests as well as unsupported requests, and distinguish
the two kinds of refusal. Otherwise a system that rejects every causal analysis may appear
dependable while providing no usable analysis.
   Publicly constructed paired cases offer an inexpensive way to test this distinction before
commissioning a bank experiment. Begin with a mechanism whose query is identified under
the supplied assumptions. Create a companion case that removes the assignment information
or introduces an unresolved alternative mechanism while keeping the business language similar.
The supported case should receive the warranted query or bounded answer; the unsupported
case should preserve uncertainty and name the missing information. A complementary pair
can retain the information and change only whether the assistant has authority to act. This
tests whether the assistant confuses execution authority with causal identification. These are
proposed evaluation contrasts. Their merit is that the mechanism and the changed information
are explicit; a public observational label alone would not supply their causal truth.

50.32.3     Lexical agreement and directional reasoning

CausalReasonBench supplies twelve underlying scenarios spanning four domains and three
difficulties. It repeats them over four task types, four prompting strategies, three models
1368                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


and two replicates, yielding 1,152 responses, or 384 per model. The models are the paper’s
Groq-hosted LLaMA 3.1-8B, LLaMA 3.3-70B and Qwen3-32B settings. The main settings
use temperature zero, with the initial contrast-case pass at 0.1 and seed 42 where supported.
These details delimit a historical evaluation; the response count is not a count of independently
sampled causal mechanisms. The gold explanations are author-defined using the stated
reference sources. In the minimum-wage example, the appendix itself notes empirical debate.
Following a stipulated textbook mechanism is a different task from resolving that debate from
an observational vignette.(Ahmed Cherif, 2026)
   The paper’s Causal Identification Rate, abbreviated CIR, is a token-set F1 score. For
response-token set R, gold-keyword set G and ε = 10−8 , its precision and recall are P =
|R ∩ G|/(|R| + ε) and Q = |R ∩ G|/(|G| + ε), and CIR = 2P Q/(P + Q + ε). Causal Logic
Precision, CLP, separately assigns 1 to a gold forward pattern, 0.5 to ambiguous directional
language, and 0 to a reverse or absent pattern. Counterfactual Coherence Ratio, CCR, uses
counterfactual-token F1 for counterfactual tasks and equals CIR otherwise. Thus the composite
score outside the counterfactual tasks reduces to

               CAR = 0.40CIR + 0.35CLP + 0.25CCR = 0.65CIR + 0.35CLP.                      (50.9)

The apparent three-component assessment has two distinct components in that regime. This
follows directly from the published definitions; it is not an empirical claim about the models.
(Ahmed Cherif, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026bq)
   Set overlap ignores token order. For example, “funding causes deposits” and “deposits
causes funding” give the same token set and hence the same CIR against that gold set. The
deliberately terse reverse statement isolates the set operation; grammatical correction is a
separate language task. CLP is intended to test direction and could distinguish the two. The
paper describes whitespace tokenization, case normalization, Porter stemming and directional
regular expressions with up to five intervening words. Its complete executable patterns have
not been inspected here. The example therefore proves a limit of the CIR component, not
an exploit of the implementation or an equal score under the whole composite. A banking
evaluation should score the proposed cause, outcome, direction, conditioning information and
intervention separately, while retaining the free-text explanation for review. (Ahmed Cherif,
2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026bq)
   The paper selects the composite weights from fifteen candidates using 24 responses rated by
two experts. The reported selected Kendall correlation of 0.78 describes agreement on the
selection set. It does not provide a held-out validation of the selected metric. The required
next evidence is a fixed metric applied to different mechanisms and independently adjudicated
responses, including plausible keyword-rich errors, appropriate refusals and alternative correct
phrasings. This protects against a score that rewards similar vocabulary while missing the
banking decision’s meaning. (Ahmed Cherif, 2026)
   Reproduction is also a substantive limit. The methods describe code, prompts, gold
annotations and raw results as released publicly, whereas the Data Availability Statement on
physical page 33 says they are available on reasonable request. No public executable copy has
been established by this inspection. Both statements must be retained; the paper alone cannot
qualify a runnable integration. Its historical zero API charge under a free tier and roughly
eighteen hours of runtime likewise leave annotation, review, waiting, infrastructure and current
prices unmeasured. These limits support using the paper as a source of test-design ideas, while
leaving direct adoption and full comparative economics unresolved.(Ahmed Cherif, 2026)
50.32. Constructed causal labels, semantic refusal and the unit of evaluation                 1369


50.32.4     The monetary meaning of answering and withholding

An all-No benchmark rewards withholding regardless of its opportunity cost. To expose that
omission, consider a deliberately stipulated banking review task. A request is either supported
or unsupported by its supplied information. Endorsing a supported request earns USD 20;
endorsing an unsupported request loses USD 80; withholding earns zero. These amounts
represent the value and error cost of a review decision, not the deposit offer’s actual causal
effect or an observed bank return. Let ρ be the supported fraction, t the probability of
endorsement given support and f the probability of endorsement without support. Then
                                     A = ρt + (1 − ρ)(1 − f ),                             (50.10)
                                     V = 20ρt − 80(1 − ρ)f.                                (50.11)
Here A is classification accuracy and V is expected USD per request. They answer different
questions. At the balanced mix ρ = 1/2, the value reduces to 10t − 40f . (Causal banking
proposal, 2026bq)

Table 50.4: Exact illustrative support-review decisions at a balanced case mix. All rates and
payoffs are stipulated.
                     Rule                   t      f Accuracy USD/request
                     A               0.80 0.10             0.850              4.00
                     B               0.95 0.20             0.875              1.50
                     Always withhold    0    0             0.500                 0

   Rule B has higher accuracy and lower monetary value than rule A. A separate 400-request
integer enumeration, with 200 supported and 200 unsupported requests, gives A 160 true
and 20 false endorsements, and B 190 true and 40 false endorsements. The resulting totals
are USD 1,600 and USD 600, respectively, reproducing the per-request values in the table.
Always withholding earns zero and obtains 50% balanced accuracy, although it would obtain
100% accuracy if every label were unsupported. The comparison explains why the refusal
benchmark’s label mix and the banking loss function must remain visible. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026bq)
   For a calibrated probability p that a request is supported, endorsement has conditional
value 20p − 80(1 − p). It beats zero-value withholding only for p > 0.8, with indifference at
0.8. Calibration here concerns the support-review label in its specified population. It does not
calibrate an intervention effect, a confidence interval or an assistant’s self-reported confidence.
Changing the case mix or loss changes the decision problem. A public prototype can vary these
declared quantities to expose an unfavorable tradeoff; it cannot discover the bank’s actual
losses merely by computing this threshold. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bq)


50.32.5     Repeated prompts are not independent mechanisms

Prompting strategies should ordinarily be compared on the same mechanisms, because differ-
ences in case difficulty otherwise obscure the contrast. Let Dij be the paired utility difference
between two strategies on mechanism i and within-mechanism variant j. An illustrative
random-effects law is
                    Dij = µ + Ui + Eij ,        Var(Ui ) = τ 2 ,   Var(Eij ) = σ 2 ,       (50.12)
with independent mechanisms, independent idiosyncratic terms and all such terms mutually
independent. Shared Ui makes variants of the same mechanism dependent even when their
1370                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


generation calls are separate. With n mechanisms and r equally weighted variants per
mechanism, the grand mean has variance

                          τ 2 + σ 2 /r          Var(D)                         τ2
               Var(D) =                ,                     = 1 + (r − 1)          .       (50.13)
                               n           (τ 2 + σ 2 )/(nr)               τ 2 + σ2

The denominator in the ratio is the variance that would follow from falsely treating the variants
as independent. For n = 12, r = 8 and τ 2 = σ 2 = 1, the true variance is 3/32, the independent-
case calculation gives 1/48, and their ratio is 4.5. Counting every ordered within-mechanism
covariance gives the same result. These are exact deductions under the stated illustrative law,
not estimates of dependence in either paper. In particular, this calculation does not replace or
reconstruct the published significance tests or bootstrap intervals. (Causal banking proposal,
2026bq)
   Extra variants reduce the idiosyncratic contribution but do not remove the mechanism
contribution. A proposed prototype should therefore preserve the mechanism identifier, compare
strategies in pairs and allocate additional budget to new mechanisms when mechanism variation
dominates. With very few mechanisms, simply choosing a cluster bootstrap does not guarantee
reliable uncertainty. The design must state its sampling population, weighting and inferential
assumptions, and may need to report a finite-case comparison without a population claim.
None of the twelve source scenarios becomes an independent bank population because many
prompts were generated from it.
   These two benchmarks suggest complementary roles in the proposal. CELLO offers a
structured translation from entities through graphs to questions, together with a warning that
refusal polarity can conceal a semantic failure. CausalReasonBench offers explicit automatic-
score definitions and prompting contrasts, together with limits in token matching, metric
selection, repeated mechanisms and reproducibility. The proposed evaluation should adopt
those test ideas only with explicit labels and information regimes, constant-answer comparators,
semantic adjudication, paired mechanisms and declared review losses. Public cases and
synthetic mechanisms can establish whether a narrow prototype is worth further investigation.
Authentic assignment information, bank outcomes and institutional economics remain different
evidence. (Meiqi Chen and Bo Peng and Yan Zhang and Chaochao Lu, 2024; Ahmed Cherif,
2026)


50.33      What literature disagreement can establish about a
           benchmark
A benchmark graph is a scientific object with a population, measurement scheme and intended
regime. Its usefulness does not follow from how often it has been reused. Yet a new paper that
appears to contradict an arrow is not automatically a correction to that graph. In banking, an
association between a credit offer and repayment can concern applicants, approved borrowers
or customers who accepted the offer. A different selection rule changes the population law.
An account-level measurement can also differ from a customer-level mechanism. Before an
assistant votes for or against a diagram, it must establish what proposition the diagram and
each retrieved result actually assert.
   Zhang and colleagues offer a useful starting point: retrieve domain papers, derive association
queries from a benchmark graph, and ask a language model whether each paper supplies
relevant empirical evidence. Their June 2026 preprint reports a survey of 96 papers using 69
benchmarks, followed by an evaluation of 11 graphs using 38,081 full texts. The approach
makes benchmark assumptions objects of investigation rather than treating every inherited
50.33. What literature disagreement can establish about a benchmark                         1371


diagram as unquestionable truth. Its statistical and graphical interfaces nevertheless need
repair before the proposed library could use the result to change a causal model. The assessment
here concerns the inspected first-version text, pseudocode and prompt; it does not claim to
reproduce the upstream implementation.(Zhang et al., 2026b)


50.33.1     A graph implication is not its converse

For a distribution P that is Markov with respect to a DAG G, graphical separation supplies
an independence implication:

                              X ⊥G Y | Z       =⇒     X ⊥P Y | Z.                        (50.14)

Here ⊥G denotes d-separation and ⊥P statistical conditional independence. Reversing this
implication requires a further assumption, such as faithfulness: the distribution has no
extra independences beyond those implied by the graph. Even dependence need not be
captured by a particular linear correlation coefficient. The paper’s description that unseparated
variables, including adjacent variables, are always correlated therefore goes beyond the Markov
premise.(Zhang et al., 2026b)
  An exact project example shows that positive density does not repair the converse. Let
independent disturbances εX , εA , εY be standard Gaussian and define

                       X = εX ,        A = X + εA ,       Y = X − A + εY .               (50.15)

The graph contains X → A, X → Y and A → Y , and the joint law is Markov for this graph.
In the order (X, A, Y ) its covariance matrix is
                                  
                     1 1  0
                Σ = 1 2 −1 ,              det(Σ) = 1,       Cov(X, Y | A) = 21 .       (50.16)
                           
                     0 −1 2

Indeed Y = −εA + εY , so X and Y are marginally independent despite their adjacency. The
independent-disturbance coefficient map is nonsingular, establishing positive density. The
direct and mediated effects cancel for this population; conditional association need not cancel.
The covariance and determinant are reproduced by exact coefficient arithmetic, not by a
sample whose correlations happen to be small. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bp)
   For an offer, subsequent account action and final outcome, such a construction distinguishes
a mechanism from its total marginal association. It is not an assertion that the bank
has these coefficients. Its role is to show why a literature result reporting independence
cannot automatically invalidate an adjacency under a Markov-only contract. A faithful-model
comparison is a different, explicitly stronger exercise. Conversely, an estimated nonzero
correlation does not by itself identify a direct arrow. A benchmark evaluator must label which
of these propositions it tests.


50.33.2     Conditioning can open a path that a hitting set overlooks

The published Algorithm 1 enumerates collider-free paths and returns minimal sets that
intersect each such path as conditional-independence sets. Blocking paths that are initially
active is necessary, but does not ensure that conditioning leaves every other path blocked.
A collider becomes active when it, or a descendant, is conditioned upon. The paper’s own
d-separation definition includes this condition; the inspected hitting-set pseudocode does not
apply it to candidate separators.(Zhang et al., 2026b)
1372                                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


  Consider the following five-node project DAG:

                       X → C,        B → C,          C → Z,       X → Z,        Z → Y,    B → Y.             (50.17)

Its collider-free paths from X to Y are X −Z −Y and X −C −Z −Y . The unique minimal hitting
set of these paths is {Z}. Conditioning on Z blocks both, but activates X → C ← B → Y
through the descendant Z of collider C. It also activates the path X → Z ← C ← B → Y by
conditioning on collider Z itself. Thus {Z} is not a d-separator. Enumerating every simple
path and applying the full activity criterion gives {B, Z} as the minimal d-separator. This
is a counterexample to the published specification, not an observed output of uninspected
code.(Causal banking proposal, 2026bp)
  A nonsingular Gaussian construction verifies the practical consequence:

                                 X = εX ,            B = εB ,        C = X + B + εC ,
                                                                                                             (50.18)
                                 Z = X + C + εZ ,                 Y = Z + B + εY ,

with independent standard Gaussian disturbances. Its coefficients give Var(Z) = 7,
Cov(X, Y ) = 2, Cov(X, Z) = 2 and Cov(Z, Y ) = 8. Therefore
                                                                     2×8   2
                                        Cov(X, Y | Z) = 2 −              =− .                                (50.19)
                                                                      7    7
The exact covariance agrees with the independent active-path enumeration. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026bp)
   The remedy is concrete. Candidate conditioning sets must pass a sound d-separation
procedure for the stated graph family, including collider and descendant activation. Small
complete path enumeration is an independent reference for testing a scalable implementation;
it is not a scalable method for every bank graph. If a graph has latent variables or selection
nodes, the evaluator needs the appropriate representation and separation criterion, rather than
treating its observed mixed graph as an ordinary DAG. The query also needs to distinguish
conditioning on a recorded covariate from intervening on it. A controlled experiment and an
observational subgroup do not generally describe the same probability distribution.


50.33.3        A nonsignificant test does not certify independence

The inspected prompt instructs the verifier to infer independence when a correlation test is
not significant. That rule confuses a sample decision with a population property. It can turn
an underpowered study into apparent evidence against a correct causal mechanism. It also
treats a selected test as if it were sensitive to every form of dependence. (Zhang et al., 2026b)
   For a finite illustration, let X be a randomized binary treatment with probability 1/2 and
let an independent flip V have probability 1/4. Set Y = X xor V . The four population cell
probabilities are

       (p00 , p01 , p10 , p11 ) = 81 (3, 1, 1, 3),        EY | do(X = 1) − EY | do(X = 0) = 12 .             (50.20)

In four independent observations, the event of one observation in every cell has probability
                                                      2  2
                                                      3       1          27
                                                4!                  =       .                                (50.21)
                                                      8       8         512
For that balanced table, Fisher’s two-sided exact test has p = 1. Conditional on both margins
being (2, 2), the upper-left cell under independence takes values 0, 1, 2 with probabilities
(1, 4, 1)/6; all three tables have probability no greater than that of the observed central table.
50.33. What literature disagreement can establish about a benchmark                         1373


The resulting sum is one. Complete enumeration of all 256 four-observation sequences finds
the 24 balanced sequences and the probability above. Yet the true randomized effect remains
1/2.(Causal banking proposal, 2026bp)
   If an outcome contributes a stipulated USD 100 and treatment costs USD 30, the population
incremental value is 100(1/2) − 30 = USD 20 per decision. Neither the four-row sample nor its
large p value establishes this value; it is known here only because the example stipulates the
structural law. The example demonstrates the possible loss from converting a nonsignificant
finding into a zero-effect declaration. It is not a proposal ROI estimate.
   A repaired extraction should preserve the estimator, sample size, sampling design, uncertainty
interval, null hypothesis and covariates. “Did not reject this null” is an admissible extracted
finding. “Established independence” requires a different justification. For a decision, an
equivalence analysis could target a scientifically chosen negligible-effect region, with its own
design and error control. A language model may help locate those details; it cannot supply
missing power, overlap or identification by rewriting the prose.

50.33.4    Unknown answers change the target of an inconsistency rate

The paper retains an unknown category and excludes unknown answers from its inconsistency
denominator. This is a useful distinction from forcing every paper into a binary label, but it
changes what a reported rate means. Write R = 1 when a query receives an answer and D = 1
when that answer is categorized as a contradiction. If r = P (R = 1) and q = P (D = 1 | R = 1),
then without an assumption on unknown cases, a latent full-query contradiction fraction d
obeys only
                                     rq ≤ d ≤ rq + 1 − r.                               (50.22)
The bound assumes that a meaningful binary contradiction status exists for every target query
and that answered labels are correct; context mismatch or misclassification requires further
treatment. The original answered-case metric does not make either additional premise true.
(Zhang et al., 2026b)
   In an authored example with 20 contradictions among 30 answered queries out of 100, the
answered-case rate is 2/3, the answer rate is 0.3, and the full-query range is [0.2, 0.9]. Both
endpoints are attained by assigning all unknown cases to one category. This is a missing-
information bound, not an interval for statistical sampling error.(Causal banking proposal,
2026bp) The pipeline should therefore report answer coverage alongside disagreement, and
distinguish unique papers, paper-pair queries and graph propositions. Several queries can
share one paper, and several papers can share a dataset; their labels are not automatically
independent replications.
   Retrieval introduces another selection layer. The inspected procedure uses PubMed/PMC
and OpenAlex-related access routes, caps ranked search results at 500 per pair, and caps
examined pairs at 200. Its verifier is the historical Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 model,
reported on an H100 80GB. Accessible text, search ranking, variable synonyms and the
relevance filter define the resulting evidence pool. An inconsistency rate in that pool is not
a random-sample estimate of all scientific evidence or all graph errors. The authors report
90 correct judgments in a manual sample of 100; the linked detailed artifact has not been
inspected here, so this remains their reported validation. (Zhang et al., 2026b)
   There are also unresolved source-accounting questions. The main text lists 69 benchmarks
while the appendix enumeration reaches 72. The introduction describes Barley as misaligned,
but the evaluated set excludes it. A separate bibliometric search reports 11,633 LLM causal-
discovery papers in 2025, while its appendix includes MATH, ImageNet and COCO among
prominent benchmark labels. Without resolving search specificity, that count cannot establish
1374                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


the size of the causal-discovery field. These limitations do not erase the value of evidence
retrieval; they limit the numerical and substantive claims that this proposal can inherit.(Zhang
et al., 2026b)


50.33.5    A repair that retains the useful human workflow

The useful adoption target is a reviewed evidence queue. Each item should link an exact
passage to the original PDF and record population, unit, variable definition, measurement date,
conditioning set, intervention and selection mechanism. A proposed conflict should identify
both propositions and explain why they refer to a comparable regime. For a banking diagram,
a relationship among approved borrowers cannot silently replace one among all applicants. An
updated sensor or accounting definition can require a new variable and measurement model
rather than an arrow reversal.
   The proposal can conditionally adopt retrieval, synonym suggestions and abstaining evidence
extraction. It should reject automatic benchmark relabeling from literature votes, adjacency-
as-correlation rules and nonsignificance-as- independence prompts. Direct software adoption
or a port remains contingent on inspecting pinned code, dependencies and rights. The
mathematical repairs are known: full separation checks, faithful versus Markov-only query
types, correct statistical statements, explicit missing-answer targets and reviewed context
alignment. Whether a repaired pipeline attains useful accuracy and cost is a prototype question,
not a result established by the present manuscript.
   A public prototype can make that question testable before a bank trial. Build a small adju-
dicated set of original passages and graph queries, including known collider cases, cancellation,
nonsignificant dependent samples, changed populations and deliberately unavailable evidence.
Keep both the graph truth for constructed cases and the expert justification for real passages
separate from the model’s suggestions. Compare keyword retrieval, human-only review and
an abstaining assistant on factual extraction, query validity, answer coverage, false conflict
alerts, review time and decision-relevant consequences. Preserve disagreements instead of
training on the test judgments. The mathematical examples specify failures that can be tested
now; broader scientific truth and banking relevance require the substantive evidence that the
workflow is designed to help a reviewer inspect.


50.34      Evaluate a causal coding workflow beyond its test-pass
           rate
A causal-analysis assistant can generate syntactically correct code, execute a query, and pass
tests while answering the wrong banking question. A repayment model might use postdecision
information; an effect estimator might target the wrong cohort; a reporting agent might
convert an execution failure to a zero effect. Evaluation must therefore identify the task, the
observations on which performance is measured, and the protocol that decides whether an
output is usable. Those choices connect the software interface to the scientific target and to
the economic case for a prototype.
   Two selected historical surveys help organize this distinction. Chang and coauthors’ evalua-
tion survey, inspected at its 6 July 2023 initial version, separates what to evaluate, where to
evaluate and how to evaluate. Its summary explicitly limits its success and failure conclusions
to particular datasets. It discusses automated and human assessment, prompt robustness,
complete behavioral tests and evolving benchmarks. It also asks whether a dynamically
constructed test is truly out of distribution. Dynamic generation is thus a design option,
50.34. Evaluate a causal coding workflow beyond its test-pass rate                             1375


not a certificate of novelty or freedom from contamination. These are historical organizing
arguments, not a current ranking of models. (Chang et al., 2023)
   Jiang and coauthors’ code-generation survey, inspected at its 1 June 2024 initial version,
covers data curation, model adaptation, repository and agent workflows, evaluation and
applications. It distinguishes text/structural similarity, execution metrics, human assessment
and model judging. The inspected performance tables compile cited model results; they are
not a harmonized experiment reproduced here. Its framework descriptions likewise need the
constituent technical originals before a package or claimed score can enter our admitted design.
The selected PDF’s template footer says September 2024, whereas the archive and first-page
stamp identify the June initial version. That footer does not establish journal publication or
equivalence to the later record that led to discovery.(Jiang et al., 2024)


50.34.1     A metric must define its sampling pool and selector

The code survey’s equation for pass-at-k uses a finite-pool expression of the form 1 − n−c    n
                                                                                                
                                                                                        k / k .
Its surrounding prose, however, describes c as the number of correct samples within the selected
k, despite defining n as the larger generated pool. These definitions conflict. Before adopting
the expression, the implementation must fix which pool the count refers to. The following
derivation is our own finite counting argument, not an attribution of an uninspected original
theorem.(Jiang et al., 2024)
   Let a fixed pool contain n = 10 candidates, of which exactly c = 3 pass a stipulated test
suite. Choose k = 2 candidates uniformly without replacement. There are 10 2 = 45 pairs, of
        7
which 2 = 21 contain no passing candidate. Thus
                                                          7
                                                          2     24   8
                         P (at least one passes) = 1 −    10 = 45 = 15 .                 (50.23)
                                                          2

The successful count in that formula is the number among all ten candidates. Substituting
the random number of successes in the selected pair instead gives a different quantity; exact
enumeration gives average 16/135, not 8/15. The source inconsistency must therefore be
resolved before it becomes a benchmark implementation or an accepted numerical comparison.
(Causal banking proposal project, 2026aj)
   An at-least-one success event does not specify how the deployed system finds that success.
If it chooses one of the two sampled candidates uniformly, its chance of selecting a passing
candidate remains 3/10. Reaching 8/15 as an output-success rate requires an oracle or a
suitably qualified selector that can recognize the passing candidate whenever one is present.
A selector using public tests, a model judge or analyst review has its own errors and costs.
For causal code, even a perfect test-suite selector establishes only success under those tests; it
does not establish identification assumptions or the relevance of the estimand.(Causal banking
proposal project, 2026aj)


50.34.2     Retain the attempted-request denominator

Consider a second authored example with twenty attempted causal coding tasks. Sixteen
produce runnable outputs; twelve pass their unit tests; seven preserve the declared causal target
and information clock; five satisfy the full output contract, including evidence and uncertainty.
These nested counts are stipulated to illustrate measurement design, not observations from a
model. The two headline rates are different:
                                       12  3                              5   1
                   rtests|runnable =      = ,     raccepted|attempted =      = .          (50.24)
                                       16  4                              20  4
1376                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


A report containing only the first rate would omit failed execution and scientific-contract
failures. The pipeline should retain the request identifier, eligibility decision, every candidate
and retry, selected result, failure or abstention reason, and final adjudication. The rates need
not be multiplied under an independence assumption: the example directly counts nested
outcomes. Correlated prompts and shared graph families also mean these twenty rows do
not automatically justify a binomial interval or twenty independent units of evidence.(Causal
banking proposal project, 2026aj)
   This requirement follows the surveys’ limitations rather than treating a benchmark as a
universal standard. The code survey stresses that execution metrics depend on unit-test quality
and omit attributes such as maintainability, efficiency, stability and repository dependencies.
Human review adds expertise but also cost, variance and reproducibility issues. Model judges
can inherit position, verbosity, self-enhancement and reasoning biases. The evaluation survey
similarly treats evaluator variability and the validity of the testing system as questions requiring
scrutiny. A causal workflow adds its own target, graph, clock, support and refusal semantics
to this broader software assessment.(Jiang et al., 2024; Chang et al., 2023)


50.34.3     Count costs on all attempts and benefits on accepted outputs

Suppose generation costs USD 2 and the test harness costs USD 1 for every attempt, while
specialist review costs USD 5 for each test-passing output. Suppose an accepted output is
worth USD 30 under an explicitly hypothetical valuation. For the twenty-task construction,

                               C = 20(2 + 1) + 12(5) = 120      USD,                        (50.25)
                    C/Naccepted = 120/5 = 24 USD per accepted output,                       (50.26)
                          B − C = 5(30) − 120 = 30 USD in total.                            (50.27)

Net value is USD 1.50 per attempted task. Equating all twelve test passes with accepted
outputs would instead produce USD 240 net and overstate value by USD 210. These prices
and benefits are assumptions; none is a model-provider quote, observed analyst saving or bank
ROI. The example demonstrates why the all-attempt cost ledger and acceptance rubric must
be frozen together before a prototype trial. A real experiment should additionally include
setup, retries, timeouts, correction, dependency maintenance and the cost of rejected work.
(Causal banking proposal project, 2026aj)


50.34.4     A public evaluation design for the proposed causal assistant

The proposal can test these ideas without authentic bank records. Generate declared structural
and tabular examples with known interventions, ambiguous graphs, missing outcomes, invalid
clocks and unsupported requests. Separate development graph families from evaluation families
and retain original generation seeds and source versions. Score formulation, diagram semantics,
identification, code execution, numerical output, uncertainty, reporting and appropriate refusal
separately. The classifier or judge for each stage must itself be checked on counterexamples;
agreement with a fluent explanation is not an independent causal oracle.
   Use unit tests for declared numerical and interface properties, source-grounded checks
for algorithm assumptions, and adjudicated scientific review where the target is ambiguous.
Report automatic, human and model-judge decisions with their disagreement rather than
substituting one for another invisibly. Randomize order when testing a model judge, retain
its version and prompt, and evaluate selection separately from candidate generation. The
survey discussions motivate these dimensions but do not prove that this proposed protocol is
calibrated. Historical benchmarks can supply leads and adverse examples; current package
50.35. Retrieval and adaptive repair need separate evidence and acceptance contracts         1377


adoption requires its own pinned originals and conformance. (Chang et al., 2023; Jiang et al.,
2024)
   The next experiment is consequently a bounded test of whether the assistant preserves a
declared causal contract at a useful all-request cost. Public and synthetic tasks can expose wrong
denominators, selection optimism, unsafe conversions and semantic errors before costly bank
experiments. They cannot verify an institution’s actual assignment mechanism, audit truth or
realized economic return. Those remain later questions after the prototype demonstrates why
further evidence would be worth acquiring.


50.35      Retrieval and adaptive repair need separate evidence
           and acceptance contracts
A causal banking assistant needs to retrieve the right evidence, translate it into a defensible
intervention question, produce an executable analysis, and recognize when the result does not
answer that question. Retrieval and iterative repair can support these stages, but their success
criteria differ. A faithfully quoted passage can be scientifically inapplicable; a program can
pass the tests it has repeatedly seen while using the wrong time window or treatment. The
proposal must therefore preserve the chain from source identity through causal meaning to
held-out decision quality.
   Two historical originals help sharpen this design. Gao and colleagues’ survey is inspected at
arXiv version 5 of 27 March 2024, distinct from its December 2023 initial discovery date. The
CoT-SelfEvolve study is inspected at arXiv version 1 of 28 August 2024. Its first page and
running footer also contain a 2025 conference template and placeholder DOI; those do not
establish a verified proceedings version. Archive metadata lists its first author as Quoc, Thai
Tang, while the PDF displays Thai Tang Quoc. The version and author-name distinction is
retained in the audit. Neither original establishes complete October 2026 frontier coverage.
(Gao et al., 2024; Quoc et al., 2024)


50.35.1     Retrieval faithfulness is narrower than causal evidence

The survey distinguishes a basic index–retrieve–generate pipeline, advanced pre- and post-
retrieval improvements, and modular pipelines that can rearrange or repeat retrieval and
generation. Basic indexing converts source documents into chunks and representations; retrieval
ranks context for a query; generation uses that context to answer. Query rewriting, finer
indexing, metadata, reranking and compression can improve the fit between question and
material. Modular search and iterative retrieval provide alternatives when a single initial query
is inadequate. These are useful architectural choices, not proof that a retrieved statement is
true or that a generated graph is identified. (Gao et al., 2024)
   For a bank asking whether a servicing call prevents default, retrieval must retain more
than a passage containing both terms. An observational prediction study, a randomized call
policy and a vendor’s marketing description can all be semantically similar to the question
while supporting different claims. The proposed evidence object therefore records source
type, original date and version, population, treatment and outcome definitions, assignment
mechanism, measurement clock, assumptions and the precise claim supported. Rewriting the
business question may produce several candidate estimands; it must not silently replace an
intervention with a correlation because that version retrieves more text. This evidence-object
design is a project proposal motivated by the survey’s retrieval and augmentation distinctions,
not a capability reported for an already integrated package. (Gao et al., 2024)
1378                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The survey separately evaluates retrieval quality and generation quality. It distinguishes
context relevance, answer faithfulness and answer relevance, and discusses noise resistance,
refusal when necessary knowledge is missing, integration across documents and resistance
to known false retrieved statements. Its term counterfactual robustness means recognizing
and rejecting inaccuracies in documents. It does not mean identifying a potential outcome or
preserving cross-world structural dependence. Confusing these uses of the same word would
let a language benchmark appear to qualify a causal capability it never tested. The survey
also warns that the listed evaluation metrics were not yet a mature, standardized system.
A package name or metric family in its comparison is a lead for primary inspection, not an
automatically adopted scoring implementation. (Gao et al., 2024)
   A public evaluation can make these distinctions concrete before a costly bank trial. Construct
matched evidence packets containing a relevant original, a wrong-population study, a later
revision, a contradictory source and an unsupported confident claim. Preserve their identities
and the gold-supported conclusions. Score retrieval of the needed evidence separately from
faithful quotation, applicability to the declared estimand and justified refusal. Then require
the proposed graph to mark unsupported edges and alternatives. Removing an irrelevant
source should not alter a justified answer; removing the only identification assumption should
change its status. These are proposed perturbation and evidence tests, not a claim that a
retrieved paper establishes an actual bank’s assignment mechanism. The survey’s discussion
of noise, contradiction and source/metadata exposure motivates such explicit checks. (Gao
et al., 2024)


50.35.2    What the self-correction study actually measures

CoT-SelfEvolve combines retrieved StackOverflow discussions, generated reasoning prompts,
initial code, syntax checking, execution against unit tests and feedback- guided revisions. Its
feedback is partly external: tracebacks and test outcomes come from an executor rather than
from a model merely reconsidering its prose. The inspected protocol uses the Completion
setting of DS-1000, comprising 1,000 problems across seven Python libraries. It reports a
retrieval collection of 558,402 posts and 972,513 comments, with a minimum-comment filter
and a token budget for assembled documents. The paper also describes its benchmark tasks as
extracted from StackOverflow. This shared origin motivates an explicit retrieval/benchmark
overlap audit; the inspected descriptions do not establish that leakage occurred or that every
relevant overlap was removed. (Quoc et al., 2024)
   The study defines pass@n as the fraction of problems for which all tests pass within at
most n sequential attempts, examining budgets from one to five. Later attempts can use
feedback from earlier ones. This differs from the event that a uniformly chosen subset of an
independent candidate pool contains a passing program. It also differs from passing a fresh
causal acceptance test. The proposed product should retain the paper’s operational definition
rather than treating identical-looking pass notation as a common metric. (Quoc et al., 2024)
   The reported comparisons are informative but protocol-specific. Table 1 gives an aggregate
change from 30.5 to 35.5 percent when both prompt generators are enabled; Table 2 gives 35.5
to 39.5 percent when the prompt generator uses the larger model while the code generator
remains fixed. Arithmetic on those printed, rounded values gives
                                                                35.5 − 30.5  10
             35.5 − 30.5 = 5.0 percentage points,                           = ,
                                                                   30.5      61
                                                                39.5 − 35.5   8
             39.5 − 35.5 = 4.0 percentage points,                           = .           (50.28)
                                                                   35.5      71
The relative changes are approximately 16.39 and 11.27 percent, respectively; they are not
50.35. Retrieval and adaptive repair need separate evidence and acceptance contracts         1379


increases of that many percentage points. Table 1 also shows heterogeneity: the SciPy entry
changes from 33.02 to 32.08 percent with both prompt generators enabled. A positive aggregate
therefore does not establish a gain for every library or every causal-analysis task. No raw
counts or paired uncertainty interval is recovered from these rounded percentages. (Quoc et al.,
2024; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ai)
   For its GPT-4 attempt-budget experiment, Table 3 reports overall success rising from 14.0
to 83.2 percent between one and five allowed attempts. The text reports prompt tokens rising
from 2.54 million to 9.29 million, while completion tokens do not rise at the same rate. This is
evidence about the reported historical protocol, not a present model benchmark or a full cost-
benefit analysis. Cross-figure and cross-table totals should not be pooled without reconciling
settings and runs. The authors themselves discuss proprietary model drift, temperature and
sampling settings, and the dependence on available unit tests. Their analogy between five
refinement steps and five usability testers does not supply an optimal-stopping theorem for
code or causal analysis. (Quoc et al., 2024)
   Executable reuse has an additional unresolved prerequisite. The selected original’s repro-
ducibility statement gives ANONYMIZED-LINK for its code and prepared data. That is not a
resolved repository identity, version or license. It is therefore appropriate to retain the method
as a research comparator while deferring code adoption. A similarly named repository cannot
be substituted without establishing authorship and correspondence. Proposed CI integration
in the discussion also does not demonstrate that such an integration has already been built
here. (Quoc et al., 2024)


50.35.3     Count failed attempts and accepted causal outputs

A small authored example shows why the stopping and acceptance records matter. Consider
ten requests with a maximum of three attempts. Their first test-passing attempts are

                                   (1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, ∅, ∅, ∅, ∅),                        (50.29)

where ∅ means that no candidate passes within the budget. The cumulative counts of passing
requests are two, five and six. The six successful requests use eleven attempts in total; the
four failures consume twelve more. Thus all-request cost uses 23 attempts, not eleven. The
average attempt count is 2.3 across all requests, compared with 11/6 if failures are omitted.
Suppose a separate causal review accepts only four of the six test-passing outputs because two
violate the frozen estimand or information clock. Test success is 6/10, while accepted causal
output is 4/10. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ai)
  Assume USD 2 per attempt and USD 15 value per accepted output. The complete cost and
net value are

                                 C = 2(23) = USD 46,
                              C/4 = USD 11.50 per accepted output,
                          Vaccepted = 15(4) − 46 = USD 14,
                          Vtest only = 15(6) − 46 = USD 44.                               (50.30)

Equating test passes with accepted causal outputs overstates this stipulated net value by USD
30. The example does not measure actual token prices, engineering labor, model performance
or bank ROI. Its role is to enforce a complete denominator before real economic evaluation,
including unsuccessful retrieval, repair, runtime and human adjudication. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026ai)

50.35.4     A public prototype protocol before paid trials

The proposal can now specify a bounded public experiment. Freeze the source corpus and
exclusions, model/backend version, prompt and package environment, maximum attempts and
stopping rule. Compare one-shot generation, executor- feedback repair and retrieval-assisted
repair under the same request budget. Keep the feedback tests distinct from a final acceptance
set that checks causal target, time alignment, graph and identification scope, uncertainty
and refusal. Include deliberate missing-evidence cases, misleading retrieval, future leakage,
wrong treatment definitions and syntactically correct but causally invalid programs. Log every
retrieved source and every attempt; assess accepted outputs and complete cost jointly. This
design combines the survey’s component-level criteria with the empirical study’s adaptive
feedback structure without borrowing either source’s reported score as a product guarantee.
(Gao et al., 2024; Quoc et al., 2024; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ai)
   Proceeding requires a genuine artifact for an executable CoT-SelfEvolve comparison, in-
spected originals for any adopted retrieval/evaluation package, and an independently specified
final acceptance oracle. Where these are absent, use explicitly authored reference components
and label them accordingly. Public evidence can justify whether a prototype merits an expen-
sive banking experiment; it cannot establish institutional data truth or replace subsequent
owner acceptance. The historical findings narrow the design and expose concrete failure modes
while leaving broader frontier coverage and adoption open. (Gao et al., 2024; Quoc et al.,
2024)


50.36      COAT: eliciting measured factors without assuming
           causal truth
Consider a servicing team with customer narratives, offer decisions and later repayment
outcomes. Its first difficulty may be defining usable variables: does a phrase describe a
pre-existing cash-flow shock, a customer’s reaction to the offer, or a retrospective explanation
written after default? A language model can suggest a factor and extract its value, but the
suggestion, the measurement and the causal role require different evidence. The selected
13 October 2025 revision of Liu and colleagues’ COAT framework addresses this interface
between unstructured observations and causal analysis. It proposes and parses factors, then
uses conventional causal-discovery feedback to refine them. The paper separates COAT-MB
for Markov blankets, COAT-PAG for refining partial ancestral graphs, and COAT-ADJ for
adjustment questions. This is a useful architecture for a banking prototype whose variables
are not already settled.(Liu et al., 2025)


50.36.1     What the representation assistant contributes

In the paper’s notation, X is unstructured input, U is a set of structured target variables
and W = h(X) is a proposed structured representation. A factor instruction specifies a
deterministic map from the input to a numerical value. The initial sampling setup uses
independently drawn paired observations. COAT-MB proposes factors in rounds, parses their
values and updates a target’s Markov blanket. Its feedback selects a cluster where the existing
factors leave high conditional entropy of the target. The algorithm stops at a maximum number
of rounds or an unchanged blanket. These choices describe an adaptive search procedure; the
stopping condition does not itself certify that all relevant factors have been found. (Liu et al.,
2025)
  For the bank, a factor definition therefore needs an observable interpretation, an extraction
50.36. COAT: eliciting measured factors without assuming causal truth                            1381


rule, a timestamp and a missingness convention. “Temporary income interruption” should not
acquire a different meaning depending on the desired intervention answer. If it is read from a
note written after repayment, its predictive usefulness does not make it a pre-offer confounder.
Proposed factors can be retained as hypotheses while their provenance and clock are examined.
An ordinary prediction improvement is useful feedback, but it does not decide which variables
are eligible adjustment controls.
  The following project derivation makes an information limit explicit. For a fixed mapping
W = h(X), if a relevant variable U is independent of X, it remains independent of W : for any
event B of the representation,
                                X
       P (U = u, W ∈ B) =               P (U = u)P (X = x) = P (U = u)P (W ∈ B)               (50.31)
                             x:h(x)∈B

in the discrete case. Naming a plausible hidden cause cannot create its customer-specific
measurement. Additional records or informative measurement assumptions may help; the
example is not a prohibition on extracting genuine information already present in text.
The paper’s “hidden world” concerns eliciting high-level factors from observations, not an
unconditional ability to identify every unobserved cause.(Liu et al., 2025)

50.36.2     The parsing assumption is scientifically substantive

The selected paper explicitly assumes faithful and Markov correspondence between a graph and
the factor distribution, with conditional independences preserved after parsing. It acknowledges
that annotation error can violate this premise. High marginal accuracy is consequently
insufficient to establish that a parsed variable can replace its true counterpart in adjustment
or conditional-independence tests.(Liu et al., 2025)
  An exact project-authored mechanism illustrates the issue. Let U be a fair binary pre-offer
cause, let the offer A and repayment Y be conditionally independent given U , and specify
 P (A = 1 | U ) = P (Y = 1 | U ) = 14 + 12 U,     W = U ⊕ E,         E ∼ Bernoulli(1/4), (50.32)
where E is independent of the other structural randomizations and ⊕ denotes exclusive-or.
There is no A → Y arrow: the true offer effect is zero, and both interventional repayment risks
equal 1/2. The proxy W is 75% accurate. Nevertheless, conditional on either value of W , U
retains variance 3/16. The conditional covariance is
                      Cov(A, Y | W = w) = 14 Var(U | W = w) = 64
                                                              3
                                                                 > 0.                         (50.33)
The factor error has destroyed the conditional independence that held given U . This is a
deliberate violation of the paper’s parsing assumption, not evidence of failure when that
assumption holds.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026z)
  The exact conditional repayment risks for (a, w) =                (0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) are
3/10, 1/2, 1/2, 7/10. Standardizing over the fair proxy gives
       X                                        X
           P (Y = 1 | A = 0, w)P (w) = 52 ,          P (Y = 1 | A = 1, w)P (w) = 35 .         (50.34)
