The spurious effect is 1/5. With an assumed USD 100 payoff per incremental repayment and
USD 10 offer cost, that calculation yields USD 10, whereas the true zero-effect offer has net
value USD −10. The positive joint law is enumerated with rational arithmetic; no COAT run,
empirical annotation rate or actual bank benefit is being reported. The proposed implication is
to evaluate extraction errors by variable, outcome, treatment and time, rather than accepting
a single overall accuracy number as a causal qualification. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026z)
1382                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


50.36.3    Separate iterative discovery from a finite stopping guarantee

COAT’s ability definition posits a positive probability of proposing a useful factor and a
positive multiplicative reduction in residual information. Its convergence discussion then uses
these quantities to characterize successful discovery rounds. The proof of Proposition 5 treats
the number of useful rounds as binomial and explicitly approximates that distribution by a
Gaussian. That calculation is informative about the proposed regime, but an uncontrolled
approximation cannot be adopted as an exact finite probability certificate for a banking run.
The model for repeated useful proposals also needs to match an adaptive agent’s history and
failure modes.(Liu et al., 2025)
   For example, four independent proposal rounds with success probability 1/2 have no-success
probability 1/16. If all four outcomes equal one shared fair Bernoulli variable, each round still
has marginal success probability 1/2, but the chance of no success is 1/2. Repeated versions of
the same unsuccessful hypothesis can resemble the latter dependence pattern. The authored
example does not diagnose a measured COAT dependence structure; it shows why marginal
responsiveness alone cannot specify a multi-round success probability.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026z)
   A public prototype should predeclare the proposal budget, the meaning of a useful factor and
the evidence supplied as feedback. If a quantitative convergence claim is sought, it must state
whether successes are independent with a fixed probability or satisfy an explicit conditional
lower bound given the preceding history. It also needs a justified contraction statement and
an exact or controlled probability bound. Without those premises, a maximum-round stop
is a resource limit and an unchanged blanket is a search observation. Neither is upgraded
to “all causal variables recovered.” Separate final tasks should remain outside the feedback
loop so that repeated improvement on the development sample is not counted again as fresh
validation.


50.36.4    Graph preservation and effect estimation retain their conditions

The paper’s graph extensions add further structure beyond a single target’s blanket. Its
Proposition 8 states adjacency and arrowhead preservation within a subset under blanket
inclusion in the enlarged variable set and the stated maximally informative PAG setup.
The adjustment development additionally uses amenability, forbidden-variable and blocking
conditions. Proposition 15 preserves an adjustment set under its specified blanket-inclusion
premise. These are conditional results about the constructed measured-variable graph; they are
not general certificates for arbitrary hidden-confounder or cross-world questions. A proposed
adapter must preserve uncertain marks and refuse an effect query when the applicable premises
or adjustment route are unresolved.(Liu et al., 2025)
   The marketing evaluation uses Hillstrom and Retail Hero in a confounded evaluation setting
with synthesized social-media text. For each experiment, the authors choose the largest valid
adjustment sets from the generated PAG and average estimated effects when there are multiple
such sets; experiments are repeated three times. The extracted Table 7 reports COAT RMSEs
of 0.47 and 0.50 for DeepSeek-V3, and 1.90 and 0.78 for GPT-4.1-mini on the two datasets. The
human-factor N-IPW reference reports 1.32 and 1.39. Thus the comparative result depends
on model and comparator: the first GPT-4.1-mini number does not beat that human-factor
reference. These are source-reported outcomes in the paper’s design, not locally reproduced
estimation or confidence-interval calibration.(Liu et al., 2025)
   For a proposed lending study, average error, graph validity, adjustment availability and
interval coverage should be recorded separately. A failure to recover a valid set must remain in
50.37. Simulated customers and causal assistants need different experiments                     1383


the request denominator. Averaging effects over several selected sets does not remove the need
to justify their validity or account for selection and dependence. A generated-text benchmark
can expose parser and graph failures at low cost, but it does not establish that authentic
customer narratives measure the same factors.


50.36.5     Financial examples motivate a clock and cost audit

COAT’s financial case uses Microsoft price and news observations from 2006–2009, with the
first 200 trading days for elicitation and the next 400 for evaluation. The target describes the
sign of a following-week return. The reported strategy fits a rolling regression and takes a long
or short position according to its predicted sign. This is an observational trading illustration.
Its reported performance does not identify the effect of a bank action on a customer outcome.
The printed rolling-window summation limits also need clarification against the executable
source; this proposal does not silently repair them and assume the code did the same thing.(Liu
et al., 2025)
  A faithful public reproduction would bind news-publication times, data availability, revision
policy, normalization windows, forecast horizon and trade execution time. Overlapping weekly
outcomes require a declared dependence treatment. It would retain transaction costs, financing
and failed-query costs before interpreting a trading return as a useful economic comparison.
This is an inexpensive way to test the proposed workflow’s meaning before requesting bank
data, rather than treating a published historical return as bank ROI.
   The proposed integration is therefore a staged representation-assistant boundary: factor
instructions and source passages enter a reviewed ontology; the parser produces values with
provenance and explicit missingness; graphical analysis preserves uncertainty and scientific
refusals; downstream estimation records its own assumptions. The paper’s project link is
a source-code lead, not an audited repository, license or runtime. Native artifact review,
measurement-error evaluation and finite stopping guarantees remain separate work. Public
or stipulated gold factors can demonstrate whether this route merits those later experiments,
while independent acceptance and authentic bank truth remain later evidence.(Liu et al., 2025;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026z)


50.37       Simulated customers and causal assistants need different
            experiments
A bank considering a new servicing message may ask a language model two different questions.
How would a customer with a given history respond to the message? Which features of the
history justify a causal explanation of the response? The first question invites a simulated
respondent; the second asks for assistance with a causal model. A convincing answer to either
question does not establish the other. This distinction determines what a public-data prototype
should test before an expensive bank experiment is justified.
   Simmons and Hare review language models as subpopulation representative models: systems
intended to reproduce behavior or opinions of a specified population. They organize prompting,
fine-tuning, grounding data and deployment, and distinguish direct comparison with observed
responses, human assessment and qualitative aggregate evaluation. Their five guiding criteria
are fidelity, necessity, robustness, sensitivity and fairness. In this use, a demographic description
is a proposed conditioning variable; it is not evidence that the generated respondent represents
a customer selected by the bank’s actual contact and response processes.(Simmons and Hare,
2023)
1384                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The selected May 2026 revision of Cai, Liu and Song instead manipulates inputs to a causal
assistant. It compares variable names, numerical information and their removal, then studies
instruction fine-tuning on pairwise discovery tasks. These experiments concern the assistant’s
behavior under controlled input conditions. They can guide a prototype evaluation without
turning an assistant’s answer into customer-level intervention evidence. (Cai et al., 2026)


50.37.1    A precise simulation can retain a population error

For a fixed customer segment, response definition and historical period, let p be the true
probability of a specified binary response. Let q be the probability that a fixed language-model
configuration generates that response. Both probabilities refer to the same question, but to
different populations of outcomes. Suppose, for this project derivation, that M independent
decoder draws have common success probability q, and let qbM be their mean. Then

                                                           q(1 − q)
                             E{(qbM − p)2 } = (q − p)2 +            .                      (50.35)
                                                              M
This follows by writing qbM − p = (qbM − q) + (q − p); the cross term has expectation zero. More
draws reduce Monte Carlo error around the model’s own response law. They do not remove
the discrepancy between that law and the target population. If p must itself be estimated from
a survey, uncertainty and selection error in that estimate are additional obligations.(Causal
banking proposal project, 2026at)
   For an exact assumed example, take p = 1/2, q = 3/5 and M = 10,000. The squared
discrepancy is 1/100, while the simulation variance is only 3/125,000. If a specified response
earns USD 100 and each contact costs USD 55, the model suggests USD 5 per contact while
the stipulated population law gives USD −5. This is a generated planning example, not an
estimated bank return. Moreover, a response forecast is not automatically an incremental
effect of contacting a customer: that decision also needs the relevant no-contact potential
outcome and identification assumptions. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026at)
   The survey’s distinction between consistency, pattern correspondence and diversity is useful
here. Producing a syntactically valid answer or a plausible customer narrative is a weaker test
than matching joint response patterns and within-segment variation. Its distinction between
apparent and actual model sensitivity also cautions against treating a demographic prompt
as a complete description of the information on which the model relies. (Simmons and Hare,
2023)
   A proposal-stage comparison can therefore use a frozen public response dataset, with its
population, dates, response construct and reuse terms documented. The comparison should
include simple empirical or statistical response models, preserve subgroup denominators, and
evaluate held-out responses and their joint variation. That establishes a bounded descriptive
task. A second, separately declared experiment must test an intervention question under
a known generated mechanism or a defensible public causal design. Simulated respondents
are useful for testing interfaces, eliciting possible failure cases and comparing designs; their
apparent realism supplies no additional observed bank customers.


50.37.2    Input ablations identify a controlled assistant experiment

In the attribution paper, context and model conditions are held fixed while names associated
with domain knowledge and numerical data are varied. Write akd for the correctness probability
under a fully specified input construction, where k = 1 retains meaningful variable names,
d = 1 retains numerical input, and zero denotes the corresponding removal. The probability
50.37. Simulated customers and causal assistants need different experiments                   1385


law must state whether it averages over tasks, decoder randomness, or both. The paper’s
conditional and marginal attributions can then be written as

                    CAK = a11 − a01 ,                      CAD = a11 − a10 ,
                    MAK = a10 − a00 ,                      MAD = a01 − a00 .               (50.36)

Here CAK and CAD retain the other input, while MAK and MAD compare against the
no-name, no-data baseline. The selected paper implements removal of name-associated cues
through arbitrary replacement names and removal of data through prompts containing names
alone. Its prompting discussion also distinguishes wording that asks an assistant to “suggest”
a relationship from wording that may induce noncommittal responses. (Cai et al., 2026)
   These are concrete changes to an interface. Replacing names does not delete the model’s
learned parameters, remove every semantic cue in the context, or prove that all other aspects
of difficulty are unchanged. The defensible experimental target is the effect of the declared
prompt transformation on assistant performance. Calling that transformation knowledge
removal requires additional construct-validity evidence. A refusal must remain an observed
outcome; a more encouraging prompt should not improve a score merely by removing refusals
from its denominator.
   The equality MAD − MAK = CAD − CAK follows algebraically from the four cells. It does
not independently test whether the prompt transformations isolate knowledge and data. To
see what the conditional comparisons count, define the project-derived interaction

                I = a11 − a10 − a01 + a00 ,     CAK + CAD = (a11 − a00 ) + I.              (50.37)

For assumed cell probabilities (a11 , a10 , a01 , a00 ) = (9/10, 3/5, 2/5, 3/10), the total gain is
3/5, the interaction is 1/5, and the two conditional attributions sum to 4/5. Adding them
as independent portions of improvement counts the interaction twice. The ordered paths
CAK + MAD and CAD + MAK each equal the total gain. These exact values illustrate the
estimand; they are not measurements from the paper.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026at)
   For a banking assistant, a paired factorial design should freeze the model, system instructions,
permitted tools, decoding settings and response parser. Each generating mechanism should
appear under all declared input conditions, with randomized ordering and separate conversation
state. The test should record correct, incorrect, ambiguous and refused outputs. Names should
include both informative and deliberately misleading descriptions, so that a familiar story
cannot substitute for the numerical assumptions that identify a graph.


50.37.3     Residual independence must survive the instruction boundary

The fine-tuning section supplies names, definitions and numerical results from discovery
algorithms in the instruction. It describes four pairwise scenarios through residual correlation,
including an undefined direction and the two possible directed relations. It then teaches an
assistant to use knowledge when the numerical direction is undefined. This description raises
a specific interface question: does the actual numerical artifact test independence under the
required model, or only ordinary zero correlation? The inspected paper does not settle the
native implementation of that boundary. (Cai et al., 2026)
   An exact project example shows why that distinction matters. Let independent X, U each
take values −1 and 1 with equal probability, and set Y = 2X + U . The forward population
least-squares residual is U , independent of X. The reverse slope and residual are

Both Cov(X, U ) and Cov(Y, R) are zero. The latter is the ordinary least-squares orthogonality

                                 9                                               16

Thus the reverse residual is dependent on its regressor despite zero linear correlation. A

this comparison. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026at)
   The proposed adapter should consequently carry the numerical method, its assumptions,
the actual dependence test, sample size, uncertainty and refusal state into the assistant’s input.
If the engine reports an unidentified direction, a language-model suggestion can become a
separately labeled hypothesis or request for additional evidence. It must not silently turn that
state into an identified edge. A benchmark that rewards confident completion of an undefined
scenario needs a different acceptance interpretation from a banking assistant that preserves
uncertainty.


50.37.4     Reported performance and a public qualification design

The attribution study uses nine datasets with fifteen column permutations each, giving 135
task instances. Its TDR divides correctly predicted pairs by true causal pairs; it also reports
false discovery rate, structural Hamming distance and F1. Those measures answer different
questions, so high TDR alone cannot certify that the assistant avoids additional false edges.
The reverse task describes keeping numerical values intact while changing the proposed ordering
or adjacency. Such a transformation is a useful input challenge, but it does not itself generate
observations from a new intervention law. (Cai et al., 2026)
   For instruction fine-tuning, the paper reports 300 pairs producing 1,200 training instances
and 106 pairs producing 424 testing instances. It names Mistral-7B-v0.2 with a LoRA adapter
in its training description. Table 4 reports overall accuracy 0.90 for the fine-tuned model,
compared with 0.82 for GPT-4 turbo, while the undefined scenario scores 0.58 versus 0.66.
The comparison therefore supports a scoped reported gain, not superiority on every scenario.
Its later table uses “Mixtral” wording despite the main training description; exact weight and
code identity require resolution before adoption. Equal scores on three additional tasks are not
a universal no-forgetting result. The paper itself leaves wider benchmark transfer, finite-sample
behavior, missing data and uncertainty-weighted evidence combination as limitations or future
work.(Cai et al., 2026)
  Repeated prompts quantify one kind of instability, not new independent domains. Under
an illustrative law in which all fifteen outcomes within each dataset are identical and the
nine datasets are independent, 135 calls contain nine independent units. This extreme is an
authored example, not an estimate of the paper’s dependence. A proposed comparison should
preserve dataset and mechanism groups, hold out causal pairs and generating mechanisms,
and report both within-task variability and variation across tasks. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026at)
   The first prototype can be inexpensive. Its generated mechanisms should include known
directions, observational ambiguity, latent-confounding violations, and the residual witness
above. Its baselines should include a numerical engine alone, a deterministic translation of
that engine’s result, an untuned assistant and the proposed tuned assistant. Success requires
faithful preservation of numerical evidence and uncertainty, alongside any improvement in
explanation or discovery; agreement with a convenient answer template alone is insufficient.
50.38. Measuring whether a causal assistant has improved                                    1387


Execution traces should separate the numerical result, its transformation into an instruction
and the assistant’s final claim, making a failed boundary localizable.
  Public population-response evaluation and generated causal tasks establish different merits.
Together they can justify whether further prototype work is worth funding, while keeping
actual bank response truth, institutional review and investment acceptance as later decisions.
Neither a large synthetic respondent pool nor a high assistant score replaces the banking
question’s population, information clock, causal assumptions and uncertainty contract.


50.38      Measuring whether a causal assistant has improved
A bank comparing two causal assistants needs to distinguish a better answer from an answer
that is easier for its grader to approve. An assistant may produce a polished diagram, an
executable adjustment formula and a confident explanation while changing the population,
conditioning on a variable measured after the decision, or overlooking an unmeasured common
cause. A test that rewards the format can improve while the scientific error remains. Conversely,
an assistant that correctly refuses a nonidentified query can look worse under a rubric that
rewards every numerical response. The evaluation must therefore specify the scientific service,
the observation used to assess it and the conditions under which the observation measures
that service.
   Lin’s validity-guided workflow separates an LLM used as a research tool, an evaluation
target, a human simulator and a cognitive model. Its six stages connect the intended claim
to instrument development, experimental design, documented execution, dependence-aware
analysis and bounded interpretation. The source is a methodological tutorial, with illustrative
supplementary code; it does not report an original empirical validation of a banking assistant.
For this proposal, its most useful contribution is the discipline of validating the measurement
before interpreting a model comparison. A classifier requires evidence that it performs its
specified task; fluent explanations do not establish a psychological mechanism, and simulated
customer answers require separate evidence of correspondence to the intended population.
(Lin, 2026)


50.38.1     The target is correctness under a declared information contract

Consider a retention-offer question whose request identifies the eligible customers, the offer
time, the balance horizon and the information available before the offer. The assistant must
preserve these elements when it proposes a graph and an estimand. A useful benchmark
includes several legitimate outputs: a supported identification formula, an explicit effect set,
or a refusal that names the missing assumption or observation. Correctness is judged against
the stated graph class and information, rather than against a single preferred diagram. If the
scenario does not determine an edge direction, selecting the examiner’s favorite direction is
not the target.
   Let A ∈ {0, 1} denote the assigned assistant workflow, with the base model, retrieval access
and available tools specified for each arm. Let C = 1 mean that an answer meets a frozen
semantic criterion. Let G = 1 mean that a grader marks the answer as passing. These are
distinct binary variables. The criterion could require a correct adjustment set and an explicit
warning about an unidentified query; other criteria, such as factual grounding and valid code,
should also be reported individually. A single binary endpoint is introduced here only to
expose a measurement problem. It cannot capture every consequence of a wrong scientific
answer.
1388                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


  Define pa = Pr(C = 1 | A = a), grader sensitivity sa = Pr(G = 1 | C = 1, A = a) and grader
specificity ca = Pr(G = 0 | C = 0, A = a). All probabilities refer to the same declared scenario
and answer population. By conditioning on correctness,

       qa := Pr(G = 1 | A = a) = sa pa + (1 − ca )(1 − pa ) = (sa + ca − 1)pa + 1 − ca .       (50.40)

This is an authored measurement model, not an empirical estimate from Lin’s tutorial. Random
assignment of A, consistency of the assigned workflows and an appropriate no-interference
condition can identify a causal effect on the observed grade for the experimental population.
Those conditions alone do not make q1 − q0 an effect on semantic correctness. The relation
between G and C must also be supported. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026aw)


50.38.2       A better grade can conceal an unchanged answer

Suppose true correctness equals p0 = p1 = 3/5. Impose grader properties (s0 , c0 ) = (4/5, 9/10)
for the first workflow and (s1 , c1 ) = (19/20, 4/5) for the second. The more polished out-
put is easier to recognize when correct but also more likely to be approved when wrong.
These properties are assumptions of the example, not observations about a particular grader.
Equation (50.40) gives
                 13                    13                          13
          q0 =      = 0.52,     q1 =      = 0.65,      q1 − q0 =       ,   p1 − p0 = 0.        (50.41)
                 25                    20                          100
More samples can estimate the observed 13-percentage-point improvement more precisely
while leaving its interpretation wrong. Randomizing the workflow does not remove this error
because the workflow itself changes the relation between the answer and its measurement.
  If the two calibration quantities are known for each arm and sa + ca ̸= 1, inversion gives
                                                 qa + ca − 1
                                          pa =               .                                 (50.42)
                                                 sa + ca − 1
It recovers 3/5 in both arms of the example. Even an invariant grader need not preserve the
size of an improvement. With s = 4/5, c = 9/10, changing true correctness from 1/2 to 7/10
changes observed passing by 7/50; dividing by s + c − 1 = 7/10 recovers the true change of
1/5. When s + c = 1, the grade contains no information about p: with s = c = 1/2, true
correctness 1/10 and 9/10 both produce a pass probability of 1/2. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026aw)
   Calibration is therefore an information requirement. In practice, sa and ca must be estimated
using held-out adjudication under the intended arms, scenario population and rubric. Both
correct and incorrect cases need support; verification only of accepted answers cannot identify
both quantities without additional sampling information. Uncertainty in the three inputs must
propagate through the ratio in (50.42). A denominator close to zero makes correction unstable.
Known bounds on calibration can instead be propagated to a set of compatible correctness
rates, intersected with [0, 1]; an unsupported point correction should not be substituted. Model
updates, subgroup differences and changes in answer style can invalidate transported calibration.
A finite example with known probabilities proves none of those transport assumptions.
   The economic consequence is immediate but remains conditional. Suppose, solely for
planning, that an additional correct result is worth USD 100 and the new workflow costs USD 8
more per request. Using true correctness, the incremental expected value is 100(p1 −p0 )−8 = −8
dollars. Substituting grades produces 100(q1 − q0 ) − 8 = 5 dollars. The sign reverses without
any improvement in the scientific service. Real costs of wrong advice, useful refusal and delayed
decisions may differ sharply; the example supplies neither a bank price nor an investment
recommendation. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026aw)
50.38. Measuring whether a causal assistant has improved                                   1389


50.38.3    Repeated answers and the population of inference

Lin distinguishes individual observations, experimental units and units of analysis, and
recommends pairing answers to shared items and respecting grouped observations. This
guidance must be applied to the actual design. A fixed model version is not automatically
a randomly sampled model from a population, and a prompt condition is not automatically
the smallest randomized unit. If a workflow is randomized across independent scenarios, the
scenario can be the assignment unit. If both workflows are run on each scenario with controlled
order and fresh contexts, the paired difference can be the analysis unit. These designs target
different sources of variation from repeatedly sampling decoder outputs for one fixed question.
(Lin, 2026)
   Aggregation preserves the dependence that remains between groups. To make this qualifica-
tion explicit, consider an authored real-valued score model
                                                                      R
                                                                   1 X
                      Zjr = U + Vj + ejr ,        Z j = U + Vj +         ejr ,          (50.43)
                                                                   R r=1

where all distinct components are independent, have zero mean, and have finite variances
σU2 , σV2 , σe2 . Here j indexes groups and r repeated scores; the common U can represent a
shared evaluation-environment shock. This is a separate real-valued example, not the binary
measurement model. For distinct groups j, k,

                                                σe2
                      Var(Z j ) = σU2 + σV2 +       ,   Cov(Z j , Z k ) = σU2 .         (50.44)
                                                R
With variances 1/4, 1/2, 1 and R = 20, group means have variance 4/5, covariance 1/4
and correlation 5/16. Averaging has reduced decoder noise but has not made the groups
independent. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026aw)
   Accordingly, the tutorial’s shorthand about aggregation eliminating correlation cannot
justify independent group means without assumptions about the shared environment and
scenario sampling. No fixed cluster-count threshold guarantees calibration, and balanced group
sizes alone do not establish a universal equivalence between aggregation and every mixed model.
For a fixed list of models, descriptive paired differences over a declared scenario collection
may be the honest result. Generalization to unseen scenarios requires a sampling or transport
argument; generalization to future model versions requires another.


50.38.4    A public evaluation design for the proposed service

The proposed first evaluation uses generated causal mechanisms with known identification
status, together with public scenario descriptions whose permitted uses and limitations are
documented. Generated mechanisms allow an exact answer key for graph compatibility and
intervention queries. Public business descriptions test translation and missing-information
detection, but their prose does not supply hidden causal truth. The two sources should retain
separate outcome denominators and support different claims.
  During development, analysts can revise prompts, retrieval rules and the semantic rubric
on a designated subset. The final evaluation then freezes those choices and withholds whole
mechanisms and scenario families, including their paraphrases and graph-isomorphic variants.
This extends the tutorial’s development/held-out distinction to leakage risks specific to causal
reasoning. Formatting perturbations, variable renaming and column order are diagnostic
conditions within a scenario family; they are not new independent domains. (Lin, 2026)
1390                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Before running the comparison, specify whether the intervention changes only the prompt,
or also the model, retrieval corpus, numerical engine and repair budget. A paired design can
compare two frozen workflows on the same held-out scenarios while controlling order and
preventing shared conversation state. The prespecified outcomes should include semantic
correctness, supported refusals, unsupported assertions, parsing failures, computation failures
and coverage of requests. Report all assigned requests, with a justified treatment of missing or
invalid outputs, so that a workflow cannot improve its headline score merely by discarding
difficult cases.
   The grading calibration sample should span both arms and include independently adjudicated
correct and incorrect answers under a prespecified verification sampling scheme. Blind
adjudicators to workflow identity where feasible, retain disagreements and report both the
original grade and the corrected or bounded semantic result. If expert judgment is itself fallible,
disagreement and verification cannot simply be renamed truth. Known generated answers
support some calibration tasks; interpretation of an ambiguous business request may require a
set of admissible answers.
   Finally, preserve the exact requests, outputs, parser decisions, model and tool versions,
retrieval snapshots, collection times, token counts and retries. Report grading and adjudication
costs alongside execution cost and decision quality. A deterministic checker for a formal
formula, independent expert adjudication and an LLM grader are substantive alternatives
with different coverage and error properties. This design specifies what a prototype should
demonstrate using public and generated evidence before an expensive bank trial; it does not
report a completed experiment or validated bank economics.


50.39      Causal reasoning checklists need matched errors and
           honest denominators
A bank may ask an agent to turn a servicing problem into a causal diagram, identify missing
assumptions and explain whether an intervention is justified. A correct final answer on one
familiar question is weak evidence for that workflow: the model might recognize the story while
missing the mechanism. CausalityCheck, by Li, Duo, Gao and Su, offers a useful response by
testing several tasks and perturbations around a seed question. The inspected original is the
27-page July 2026 ACL Findings article. Its contribution is a textual evaluation framework; it
does not establish an identified banking effect or a qualified diagram-construction service.(Li
et al., 2026a)


50.39.1     What the checklist tests, and what generates its gold answers

The framework crosses four tasks—original questions, answerability judgment, process judg-
ment and causal-validity assessment—with four settings: original problem solving, rewritten
understanding, irrelevant disturbances and virtual-vocabulary reasoning. Answerability tasks
remove key information; process tasks alter a proposed chain; causal-validity tasks distinguish
four categories combining correctness and reliability. Virtual reasoning replaces real entities
with fictional names. This design is attractive for testing whether a system attends to the
provided context and whether its answer survives intended meaning-preserving changes.(Li
et al., 2026a)
  The source of the labels matters. The paper uses GPT-5 to expand CausalProbe seeds and
reports two rounds of manual checks with ten trained graduate students. One seed produces
36 instances across the 16 task-by-setting groups because the tasks have different numbers of
50.39. Causal reasoning checklists need matched errors and honest denominators               1391


answer variants. The reported sequence is 1,200 seeds, 43,200 generated instances, a selected
25% subset of 10,800, and 8,920 retained instances after filtering. The printed cell counts
reproduce that final total. These are the authors’ reported construction and project-checked
arithmetic, not a reproduction of the original model calls or manual judgments.(Li et al., 2026a;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026ay)
  The four task totals in the printed figure are 482, 2,052, 2,190 and 4,196. Consequently,
equal weighting of tasks or cells differs from weighting all retained instances equally. With cell
accuracies rj and cell sizes nj , the two summaries are
                                      J                     PJ
                                   1X                         j=1 nj rj
                          Rmacro =       rj ,     Rmicro = PJ             .               (50.45)
                                   J j=1                         j=1 nj

The paper describes its table entries as averages of related units. A product evaluation must
specify the unit and aggregation weights, retain seed identifiers, and avoid treating multiple
transformations of the same seed as independent observations. A reported model ranking is
otherwise inseparable from the chosen mixture of tasks. Recovering raw instances and their
grouping is a prerequisite for a new statistical comparison.(Li et al., 2026a; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026ay)
   The paper’s annotation table also supports a more qualified conclusion than blanket excellent
agreement. It prints answerability kappa values of 0.72 and 0.78 in two settings and causal-
validity values from 0.59 to 0.65. Several other entries exceed 0.8. Agreement is informative
about labeling consistency, but does not make a causal interpretation true. For a bank, gold
labels should distinguish claims entailed by a stipulated mechanism from domain judgments
needing an owner or additional evidence. Disputed reliability categories should remain visible
rather than be converted silently into certain causal facts.(Li et al., 2026a)


50.39.2     A difference of accuracies is not a frequency of reasoning errors

The article uses the difference between answerability and process-judgment accuracies to
diagnose causal-chain errors. Table 1 reports 82.27% and 59.46% respectively for one model,
producing a 22.81 percentage-point difference. A useful diagnostic contrast is not automatically
the probability that a model gets answerability right but the chain wrong. To see the distinction,
consider an ideal matched population of problems and let A denote a correct answerability
judgment and B a correct process judgment. Then

                           P (A) − P (B) = P (A ∩ B c ) − P (Ac ∩ B).                     (50.46)

The subtraction nets two different kinds of discordance. Without the joint outcomes, it does
not identify either one.(Li et al., 2026a; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ay)
  For marginal probabilities a = P (A) and b = P (B), the compatible matched-error range is

                          max(0, a − b) ≤ P (A ∩ B c ) ≤ min(a, 1 − b).                   (50.47)

Using a = 0.8227 and b = 0.5946 as an authored matched-design illustration gives a range
from 22.81% to 40.54%. At the lower endpoint, the joint probabilities for both-correct,
A-only, B-only and neither are 0.5946, 0.2281, 0, 0.1773. At the upper endpoint they are
0.4173, 0.4054, 0.1773, 0. Both reproduce the same marginals. The exact reference checks
nonnegativity and every marginal. Because the paper’s task populations and counts differ,
these illustrative bounds are not asserted to be empirical bounds for its actual model responses.
Matching must be established first.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ay)
1392                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


   A negative accuracy difference is equally important. With matched marginals 71.68% and
76.80%, their difference is −5.12 points, but P (A ∩ B c ) can still range from zero to 23.2%.
The article’s negative challenge score therefore does not by itself demonstrate an absence of
chain errors. A proper evaluation should retain paired predictions and gold judgments at seed
level and report both discordance directions, uncertainty under the seed sampling law and the
intended causal level of each task. Even a well-measured process-label error rate is not a rate
of incorrect interventional conclusions unless the labels establish that connection.(Li et al.,
2026a; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ay)


50.39.3    Filtering changes the decision population

The paper removes incomplete fields, ambiguous relationships and sensitive material, and
reports 1,880 exclusions from the 10,800 selected instances. Such filtering may be appropriate
for a clearly defined benchmark, but the resulting accuracy concerns accepted instances. A
production agent will also encounter underspecified, disputed and unanswerable requests. Its
refusal policy, escalation burden and error rate on those requests matter to the bank. A
benchmark should therefore publish the sampling and exclusion flow, reasons by category and
the scope of the reported denominator. The original article’s filter is not evidence that the
excluded requests are solved.(Li et al., 2026a; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ay)
   An authored illustration makes the economic issue explicit. Start with 100 requests, retain
50 and answer 45 of those correctly. Selected accuracy is 90%. If nothing is known about the
excluded half, full-population accuracy lies between 45% and 95%. Suppose a correct action
yields USD 10, an incorrect action loses USD 30, and every attempted action costs USD 1. At
success probability p, stipulated expected margin is

                           V (p) = 10p − 30(1 − p) − 1 = 40p − 31.                       (50.48)

Applying selected accuracy to every request gives USD 5, whereas the compatible full-population
margins range from USD -13 to USD 7. These are sensitivity bounds under a deliberately
incomplete observation law, not a confidence interval or a measured bank return. If the system
abstains on excluded cases, the evaluation must instead model that action’s cost and residual
human workload explicitly.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ay)
   The same lesson applies to source filtering and data-generation quality. GPT-generated
items followed by manual review may be useful, but a competing model outperforming the
generator does not prove that generator-specific artifacts are absent. The paper’s Appendix G
offers such a relative-performance argument. A stronger design would compare independently
generated and human-authored items, blind the adjudicators to model identity, retain difficult
disagreements, and separate development from evaluation seeds. A generator can bias every
model while still failing to rank first.(Li et al., 2026a)


50.39.4    Entity replacement is a stress test, not a unique causal diagnosis

The article reports higher performance on virtual-vocabulary tasks and discusses a case where
replacing a familiar entity changes a model’s handling of a negative conclusion. This motivates
a practical perturbation test. It does not uniquely identify memorization or any single internal
failure mechanism: replacement can also change tokenization, semantic cues, question difficulty
and response-policy triggers. Repeated identical answers to one prompt support repeatability
under that setting, not the exclusion of those alternative explanations.(Li et al., 2026a)
  For a banking prototype, the controlled object should be a known mechanism with explicit
variables, action clock and admissible observations. Multiple names and paraphrases can be
50.40. From failure documents to bowties: useful extraction without causal overclaiming       1393


assigned to the same mechanism while keeping its causal query fixed. A second axis can
change the mechanism while retaining familiar surface vocabulary. Contrasting these axes
tests whether the system follows the stipulated structure rather than a remembered story.
Labels should include answerable, unidentified, unsupported and internally inconsistent cases.
This is a proposed experiment motivated by the paper, not an experiment that the library has
already run.


50.39.5     How to use the framework in the proposal

CausalityCheck’s task matrix is a candidate design component for evaluating business-question
translation, assumption elicitation and diagram explanation. Its textual gold labels should not
become an oracle for graph identification, counterfactual effects or hidden-confounder exclusion.
The article itself acknowledges limited treatment of structural rigor and counterfactual reasoning.
The proposal should combine checklist perturbations with exact finite causal models, known
nonidentification pairs and independently adjudicated domain tasks. That combination
tests both linguistic robustness and whether the requested effect follows from the available
information.(Li et al., 2026a)
   Before adopting the package or dataset, recover a pinned repository and data revision, trace
the transformation and filtering code, inspect license and redistribution terms, and bind item-
level provenance. The current review has inspected the genuine article, not executed its code
or live models. The library, CLI and MCP should expose seed and variant identity, requested
causal level, gold-label origin, inclusion status, paired predictions and uncertainty scope.
Agents may organize and explain that evidence; a single aggregate accuracy must not authorize
a banking intervention. Public mechanism tests can establish whether a prototype merits an
expensive institutional trial while preserving the limits of textual benchmark evidence.


50.40      From failure documents to bowties: useful extraction
           without causal overclaiming
A bank’s operational-risk team may want to turn incident reports and control inventories into
a diagram of causes, a critical event, preventive barriers, consequences and mitigating barriers.
Such a representation can organize evidence and expose missing controls. It does not yet
specify the effect of installing a control. ACE, by Venkatesh, Oudmans and Zurfluh, supplies
a useful industrial analogue: three pipelines generate bowtie diagrams from Failure Mode and
Effects Analysis documents. The 3 July 2026 publisher edition compares retrieval, OCR and a
vision-assisted pipeline, with substantially better results on selected structured tables than on
narrative text. Its central contribution for this proposal is a concrete extraction workflow and
a set of failure modes to test before treating a diagram as a causal model.(Venkatesh et al.,
2026)


50.40.1     What is extracted, and from which evidence?

In the retrieval pipeline, Markdown FMEA content is chunked, embedded with all-MiniLM-
L6-v2 and indexed with FAISS; part-name queries select context for a structured prompt. The
OCR pipeline uses PaddleOCR and Img2Table to convert table images to Markdown before
generation. In the vision pipeline, Mistral-Small produces a Markdown table and description
for a second language model to convert into bowtie JSON. The reported implementation uses
Python 3.9, sentence-transformers and local GGUF inference through llama-cpp-python. These
1394                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


are named dependencies and reported components, not a pinned, independently reproduced
installation in this project.(Venkatesh et al., 2026)
   The evaluation first screens eight model variants on four causal-loop extraction texts and
ten false-premise questions. It then selects three instruction-tuned model families and builds
tabular references for a sensor, valve assembly and shaft from the US Navy reliability handbook.
A domain expert constructs those reference diagrams. Narrative evaluation uses dynamic-seal
text and three reference bowties. The paper explicitly notes that expert diagrams sometimes
contain implicit variables absent from the source. This is a serious labeling distinction:
agreement with an expert’s augmented interpretation and faithful extraction of explicit text
are different tasks.(Venkatesh et al., 2026)
   A bank-facing interface should therefore retain a source span or table-cell identity for each
proposed role and edge. It should separately label an explicit statement, an expert-supplied
hypothesis, a model inference and an unresolved conflict. If a narrative does not state a
mitigating barrier or consequence, the result can be incomplete. A schema requiring every field
to contain a plausible phrase would reward invention. ACE identifies precisely this problem in
fallback prompts that ask for a mechanism and otherwise insert a generic mechanism label.
Its narrative example also lacks enough information to complete the consequence side of the
expert bowtie.(Venkatesh et al., 2026)
  The article’s attribution license is recorded with the genuine PDF. It does not establish
reuse rights for handbook data, model weights, pipeline code or dependencies. Recovering
the actual prompts, preprocessing, model hashes, generation settings and evaluation files is a
separate step before adopting an implementation. The proposal can adopt the representation
and provenance requirements now while keeping executable reuse a conditional choice.


50.40.2     Read metrics with their alignment and denominator

ACE matches predicted and reference labels with SBERT cosine similarity at an empirically
selected threshold of 0.75. It reports node and edge precision, recall and F1 by role or edge
type. Its reported graph edit distance is a count of false-positive and false-negative nodes
and edges after matching, rather than the minimum edit path in the usual graph-theoretic
problem. Threshold choice, matching constraints and reference roles are consequently part of
the measurement contract. Semantically similar labels cannot be allowed to erase a reversal of
causal direction or the distinction between a cause and a barrier.(Venkatesh et al., 2026)
   Table 4’s selected configurations range from node F1 0.81 to 0.94 and edge F1 0.58 to 0.93.
The paper describes a missed critical event yielding node F1 0.80 but edge F1 0.44 for a
shaft case. On narratives, Table 5’s average accuracy ratings range from 1.20 to 3.00 on a
five-point scale. The strongest clarity rating, 3.80, is not evidence that the same output has
correct causal structure. Expert-level records, rating units, missing ratings and aggregation
rules remain necessary to interpret the reported means. These are small, selected industrial
evaluations, not banking transfer results.(Venkatesh et al., 2026)
  The counts also deserve direct reconciliation. For each of two prompting conditions,
hallucinated, unclear and correct-rejection responses are respectively (21, 10, 49) and (9, 11, 60),
each summing to 80. Hallucinations decline from 21/80 = 26.25% to 9/80 = 11.25%, a
15 percentage-point reduction. Unclear responses increase by one, despite prose describing
them as reduced. Separately, 12 of 32 schema outputs are invalid JSON, or 37.5%. These
experiments have different denominators and cannot be merged into one accuracy measure.
The reference calculation checks the printed arithmetic; no model responses are reproduced
here.(Venkatesh et al., 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ax)
  Aggregate F1 can conceal a consequential omission. Consider an authored chain of 101
50.40. From failure documents to bowties: useful extraction without causal overclaiming      1395


nodes with 100 directed edges from node zero to node 100. A prediction retains every node
and 99 correct edges but omits the bridge from node 49 to node 50. Node F1 is one, and
                                            2TP          198
                          F1,edge =                    =     ≃ 0.995.                   (50.49)
                                     2TP + FP + FN       199
Nevertheless, the predicted graph contains no directed path from the initiating event to the
final consequence. For a bank tracing a payment outage through failed controls to a customer
loss, a critical-path or control-role error can outweigh many correctly extracted labels. This
example motivates reporting decision-critical role and path errors alongside aggregate graph
scores; it does not characterize an observed ACE run.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ax)

50.40.3     Sensitivity indices do not establish interchangeability

The reported Sobol experiments vary prompt strictness, prompt type, context pipeline and
selected decoding settings. They attribute much of the output variation to prompt factors and
their interactions. The text interprets a near-zero first-order context index as evidence that
the three pipelines are interchangeable under equivalent prompts. That conclusion needs more
than a first-order variance decomposition.(Venkatesh et al., 2026)
  For independent design factors P and C, let f (P, C) be an evaluation score with positive
variance. A first-order context index and a total-order context index are
                             Var(E[f | C])               E[Var(f | P )]
                       SC =                ,    ST,C =                  .           (50.50)
                                 Var(f )                    Var(f )
These quantities concern variation under a specified experimental input distribution. To see
the distinction directly, stipulate independent uniform binary P, C and f (P, C) = 1{P = C}.
Both conditional means given C are 1/2, while the marginal variance is 1/4. Thus SC = 0 but
ST,C = 1. Changing context at fixed prompt changes the score by either one or minus one:
the averaged main effect cancels, although the context matters completely through interaction.
Exact enumeration verifies all four cells.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ax)
   This witness does not show that ACE’s actual total-order estimate is one. It establishes why
a near-zero first-order estimate alone cannot prove equivalence. Even small estimated total
effects over three component tables cannot establish agreement on new formats or rare critical
failures. The next experiment should freeze categorical encodings, factor probabilities, semantic
matching and decoding controls; retain the full sample matrix and all invalid outputs; and
compare pipelines on paired held-out documents with prespecified tolerances for critical-role
errors, ordinary extraction accuracy, latency and cost. The precise factor list in the expanded
Sobol run, including whether decoding factors remain, should be recovered from code rather
than inferred from its abbreviated paragraph.
   ACE reports identical JSON in ten runs with different seeds for selected fixed configurations
and attributes this to quantization and constrained prompts. Repeated identity establishes
observed stability in those trials, not truth or its mechanism. A controlled precision comparison,
verified seed propagation and decoding configuration, cache checks and raw token/output
records would distinguish competing explanations. Ten repetitions of an erroneous diagram
remain the same error. Schema-constrained prompting also should not be described as a hard
grammar-constrained decoder without evidence of such an implementation.(Venkatesh et al.,
2026)

50.40.4     From a role diagram to an intervention question

An unsigned arrow is insufficient to price an intervention. In a deliberately minimal example,
both structural laws Y = A and Y = 1 − A have topology A → Y , with binary action A and
1396                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


loss event Y . Their intervention contrasts E[Y | do(A = 1)] − E[Y | do(A = 0)] are respectively
one and minus one. If a loss event costs an assumed USD 10 and the action costs USD 2, the
incremental margin is

                    V = −10{E[Y | do(A = 1)] − E[Y | do(A = 0)]} − 2,                    (50.51)

giving USD −12 or USD 8. These two laws illustrate missing mechanism information in a
common topology; they are not claimed to have identical observational distributions or to
satisfy the same signed barrier interpretation. A diagram extractor has not supplied either
law merely by naming an edge.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ax)
   For a bank, the translation layer must additionally identify the action that can be changed,
the time at which it is assigned, the eligible unit and population, the loss horizon, the data-
generating and observation processes, and any confounding or feedback. A generic barrier
node might represent an existing control, a proposed policy, a measured proxy or an expert
belief. These possibilities imply different models. Time indexing may be necessary before
a feedback description can be represented as an acyclic causal query. Unresolved semantics
should remain explicit and should prevent an automatic effect estimate.


50.40.5    A bounded agentic workflow and public validation route

ACE proposes future agentic correction and knowledge-graph reasoning, while its reported
pipelines are single-pass and single-component. The proposal should keep that boundary
visible. A candidate workflow retrieves immutable evidence, proposes typed roles and edges,
checks schema and source support, and asks a bounded correction stage to address a specific
omission or contradiction. It preserves all attempts and unresolved results. A graph database
can store those objects, but neither storage nor repeated agent agreement validates a causal
claim.(Venkatesh et al., 2026)
   The CLI or MCP contract should expose source hashes and spans, role types, temporal
scope, explicit versus inferred status, schema/model/prompt versions, costs and distinct failure
states. Invalid JSON, missing source evidence, a disputed expert addition and a scientifically
unidentified intervention are different outcomes. No pipeline should convert all four into
a generic failure, fabricate a completed bowtie, or silently grant an intervention-analysis
capability.
   Public documents and generated mechanisms can justify the next experiment before costly
institutional evidence is requested. Split by document family or component, not repeated
prompts on the same case. Include explicit and implicit causes, absent barriers, contradic-
tory statements, multi-line tables and misleading nearby components. Freeze the reference
construction and separate text-supported truth from expert augmentation. Report invalid
outputs, critical-role/path loss, false additions, disagreement, correction attempts and total
review cost. Add known-mechanism tasks only where the desired intervention is defined, and
retain refusal when extraction cannot support it. Such a prototype can establish whether
assisted diagram construction merits a bank trial without claiming that the trial’s outcome is
already known.(Venkatesh et al., 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ax)


50.41      Causal programs of thought: computation after the
           question is justified
A servicing manager asks whether offering a payment holiday today would reduce losses over
the next ninety days. A useful assistant must determine what the offer changes, whose losses
50.41. Causal programs of thought: computation after the question is justified              1397


are being compared, and what information is available before the offer. Only then can it
choose a calculation. Shrestha, Malberg and Groh’s From Causal Parrots to Causal Prophets?
examines a narrower but relevant part of this workflow: answering formal causal questions
whose numerical facts and causal structure are encoded in a synthetic benchmark. Its causal
tree and program of thoughts provide concrete alternatives to a single verbal reasoning chain.
The reported improvement motivates a public prototype of assisted calculation. It does not
establish that the assistant can recover the right banking question or identify an effect from
available customer records. (Shrestha et al., 2025)


50.41.1     Preserve the question before selecting a solver

Let A denote the offer made at the decision time, Y (a) a default indicator over the specified
horizon under offer a, L(a) the monetary loss if default occurs, and C(a) the cost of that offer.
A possible decision target is the incremental expected cost

                        ∆ = E[C(1) − C(0)] + E[Y (1)L(1) − Y (0)L(0)].

This is a proposed banking target, not an estimate supplied by the paper. It requires a declared
eligible population, treatment versions, horizon and accounting convention. A probability
contrast alone is insufficient if the offer also changes exposure or recovery. A question about
customers who accept an offer differs from a question about making the offer: acceptance can
be a post-offer variable. An assistant that silently changes the action can produce correct
arithmetic for a different decision.
   The paper samples 1,000 commonsensical questions from CLADDER and excludes backdoor-
adjustment questions because those questions do not require the formal calculations and
multistep reasoning being studied. It generates anti-commonsensical and nonsensical variants
using GPT-4o and reports manual checks of those variants. The former replace an outcome
with an unrelated noun; the latter replace variables with generated four-letter strings. These
transformations probe dependence on familiar associations. They do not test whether a
free-form bank request supplies enough information to define an intervention, an observation
process or an eligible population. (Shrestha et al., 2025)
   That exclusion matters to the proposed architecture. Selecting a defensible adjustment set
is precisely one of the tasks between a diagram and a numerical effect estimate. A score on
the retained tasks cannot be used as evidence that this omitted step works. The evaluation
should therefore distinguish a question with a supplied structural model and probabilities
from one requiring model elicitation, identification or data assessment. The former supports a
calculation test. The latter may properly end with an unresolved assumption or a request for
additional evidence.


50.41.2     Alternative thoughts are proposals, not independent evidence

The study evaluates thirteen model variants, with the reported experiments using temperature
1.0. Its causal tree of thoughts follows a six-step causal reasoning prompt. At selected
steps, it generates three alternatives, asks the model to score them from one to ten, and
continues with the highest-scoring alternative. Other steps have a single continuation. The
retained state includes the question and preceding selected thoughts. This is a greedy selection
procedure, rather than an enumeration of all compatible causal models or a confidence set
over graphs.(Shrestha et al., 2025)
   For the servicing example, candidate diagrams might disagree about whether financial
distress precedes the offer, whether acceptance mediates its effect, or whether a collections
1398                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


contact is observed after treatment. Model scores can rank these proposals for examination.
They cannot establish the timing or direction of an edge. The interface should retain the source
statement, time index and unresolved alternatives when an edge matters to identification. A
graph rejected by the model’s own score can still express a scientifically relevant alternative.
Premature pruning would hide that uncertainty from the downstream solver.
   Self-consistency is a different procedure: the paper samples several reasoning chains and
votes over their answers. The errors of chains generated by the same model from the same
question can be shared. Unanimity measures agreement among those outputs, not independent
confirmation of the causal assumptions. A comparison of verbal reasoning, voting and tree
search should consequently measure selection mistakes and unresolved alternatives as well as
final-answer accuracy. Their additional model calls and reviewer effort must enter the same
cost accounting as code-assisted methods.(Shrestha et al., 2025)


50.41.3    Generated code computes a supplied interpretation

The causal program of thoughts asks a model to generate DoWhy/Python code for the question,
executes the code through a Python REPL, and returns the computed estimate to the model
for its final answer. The illustrated workflow generates synthetic data using numerical facts in
the question. Its attraction is clear: a numerical library can perform operations that a verbal
chain might calculate incorrectly. The causal interpretation still enters through the question,
chosen graph, generated data and selected library operation. (Shrestha et al., 2025)
   Suppose a question supplies probabilities under a declared structural law. Artificial rows
sampled from those probabilities may approximate a functional of that law. They are not newly
observed customers and do not strengthen its empirical support. Increasing the generated
sample size can reduce a Monte Carlo approximation error while leaving the uncertainty about
the law intact. Where the supplied finite probability table permits direct evaluation, an exact
formula checker is therefore a substantive comparator. It avoids introducing sampling variation
solely to recover a quantity already specified numerically. This is a proposed comparison, not
a replication of the study’s code.
   The same boundary applies to selecting an estimator. A successful function call does not
demonstrate exchangeability, positivity, correct measurement or an appropriate counterfactual
model. The paper’s program error analysis separates incorrect extracted graphs, incorrect
library function calls and code execution failures. Those distinctions should survive in the
product result. A tool error can invite a bounded retry; an unidentified target requires new
assumptions, information or a refusal to provide the requested effect. Treating both as syntax
errors encourages an agent to search until some numerical output appears. (Shrestha et al.,
2025)


50.41.4    Read gains with their task and denominator

Table 4 reports GPT-4o overall accuracies of 82.0% for the baseline, 86.4% for the causal tree
and 90.8% for the causal program. These are overall averages across the three variants. The
corresponding commonsensical subset averages are 84.3%, 87.5% and 92.5%. Keeping the
two columns distinct prevents a favorable overall number from being assigned to the wrong
population. Subtraction of the rounded overall scores gives gains of 4.4 and 8.8 percentage
points. The causal program’s counterfactual scores are 92.5%, 90.2% and 87.4% across
commonsensical, anti-commonsensical and nonsensical questions, compared with baseline
scores of 70.1%, 68.8% and 64.1%. The corresponding differences are 22.4, 21.4 and 23.3
percentage points. (Shrestha et al., 2025; Causal banking proposal project, 2026bd)
50.41. Causal programs of thought: computation after the question is justified               1399


  Those differences are descriptive calculations over published rounded entries. The inspected
tables do not supply the question-level paired outcomes and uncertainty needed to reconstruct
a statistical comparison. The variants derive from common underlying questions, so they
should not automatically be treated as independent observations. Nor is an error selected for
explanation a random draw from all deployment errors. The appropriate sampling unit, model
revision, prompt, retries and treatment of failed outputs must accompany a comparison.
   Several appendix counts need reconciliation before secondary rates are computed. Table
5’s sampled query-type counts sum to 999, whereas its rung counts sum to 1,000; both
corresponding original-dataset totals are 8,690. The response-pattern counts in Tables 7 and
8 sum to 995 and 999 for ten-chain and five-chain voting. Table 10 lists error counts of 10,
37 and 13, totaling 60, although its preceding description states an analysis of 50 samples.
Overlapping categories, missing outputs or transcription errors are possible explanations, but
the inspected text does not settle them. Recovering identifiers and raw records is necessary
before choosing a denominator or asserting an error-category rate. (Shrestha et al., 2025;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026bd)
   The paper also reports unsuccessful memorization probes and acknowledges that GPT-4o
generated the perturbations on which it was evaluated. Failed recall of three questions does not
establish that related training data were absent. The authors explicitly restrict their study to
formal causal reasoning and one synthetic benchmark, and call for evaluation on further tasks.
These limitations make the paper useful evidence for a narrowly specified prototype. They
prevent its scores from establishing general causal discovery, faithful diagram construction or
business-language translation.(Shrestha et al., 2025)


50.41.5      Audit the reference calculation as well as the agent

Appendix D.3 illustrates why a benchmark answer cannot be accepted solely because it is
printed beside a worked solution. Write mxv for the numerical outcome probability displayed
for treatment x and mediator v, and πx for the displayed probability that the mediator is
one. The appendix supplies m00 = 0.28, m01 = 0.60, m10 = 0.35, m11 = 0.74, π0 = 0.57 and
π1 = 0.22. Evaluating its step-4 expression literally gives
   1
   X
        m0v {P (V = v | X = 1) − P (V = v | X = 0)} = (m01 − m00 )(π1 − π0 )
  v=0

                    {0.22(0.60 − 0.28) + 0.78(0.74 − 0.35)}

   The numerical discrepancy is only part of the issue. The narrative supplies death probabilities
but names the outcome as survival, and its displayed counterfactual notation must be reconciled
with the intended natural indirect effect. Equations (50.52) and (50.53) consequently identify
inconsistencies; neither is declared the corrected benchmark truth. Establishing that truth
requires the intended coding, structural model, counterfactual target and actual generator. A
library can faithfully calculate the wrong expression or use the right expression with reversed
