   The protocol transition rule is subtle. A dual-era stdio client probes server/discover. A
discovery result means modern; the client chooses a mutually supported version. A recognized
modern protocol-version error also means modern: retry with one of its advertised supported
versions or report incompatibility, but do not fall back to legacy initialization. A different error
or timeout identifies the legacy era, so a dual-era client tries the legacy handshake. The fallback
cannot depend on one specific unknown-method error code because legacy implementations may
return several codes or no response. This is a protocol decision, not a scientific operation.(Model
Context Protocol contributors, 2026g,h)
   The authored decision table covers a discovery result with and without a common version,
a recognized unsupported-version error, another recognized modern error, two ordinary errors,
timeout, and a modern-only client. It retains the no-downgrade rule for every recognized
modern error. The table is not a wire parser and no simulated row establishes actual SDK
behavior. Before advertising dual-era support, a real client/server matrix must test malformed
discovery bodies, empty and contradictory version lists, advertised-version retry, recognized
errors, unknown errors, timeout, cache lifetime, and server restart. It must also compare
the exact canonical response and tool capability map across each supported protocol.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026bs,br)
  Compatibility must not silently widen the scientific request. A protocol version negotiates
53.19. A Java discovery boundary that retains the question                                  1463


message behavior; it cannot decide whether an interval is a confidence region, convert a
posterior set to a sensitivity region, or repair an ambiguous treatment. A schema version does
not prove assignment truth, temporal ordering, or graph-class validity. The adapter should
reject unknown mandatory semantic fields, support only explicit migrations, and retain original
request bytes and version identities for audit. Unrecognized scientific semantics require refusal
or a new reviewed operation contract, not best-effort coercion. (Model Context Protocol
contributors, 2026a; Causal banking proposal, 2026bi)


53.19      A Java discovery boundary that retains the question
The Java comparison motivates a concrete first integration: a pinned Tetrad process for
a restricted PC discovery request, with a separate admission path for FGES. The initial
request concerns complete continuous observations under an explicitly assumed IID linear
Gaussian model with causal sufficiency, acyclicity, faithfulness and no unmodeled selection.
These restrictions identify a reviewable prototype. They do not imply that a table of banking
observations satisfies them. Clustered customers, repeated account histories, missing-data
correction, latent-variable discovery and background-knowledge constraints require other
profiles. The adapter is a proposal contract; no Java engine or new transport endpoint has
been implemented here. (Causal banking research project, 2026v; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a)
   The request retains the downstream target even though discovery does not compute it. A
funding analyst’s population, treatment contrast, outcome, time horizon, units and sampling
declarations remain attached to the graph. They prevent a later identification step from
silently changing the question. The generic operation contract already provides these fields
for effect operations. The Java discovery profile deliberately requires that context as well.
A standalone graph request without a downstream treatment and outcome needs its own
reviewed context extension; inserting arbitrary variable names would create a fictitious causal
question. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)
   The logical interface is the same across the proposed library invocation, causalbank
operation graph.discover command and causal_graph_discover MCP tool. Each trans-
ports a versioned canonical request and receives the same typed result. A complete scientific
context digest accompanies a broader request digest containing input hashes, engine revision,
algorithm settings, adapter version and resource limits. An interface that changes USD into
thousands of USD, reverses the treatment contrast, changes the sampling law or orients an
ambiguous edge has changed the scientific request, even if its JSON remains valid. The
reference serialization examples demonstrate those identity changes on local objects; they are
not executions of a server or MCP client. (Causal banking research project, 2026v,w)


53.19.1     The graph object preserves a class of possible interventions

Use opaque variable identifiers and a bijection into engine symbols. Store the original column
order and its permutation separately from the engine’s order. Every variable, including an
isolated node, travels through the conversion. Human-readable labels, availability times and
units remain metadata with their own scientific meaning; names do not supply an orientation
rule. For every pair, retain its two endpoint marks. When the serialization orders the pair
lexically, it swaps the marks with the nodes. Thus R → B, expressed as a tail at R and an
arrowhead at B, agrees with the reversed pair representation having an arrowhead at B and a
tail at R. Reversing only the node order changes the graph. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; Causal
banking research project, 2026w)
  A Gaussian example illustrates why an unoriented link must survive this boundary. Consider
1464                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


three standardized variables X, Y, Z with covariance
                                                           
                                           1 4/5 2/5
                                     Σ = 4/5 1 1/2 .
                                                    
                                          2/5 1/2 1

For a banking interpretation, X can denote a rate concession, Y a balance response and Z a
funding outcome, all in stipulated standardized units. The covariance obeys X ⊥ Z | Y . The
undirected path X − Y − Z represents three acyclic orientations without an unshielded collider.
The orientation X → Y ← Z is excluded because it would require a different independence
pattern under faithfulness. (Causal banking research project, 2026w)
  For each retained orientation, regress a variable on its proposed parents using the same
Σ, and assign the residual variance as its independent Gaussian noise variance. In matrix
notation, if Wij is the coefficient from source i to target j, then

                                  Σ = (I − W T )−1 Ω(I − W )−1 ,

where Ω is the diagonal noise covariance. The exact reference calculation verifies this equality
for all three models. In the forward chain, the coefficients are 4/5 and 1/2; intervening on X
changes Z by 2/5 per unit. In the fork and the reverse chain, X has no directed path to Z, so
the effect is zero. The same observational covariance therefore supports the effect multiset
{2/5, 0, 0}. (Causal banking research project, 2026w)
   Returning the forward chain alone would select the positive effect by an unrecorded conven-
tion. Returning the interval [0, 2/5] would introduce values such as 1/5 that none of these
three specified linear Gaussian models produces. That interval is a hull, not the discrete effect
set, and neither object is a confidence set without a separate statistical construction. The
discovery response consequently retains the CPDAG and returns no effect estimate, effect
region or uncertainty level. A later identification operation must state how it handles the whole
class and the additional functional assumptions. (Causal banking research project, 2026v,w)
   Checking endpoint syntax is insufficient to award the CPDAG label. A graph can contain
only tails and arrows and still fail to represent a completed Markov equivalence class. The
existing reference validator does not recognize all such cases. The proposed Java boundary
therefore requires an independently reviewed graph-class check before publishing a completed
CPDAG. A circle, bidirected conflict or invalid completion in the initial route is an invalid-
engine-output failure, with the raw graph retained for diagnosis. It is not silently coerced
into a DAG. Background knowledge is initially excluded because orienting an observational
CPDAG using additional restrictions requires an appropriate constrained-graph representation
and provenance. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)


53.19.2     Admission must cover the failure path as well as the constructor

The proposed PC profile sets the conditioning depth to the inspected unbounded value, enables
the stable skeleton option, selects the separating-set collider rule, disallows bidirected conflicts,
and prevents directed cycles. It supplies empty background knowledge and a caller-declared
test level. These choices make the attempted operation explicit. A user-requested depth cap is
initially unsupported; exhausting a runtime budget returns an incomplete job, not a graph
advertised as the result of the completed search. (Causal banking research project, 2026v;
Tetrad contributors, 2026a)
  The numerical test profile is equally specific: complete data, no shrinkage, zero ridge and
no pseudoinverse fallback, with all settings frozen before search. The inspected Fisher-Z
source exposes these alternatives separately. Automatically activating regularization after
53.19. A Java discovery boundary that retains the question                                   1465


a singularity would change the test while keeping the same apparent method name. That
may be useful in a different profile, but it needs a separate calibration argument. The initial
profile requires at least n ≥ p + 2 complete observations for p variables so that even the largest
possible conditioning set has positive Fisher-Z degrees of freedom. This is only an arithmetic
prerequisite; it does not guarantee useful power or stable covariance inversion. (Causal banking
research project, 2026v; Tetrad contributors, 2026a)
   As the Java comparison showed, the inspected checkIndependence path converts a singular-
matrix exception into a dependence result with p = 0. The proposed wrapper instead uses the
exception-preserving getResult path and derives a decision only from a valid result. Every
invocation receives a query identity and a terminal record. Before propagating an exception,
the wrapper sets a job-level failure flag. Publication then checks that every issued call has a
valid terminal record and that the flag is clear. This matters because search code may catch
interruptions internally: receiving a graph object alone does not prove that all its requested
tests completed. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; Tetrad contributors, 2026a; Causal banking research
project, 2026v)
   That wrapper remains an implementation prerequisite. Its full independence-test interface,
ancillary methods and interaction with the search implementation must be inspected and com-
piled; calling one method in a design document is not sufficient. Numerical rank checks before
dispatch help detect duplicate accounting columns, but per-query records remain necessary
for failures that arise during the search. A zero test probability cannot be reinterpreted as
maximal causal confidence. If the required failure provenance cannot be obtained, the route is
unavailable in this runtime. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)
   Parallelism and deadlines also belong to admission. The stable FAS path uses a parallel
stream and requires thread-safe records. FGES’s separate worker setting does not control that
path. The inspected PC search delegates the skeleton phase to FAS without demonstrating an
end-to-end deadline guarantee from PC’s timeout setting alone. The proposed parent process
therefore enforces the whole-job deadline, memory and output budget. An engine’s cooperative
timeout is supplementary. A cancellation or a process death preserves the attempt’s failure
record and withholds its graph. (Tetrad contributors, 2026a; Causal banking research project,
2026v)


53.19.3     Units, unsupported requests and the next executable comparison

The signed funding model in the Java survey provides a useful independent conversion reference.
If x′i = di xi , the source-row coefficients must transform as Wij′ = dj Wij /di . Rescaling the
rate by 100, balances by 1000 and cost by 10, then applying the correspondingly rescaled
rate intervention, must recover the original responses after converting units back. The exact
reference does so. It also verifies that an unchanged absolute coefficient threshold can select a
different graph after rescaling. This does not give coefficients to the PC adapter, whose result
is graph-only; it supplies an admission example for any later weighted route. (Causal banking
research project, 2026w,x)
   A valid request outside the initial scientific scope receives a completed unsupported response
with its context preserved and a specific alternative. Repeated account observations point
toward a separately reviewed temporal or cluster profile; latent-variable assumptions point
toward an appropriate PAG route; missing values require an explicit observation mechanism
and correction profile. An uninstalled or unqualified runtime receives an unavailable response.
Neither condition is called nonidentification, which would be a stronger scientific conclusion
about an effect under a model. Malformed inputs and failed computations carry structured
errors, with no effect or graph result masquerading as a completed calculation. (Causal banking
1466                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


research project, 2026v)
   The first prototype should use a fixed local Java process so its dependency and runtime
identity can be measured. The process boundary does not remove the inspected GPL conditions.
The actual compiler target, runtime vendor and version, dependency artifacts, operating system
and thread configuration must be locked for the chosen route; the source’s compiler setting
and bridge README cannot substitute for that environment check. Result publication is
atomic after validation. A crashed search is restarted as a new retained attempt under the
same immutable request, with no promise of resuming an internal search state. If completion
wins a cancellation race, the immutable published result remains the observed outcome.
(cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; Causal banking research project, 2026v)
   The executable comparison begins with independent oracles: the three-model Gaussian
class, a collider and an isolated node, the depth-three separator, signed matrices and unit
changes, singular input, and injected failures. Only after these pass should a prospectively
specified generated-sample study estimate graph error and resource use under the declared
assumptions and their violations. It should retain every attempted request, including timeouts
and refusals, and compare a matched baseline under the same budgets. These steps test
whether the proposed boundary deserves a prototype claim. Expensive bank experiments
become relevant when that bounded evidence exposes a decision-relevant uncertainty that
public or generated data cannot settle.


53.19.4     Encoding algorithm settings without changing the shared schema

The existing discovery request schema permits only an algorithm identifier and algorithm
version in its parameter object. The proposed Java profile therefore places the detailed
settings in a separate immutable configuration artifact. The request supplies its opaque
handle, hash, media type, schema version and role, alongside the data artifact. Resolving
that artifact recovers the test level, conditioning depth, missingness policy, numerical controls
and background-knowledge choice. The full request identity includes its hash, so changing
a setting creates a different request even when the downstream scientific context remains
identical. This preserves compatibility with the shared schema while retaining the scientifically
relevant settings. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)
  The adapter’s admission check must require exactly one configuration artifact of the reviewed
version, verify its bytes and recognized fields, and check that the declared algorithm version
admits that profile. Generic schema validation alone cannot establish those conditions. The
worked wire records separately represent an unavailable runtime, an unsupported sampling
regime, a failed invocation and a graph response from an independent population reference.
Their data fixture is deterministic, and their graph is not a fitted result. These records make
the proposed response contract concrete without treating a valid message as evidence of an
executed engine.


53.20      A native forest boundary that preserves the banking
           question
A servicing analyst asks whether making a specified offer changes twelve-month net receipts
for eligible customers. The proposed treatment is the offer, coded one, against no offer, coded
zero. The outcome includes the offer’s cost and is measured in dollars per customer over the
stated horizon. A heterogeneous-effect forest can help estimate this contrast under a declared
identification model. Its C++ implementation cannot decide whether the recorded offer was
53.20. A native forest boundary that preserves the banking question                                   1467


randomized, whether all confounders were measured, or whether the analyst actually wants
the mean over customers, branches, or treated customers. Those choices must precede engine
dispatch and survive it.
   The proposed first grf integration uses its maintained R interface in a pinned local process,
which in turn invokes the native C++ core. Direct native embedding is a separate alternative.
Inspection covers commit 5bee99b51471, dated 30 April 2026, whose package description
declares version 2.6.1. The snapshot therefore precedes the literature cutoff; its October
acquisition date is separately retained. The design is not an installed adapter. The executed
examples below are project-owned arithmetic references; they neither train grf nor measure its
statistical performance GRF contributors (2026d); Causal banking research project (2026l,m).


53.20.1     From an offer question to a local moment

Let X contain information available before the offer, W ∈ {0, 1} denote assignment, and Y (w)
denote the potential twelve-month net receipt. With consistency, no interference, conditional
exchangeability and positivity, the target is

                       τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x],          θ = E[τ (X)].

The outer expectation defines the customer population. An observed treated subpopulation or
an overlap-weighted population gives a different target. The initial proposed profile accepts
complete observations from independent customers, a binary treatment, one fixed outcome and
a fixed horizon. It excludes repeated decision histories, unmeasured confounding, interference,
survey weighting and latent-graph ambiguity that has not been resolved for this estimand.
These are restrictions of the proposed profile, not assertions that the package has no other
functionality.
   Write m(x) = E[Y | X = x] and e(x) = E[W | X = x]. The inspected R wrapper either
obtains nuisance predictions or uses supplied predictions, then passes Y − m(X)
                                                                             b     and W − eb(X)

In the exact reference, equal weights on residual outcomes (−2, −1, 1, 2) and residual treatments
(−1/2, −1/2, 1/2, 1/2) give slope three. Constant residual treatment gives zero denominator
and the reference refuses the calculation. Its numerical threshold is an explicit arithmetic
rule, not evidence that positivity holds in a bank population. The native source divides by
its local first-stage quantity; the adapter must inspect finite outputs and retain weak-support
diagnostics instead of silently replacing a failed division with zero.
   Honest tree splitting and out-of-bag prediction address particular reuse of observations.
They do not establish the causal premises or turn customer rows from a common branch shock
into independent samples. Generalized forest theory also imposes regularity, subsampling,
smooth local identification and variance conditions; a named package and a successful fit do
not verify them Athey et al. (2018). The proposed first profile retains the R nuisance path and
1468                                                                       Causal analysis for a universal bank


its out-of-bag predictions. Supplying an independently estimated nuisance vector requires a
later profile with explicit training identities, alignment and sampling-unit split rules. A known
randomized propensity may be supplied only with the corresponding assignment declaration;
it is never inferred from a convenient constant.

The average of fitted conditional effects is not interchangeable with the package’s default
augmented average-effect estimator. In the inspected binary path, write τbi for the out-of-bag
conditional prediction. Its score is

This equals the familiar two-outcome-regression expression after setting µ  b0i = mb i − ebi τbi and

  The reference uses four tuples (Y, W, m, b eb, τb): (0, 0, 1, 1/4, 2), (1, 0, 1, 1/2, 2), (3, 1, 2, 1/2, 2),
and (5, 1, 2, 3/4, 2). Their scores are 8/3, 0, 2, 16/3. The mean score is 5/2, whereas the mean
conditional prediction is two. The C++ residual-score calculation and an independent rational
Python calculation using the two-regression formula agree. This is an exact conversion check
with deliberately supplied numbers, not fitted evidence for double robustness or coverage
Causal banking research project (2026m).
                                                                            P            P
   For target weights qi , the corresponding estimator is θb = i qi Γi / i qi . Choosing qi = 1
targets a customer-weighted population; choosing inverse branch sizes gives each observed
branch equal total weight. A branch with two customer scores of ten dollars and a branch with
four scores of forty dollars produce a customer mean of thirty dollars and an equal-branch
mean of twenty-five dollars. A planning cohort of ten thousand customers turns the five-dollar
difference into fifty thousand dollars in a naive projection. That calculation exposes the target
change; it does not justify applying an equal-branch mean to an arbitrary customer portfolio.
   The R interface documents that equal cluster weighting changes both training sampling
and average-effect weights, and disallows user sample weights in that mode. Replacing the
final mean alone cannot reproduce training under that option. A native port would have to
preserve both mechanisms. The initial independent-customer profile therefore rejects cluster
and weight options; the independent-cluster extension is specified for later qualification and
must name whether customers or clusters define its target GRF contributors (2026c).

  For the six scores above, treating all rows as independent gives variance forty dollars squared.
Preserving two branch clusters while retaining the customer target gives 1600/9 dollars squared.
53.20. A native forest boundary that preserves the banking question                          1469


Giving the two branches equal total weight gives variance 225 dollars squared around the
changed target of twenty-five dollars. The standard errors are approximately 6.325, 13.333
and 15 dollars. Two clusters make a useful arithmetic counterexample and supply no empirical
confidence-coverage qualification. A single positive-weight cluster is refused. Zero total weight
is separately refused Causal banking research project (2026m); GRF contributors (2026c).
   Conditional prediction variance is another quantity. The native prediction strategy estimates
it using grouped trees and a variance-debiasing calculation; the binding copies the variance
values into variance.estimates. The R average-effect operation instead returns std.err,
already square-rooted. Squaring the wrong field or taking its square root twice changes the units.
The proposed adapter keeps the raw field identity, method and units, then creates any reported
interval only under a declared inference profile. Pointwise conditional intervals cannot become
a simultaneous customer band or an interval for their average through serialization. Likewise
excess.error, a finite-forest error diagnostic, is not a substitute for sampling uncertainty
GRF contributors (2026b,c).


53.20.4     Memory ownership, coordinates and model persistence

The inspected Data class is a read-only view of a borrowed contiguous column-major buffer.
Element (r, c) is read at offset cn + r, where n is the number of rows. Constructing the view
from a temporary vector does not transfer ownership. The host must keep the allocation alive
until all training or prediction threads have finished; it must validate shape, index ranges
and multiplication overflow before the call. A three-row, two-column example has columns
(1, 2, 3) and (10, 20, 30). Correct layout reads twenty at zero-based coordinate (1, 1); passing
row-major bytes to the same index formula reads three. Neither value is a memory error, so a
mere successful call cannot detect the scientific corruption GRF contributors (2026a); Causal
banking research project (2026m).
   Role coordinates must remain separate from predictor coordinates. The native setters
mark outcome, treatment, instrument and weight columns as disallowed split variables. The
host records the ordered covariate dictionary, row identifiers, role indices and training/query
distinction. It cannot infer those roles from whichever columns happen to be numeric. Missing
values in covariates are supported by inspected package paths, but are excluded by the initial
profile so that an undocumented imputation or missingness assumption is not introduced.
Conversion to double precision must preserve identifier strings separately and refuse nonfinite
numerical values rather than silently dropping affected customers.
   Model serialization also has ownership semantics. The inspected Rcpp helper iterates by
moving the unique pointer to each native tree into its serialized representation. The header
explicitly says the original forest cannot be used after that operation. A direct embedding
that serializes and then predicts on the consumed forest is therefore invalid. Either serialize an
explicitly supported copy, or deserialize the saved representation into a new object. Retain the
engine commit, ordered feature map, original training-data identity, nuisance vectors, options
and format version beside the forest. The selected source does not establish a stable C++ ABI
or a portable standalone model format. These are admission questions for a native route, not
problems solved by choosing a file extension GRF contributors (2026a).


53.20.5     A concrete request and result contract

The operation is estimate.effect. Its generic parameter schema accepts an engine
identifier and estimator identifier, so the proposed profile uses grf-r-native-2.6.1 and
binary-iid-aipw-all-v1 there. Detailed settings reside in an immutable configuration
1470                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


artifact, carried through the existing artifact list. That artifact binds the exact source commit,
treatment contrast, outcome/horizon, row and column roles, seed, thread count, tree options
and target. The adapter validates its own profile before dispatch; generic JSON acceptance
alone does not validate these scientific restrictions Causal banking research project (2026l).
   Library, CLI and MCP surfaces must resolve identical authorized data and configuration
identities. The context digest retains the estimand, population, units, information clock,
assumptions, sampling declaration and graph. The full request identity additionally binds
data bytes, configuration, engine environment and numerical settings. Changing the target
population or turning branch weighting on produces a different request; transport names
cannot cause reuse of a previous result. Graph endpoint marks and unresolved sets remain
intact. A forest is not a graph-identification service: if a retained model class gives different
effects and the query has no accepted identification argument, this profile cannot silently select
a graph.
   Before runtime admission, discovery of this engine returns unavailable. A recognized but
unsupported sampling regime, continuous treatment, dynamic policy request or unresolved
graph requirement returns unsupported with an actionable explanation. Nonfinite output,
failed subprocess execution or an invalid model artifact is a failure; no finite effect accompanies
it. A reviewed identification failure can return not-identified with its evidence, but the adapter’s
inability to analyze a model is not an impossibility proof. An overlap alarm produces a refusal
under the declared profile. Trimming or switching to an overlap population requires a newly
reviewed target and request.
   After engineering admission, a computed scalar estimate keeps its dollar unit, signed offer-
minus-no-offer contrast and target identifier. A diagnostic conditional-prediction artifact retains
query-row coordinates and explicitly denotes conditional means, not individual counterfactual
differences. The initial engineering result carries execution-only qualification and no confidence
claim. Conditional inference needs its own reviewed uncertainty construction and evidence.
A mathematically unbounded or disconnected result from another method must be returned
with its topology; this forest profile does not approximate it by a large finite interval.


53.20.6     Deployment choices and the next informative comparison

The package description requires R at least 3.5.0, C++17 and GNU make, links Rcpp and
RcppEigen, and imports additional packages including Matrix, DiceKriging, lmtest and
sandwich. These declarations are minimum/source requirements, not a tested environment
lock. The proposed R process must record the installed R and dependency versions, source and
binary hashes, compiler and flags, thread settings and runtime options. The inspected native
CMake file collects both source and test files into an executable; its presence does not supply a
ready production shared library or a reviewed installed ABI. Package metadata declares GPL-3
and the inspected source headers state GPL version 3 or later. Preserve file and dependency
terms and review distribution obligations before shipping; a subprocess boundary alone settles
neither licensing compatibility nor distribution duties GRF contributors (2026d).
   The parent process bounds wall time, memory and output size and publishes only a
complete validated result atomically. Standard output is the protocol channel; diagnostics
have a bounded separate log. A crash or timeout leaves a typed failure and its input identities.
No mid-tree recovery is promised. Replaying an immutable request starts from its recorded
seed and environment; bitwise equality across different compilers or thread settings remains
a measured property. One worker per isolated R process is the conservative initial choice
because the inspected binding also writes global runtime context. Concurrency inside a shared
embedding requires its own review.
53.20. A native forest boundary that preserves the banking question                         1471


   The proposal recommends the R/native route first because it retains the inspected nuisance,
score and aggregation paths. Direct native embedding may later reduce interface overhead
or fit a host’s deployment constraints, but would transfer those statistical and ownership
responsibilities to the host. A full algorithm port has the greatest maintenance and conformance
burden. Reject direct embedding for the initial profile until it reproduces the R path; this is a
scoped engineering choice, not a claim that native integration is impossible.
   The next comparison should freeze one environment and the complete workload: data
conversion, nuisance estimation, forest training, average-effect scoring, serialization, output
validation and failure handling. Compare the maintained R route with a direct-native candidate
only under identical inputs, target, options and estimator formulas. Exact fixtures first check
coordinates, residualization, score aggregation and refusal behavior. A separately registered
generated-data study can then examine coverage, availability, heterogeneity recovery and
resources, retaining weak-overlap and dependent cases in its denominator. Pure arithmetic
agreement cannot replace that study, and local runtime cannot establish bank workflow savings.
The useful investment question is whether a native route improves the complete workload
enough to justify owning the additional statistical and deployment machinery.
Chapter 54

The library, command line and MCP
service

54.1     An interface must preserve a scientific question
A servicing analyst asks whether an offer would improve the next twelve months’ net value
for accounts eligible today. A notebook, a scheduled command and an agent can all transmit
this question. They should receive the same conditional answer when they submit the same
declaration, inputs and method. They should also retain the same unresolved assumptions. A
successful call which replaces the target population, changes the sign or drops an unbounded
component of an uncertainty set has failed as a scientific interface even if its JSON is valid.
The preceding chapter establishes the exchange contract; this chapter develops the actual
access paths and the client behavior needed to preserve it.
   The implemented library entry is causalbank.runtime_v12.Runtime.invoke. The
command-line adapter and local MCP server use that runtime, its artifact store and the
scientific dispatcher. This shared implementation reduces divergence among surfaces. It does
not prove their equivalence: parsing, version negotiation, error handling and asynchronous
state can still alter the result seen by a client. Consequently an interface comparison must
examine complete canonical responses, including negative findings, rather than compare only
the estimated coefficient. The inspected source and recorded local trials support this narrow
architecture claim (Causal banking research project, 2026bi,n).
   The runtime advertises nine operations. Capability inspection reports the implemented
subset. Graph review checks a supplied declaration’s syntax. Identification attempts a supplied-
DAG back-door expression for independent units and a binary contrast. Estimation inverts
a Gaussian residual test using supplied moments and covariance. Sensitivity solves supplied
quadratic inequalities. Observation auditing checks declared timestamps. Report building,
job status and job cancellation provide the remaining three operations. Automatic problem
formulation, data-driven graph discovery and design comparison have no engine in this runtime.
They belong to the proposed architecture, and are absent from the advertised MCP tool list.
   These distinctions matter when an agent chooses a tool called estimate.effect. The
name identifies an operation family; the supported engine and estimator identifiers determine
what can actually run. An agent cannot turn the supplied-moment engine into a fitted causal
forest by changing its description. Nor does the graph syntax operation establish that a graph
represents the bank’s assignment mechanism. Capabilities should be inspected at the start
of a client session and retained with its results, because a proposed method and an installed
method are different inputs to a decision.


                                             1472
54.2. A complete request for an offer decision                                              1473


  Write a canonical request as Q = (o, C, A, p, B, k), where o is the operation, C the scientific
context, A the artifact references, p the operation parameters, B the resource budget and
k an optional replay key. The separate request identifier correlates a reply with a call. For
deterministic synchronous examples, the desired transport property is

                               Rlibrary (Q) = RCLI (Q) = RMCP (Q),

after decoding each transport’s wrapper. This is a scoped design property, tested on selected
cases. For jobs, compare stable handles and the same observed terminal state; two polls at
different times need not report the same intermediate state. Neither equality proves that C is
causally correct.


54.2      A complete request for an offer decision
Let A denote a binary offer, Y twelve-month net value in USD and X a pre-decision risk
score. The generated example declares the arrows X → A, X → Y and A → Y . Its target is
the offer-minus-no-offer average effect for eligible accounts. These are example declarations,
without bank observations or independently verified graph truth. An explicit unverified
assumption is more useful than silently treating the graph as known.
   The following Python file creates a complete request. Save it as offer_request.py and run
it with Python; its only output file is request.json. The example uses a loop to retain the
same evidence and review fields on each edge. There is no hidden inference step in that loop.

   The budget declares a twelve-second worker limit, one GiB of worker address space and
a 100,000-byte output limit. It requests zero model calls because this runtime has no model
backend. The observation clock names three fields; it does not assert that real records satisfy
the ordering. Actual row checks are a separate operation. Likewise, the sampling law records
independent accounts; repeated monthly observations do not become independent simply
because the client uses this string.
  This request is deliberately an identification request, with no data artifacts. Its answer is an
expression and the conditions under which that expression identifies the target. Converting that
expression into a numerical estimate requires an appropriate estimator and data construction.
The current moment engine is not a general next stage which accepts arbitrary account rows.
A client must identify a supported numerical path instead of treating a common operation
vocabulary as a guarantee of automatic end-to-end composition.


54.3     Calling the library and the command line
For the inspected installation, run Python with PYTHONPATH=src from the causal repository
root. The local environment is .runtime/in04/bin/python. The library use is small enough
to expose the whole boundary:
import json
from pathlib import Path
from causalbank.runtime_v12 import Runtime

request = json.loads(Path("request.json").read_text())
runtime = Runtime(Path.cwd() / ".runtime" / "offer-client")
response = runtime.invoke(request)
Path("response.json").write_text(json.dumps(response, indent=2) + "\n")

The runtime root is an operator configuration inside this repository’s .runtime tree. The
scientific request has no field for choosing an arbitrary directory, Python module or shell
command. The library can still raise validation exceptions for malformed requests before
producing a canonical response; the caller must retain those as invocation failures. The
example assumes its displayed valid request (Causal banking research project, 2026n).
  The corresponding CLI call takes the operation name and the same JSON file:
PYTHONPATH=src .runtime/in04/bin/python -m causalbank.cli_v12 \
  operation identify.effect --input request.json
54.4. Conditional identification and a useful refusal                                         1475


The command’s operation must agree with the request. Standard input is used when –input
is omitted or is -. To share the library’s operator store, set CAUSALBANK_STATE_ROOT in the
launching environment to its absolute path. The path is launch configuration, rather than
text supplied by an agent in the scientific request. Without this setting the CLI uses its
documented default local store.
   A notebook should save the complete response before displaying a concise interpretation.
In this example, the useful interpretation is “conditional adjustment expression, no fitted
dollar estimate.” Displaying only result.estimate would show null and omit the successful
identification result. Conversely, replacing null with zero would falsely assert that the offer has
no effect. The result’s kind, disposition and qualification determine what presentation
is appropriate.
   A scheduled consumer should retain both the process return code and parsed JSON. It must
first determine whether it received a canonical response or an adapter error object; the latter
need not contain result or scientific_context. Blindly indexing a nonexistent estimate can
convert a well-explained input failure into an opaque client crash. These practical distinctions
are part of the proposed common client library: validated decoding, faithful storage and an
explicit outcome for each branch. They are not supplied by printing an arbitrary JSON scalar.


54.4      Conditional identification and a useful refusal
For the declared graph, adjustment for X blocks the back-door path A ← X → Y . Let
Y (a) be the potential net value under offer state a. Consistency, conditional exchangeability
Y (a) ⊥ A | X, positivity on the target population’s support, and the declared sampling
interpretation give
                           Z
             E{Y (a)} =        E{Y (a) | X = x} dPX (x)
                           Z
                       =       E{Y | A = a, X = x} dPX (x),
                           Z
                     τ=        [E{Y | A = 1, X = x} − E{Y | A = 0, X = x}] dPX (x).

The first equality averages over the target risk distribution. The second uses the identifying
assumptions. The resulting units are USD per account over the declared horizon. This
derivation explains the returned adjustment_contrast: integrate over risk, take the one-
versus-zero contrast, and retain the outcome unit and independent-unit sampling declaration.
It is an application of the identification argument developed earlier in the monograph; the
execution confirms the expression and its metadata, not the causal premises (Causal banking
research project, 2026n).
   Two counterexamples clarify the consumer’s next action. If the sampling field is changed
to dependent months, the local identification routine returns unsupported. It is refusing
a request outside this implementation’s scope; it has not proved that a panel estimand is
unidentified. The appropriate next step is a reviewed longitudinal or dependent-sampling path.
Changing the field back solely to make the call succeed would conceal a scientific problem. If
a declared premise is marked contradicted, identification instead returns refused, with no
scientific result. The premise or target must then be reconsidered; an automatic retry with
unchanged information has no scientific benefit.
  Even within a supplied DAG, failure of the selected back-door attempt is not a general
nonidentification theorem. An alternative graph assumption or identification strategy may
succeed, while another query may require only a bound. The service states the failed method’s
1476                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


boundary in its result when available. A proposed agent should preserve that explanation,
route the case to a substantive alternative, and label any new assumptions. It should never
replace “this adjustment attempt failed” with “causal analysis is impossible.”


54.5     Uncertainty sets are part of the result type
A response may carry a set without a scalar estimate. To understand why the client must
preserve its topology, consider the explicitly generated inequality ab2 + cb + d ≤ 0, where b is
a scalar effect coordinate. Coefficient units are understood to make the terms commensurate;
the example uses a fixed normalized USD coordinate. The deterministic sensitivity operation
returns the solution set. Four elementary choices give independent algebraic checks of the
numerical representation:

Inequality            Real solution                Canonical interval array
b2 − 4 ≤ 0            [−2, 2]                      [[-2,2]]
b2 + 1 ≤ 0            ∅                            []
−b2 − 1 ≤ 0           R                            [[null,null]]
−b2 + 4 ≤ 0           (−∞, −2] ∪ [2, ∞)            [[null,-2],[2,null]]

The first and fourth follow by comparing b2 with four. The second is empty because b2 + 1
is strictly positive; the third is the whole line because −b2 − 1 is strictly negative. In these
interval arrays null denotes an unbounded endpoint according to position, not missing data.
An unknown set has a different representation: unknown topology and null intervals. All four
arrays agreed between the library and CLI and with these independent calculations. Their
uncertainty kind is sensitivity, coverage is none, and the probability level is null (Causal
banking research project, 2026n).
   An empty result is not a numerical failure and is not evidence of a zero effect. It can mean
that the stipulated restrictions have no joint solution. A whole-line result supplies no finite
restriction on this coordinate. For the disconnected result, taking the convex hull discards
the excluded central region; truncating the tails fabricates information. A client chart should
retain the two rays and label their interpretation. A lending decision that requires a guaranteed
positive net benefit cannot infer it from a set containing an unbounded negative ray.
   The moment engine supplies a second reason for preserving these objects. Suppose a moment
relation is mY −bmA = 0. Under the supplied Gaussian approximation, test inversion compares
                                             cα b
                     (m      b A )2
                      b Y − bm        with               b Y A + b2 Ω
                                               (ΩY Y − 2bΩ          b AA ),
                                             n

where n and the covariance matrix Ω b are supplied inputs and cα is the squared normal critical
value. For m coordinates the simultaneous option uses cα = {Φ−1 (1 − α/(2m))}2 , with Φ
the standard normal distribution function; the pointwise option uses m = 1 in that formula.
Rearrangement produces a quadratic inequality in b. A weak or zero denominator moment
can make its accepted set disconnected or unbounded. The generated input m     b = (1, 0), Ω
                                                                                           b =
diag(0.01, 1) and n = 100 indeed produces two unbounded components in the reference engine.
The supplied covariance and Gaussian approximation are assumptions of this calculation; this
fixture does not establish coverage for an arbitrary bank estimator.
   The client must also retain pointwise versus simultaneous interpretation, sampling law,
probability level, numerical limitations and construction evidence. A simultaneous collection
of coordinate sets does not by itself describe the full joint geometry. Downstream portfolio
54.6. Four different meanings of success                                                       1477


aggregation therefore needs an explicitly justified construction, rather than treating separately
reported endpoints as a joint distribution. Changing transport cannot supply the missing
dependence information.


54.6      Four different meanings of success
Transport success, invocation completion, scientific disposition and qualification answer different
questions. The first says a reply arrived. The second says the operation finished. The third
distinguishes a computed object from an unsupported, refused or unavailable scientific result.
The fourth records what evidence supports using that object. A proposed client must preserve
all four, because none is a substitute for the next.
   The observed examples illustrate the distinction without a hypothetical failure rate. The
back-door request completed with a computed expression and conditional-inference qualification.
The unimplemented discovery request and the dependent-sampling request completed with
an unsupported disposition. The contradicted-premise request completed with a refused
disposition. All four returned CLI exit zero. In contrast, changing the sign convention
while reusing an artifact bound to the old context produced a failed canonical response,
invalid_or_unavailable_input, and exit four. Adding an undeclared request property
produced an adapter validation error and exit two (Causal banking research project, 2026n).


CLI outcome          What the adapter establishes            What the client must inspect
Exit 0               Canonical status is completed,          Disposition, result kind,
                     queued, running or cancelled            qualification, and job payload state
                                                             when present
Exit 2               Request parsing, schema or              Error object; correct the request
                     semantic validation reached an          while retaining the original failure
                     adapter error
Exit 3               A missing-file or permission            Which operator input or local
                     exception reached the adapter           artifact was unavailable
Exit 4               Failed/rejected canonical response      Canonical error if present;
                     or another execution failure            otherwise the adapter error object

This is an adapter rule, not a universal classification of root causes. The runtime catches some
artifact access failures itself, returning a failed envelope that leads to exit four. Thus “artifact
problem” does not imply exit three. A client should branch on the actual response and record
the underlying cause, instead of guessing it from a coarse return code.
   For decision use, a conservative proposed display sequence is: validate and retain the
response; check operation and context identity; inspect execution status; interpret scientific
disposition; then render the typed result with its assumptions, uncertainty and qualification. A
computed timestamp diagnostic can contain failed rows. A computed set can be the whole line.
A completed identification operation can leave estimation entirely undone. The user-facing
conclusion should express these facts directly, rather than use a green success icon as a surrogate
for a supported financial decision.
   The same distinctions constrain automated repair. Malformed dates may admit a docu-
mented format correction. Missing causal assumptions require new information or an explicitly
changed problem. An unsupported engine may require another implementation. A weak-
information set may be the correct answer. A loop that retries until it obtains a positive scalar
would replace scientific reasoning with selection on favorable outputs.
