56.18.4     Useful precision is a property of the decision

Consider an explicitly assumed annual funding scenario. A baseline average balance of USD
2.6 million is repriced by 0.25 percentage points, costing USD 6,500. Incremental retained
funds earn a 1.5% annual spread net of their own offered deposit interest. The incremental
average balance is 0.25β million USD. With an illustrative workflow allowance of USD 500,
net profit is

       Π(β) = 106 (0.25β)(0.015) − 2.6 · 106 (0.0025) − 500 = 3750β − 7000 USD.               (56.6)

The average-balance convention is necessary for this annual spread calculation. A different
repricing base, within-year balance path, liquidity cost or net spread changes the function and
should be represented explicitly.
  The scenario allowance assigns USD 120 to data and identity preparation, 150 to integration
amortization, 100 to scientific review, 30 to computation and 100 to monitoring and recovery.
These are planning assumptions. Actual human adjudication, optional model calls, platform
review, implementation, security, deployment and continuing operations may exceed them.
Failed requests and retries belong in the workflow denominator. The allowance cannot be
presented as an observed bank price.
56.18. From a funding response to a defensible treasury decision                                1523


   The break-even response is β = 28/15. A point estimate β = 2 gives profit USD 500.
Mapping the two intervals from the fitted-nuisance example through the increasing function in
(56.6) gives

               Π([1.9, 2.1]) = [125, 875],      Π([1.7, 2.3]) = [−625, 1625]   USD.

The first interval excludes a loss under the stated cost scenario; the second does not. This is
the practical importance of the missing variance component. It neither demonstrates bank
profit nor makes every interval decision-ready. The identification, unit map and covariance
premises must also be justified. Uncertainty about costs can be propagated by taking the
financial image over their declared scenario set as well.
  For the weak-denominator rays, a finite favorable point estimate is especially misleading.
Under the same monotone profit map their image is

                                  (−∞, −10750] ∪ [−3250, ∞).

Neither a finite lower bound nor a narrow range is available. Increasing the number of
observations need not resolve a structurally weak or invalid normalization. Possible responses
include changing the target, seeking a better justified design or reporting sensitivity. Choosing
a favorable representative point does not resolve the information problem.


56.18.5     What the local library and CLI actually demonstrated

The bounded exercise specified 29 authored cases, each invoked through the library and CLI
initially and after re-instantiation or process restart. Two further calls changed the horizon
under a previously used key. The resulting 118 service slots all matched their fixed expectations
after two disclosed harness repairs. The original harness first omitted a standard library import
and later referred to a nonexistent copied fixture identifier. The first failure preceded any
service call; the second occurred after 116 completed slots. Both failures and the unchanged
116-result prefix were preserved, and the corrections were recorded before the affected calls.
This is evidence from an amended execution, not evidence that the original executable ran
without repair (Causal banking research project, 2026j).
   Of the 118 responses, 48 were computed outputs, 40 were failed or unavailable input results,
eight refused contradicted premises, twenty reported unsupported operations and two rejected
changed-horizon reuse. The computed outputs include diagnostics, deterministic sensitivity,
unbounded and empty sets. They must not be counted as 48 useful causal estimates. All
29 library/CLI/restart comparisons agreed on complete semantic responses, excluding only
the request identifier. Independent decimal root calculations and 451 direct rational-grid
membership checks agreed with the retained sets. This finite screen does not estimate statistical
coverage or a population failure probability.
   The feature-clock case retained four failures: availability at the decision, a missing availability
field, availability before the event, and timestamps without time zones. The valid row passed.
Changing units or the availability field after binding a moment artifact caused a context
failure, and corrupting the artifact bytes caused an access failure. Continuous-treatment
and dependent-unit back-door requests, identity/inclusion audits, nuisance fitting and design
evaluation remained unsupported in the selected paths.
   Most consequentially, summaries with explicitly unresolved household identity or unknown
inclusion still returned conditional intervals. Contradicted premises caused refusal, but an
unverified premise was not automatically treated as a contradiction. The service also retained a
declared dependent sampling label without verifying an upstream long-run covariance estimator.
1524                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


These observed boundaries mean the proposed consumer needs an explicit prerequisite review
before presenting a financial recommendation. Passing schema validation, a hash check or a
clock audit is insufficient.
   The measured sum of invocation times was approximately 56.46 seconds, including failed,
replayed and rejected service requests and their worker or CLI startup. This is a local
measurement of the stated exercise. The initial failed harness startup was not timed, and
the measure excludes authoring, repairs, review, manuscript work and idle intervals. Process
high-water memory is not simultaneous memory for an entire process tree. These measurements
therefore cannot establish complete bank workflow cost or production throughput. No new MCP
transport qualification, foreign-language adapter, live model or actual workspace consumer
was exercised.


56.18.6     A minimal next prototype with an informative stopping rule

The next prototype should first restrict the scientific claim. One useful design jointly generates
dependent monthly funding histories, known households, observed and missing follow-up, and
a specified nuisance estimator. It can compare covariance methods under the same generated
law, keeping the household truth and future outcomes outside the analysis inputs. Useful
outputs are all-attempt coverage where justified, set topology, availability, width relative to the
financial threshold, erroneous action rates and complete resource categories. A matched simple
estimator supplies a baseline; a flexible learner must justify its extra cost and assumptions.
   This experiment needs a reviewed derivation and prospectively fixed regimes, replications,
criteria and stopping rule. The present finite conformance screen cannot supply those perfor-
mance results. Public funding panels can inform plausible scales, release delays and institutional
continuity. Generated truth supplies controlled interventions and unit maps that the public
observations may lack. Neither source should be credited with information that it does not
contain.
   A contract double for a treasury consumer can separately test whether absent identity,
inclusion, covariance or decision-cost evidence causes the intended hold disposition. Such a
double demonstrates a proposed consumer boundary; it is not an accepted sibling-repository
workflow. An owner-run bank study becomes informative after a bounded prototype identifies
a consequential remaining uncertainty, an attainable precision target and plausible value from
resolving it. This preserves a practical path from proposal to evidence while retaining the
distinction between a computed response set and a defensible funding decision.


56.19      An observation contract from source records to a contact
           decision
A servicing manager wants to know whether contacting an eligible borrower reduces the
probability of an adverse event during the following twelve months. Before comparing contact
with no contact, the analysis must establish which borrower each record describes, what
the adverse-event label means, which borrowers could enter the observed sample, and which
information was available when contact was chosen. These requirements are related, but one
cannot stand in for another. A correctly dated row can belong to the wrong borrower; a
correctly linked record can carry a noisy label; and a table of correct labels can represent
a selected population. The proposed observation contract makes these distinctions explicit
before downstream causal analysis.
  The immediate design uses generated laws and the existing local library and command-line
56.19. An observation contract from source records to a contact decision                        1525


service. Its purpose is to establish what a minimal prototype can preserve and which further
operation is justified. It does not require an expensive bank validation merely to explain a
failure mechanism. The development sequence is to specify the observation law, demonstrate
the consequence of violating it, implement a narrow supported path, and then ask whether
an unresolved bank-specific question could change the investment decision (Causal banking
research proposal project, 2026g).


56.19.1     Keep the information clock separate from outcome ascertainment

For a feature record, write event time te , first usable availability ta , and decision time td . The
selected admission rule is te ≤ ta < td . Equality of event and availability is permitted; equality
of availability and decision is not. A corrected value published after the decision retains its
later availability even when it refers to an earlier event. Comparing timezone-aware instants
avoids inventing a time ordering from differently displayed local times. None of these checks
establishes that the supplied timestamps themselves are truthful.
   An outcome has a different role. An event six months after contact can be an eligible twelve-
month outcome, although it must not appear among the features available before contact. Its
ascertainment date, censoring rule, revision history and horizon belong in the outcome contract.
Applying the feature clock to every row would reject legitimate follow-up observations; ignoring
availability would admit future information. The proposed consumer therefore declares the
row’s role before selecting an audit. The present reference service implements the strict feature
clock only and explicitly withholds its alternative-clock operation (Causal banking research
proposal project, 2026i).
   The proposed manifest also retains the source identity and owner declaration, license and
version, extraction and transformation history, origin and household identifiers, candidate
linkage maps, inclusion declarations, label definition and adjudication evidence, and the counts
of accepted, rejected and unavailable records. A byte hash binds the content that was used. It
cannot establish who originally observed an event or whether the contents are correct. Source
custody, content integrity and scientific measurement validity consequently have separate
evidence fields and separate failure reasons (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026g).


56.19.2     Marginal inclusion probabilities do not determine precision

Consider a fixed population with two origin values y1 = 20 and y2 = 80. The equally
weighted population mean is 50. Let Ri indicate inclusion and suppose both marginal inclusion
probabilities are πi = 1/2. The expansion estimator is
                                         2
                                      1X   Ri yi
                                 µ
                                 b=              = 20R1 + 80R2 .
                                      2 i=1 πi

Its expectation is 50 under either independent inclusion or a shared inclusion decision R1 = R2 .
Under independent inclusion, its four equally likely values are 0, 20, 80, 100, giving variance 1700.
Under shared inclusion, it equals zero or 100 with equal probability, giving variance 2500. The
marginal probabilities and expected sample size are identical in the two experiments (Causal
banking research proposal project, 2026h).
   More generally, for a fixed population of size N , known positive inclusion probabilities and
joint probabilities πij = E(Ri Rj ), direct expansion gives
                                     1 X πij − πi πj
                         Var(µ
                             b) =                    yi yj ,      πii = πi .                  (56.7)
                                    N 2 i,j πi πj
1526                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


This is a design identity, obtained by expanding the variance of a weighted sum. It is not
an estimated variance from the observed sample, and it assumes that the origin values and
selection law have the stated meaning. In the two-origin example the extra cross term is 800.
Replacing the joint law by independent selection because a file contains only the two marginal
probabilities would discard that term.
   If the second origin is never included, populations (20, 80) and (20, 120) induce the same
observed law but have means 50 and 70. The missing information is different from an imprecise
estimate of a positive inclusion probability. No finite replacement for 1/0 identifies the unseen
value. Outcome bounds, a changed sampling design or additional information can restrict
the answer. If inclusion probabilities are fitted, their estimation error and relation to the
outcome contribution enter a new uncertainty argument; Equation (56.7) does not supply that
argument automatically (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026h).
   Identity ambiguity has another geometry. Two received records with values 20 and 80 can
be mapped bijectively to two origins in either order. The total is 100 under both maps, but
the second-minus-first origin contrast is 60 or −60. Independently drawing a match for each
record could assign both to one origin, which is outside this stipulated bijective class. The
consumer should retain the admissible joint maps, the target functional and any evidence used
to remove a map. These two values describe an authored measurement contrast; they are not
a treatment effect or a probability distribution over all possible linkage mechanisms.


56.19.3     Noisy audit labels can change the proposed action

Let Z be a true binary adverse event and B its recorded label. Write p = P (Z = 1),
s = P (B = 1 | Z = 1) and f = P (B = 1 | Z = 0) for prevalence, sensitivity and false-positive
probability in the declared target population. The law of total probability gives

                                  q = P (B = 1) = f + (s − f )p.                             (56.8)

This relation is about measurement. It does not identify a contact effect. If sensitivity or false
positives vary with contact, borrower state or time, the corresponding conditional laws must
be specified and transported appropriately. Correcting an aggregate prevalence cannot replace
the assignment and identification assumptions needed to compare interventions.
   Two strictly positive authored joint laws illustrate the information gap. The triples (s, f, p) =
(9/10, 1/10, 3/10) and (1/2, 1/10, 3/5) both give q = 17/50. More records of B alone cannot
distinguish these two measurement mechanisms. An audit may resolve the issue only to
the extent that it supplies suitable independent truth, known or justified inclusion, and
a relevant population. Calling the same noisy label a gold standard does not create that
information (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026h).
   Suppose, solely for a planning example, that contact prevents an event with probability
one half among borrowers who would otherwise experience it, has no adverse event effect
on the others, and costs USD 200. With an event loss of USD 1000, the assumed expected
incremental value is

                        V (p) = 500p − 200    USD per eligible borrower.

The two equally compatible reported-label laws imply values −50 and 100. The sign changes
even before sampling error is considered. The one-half prevention mechanism is an additional
stipulated causal model; it is not a measured treatment effect inferred from q. The example
therefore motivates an experiment on the consequential missing information, without asserting
measured bank returns (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026h).
56.19. An observation contract from source records to a contact decision                            1527


56.19.4      Propagate the fitted measurement law and preserve singular cases

When d = s − f ̸= 0, the algebraic inverse is p = (q − f )/d. Suppose a particular sampling
and fitting design justifies a joint expansion of (qb, sb, fb) with leading contributions (ψq , ψs , ψf ).
Differentiating the inverse gives
                                            ψq − pψs − (1 − p)ψf
                                     ψp =                        .                                 (56.9)
                                                   s−f
For a declared common normalization, write the justified covariance of those contributions as
Ω. Then the corresponding leading variance is g ⊤ Ωg, where g = (1, −p, −(1 − p))⊤ /d. Different
audit and main-sample sizes require their proper scaling in the joint expansion. Household
dependence, shared label adjudication, reused fitting data and selection weights cannot be
omitted merely because each marginal estimate has a reported standard error.
   An exact covariance illustration makes the cross terms visible. Take independent unit-
variance X, Y , and stipulate ψq = X, ψs = −X + Y , ψf = 0, p = 3/10 and d = 4/5.
Equation (56.9) then gives leading variance 89/32, whereas treating the fitted measurement
law as fixed gives 25/16. These are authored influence contributions, separate from any claim
about the sampling law of the binary example. They show why a covariance argument must
concern the whole construction. They do not establish that arbitrary audit estimators have
this expansion (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026h).
  When s = f , the recorded label probability is f for every p. Near this regime the inverse
and its derivative can be unstable. A more faithful proposed interface carries a region C for
the joint observable and measurement parameters and reports
                      P(C) = {p ∈ [0, 1] : ∃(q, s, f ) ∈ C, q = f + (s − f )p}.                  (56.10)
If the true triple lies in C, its true prevalence belongs to this set, by substitution. Thus a
genuinely justified joint-region coverage statement transfers to the projected set. The projection
cannot manufacture that joint guarantee from an arbitrary collection of marginal intervals. Nor
does this argument establish a sharp identified set for a richer observed law. The observation
model, candidate region and target restriction remain part of the claim.
   For fixed s = 9/10, f = 1/10 and an expressly deterministic sensitivity range q ∈
[3/10, 19/50], the compatible prevalence interval is [1/4, 7/20]. Equivalently, (4p−1)(20p−7) ≤
0. Mapping that whole interval through the illustrative value function gives [−75, −25] USD.
At complete loss of label information, the physical range p ∈ [0, 1] gives [−200, 300] USD. An
empty compatibility set instead indicates conflict among the supplied ranges and restrictions;
it is not evidence of zero loss. The generic local quadratic service can represent finite intervals,
empty sets, the whole line and disconnected rays, but does not impose every target’s physical
range. The proposed consumer must preserve the original result and apply justified target
restrictions explicitly (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026h,i).

56.19.5      What the local boundary comparison can establish

The registered comparison fixes 26 authored cases across the library and command-line routes,
with an initial call and a restarted call through each. Two further calls retain an existing
key while changing the target horizon. All 106 slots include refused, unsupported and failed
requests as well as computed results. Complete-response parity excludes only the request
correlation identifier. This tests a bounded local contract; it does not estimate graph accuracy,
sampling coverage or bank decision value (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026g,j).
  The cases deliberately expose the distinction between a completed diagnostic and a validated
observation. An empty row array can satisfy every declared clock vacuously. Duplicate origins,
1528                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


false labels and an explicitly contradicted identity statement can accompany valid timestamps.
The present clock operation checks their timing and retains its limited qualification; it does
not repair the other defects. Asking it jointly for clocks and identity does not silently upgrade
its scope. Measurement fitting, inclusion validation and noisy-label truth remain separate
unsupported requests (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026i,j).
   Supplied-moment calculations reveal another boundary. An unverified measurement state-
ment can accompany a conditional numerical answer, while an explicitly contradicted premise
causes the selected estimator to refuse. The service does not establish the truth of either
declaration, automatically require a preceding relevant audit, or connect that audit to a full
causal analysis. The prototype recommendation is therefore a consumer admission rule that
requires a nonempty audit of the right role and version, then either verifies the remaining
premises or propagates their uncertainty and limitations. This admission rule is specified here;
it is not claimed as an implemented bank workflow (Causal banking research proposal project,
2026g,j).
   All 106 registered requests matched the frozen boundary expectations, and all 26 cases
preserved semantic responses across the two routes and restart. The denominator contains
52 computed outputs, 20 unsupported requests, four scientific refusals, 28 failed/unavailable
results and two rejected changed-horizon requests. A computed output includes diagnostics
and generic sets; this count is not the number of identified or useful causal estimates. All
negative dispositions remain in the comparison. Independent rational evaluation checked 1,446
points against the supplied inequalities (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026j).
   Total invocation wall time, including failed requests, replay and worker or CLI launch, was
42.398 seconds in this local run. Active runner time was 43.542 seconds, including fixture
import and journaling. These measurements exclude idle gaps between bounded segments,
initial runner startup, author review and all unimplemented work. Parent and child memory
records are separate process high-water readings, not simultaneous process-tree memory. They
do not establish a bank service level, a full workflow price or a performance advantage over
another product.
   The journal preserved every earlier request across four execution segments and a final
aggregation-only resume. Restart reused the saved artifact references and idempotency
identities. It did not test process termination at every possible publication point or multi-host
recovery. No native foreign-language engine, sibling repository, live model or authentic bank
owner participated in this screen (Causal banking research proposal project, 2026j).


56.19.6    Choose the next information purchase by its decision consequence

The first useful prototype combines the existing clock and artifact boundary with one explicit
observation model and a consumer that preserves unresolved maps, selection and label uncer-
tainty. A public dictionary can explain a recorded field, and generated truth can test whether
the interface loses information. Neither proves that a bank’s historical labels are correct.
Source navigation, proposed transforms and numerical operations should remain separately
accountable when an agent or another repository supplies them. An actual sibling trial needs
its own request, source/export identity, response, failure/restart trace and owner disposition.
A contract double cannot substitute for that execution.
   The complete cost account includes source acquisition and rights, extraction, identity resolu-
tion, audit sampling and adjudication, fitting and covariance work, data transfer, integration,
scientific review, storage, failed requests, monitoring and recovery. Local invocation time
prices only a subset of that work. Missing prices stay unknown. Before purchasing costly bank
evidence, the proposal asks whether the current feasible decision values differ enough that
56.20. What an executed interface result actually establishes                                1529


improved identity, inclusion or label information could change the action. If all admitted values
already imply the same feasible action, more precise measurement may have little incremental
decision value. When signs differ, the relevant study targets the uncertainty causing that
difference, with its cost compared against a justified expected benefit. The present generated
examples establish this rationale for a bounded prototype and an explicit later experiment;
they do not establish that any particular bank experiment will be profitable (Causal banking
research proposal project, 2026g,h).


56.20       What an executed interface result actually establishes
A proposal can contain an implemented local dispatcher, a proposed Java adapter, a mocked
external consumer and an exact mathematical reference at the same time. The integration
argument depends on keeping their evidence separate. The scientific meaning of an output
does not become stronger merely because it passes through a real CLI or MCP server. A graph-
syntax check remains a syntax check; an unsupported policy request remains unsupported
when its refusal is correctly transported to a client.
   The shared response therefore needs two independent descriptions. One records how the
result was obtained: design only, static inspection, project reference, consumer double, actual
local engine, actual transport, or an externally run consumer. The other records the scientific
disposition: computed within a specified method, refused because declared premises conflict,
unsupported, unknown or unavailable. A generated dataset can be processed by an actual
engine. A mock can also return realistic numbers. Input provenance and execution provenance
must both be visible before a result is interpreted.
   For an actual execution claim, the evidence binds the selected source and schema, runtime
and dependency versions, scientific context, input bytes, route, request, response and terminal
failure state. A run journal retains all attempts and resource scope. An external package
name or a source-code pin alone is insufficient. Replays should be distinguished from fresh
computations and conflicting context should invalidate an idempotency key. Owner-run
consumer acceptance adds a named owner, actual consumer configuration and its acceptance
criteria; a local substitute cannot confer that acceptance.
   The available local runtime implements nine narrow operations: capabilities, graph syntax
review, supplied-DAG back-door identification, supplied-moment Gaussian residual inversion,
deterministic quadratic sensitivity sets, observation-clock diagnostics, reports and job status/-
cancellation. Its actual local transport evidence includes eleven scientific cases agreeing across
library, CLI and an MCP SDK client/server exchange using protocol 2025-11-25. The qualifi-
cation applies to the recorded local stdio environment. It does not establish modern-protocol
or HTTP support, arbitrary discovery, a longitudinal policy estimator or a live language-model
backend. The local agent controller’s 80 conformance checks involved zero live model calls
(Causal banking proposal, 2026q).
   A further servicing screen exercised 98 actual library and CLI invocations, including
restart/replay and changed-horizon conflicts. All 24 four-way semantic comparisons agreed,
and 964 independent rational membership checks reproduced the returned deterministic
sensitivity sets. The frozen suite nevertheless retains a negative result: 94 of 98 expected
outcomes matched. Four corrupt-input cases returned the documented artifact_access code
where the authored expectation named a different error. Each failed safely with no numerical
result or qualification. Diagnosing an expectation error does not rewrite the original trial as a
pass. The same trial shows that an actual engine can return correctly scoped unsupported
and refused results; it does not show that a servicing estimator has been installed (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ao).
1530                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The distinction also changes cost interpretation. The servicing runner measured 35.4281
seconds summed across invocations and 36.5564 seconds of active runner time. Parent and child
peak resident memory were 45,056 and 104,448 KiB, respectively; these are separate process
maxima and cannot be added to claim a concurrent memory peak. The timing covers this
bounded local screen, not a commercial engine, an external consumer or bank-scale deployment.
A future comparison should include setup, transfer, failures, review and recovery in the same
accounting boundary before proposing a service-level or economic benefit (Causal banking
proposal, 2026ao).


56.21      Servicing evidence, policy values and the proposed next
           experiment
The servicing example has two different mathematical tasks. Exact enumeration of a finite
declared model can compare fixed policies. Estimating the value of a policy from incomplete
histories under hidden assignment information is a harder problem. The available finite
reference gives values 11/8 for no assistance, 2 for assistance to everyone and 133/80 under
the stipulated stress construction. These are generated model values, not fitted bank effects.
The library/CLI screen exercises supported graph, clock and sensitivity operations; requests
for the absent policy estimator return no policy estimate (Causal banking proposal, 2026ao).
   The conservative precision calculation is an adverse result worth retaining. At n = 1000 the
evaluation radius is approximately 8.242685524, greater than the complete single-policy range
width of eight in the declared finite model. The illustrative combined radius is approximately
9.615113642. Such a bound can be mathematically valid yet unhelpful for deciding between the
fixed policies. It is not evidence that collecting 1000 bank histories is a worthwhile experiment.
Better precision requires an explicitly justified sharper method or a better information design;
replacing the number with a narrow heuristic would change the guarantee (Causal banking
proposal, 2026ao).
   The missing-information examples are equally consequential. Two hidden-state models can
have identical observations but effects .6 and zero. Two informative-dropout models can have
identical observed histories but cohort means .25 and .75. More observations of the same
incomplete information do not identify the missing distinction. A separate proposed continuous
Gaussian policy benchmark with quadratic reward also lies outside the bounded finite-table
theorem. It must retain its own tail and integrability analysis rather than inherit the bounded
guarantee by analogy (Causal banking proposal, 2026ao).
   A planning scenario can still indicate what a prototype might be worth studying. The
fixed-policy contrast 2 − 11/8 = 5/8, multiplied by 1000 customers and an assumed USD100
per utility unit, gives USD62,500. Subtracting an assumed additional full-workflow cost of
USD10,000 gives USD52,500. Assistance costs were already deducted inside the reward and
are not subtracted again. Every currency conversion, customer count and additional cost
is stipulated. The calculation is a scenario for sensitivity analysis, not measured bank ROI
(Causal banking proposal, 2026ao).
   The next experiment should first test a selected policy estimator against exact references
under controlled assignment, overlap and dropout mechanisms. It should keep training and
evaluation separate, retain every failed request, and compare a fixed policy with the chosen
trained-policy alternative under the same reward and observation law. Bank data become
relevant only if the prototype isolates a consequential assumption or precision requirement
that the public and generated study cannot resolve. Until then, an honest negative precision
result and a typed refusal are useful proposal evidence.
Chapter 57

Data organization, execution and
reusable interfaces

The mathematical operations of Chapter 52 share infrastructure, but not every fitted model or
sampling argument. Their common construction starts with reproducible decision histories,
then separates the scientific plan from its physical execution. A standalone application and an
embedded library should submit the same request and receive the same result. Otherwise an
analysis can change meaning when moved from a research notebook into a bank workflow.


57.1      Constructing a history from economic and information
          time
Represent an event revision by e = (k, j, v, te , ta , x, u, z): stable event key k, entity j, revision
v, economic time te , availability time ta , value x, unit u and void marker z. A decision has a
stable key and time τ . Under an explicitly chosen inclusive availability convention, its known
revision of event k is
                                 v ∗ (k, τ ) = max{v : ta (k, v) ≤ τ }.
If the source has a different revision order, that order must replace the numerical maximum.
For a lookback ℓ, a monetary feature is

Revision selection precedes economic-window filtering. If a later correction moves an event
beyond τ , filtering time first would resurrect an obsolete revision. Likewise a late-arriving past
event belongs to a retrospective accounting view but may be absent from the history available
to the historical policy.
   The feature computation needs a source-completeness declaration. Zero observed transac-
tions can mean a complete feed with no activity, an unconnected account or a failed batch.
Only the first supports a zero activity value under the stated feed contract. Missingness
indicators, known outages and event-count denominators should survive construction. Treating
each absent row as zero would silently replace the observation operator in Chapter 11.
   A bank may have several decision clocks: quote, approval, acceptance, settlement and
account posting. Features available at approval need not have been available at quotation. A
timestamp equality may also conceal unknown within-batch ordering. The initial convention


                                                         1531
1532                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


can reject such ambiguity or use a documented cutoff; it should not invent millisecond order.
Period-end stocks, period sums and period averages need separate aggregation definitions, as
the aliasing calculations demonstrated.
   Entity linkage introduces another layer. Legal customer, household, account, facility, branch
and corporate group are distinct units. A household action can affect several accounts; a branch
rollout induces shared assignment. Crosswalks need effective and availability dates. When
entity membership is uncertain, the product should preserve the linkage hypothesis or weighted
alternatives needed by the declared analysis. A hard merge changes both potential outcomes
and the independent sampling units. The total-variance decomposition in Section 11.5 shows
why exporting one identifier without its uncertainty can understate error.


57.2     What automatic organization can and cannot infer
Automatic profiling can propose event keys, candidate clocks, repeated decisions, missingness
patterns, currencies, ownership crosswalks and aggregation rules. It can compare the proposal
with physical data, report violations and display the rows that justify a mapping. An analyst
then supplies the economic semantics: which field is the action, when the bank knew a
value, what the outcome means, and which changes were possible. This produces a reusable
observation specification rather than an unexplained cleaned table.
  The proposal process should use competing hypotheses when evidence is ambiguous. For
example, a table with several rows per customer-month may contain revisions, different
products, or repeated actions. Deduplicating it under the first hypothesis can delete genuine
decisions under the third. The system can rank the hypotheses by key consistency and source
metadata, but causal conclusions require the selected interpretation. A useful user view shows
the consequences: population size, affected histories, assignment timing and target units under
each mapping.
   Schema tools, columnar engines, feature stores and catalogs provide parts of this workflow
(duckdb contributors, 2026b; pola-rs contributors, 2026; unionai-oss contributors, 2026; feast-
dev contributors, 2026; datahub-project contributors, 2026; open-metadata contributors, 2026;
moj-analytical-services contributors, 2026). Their source-specific limitations were established
in Section 17.7. The common product should preserve the bank’s existing asset identifiers and
attach the causal observation semantics. It should avoid maintaining a competing catalog or
treating catalog lineage as a discovered economic graph.
   The output is a versioned trajectory or panel view with an explicit loss-of-information
declaration. For example, a monthly snapshot may discard within-month action order. That
view is suitable for a model assuming one monthly decision, but cannot support a finer
sequential intervention merely by adding a lag column. The original event references must
remain recoverable so an alternative clock can be reconstructed.


57.3     A scientific plan and a physical plan
The scientific plan fixes the target, model restrictions, observation view, identification expres-
sion, estimator, inference construction, statistical split and numerical tolerances. The physical
plan chooses data partitions, workers, memory limits, caching and reduction order. Changes to
the latter are permitted only when they preserve the former. This is the execution counterpart
of Equation (52.2).
  Each materialized object should identify its inputs and semantic version. A result refers to
57.4. The algebra that can be distributed                                                    1533


the frozen scientific plan, data snapshot, qualified backend revision, random seeds, numerical
diagnostics and source lineage. An input correction creates a new result lineage; it does not
rewrite the earlier answer. Deterministic content hashes are useful identities, but they do not
establish that two differently serialized scientific models are equivalent. Canonicalization rules
need their own specification.
   For cross-fitting, a fold is a function of the permitted sampling unit, assigned before
scheduling. A household remains in the same fold when its account rows move between
workers. Multiway or blocked-time designs need their own split objects. Hyperparameter
selection, feature screening and representation learning must follow the same training/evaluation
boundary as the nuisance model. Storing only a model checkpoint while losing its training
population makes later leakage review impossible.
   Retries need contribution identities. A task can be retried without adding its score twice if
the reducer commits at most one completed artifact for each tuple of analysis, fold, partition
and attempt lineage. This is an engineering idempotency requirement; a mathematical sum
alone does not supply it. Partial failure should leave a resumable plan and an incomplete
result, not a silently smaller study.

each partition by its own mean destroys this identity. For entity/date clustering, retain sums

   Different estimators require different reductions. Linear IV/GMM can accumulate moment

regularized inverse problem do not generally reduce to the same score mean. The operation
catalogue must advertise its actual sufficient computational outputs.

construction, and outer products cost O(Cd2 ). Dense storage for E entities by D dates uses
O(EDd) even when few intersections occur. A sparse implementation can reduce storage to
the observed intersections, but its hash/sort costs and data skew must be measured. Streaming
over rows is not a guarantee of bounded memory as the number of statistical groups grows.

57.5     State-space and discovery workloads scale differently
For N independent trajectories, horizon T and K hidden states, dense forward/backward
evaluation costs O(N T K 2 ) per likelihood pass. An EM iteration can distribute trajectories
and combine expected transition/emission counts under a common parameter vector. Mixing
counts from different parameter iterations breaks the EM objective and its ascent argument.
Online or asynchronous updates are different algorithms and need their own convergence
conditions.
   Within a single trajectory, messages have a chronological dependency. Unnormalized
transition/emission matrices can be composed associatively, so a parallel prefix construction
is possible, but dense matrix products cost O(K 3 ) instead of the O(K 2 ) vector update and
require careful scaling. It is a performance tradeoff, not free parallelism. Smoothing requires
corresponding backward information. For continuous states, particle count, state dimension,
degeneracy and resampling communication can dominate costs; likelihood error must be
assessed in the downstream parameter or policy units.
   A learned structural model also has repeated optimizer, posterior or regularization loops.
Reporting only the speed of one filter pass omits much of its cost. The relevant workload
includes initialization, multiple starts, rank diagnostics, parameter uncertainty and policy
evaluation. The approximation should be named: sparse transition, low-rank factor, variational
family, particle distribution or finite state truncation. Each may change a scientific model or
numerical error.
  For p observed series and maximum lag L, even storing candidate lagged pairs requires
order p2 L objects. Conditional-independence searches add conditioning-set complexity; dense
matrix-exponential acyclicity constraints have another scaling profile. Screening or hierarchical
grouping can make the workload feasible, but may remove an adjustment path or a weak
confounder. Any screening restriction therefore belongs in the discovery model or its recovery
argument. Changing to monthly frequency is an observation change, not merely a compute
optimization.
   The initial deployment should support local columnar execution for bounded workloads,
then qualified distribution where the algebra allows it. Ray is a potential scheduling component
(ray-project contributors, 2026); it does not provide the cluster or mixing assumptions. GPU
acceleration is most plausible for dense numerical kernels and learned nuisance models. Sorting
temporal revisions, irregular groups and small exact identification problems can have different
bottlenecks. A hardware choice should follow a measured workload and error tolerance.


57.6     One core library and three standalone workspaces
The standalone product should offer three initial workspaces sharing the same request and
evidence objects.
   The intervention study workspace starts with a population and a proposed or historical
decision. It constructs an encouragement, adjusted effect or rollout analysis; shows overlap,
timing and comparison groups; and produces effects in outcome and financial units. A reviewer
can inspect which assumptions distinguish receipt from invitation and which aggregation
defines the reported business effect.
   The sequential decision workspace reconstructs customer histories, compares observed-
history policies and controlled-state explanations, and displays feasible actions, support and
value uncertainty. It includes policy alternatives and the cost account. An attractive latent
policy cannot bypass its logger and identification review.
57.7. Interfaces for neighboring financial applications                                     1535


  The dynamic systems workspace combines panel and macro time series, observation-frequency
analysis, structural-shock alternatives and discovery. It compares graph/model classes and
their implied response sets. A user can see why finer data, a new instrument or an experiment
would change the conclusion.
   In each workspace the primary view should answer the user’s decision: what action is
compared, for whom, over which horizon, at what expected value and with which unresolved
assumptions. Technical traces, scores and solver logs remain available to researchers and
validators without becoming mandatory steps for every business reader. An embedded client
uses the same operations through a library or job service and can render its own application-
specific view.

57.8      Construction sequence and measurable acceptance
The first construction stage implements immutable observation views, scientific requests,
identification traces and bounded result types. It needs exact positive and negative fixtures
before a general interface is advertised. Stage two qualifies adjusted/encouragement/cohort
methods and finite-horizon observed-history values against independent numerical references,
including their cluster and policy-specific scores.
   Stage three connects controlled-state fitting and discovery to the same scientific objects. It
starts with finite models, supported graph classes and explicit unresolved outputs. Latent
causal identification, proxy stability, uncertainty propagation and structural choice remain
visible subtasks. They belong in the initial research architecture, even where their numerical
qualification takes longer than ordinary adjustment.
   Stage four measures the complete workflow and tests reuse in the three workspaces. For
a fixed scientific request, measure data reconstruction, nuisance/latent fitting, inference,
sensitivity, review and report production separately. Record wall time, peak memory, pro-
cessor/accelerator use, retries, spill volume and numerical disagreement against the qualified
reference. Throughput without the required diagnostics is a different output and an invalid
economic comparison.
   Acceptance should require successful replay, deliberate failure behavior, target-preserving
adapter tests and appropriate repeated-sample checks. Performance targets must be attached
to a workload: number of entities, decisions, variables, lags, clusters and latent states, rather
than a single bank-wide row count. Availability, access control, locality and operational
recovery are deployment requirements to be specified with a particular bank; the proposed
scientific core does not establish their implementation.
   This sequence permits a useful independent product and shared library without assuming
that all host applications use the same causal model. Its central reusable asset is the preserved
scientific meaning of an analysis, supported by qualified computation and a traceable financial
decision.


57.9      Computational scale follows the statistical construction
Ten million precomputed scores say little about the cost of fitting a latent decision model. A
scientific workload must retain the dimensions that make its inference difficult. For responses
these include dates, horizons and covariance coordinates; for controlled states, the number
of states, trajectory length, validation sample and complete refits; for discovery, variables,
57.9. Computational scale follows the statistical construction                              1537


lag window and conditioning-set search. The expanded measurements therefore execute the
operations developed in the preceding chapters.

57.9.2    Deriving the execution choices

For N independent trajectories, H decisions and K finite states, one forward/backward pass
with dense transitions costs O(N HK 2 ). With A actions and M signal categories, the parameter
count is
                 p = (K − 1) + K(M − 1) + K(A − 1) + AK(K − 1) + AK.
The current reference retains adjacent-state posterior arrays, requiring O(N HK 2 ) memory
as well as forward/backward arrays. Batching whole trajectories can reduce that memory
because their likelihoods and scores add at a common parameter. It cannot replace the shared
parameter by independently optimized shard parameters. Finite-differencing an analytic score
for information adds 2p score evaluations and an O(p3 ) dense factorization. Extra starts and
B full refits multiply the fitting cost; the elapsed-time table includes only its stated B = 3
cost experiment.
   Independent trajectories and independent bootstrap fits are natural parallel units. For a
fixed parameter, deterministic reductions can combine batch log likelihoods, gradients and
information, with roundoff checked against the serial reference. Distributed optimization
additionally needs synchronized parameters and a stopping rule on the global score. Emission
validation terms must enter exactly once, with their original sample weight; duplicating them
on every worker changes the likelihood and understates calibration uncertainty. A trajectory
cannot be cut into independent fragments without transferring the correct filtering distribution
and its parameter sensitivities across the boundary.
   For a response vector with d coordinates, direct dense Bartlett covariance cost is O(nLd2 )
and storage includes the n × d scores. Prefiltering adds a d-variable regression and recolouring
solves. A date partition needs the original lagged observations, future outcome horizons
and score-lag cross-products that straddle its boundaries. Halo records supply context; only
owned origins contribute to the target sum. Center with the global mean and retain the
cross-boundary terms. Dropping them for faster reduction changes the covariance. Customer
shards under common shocks must combine their scores by calendar date before a time-series
covariance is formed.
   Conditional-independence search has a different obstacle. With v variables and lag window
L, each node can have    order vL candidate parents. Testing all conditioning sets of size s
involves up to vL
                   
                 s   sets per candidate relation before pruning; a dense partial-regression
calculation also depends on sample size and s. Actual parent selection can remove much
of this work, explaining why two samples with the same dimensions need different time. A
search cap is an algorithmic restriction that can remove oracle completeness, not a purely
physical optimization. Parallel tests must preserve stage dependencies and orientation rules.
Distributed throughput cannot be inferred by multiplying the one-thread table by the host’s
256 logical CPUs.
   The resulting architecture uses whole-customer batches for history and controlled fits,
date-aware reductions for common-shock responses, and explicit stage scheduling for discovery.
Every physical plan must reproduce the declared serial target and numerical tolerance before
claiming a speed benefit. The measured references identify dominant costs and feasible parallel
units. Large distributed storage, fault recovery, accelerator qualification and institutional
workload service levels remain concrete construction tasks rather than conclusions of these
local measurements.

57.10      Partition the experiment without changing its informa-

A serial reference is especially useful when calibration, nuisance fitting and dependent inference
interact. In the dynamic funding construction, workers first accumulate independent audit
successes and counts by stratum. The pilot fitting pass accumulates X ′ X, X ′ Y , response sums
and squared sums on the same fixed training half. Validation losses use the same candidate
penalties and pilot holdout. After choosing the penalty, a second pilot pass forms the full
normal equations. The evaluation pass accumulates the candidate score numerators and
denominators by stratum. No evaluation outcome chooses the learner or covariance bandwidth.
  Let ψ̂t be the stacked candidate-response influence, and let ψ̄ be its global mean. For lag k,
partition the later index t:

                           Γ̂k = T −1                  (ψ̂t − ψ̄)(ψ̂t−k − ψ̄)′ .

                                        b t∈Ib , t>k

Each partition receives a left halo of at most L dates, so cross-boundary products occur once.
Computing a covariance inside each partition and then averaging would omit those products
and could center different experiments. The resulting Bartlett matrix, inverse-linkage Jacobian,
audit covariance and financial weights are applied in the same order as the serial derivation.
Partition counts are not independent-cluster counts.
   Eighteen fresh-process runs compare one, two and four workers at 720, 5,760 and 23,040
evaluation origins, with four times as many pilot origins, 48 branches, seven horizons, two
candidate portfolios and two audit strata. Each worker’s numerical libraries are limited to one
observed thread. The measured workflow includes synthetic source generation, revision-aware
materialization, calibration, pilot selection/fitting, response fitting, covariance and financial
result construction. The direct reference comparison, consumer formatting, semantic checks
and receipt serialization are excluded from the reported workflow time. All serial/partitioned
financial and covariance outputs agree with the separate reference to below 5 × 10−10 in the
recorded absolute comparisons. Floating-point reduction order can change last bits; it cannot
change the data splits or the number of independent dates.
   Mean times over two fresh processes are about .195/.282/.367 seconds at 720 origins and
4.818/5.038/5.024 seconds at 23,040 origins, in one/two/four-worker order. The largest parent
process peaks around 474 MiB; this whole-process peak also includes the untimed reference
comparisons and semantic checks, rather than isolating the timed workflow’s memory. Child
peak-RSS counters are also retained, but are process-accounting maxima, not a measured
simultaneous sum across hosts or workers. Parallel execution is slower here: process and
transfer overhead dominate this small fixed basis. The evidence supports serial execution as
the default for these dimensions. It does not support a claim of distributed speedup.
   The partition construction nevertheless qualifies a harder boundary than reducing precom-
puted independent scores: audit uncertainty, pilot model selection, complete nuisance fits and
chronological covariance remain in one experiment. It is still a single-host, in-memory reference.
At scale, the source materialization and sufficient-statistic passes can be streamed, but network
transfer, object storage, fault recovery and concurrent study load remain unmeasured. Longer
POMDP histories and graph search have different dominant costs and cannot inherit this
timing result. Capacity planning must combine these measured dimensions with the earlier
latent and discovery workload profiles.

57.11      Streamed reconstruction and restartable score account-
           ing
A physical execution plan must preserve the statistical experiment after interruption. The
selected calendar source is a sorted retrospective feed: predecision controls arrive by their
decision date, outcomes correspond to the declared horizon, and realized outcomes arrive by a
fixed extraction cutoff. Streaming materialization validates these clocks and exactly one record
per origin, writes numeric columns to a temporary memory-mapped array, checks the complete
source identity, then commits the completed array. Incomplete output is not advertised as a
valid observation view. The dense reference parses the same feed and must produce identical
columns.
   The nuisance learner may still copy those columns into its fitting matrices. Streaming the
source is therefore not a claim of a general out-of-core Lasso. Where the estimator admits
sufficient-statistic passes, the score computation can stream without changing inference. For
scalar scores st , first obtain the global mean s̄. A second pass accumulates

Each partition carries its immutable bytes, fold, chronological offset and contribution identity.

resets between blocks, so no artificial lag pair bridges a deleted temporal gap.
   The checkpoint binds data and procedure identities, completed contribution prefixes, count,
global sum, lag products and halo. Atomic rename commits a coherent state; a content
checksum detects corruption of that state. Retrying a committed contribution verifies its
source and skips its numerical update. A changed source, changed bandwidth, overlapping
contribution or reordered manifest is rejected. The design is an exactly-once contribution
calculation on one host, not a claim about a distributed transactional service.
  Failure injection covers interruptions after committed moment and lag passes, interruptions
before rename, duplicate retry attempts, corrupted checkpoints, changed inputs and changed
procedures. Recovered results agree with a separately computed dense Bartlett reference to
10−12 . Source fixtures reject late features, wrong horizons, duplicate origins and outcomes
beyond the cutoff. These checks substantiate the local recovery mechanism. Network partitions,
concurrent writers and remote object-store semantics require their own platform experiment.
   The complete local comparison includes reading, fitting, uncertainty, both consumers and
serialization in fresh processes. It matches direct expert composition to the shared operations
under the same unit, provenance and inference obligations, asserting identical public output
bytes. Separate workloads vary pair counts, learner dates, audited nonlinear trajectories and
finite Gaussian episodes; peak memory and source/output/checkpoint bytes are recorded
alongside elapsed time. First JIT compilation is included in the nonlinear interval, while
imports and generation of the synthetic source are outside it. These boundaries matter more
than a favorable isolated kernel time.
   Local wrappers show computational parity for the shared scientific kernels; restartable
score persistence adds work and does not establish a speedup. The recommendation is a
serial local reference with optional checkpointing when recoverability matters. A real multi-
host comparison must retain identical samples, outputs and numerical tolerances, introduce
storage/network faults, and measure concurrent complete requests. Analyst time, adoption
and business value require repeated matched tasks by independent users, rather than an
57.11. Streamed reconstruction and restartable score accounting   1541


extrapolation from this author’s implementation effort.
Chapter 58

Banking studies as tests of the
scientific construction

The preceding design becomes concrete when the same analysis is followed from its intervention
to its financial account. This chapter uses published banking designs to explain which
information is useful, and reproducible synthetic studies to test selected estimators and
interfaces. The simulated populations and cash schedules are deliberately specified. None is
data from JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, HSBC or another institution.


58.1     What banking evidence can transfer
Published estimates arrive with an institutional design and population. In Drechsler et al.
(2017, printed pp.2–4), the deposits-channel argument uses within-bank branch comparisons
across local market concentrations. Bank-specific lending opportunities are controlled through
the comparison; the interpretation relies on a bank being able to transfer funding across its
branches. The subsequent lending analysis compares banks within a county and uses their
deposit-market exposure. Those are different aggregation levels and identifying comparisons.
The design supports a mechanism linking market power, deposit pricing and transmission, not
an effect for any new household retention offer.
   Relationship banking adds endogenous selection. The mover design in Basten and Juelsrud
(2026, Section 4.2.1, equations (6)–(8)) instruments an existing deposit relationship with the
bank’s market share in the household’s former municipality, while controlling current share
in the new location. It investigates stickiness and persistent preferences. The exclusion that
prior market availability affects later borrowing through the relationship remains substantive;
the mover population also limits transfer. This is a useful banking connection to Chapter 2,
not a universally valid instrument recipe.
   For credit supply, the preserved 2006 version of Mian and Khwaja (2006, Section III.B,
equation (5)) compares lenders to the same firm after differencing. Firm effects remove
common borrower-demand shocks. The paper explicitly discusses the multiple-bank population,
anticipated adjustments and bank-specific demand components that might remain correlated
with funding shocks. A same-borrower comparison is therefore much stronger than a pooled
lending regression, while still requiring a defensible residual supply variation.
   The HARP design of Agarwal et al. (2020, printed pp.2–3) compares program exposure
for similar agency and non-agency high-LTV mortgages. It distinguishes selected refinancing
outcomes from program-level differences including take-up. The product lesson is to retain
eligibility, assignment, application, acceptance and closing separately, and evaluate the original

                                              1542
58.2. A deposit rollout with a complete contribution account                                 1543


eligible population. A borrower cash-flow gain is not automatically a gain to the bank that
owns or services the old mortgage.
   Finally, Beraja et al. (2019, printed pp.112–113) explains why regional refinancing differences
do not identify common aggregate responses: those responses were differenced out. Its model
adds collateral and lender-income channels. Benetton (2021, pp.5–6) combines discrete-
continuous mortgage demand with multiproduct lender pricing, using capital requirements
as cost shifters under additional exclusions. These sources motivate a structural extension
interface when the bank asks about competitor responses or market-wide regulation. A local
causal estimate may discipline that model but does not determine its entire equilibrium
counterfactual.


58.2     A deposit rollout with a complete contribution account
The first synthetic study has 96 branches and 30 months indexed from zero. Twenty-four

                 Bit (0) = 30 + αi + .07t + .4 sin(t/3) + ϵit ,   αi ∼ N (0, 32 ),

For adoption cohort g and event month k = t − g ≥ 0, the stipulated balance effect is

                              τgk = {.85 + .025(g − 12)}(1 + .14k).

   The estimator compares each treated cohort’s change from g − 1 with the same change in
never-treated branches, then averages all treated cohort-month cells equally. Since cohort
sizes are equal, this target also equally weights treated branch-months. Earlier cohorts receive
more total weight because they contribute more treated months. The challenger is a single
treatment-indicator regression with branch and calendar effects. Chapter 8 explains why its
heterogeneity weights need not equal the requested aggregation.
   The financial account uses an annual funding margin m = .025, promotional rate increment
r = .0025, and monthly program cost c = 1800 dollars per treated branch. Let balances now

The credit-supply example has 600 firms, 24 banks and three distinct lenders per firm. Draw

              ∆Lf b = 2 − 3Zb + 4Uf + ηb + ϵf b ,     sd(ηb ) = .45,   sd(ϵf b ) = 1.5.

interval is [−3.027, −2.819]. This single simulation does not establish network or few-cluster
inference; it isolates the identifying comparison. A single bank would need outside-lender data
to implement it faithfully.

58.6      Joint response inference, persistence and learned adjust-
          ment
The response experiments instantiate Section 9.6 with two banking outcomes, 13 horizons
from zero through twelve, and a common set of origins. Each row of Table 58.5 contains
500 independent replications. Whole-curve coverage requires all 26 true coordinates to lie in
their reported sets. Applying 95% pointwise intervals to every plotted horizon is therefore
deliberately an adverse comparison. Zero numerical failures occurred; failed replications, had
they occurred, would remain in the denominator.

                   Case                   Iid HAC Joint         Max IV set VAR
                   Strong, white        0.434   0.414   0.958   0.930   0.952   0.950
                   Strong, persistent   0.132   0.452   0.934   0.886   0.930   0.938
                   Persistent, long     0.116   0.468   0.926   0.876   0.928   0.978
                   Weak, persistent     0.670   0.850   0.962   0.944   0.924   0.986
                   Near unit            0.246   0.598   0.818   0.724   0.776   0.966
                   Invalid IV           0.002   0.012   0.182   0.136   0.270   0.000

Table 58.5: Whole-curve coverage of nominal 95% procedures. “Joint” uses Bonferroni; “max”
uses the estimated Gaussian maximum; “IV set” inverts the joint residual tests. Standard
Monte Carlo errors near .95 are about .010. These are synthetic experiments, not coverage
guarantees.

   Strong instruments have innovation loading one; the weak case has loading .06. The reference
system has spectral radius .81; the near-unit case uses .985. Persistent instrument noise has
AR coefficient .85, rising to .95 in the near-unit case. Most experiments use 800 origins;
the long persistent case uses 5,000. The invalid instrument additionally loads on another
structural innovation by .6. The initial stationary law and all generating matrices are fixed in
the reproducible specification.
   Several method decisions follow. Joint covariance matters because a pointwise interval is
not a curve guarantee. Yet a consistent HAC estimator can still underestimate finite-sample
uncertainty: the Gaussian-maximum band covers only .886 and .876 in the two persistent strong-
instrument experiments, and .724 near the unit boundary. Bonferroni is more conservative,
but its .818 near-unit coverage also fails the preset adequacy threshold. These failures prohibit
1548                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


presenting the default bandwidth as automatically calibrated for persistent bank series. The
statistical result remains asymptotic under a fixed stability margin, not uniform near a unit
root.
   The proxy VAR has much smaller mean squared error in the correctly specified finite-order
generating law. That advantage is a consequence of its propagation restriction. It does not
establish that an economist should replace direct moments when finite-order dynamics are
misspecified. Weak normalization makes the direct and proxy mean squared errors about
752 and 13.5; 96.4% of runs yield an unbounded residual-test set in at least one coordinate.
A narrow decision recommendation would conceal the information deficiency. Instrument
invalidity defeats both routes, including zero proxy-VAR coverage in this example.
   A separately specified follow-up, with a new random seed, compares bandwidth L = ⌊n1/4 ⌋
and 4L at 5,000 origins. Their whole-curve coverages are .948 and .968, with mean widths
.312 and .338. This new experiment does not replace the original .926 finding or establish
that 4L is universally preferable. The selected workflow reports sensitivity to the lag window,
compares the structural challenger when justified and withholds a calibrated finite-sample
claim in regimes that fail the stated qualification. Picking the more favorable seed or interval
after observing the answer would be a different, unqualified procedure.
   The integrated experiment has one common random-walk trend and two stationary spreads.
Mapping stationary-change IV estimates to cumulative level responses gives whole-curve
coverage .966 and mean squared error .0479. Treating the levels as stationary gives .586
coverage and error 55.66. Cointegration is substantive here: it defines which components are
stationary and which intervention response is being summed. The comparison does not certify
unknown rank selection or arbitrary local-to-unit triangular arrays.
   With 4,000 dates and 80 bounded controls, separated-block sparse IV gives .942 coverage of
the scalar effect 1.2, compared with .950 for oracle nuisances. A three-factor reduction and an
unadjusted estimator both have zero coverage, with mean squared errors about .058 versus
.00102 for sparse adjustment. The causal confounder is sparse in this generator and need not
align with its leading covariance components. Factor compression requires an information-
preservation argument, not only a prediction score. The fixed penalty multiplier in this
experiment establishes feasibility; the required population nuisance rates remain assumptions
to justify in each application.
   For a fixed 96-bank panel, the additional mean-score experiment separates common and
bank-specific Gaussian AR components. At 800 dates, row-iid intervals cover in .116 of runs;
date-aggregate HAC covers in .856; an oracle using the exact finite-sample Gaussian variance
covers in .938. At 2,000 dates the corresponding values are .104, .890 and .946. Correctly
recognizing the date as the information unit removes a gross variance error, but the short
Bartlett lag window still underestimates persistent uncertainty. More customer rows do not
repair either problem.

the record count does not create millions of independent macroeconomic shocks.

large case has 12,000 dates and 200 controls. The temporal graph workload fits 12 variables
at 4,000 dates and propagates the joint coefficient box through 13 horizons. Its timing does
not establish uniform high-dimensional graph coverage; the inferential reference remains the
declared fixed-dimensional structural class. Exponential DAG enumeration and the 25-DAG
Gaussian reference are different workloads.
   The latent workload reconstructs complete customer trajectories, fits the unknown-emission
model with multiple starts, computes observed-information value uncertainty and refits every
bootstrap sample. The larger case has 3,200 customers and 12 decisions. Its model fit and
information calculation cost only a small fraction of the 19-refit workflow. Nineteen bootstrap
draws are suitable for demonstrating cost scaling, not precise 95% interval endpoints. The
separate 79-refit fixed-policy example and repeated-sampling study address different inferential
questions. All caps, boundary and optimizer diagnostics remain in the receipts, including
intermediate EM caps followed by likelihood refinement.
   These results change the engineering priority. For short response curves, data reconstruc-
tion and process overhead can dominate the numerical moment calculation. For controlled
likelihoods, repeated fitting dominates. Caching immutable views helps the first workload;
efficient likelihood scores, warm initial proposals checked against independent starts and
parallel independent bootstrap fits can help the second. Each proposed acceleration must
retain the same target and numerical tolerance. No bank-level labor saving follows from these
CPU timings: the expert composition comparator can use the same engines and estimators.

58.8      The implemented data and score components
Two small local components implement selected parts of Chapter 57. The temporal component
constructs Equation (57.1) under its declared inclusive availability convention. In an adversarial
fixture, the correct early and later amounts are 160 and 90. Using the latest retrospective
values gives 90 at the early decision; filtering economic time before choosing the revision
gives 110 at the later decision. Delayed data, voids and a moved economic date explain the
differences.
   The component rejects duplicate event revisions, incompatible currencies, unqualified feed
completeness and naive timestamps. Reconstruction review also added explicit rejection of
empty or non-string event/decision identities. Without it, a missing decision entity could
return a misleading zero. This is a per-decision semantic reference, not a bank-scale temporal
query engine.
   The score reducer retains raw sums/counts for entities, dates and their intersections, centers
globally and computes the stated crossed covariance. Independent batch calculations agree to
numerical precision for both unique and repeated entity/date cells. Partition merges preserve
the result. Invalid multidimensional cluster keys now fail before changing accumulator state.
The caller still owns the target weighting, Jacobian, training split and dependence argument;
duplicate-task protection remains part of the proposed execution layer.

                       Rows Total seconds Reduce seconds Peak RSS (MiB)
                     100,000          0.097            0.078              77.1
                   1,000,000          0.233            0.133             115.2
                  10,000,000          1.186            0.630             123.1

Table 58.7: Median of three fresh processes at each size on the recorded host. The workload
generates and reduces precomputed two-dimensional scores; it excludes source I/O, history

   The largest run uses ten million scores, 10,000 declared entities and 120 dates. Its dense
intersection allocation grows with the product of those group counts. Peak memory includes the
interpreter and libraries. This measurement supports only the bounded reduction operation; it
is not ten million fitted causal analyses or evidence of distributed end-to-end bank performance.
   The combined evidence establishes several useful construction tests: incorrect cash accounts
can reverse a business conclusion, current-only weights can answer the wrong dynamic question,
omitted private logging can reverse a policy estimate, and row counts can conceal shared shocks.
The additional constructions above qualify local study recipes and selected package operations.
Complete product workspaces, institutional validation and accepted sibling adoption remain
distinct engineering and review tasks.


58.9      A public household-finance analysis with unknown causal
          truth
Public data expose choices that a known-truth simulation cannot. The archived 401(k)
application extract contains 9,915 observations from the SIPP 1991 design used in the DML
literature (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; DMLonGitHub application-data repository, 2026, Section
6.2). The outcome is net financial assets; eligibility and participation are separate binary
variables. The declared controls are age, income, education, family size, marriage, two-earner
status, defined-benefit pension status, IRA participation and home ownership. All required
58.10. Public monetary histories and the boundary of an empirical claim                         1551


fields are observed in the retrieved extract, so no row is removed by the declared missingness
rule. The dollar values are those in the archive, without an inflation conversion.
   The first question is the average effect of eligibility on assets under conditional exchangeability
given these controls. This is an identifying assumption about employer/program selection
and saving behavior, not a consequence of fitting a flexible model. The second question is
participation’s complier effect with eligibility as an instrument. It adds exclusion, instrument
independence and monotonicity. The ratio of the adjusted eligibility effect on assets to
its adjusted effect on participation yields that target under those restrictions. Ordinary
participation regression would answer neither question without a different selection argument.
The graph and observation choices must also establish which controls are appropriate pre-
exposure covariates; the cross-sectional extract alone cannot verify their timing or rule out
unmeasured saving preference.
   Two nuisance families are compared: standardized quadratic features with ridge outcome
regression and logistic propensity regression, and histogram gradient boosting for both roles.
Three folds and seeds 7101–7103 are fixed in advance. The original paper’s 100-split aggregation
and learner collection are not replicated numerically; this reproduces the design and score with
declared alternative learners. The matched DoubleML check isolates score agreement from
those learner differences.
